translation: We have certainly seen the turning of your face, [O Muhammad], toward the heaven, and We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you [O believers] are, turn your faces toward it [in prayer]. Indeed, those who have been given the Scripture know that it is the truth from their Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine guidance and reassurance given to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding the change in the direction of prayer (qiblah) from Jerusalem to the Kaaba in Mecca, reflecting Allah's responsiveness to the Prophet's concerns and the affirmation of truth for those who possess scriptural knowledge.

translation: And if you brought to the People of the Book every sign, they would not follow your qiblah. Nor will you follow their qiblah, nor will they follow each other's qiblah. And if you were to follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you would then be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of seeking validation from those who are bound by their entrenched traditions and the importance of adhering to divine guidance, even when it conflicts with prevailing norms or desires.

translation: Those to whom We gave the Book recognize him (the Prophet) as they recognize their own sons. Yet a party of them conceal the truth while they know [it].
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and selective denial of truth among some of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who, despite recognizing the signs of prophethood in Muhammad (peace be upon him) from their own scriptures, deliberately conceal this truth out of arrogance, envy, or fear of losing their status, even though they are fully aware of the evidence.

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute certainty and divine origin of the truth conveyed in the Qur'an, urging believers to reject doubt and place unwavering faith in its guidance.

translation: And for each [religious following] is a direction toward which it faces. So race to [do] good deeds. Wherever you may be, Allah will bring you forth [for resurrection]. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the diversity of paths people may follow in their religious or ideological beliefs, yet it calls for a unified pursuit of righteousness and good deeds, transcending individual differences. It reassures believers that Allah’s power encompasses all things, including the ability to gather them on the Day of Judgment, reinforcing accountability and divine justice.

translation: And from wherever you go out, turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And indeed, it is the truth from your Lord. And Allah is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the Muslim community in their worship and submission to Allah, directing them to face the Kaaba in Mecca during prayer, regardless of their physical location, as a symbol of their collective devotion and alignment with divine truth.

translation: And from wherever you go out [for prayer], turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram. And wherever you [believers] are, turn your faces toward it in order that the people will not have any argument against you, except for those of them who commit wrong; so fear them not, but fear Me. And so that I may complete My favor upon you, and that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the Muslim community in their worship, directing them to face the same qibla (direction of prayer) regardless of their location, to strengthen their collective identity and devotion. It also reassures believers that they should not fear criticism or opposition from others, except those who act unjustly, while maintaining reverence for Allah. The verse underscores the completion of divine favor through guidance and unity.

translation: Just as We sent among you a Messenger from among you who recites to you Our verses and purifies you and teaches you the Book and wisdom and teaches you that which you did not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in guiding humanity, not just as a conveyor of divine revelation but also as a purifier of hearts, a teacher of divine knowledge, and an instructor in wisdom and practical understanding that transcends human experience.

translation: So remember Me; I will remember you. And be grateful to Me and do not deny Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reciprocal relationship between human remembrance of Allah and His remembrance of them, highlighting the importance of gratitude and the prohibition of ingratitude or denial of Allah's favors.

translation: O you who have believed, seek help through patience and prayer. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying on spiritual endurance and devotion to Allah in times of hardship, assuring believers that divine support is guaranteed for those who persevere with patience and faith.

translation: And do not say of those who are martyred in the cause of Allah that they are dead. Rather, they are alive, but you perceive it not.
interpretation: This verse underscores the spiritual reality of martyrdom in Islam, affirming that those who die in the path of Allah do not cease to exist but remain in a higher state of life, beyond the limited perception of the material world.

translation: And We will surely test you with something of fear and hunger and a loss of wealth and lives and fruits. But give good tidings to the patient.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of trials and tribulations in life, which serve as tests of faith and patience. It reminds believers that hardships—whether emotional, material, or physical—are part of the divine plan to purify and strengthen their resolve, and that perseverance and steadfastness in the face of adversity are rewarded with divine grace and mercy.

translation: Who, when afflicted by a calamity, say, 'Indeed we belong to Allah, and indeed to Him we will return.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the proper Muslim response to adversity—acknowledging divine ownership and the inevitability of returning to Allah, which fosters patience, submission, and trust in His decree.

translation: Those - upon them are blessings from their Lord and mercy. And it is those who are the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse underscores that divine guidance is not merely a matter of knowledge or effort but is ultimately a gift from Allah, manifesting as blessings and mercy upon those whom He has chosen to guide. It implies that true guidance is a combination of Allah's favor and the individual's response to that guidance, leading to righteousness and steadfastness.

translation: Indeed, As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the symbols of Allah. So, whoever performs Hajj or 'Umrah to the House, there is no blame upon him for walking between them. And whoever volunteers good, then indeed, Allah is appreciative and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the spiritual significance of the acts of worship, emphasizing that devotion to Allah is not merely about the physical rituals but about the sincerity and intention behind them. The mention of Allah's attributes as 'appreciative' (Shaakir) and 'Knowing' (Aleem) highlights that He recognizes and values the extra efforts and voluntary acts of goodness that believers undertake, even in the context of established rituals like Hajj and 'Umrah.

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what We have sent down of clear proofs and guidance after We made it clear for the people in the Scripture - those are cursed by Allah and cursed by those who curse,
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of concealing divine truths or guidance after it has been clearly revealed, warning that such concealment incurs divine wrath and the curse of both Allah and the righteous who uphold truth.

translation: Except for those who repent, correct themselves, and make amends. For them, I will accept their repentance, for I am the Accepting of Repentance, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless mercy of Allah, emphasizing that sincere repentance—marked by genuine remorse, corrective action, and making amends—can lead to forgiveness, regardless of past sins, as long as the repentance is heartfelt and accompanied by change.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers—upon them will be the curse of Allah and of the angels and the people, all together.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality and severity of unbelief (kufr) in the sight of Allah. The curse here signifies exclusion from divine mercy and eternal punishment, emphasizing that rejection of faith, especially when persistent until death, leads to irreversible consequences. It also highlights the unanimity of condemnation from Allah, the angels, and humanity, reflecting the gravity of such a stance.

translation: Abiding therein forever, their punishment will not be lightened, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality and severity of divine punishment for those who persist in unbelief and disobedience, emphasizing that there is no escape or mitigation of their suffering in the Hereafter.

translation: And your god is one God. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness (Tawheed) of Allah, negating any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him. It also highlights two of His most beautiful names—Ar-Rahman (The Entirely Merciful) and Ar-Raheem (The Especially Merciful)—indicating that His mercy encompasses all creation and is particularly bestowed upon the believers.

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, and the ships which sail through the sea with that which benefits people, and what Allah has sent down from the heaven of rain, giving life thereby to the earth after its death, and dispersing therein all kinds of moving creatures, and [His] directing of the winds and the clouds controlled between the heaven and the earth; [all] are signs for a people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reflecting on the signs of Allah in the natural world as a means to recognize His existence, power, and wisdom, urging those who possess intellect and understanding to ponder deeply over these signs to attain true faith and guidance.

translation: And among the people are those who take besides Allah equals [to Him] whom they love as they love Allah. But those who believe are stronger in [their] love for Allah. And if the wrongdoers could see, when they see the punishment, that all power belongs to Allah and that Allah is severe in punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the love of Allah by true believers and the misplaced devotion of those who associate partners with Him. It underscores the depth of a believer's love for Allah, which is unparalleled and absolute, while also warning those who commit shirk (associating partners with Allah) of the severe consequences of their actions, emphasizing Allah's ultimate power and the inescapable nature of His punishment.

translation: When those who were followed disown those who followed them, and they see the punishment, and all ties are cut asunder between them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate severance of relationships and disavowal in the Hereafter, where followers will disown their leaders who misled them, and the consequences of their choices will become undeniable, emphasizing the finality of divine justice and the truth of accountability.

translation: And those who followed will say, 'If only we had a turn back (to the worldly life), we could disassociate ourselves from them (the leaders) as they disassociated themselves from us.' Thus will Allah show them their deeds as regrets for them. And they are never to emerge from the Fire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate regret and realization of the followers who blindly followed their misguided leaders in this world, only to face divine justice in the Hereafter. It underscores the irreversible nature of the Hereafter and the futility of regret when it is too late, emphasizing personal accountability for one's choices and associations.

translation: O mankind, eat from whatever is on earth lawful and good and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming lawful (halal) and wholesome (tayyib) sustenance while warning against the deceptive influence of Satan, who seeks to lead people astray from righteousness and obedience to Allah.

translation: He only commands you to evil and immorality and to say about Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against false claims and attributions to Allah, emphasizing the gravity of speaking about Him without knowledge or evidence. It highlights the moral and spiritual corruption that arises from spreading misinformation or engaging in sinful acts under the guise of divine command.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Follow what Allah has revealed,' they say, 'Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.' Even though their fathers understood nothing, nor were they guided?
interpretation: This verse critiques the blind following of ancestral traditions without critical examination or adherence to divine guidance, emphasizing the importance of reason and truth over inherited customs.

translation: And the example of those who disbelieve is like one who shouts at what cannot hear except a call and cry. [They are] deaf, dumb, and blind, so they will not reason.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of calling to guidance those who are spiritually deaf, dumb, and blind to the truth due to their disbelief and arrogance. Just as shouting at an animal that cannot comprehend the words, attempting to guide those who reject divine signs with hardened hearts is equally ineffective, as their rejection stems from a deeper spiritual incapacity rather than mere ignorance.

translation: O you who have believed, eat from the good things which We have provided for you and be grateful to Allah if it is [indeed] Him that you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and mindfulness in all aspects of life, particularly in sustenance. It encourages believers to consume lawful and wholesome provisions granted by Allah and to express gratitude to Him, recognizing that true worship involves acknowledging His blessings and provisions.

translation: He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the prohibition of certain foods in Islam, emphasizing the sanctity of life and the avoidance of what is impure or associated with idolatry. The exception for those in dire necessity highlights Allah's mercy and understanding of human frailty, ensuring that survival takes precedence without indulgence or excess.

translation: Indeed, those who conceal what Allah has sent down of the Book and exchange it for a small price - those do not consume in their bellies except fire. And Allah will not speak to them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who deliberately hide or alter the teachings of the divine scripture for personal gain, emphasizing the gravity of such actions as leading to spiritual corruption and divine punishment, where even Allah's mercy and recognition are withheld from them.

translation: These are the ones who exchanged guidance for misguidance and forgiveness for punishment. How patient they are for the Fire!
interpretation: This verse highlights the folly of those who deliberately choose misguidance and wrongdoing over divine guidance and forgiveness, despite knowing the consequences. Their persistence in sin, despite the clear warnings, reveals a stubbornness that makes their eventual punishment in Hell all the more deserved.

translation: That is because Allah has sent down the Book with the truth. And indeed, those who differ about the Book are in extreme dissension.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin of the Qur'an and warns against those who dispute its truth, implying that such disagreements stem from arrogance or misguidance rather than genuine pursuit of knowledge.

translation: Righteousness is not that you turn your faces toward the east or the west, but [true] righteousness is [in] one who believes in Allah, the Last Day, the angels, the Book, and the prophets and gives wealth, in spite of love for it, to relatives, orphans, the needy, the traveler, those who ask [for help], and for freeing slaves; [and who] establishes prayer and gives zakah; [those who] fulfill their promise when they promise; and [those who] are patient in poverty and hardship and during battle. Those are the ones who have been true, and it is those who are the righteous.
interpretation: This verse underscores that true righteousness (birr) is not merely external acts like facing a particular direction in prayer, but rather it is rooted in sincere faith and consistent moral conduct. It highlights that genuine belief in Allah and the Hereafter must manifest in tangible actions—such as charity, even when one is attached to wealth, fulfilling obligations, and enduring hardships with patience—demonstrating a deep commitment to justice, compassion, and piety.

translation: O you who have believed, prescribed for you is legal retribution for those killed - the free for the free, the slave for the slave, and the female for the female. But whoever overlooks from his brother anything, then there should be a following [of rules] in a fair manner and payment to him with good conduct. That is a relief from your Lord and a mercy. But whoever transgresses after that - for him is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of justice through proportional retaliation (qisas) in cases of murder or manslaughter, ensuring that the punishment matches the crime while also allowing for mercy and forgiveness. The allowance for compensation (diyah) and the emphasis on fair resolution reflect a balance between justice and compassion, highlighting that forgiveness and reconciliation are preferred over strict retaliation. The verse underscores the divine origin of these laws as both a mercy and a means to maintain societal harmony.

translation: And for you in retaliation is life, O people of understanding, that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle that the law of retaliation (qisas) serves as a deterrent, preserving life by ensuring justice and preventing further harm, thereby fostering a society grounded in righteousness and self-restraint.

translation: Prescribed for you—when death approaches one of you—is to make a bequest to the parents and near relatives in a fair manner. This is an obligation upon the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral and religious duty of making a fair and just will to benefit one's parents and close relatives upon one's death, reflecting the importance of maintaining family ties and fulfilling obligations even in the face of mortality.

translation: But whoever alters it after hearing it - his sin is only upon those who alter it. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of altering or distorting the message of the Qur'an after its revelation, assigning the burden of sin solely to those who commit such an act, while affirming Allah's omniscience in hearing and knowing all things.

translation: But if someone fears from the testator any error or sin, and corrects between the two parties, there is no sin upon him. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of fairness and rectification in matters of inheritance or wills. It acknowledges human fallibility and encourages proactive steps to correct any perceived injustice or error, emphasizing that Allah's mercy and forgiveness are available to those who act with integrity and seek to resolve disputes.

translation: O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse establishes fasting as an obligatory act of worship for believers, drawing a parallel with previous religious traditions to emphasize its universal significance in cultivating God-consciousness (taqwa). The primary purpose of fasting is not merely abstention but spiritual refinement, fostering self-discipline, empathy for the less fortunate, and heightened awareness of divine accountability.

translation: For a limited number of days. So whoever among you is ill or on a journey, then an equal number of days [are to be made up] from other days. And upon those who can afford it, a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a needy person [each day]. And whoever volunteers excess [i.e., good deeds], it is better for him. But to fast is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse highlights the flexibility and mercy in Islamic practice, allowing for adjustments in acts of worship (like fasting) due to valid reasons such as illness or travel. It also emphasizes the spiritual and moral benefits of voluntary good deeds, while reaffirming that fasting itself is a superior act of devotion when one is able to perform it.

translation: The month of Ramadhan [is that] in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for the people and clear proofs of guidance and criterion. So whoever sights [the new moon of] the month, let him fast it; and whoever is ill or on a journey - then an equal number of other days. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the obligation of fasting during Ramadan, emphasizing its spiritual significance as a month of divine revelation and guidance. The concession for those who are ill or traveling highlights Islam's principle of ease and mercy, ensuring that worship does not become a burden. The command to complete the fast and express gratitude underscores the purpose of Ramadan: to cultivate patience, devotion, and appreciation for Allah's guidance, fostering a deeper connection with faith and submission.

translation: And when My servants ask you, [O Muhammad], concerning Me - indeed I am near. I respond to the invocation of the supplicant when he calls upon Me. So let them respond to Me [by obedience] and believe in Me that they may be [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the immediacy and accessibility of Allah's response to those who sincerely call upon Him, underscoring the importance of turning to Allah in all matters and responding to His guidance with faith and obedience.

translation: It has been made permissible for you the night preceding fasting to go to your wives [for sexual relations]. They are clothing for you, and you are clothing for them. Allah knows that you used to deceive yourselves, so He accepted your repentance and pardoned you. So now, have relations with them and seek what Allah has decreed for you. And eat and drink until the white thread of dawn becomes distinct to you from the black thread [of night]. Then complete the fast until the sunset. And do not have relations with them when you are staying for worship in the mosques. These are the limits [set by] Allah, so do not approach them. Thus does Allah make clear His verses to the people that they may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse establishes the permissibility of marital relations during the nights of Ramadan, acknowledging human nature while setting clear boundaries. It highlights Allah’s mercy in accepting repentance and removing past hardships, emphasizing the balance between spiritual devotion and natural human needs. The distinction between the white and black threads symbolizes the clarity of divine guidance in distinguishing right from wrong, urging believers to adhere strictly to Allah’s limits to attain righteousness.

translation: And do not consume one another's wealth unjustly or send it [in bribes] to the authorities in order that [they might aid] you [to] consume a portion of the wealth of the people in sin, while you know [it is unlawful].
interpretation: This verse condemns the exploitation of wealth through deceit, fraud, or unjust means, including bribery, which corrupts both the giver and the receiver, undermining societal justice and moral integrity.

translation: They ask you [O Muhammad] about the new moons. Say, "They are measurements of time for the people and for Hajj." And it is not righteousness to enter houses from the back, but righteousness is [in] one who fears Allah. And enter houses from their doors. And fear Allah that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following divine guidance in both temporal and spiritual matters, highlighting that true righteousness lies in piety and adherence to Allah's commands rather than superficial or ritualistic actions.

translation: And fight in the cause of Allah those who fight you, but do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of just and defensive warfare in Islam, permitting fighting only against those who initiate hostilities, while strictly prohibiting aggression or exceeding the bounds of justice, as Allah's disapproval is directed toward those who transgress these limits.

translation: And kill them wherever you find them, and drive them out from where they drove you out. And fitnah (persecution) is worse than killing. And do not fight them at the Sacred Mosque until they fight you there. But if they fight you, then kill them. Such is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse outlines the rules of engagement in warfare for Muslims, emphasizing the gravity of persecution (fitnah) over killing, and restricting combat within the Sacred Mosque unless initiated by the enemy. It reflects a principle of self-defense and justice, where retaliation is proportional to aggression, and the sanctity of holy spaces is upheld unless violated.

translation: But if they cease [from hostility], then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine attributes of forgiveness and mercy, emphasizing that Allah's compassion is extended to those who desist from wrongdoing or conflict, encouraging repentance and reconciliation.

translation: And fight them until there is no fitnah and [until] the religion, all of it, is for Allah. And if they cease - then indeed, Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate objective of fighting in the cause of Allah: to eliminate oppression (fitnah) and establish the worship of Allah alone, free from any association or corruption. It does not sanction aggression but rather permits defensive or restorative action to uphold justice and monotheism, with the condition that hostilities cease once the oppressive system is dismantled, and punishment is reserved only for those who persist in wrongdoing.

translation: The sacred month for the sacred month, and all sacred things are subject to retaliation. So whoever has assaulted you, then assault him in the same way he has assaulted you. And fear Allah and know that Allah is with those who fear Him.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of reciprocity in justice, particularly within the sacred context of the sacred months and sacred inviolabilities. It emphasizes that transgressions against sanctity or personal rights must be met with proportional response, but within the bounds of divine law. The verse also underscores the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness), reminding believers that Allah is with those who uphold justice and restraint, guiding them in their actions.

translation: And spend in the cause of Allah and do not throw yourselves with your own hands into destruction. And do good; indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving in the path of Allah (jihad) while also warning against reckless actions that could lead to harm or destruction. It encourages balanced and thoughtful expenditure of resources, whether in personal efforts or financial contributions, and underscores the virtue of excellence (ihsan) in all actions, as Allah rewards those who act with excellence and righteousness.

translation: And complete the Hajj and 'Umrah for Allah. But if you are prevented, then [offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And do not shave your heads until the sacrificial animal has reached its place of slaughter. And whoever among you is ill or has an ailment of the head [making shaving necessary must offer] a ransom of fasting [three days] or charity or sacrifice. And when you are secure, then whoever utilizes the 'Umrah [during the Hajj months] for [his] enjoyment, [he must offer] what can be obtained with ease of sacrificial animals. And whoever cannot find [a sacrificial animal], then a fast of three days during Hajj and seven when you return [home]. That is ten complete [days]. This is for those whose family is not in the area of al-Masjid al-Haram. And fear Allah and know that Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse outlines the obligations and procedures for performing Hajj and 'Umrah, emphasizing the importance of fulfilling these acts of worship for Allah with sincerity and devotion. It highlights the flexibility and mercy in Islam, allowing for alternative acts (such as fasting or charity) when physical constraints prevent full observance. The verse also underscores the significance of patience, adherence to divine commands, and the awareness of Allah’s severe punishment for those who disregard His laws.

translation: The Hajj months are well-known. So whoever has made Hajj obligatory upon them, then [let there be no] sexual relations, wrongdoing, nor disputing during Hajj. And whatever good you do, Allah knows it. And take provisions, but indeed, the best provision is fear of Allah. And fear Me, O you of understanding!
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of the Hajj pilgrimage by prohibiting immoral behavior, sin, and argumentation during its prescribed months. It also underscores the importance of righteous actions, which Allah is fully aware of, and encourages believers to prepare spiritually by cultivating taqwa (God-consciousness) as the ultimate provision for the journey of faith.

translation: There is no blame upon you for seeking bounty from your Lord. So when you have completed your rites from Arafat, then remember Allah at al-Mash'ar al-Haram. And remember Him, as He has guided you, and indeed, you were before that among those astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permissibility of engaging in trade and seeking livelihood during Hajj, reassuring pilgrims that worldly pursuits do not invalidate their acts of worship. It also underscores the importance of gratitude and remembrance of Allah, linking guidance to sincere devotion and contrasting past ignorance with present clarity.

translation: Then depart from where the people depart, and seek forgiveness from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of following the established practices of the pilgrimage (Hajj) and the unity of the Muslim community in their acts of worship, while also reminding believers of the need for repentance and seeking Allah's forgiveness, highlighting Allah's attributes of mercy and forgiveness.

translation: But when you have completed your rites, remember Allah as you remember your forefathers or even more. And there are among the people who say, "Our Lord, give us [something] in this world," and for such there will be no share in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of sincere and profound remembrance of Allah after completing the rites of Hajj or any other act of worship, emphasizing that such remembrance should surpass even the intensity of worldly attachments like remembering one's ancestors. It also serves as a caution against those who prioritize worldly gains over spiritual and eternal rewards, highlighting the stark contrast between their fate and the true believers who seek Allah's favor in both this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And among them are those who say, 'Our Lord, grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and save us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the balanced supplication of a believer, seeking both worldly blessings and eternal success while also seeking protection from divine punishment, reflecting a comprehensive and humble approach to faith.

translation: For them will be a share of what they have earned. And Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, affirming that individuals will receive a just recompense for their deeds, whether good or evil, without injustice or delay. The mention of Allah's swift accounting serves as both a reassurance to the righteous that their deeds will be promptly rewarded and a warning to the wrongdoers that their actions will be swiftly accounted for, emphasizing the inevitability and immediacy of divine justice.

translation: And remember Allah during the counted days. Then whoever hastens [his departure] in two days - there is no blame upon him; and whoever delays - there is no blame upon him - for whoever fears Allah. And fear Allah and know that you will be gathered to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of remembering Allah during specific days, highlighting that the prescribed acts of remembrance are flexible in their timing within those days, as long as one fulfills the obligation with sincerity and piety. The underlying meaning is that Allah's commands are designed to be practical and accommodating, provided they are approached with a sense of duty and consciousness of Allah (taqwa).

translation: And among the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life, and he calls Allah to witness as to what is in his heart, yet he is the most intense of adversaries.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who outwardly present themselves as believers or allies, using eloquent speech and invoking Allah’s name to appear sincere, while their hearts harbor enmity and opposition. It serves as a warning against being deceived by superficial piety or flattery, emphasizing the importance of discerning true intentions beyond mere words.

translation: And when he turns away, he strives throughout the earth to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And Allah does not like corruption.
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive nature of those who turn away from guidance, emphasizing that their actions lead to widespread harm—both to the environment (crops) and society (progeny)—while God’s divine nature inherently opposes such corruption, underscoring the moral responsibility of humans to uphold justice and preservation.

translation: And when it is said to him, 'Fear Allah,' pride in sin takes hold of him. Hellfire will be enough for him—and what an evil resting place!
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive nature of arrogance and defiance in the face of divine guidance, illustrating how pride can blind a person to their own wrongdoing, leading them to reject righteousness and ultimately face severe punishment.

translation: And among the people is he who sells himself seeking the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is Kind to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate act of devotion and sacrifice, where an individual surrenders their own desires and even their life for the sake of Allah’s pleasure, demonstrating unwavering faith and trust in divine reward.

translation: O you who have believed, enter into Islam completely and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fully embracing Islam in all aspects of life, not just superficially, and warns against being influenced by Satan's deceptions, which can lead one astray from the path of righteousness.

translation: But if you slip after the clear proofs have come to you, then know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that even after receiving clear guidance, humans are prone to faltering or making mistakes, and such slips do not escape Allah's knowledge or power. The mention of Allah's attributes—'Exalted in Might' and 'Wise'—implies that He has the power to correct or punish, but also the wisdom to guide back to the right path, emphasizing both divine justice and mercy.

translation: Do they await except that Allah should come to them in covers of clouds and [with] the angels and the matter is [then] decided? And to Allah [all] matters are returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine judgment and the finality of Allah's decree, emphasizing that all affairs ultimately return to Him, leaving no room for delay or escape from accountability.

translation: O children of Israel, remember My favor which I have bestowed upon you, and how I favored you over the worlds. And whoever changes the favor of Allah after it has come to him - then indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder to the Children of Israel of the numerous clear signs and blessings Allah has bestowed upon them, emphasizing their unique status among nations. It warns against ingratitude or altering the divine favors through disobedience or rejection of truth, highlighting that such actions incur severe divine punishment, underscoring the importance of recognizing and preserving Allah's blessings through faith and righteousness.

translation: The life of this world has been made to appear attractive to those who disbelieve, and they ridicule the believers. But those who fear Allah will be above them on the Day of Resurrection. And Allah provides for whom He wills without account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly attractions for the disbelievers, who mock the believers, while emphasizing that true honor and provision lie in piety and trust in Allah's wisdom, which transcends mere worldly measures.

translation: Mankind was [of] one religion [before their deviation]; then Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good tidings and warners and sent down with them the Scripture in truth to judge between the people concerning that in which they differed. And none differed over the Scripture except those who were given it - after the clear proofs came to them - out of jealous animosity among themselves. And Allah guided those who believed to the truth concerning that over which they had differed, by His permission. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse underscores the fundamental unity of humanity's original guidance from Allah, which was later obscured by human deviation and conflict. It highlights the role of the prophets as messengers of truth and justice, sent to clarify divine guidance and resolve disputes among people. The subsequent divergence among those entrusted with the Scripture is attributed not to a lack of clarity in the message but to human arrogance and envy, which led to schism and injustice. The verse also emphasizes Allah's mercy in guiding those who seek truth and submit to His will, reaffirming that ultimate guidance is a divine gift contingent upon sincere faith and righteousness.

translation: Do you think that you will enter Paradise without being tested like those who came before you? They were afflicted with hardship and adversity, and were shaken until [even] the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of Allah?" Unquestionably, the help of Allah is near.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of trials and tribulations in the path of faith, emphasizing that ease and success are not granted without enduring hardship. It serves as a reminder that even the righteous and the prophets faced severe tests, and their perseverance was ultimately rewarded by divine assistance. The verse also highlights the importance of steadfastness in faith, as the companions of the Prophet (peace be upon him) questioned the delay in divine help, yet their unwavering belief was eventually vindicated.

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], what they should spend. Say, "Whatever you spend of good is [to be given] to parents and relatives and orphans and the needy and the traveler. And whatever you do of good - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of spending in the way of Allah with sincerity and for the rightful recipients, highlighting that Allah is fully aware of all acts of goodness, ensuring that such deeds are not in vain and will be rewarded appropriately.

translation: Fighting has been enjoined upon you, while it is hateful to you. But it is possible that you dislike a thing and it is good for you; and it is possible that you love a thing and it is bad for you. And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine wisdom behind seemingly unfavorable obligations or circumstances, emphasizing that human perception is limited compared to Allah's infinite knowledge. It teaches believers to trust in Allah's decree, even when faced with hardships or commands that may initially seem burdensome, as what may appear harmful or unpleasant could ultimately lead to greater good.

translation: They ask you about the sacred month—about fighting therein. Say, 'Fighting therein is great [evil], but averting [people] from the way of Allah, rejecting it, and [preventing access to] al-Masjid al-Haram, and expelling its people from it, are greater [evil] in the sight of Allah. And fitnah (persecution) is worse than killing.' And they will not cease to fight you until they turn you back from your religion if they are able. And whoever of you reverts from his religion [to disbelief] and dies while he is a disbeliever—for those, their deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter. And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of disrupting religious sanctity and spreading persecution (fitnah) over the mere act of fighting, even in a sacred month. It highlights that the true evil lies in obstructing faith, denying truth, and forcibly expelling believers from their sacred spaces. The verse also warns of the relentless opposition faced by believers, where enemies will strive to extinguish their faith, and emphasizes the irreversible consequences of apostasy, where turning away from Islam results in the nullification of all deeds and eternal damnation.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed, those who have emigrated and striven in the cause of Allah - it is those who can expect the mercy of Allah. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith is not merely a declaration but is proven through action—migration (hijrah) for the sake of Allah and striving (jihad) in His path. It reassures believers that their efforts, no matter how challenging, are recognized by Allah, who is ultimately the source of mercy and forgiveness.

translation: They ask you about wine and gambling. Say, 'In them is great sin and [yet, some] benefit for people. But their sin is greater than their benefit.' And they ask you what they should spend. Say, 'The excess [beyond your needs].' Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses [of revelation] that you might give thought.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of prioritizing moral and spiritual well-being over worldly gains, even when the latter may seem beneficial. It teaches that some actions, though they may offer temporary advantages, carry a greater burden of harm—both individually and societally—than their perceived benefits, and thus should be avoided. The directive to spend 'the excess' reflects a balanced approach to charity, emphasizing generosity without causing hardship to oneself.

translation: In this world and the Hereafter. And they ask you about the orphans. Say, 'Improving their condition is best. And if you associate with them, they are your brothers.' And Allah knows the corrupter from the reformer. And if Allah willed, He could have imposed difficulties upon you. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of treating orphans with kindness and fairness, highlighting that their well-being is a matter of concern in both this life and the Hereafter. It instructs that improving their situation is the best course of action, and even if one chooses to interact with them closely, they should be treated as brothers, fostering a sense of familial responsibility. The verse also underscores Allah’s omniscience in distinguishing between those who seek to corrupt and those who strive to reform, reminding believers that Allah’s wisdom and power could have made their duties more burdensome if He willed. This serves as a call to act with compassion and integrity in all dealings with orphans, trusting in Allah’s justice and wisdom.

translation: And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe. And a believing slave woman is better than a polytheist, even if she pleases you. And do not marry polytheistic men until they believe. And a believing slave is better than a polytheist, even if he pleases you. Those invite to the Fire, but Allah invites to Paradise and to forgiveness, by His permission. And He makes clear His verses to the people that perhaps they may remember.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of faith as the foundation for marital relationships, emphasizing that a person's belief system takes precedence over superficial attractions or social status. It warns against forming bonds with those who reject monotheism, as their influence may lead to spiritual harm, while Allah's guidance leads to salvation and mercy.

translation: And they ask you about menstruation. Say, 'It is harm, so keep away from wives during menstruation. And do not approach them until they are purified. And when they are purified, then come to them from where Allah has ordained for you. Indeed, Allah loves those who repent and those who purify themselves.'
interpretation: This verse establishes a temporary separation between spouses during menstruation due to its physical discomfort ('adha'), emphasizing patience and discipline. The command to approach wives only after purification underscores the sanctity of intimacy, which should be entered with purity—both physical and spiritual—reflecting a balance between natural human needs and divine boundaries.

translation: Your wives are a place of cultivation for you, so come to your place of cultivation however you wish and send forth [righteousness] for yourselves. And fear Allah and know that you will meet Him. And give good tidings to the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permissibility and flexibility in marital relations within the bounds of Islamic law, while also reminding believers of their ultimate accountability before Allah. It underscores the balance between fulfilling one's desires in a lawful manner and the importance of righteous deeds and piety, as all actions will be answered for on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And do not make [your oath by] Allah an excuse against being righteous and fearing Allah and making peace among people. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse cautions against using oaths or vows as a pretext to avoid acts of righteousness, piety, or reconciliation, emphasizing that sincerity in faith and deeds is paramount, regardless of past oaths, as Allah is fully aware of intentions and actions.

translation: Allah does not impose blame upon you for what is unintentional in your oaths, but He imposes blame upon you for what your hearts have earned. And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between intentional and unintentional actions, emphasizing that God's judgment is based on the sincerity and intent of the heart rather than mere outward words or slips of the tongue.

translation: For those who swear abstinence from their wives, there shall be a waiting period of four months. If they return [to normal relations], then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the practice of 'ila' (oath of abstinence) in pre-Islamic Arabia, where a husband would swear to abstain from sexual relations with his wife for an indefinite period. The verse imposes a fixed waiting period of four months, after which the husband must either resume marital relations or face divorce. This regulation prevents indefinite separation and protects the rights of the wife, emphasizing Allah's mercy and forgiveness in cases where the husband repents and reconciles.

translation: And if they are determined on divorce, then indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's awareness of all intentions and decisions, including those related to divorce, emphasizing that nothing escapes His knowledge, and He is fully cognizant of the consequences and wisdom behind such actions.

translation: Divorced women remain in waiting for three periods, and it is not lawful for them to conceal what Allah has created in their wombs if they believe in Allah and the Last Day. And their (former) husbands have more right to take them back in this [period] if they want reconciliation. And due to the wives is similar to what is expected of them, according to what is reasonable. But the men have a degree [of responsibility] over them. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the waiting period (*iddah*) for divorced women, ensuring clarity in lineage and the possibility of reconciliation. It emphasizes the husband's right to reconsider the divorce during this period if reconciliation is intended, while also outlining mutual rights and responsibilities in marriage, highlighting the elevated role of men in maintaining family structure, all within the framework of divine wisdom and justice.

translation: Divorce is twice. Then, either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment. And it is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them unless both fear that they will not maintain the limits of Allah. But if you fear that they will not maintain the limits of Allah, then there is no blame upon either of them for what she gives up [from her dowry] to obtain her freedom. These are the limits of Allah, so do not transgress them. And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah - it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes a structured approach to divorce within Islamic law, emphasizing balance, fairness, and the sanctity of marital boundaries. The mention of 'twice' signifies that reconciliation is encouraged before final separation, promoting the preservation of family ties where possible. The allowance for the wife to 'give up' part of her dowry in exchange for freedom reflects a recognition of mutual consent and financial equity in difficult marital circumstances. The prohibition against transgressing Allah's limits underscores the divine wisdom behind these rulings, cautioning against exploitation or injustice in marital disputes.

translation: But if he divorces her [for the third time], then she is not lawful for him afterward until she marries a husband other than him. And if he divorces her, there is no blame upon them for returning to each other if they fear that they will maintain the limits of Allah. And these are the limits of Allah, which He makes clear for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of divorce in Islam, emphasizing that it should not be taken lightly or repeated unnecessarily. The requirement for the woman to marry another man before reconciling with her first husband serves as a deterrent against hasty or repeated divorces, ensuring that the sanctity of marriage is preserved. The mention of maintaining 'the limits of Allah' highlights that reconciliation is only valid if it is done within the bounds of Islamic law and with sincere intention to uphold those boundaries.

translation: And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their waiting period, either retain them honorably or release them honorably. And do not retain them to harm them, to transgress [against their rights]. And whoever does that has certainly wronged himself. And do not take the verses of Allah in jest. And remember the favor of Allah upon you and what has been revealed to you of the Book and wisdom, by which He instructs you. And fear Allah and know that Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ethical and balanced approach Islam mandates in marital dissolution, emphasizing justice, kindness, and the avoidance of harm or malice. It warns against using divorce as a tool for oppression or retaliation, highlighting the moral and spiritual consequences of such actions. The verse also calls for gratitude toward divine guidance and the recognition of Allah’s knowledge and authority over all matters, reinforcing the importance of adhering to divine principles in personal and social conduct.

translation: And when you divorce women and they have fulfilled their waiting period, do not prevent them from remarrying their husbands if they agree among themselves in a recognized manner. That is an admonition for whoever of you believes in Allah and the Last Day. That is purer and more righteous for you. And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of fairness and kindness in marital matters, even after divorce, by allowing women the freedom to remarry if they mutually agree with their former husbands, provided it is done in a just and recognized manner. It serves as a reminder for believers to act with righteousness and piety, trusting in Allah's wisdom over their own limited understanding.

translation: Mothers may breastfeed their children for two full years—if the father wishes the breastfeeding to be completed. And it is the duty of the father to provide for them and clothe them reasonably. No soul shall be burdened beyond its capacity. No mother shall be harmed by her child, nor shall the father be harmed by his child. And the same duty is incumbent upon the heir. If the parents decide, by mutual consent and consultation, to wean the child, there is no blame on them. And if you decide to have your children breastfed by another woman, there is no blame on you as long as you pay what you agreed upon reasonably. And fear Allah, and know that Allah sees what you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes the rights and responsibilities of parents towards their children, particularly in the context of breastfeeding and financial support. It emphasizes the importance of mutual consultation and consent between parents in decisions regarding their child’s upbringing, ensuring that no harm comes to either party. The verse also highlights the principle of fairness and reasonableness in fulfilling obligations, whether in breastfeeding arrangements or financial provisions. Ultimately, it underscores the need for piety and awareness of Allah’s watchfulness over human actions.

translation: And those who are taken in death among you and leave wives behind - they shall wait by themselves for four months and ten days. Then when they have fulfilled their term, there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner. And Allah is [fully] Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes a waiting period (*iddah*) for widows to mourn and reflect, ensuring emotional and legal clarity before remarriage, while also protecting their dignity and autonomy within the bounds of Islamic law.

translation: And there is no blame upon you for what you indirectly suggest or conceal within yourselves concerning marriage proposals with women. Allah knows that you will mention them, but do not secretly promise them except by saying a recognized word. And do not resolve on the marriage contract until the waiting period reaches its appointed time. And know that Allah knows what is within yourselves, so beware of Him. And know that Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the etiquette of proposing marriage, emphasizing sincerity and patience. It permits indirect or subtle hints about marriage without blame, while discouraging secret or deceptive promises. The waiting period (iddah) is highlighted as a time for reflection and adherence to divine timelines, reinforcing trust in Allah’s knowledge of human intentions and His attributes of mercy and forbearance.

translation: There is no blame upon you for divorcing women you have not touched or for which you have not specified a dowry. But [if you do so], provide them with compensation—the wealthy according to his capability and the poor according to his capability—a provision according to what is acceptable, a duty upon the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse establishes the permissibility of divorce under certain conditions while emphasizing the ethical obligation to provide fair and reasonable compensation to the wife, proportional to the husband's financial means. It underscores the principle of justice and kindness in marital dissolution, ensuring that the wife is not left destitute, reflecting the Qur'an's broader emphasis on equity and compassion in human relationships.

translation: And if you divorce them before you have touched them but have already specified for them a dowry, then [give them] half of what you specified—unless they forgo it or the one in whose hand is the marriage contract forgoes it. And to forgo it is nearer to righteousness. And do not forget to show mutual kindness; indeed, Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of fairness and kindness in marital and financial dealings, even in the context of divorce. It emphasizes that while a husband is obligated to fulfill half of the agreed dowry if he divorces his wife before consummation, the wife has the right to waive this right entirely, and the husband is encouraged to accept this waiver as an act of righteousness. The verse also underscores the broader principle of mutual kindness and generosity in relationships, reminding believers that Allah is fully aware of their actions and intentions.

translation: Guard strictly the prayers, especially the middle prayer, and stand before Allah in obedience.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the paramount importance of maintaining regular and focused prayer, particularly the middle prayer (often understood as the 'Asr prayer), as a fundamental act of devotion and submission to Allah. It underscores the need for mindfulness and sincerity in worship, ensuring that prayers are performed with full attention and humility.

translation: But if you are in fear, then [pray] on foot or riding. But when you are secure, then remember Allah as He has taught you what you did not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the flexibility of religious practice in times of hardship, while underscoring the importance of gratitude and remembrance of Allah once security is restored, highlighting the balance between practicality and devotion.

translation: And those of you who die and leave behind wives should bequeath for their wives a provision for one year without causing them to leave. But if they leave [on their own], then there is no blame upon you for what they do with themselves in an acceptable manner. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of providing for one's spouse after death, ensuring financial security for the widow during the waiting period (iddah) while also granting her the freedom to remarry if she chooses, without coercion or restriction.

translation: And for divorced women is [a right of] accommodation and provision in a recognized manner—a duty upon the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ethical and moral obligation of providing for divorced women with kindness and fairness, highlighting that such conduct is a hallmark of righteousness and piety, rather than mere legal compliance.

translation: Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses so that you may use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and rational thought in understanding divine guidance, implying that true comprehension of Allah's signs requires intellectual engagement rather than mere passive acceptance.

translation: Have you not considered those who left their homes in thousands, fearing death? Allah said to them, "Die," then He restored them to life. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of them are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of life and the absolute power of Allah over it, serving as a reminder of human dependence on divine will rather than relying solely on worldly precautions.

translation: And fight in the cause of Allah and know that Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fighting for a just cause, specifically in the path of Allah, while reminding believers that Allah is fully aware of their intentions and actions, thus encouraging sincerity and righteousness in their endeavors.

translation: Who is it that would loan Allah a goodly loan so that He will multiply it for him many times over? And Allah restricts and expands [His provision], and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine reward for righteous deeds, particularly acts of charity or generosity, which Allah magnifies manifold in the Hereafter. It also underscores Allah's absolute control over sustenance and provision, reminding humans of their dependence on Him and the transient nature of worldly wealth, which is subject to His will.

translation: Have you not considered the assembly of the Children of Israel after [the time of] Moses when they said to a prophet of theirs, 'Send to us a king, and we will fight in the way of Allah.' He said, 'Would you perhaps refrain from fighting if fighting was prescribed for you?' They said, 'And what is wrong with us that we should not fight in the way of Allah while we have been driven out from our homes and our children?' But when fighting was prescribed for them, they turned away, except for a few of them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the test of true commitment to faith and the struggle for justice. Initially, the Israelites expressed a strong desire to fight for the sake of Allah when faced with oppression, but when the actual command to fight was given, most faltered. This serves as a lesson about the difference between verbal declarations of faith and the willingness to act upon them, especially when it requires sacrifice. It also underscores Allah's awareness of those who are truly sincere versus those who are merely claiming faith without genuine conviction.

translation: And their prophet said to them, "Indeed, Allah has appointed for you Talut (Saul) as a king." They said, "How can he have kingship over us when we are more entitled to kingship than him, and he has not been given wealth in abundance?" He said, "Indeed, Allah has chosen him over you and increased him greatly in knowledge and stature. And Allah gives His kingdom to whom He wills, and Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine selection over worldly criteria such as wealth or lineage. The people initially rejected Talut (Saul) as their king due to his lack of material wealth and their own perceived superiority. However, the prophet clarified that Allah's choice is based on qualities like knowledge, wisdom, and physical strength, not material wealth. This underscores that true leadership and authority come from Allah, who knows what is best for His creation, and that human judgments based solely on worldly standards are often flawed.

translation: And their prophet said to them, 'Indeed, a sign of his kingship is that the Ark will come to you, containing tranquility from your Lord and a remnant left by the families of Moses and Aaron, carried by the angels. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine signs (ayaat) as evidence of truth and guidance, particularly for those who are believers. The presence of the Ark—symbolizing divine favor and continuity of guidance—along with the angels carrying it, serves as a tangible proof of Allah’s sovereignty and support for His prophets and their followers. It also underscores the concept that true belief is not merely intellectual assent but is demonstrated through recognizing and affirming Allah’s signs in the world.

translation: Then when Saul departed with the soldiers, he said, "Indeed, Allah will test you with a river. So whoever drinks from it is not [worthy] of me, and whoever does not taste it is [worthy] of me, except one who takes [from it] in the hollow of his hand." But they drank from it, except for a few of them. Then when he had crossed it—he and those who believed with him—they said, "We have no power today against Goliath and his soldiers." Said those who were certain that they would meet Allah, "How many a small company has overcome a large company by permission of Allah. And Allah is with the patient."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and perseverance in the face of overwhelming odds. It demonstrates that true strength comes from trust in Allah and steadfastness, rather than sheer numbers or physical power. The few who resisted drinking from the river symbolize those who remain steadfast in their faith and discipline, even when faced with temptation or hardship. The subsequent statement about small groups overcoming larger ones by Allah's permission reinforces the idea that divine support is granted to those who are patient and steadfast in their reliance on Him.

translation: And when they faced Goliath and his troops, they said, "Our Lord, pour upon us patience and make our steps firm, and help us against the disbelieving people."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking divine assistance and steadfastness in the face of overwhelming challenges, emphasizing reliance on God's support rather than solely on one's own strength.

translation: So they defeated them by the permission of Allah, and David killed Goliath. And Allah gave him the kingship and wisdom and taught him from that which He willed. And if it were not for Allah's repelling [some] people by means of others, the earth would have been corrupted, but Allah is full of bounty to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the interplay between divine decree and human agency, emphasizing that victory and success come from Allah's permission and support. It also underscores the importance of wisdom and knowledge as gifts from Allah, which can lead to just leadership and governance. The latter part of the verse serves as a reminder of Allah's mercy in preventing widespread corruption through the balance of power among people, reflecting the principle of divine wisdom in sustaining order in the world.

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you in truth, and indeed, you [O Muhammad] are from among the messengers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and absolute truthfulness of the Qur'anic revelations, affirming the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) status as a genuine messenger of Allah, tasked with conveying these unerring signs to humanity.

translation: These messengers—We have preferred some of them over others. Among them were those Allah spoke to directly, and He raised some of them in degree. And We gave Jesus, son of Mary, clear proofs and supported him with the Holy Spirit. If Allah had willed, those who came after them would not have fought each other after the clear proofs had come to them. But they differed—some of them believed, and some of them disbelieved. If Allah had willed, they would not have fought, but Allah does what He intends.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom in the varying ranks and roles assigned to different prophets, highlighting that Allah’s will is supreme and that human free will operates within His predetermined plan. The mention of Jesus (peace be upon him) receiving clear proofs and divine support serves as a reminder of Allah’s power to elevate whom He wills, while the subsequent conflict among later generations—despite the clarity of guidance—illustrates the consequences of human choice and the reality of trial in faith.

translation: O you who have believed, spend from what We have provided for you before there comes a Day in which there is no exchange and no friendship and no intercession. And the disbelievers - they are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the urgency of charitable spending in this life, as the Hereafter offers no opportunities for transactions, relationships, or intercession to alter one's fate, highlighting the absolute justice of Allah and the futility of relying on anything other than sincere faith and righteous deeds.

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is [presently] before them and what will be after them, and they encompass not a thing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth, and their preservation tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting His eternal and self-sustaining nature, which transcends any human limitations such as sleep or drowsiness. It underscores His comprehensive knowledge and authority over all creation, while also affirming that intercession is only possible through His divine permission. The mention of His 'Kursi' (often interpreted as His Throne or Authority) encompassing the heavens and the earth signifies His boundless power and the ease with which He sustains and governs all existence, free from any burden or fatigue.

translation: There shall be no compulsion in religion. The right path has become distinct from the wrong path. So whoever disbelieves in Taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold that will never break. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of free will in matters of faith, asserting that true belief must be a matter of personal conviction rather than coercion. It highlights the clarity of guidance, where the distinction between truth (righteousness) and falsehood (error) is evident. The 'most trustworthy handhold' metaphorically represents unwavering faith in Allah, which is unshakable and eternal, contrasting with the fleeting nature of false idols or corrupt systems (Taghut). The verse underscores that genuine faith is a choice, not an imposition, and that Allah is fully aware of the sincerity behind one's beliefs.

translation: Allah is the ally of those who believe. He brings them out from darknesses into the light. And those who disbelieve - their allies are Taghut, they take them out from the light into darknesses. It is those who are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental distinction between the paths of believers and disbelievers, emphasizing divine guidance versus misguidance. It underscores that true guidance comes solely from Allah, who leads the believers from spiritual darkness (ignorance, disbelief, or sin) to light (faith, righteousness, and clarity). Conversely, the disbelievers are misled by 'Taghut'—often interpreted as false deities, oppressive forces, or any system that opposes Allah’s commandments—which drags them further into spiritual darkness, away from divine truth. The verse serves as a stark warning about the consequences of rejecting Allah’s guidance, as those who persist in disbelief are destined for eternal punishment in the Fire.

translation: Have you not considered the one who argued with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him kingship? When Abraham said, "My Lord is the One who gives life and causes death," he said, "I give life and cause death." Abraham said, "Indeed, Allah brings the sun from the east; so bring it from the west." So the disbeliever was overwhelmed [by astonishment], and Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of human arrogance in the face of divine omnipotence, demonstrating that no amount of worldly power or intellect can rival the absolute authority of Allah, who alone controls life, death, and all natural phenomena.

translation: Or [consider such a one] as the one who passed by a township which had fallen into complete ruin, saying, 'How shall Allah bring this back to life after its death?' So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years; then brought him back to life [and] said: 'How long did you remain [in this state]?' He said: 'I remained a day or part of a day.' [Allah] said: 'Nay, you have remained thus a hundred years. Now look at your food and your drink which have not spoiled, and look at your donkey. And [We did so] in order to make you a sign for mankind. And look at the bones, how We bring them together, then clothe them with flesh.' When this was clearly shown to him, he said: 'I know that Allah has power over all things.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power of Allah to resurrect the dead and restore life, even after complete decay, as demonstrated by the revival of the man and his donkey. It serves as a profound reminder of divine omnipotence and the inevitability of resurrection, challenging human skepticism and inviting reflection on the signs of Allah's creative power in the natural world.

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said, 'My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead.' [Allah] said, 'Have you not believed?' He said, 'Yes, but [I ask] only that my heart may be satisfied.' [Allah] said, 'Take four birds, then incline them to yourself, then place on each mountain a portion of them, then call them; they will come [flying] to you in haste. And know that Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human need for tangible proof to strengthen faith, even when one's belief is already firm. It demonstrates Allah's ability to transcend the natural order, affirming His omnipotence and wisdom in ways that resonate with human understanding.

translation: The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a seed [of grain] which grows seven spikes; in each spike is a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies [His reward] for whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the principle of divine multiplication of righteous deeds, emphasizing that Allah rewards generosity in His cause abundantly and beyond human calculation, reflecting His boundless generosity and perfect knowledge of intentions and deeds.

translation: Those who spend their wealth in the cause of Allah and then do not follow up what they have spent with reminders of their generosity or with injury, their reward is with their Lord. And there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purity and sincerity of charitable acts in Islam. It highlights that true generosity is not merely the act of spending wealth but is also free from any ulterior motives, such as seeking praise or causing harm to the recipient. The reward for such selfless giving is guaranteed by Allah, ensuring the giver's freedom from fear and sorrow in the Hereafter, reflecting the spiritual and moral integrity of their actions.

translation: Kind words and forgiveness are better than charity followed by injury. And Allah is Self-Sufficient and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the superiority of moral and ethical conduct over mere ritualistic acts of charity. It emphasizes that the manner in which we engage with others—through kindness, patience, and forgiveness—holds greater value than actions that may appear charitable but are tainted by ulterior motives or subsequent harm. The mention of Allah's attributes as 'Self-Sufficient' and 'Forbearing' serves as a reminder that true virtue lies in aligning our actions with divine attributes, fostering a society built on compassion rather than transactional or superficial deeds.

translation: O you who have believed, do not invalidate your charities by reproach and injury, as one who spends his wealth to show off to the people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like a smooth rock on which is dust and it is hit by a downpour that leaves it bare. They are unable to get anything of what they have earned. And Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse warns against performing acts of charity with the intention of showing off to others or seeking praise, as such actions nullify the spiritual reward of the deed. True sincerity in worship and charity is essential, as hypocrisy and insincerity are condemned, and those who perform deeds for worldly recognition rather than for the sake of Allah will find their efforts devoid of lasting benefit.

translation: And the example of those who spend their wealth seeking the pleasure of Allah and as a firm resolve from themselves is like a garden on a high ground which is hit by a downpour, so it yields its fruit in double. And if it is not hit by a downpour, then a light rain. And Allah is All-Seer of what you do.
