interpretation: This verse highlights the sincerity and steadfastness of those who spend their wealth in the path of Allah. Their spending is not merely an act of charity but a reflection of their deep faith and trust in Allah's promise of reward. The parable of the garden illustrates that sincere and consistent acts of worship and charity, rooted in faith, will yield abundant spiritual and worldly blessings, regardless of external circumstances, as Allah is fully aware of and appreciates the intentions and efforts of the believers.

translation: Would one of you like to have a garden of palm trees and vines, under which rivers flow, with all kinds of fruits for him, and old age strikes him while he has weak offspring, then a fiery whirlwind strikes it and it burns? Thus does Allah make clear to you the signs, so that you may give thought.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound warning against the dangers of arrogance and ingratitude, illustrating how material blessings can become a source of ruin if one becomes heedless of their transient nature and fails to acknowledge their true Owner. It underscores the importance of humility, gratitude, and reliance on Allah, while highlighting the fragility of worldly attachments when detached from divine consciousness.

translation: O you who have believed, spend from the good things which you have earned and from what We have produced for you from the earth. And do not aim for the bad of it to spend from it, when you would not take it [yourself] except with closed eyes. And know that Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincerity and purity in acts of charity, urging believers to give only from what is lawful and good, not from what is inferior or acquired through questionable means.

translation: Satan threatens you with poverty and commands you to immorality, while Allah promises you forgiveness from Him and bounty. And Allah is All-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of human temptation and divine promise: Satan preys on human fears and weaknesses, exploiting them to lead people toward sin and despair, while Allah, in His boundless mercy and knowledge, offers forgiveness and abundant grace to those who seek repentance and righteousness.

translation: He grants wisdom to whom He pleases, and whoever is granted wisdom, indeed, he is given a great good. But none will remember except those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights that true wisdom is a divine gift, bestowed by Allah upon whom He wills, and it is the most valuable of all provisions. Those who receive it are granted immense good, not merely in worldly knowledge but in the ability to discern truth, make righteous choices, and attain spiritual enlightenment. The mention of 'those of understanding' (ulu al-albab) underscores that wisdom is not merely intellectual but requires a heart and mind attuned to divine guidance, reflecting a deep awareness of Allah’s signs and the purpose of existence.

translation: And whatever you spend of an expenditure or make of a vow - indeed, Allah knows of it. And for the wrongdoers there are no helpers.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's omniscience regarding human actions, emphasizing that nothing escapes His knowledge, whether it be charity or vows. It also serves as a warning to the wrongdoers, reminding them that they will find no allies or protectors on the Day of Judgment, as their actions have distanced them from divine mercy.

translation: If you disclose your charitable expenditures, they are good; but if you conceal them and give them to the poor, it is better for you. And He will remove from you some of your sins. And Allah, with what you do, is Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of sincerity in acts of charity, emphasizing that hidden charity is superior as it purifies the heart from the desire for praise and recognition, while also serving as an expiation for sins by aligning the giver’s intentions solely with the pleasure of Allah.

translation: It is not your responsibility to guide them, but Allah guides whom He wills. And whatever good you spend is for yourselves. And you do not spend except seeking the countenance of Allah. And whatever you spend of good will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the responsibility of guiding others ultimately lies with Allah, not the individual. It underscores the sincerity required in acts of charity and good deeds, which must be done solely for the sake of Allah, not for recognition or worldly gain. The assurance that such deeds will be fully rewarded without injustice highlights the divine justice and the importance of selfless devotion in worship and charity.

translation: For the poor who have been restricted [from travel] in the cause of Allah, unable to move about in the land - the unknowing might think them self-sufficient due to their restraint, but you will recognize them by their [marked] countenance. They do not ask people insistently [or at all]. And whatever you spend of good - indeed, Allah is Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of those who, despite their poverty and inability to earn due to their dedication to Allah’s cause, maintain dignity and restraint, avoiding begging or imposing on others. Their piety and self-sufficiency are evident in their demeanor, and Allah acknowledges their sacrifices, rewarding them for their hidden struggles and sincerity.

translation: Those who spend their wealth [in the cause of Allah] by night and by day, secretly and publicly - they will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sincerity and selflessness required in acts of charity, highlighting that true devotion to Allah is not bound by time, secrecy, or public display, but rather by the purity of intention. It reassures believers that Allah recognizes and rewards such deeds without conditions, granting them ultimate security and freedom from distress in the Hereafter.

translation: Those who consume interest will not stand [on the Day of Resurrection] except as one stands who is being beaten by Satan into insanity. That is because they say, "Trade is [just] like interest." But Allah has permitted trade and forbidden interest. So whoever has received an admonition from his Lord and desists may have what is past, and his affair rests with Allah. But whoever returns to [dealing in interest or usury]—those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide eternally therein.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe moral and spiritual consequences of engaging in riba (usury or interest), likening the state of those who persist in it to a state of spiritual derangement induced by Satan. It clarifies the distinction between halal trade, which is lawful and beneficial, and haram interest, which exploits and harms others. The verse also offers a path to redemption for those who repent, emphasizing accountability to Allah, while warning of eternal punishment for those who refuse to desist.

translation: Allah destroys interest and gives increase for charities. And Allah does not like any sinful disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine principle that worldly gains through unlawful means, such as interest (riba), are ultimately nullified by Allah, while righteous deeds like charity (sadaqah) are blessed and multiplied. It also underscores Allah's disapproval of those who persist in disbelief and sin, emphasizing the moral and spiritual consequences of such actions.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and establish prayer and give zakah will have their reward with their Lord, and there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse underscores the assurance of divine reward and eternal security for believers who embody faith through both belief and righteous action, including the fulfillment of religious obligations like prayer and charity. The absence of fear and grief signifies the ultimate tranquility and peace granted to such individuals in the Hereafter, reflecting the Qur'an's emphasis on a holistic relationship with Allah that integrates spiritual devotion with ethical conduct.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and give up what remains [due] of interest, if you should be believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete obedience to Allah's commands, even in financial matters, and underscores that true faith requires abandoning all forms of usury (riba), not just partially but fully, as a test of sincerity and submission to divine will.

translation: But if you do not, then know that you are at war with Allah and His Messenger. And if you repent, you may keep your principal—neither wronging nor being wronged.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of failing to fulfill financial obligations, equating such a default with open hostility against Allah and His Messenger. It serves as a stern warning to uphold contracts and debts, emphasizing that repentance is possible, and upon it, one retains their original capital without injustice, highlighting the balance of justice in Islamic financial ethics.

translation: And if someone is in hardship, then [grant him] respite until a time of ease. But if you give [from your wealth] in charity, it is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of compassion and financial flexibility towards those facing hardship, while also highlighting the spiritual and moral benefits of voluntary charity, encouraging believers to act with both generosity and wisdom.

translation: And fear a Day when you will be returned to Allah. Then every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine accountability, emphasizing that all actions—good or bad—will be justly recompensed by Allah without the slightest injustice, reinforcing the moral responsibility of individuals to live righteously in anticipation of that Day.

translation: O you who have believed, when you contract a debt for a specified term, write it down. And let a scribe write [it] between you in justice. Let no scribe refuse to write as Allah has taught him. So let him write and let the one who has the obligation dictate. And let him fear Allah, his Lord, and not leave anything out of it. But if the one who has the obligation is of limited understanding or weak or unable to dictate himself, then let his guardian dictate in justice. And bring to witness two witnesses from among your men. And if there are not two men [available], then a man and two women from those whom you accept as witnesses - so that if one of the women errs, then the other can remind her. And let not the witnesses refuse when they are called upon. And do not be [too] weary to write it, whether it is a large or small amount; its term specified. That is more just in the sight of Allah and stronger as evidence and more likely to prevent doubt between you, except when it is an immediate transaction which you conduct among yourselves. For [then] there is no blame upon you if you do not write it. And take witnesses when you conclude a contract. Let no harm be done to the scribe or witness. And if you do [that], then indeed, it is [grave] disobedience in you. And fear Allah. And Allah teaches you. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of justice, clarity, and mutual accountability in financial dealings, emphasizing that even in mundane transactions, ethical conduct and transparency are paramount to maintain trust and prevent disputes.

translation: And if you are on a journey and do not find a scribe, then a pledge taken by hand is sufficient. And if one of you entrusts the other, then let him who is entrusted discharge his trust and fear Allah, his Lord. And do not conceal testimony, for whoever conceals it, his heart is indeed sinful. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of trustworthiness and integrity in financial dealings, even in the absence of formal documentation. It highlights that while written agreements are ideal, oral pledges or handshakes can suffice in exigent circumstances, provided there is mutual trust. The verse also warns against concealing testimony, emphasizing that withholding truth out of greed or deceit corrupts the heart and incurs divine accountability.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. Whether you show what is within yourselves or conceal it, Allah will bring you to account for it. Then He will forgive whom He wills and punish whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and knowledge of Allah over all creation, including the hidden thoughts and intentions of human beings. It serves as a reminder of divine accountability, where no action or thought—whether manifest or concealed—escapes Allah's reckoning. The subsequent mention of forgiveness and punishment highlights Allah's mercy and justice, emphasizing that His decisions are based on His infinite wisdom and authority, not human limitations.

translation: The Messenger has believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord, and [so have] the believers. All of them have believed in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers, [saying], "We make no distinction between any of His messengers." And they say, "We hear and we obey. [We seek] Your forgiveness, our Lord, and to You is the [final] destination."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of faith among believers, affirming that true belief in Allah encompasses belief in all His messengers and scriptures without discrimination. It highlights the submission and obedience of the believers to Allah's commands, coupled with their recognition of their need for His forgiveness and the ultimate return to Him.

translation: Allah does not burden any soul beyond what it can bear. It will have [the reward for] what it has earned, and it will bear [the punishment for] what it has earned. Our Lord, do not impose blame on us if we forget or make a mistake. Our Lord, and burden us not as You burdened those before us. Our Lord, and lay not on us a burden for which we have no ability. And pardon us; and forgive us; and have mercy upon us. You are our protector, so grant us victory over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and mercy, emphasizing that Allah does not impose obligations beyond human capacity, while also highlighting the importance of seeking forgiveness for human shortcomings and relying on Allah's support in overcoming challenges.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as an invocation and reminder of Allah's boundless mercy, which encompasses all things before any specific act of mercy is sought. It establishes the context for the subsequent revelation, emphasizing that all guidance and knowledge come from the source of all mercy, setting a tone of compassion and divine benevolence.

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of [all] existence.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah, rejecting any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him. The attributes 'Ever-Living' (Al-Hayy) and 'Sustainer of existence' (Al-Qayyum) highlight His eternal nature and His role as the sole source of all sustenance and support for creation, underscoring His absolute independence and the dependence of all else upon Him.

translation: This Book has been sent down to you (O Muhammad) with the truth, confirming what was before it, and He sent down the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin and truthfulness of the Qur'an, affirming its role as a confirmation of earlier revelations (the Torah and the Gospel) while also establishing its own authority as the final and complete guidance for humanity.

translation: Before, as guidance for mankind; and He sent down the Criterion (of right and wrong). Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah will have a severe punishment, and Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine purpose behind the revelation of the Qur'an—as guidance for humanity and a criterion to distinguish truth from falsehood. The severe punishment mentioned for those who reject Allah's signs is not merely punitive but serves as a reminder of the gravity of rejecting divine guidance, emphasizing Allah's absolute justice and power to enforce consequences for disbelief.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not conceal anything from anything in the earth or in the heaven.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute knowledge and awareness of all things, whether hidden or apparent, in the heavens or on earth, underscoring His omniscience and the futility of attempting to conceal anything from Him.

translation: It is He who forms you in the wombs however He wills. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and wisdom of Allah in shaping human life from its earliest stages, highlighting His sovereignty over creation and the futility of seeking any other deity, as He alone possesses ultimate authority and wisdom.

translation: It is He who has sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book; in it are verses [that are] precise - they are the foundation of the Book - and others unspecific. As for those in whose hearts is deviation [from truth], they follow that of it which is unspecific, seeking discord and seeking an interpretation [suitable to them]. And no one knows its [true] interpretation except Allah. But those firm in knowledge say, "We believe in it. All [of it] is from our Lord." And no one will be reminded except those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of recognizing the distinction between clear (muḥkamāt) and ambiguous (mutashābihāt) verses in the Qur'an. It warns against those who exploit ambiguity to sow discord or misinterpret scripture to fit their desires, emphasizing that only Allah truly knows the full interpretation of such verses. Meanwhile, those grounded in knowledge accept all of the Qur'an as divine truth, trusting in Allah's wisdom, demonstrating humility and submission to the divine will.

translation: Our Lord, do not let our hearts deviate after You have guided us, and grant us mercy from Yourself. Indeed, You are the Bestower.
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound acknowledgment of human vulnerability and the need for divine guidance and mercy. It expresses a plea for steadfastness in faith, recognizing that guidance from Allah is a gift that must be preserved through His mercy. The supplicant acknowledges Allah's role as the ultimate Bestower (Al-Wahhab), emphasizing that true guidance and mercy come solely from Him, and that without His continuous grace, hearts can easily stray from the path of truth.

translation: Our Lord, indeed You will gather the people for a Day about which there is no doubt. Indeed, Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the absolute trustworthiness of Allah’s promises. It serves as a reminder of the inevitability of resurrection and accountability, urging believers to live righteously in anticipation of that Day, knowing that Allah’s justice and fulfillment of His word are unwavering.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved - never will their wealth or their children avail them against Allah at all. And it is they who will be fuel for the Fire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate futility of worldly possessions and lineage in securing divine protection or salvation for those who reject faith, emphasizing that true success lies in righteousness and submission to Allah alone.

translation: Like the way of the people of Pharaoh and those before them; they denied Our signs, so Allah seized them for their sins. And Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who persistently deny the truth despite clear signs, drawing a parallel with historical figures like the people of Pharaoh who faced divine punishment for their arrogance and rejection of divine guidance.

translation: Say to those who disbelieve, 'You will be overcome and gathered to Hell—and what an evil resting place!'
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance of those who reject faith, warning them of their ultimate defeat and the severe consequence of their disbelief, emphasizing the justice of divine retribution.

translation: There has already been for you a sign in the two armies that met [in combat]. One was fighting in the cause of Allah, and another was disbelieving. They saw the believers as twice their [own] number by [their] eyesight. But Allah supports with His victory whom He wills. Indeed in that is a lesson for those of vision.
interpretation: This verse underscores the power of divine intervention and the relativity of human perception. Despite the numerical disadvantage faced by the believers, Allah's support ensured their victory, demonstrating that true strength lies not in numbers or worldly means but in faith and divine favor. It serves as a reminder that outward appearances can be deceptive, and ultimate success is determined by Allah's will.

translation: Beautified for people is the love of that which they desire - of women and sons, heaped-up sums of gold and silver, fine branded horses, and cattle and well-tilled land. That is the enjoyment of worldly life, but Allah has with Him the best return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the allure of worldly attractions and the temporary nature of earthly pleasures, contrasting them with the superior and lasting rewards that Allah has prepared for the righteous in the Hereafter.

translation: Say, 'Shall I inform you of [something] better than that?' For those who fear Allah, there will be gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally, and purified spouses, and pleasure from Allah. And Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse underscores the superiority of spiritual and eternal rewards over worldly pleasures, emphasizing that true success lies in piety and devotion to Allah, which leads to everlasting bliss in Paradise.

translation: Who say, 'Our Lord, indeed we have believed, so forgive us our sins and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and sincerity of believers who acknowledge their sins and seek Allah's forgiveness and protection from punishment, demonstrating their reliance on divine mercy and justice.

translation: The patient, the truthful, the obedient, the spenders (in charity), and those who seek forgiveness before dawn.
interpretation: This verse highlights five distinct qualities of righteous believers: steadfastness in adversity, unwavering truthfulness, humble devotion, generosity in charity, and the habit of seeking forgiveness at the earliest hours of the night—a time of heightened spiritual awareness and humility before Allah.

translation: Allah bears witness that there is no deity except Him, and [so do] the angels and those of knowledge - [He is] maintaining [creation] in justice. There is no deity except Him, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and His sovereignty over all creation, with the testimony of Allah Himself, the angels, and those endowed with knowledge. The mention of 'maintaining [creation] in justice' highlights Allah's role as the sustainer who ensures balance and fairness in the universe, while 'the Exalted in Might, the Wise' emphasizes His unmatched power and perfect wisdom in governing all affairs.

translation: Indeed, the religion in the sight of Allah is Islam. And those who were given the Scripture did not differ except after knowledge had come to them - out of jealous animosity between themselves. And whoever disbelieves in the verses of Allah, then indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of divine truth, affirming that Islam—submission to Allah’s will—is the only acceptable path in His sight. It also highlights the historical reality of religious divergence among the People of the Book, which arose not from genuine pursuit of truth but from arrogance and rivalry. The warning against disbelief in Allah’s signs serves as a reminder of the swift and inevitable reckoning that awaits those who reject divine guidance.

translation: But if they argue with you, say, "I have submitted myself to Allah, and so have those who follow me." And say to the People of the Book and the unlettered, "Have you submitted yourselves?" If they submit, they are rightly guided; but if they turn away, your duty is only to convey the message. And Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of unwavering submission to Allah and the conveyance of divine guidance without coercion, emphasizing that true guidance is in Allah's hands alone.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah and kill the prophets without right and kill those who call for justice among the people - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of rejecting divine guidance, the sanctity of prophets, and the oppression of those who advocate for justice, warning of severe consequences for such transgressions.

translation: Those are the ones whose deeds have become worthless in this world and the Hereafter, and for them there will be no helpers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequence of actions that are devoid of sincerity, faith, or righteousness, emphasizing that such deeds are rendered futile both in this life and the Hereafter, with no one to advocate for or assist them.

translation: Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture, inviting [people] to the Book of Allah that it should judge between them? Then a party of them turned away, averting [themselves]?
interpretation: This verse critiques those who claim to follow divine guidance but selectively adhere to it only when it suits their interests, while turning away when it contradicts their desires or biases. It highlights the hypocrisy of invoking divine authority to justify their actions while ignoring its true purpose—justice and truth.

translation: That is because they said, "The Fire will not touch us except for [a few] numbered days," and [because] falsehood deceived them in their religion.
interpretation: This verse critiques those who falsely believe that their sins or disbelief will only result in temporary punishment, underestimating the severity of divine justice. It highlights the deception of their own making—justifying their actions through fabricated excuses—while ignoring the truth of accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: So how will it be when We gather them for a Day about which there is no doubt, and each soul will be fully compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged?
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the absolute justice of Allah, where every individual will be held accountable for their deeds without any injustice or favoritism.

translation: Say, 'O Allah, Owner of Sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty away from whom You will. You honor whom You will and You humble whom You will. In Your hand is [all] good. Indeed, You are over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and authority of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that sovereignty, honor, and disgrace are entirely in His hands. It serves as a reminder of human humility and dependence on Allah, rejecting any notion of self-sufficiency or entitlement to power or status.

translation: You cause the night to enter the day, and You cause the day to enter the night; You bring the living out of the dead, and You bring the dead out of the living. And You give provision to whom You will without account.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute power and control over all aspects of existence, demonstrating His ability to transform and sustain life in ways that transcend human comprehension, emphasizing His boundless mercy in providing for His creation without measure or restriction.

translation: The believers should not take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. And whoever does that has nothing to do with Allah, except when taking precautions against them in a manner that does not involve sin. And Allah warns you about Himself, and to Allah is the final destination.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of maintaining loyalty and alliance within the Muslim community, warning against forming close relationships with non-believers that could compromise Islamic values or lead to disloyalty to the faith. However, it allows for necessary caution in interactions with non-believers to protect oneself from harm, as long as it does not involve sin or betrayal of Islamic principles.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'If you conceal what is in your breasts or reveal it, Allah knows it. And He knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And Allah is over all things competent.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute knowledge of Allah, emphasizing that nothing—whether hidden in the heart or openly declared—escapes His awareness. It serves as a reminder of divine omniscience and the accountability of human actions, urging sincerity and mindfulness in both intention and deed.

translation: The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present [before it] and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between itself and that [evil] was a great distance. And Allah warns you of Himself, and Allah is Kind to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of facing one's deeds on the Day of Judgment, where no soul can escape the consequences of its actions. The intense regret expressed by the soul reflects the weight of accountability and the desire for even a momentary reprieve from punishment. The verse also highlights Allah's mercy, as He warns humanity out of compassion, reminding them of His ultimate authority and benevolence.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'If you should love Allah, then follow me, [so] Allah will love you and forgive you your sins. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true love for Allah is demonstrated through following the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his teachings. It assures that sincere adherence to his guidance will result in Allah's love and forgiveness of sins, highlighting the divine mercy and the importance of obedience to the Prophet as a means to attain Allah's pleasure.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "Obey Allah and the Messenger." But if they turn away - then indeed, Allah does not like the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute necessity of obedience to both Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him) as a fundamental aspect of faith, while also highlighting the consequence of rejecting this obedience—namely, that Allah does not guide or approve of those who persist in disbelief or defiance.

translation: Indeed, Allah chose Adam and Noah and the family of Abraham and the family of 'Imran over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's divine selection of certain prophets and their families for special favor and distinction, emphasizing their elevated spiritual status and the responsibility that comes with such distinction.

translation: A lineage deriving from one another; and Allah is Hearing, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the interconnectedness and continuity of human lineage, emphasizing that all people are part of a single, divinely ordained family tree. The attributes of Allah being 'Hearing' and 'Knowing' underscore His awareness of every individual's lineage, actions, and circumstances, reinforcing the idea of divine accountability and justice.

translation: Behold, the wife of ‘Imran said: ‘My Lord, I have pledged to You what is in my womb to be dedicated [to Your service]; accept it from me. Indeed, You are the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.’
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincerity and devotion of a believer in making a vow to Allah, trusting in His acceptance and knowledge of their intentions. It underscores the importance of dedicating one's life or resources to the service of Allah with complete faith in His wisdom and responsiveness.

translation: So when she delivered her, she said, "My Lord, I have delivered a female." And Allah is most knowing of what she delivered, "And the male is not like the female. And I have named her Mary, and I seek refuge for her and her descendants in You from the accursed Satan."
interpretation: This verse highlights the mother's initial surprise and submission to Allah's wisdom when she gave birth to a daughter instead of a son, acknowledging that Allah's knowledge surpasses human understanding. It also reflects the mother's deep faith and trust in Allah's plan, as she names her child Mary and seeks divine protection for her and her lineage from Satan's influence.

translation: So her Lord accepted her graciously and made her grow in a good manner and put her in the care of Zakariya. Every time Zakariya entered upon her in the prayer chamber, he found with her provision. He said, 'O Mary, from where is this [coming] to you?' She said, 'It is from Allah. Indeed, Allah provides for whom He wills without account.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor and miraculous provision bestowed upon Maryam (Mary), demonstrating Allah's power to grant sustenance without measure to whom He wills, as a sign of His mercy and a test of faith for those who witness it.

translation: There Zakariya prayed to his Lord, saying, "My Lord, grant me from Yourself a good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication."
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincerity and humility in Zakariya's (peace be upon him) supplication to Allah, demonstrating that even the most righteous individuals turn to Allah in times of need, acknowledging His power and responsiveness to prayers.

translation: So the angels called him while he was standing in prayer in the prayer chamber: 'Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, who will confirm a word from Allah, a leader, a chaste one, a prophet, and one of the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine selection and honor bestowed upon Yahya (John the Baptist), emphasizing his purity, leadership, and role as a prophet who would affirm the truth of Jesus (a 'word from Allah'). It underscores the idea that Allah elevates individuals for specific missions, even in seemingly impossible circumstances, as Yahya was born to an elderly, barren couple.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, how can I have a son when I have reached old age and my wife is barren?' [An angel] said, 'Thus Allah does what He wills.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the power of Allah to bring about the impossible, demonstrating that divine decree transcends human limitations and natural constraints, affirming absolute trust in Allah's will.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, make for me a sign.' He said, 'Your sign is that you will not speak to people for three days except by gesture. And remember your Lord much and exalt [Him] with praise in the evenings and the mornings.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine signs and the necessity of patience and remembrance in fulfilling them. It also underscores the virtue of constant remembrance of Allah and the significance of praising Him at all times, particularly during the transitions of the day, as a means of spiritual sustenance and connection with the Divine.

translation: And [remember] when the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed Allah has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the world.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and honor granted to Maryam (Mary) by Allah, emphasizing her spiritual purity and distinction among all women, which serves as a testament to the divine favor bestowed upon her.

translation: O Mary, be devoutly obedient to your Lord and prostrate, and bow with those who bow [in prayer].
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of complete submission and devotion to Allah, exemplified by Maryam (Mary), who is praised for her unwavering faith and humility in worship. It also emphasizes the communal aspect of worship, encouraging believers to join others in prayer and submission to Allah.

translation: This is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you. You were not with them when they cast their pens (to draw lots) as to which of them should be the guardian of Mary, nor were you with them when they were disputing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'anic narrative, emphasizing that the knowledge conveyed is beyond human experience and is revealed by Allah. It highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a recipient of revelation rather than a witness to these events, affirming the authenticity and miraculous nature of the Qur'an as a source of unseen knowledge.

translation: When the angels said, 'O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good tidings of a word from Him, whose name will be the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary—distinguished in this world and the Hereafter, and among those brought near [to Allah].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine selection and honor bestowed upon Jesus (peace be upon him) and his mother Mary (peace be upon her), emphasizing his elevated status in both this world and the Hereafter, as well as his closeness to Allah, which underscores the importance of their mission in the divine plan.

translation: And [Jesus] will speak to the people in the cradle and in maturity, and he will be among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights Jesus' (peace be upon him) unique status as a prophet who was granted miraculous speech from infancy, demonstrating divine favor and his role as a messenger of God, while also emphasizing his lifelong righteousness and unwavering devotion to truth.

translation: She said, 'My Lord, how can I have a child when no man has touched me?' He said, 'Thus [it will be]; Allah creates what He wills. When He decrees a matter, He only says to it, "Be," and it is.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power and will of Allah, demonstrating that divine creation transcends human norms and limitations, affirming that Allah’s command is sufficient to bring about what He decrees without the need for conventional means.

translation: And He teaches him the Book and wisdom, and the Torah and the Gospel.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine bestowal of knowledge and wisdom upon a chosen servant of God, equipping him with the sacred texts of the Torah and the Gospel, signifying the continuity and preservation of divine guidance across different eras and communities.

translation: And [I have been sent as] a messenger to the Children of Israel, [saying], 'Indeed, I have come to you with a sign from your Lord. I will create for you from clay the form of a bird, then I will breathe into it, and it will become a bird by the permission of Allah. And I will heal the blind and the leper, and I will bring the dead to life by the permission of Allah. And I will inform you of what you eat and what you store in your houses. Indeed, in that is a sign for you, if you are believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous signs granted to Jesus (peace be upon him) as evidence of his prophethood and the truthfulness of his message, demonstrating divine power over creation and life, which should inspire faith in those who witness or reflect upon them.

translation: And [I have come] confirming what was before me of the Torah and to make lawful for you some of what was forbidden to you. And I have come to you with a sign from your Lord, so fear Allah and obey me.
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophetic mission of Jesus (peace be upon him) to affirm the divine origin of the Torah given to Moses (peace be upon him) while also introducing new dispensations, such as lifting certain prohibitions for his followers. It underscores the continuity of divine guidance while emphasizing the need for reverence and submission to Allah’s commandments, as conveyed through His messengers.

translation: Indeed, Allah is my Lord and your Lord, so worship Him. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of God (Tawhid) and the obligation of worshipping Him alone, rejecting any form of association or deviation from the straight path of Islam.

translation: Then when Jesus felt [persistence in] disbelief from them, he said, 'Who are my supporters for [the cause of] Allah?' The disciples said, 'We are supporters of Allah; we have believed in Allah. And bear witness that we are Muslims [submitting to Him].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of truth when Jesus (peace be upon him) recognizes the disbelief of his people and seeks those who will stand with him in upholding the message of Allah. The response of the disciples (Hawariyyun) reflects their unwavering faith and commitment to Islam, affirming their submission to Allah and their readiness to support His cause, even in the face of opposition. It underscores the importance of steadfastness in faith and the role of sincere believers as allies in the path of divine truth.

translation: Our Lord, we have believed in what You have revealed and have followed the Messenger, so register us among the witnesses.
interpretation: This supplication reflects a profound act of submission and trust in divine revelation, acknowledging the truth of what has been sent down and the guidance of the Messenger, while seeking to be counted among those who bear witness to the truth in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And they planned, and Allah planned. And Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate sovereignty of Allah over all plans and schemes, no matter how intricate or deceptive they may be. It highlights that human machinations, no matter how cunning, are ultimately subject to Allah’s wisdom and power, and that divine retribution or justice will prevail in ways that transcend human understanding.

translation: When Allah said, 'O Jesus, indeed I will take you and raise you to Myself and purify you from those who disbelieve and make those who follow you [in submission to Allah] superior to those who disbelieved until the Day of Resurrection. Then to Me is your return, and I will judge between you concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's divine plan for Jesus (peace be upon him), affirming His protection and elevation of Jesus above the disbelief of his contemporaries, while also establishing a hierarchy of truth and guidance that persists until the Day of Judgment. It highlights the ultimate accountability before Allah, where all disputes and differences will be resolved by divine justice.

translation: As for those who disbelieved, I will punish them with a severe punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine retribution for those who reject faith, emphasizing that their punishment is not only deferred to the Hereafter but can also manifest in severe worldly consequences, while simultaneously affirming that no external force—whether human or otherwise—can avert this decree.

translation: But as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, He will give them in full their rewards, and Allah does not love the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine principle of justice and recompense, affirming that true faith must be accompanied by righteous actions, and that Allah’s justice is perfect—He rewards the righteous and does not tolerate oppression, even from those who claim to be believers.

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you, [O Muhammad], with truth. And indeed, you are from among the messengers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and absolute truth of the Qur'anic revelations being conveyed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), affirming his role as a messenger of Allah and the authenticity of the scripture.

translation: Indeed, the example of Jesus to Allah is like that of Adam. He created him from dust; then He said to him, "Be," and he was.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine power of creation, emphasizing that Jesus (peace be upon him) was created by Allah in a manner similar to Adam (peace be upon him), without a father, solely through the command 'Be,' demonstrating Allah's absolute authority over all existence.

translation: The truth is from your Lord, so do not be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an and the importance of accepting its guidance without hesitation. It cautions against doubt and encourages steadfast faith in the truth revealed by Allah.

translation: But whoever disputes with you concerning him (Jesus) after the knowledge that has come to you, say, 'Come, let us call our sons and your sons, our women and your women, ourselves and yourselves, then let us invoke Allah's curse upon the liars.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of falsehood and the importance of seeking divine truth through sincere and solemn means. It invites a mutual challenge to invoke divine judgment upon those who persist in falsehood, emphasizing that truth is not merely a matter of debate but a matter of divine verification.

translation: Indeed, this is the true narration. And there is no deity except Allah. And indeed, Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute truth of the Qur'anic narrative about previous prophets and their stories, affirming the oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and highlighting His supreme power and wisdom in both creation and command.

translation: But if they turn away, then indeed, Allah is Knowing of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's omniscience regarding those who persist in spreading corruption and injustice, even after being presented with the truth. It serves as a warning that no act of mischief or oppression goes unnoticed by Allah, and such individuals will face divine reckoning for their deeds.

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, come to a common word between us and you: that we will worship none but Allah, associate nothing with Him, and take not one another as lords besides Allah.' But if they turn away, then say, 'Bear witness that we are Muslims [submitting to Him].'
interpretation: This verse calls for unity and mutual understanding between Muslims and the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) based on shared monotheistic principles, rejecting any form of idolatry or false worship, and emphasizing absolute submission to Allah alone.

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you argue about Abraham while the Torah and the Gospel were not revealed until after him? Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse challenges the People of the Book to reflect on their disputes regarding Abraham (peace be upon him), emphasizing that their scriptures (Torah and Gospel) were revealed long after his time. It underscores the futility of arguing over figures from the past when the guidance meant to clarify their true status came much later, urging them to use reason and recognize the divine wisdom behind the timing of revelation.

translation: Here you are—you have argued about that of which you have knowledge, so why do you argue about that of which you have no knowledge? And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: This verse critiques the act of engaging in baseless disputes or arguments about matters beyond one's knowledge or understanding, emphasizing the importance of limiting discourse to what is known and verifiable. It underscores the humility required in intellectual or theological discussions, warning against overreach into domains where certainty is unattainable, and highlights the contrast between divine omniscience and human limitation.

translation: Abraham was neither a Jew nor a Christian, but he was a true monotheist (Hunafa) and a Muslim (submissive to Allah), and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse underscores the universal nature of monotheism (Tawheed) and submission to Allah, highlighting that true faith is not confined to any particular religious label or tradition. It emphasizes that the essence of Islam—submission to the One God—was the core of Abraham's faith, predating and transcending the later labels of Judaism and Christianity.

translation: Indeed, the most worthy of Ibrahim (Abraham) are those who followed him, and this Prophet (Muhammad), and those who believe. And Allah is the ally of the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual lineage and unity among the followers of Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), emphasizing that true closeness to Ibrahim (AS) is not merely by birth but by following his monotheistic path and the guidance brought by the final Prophet (PBUH). It also underscores Allah's role as the ultimate Protector and Supporter of the believers, reinforcing the concept of divine guardianship over those who submit to Him.

translation: A faction of the People of the Book wish they could mislead you, but they only mislead themselves and they do not perceive it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and self-destruction of those who attempt to lead others astray from the truth, as their deception ultimately harms only themselves without them realizing the spiritual and moral consequences of their actions.

translation: O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while you witness [to their truth]?
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who, despite acknowledging the divine origin of earlier scriptures and recognizing signs of truth in them, reject the final revelation of the Qur'an. It highlights their inconsistency in accepting divine guidance despite their witness to it, implying a willful rejection or hypocrisy in their stance.

translation: O People of the Book, why do you mix truth with falsehood and conceal the truth while you know [it]?
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) for their selective adherence to scriptural truths, accusing them of distorting divine revelations by blending them with falsehood or suppressing the truth they already recognize, likely referring to the prophecies of Muhammad (peace be upon him) in their scriptures.

translation: And a group of the People of the Book said, 'Believe in what has been revealed to the believers at the beginning of the day and reject it at the end, so that they may return [from their faith].'
interpretation: This verse critiques a deceptive tactic employed by some of the People of the Book (Jews or Christians) to undermine the faith of new Muslim converts by encouraging them to waver in their belief, hoping to lead them back to their original religion.

translation: And do not believe except in those who follow your religion.' Say, 'Indeed, the true guidance is Allah's guidance.' [Do you fear] that someone will be given [revelation] like what was given to you or that they will argue with you before your Lord? Say, 'Indeed, all bounty is in the hand of Allah; He grants it to whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the exclusivity of religious truth claimed by certain groups, emphasizing that true guidance belongs solely to Allah and is not monopolized by any particular community. It rejects the notion that salvation or divine favor is restricted to followers of a specific creed, affirming Allah's absolute sovereignty in granting guidance and blessings to whomever He wills, regardless of human claims or disputes.

translation: He selects for His mercy whom He wills. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty and wisdom in granting mercy, emphasizing that it is not based on human merit alone but on His divine will and boundless grace.

translation: And among the People of the Scripture is he who, if you entrust him with a great amount of wealth, will return it to you. And among them is he who, if you entrust him with a single silver coin, will not return it to you unless you keep standing over him. That is because they say, "There is no blame upon us concerning the unlettered ones." And they speak untruth about Allah while they know [it].
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and ethical inconsistency of some among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), who claim religious superiority while justifying dishonesty toward those they deem inferior (the 'unlettered ones'—likely referring to non-Arabs or non-literate people). Their hypocrisy is exposed by their selective adherence to trustworthiness based on personal gain, and their false assertions about divine permission for such behavior, revealing their deliberate deception despite their knowledge of the truth.

translation: Yes, whoever fulfills his covenant and fears Allah—indeed, Allah loves those who are mindful of Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling promises and maintaining piety as a means to earn Allah's love, highlighting that true faith is demonstrated through both actions and devotion.

translation: Indeed, those who exchange the covenant of Allah and their [own] oaths for a small price will have no share in the Hereafter, and Allah will not speak to them or look at them on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify them, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of betraying one's covenants and oaths made with Allah for worldly gain, emphasizing that such actions nullify one's spiritual standing and invite severe divine displeasure in the Hereafter.

translation: And indeed, there are some among them who distort the Scripture with their tongues, so that you may think it is from the Scripture, whereas it is not from the Scripture. And they say, "It is from Allah," whereas it is not from Allah. And they attribute lies to Allah knowingly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive tactics of certain individuals who manipulate religious texts to serve their own agendas, presenting falsehood as divine truth while fully aware of their deceit. It underscores the importance of discernment and sincerity in matters of faith, warning against those who distort scripture to mislead others.

translation: It is not for any human that Allah should give him the Book, authority, and prophethood and then he would say to the people, 'Be worshippers for me rather than Allah.' But rather, [he would say], 'Be devoted scholars to the Lord because of what you have taught of the Book and what you have studied.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of humility and servitude to Allah alone, rejecting any form of self-aggrandizement or false claims of divinity. It emphasizes that those granted divine knowledge and authority should use it to guide others toward true worship of Allah, not to elevate themselves above others or demand worship for themselves.

translation: And [remember] when Allah said, 'Indeed, I am with you. If you establish prayer and give zakah and believe in My messengers and support them and loan Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever of you disbelieves after that has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of sincerity in faith and worship, warning against hypocrisy or associating partners with Allah, even if it involves revering angels or prophets as divine figures, which would constitute disbelief (kufr). It highlights that true submission to Allah requires exclusive devotion and righteous deeds, not blind imitation or misplaced reverence.

translation: And [recall, O People of the Book,] when Allah took the covenant of the prophets, [saying], 'Whatever I give you of the Book and wisdom - then there comes to you a messenger confirming what is with you - you [must] believe in him and support him.' [Allah] said, 'Have you acknowledged and taken upon that My obligation?' They said, 'We have acknowledged.' He said, 'Then bear witness, and I am with you among the witnesses.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the unity of divine guidance across all prophets, emphasizing that their missions were interconnected and that the followers of earlier scriptures were obligated to believe in and support subsequent messengers, particularly the final Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The covenant highlights the continuity of revelation and the shared responsibility of all believers to uphold the truth, regardless of their era or scripture.

translation: But whoever turns away after that - they are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of turning away from divine guidance after having acknowledged it, emphasizing that such defiance constitutes a state of moral and spiritual corruption, severing one from the path of righteousness.

translation: Do they seek other than the religion of Allah while to Him have submitted [all] those within the heavens and earth, willingly or by compulsion? And to Him they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and universality of Allah's religion, emphasizing that all creation—whether in the heavens or the earth—submits to Him by necessity, regardless of their conscious choice. It refutes any alternative paths or beliefs, asserting that ultimate return and accountability are to Allah alone.

translation: Say, 'We have believed in Allah and what has been revealed to us and what was revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and the Descendants [of Jacob], and what was given to Moses and Jesus and the prophets from their Lord. We make no distinction between any of them, and we are Muslims [submitting] to Him.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of faith across all divine revelations, rejecting any form of discrimination among the prophets and their messages, affirming that true belief requires submission to Allah alone without division or distinction between His messengers.

translation: And whoever seeks a religion other than Islam, it will never be accepted from him, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the exclusivity of Islam as the true path to divine acceptance, emphasizing that no other religious system can substitute for it in the sight of God, and those who reject Islam in favor of other faiths will face ultimate loss in the Hereafter.

translation: How can Allah guide a people who disbelieved after their belief, and bore witness that the Messenger is true, and clear proofs came to them? And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the irreversibility of divine guidance once it is firmly rejected, emphasizing that Allah does not guide those who persist in injustice and defiance despite clear evidence and conviction in their hearts.

translation: For them is the recompense that upon them is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all the people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of divine punishment for those who persist in unbelief and wrongdoing, emphasizing that their condemnation is universal—from Allah, the angels, and humanity—reflecting the gravity of their transgressions and the finality of their fate.

translation: Abiding therein, the punishment will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse underscores the eternal and unrelenting nature of punishment for those who persist in disbelief or wrongdoing, emphasizing that there is no hope of mitigation or delay in their suffering.

translation: Except for those who repent after that and correct themselves, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless mercy of Allah, emphasizing that sincere repentance and righteous correction can restore one's relationship with Him, regardless of past sins.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved after their belief and then increased in disbelief—never will their repentance be accepted, and they are the ones astray.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of apostasy after faith, emphasizing that persistent rejection of truth, especially after clear guidance, leads to a state where repentance is no longer accepted, highlighting the irreversible consequences of such a choice.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and died while they were disbelievers—never would the equivalent of the earth's weight of gold be accepted from one of them if he [ever] offered it as ransom. For those there will be a painful punishment, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute finality of disbelief in the sight of Allah, emphasizing that no amount of wealth or effort can atone for a heart that remains closed to faith until death.

translation: You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love. And whatever you spend of anything, indeed Allah is Knowing of it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the essence of true sacrifice in charity, emphasizing that genuine righteousness is demonstrated not by what is easy to part with, but by giving up what one cherishes most, as a test of sincerity and devotion to Allah.

translation: All food was lawful for the Children of Israel except what Israel had made unlawful for itself before the Torah was revealed. Say, 'Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle that divine laws are not subject to personal whims or arbitrary restrictions, but must be based on revelation and divine command. It also challenges those who claim to follow scripture to demonstrate their adherence by presenting it, highlighting the importance of scriptural authority over human innovation in matters of faith.

translation: But whoever invents a lie about Allah after that - then those are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse warns against attributing falsehood to Allah, whether in speech, belief, or action, emphasizing that such behavior constitutes a grave injustice against Allah's divine nature and the truth He has revealed.

translation: Say, 'Allah has told the truth.' So follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth; and he was not of the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truthfulness of Allah's message and commands believers to adhere to the monotheistic faith of Prophet Abraham, who rejected idolatry and polytheism, serving as a model of pure devotion to Allah alone.

translation: Indeed, the first House [of worship] established for mankind was that at Makkah - blessed and a guidance for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the primacy and sacredness of the Ka'bah in Makkah as the first house of worship established for humanity, highlighting its divine blessing and role as a universal guide for all people, transcending temporal and cultural boundaries.

translation: In it are clear signs [such as] the standing place of Abraham. And whoever enters it shall be safe. And [due to] Allah upon mankind is the pilgrimage to the House - for whoever is able to find thereto a way. But whoever disbelieves - then indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sacredness of the Kaaba and its surroundings, where even the standing place of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) holds significance as a sign of divine guidance. The safety granted to those who enter this sacred precinct reflects the honor and protection bestowed by Allah upon this place. The obligation of Hajj for those who are physically and financially capable highlights the universality of Islam’s call to worship and submission, while the mention of disbelief serves as a reminder of Allah’s complete independence from His creation, emphasizing that true benefit or harm in faith is intrinsic to the individual’s choices.

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, why do you disbelieve in the verses of Allah while Allah is Witness over what you do?'
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who reject the truth of the Qur'an despite its clear signs and the evidence of its divine origin. It highlights their stubbornness in denying the truth while Allah, who is fully aware of their actions and intentions, bears witness to their disbelief.

translation: Say, 'O People of the Book, why do you avert [people] from the way of Allah, seeking [to make it] crooked, while you are witnesses [to its straightness]? And Allah is not unaware of what you do.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who, despite knowing the truth of Islam and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him), intentionally obstruct others from embracing the straight path of Allah. It highlights their hypocrisy in distorting the truth while being fully aware of its correctness, and warns them of Allah's awareness of their deceitful actions.

translation: O you who have believed, if you obey a party of those who were given the Scripture, they would turn you, after your belief, [back] to disbelief.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to believers against blindly following the misguided interpretations or deceptive influences of those who were given the Scripture (Jews and Christians), as their guidance may lead them away from the truth of Islam, undermining their faith.

translation: And how can you disbelieve while to you are being recited the verses of Allah and among you is His Messenger? And whoever holds firmly to Allah has [indeed] been guided to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse underscores the paradox of disbelief in the face of clear divine guidance and the presence of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) among the people. It emphasizes that true guidance comes from steadfast adherence to Allah, as those who cling to Him are led to the straight path—a metaphor for righteousness and salvation.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah as He should be feared and do not die except as Muslims [in submission to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere and complete devotion to Allah, urging believers to embody taqwa (God-consciousness) in their lives to the fullest extent, ensuring that their faith remains unwavering until their final moments.

translation: And hold firmly to the rope of Allah all together and do not become divided. And remember the favor of Allah upon you - when you were enemies and He brought your hearts together and you became, by His favor, brothers. And you were on the edge of a pit of the Fire, and He saved you from it. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity and brotherhood among Muslims, highlighting that true guidance and salvation come from adhering to Allah's guidance collectively rather than dividing into factions.

translation: And let there be [arising] from you a nation inviting to [all that is] good, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, and those will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the collective responsibility of the Muslim community to actively promote virtue, justice, and righteousness while preventing evil and oppression, highlighting that true success lies in fulfilling this communal duty.

translation: And do not be like those who became divided and differed after the clear proofs had come to them. And for those there is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against division and discord within the Muslim community after the guidance of the Qur'an and the Sunnah has been clearly established, emphasizing that such behavior leads to severe consequences.

translation: On the Day [some] faces will turn white and [some] faces will turn black. As for those whose faces turn black, [to them it will be said], 'Did you disbelieve after your belief? Then taste the punishment for what you used to reject.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the Day of Judgment as a moment of ultimate truth, where faith and disbelief are definitively revealed. The contrast between 'whitening' and 'blackening' of faces symbolizes divine approval or condemnation, reflecting the purity of righteous deeds versus the corruption of disbelief. The rhetorical question 'Did you disbelieve after your belief?' serves as a reproach, emphasizing that apostasy is a grave betrayal of divine trust, and the punishment is a direct consequence of one's conscious rejection of faith after having acknowledged it.

translation: But as for those whose faces turn white, they will be in the mercy of Allah, wherein they will abide forever.
interpretation: This verse highlights the eternal reward for the righteous believers who have lived a life of faith and righteousness, emphasizing that their ultimate reward is the everlasting mercy and pleasure of Allah, free from any end or cessation.

translation: These are the verses of Allah, which We recite to you in truth; and Allah wants no injustice to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'anic revelations are truthful and just, and that Allah's justice extends to all creation, ensuring that no wrongdoing or oppression will go unaddressed in the divine scheme.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And to Allah are [all] matters returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that nothing in the heavens or the earth exists independently of Him. The second part highlights that all affairs, whether in this world or the Hereafter, ultimately return to Allah for judgment and resolution, affirming His ultimate authority and the inevitability of divine accountability.

translation: You are the best nation produced [as an example] for mankind. You enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong and believe in Allah. If only the People of the Book had believed, it would have been better for them. Among them are believers, but most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the elevated status of the Muslim community as a model for humanity, emphasizing their role in promoting moral and ethical conduct through enjoining good and forbidding evil. It also underscores the responsibility of Muslims to uphold these principles, while acknowledging that even within communities of faith, there are varying levels of commitment, as seen in the People of the Book.

translation: They will not harm you except for a little annoyance. And if they fight you, they will turn their backs [in flight], then they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that the harm inflicted by enemies will be minimal and temporary, and that true victory belongs to Allah, as the disbelievers will ultimately fail in their efforts against the righteous.

translation: Humiliation was stamped upon them wherever they were seized, except by a bond from Allah and a bond from the people, and they incurred wrath from Allah. And humiliation was stamped upon them. That was because they disbelieved in the signs of Allah and killed the prophets without right. That was because they disobeyed and were transgressing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and committing oppression, particularly the killing of prophets. It underscores that true security and dignity come only through adherence to Allah’s commands and righteous alliances, while defiance leads to divine wrath and societal degradation.

translation: Not all of them are alike. Of the People of the Book is a community standing [in obedience], reciting the verses of Allah during periods of the night and prostrating [in prayer].
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between individuals within the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), emphasizing that not all are equal in their devotion and righteousness. It specifically praises those among them who remain steadfast in their faith, consistently reciting Allah’s revelations and engaging in acts of worship, such as prayer, demonstrating their sincere commitment to divine guidance.

translation: They believe in Allah and the Last Day, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong, and hasten to good deeds. And those are among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the core qualities of a true believer: unwavering faith in Allah and the Hereafter, active engagement in promoting virtue and preventing vice, and a proactive pursuit of righteous deeds, positioning them as exemplars of moral and spiritual excellence.

translation: And whatever good they do, it will not be denied them. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that Allah does not overlook or reject any sincere good deed, no matter how small, and that He is fully aware of those who strive to live righteously, ensuring their deeds will be rewarded in full.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved - never will their wealth or their children avail them against Allah at all. And it is they who will be companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate futility of worldly attachments—wealth and progeny—when it comes to averting divine judgment for those who reject faith. It serves as a stark reminder that no material or familial privilege can shield one from accountability before Allah, emphasizing the transient nature of this life's pursuits compared to the eternal consequences of one's beliefs and deeds.

translation: The example of what they spend in this worldly life is like a wind containing scorching frost which strikes the harvest of a people who wronged themselves, thus destroying it. And Allah wronged them not, but they wronged themselves.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of expending wealth or effort in ways that contradict divine guidance or ethical principles, as such actions ultimately lead to self-inflicted harm rather than benefit, despite initial appearances of worldly gain.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take as intimates [i.e., advisors or close associates] anyone other than yourselves, for they will not spare any effort to corrupt you. They wish you hardship. Hatred has already appeared from their mouths, and what their breasts conceal is greater. We have certainly made clear to you the signs, if you will use reason.
interpretation: This verse warns believers against forming close alliances with those who are not genuinely trustworthy or aligned with their faith and values, as such associations can lead to spiritual and moral corruption, even if the harm is not immediately apparent.

translation: Behold, you love them but they do not love you, and you believe in the entire Book. When they meet you, they say, "We believe," but when they are alone, they bite their fingertips in rage against you. Say, "Perish in your rage! Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of what the breasts conceal."
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy of those who outwardly profess faith but harbor deep resentment and enmity in their hearts, particularly towards the believers. It highlights the contrast between the sincerity of true believers and the duplicity of hypocrites, who pretend to accept the truth while concealing their true feelings of hatred and rejection.

translation: If good befalls you, it grieves them; but if evil befalls you, they rejoice at it. Yet if you are patient and guard against evil, their scheming will not harm you in the least. Indeed, Allah encompasses what they do.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that divine protection is absolute, and the harm or scheming of enemies, no matter how malicious, cannot prevail against those who remain steadfast in faith and righteousness. It underscores the futility of opposition to God’s will and the ultimate accountability of all actions in His knowledge.

translation: And [remember] when you set out from your home in the morning to assign battle positions for the believers. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of strategic preparation and divine oversight in the pursuit of noble goals, emphasizing that human efforts are complemented by Allah's knowledge and awareness of all actions.

translation: When two groups from among you were about to lose heart, but Allah was their Protector. And in Allah let the believers put their trust.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of relying on Allah in moments of weakness or doubt, reminding believers that divine support is ever-present even when human resolve falters.

translation: And Allah had certainly helped you at Badr while you were weak (or few). So fear Allah that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of victory, reminding believers that success comes from Allah alone, not from their own strength or numbers, and thus they should maintain humility and gratitude.

translation: When you said to the believers, 'Is it not sufficient for you that your Lord should reinforce you with three thousand angels sent down?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust in divine support and reassurance in times of hardship, emphasizing that even when facing overwhelming odds, faith in Allah's aid can be a source of strength and confidence for believers.

translation: Yes! If you remain patient and conscious of Allah, and the enemy comes upon you [attacking] in this [battle], Allah will reinforce you with five thousand marked angels.
