interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of steadfastness (patience and piety) in the face of adversity, assuring divine support and victory to those who uphold these virtues, even in overwhelming circumstances.

translation: And Allah did not assign it (the Qur'an) except as good tidings for you and to reassure your hearts with it. And victory is not except from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine purpose behind the revelation of the Qur'an: it serves as a source of hope and tranquility for believers, while also reminding them that ultimate success and victory come solely from Allah, whose wisdom and power are beyond human comprehension.

translation: To strike terror into the hearts of the disbelievers, or to humiliate them, so that they retreat in frustration.
interpretation: This verse highlights the use of decisive action against those who persistently reject faith and oppose Islam, aiming to either deter them through force or strip them of their arrogance, leading to their ultimate failure and despair.

translation: You have no authority over the matter, whether He turns to them in mercy or punishes them, for they are wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over judgment and mercy, emphasizing that human beings cannot dictate divine outcomes. It highlights the consequences of wrongdoing (ظلم) while affirming Allah’s prerogative to forgive or punish as He wills, reminding humans of their limited role in divine affairs.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills, and Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty over all creation, emphasizing His unrestricted authority to forgive or punish as He deems fit, while also highlighting His inherent attributes of forgiveness and mercy, which are extended to whom He wills.

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume usury, doubled and multiplied, and fear Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the moral and spiritual corruption of usury (riba), emphasizing that its practice—especially in exploitative forms—is forbidden in Islam, as it leads to injustice and societal harm. The warning to 'fear Allah' serves as a reminder that true success lies in adherence to divine commandments, which prioritize fairness, compassion, and the well-being of the community over personal greed.

translation: And fear the Fire, which has been prepared for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the severe consequences awaiting those who reject faith, emphasizing the importance of righteousness and devotion to God as a means of protection from such punishment.

translation: And obey Allah and the Messenger so that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him) as a means to attain Allah's mercy and blessings, highlighting the connection between righteous action and divine favor.

translation: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a Paradise whose width is [like that of] the heavens and earth, prepared for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency of seeking spiritual purification and divine mercy, while also highlighting the vastness and exclusivity of Paradise for those who embody piety and God-consciousness.

translation: Who spend [in the cause of Allah] during ease and hardship and who restrain anger and who pardon the people - and Allah loves the doers of good;
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtues of true believers who demonstrate unwavering generosity, self-control, and forgiveness regardless of their circumstances, reflecting a profound level of moral excellence that earns divine love.

translation: And [also for] those who, when they commit an immoral act or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins—and who can forgive sins except Allah?—and [who] do not persist in what they have done while they know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the nature of true repentance, emphasizing that a believer, upon committing a sin, should immediately turn to Allah in remembrance, seek forgiveness, and resolve not to repeat the sin, fully aware of its wrongfulness. It underscores the exclusivity of Allah's capacity to forgive sins and the importance of sincere repentance without delay or persistence in error.

translation: For them is forgiveness from their Lord and gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally; and excellent is the reward of the [righteous] workers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for those who strive in righteousness and good deeds, emphasizing that their recompense is not merely material but includes divine forgiveness and eternal bliss in Paradise, underscoring the profound value of sincere devotion and righteous action.

translation: Sunnahs (ways) have indeed passed before you, so travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those who denied (the messengers).
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on historical consequences to reinforce the importance of heeding divine guidance, implying that rejecting truth leads to inevitable destruction, while obedience brings lasting success.

translation: This is a clear statement for mankind, and a guidance and an admonition for those who fear Allah.
interpretation: The verse underscores the universal accessibility of the Qur'an's message, emphasizing that it serves as a clear proof and guidance for all people, while its deeper spiritual benefits—such as divine guidance and moral admonition—are specifically reserved for those who are conscious of Allah and strive to live by His commandments.

translation: So do not weaken or grieve, for you will be superior if you are [true] believers.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers facing hardship that their faith grants them ultimate strength and victory, urging them not to falter in resolve or succumb to despair, as divine support ensures their superiority in the long term.

translation: If a wound touches you, a wound like it has touched the people. And these days [of varying fortunes] We alternate among the people, that Allah may make evident those who believe and take from among you martyrs - and Allah does not like the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of worldly trials and the importance of steadfastness in faith. It reassures believers that hardships are part of a cyclical pattern experienced by all people, serving as a test to distinguish true faith from hypocrisy. The mention of martyrs highlights the ultimate sacrifice for belief, while the condemnation of wrongdoers emphasizes divine justice, reminding that oppression and injustice will not go unpunished.

translation: Allah will refine the believers and will destroy the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual outcome for believers and disbelievers in the sight of Allah: purification and reward for the faithful, and annihilation or ruin for those who reject faith, reflecting divine justice and the consequences of one's choices.

translation: Do you think that you will enter Paradise while Allah has not yet made evident those who strive among you [for His cause] and [has not made evident] the patient?
interpretation: This verse underscores the necessity of genuine faith and righteous action as prerequisites for attaining Paradise, emphasizing that Allah alone knows the true extent of one's struggle and perseverance in His path.

translation: And you had certainly wished for death before encountering it, so you have [now] seen it while you are looking on.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who, during the lifetime of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), expressed a desire for death due to their fear of confrontation with the truth and the hardships of jihad. The verse exposes their hypocrisy by reminding them that they now witness the consequences of their cowardice and false wishes, as they see the reality of death and its inevitability, yet they are powerless to escape it.

translation: And Muhammad is not but a messenger. [Other] messengers have passed on before him. So if he was to die or be killed, would you turn back on your heels [to unbelief]? And whoever turns back on his heels will never harm Allah at all; but Allah will reward the grateful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of all messengers, including the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, and cautions against abandoning faith or reverting to disbelief upon their passing, emphasizing that true faith is rooted in conviction, not in attachment to individuals.

translation: And no soul dies except by permission of Allah at a decree determined. And whoever desires the reward of this world - We will give him from it; and whoever desires the reward of the Hereafter - We will give him from it. And We will reward the grateful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over life and death, emphasizing that all outcomes are preordained by divine decree. It also highlights the principle of divine justice and reciprocity, where individuals are rewarded according to their intentions and desires—whether they seek worldly gains or the eternal rewards of the Hereafter—while those who express gratitude for Allah’s blessings will receive their due recompense.

translation: And how many a prophet [fought and] with him fought many Godly men. But they never lost heart due to what afflicted them in the cause of Allah, nor did they weaken or yield. And Allah loves the steadfast.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue of steadfastness and perseverance in the face of hardship, particularly in the path of faith and righteousness. It highlights that true believers, even when facing immense trials and tribulations, should remain resolute and unwavering, for such steadfastness is beloved to Allah.

translation: And their only statement was that they said, "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and our excessiveness in our affairs, and make firm our steps, and help us against the disbelieving people."
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and sincerity of believers in seeking Allah's forgiveness and steadfastness in their faith, demonstrating that true success lies in repentance, reliance on divine guidance, and perseverance against adversity.

translation: So Allah gave them the reward of this world and the excellent reward of the Hereafter. And Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine principle that righteousness and good deeds are not only rewarded in the Hereafter but can also manifest tangible blessings in this world, reflecting Allah’s justice and mercy. The emphasis on Allah’s love for the 'doers of good' underscores that true success lies in consistent ethical conduct, as it aligns with divine values and attracts both worldly and eternal rewards.

translation: O you who have believed, if you obey those who disbelieve, they will turn you back on your heels, and you will become losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to believers against following the guidance or influence of those who reject faith, as doing so would lead them away from the path of truth and cause them to incur loss in both worldly and spiritual matters.

translation: But Allah is your protector, and He is the best of helpers.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that no matter the challenges they face, their ultimate support and protection come from Allah alone, who is far superior to any worldly ally or helper.

translation: We will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieve for what they have associated with Allah of which He authorized no warrant, and their refuge will be the Fire. And wretched is the residence of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of associating partners with Allah (shirk), emphasizing that such disbelief incurs divine displeasure and leads to eternal punishment in Hellfire, highlighting the gravity of shirk as an unforgivable sin unless repented from before death.

translation: And Allah had certainly fulfilled His promise to you when you were killing the enemy by His permission, until [after] you lost courage and fell to disputing about the order [given by the Prophet] and disobeyed after He had shown you that which you love. Among you are some who desire this world, and among you are some who desire the Hereafter. Then He turned you back from them that He might test you; and He has certainly forgiven you. And Allah is the possessor of bounty for the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the test of faith and sincerity in believers, where Allah allows a situation to unfold that reveals the true intentions of people—whether they prioritize worldly gains or the Hereafter. The turning away of victory and the subsequent forgiveness underscore Allah’s mercy, but also serve as a reminder that trials are meant to purify and strengthen faith.

translation: When you were ascending [the hill] and not even turning to look back at anyone, while the Messenger was calling you from behind you, so He punished you with distress upon distress so that you would not grieve for what you missed or what afflicted you. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of steadfastness and trust in Allah's plan during trials, even when it seems contrary to immediate desires or expectations. It underscores that hardships are not random but purposeful, designed to refine believers and prevent deeper spiritual or emotional harm.

translation: Then after distress, He sent down upon you security of sleep, overcoming a group of you, while another group worried about themselves, thinking about Allah other than the truth—the assumption of ignorance. They say, "Is there anything for us in the matter?" Say, "Indeed, the matter is entirely for Allah." They conceal within themselves what they do not reveal to you. They say, "If there had been anything for us in the matter, we would not have been killed here." Say, "Even if you had been in your homes, those for whom killing was decreed would have come out to their death beds. And Allah will test what is in your breasts and purify what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to attribute events to causes other than divine will, reflecting a lack of trust in Allah's wisdom. It also underscores the concept of predestination (Qadr), emphasizing that everything happens by Allah's decree, and human efforts or desires alone do not alter fate. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of sincere faith and reliance on Allah, even in the face of adversity.

translation: Indeed, those of you who turned their backs on the day the two armies met—it was Satan who caused them to slip because of some of their misdeeds. But Allah has pardoned them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of human fallibility and divine mercy, illustrating that while individuals may falter due to their own shortcomings or the influence of Satan, Allah’s forgiveness and forbearance are ever-present for those who repent and seek redemption.

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who disbelieved and said about their brothers when they traveled through the land or were fighting, 'If they had been with us, they would not have died or been killed,' so Allah makes that regretful for them. And Allah gives life and causes death, and Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse cautions against harboring false assumptions about divine decree and the outcomes of events, particularly in matters of life, death, or worldly struggles. It warns against the hypocritical mindset of claiming to have superior faith or judgment while failing to recognize that Allah alone controls life and death, and that worldly outcomes are not a measure of righteousness or favor. The verse also subtly reminds believers that their actions are under divine scrutiny, reinforcing accountability and trust in Allah's wisdom.

translation: And if you are killed in the cause of Allah or die, surely forgiveness and mercy from Allah are better than what they accumulate [of worldly wealth].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the superiority of divine reward—namely forgiveness and mercy—over worldly gains, even in the face of death or martyrdom in the path of Allah.

translation: And if you should die or be killed, to Allah you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of death and the ultimate return of all souls to Allah, emphasizing divine accountability and the transient nature of worldly life.

translation: It was by the mercy of Allah that you (O Prophet) were lenient with them—and had you been harsh or hard-hearted, they would have certainly abandoned you. So pardon them, ask Allah’s forgiveness for them, and consult them in the matter. Once you have made a decision, put your trust in Allah. Indeed, Allah loves those who trust in Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) exemplary character, emphasizing that his gentleness and mercy were divinely ordained instruments for uniting and guiding people. It underscores the importance of compassion, humility, and consultation in leadership, while also teaching that after making a decision with wisdom and consultation, one must place trust in Allah’s decree, recognizing that ultimate success depends on divine support rather than human effort alone.

translation: If Allah should aid you, no one can overcome you; but if He should forsake you, who is there that can aid you after Him? And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute dependence of the believers on Allah's support and the futility of relying on anything or anyone else. It serves as a reminder that ultimate victory and success come solely from Allah, and that true faith is demonstrated by trusting in Him alone, especially in times of hardship or apparent defeat.

translation: And it is not [attributable] to any prophet that he would act dishonestly [in war]. And whoever betrays his trust will come with what he took on the Day of Resurrection. Then every soul will be compensated for what it earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute necessity of integrity and trustworthiness in all dealings, especially for those in positions of leadership or prophethood, as their actions serve as a model for others. It warns against betrayal or dishonesty, emphasizing that such actions will be exposed and accounted for on the Day of Judgment, where justice will prevail without any injustice or favoritism.

translation: So is one who pursues the pleasure of Allah like one who comes with the wrath of Allah and whose refuge is Hell? And it is an evil destination.
interpretation: This verse underscores the stark contrast between those who strive to earn Allah's pleasure through righteous deeds and those who incur His wrath through disobedience and sin. It serves as a moral warning, emphasizing that the path of faith and obedience leads to divine acceptance and eternal bliss, while the path of rebellion and transgression leads to divine punishment and eternal damnation.

translation: They are [of] varying degrees [of high position] in the sight of Allah. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine justice and wisdom in assigning different ranks or stations to individuals based on their deeds, intentions, and spiritual status in the sight of Allah, emphasizing that Allah is fully aware of all actions and will reward accordingly.

translation: Allah has certainly conferred favor upon the believers by sending among them a Messenger from themselves, reciting to them His verses, purifying them, and teaching them the Book and wisdom, although they had been before in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound mercy of Allah in sending a prophet from the same community he is sent to, ensuring that the message is not only conveyed but also internalized through purification of the heart and teaching of divine wisdom, contrasting their prior state of ignorance and misguidance.

translation: And when disaster strikes you, [O believers], although you have struck [the enemy] with a similar [disaster], you say, 'How is this?' Say, 'It is from yourselves.' Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse addresses the human tendency to question divine wisdom when adversity strikes, even after having experienced similar trials or victories, suggesting that such questioning often stems from a lack of trust in Allah's wisdom and decree, rather than from the event itself.

translation: And [remember] when you were struck with grief on the day the two armies met, it was by Allah's permission, and so that He may make evident the believers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine decree (qadr) in human affairs, affirming that events—even those causing hardship—occur by Allah's will, while simultaneously highlighting the moral purpose behind trials: to distinguish true faith and steadfastness in believers from others.

translation: And [it was said to them]: "Come, fight in the way of Allah, or at least defend yourselves." They said, "If we knew how to fight, we would certainly have followed you." They were closer to disbelief that day than to faith, saying with their mouths what was not in their hearts. And Allah knows best what they conceal.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who outwardly claim faith but lack sincerity in their hearts, as their true allegiance lies with disbelief rather than submission to Allah.

translation: Those who stayed behind said about their brothers, 'If they had obeyed us, they would not have been killed.' Say, 'Then avert death from yourselves, if you are truthful.'
interpretation: This verse addresses hypocrisy and the false sense of security people may derive from the actions or inactions of others. It highlights the individual responsibility of each person before Allah, emphasizing that no one can escape accountability by blaming others or relying on their obedience. True faith requires personal conviction and action, not mere association or passive agreement.

translation: And never think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, well provided for,
interpretation: This verse underscores the spiritual and metaphysical reality of martyrdom in Islam, emphasizing that death in the path of Allah is not an end but a transition to a higher state of existence where the martyrs remain spiritually alive and sustained by divine grace.

translation: Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty, and they rejoice in (the success of) those who have not yet joined them, who have not yet caught up with them. No fear will there be concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound sense of contentment and spiritual security granted to the believers in Paradise. Their joy is not only in their own blessings but also in the success of those who come after them, reflecting a selfless and expansive happiness. The absence of fear and grief signifies the ultimate peace and security that comes from divine favor and the assurance of salvation.

translation: They rejoice in the favor and bounty of Allah, and [in their assurance] that Allah does not waste the reward of the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and emotional state of believers who find joy not only in their faith but also in the tangible blessings and divine grace bestowed upon them by Allah. It underscores the certainty of divine justice, assuring believers that their efforts and sacrifices in the path of faith will not go unnoticed or unrewarded, reinforcing trust in Allah's promise of ultimate justice and recompense.

translation: Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after the injury had afflicted them—for those among them who did good and feared Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of steadfastness and righteousness in the face of hardship, emphasizing that true success lies in responding to divine guidance and maintaining piety, even when trials strike.

translation: Those to whom the people said, 'Indeed, the people have gathered against you, so fear them.' But it [only] increased them in faith, and they said, 'Sufficient for us is Allah, and [He is] the best Disposer of affairs.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith of believers in the face of overwhelming external threats. Despite being warned of impending danger, their trust in Allah's protection and decree ('hasbunAllah wa ni'mal wakeel') strengthens their resolve rather than diminishing it, demonstrating that true faith is fortified by trials and reliance on divine power.

translation: So they returned with a favor from Allah and bounty, no harm having touched them. And they pursued the pleasure of Allah. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for those who remain steadfast in faith and righteousness, even in the face of hardship. It emphasizes that their perseverance is met with divine favor and protection, ensuring they are unharmed, and their ultimate success lies in attaining Allah's pleasure, underscoring the boundless generosity and mercy of Allah.

translation: That is only Satan frightening his allies, so do not fear them, but fear Me if you are [true] believers.
interpretation: This verse cautions against giving in to fear instigated by Satan or his allies, emphasizing that true faith requires placing trust in Allah alone rather than being intimidated by external threats.

translation: And do not be grieved by those who hasten into disbelief. Indeed, they will not harm Allah at all. Allah intends that He will not grant them any share in the Hereafter, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and believers that the actions of those who rush into disbelief do not diminish Allah's power or glory, as their harm is ultimately inconsequential to Allah. It also underscores Allah's justice in withholding a share of the Hereafter from the disbelievers, emphasizing that their punishment is a reflection of divine justice rather than a personal vengeance.

translation: Indeed, those who exchange faith for disbelief will not harm Allah at all, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of those who abandon their faith for disbelief, as their actions do not harm Allah in any way, but rather bring severe consequences upon themselves.

translation: And those who disbelieve should not think that Our granting them respite is good for themselves. We only grant them respite so that they may increase in sin, and for them is a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse cautions against the false assumption that worldly prosperity granted to disbelievers is a sign of divine favor or success, when in reality it is a test that may lead them deeper into wrongdoing, ultimately resulting in severe and disgraceful punishment.

translation: Allah will not leave the believers in the state you are in [still having faith] until He separates the wicked from the pure. Nor will Allah reveal to you the unseen, but Allah chooses of His messengers whom He wills. So believe in Allah and His messengers. And if you believe and fear Allah, then for you is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse underscores the necessity of divine trial and distinction in the life of believers, where faith is tested to separate the sincere from the insincere, and the righteous from the wicked. It also emphasizes that knowledge of the unseen is solely in Allah’s hands, and He grants it to whom He wills among His messengers. The call to faith and piety is framed as a path to immense reward, highlighting the importance of trust in Allah’s wisdom and justice.

translation: And let not those who withhold what Allah has given them of His bounty ever think that it is [in any way] better for them. Rather, it is worse for them. What they withhold will be tied to their necks on the Day of Resurrection. And to Allah belongs the heritage of the heavens and the earth. And Allah, with what you do, is Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse warns against stinginess and hoarding wealth, emphasizing that withholding what Allah has blessed a person with does not benefit them in the Hereafter—instead, it will be a burden around their neck on the Day of Judgment, while all wealth ultimately belongs to Allah, who is fully aware of all deeds.

translation: Allah has certainly heard the statement of those who said, "Indeed, Allah is poor, while we are rich." We will record what they said and their killing of the prophets without right and will say, "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire."
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance and ingratitude of those who deny Allah's absolute richness and self-sufficiency, attributing poverty to Him while boasting of their own wealth. It underscores the severe consequences of their disbelief and oppression, particularly the unjust killing of prophets, as a definitive rejection of divine guidance. The punishment mentioned reflects the gravity of their transgressions, serving as a reminder of Allah's justice and the futility of defying His commands.

translation: This is because of what your hands have earned. And indeed, Allah is not unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of personal accountability in Islam, where individuals are held responsible for their own actions and choices. It serves as a reminder that divine justice is absolute and impartial, ensuring that no one is wronged, even in the slightest, by Allah’s decree.

translation: Those who said, "Indeed, Allah has taken our promise not to believe in a messenger unless he brings us an offering consumed by fire." Say, [O Muhammad], "There certainly came to you messengers before me with clear proofs and [even] what you asked for. So why did you kill them if you are truthful?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the hypocrisy of those who demand impossible proofs from prophets while ignoring the clear signs already presented to them, exposing their insincerity and refusal to accept truth even when confronted with it.

translation: But if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already have denied messengers before you who brought clear proofs, scriptures, and the illuminating Scripture.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that rejection of his message does not invalidate its truth; rather, it is a recurring pattern in divine communication, where earlier messengers faced similar denial despite presenting undeniable evidence and guidance.

translation: Every soul will taste death. And you will only be given your [full] compensation on the Day of Resurrection. So he who is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has attained [his desire]. And what is the life of this world except the enjoyment of delusion.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of death and the transient nature of worldly life, urging reflection on the ultimate reality beyond this life. It emphasizes that true success lies in salvation from Hell and entry into Paradise, which is achieved through righteous deeds and divine mercy, not through the fleeting pleasures of this world.

translation: You will surely be tested in your wealth and in yourselves, and you will surely hear from those who were given the Scripture before you and from those who associate others with Allah much abuse. But if you are patient and fear Allah, indeed, that is of the matters [worthy] of determination.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of trials in life, both in material wealth and personal hardships, as well as the likelihood of encountering hostility from those outside the faith—whether from the People of the Book or polytheists. The emphasis on patience (*sabr*) and piety (*taqwa*) as the path to overcoming these challenges highlights the importance of steadfastness in faith and reliance on divine guidance, rather than reacting to provocation with anger or despair.

translation: And [recall] when Allah took a covenant from those who were given the Scripture, [saying], "You must render it [the Scripture] to the people in truth and not conceal it." But they threw it away behind their backs and exchanged it for a small price. And wretched is that which they purchased.
interpretation: This verse underscores the moral and religious obligation of those entrusted with divine scriptures to convey their teachings truthfully and without concealment, even if it incurs personal cost or discomfort. The condemnation of their actions—trading truth for a paltry gain—serves as a timeless critique of prioritizing worldly interests over spiritual and moral responsibilities, highlighting the gravity of betraying divine trust.

translation: Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have been given and love to be praised for what they did not do—do not think they will be saved from the punishment. And for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against hypocrisy and self-deception, emphasizing that outward displays of piety or achievement, without genuine righteousness or truth, will not shield one from divine accountability. The emphasis on 'what they did not do' highlights the danger of seeking validation for actions not truly performed, underscoring the importance of sincerity in faith and deeds.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that nothing in the heavens or the earth exists outside His control or authority. The mention of His competence ('*Qadir*') highlights that His power is not only encompassing but also effortless and unrestricted, reinforcing the idea that all events—whether in the heavens, the earth, or between them—are subject to His will and wisdom.

translation: Indeed, in the creation of the heavens and the earth and the alternation of the night and the day are signs for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the intricate design and order in the universe serve as profound evidence of the existence and oneness of Allah, inviting those with wisdom and insight to reflect deeply on these signs to recognize the truth.

translation: Those who remember Allah while standing, sitting, and lying on their sides, and who reflect on the creation of the heavens and the earth [saying], 'Our Lord, You did not create this in vain; exalted are You [above such a thing]; protect us from the punishment of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the multifaceted devotion of believers—engaging in remembrance (dhikr) of Allah in all states of life—and their deep reflection on the signs of Allah in creation, which leads them to acknowledge Allah’s perfection and seek His protection from the consequences of misguidance or neglect.

translation: Our Lord, indeed whoever You admit into the Fire, You have disgraced him, and the wrongdoers will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power and justice of Allah in determining the fate of individuals, emphasizing that admission into Hell is a form of disgrace for the wrongdoers, and that no one can intervene or help them escape Allah's judgment.

translation: Our Lord, indeed we have heard a caller calling to faith, [saying], 'Believe in your Lord,' and we have believed. Our Lord, so forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds and cause us to die with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound transformation that occurs when one responds to the call of faith with sincerity and conviction. It highlights the believer's acknowledgment of divine guidance, their repentance for past wrongs, and their ultimate desire to be among the righteous at the end of their life, underscoring the importance of seeking forgiveness and righteousness as a continuous journey.

translation: Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers and do not disgrace us on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, You never fail in [Your] promise.
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound supplication of believers, acknowledging Allah's promises conveyed through His messengers and seeking their fulfillment in this life and the Hereafter. It also expresses a deep sense of reliance on Allah's justice and mercy, asking not to be disgraced on the Day of Judgment, while affirming absolute trust in Allah's unbreakable promise—a reminder of divine accountability and the importance of steadfast faith in divine justice.

translation: So their Lord responded to them: 'Indeed, I will never waste the deeds of any doer among you, whether male or female; each of you is from the other. So those who migrated, were expelled from their homes, were harmed in My cause, fought, and were killed—I will surely remove their sins from them and admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, as a reward from Allah. And Allah has the best reward.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice and mercy of Allah, affirming that He does not overlook the sincerity and effort of any believer, regardless of gender, as long as their deeds are rooted in faith and righteousness. It highlights the principle of divine equity, where all are rewarded based on their deeds, not their worldly status or circumstances. The mention of migration, struggle, and sacrifice for Allah's cause emphasizes that true faith is tested through action, and such trials are not in vain. The promise of forgiveness and paradise for those who endure hardship for Allah's sake reflects the boundless generosity of divine reward, which transcends human limitations and expectations.

translation: Let not the movement of the disbelievers in the land deceive you.
interpretation: This verse cautions against being misled by the apparent prosperity, power, or influence of those who reject faith, reminding believers that their temporary success does not reflect divine approval or ultimate justice.

translation: A brief enjoyment, then their refuge is Hell—and what an evil resting place!
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of worldly pleasures and the severe consequence of heedlessness toward divine guidance, emphasizing that those who prioritize fleeting gains over eternal accountability will face a wretched end.

translation: But those who fear their Lord will have gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally—a gift from Allah. And what is with Allah is best for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate reward for the God-conscious ( muttaqeen ), emphasizing that their eternal abode in Paradise is not merely a reward but a divine gift, highlighting Allah's generosity and the superiority of His provision over all worldly attainments.

translation: And indeed, among the People of the Scripture (Jews and Christians) there are some who believe in Allah, and in what has been revealed to you (O Muhammad), and in what has been revealed to them, humbling themselves before Allah. They do not sell the verses of Allah for a small price (i.e. for this worldly life only). They shall have their reward with their Lord. Surely, Allah is Swift in account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincerity and steadfastness of certain believers from the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) who recognize the truth of Islam, including its scriptures and the finality of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), without letting worldly gains or societal pressures deter them from their faith.

translation: O you who have believed, persevere and endure and remain stationed and fear Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness, perseverance, and constant vigilance in the path of faith and righteousness, coupled with piety, as the means to attain true success in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. O mankind, fear your Lord, who created you from one soul and created from it its mate and dispersed from both of them many men and women. And fear Allah, through whom you ask one another, and [honor] the wombs. Indeed Allah is ever, over you, an Observer.
interpretation: This verse underscores the fundamental unity of humanity, emphasizing that all people originate from a single soul (Adam), and thus share a common origin and inherent dignity. It calls for reverence toward Allah as the Creator and Sustainer, and highlights the importance of maintaining ties of kinship and mutual respect, as these relationships are sacred and subject to divine accountability.

translation: And give the orphans their wealth, and do not substitute the defective for the good. And do not consume their wealth with your own. Indeed, that is a great sin.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ethical and moral responsibility of guardians or caretakers towards the wealth of orphans, prohibiting any form of exploitation or unjust appropriation. It underscores the sanctity of trust and the severe gravity of betraying that trust, as consuming an orphan's wealth unjustly is described as a 'great sin,' highlighting the moral and spiritual consequences of such actions.

translation: And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry [other] women that you like—two, three, or four. But if you fear you will not be just, then [marry only] one or whom your right hand possesses. That is more likely to prevent you from committing injustice.
interpretation: This verse addresses the ethical and social responsibility of men towards orphans and women in general, emphasizing justice and fairness in marital relationships. It acknowledges human limitations in perfect justice, especially in polygamous marriages, and encourages moderation (monogamy) as a safer path to avoid oppression or injustice.

translation: And give the women [upon marriage] their [bridal] gifts graciously. But if they should, of their own accord, remit part of it to you, then you may enjoy it [in full] with wholesome appetite.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling financial obligations in marriage with sincerity and generosity, while also acknowledging the mutual consent and kindness that can exist between spouses, allowing for flexibility in the return of part of the dowry if both parties agree.

translation: And do not give the foolish your wealth which Allah has made for you a means of support, but provide for them from it and clothe them, and speak to them with appropriate words.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to manage their wealth wisely, ensuring that it is not entrusted to those who are incapable of handling it responsibly, such as minors or individuals lacking sound judgment. Instead, it emphasizes the duty to provide for their needs—financially, materially, and with kind words—while maintaining authority and care over the wealth until they are capable of managing it themselves.

translation: And test the orphans [in their abilities] until they reach marriageable age. Then if you perceive in them sound judgement, release their wealth to them. And do not consume it excessively and hastily before they grow up. And whoever [among guardians] is rich let him abstain [from taking the orphan's wealth], and whoever is poor let him take therefrom in a reasonable manner. Then when you release their wealth to them, bring witnesses upon them. And sufficient is Allah as Accountant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of responsible guardianship over orphans' wealth, requiring careful assessment of their maturity and sound judgment before entrusting them with their inheritance. It prohibits misuse or hasty consumption of their assets, urging guardians to act with integrity—whether wealthy (to refrain from taking any) or poor (to take only what is necessary). The requirement for witnesses ensures transparency and accountability, reinforcing the ethical and legal duty to protect the orphan's rights until they are capable of managing their own affairs.

translation: For men is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, and for women is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave, be it little or much—an obligatory share.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of fixed inheritance shares in Islam, ensuring that both men and women receive a predetermined portion of an estate based on divine decree, reflecting justice and equity in the distribution of wealth among heirs.

translation: And when relatives and orphans and the needy are present at the division [of inheritance], then provide for them from it and speak to them words of appropriate kindness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ethical responsibility of believers to ensure that the distribution of inheritance does not overlook the rights of vulnerable family members—relatives, orphans, and the poor—by allocating a portion of it to them, while also addressing them with dignity and respect.

translation: And let those who would be reluctant to leave weak offspring behind them, if they were themselves to die, observe their duty to Allah and speak correct and just words.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral responsibility of individuals to ensure that their dependents are cared for and protected, even in their absence, by upholding justice and righteousness in their words and actions.

translation: Indeed, those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly are only consuming into their bellies fire. And they will be burned in a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse serves as a severe warning against the exploitation of the vulnerable, particularly orphans, for personal gain. It underscores the gravity of injustice in consuming their wealth unlawfully, equating such actions to the consumption of fire in the hereafter, symbolizing both the moral corruption in this life and the severe punishment in the next.

translation: Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females. But if there are [only] women, two or more, for them is two-thirds of what [the deceased] left. And if there is only one, for her is half. And for one's parents, to each one of them is a sixth of his estate if he left children. But if he had no children and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is one-third. And if he had brothers [or sisters], for his mother is a sixth, after any bequest he [may have] made or debt. Your parents or your children - you do not know which of them are closer to you in benefit. [This is] an obligation from Allah, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes a system of inheritance that prioritizes justice and practical benefit, recognizing that financial responsibility often falls more heavily on males in traditional family structures. It also highlights the importance of fulfilling obligations (such as debts and bequests) before distributing inheritance, ensuring fairness and preventing disputes. The mention of uncertainty about which heirs are 'closer in benefit' underscores the divine wisdom behind these fixed shares, as human judgment may be flawed or biased.

translation: And for you is half of what your wives leave if they have no child. But if they have a child, for you is one fourth of what they leave, after any bequest they [may have] made or debt. And for them [i.e., the wives] is one fourth of what you leave if you have no child. But if you have a child, for them is one eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you [may have] made or debt. And if a man or a woman leaves neither ascendants nor descendants but has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is a sixth. But if they are more than two, they share a third, after any bequest which was made or debt, without causing harm. [This is] an ordinance from Allah, and Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Islamic laws of inheritance, emphasizing fairness and the rights of both spouses and extended family members, ensuring that no one is deprived unjustly while also preventing harm or exploitation in the distribution of an estate.

translation: These are the limits [set by] Allah. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger will be admitted by Him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they abide eternally, and that is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine boundaries set by Allah, as obedience to Him and His Messenger (peace be upon him) leads to eternal bliss in Paradise, highlighting the ultimate success and reward for those who follow the path of righteousness.

translation: And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits, He will admit him to a Fire, wherein he will abide eternally, and he will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of disobedience to divine commandments and the severe consequences of overstepping the boundaries set by Allah. It serves as a stern warning against defiance of Allah's laws, emphasizing that such actions lead to eternal punishment in Hell, highlighting the importance of obedience and adherence to divine guidance.

translation: And those who commit an immoral act from your women - bring against them four [witnesses] from among you. And if they testify, then confine the guilty women to houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them [another] way.
interpretation: This verse addresses the severe consequences of adultery committed by women, emphasizing the need for strict evidentiary standards (four witnesses) to establish guilt. It reflects the gravity of the offense in the societal and legal context of the time, where honor and chastity were paramount, and confinement to the home served as both a punishment and a means of preventing further moral transgression until divine or legal resolution could be determined.

translation: And those who commit it among you, dishonor them both. But if they repent and correct themselves, leave them alone. Indeed, Allah is Accepting of repentance, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the punishment for the act of homosexuality (liwat) in the context of the society at the time, emphasizing both accountability and the possibility of repentance and reform. It underscores the balance between justice and mercy, reflecting Allah’s willingness to forgive those who sincerely turn back to Him.

translation: Allah accepts only the repentance of those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon after, and it is they whom Allah turns to in forgiveness, and Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless mercy of Allah towards those who sincerely repent from their sins, even if they were committed out of ignorance, provided the repentance is prompt and genuine. It underscores that Allah’s forgiveness is not restricted by the severity of the sin but is contingent upon the sincerity and immediacy of the seeker’s return to Him, reflecting His infinite knowledge and wisdom in judging the hearts of His servants.

translation: But repentance is not [accepted] for those who do evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now." Nor [is repentance accepted] for those who die while they are disbelievers. For them We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the urgency and sincerity required for repentance, emphasizing that true repentance must precede the moment of death, as after death, the opportunity for repentance is lost. It also highlights the finality of disbelief, where even a last-minute claim of repentance is rejected if one dies in a state of unbelief, reinforcing the gravity of faith and the consequences of rejecting it.

translation: O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force. And do not constrain them to take away part of what you gave them unless they commit a clear immorality. And live with them in kindness. For if you dislike them - perhaps you dislike a thing and Allah makes therein much good.
interpretation: This verse establishes the ethical and legal framework for marital relationships in Islam, emphasizing mutual respect, consent, and kindness. It prohibits forced inheritance of women, ensuring their autonomy and dignity in marriage. The permission to withhold part of the dowry (mahr) is conditional upon clear immorality (fahisha mubayyina), not arbitrary or unjust actions. The instruction to live with wives in kindness ('urf) underscores the importance of mutual respect, patience, and fairness, even in difficult circumstances. The concluding statement highlights the divine wisdom in trials, encouraging believers to trust in Allah’s plan, as hardship may conceal unseen blessings.

translation: And if you wish to replace one wife with another and you have given one of them a great amount [of dowry], do not take [back] from it anything. Would you take it in slander and manifest sin?
interpretation: This verse addresses the moral and ethical responsibility of men towards women in the context of marriage and divorce. It prohibits taking back any part of the dowry given to a wife when replacing her with another, emphasizing that doing so would constitute a grave injustice and sin, as it would be an act of deceit and open wrongdoing against the woman.

translation: And how could you take it while you have already met each other and taken from each other a solemn covenant?
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of breaking a covenant, particularly in the context of marital relationships, by questioning the moral justification for taking back a dowry after intimate relations have occurred, underscoring the sanctity and binding nature of the promises made.

translation: And do not marry women whom your fathers married, except what has already passed. Indeed, it was an outrage, an abomination, and an evil way.
interpretation: This verse prohibits marrying women who were previously married to one's father, emphasizing that such marriages are forbidden due to their inherent wrongness and moral corruption, as they were considered highly disgraceful and contrary to natural human decency in the pre-Islamic Arab context.

translation: Prohibited to you [for marriage] are your mothers, your daughters, your sisters, your paternal aunts, your maternal aunts, your brother's daughters, your sister's daughters, your [milk] mothers who nursed you, your sisters through nursing, your wives' mothers, your step-daughters under your guardianship born of your wives with whom you have consummated marriage—if you have not consummated marriage with them, there is no blame upon you—and [prohibited are] the wives of your sons who are from your [own] loins, and that you take [in marriage] two sisters simultaneously, except for what has already occurred. Indeed, Allah is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the boundaries of permissible and impermissible marriages in Islam, emphasizing the sanctity of family ties and the prevention of potential conflicts within close-knit relationships. It reflects a broader ethical and social framework aimed at preserving moral integrity, protecting vulnerable individuals (such as stepdaughters), and avoiding exploitation or harm within familial or marital structures. The exceptions and conditions highlight the importance of intention, action, and context in determining permissibility, underscoring Allah's mercy and forgiveness in cases where boundaries may have been unintentionally transgressed.

translation: And [also prohibited to you are all] married women except those your right hands possess. [This is] the decree of Allah upon you. And lawful to you are [all others] beyond that, [provided that] you seek them [in marriage] with [gifts from] your property, desiring chastity, not unlawful sexual intercourse. So for whatever you enjoy [i.e., consummate marriage] with them, give them their due compensation as an obligation. And there is no blame upon you for what you mutually agree to beyond the obligation. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse outlines the ethical and legal framework for marriage in Islam, distinguishing between two categories: (1) women who are already married, whom a Muslim is prohibited from marrying unless they are widowed or divorced (with exceptions for those in one's possession under strict historical and ethical conditions), and (2) women who are not married to others, whom a Muslim may marry with the intention of chastity and commitment, not merely for sexual gratification. The verse emphasizes the sanctity of marriage as a covenantal relationship, requiring mutual consent, financial responsibility (dowry), and adherence to divine law. The mention of 'mutual agreement beyond the obligation' suggests flexibility in marital arrangements, provided they align with Islamic principles of justice and dignity.

translation: And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then [he may marry] from those whom your right hands possess of believing young women. And Allah is most knowing about your faith. You [believers] are of one another. So marry them with the permission of their people and give them their due compensation (dowry) in a recognized manner. [They should be] chaste, neither committing unlawful sexual intercourse nor taking lovers. But once they are sheltered in marriage, if they commit an immorality, then for them is half the punishment for free [unmarried] women. This is for whoever fears difficulty among you. But to endure is better for you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse addresses the permissibility of marrying chaste believing slave women for those who cannot afford to marry free believing women, emphasizing modesty, proper dowry, and the consequences of immorality, while highlighting the virtue of patience and the mercy of Allah in cases of hardship.

translation: Allah wants to make clear to you [the lawful from the unlawful] and guide you to the [good] practices of those before you and to accept your repentance. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah’s mercy and guidance, indicating that He provides clarity in religious matters not only to distinguish right from wrong but also to steer people toward the righteous paths followed by previous generations of believers. It also highlights the possibility of repentance, reassuring that Allah, in His infinite knowledge and wisdom, is both forgiving and just.

translation: But Allah intends to accept your repentance, while those who follow [their] passions desire that you should deviate with [your] deviation a great deviation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between Allah's mercy and forgiveness, which He readily offers to those who repent, and the destructive influence of those who are driven by their base desires, seeking to lead others astray from the path of righteousness.

translation: Allah intends to lighten the burden for you, for man was created weak.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that Allah’s laws and rulings are designed with mercy and ease in mind, acknowledging human limitations and imperfections, particularly the inherent weakness of human nature.

translation: O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly but only [in lawful] business by mutual consent. And do not kill yourselves [or one another]; indeed, Allah is to you ever Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of life and property in Islam, prohibiting any form of exploitation, deceit, or harm within the Muslim community. It establishes the principle of mutual consent and fairness in financial transactions, while also underscoring the value of human life, equating unjust killing with self-destruction, and reminding believers of Allah’s mercy as the foundation for ethical conduct.

translation: But whoever commits it intentionally and wrongfully, he shall be punished with a Fire; that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of committing sins with full knowledge and deliberate intent, emphasizing that such actions are not only a transgression against divine law but also a manifestation of oppression (zulm). The severe punishment of Hellfire is presented as a certainty for those who engage in such willful wrongdoing, highlighting Allah’s justice and the inevitability of accountability for intentional sin.

translation: If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden from, We will remove from you your evil deeds and admit you to an honored entrance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and forgiveness of Allah, emphasizing that sincere avoidance of major sins leads to expiation of lesser sins and entry into Paradise, underscoring the importance of repentance and righteousness.

translation: And do not wish for what Allah has favored some of you over others. For men is a share of what they have earned, and for women is a share of what they have earned. And ask Allah of His bounty. Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse discourages envy and resentment towards others' blessings, emphasizing that everyone's sustenance and status are determined by Allah's wisdom and justice. It underscores the principle of individual accountability and the importance of seeking Allah's grace rather than coveting others' positions or possessions.

translation: And for all [We have appointed] heirs from what is left by parents and near relatives. And for those with whom you have made a solemn covenant, give them their share. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of fulfilling obligations, even those beyond blood relations, such as those established through solemn pledges or alliances. It highlights that justice and fairness must extend to all, including those with whom one has entered into a covenant, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of honoring commitments and maintaining trust in all dealings.

translation: Men are in charge of women by [right of] what Allah has given one over the other and what they spend [in maintenance] from their wealth. So righteous women are devoutly obedient, guarding in [the husband's] absence what Allah would have them guard. But those [wives] from whom you fear arrogance and defiance, [first] advise them; [then if they persist], forsake them in bed; and [finally], strike them. But if they obey you [once more], seek no means against them. Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted and Grand.
interpretation: This verse outlines the Islamic framework for marital roles, emphasizing mutual responsibility, patience, and justice. The authority of men as 'qawwamun' (protectors/maintainers) is not absolute but tied to their duty of financial provision and moral leadership. The instruction to discipline disobedient wives is framed as a last resort, with escalating measures (advice, separation, light striking) meant to correct behavior, not punish. The final condition—that obedience nullifies further action—underscores that discipline is conditional on reconciliation, reflecting a balance between authority and accountability. The verse’s closing affirmation of Allah’s greatness reminds believers that all actions must align with divine justice.

translation: And if you fear dissension between them, send an arbitrator from his people and an arbitrator from her people. If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will cause them to succeed. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of mediation and reconciliation in marital disputes, emphasizing that even in conflict, the door to resolution remains open through fair and balanced intervention, with divine facilitation when the intent for peace is sincere.

translation: And worship Allah and associate none with Him, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the neighbor who is near, the neighbor who is distant, the companion by your side, the traveler, and those whom your right hands possess. Indeed, Allah does not like whoever is arrogant and boastful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere worship of Allah alone, without associating partners with Him, while also highlighting the duty of kindness and justice toward all people, regardless of their social status or relationship to the believer. It underscores the need for humility and rejection of arrogance, as Allah does not approve of those who are boastful or prideful in their actions.

translation: Those who are stingy and enjoin upon [other] people stinginess and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who hoard their wealth out of greed, encourage others to do the same, and hide the blessings Allah has bestowed upon them, denying their duty to share and be grateful. It serves as a warning that such behavior, driven by selfishness and ingratitude, will lead to severe punishment in the Hereafter, highlighting the moral and spiritual consequences of miserliness and the rejection of divine generosity.

translation: And [also] those who spend their wealth to be seen by the people, and believe neither in Allah nor in the Last Day. And whoever has Satan as a companion—what an evil companion he is!
interpretation: This verse condemns hypocritical spending, where acts of charity are performed not for the sake of Allah but solely to gain praise from others, devoid of true faith in Allah or the Hereafter. It warns that associating with Satan—through such insincere actions—leads to ruin, as Satan’s influence corrupts intentions and deeds.

translation: And what is [the matter] with them that they do not believe in Allah and the Last Day, and spend out of what Allah has provided for them? And Allah is ever, about them, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse underscores the natural expectation of faith and gratitude towards Allah, especially when one is provided for by His bounty. The rhetorical question highlights the irrationality of disbelief despite clear signs of Allah's providence, while also reminding that Allah is fully aware of human actions and intentions, implying accountability in both belief and deeds.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not do injustice, [even] as much as an atom's weight; and if there is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of Allah, emphasizing that He does not withhold even the smallest reward for any good deed, and in fact, He magnifies its reward beyond measure. It also highlights the boundless generosity of Allah, who bestows immense rewards not merely as a matter of justice but as an act of pure grace ('min ladunh'). This serves as both a reassurance to believers that their efforts are not in vain and a warning to those who might rely solely on their deeds without recognizing Allah's ultimate generosity.

translation: So how will it be when We bring from every nation a witness and We bring you (O Muhammad) as a witness against these people?
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate accountability of all nations and individuals before Allah, emphasizing that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) will bear witness against his own community on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the gravity of moral and spiritual responsibility.

translation: On that Day, the disbelievers and those who disobeyed the Messenger will wish that they could be levelled with the earth, and they will not be able to hide anything from Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense regret and despair of the disbelievers and those who defied the Prophet on the Day of Judgment, when they realize the gravity of their actions and the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying, nor in a state of janabah (major impurity), except those passing through [a place of prayer], until you have bathed. And if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and your hands with it. Indeed, Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse establishes the conditions of ritual purity required before engaging in prayer, emphasizing both physical and mental readiness as essential to the act of worship. It highlights the importance of clarity and presence of mind in connecting with the Divine, while also demonstrating Allah’s mercy by providing practical alternatives (such as tayammum) when water is unavailable or impractical, ensuring that worship remains accessible to all believers regardless of their circumstances.

translation: Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture, how they choose error and wish for you to lose the way?
interpretation: This verse critiques those who, despite having access to divine guidance, deliberately choose misguidance and actively seek to lead others astray, reflecting a rejection of truth despite its availability.

translation: And Allah is most knowing of your enemies. And sufficient is Allah as a protector, and sufficient is Allah as a helper.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that Allah is fully aware of the intentions and actions of their enemies, implying that no harm can come to them without Allah's permission. It also emphasizes complete reliance on Allah for protection and support, highlighting His ultimate authority and sufficiency in all matters.

translation: Among the Jews are those who distort words from their [proper] places and say, "We hear and disobey," and "Hear, [O Muhammad], and be not heard," and "Ra'ina," twisting their tongues and defaming the religion. And if they had said [instead], "We hear and obey" and "Wait for us [to understand]," it would have been better for them and more upright; but Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and deceit of certain Jewish groups who deliberately misinterpreted or altered the meanings of divine commands to suit their own agendas, while also mocking the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) through linguistic manipulation. It underscores the importance of sincerity and obedience in faith, contrasting true submission with the false pretense of those who distort truth for personal or communal gain.

translation: O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down [to Muhammad], confirming that which is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them toward their backs or curse them as We cursed the companions of the Sabbath. And ever is the command of Allah accomplished.
interpretation: This verse underscores the urgency of recognizing divine truth and the consequences of rejecting it, emphasizing that God's decrees are absolute and inevitable, while also affirming the continuity of divine revelation.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating others with Him [shirk], but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of shirk (associating partners with Allah) as the one unforgivable sin, highlighting its absolute rejection in Islam. It also reflects Allah’s boundless mercy in forgiving lesser sins for those He wills, emphasizing the importance of repentance and sincere faith.

translation: Have you not considered those who claim purity for themselves? Rather, Allah purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse underscores that true purity and righteousness come solely from Allah's judgment, not self-proclaimed virtue. It cautions against arrogance in claiming spiritual superiority, emphasizing that Allah alone has the authority to purify hearts and deeds, and no injustice—no matter how small—will go unaddressed in His justice.

translation: See how they invent falsehood about Allah. And sufficient is that as a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of falsely attributing lies to Allah, emphasizing that such an act is not merely a minor transgression but a clear and undeniable sin, reflecting a profound disrespect and rebellion against divine truth.

translation: Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture? They believe in idolatry and false deities and say of the disbelievers, 'These are more guided than the believers are in their way?'
interpretation: This verse critiques those who claim adherence to divine scripture yet deviate by associating partners with Allah (shirk) and falsely elevating the guidance of disbelievers over that of true believers. It highlights the hypocrisy of those who distort scriptural teachings to justify their misguidance, emphasizing that true guidance is only found in submission to Allah's oneness (tawhid) and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

translation: It is they whom Allah has cursed; and he whom Allah curses, you will never find for him a helper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequence of divine rejection, indicating that those who incur Allah's curse are devoid of any aid or intercession, emphasizing the finality and irrevocability of Allah's judgment.

translation: Or do they have a share in the dominion? Then they would not give people even the speck on a date stone.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah and the futility of any claim to power or authority by others, as even the smallest measure of control or benefit they might possess is entirely dependent on His will and granting.

translation: Or do they envy people for what Allah has given them of His bounty? But We had already given the family of Abraham the Scripture and wisdom and conferred upon them a great kingdom.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy and envy of those who resent the blessings Allah has bestowed upon others, particularly the believers. It highlights that divine favor is not a matter of human entitlement but a test of gratitude and righteousness, reminding us that Allah's grace is distributed according to His wisdom, not human jealousy.

translation: So among them is he who believes in it, and among them is he who turns away from it. And sufficient for the Fire is it as a blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity in human response to divine guidance—some accept it with faith, while others reject it out of arrogance or disbelief. The mention of Hell as sufficient 'as a blaze' underscores the severity of rejecting truth, emphasizing that such defiance carries grave consequences, serving as a warning to those who turn away from guidance.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses - We will drive them into a fire. Every time their skins are roasted through We will replace them with other skins so they may taste the punishment. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of divine punishment for those who reject the signs of Allah, emphasizing both the perpetual nature of their suffering and the justice of Allah’s decree, as He replaces their burnt skins to prolong their torment, illustrating His absolute power and wisdom in administering justice.

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. For them will be purified spouses, and We will admit them to deep, shady shade.
interpretation: This verse underscores the eternal reward for believers who combine faith with righteous actions, emphasizing both the physical and spiritual dimensions of Paradise—rivers symbolizing divine sustenance, purified spouses reflecting moral perfection, and shade representing ultimate comfort and peace.

translation: Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to whom they are due and when you judge between people to judge with justice. Excellent is that which Allah instructs you. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the moral and legal obligations of justice and trustworthiness in human dealings, framing them as divine commands that reflect Allah's attributes of hearing and seeing, thereby emphasizing the accountability of one's actions before Allah.

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you. And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger, if you should believe in Allah and the Last Day. That is the best [way] and best in result.
interpretation: This verse establishes the hierarchy of authority and the principle of resolving disputes within the framework of divine guidance. It emphasizes that obedience to Allah and His Messenger is paramount, and that in matters of disagreement, the final authority lies with the Qur'an and the Sunnah (teachings of the Prophet), not personal opinions or worldly power. This ensures that decisions are just, aligned with divine wisdom, and lead to the best possible outcomes for the community.

translation: Have you not considered those who claim to have believed in what was revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you? They wish to refer legislation to Taghut, while they were commanded to reject it; and Satan wishes to lead them far astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim faith but seek guidance from false authorities (Taghut) instead of adhering to divine revelation, exposing their deviation from true monotheistic submission.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger,' you see the hypocrites turning away from you in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrites' refusal to submit to divine guidance and their aversion to the truth, despite clear calls to follow Allah's commandments and the teachings of the Prophet.
