Their rejection is not based on ignorance but on arrogance and insincerity, as they deliberately turn away from the path of righteousness.

translation: So how [will it be] when disaster strikes them for what their hands have put forth and then they come to you swearing by Allah, 'We intended nothing but good and reconciliation'?
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim righteous intentions after facing consequences for their wrongdoings, revealing their true disregard for accountability and divine justice.

translation: As for those whose intentions Allah knows well [being insincere], so disregard them, but admonish them, and speak to them a telling word to their souls.
interpretation: This verse advises the believers to be discerning in their interactions with insincere individuals, avoiding excessive engagement while still fulfilling the duty of guidance through clear and impactful words that may penetrate their hearts.

translation: And We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by permission of Allah. And if, when they wronged themselves, they had come to you, [O Muhammad], and asked forgiveness of Allah and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the necessity of obedience to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) as a reflection of obedience to Allah Himself, highlighting that true repentance involves seeking forgiveness through the Prophet (peace be upon him) and recognizing his intercessory role as a mercy from Allah.

translation: But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you, [O Muhammad], judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves and then find within themselves no discomfort from what you have judged and submit in [full, willing] submission.
interpretation: This verse underscores the depth of true faith, which requires absolute submission to the Prophet's (ﷺ) authority in both judgment and personal conviction, leaving no room for hesitation or internal resistance to divine rulings.

translation: And if We had decreed for them: 'Kill yourselves' or 'Leave your homes,' they would not have done it except for a few of them. And if they had done what they were admonished [to do], it would have been better for them and a more firm establishment [of faith].
interpretation: This verse underscores the natural human resistance to extreme sacrifices or hardships, even when commanded by divine will, highlighting the rarity of absolute submission. It also implies that true faith is not merely in grand gestures but in consistent adherence to moral and spiritual guidance, which would strengthen one's resolve and lead to greater spiritual stability.

translation: And indeed, We would have given them from Ourselves a great reward.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine principle that true and lasting reward comes solely from Allah, not from worldly means or human effort alone. It highlights the exclusivity of Allah's grace and the magnitude of His recompense for those who remain steadfast in faith and righteousness.

translation: And We have guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's guidance as a continuous and unwavering direction for humanity, highlighting the clarity and steadfastness of the path He has ordained, which is the path of truth, righteousness, and submission to His will.

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger - those will be with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast affirmers of truth, the martyrs and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for those who follow divine guidance and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), promising them companionship with the highest ranks of righteous individuals in Paradise. It underscores the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger as the path to eternal fellowship with the prophets, truthful believers, martyrs, and the righteous, emphasizing the honor and closeness to Allah that such companionship entails.

translation: That bounty is from Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores that all favors, blessings, and bounties come solely from Allah, emphasizing His absolute sovereignty and generosity. It also reassures believers that Allah is fully aware of all things, including their needs and deeds, reinforcing trust in His wisdom and justice.

translation: O you who have believed, take your precaution and [either] go forth in detachments or go forth all together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of preparedness and unity in the face of potential threats, urging believers to organize themselves effectively for defense while maintaining collective strength and cohesion.

translation: And indeed, among you is he who would linger behind. If a calamity befalls you, he says, 'Allah has certainly favored me that I was not present with them.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocritical nature of some individuals who avoid participating in righteous deeds or facing trials alongside the believers, only to later claim that their absence was a blessing from Allah when adversity strikes others, revealing their lack of sincerity and true faith.

translation: And if a favor from Allah touches you, they will surely say, 'It is as if there had never been any affection between you and them. I wish I had been with them so I could have attained a great attainment.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and insincerity of those who claim to be allies but abandon their supposed friends in times of hardship, only to express regret when they witness the blessings bestowed upon them. It underscores the transient nature of worldly relationships devoid of true faith and warns against relying on such superficial bonds.

translation: So let those who exchange the life of this world for the Hereafter fight in the cause of Allah. And whoever fights in the cause of Allah and is killed or achieves victory, We will grant him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing the Hereafter over worldly gains and encourages believers to strive in the path of Allah, even if it leads to sacrifice or struggle, with the assurance of divine reward for their steadfastness and commitment.

translation: And what is [the matter] with you that you do not fight in the cause of Allah and [for] the oppressed among men, women, and children who say, 'Our Lord, take us out of this city of oppressive people and appoint for us from Yourself a protector and appoint for us from Yourself a helper?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the moral and religious obligation to defend the oppressed and fight against tyranny, even if it requires active struggle, as long as it is done with justice and in the path of Allah. It highlights the plight of those who are wronged and seek divine intervention, emphasizing that their cause is just and worthy of support.

translation: Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of false idols. So fight against the allies of Satan; indeed, the plot of Satan has ever been weak.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental difference in the motivations and allegiances of believers versus disbelievers, framing their struggles as diametrically opposed. It underscores the spiritual nature of the conflict, where believers engage in a righteous struggle for divine truth, while disbelievers are driven by allegiance to falsehood and misguidance. The call to fight the allies of Satan is not a literal incitement to violence but a metaphorical reminder to resist and counter the forces of evil and corruption in all its forms, emphasizing that the schemes of Satan, though persistent, are ultimately weak and destined to fail.

translation: Have you not considered those who were told, 'Restrain your hands, establish prayer, and give zakah'? But then when fighting was prescribed for them, at once a party of them feared people as they fear Allah or with [even] greater fear. They said, 'Our Lord, why have You decreed upon us fighting? If only You had postponed [it for] us for a short time.' Say, 'The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for he who fears Allah. And you will not be wronged [in the Hereafter] [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and weakness of faith in some who were commanded to restrain from aggression and uphold their religious duties, yet when faced with the obligation of jihad (struggle in the cause of Allah), they faltered and prioritized worldly fear over divine accountability. It underscores the transient nature of worldly life and the eternal value of the Hereafter, warning against the pitfalls of prioritizing immediate comfort over divine commandments.

translation: Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you should be within towers of lofty construction. But if good comes to them, they say, "This is from Allah," and if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you." Say, "All is from Allah." So what is [the matter] with those people that they can hardly understand any statement?
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all events, both good and bad, in a person's life, and highlights the hypocrisy of those who attribute blessings to Allah while blaming others (or circumstances) for misfortunes, revealing their lack of true understanding of divine decree (Qadr).

translation: Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever ill befalls you is from yourself. And We have sent you (O Muhammad) as a messenger to mankind, and sufficient is Allah as a Witness.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine decree and personal responsibility, emphasizing that blessings come from Allah as a manifestation of His grace, while hardships often stem from human actions or choices, serving as a reminder of accountability and the need for self-reflection.

translation: Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah. And whoever turns away—We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], over them as a guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute authority of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in conveying and implementing divine guidance, establishing that obedience to him is synonymous with obedience to Allah. It also reassures the Prophet that his responsibility is to convey the message, not to enforce belief or compel obedience, as guidance ultimately rests with Allah.

translation: And they say, 'Obedience.' But when they leave your presence, a group of them conspire by night to do other than what you say. And Allah records what they conspire by night. So turn away from them and rely upon Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of some who outwardly claim obedience but secretly plot against the Prophet (peace be upon him) and his teachings. It underscores Allah's omniscience in recording their hidden actions, while also commanding the Prophet to disregard their deceit and place his trust entirely in Allah's protection and decree.

translation: Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an? If it had been from [any] other than Allah, they would have found within it much contradiction.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an by challenging skeptics to examine its consistency; any human-authored text would inevitably contain contradictions, whereas the Qur'an's flawless coherence serves as proof of its supernatural source.

translation: And when there comes to them some matter concerning public security or fear, they spread it about; but if they had referred it to the Messenger or to those charged with authority among them, the truthful ones among them would have known about it. And if it were not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of verifying information and seeking guidance from authoritative sources, particularly in matters of public concern, rather than spreading unverified rumors. It highlights the consequences of neglecting this principle—leading to chaos or misguidance—and emphasizes that divine mercy and guidance are essential to avoid falling into the traps of Satan.

translation: So fight in the cause of Allah; you are not held responsible except for yourself. And urge the believers on. Perhaps Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve. And Allah is the strongest in might and the strongest in punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility of a believer in fulfilling their duty to strive in the way of Allah, while also encouraging collective action among the Muslim community. It reassures believers that Allah has the ultimate power to restrain the aggression of the disbelievers, highlighting divine justice and the strength of Allah's retribution against wrongdoers.

translation: Whoever intercedes with a good intercession will have a share in it, and whoever intercedes with an evil intercession will have a burden of it. And ever is Allah, over all things, a Keeper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the moral responsibility that comes with influence and advocacy. It teaches that any action taken to facilitate good—whether in word or deed—will yield positive consequences for the one who initiates it, while actions that enable or promote harm will likewise bear negative repercussions. It highlights the principle of accountability, where individuals are held responsible not only for their direct actions but also for the indirect effects of their influence, emphasizing the need for righteousness and caution in all forms of intercession or advocacy.

translation: And when you are greeted with a greeting, greet [in return] with one better than it or [at least] return it. Indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, an Accountant.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reciprocating kindness and respect in social interactions, encouraging Muslims to respond to greetings with even greater warmth or, at minimum, to acknowledge them graciously, reflecting the virtue of humility and the recognition of Allah's meticulous recording of all deeds.

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah (Tawheed) and underscores the certainty of the Day of Resurrection, affirming that no one is more truthful in speech than Allah, thereby reinforcing the authenticity of divine revelation and the inevitability of the Hereafter.

translation: So why do you have two factions among the hypocrites? Allah has caused them to fall back [into disbelief] for what they earned. Do you want to guide he whom Allah has sent astray? And whoever Allah sends astray - never will you find for him a way [of guidance].
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of attempting to guide those whom Allah has decreed to misguidance due to their own actions, highlighting the importance of recognizing divine will and the limits of human influence in matters of faith.

translation: They wish you would disbelieve as they disbelieved so you would be alike [to them]. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate for the sake of Allah. But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them and take not from among them any ally or helper.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocritical and hostile stance of those who reject faith, emphasizing the importance of maintaining distinct religious boundaries. It underscores that true faith requires commitment beyond mere lip service, as seen in the condition of emigration (*hijrah*) for the sake of Allah. The directive to fight those who persist in disbelief is a response to active persecution and opposition to Islam, not a general command to wage war against all non-Muslims. It reflects a context of self-defense and preservation of the Muslim community in the face of existential threats during the early Islamic period.

translation: Except for those who join a people between whom and you there is a treaty, or those who come to you with their hearts constricted, feeling constrained to fight you or fight their own people. Had Allah willed, He could have given them power over you, and they would have fought you. So if they withdraw from you, do not fight you, and offer you peace, then Allah has not made for you a way against them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of reciprocity and restraint in warfare, emphasizing that Muslims should not initiate hostilities against those who seek peace or are bound by treaties, even if they are initially hostile. It highlights the importance of distinguishing between those who are genuinely inclined toward peace and those who are not, while leaving the final judgment to Allah’s wisdom and will.

translation: You will find others who wish to be secure from you and secure from their people. Every time they are returned to fitnah (trial or discord), they fall back into it. So if they do not withdraw from you and offer you peace and restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you encounter them. And against these, We have given you a clear authorization.
interpretation: This verse addresses the permissibility of fighting those who persistently threaten the Muslim community, even if they outwardly seek temporary peace, as their actions reveal their true intent to undermine or harm the believers. It underscores the principle that actions, not just words, determine the response of the Muslim community in matters of security and defense.

translation: And never is it for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake - then the freeing of a believing slave and compensation [diya] paid to his [the victim's] family, unless they give [it] in charity. But if he was from a people at war with you and he was a believer, then [only] the freeing of a believing slave [is required]; and if he was from a people with whom you have a treaty, then a compensation paid to his family and the freeing of a believing slave. And whoever does not find [a slave to free], then [he should fast for] two consecutive months as repentance to Allah. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the gravity of unintentional killing within the Muslim community, emphasizing that even an accidental killing of a believer is a grave sin requiring expiation. The prescribed atonement—freeing a believing slave, paying blood money (diya), or fasting—reflects a balance between justice and mercy, ensuring accountability while allowing for repentance. The distinction based on the victim's affiliation (whether from a hostile or treaty-bound people) underscores the ethical and legal framework governing inter-community relations, reinforcing the sanctity of life and the importance of upholding covenants.

translation: But whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, wherein he will abide eternally, and Allah has become angry with him and has cursed him and has prepared for him a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of intentionally taking a believer's life, equating it with a severe spiritual and moral transgression that incurs divine wrath, eternal punishment, and exclusion from Allah's mercy.

translation: O you who have believed, when you travel in the cause of Allah, investigate; and do not say to one who gives you a greeting of peace, "You are not a believer," aspiring for the goods of worldly life. For with Allah are abundant gains. You were like that before, so Allah conferred favor upon you. Therefore, investigate. Indeed, Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse cautions against hasty judgments or superficial assessments, especially in matters of faith, when worldly interests are at stake. It warns against denying the sincerity of those who outwardly profess peace (a sign of submission to Islam) merely to exploit material gains, as true rewards lie with Allah. The verse also reminds believers of their own past state of ignorance before Allah guided them, urging them to exercise discernment rather than suspicion, as Allah is fully aware of their actions and intentions.

translation: Not equal are those believers who sit at home (without any valid excuse) and those who strive and fight in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred in grades those who strive and fight with their wealth and their lives above those who sit at home. Unto each Allah has promised good (Paradise), but Allah has preferred those who strive and fight above those who sit at home by a huge reward.
interpretation: This verse underscores the spiritual and moral distinction between those who actively strive in the path of Allah (through jihad, sacrifice, or service) and those who remain passive without valid reason, emphasizing that true faith is demonstrated through action and sacrifice rather than mere belief alone.

translation: Levels [of reward] from Him and forgiveness and mercy. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's rewards, forgiveness, and mercy are not uniform but are granted in varying degrees based on His wisdom and justice, highlighting both His boundless mercy and the importance of striving for higher spiritual attainment.

translation: Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, the angels will say, 'In what [condition] were you?' They will say, 'We were oppressed in the land.' The angels will say, 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious enough for you to emigrate therein?' For those, their refuge is Hell - and evil it is as a destination.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of failing to act against oppression or injustice when one has the means to do so, particularly when the earth provides ample opportunities for migration or resistance. It highlights a moral and spiritual accountability for those who remain complicit in their oppression rather than seeking justice or fleeing from tyranny, even if they perceive themselves as powerless.

translation: Except the weak among men, women and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they guided to the way.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine principle of justice and mercy, exempting those who are truly unable to act or defend themselves—such as the vulnerable, the oppressed, and those without means or guidance—from obligations or punishments they cannot fulfill.

translation: So it is expected that Allah will pardon them. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's attribute of forgiveness and mercy, suggesting that even those who have committed wrongdoings may still hope for Allah's pardon, emphasizing the boundless nature of divine mercy when sincere repentance is present.

translation: And whoever emigrates for the sake of Allah will find on earth many [alternative] places of refuge and abundance. And whoever leaves his home as an emigrant to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him - his reward has already become incumbent upon Allah. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the profound reward for those who migrate for the sake of Allah, emphasizing that such migration is not merely a physical act but a spiritual journey with divine recompense. It highlights Allah's boundless mercy and forgiveness, assuring that those who strive in His path will be rewarded even if death overtakes them before reaching their destination, reinforcing the idea that sincere intention and effort in the cause of Allah are ultimately accepted and rewarded by Him.

translation: And when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may disrupt you. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse permits the shortening of obligatory prayers during travel when there is a genuine fear of harm or disruption from enemies, emphasizing the prioritization of safety and the preservation of one's faith over strict adherence to ritual forms under such circumstances.

translation: And when you are among them and lead the prayer for them, let a group of them stand with you and let them take their weapons. And when they prostrate, let them be behind you. And let another group who have not prayed come and pray with you, taking their precautions and their weapons. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your weapons and your baggage so that they could attack you in one assault. But there is no blame upon you, if you are troubled by rain or are ill, for putting down your weapons. And take precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of maintaining security and vigilance even during acts of worship, emphasizing the balance between devotion to Allah and practical preparedness against potential threats.

translation: And when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, or [lying] on your sides. But when you become secure, re-establish [regular] prayer. Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times.
interpretation: This verse underscores the obligation of remembering Allah in all states and positions, emphasizing the constant connection between a believer and their Creator. It also highlights the structured nature of worship, reminding Muslims that prayer is not just a ritual but a disciplined act of devotion with prescribed times, reinforcing the importance of regularity and mindfulness in their spiritual practice.

translation: And do not weaken in pursuit of the enemy. If you are suffering, they too are suffering just as you are suffering, but you have hope from Allah that which they do not have. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse encourages perseverance in the face of hardship during struggle or conflict, reminding believers that their suffering is not unique and that their ultimate hope lies in divine reward and justice, which their adversaries lack.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth that you may judge between the people by that which Allah has shown you, and do not be a supporter of the deceitful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of justice and impartiality in judgment, emphasizing that decisions should be based solely on divine guidance rather than personal biases or alliances, even when dealing with those who may be deceitful or untrustworthy.

translation: And seek forgiveness from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to constantly seek Allah's forgiveness, reminding them of His boundless mercy and willingness to pardon, which should inspire hope and motivate repentance.

translation: And do not argue on behalf of those who deceive themselves. Indeed, Allah does not like whoever is deceitful, sinful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of justice and integrity, warning against defending those who persistently deceive themselves and others, as such behavior is abhorrent to Allah and contradicts the principles of righteousness.

translation: They seek to hide (their deeds) from men, but they cannot hide (them) from Allah, for He is with them (by His Knowledge) when they plot by night, in words that He does not approve. And Allah is Ever All Encompassing (of what they do).
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of trying to conceal one's wrongdoings from Allah, as He is fully aware of all actions, even those committed in secrecy. It serves as a reminder of divine omniscience and the inevitability of facing accountability for one's deeds, regardless of attempts to hide them from others.

translation: Here you are—you have argued about them in the life of this world. But who will argue for them with Allah on the Day of Resurrection? Or who will be their protector?
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of human advocacy for others in the sight of Allah on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that no intercession or protection will avail unless it is granted by Allah Himself, highlighting the absolute sovereignty and justice of Allah in judgment.

translation: But whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy of Allah, highlighting that sincere repentance and seeking forgiveness can erase even grave sins, as long as one turns to Allah with a genuine heart and does not persist in wrongdoing.

translation: And whoever earns sin, then indeed, he earns it only against himself. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the personal accountability of one's actions, emphasizing that sinful deeds ultimately harm the doer alone, with no burden falling on Allah or others, while also affirming Allah's perfect knowledge of all deeds and His ultimate wisdom in judgment.

translation: And whoever earns a sin or a crime and then casts it upon an innocent person, has indeed burdened himself with slander and a manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of falsely accusing an innocent person, highlighting that such an act is not only unjust but also a grave sin that tarnishes the accuser's own soul with both slander and manifest wrongdoing.

translation: And if it were not for the favor of Allah upon you, [O Muhammad], and His mercy, a group of them would have determined to mislead you. But they do not mislead except themselves, and they will not harm you at all. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom and has taught you that which you did not know. And ever has the favor of Allah upon you been great.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine protection and guidance granted to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) despite the efforts of some to mislead him. It highlights that any attempt to deviate from the truth ultimately harms only the perpetrators themselves, not the Prophet or his mission. Additionally, it emphasizes the immense blessings of Allah in revealing the Qur'an, wisdom, and knowledge to the Prophet, which were beyond his prior understanding, reinforcing the idea of Allah's boundless grace and favor.

translation: There is no good in most of their secret counsels, except [in the case of] one who enjoins charity, or what is right, or setting things right between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah, We shall soon give him a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of righteous actions that benefit others and are done purely for the sake of Allah. It distinguishes between idle or harmful secret talks and those that serve a higher moral or social purpose, such as charity, promoting good, or reconciling disputes. The emphasis is on the sincerity of intention (seeking Allah's pleasure) and the reward that follows such actions, underscoring the value of selfless deeds in Islam.

translation: And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers—We will give him what he has taken and drive him into Hell, and how wretched is that destination.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences of defying the Prophet's guidance after it has been clearly established, emphasizing that such defiance leads to divine retribution and a wretched end, while also implicitly warning against deviating from the consensus of the believers.

translation: Indeed, Allah does not forgive associating others with Him [shirk], but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of shirk (associating partners with Allah) as the one unforgivable sin, while emphasizing Allah's boundless mercy in forgiving lesser sins for those He wills. It serves as a stark warning against idolatry or any form of associating others with Allah in worship or divinity, highlighting the severe deviation and loss incurred by those who commit shirk.

translation: They invoke instead of Him none but female [deities], and they invoke not except a rebellious Satan.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and misguidance of associating partners with Allah, as those who do so are not only worshipping false deities (often depicted as female in pre-Islamic Arabian polytheism) but are also unknowingly invoking a rebellious and deceitful force—Satan—who leads them astray from the truth.

translation: Allah has cursed him, and said, 'I will surely take from among Your servants a fixed portion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering resolve of Iblis (Satan) to mislead and corrupt a specific portion of humanity, whom he will claim as his followers, despite Allah's curse upon him.

translation: I will surely mislead them, and I will surely arouse in them [sinful] desires, and I will surely command them so they will slit the ears of cattle, and I will surely command them so they will change the creation of Allah. And whoever takes Satan as an ally instead of Allah has certainly sustained a clear loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive tactics of Satan, who seeks to lead people astray by distorting their desires and commanding them to commit acts that defy divine creation, such as mutilating animals or altering Allah’s natural design. It underscores the severe spiritual loss of those who ally themselves with Satan over Allah, emphasizing the importance of rejecting such influences to preserve faith and moral integrity.

translation: He [Satan] promises them and gives them false hopes, yet Satan's promise is nothing but delusion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan's promises and hopes, which are ultimately empty and misleading, designed to lead people astray from the path of truth and righteousness.

translation: For them, their refuge will be Hell, and they will not find any way to escape it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality and inescapability of divine punishment for those who persist in unbelief or wrongdoing, emphasizing that Hell is their inevitable destination with no possibility of evasion.

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. [It is] the promise of Allah [which is] true, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of Allah's promise to the believers who combine faith with righteous actions, guaranteeing them eternal residence in Paradise, highlighting the absolute truthfulness of Allah's word as the ultimate standard of honesty.

translation: It is not by your wishes, nor the wishes of the People of the Book. Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it, and he will not find besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of Allah’s judgment, emphasizing that salvation is not attained through mere desires or claims of faith, but through righteous deeds and accountability for one’s actions. It rejects any notion of favoritism or exemption based on lineage or affiliation, affirming that divine justice is impartial and that no intermediary can shield a person from the consequences of their wrongdoing.

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer—those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, [even as much as] the speck on a date seed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of Allah in rewarding deeds, emphasizing that gender does not diminish the value of righteous actions, and that even the smallest good deed will be justly compensated in the Hereafter.

translation: And who is better in religion than one who submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Ibrahim, inclining toward truth? And Allah took Ibrahim as an intimate friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the pinnacle of true faith and submission to Allah, emphasizing that the best religion is one where a person fully surrenders to Allah, lives righteously, and adheres to the pure monotheistic path of Prophet Ibrahim (AS), who was so beloved to Allah that He chose him as a close friend (Khalil). It underscores that true excellence in faith is marked by sincere devotion, moral excellence, and unwavering adherence to the truth.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is ever, over all things, encompassing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute ownership and sovereignty over all creation, asserting that nothing in the heavens or the earth exists independently of Him. The mention of Allah's encompassing knowledge ('محيطا') underscores His all-encompassing awareness and control over every aspect of existence, leaving no space or entity outside His dominion or beyond His knowledge.

translation: And they ask you [O Muhammad] about women. Say, "Allah instructs you concerning them, and [He does so] in the Book about the orphan girls to whom you do not give what was written for them [in their dowries] while you desire to marry them, and [concerning] the oppressed among children, and that you maintain justice for orphans. And whatever you do of good - indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of it."
interpretation: This verse addresses the ethical and legal responsibilities toward orphans and vulnerable individuals, particularly women and children, emphasizing justice, fairness, and the fulfillment of rights as ordained by Allah, while also highlighting the importance of acting righteously in all matters, as Allah is fully aware of all deeds.

translation: And if a woman fears from her husband either contempt (nushūz) or evasion (i‘rāḍ), there is no blame upon them if they make terms of reconciliation between them—and reconciliation is best. And present is the soul’s stinginess (shuḥḥ). But if you do good and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of reconciliation in marital disputes, emphasizing that compromise and mutual understanding are preferable to discord, even when one party's behavior is driven by selfishness or resentment.

translation: And you will never be able to be equitable between wives, even if you should strive [to do so]. So do not incline completely [toward one] and leave another suspended. And if you amend [your affairs] and fear Allah, then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inherent human limitation in achieving perfect justice between multiple wives, emphasizing that absolute fairness is unattainable despite sincere efforts. It cautions against extreme partiality, which could leave a wife in a state of emotional neglect, likening her to one suspended in limbo. The verse encourages reconciliation and piety, reminding that Allah’s forgiveness and mercy are available to those who strive to balance their affairs and maintain righteousness.

translation: And if they separate, Allah will enrich each from His abundance. And ever is Allah All-Encompassing [of all things], All-Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's boundless provision and wisdom, assuring that He will sustain both parties involved in a separation (such as divorce) according to His vast resources and perfect judgment, without leaving either in deprivation.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And We have certainly enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you and [upon] you that you fear Allah. But if you disbelieve, then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that everything in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him alone. It also highlights the continuity of the divine command to all who received scriptures before the Qur'an and to the Muslims, to fear and obey Allah. The verse serves as a reminder that disbelief does not diminish Allah's dominion, as He is free from any need and is inherently praiseworthy, regardless of human actions.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and control of Allah over all creation, asserting that nothing in the heavens or earth exists outside His dominion. The mention of Allah being 'sufficient as a Disposer of affairs' reassures believers that they need not rely on any other power or authority, as Allah alone governs all matters with perfect wisdom and justice.

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you, O people, and bring others [in your place]. And ever is Allah competent over that.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty over creation, emphasizing that human existence is entirely dependent on His will. It serves as a reminder of human humility and the transient nature of worldly life, cautioning against arrogance or complacency, as Allah can replace any people with others if He wills, demonstrating His ultimate power and justice.

translation: Whoever desires the reward of this world - then with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true and complete reward, whether in this world or the Hereafter, belongs to Allah alone, and He is fully aware of all intentions and deeds, rewarding accordingly.

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute necessity of justice, even in the face of personal biases or animosity, and emphasizes that fairness should transcend familial or material considerations, as God is the ultimate Owner of all.

translation: O you who have believed, believe in Allah, His Messenger, the Book that He sent down to His Messenger, and the Scripture which He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day has certainly gone far astray.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unwavering faith in all aspects of divine revelation, including the unity of Allah, the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him), and the authenticity of all revealed scriptures, while warning against selective belief or outright rejection of any fundamental tenet of faith, as such rejection leads to profound deviation from the truth.

translation: Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, and then increased in disbelief—Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a [right] way.
interpretation: This verse addresses the severe consequences of oscillating between faith and disbelief, highlighting that persistent and increasing rejection of truth after acknowledging it leads to a state where divine forgiveness and guidance are withheld, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness in faith.

translation: Give tidings to the hypocrites that there awaits them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who outwardly profess faith but harbor disbelief or insincerity in their hearts, emphasizing that their hidden hypocrisy will not escape divine justice.

translation: Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers—do they seek honor from them? But honor belongs entirely to Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of seeking validation or protection from those who reject faith, as true honor and strength come solely from Allah, not from alliances with the disbelieving.

translation: And it has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], in the Book that when you hear the verses of Allah (recited), they are denied (by the disbelievers) and ridiculed, so do not sit with them until they enter into some other discourse. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, Allah will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of not engaging in or giving tacit approval to mockery or denial of divine revelations, even if done by others in one's presence. It warns against associating with those who disrespect sacred matters, as passive participation can imply complicity. The verse also serves as a reminder that Allah will ultimately hold all those who reject faith and hypocritically undermine divine truth accountable in the Hereafter.

translation: Those who wait and watch for your misfortune: if a victory comes to you from Allah, they say, 'Were we not with you?' But if a share belongs to the disbelievers, they say, 'Did we not gain dominance over you and prevent you from the believers?' Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection. And Allah will never give the disbelievers any way [of dominance] over the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to support the believers but abandon them or even oppose them when circumstances shift, revealing their true loyalty lies with their own interests rather than faith. It underscores Allah’s ultimate justice, where He will distinguish between truth and falsehood on the Day of Judgment, ensuring that the believers are never subjected to the dominance of the disbelievers in the long term.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites try to deceive Allah, but it is He Who deceives them. And when they stand for prayer, they stand lazily, showing off to people and not remembering Allah except a little.
interpretation: This verse exposes the hypocrites' false piety, revealing that their outward acts of worship are tainted by insincerity and self-deception, as Allah ultimately sees through their hidden intentions and exposes their true nature.

translation: Wavering between this and that, belonging neither to these [believers] nor to those [disbelievers]. And whoever Allah sends astray - for him you will never find a way [of guidance].
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual peril of indecision and moral ambiguity in matters of faith, where one neither fully commits to truth nor rejects falsehood. It underscores that divine guidance is a gift, and when Allah deprives a person of this guidance, no human effort can restore it, emphasizing the importance of sincere conviction and steadfastness in the path of righteousness.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the disbelievers as allies [or protectors] instead of the believers. Do you wish to give Allah against yourselves a clear case?
interpretation: This verse warns against forming alliances or close relationships with those who reject faith, emphasizing the importance of loyalty and trust among believers. It challenges the hypocritical or opportunistic inclination to seek support from non-believers at the expense of the Muslim community, highlighting the moral and spiritual consequences of such actions.

translation: Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depths of the Fire, and you will never find for them a helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe punishment awaiting hypocrites who outwardly profess faith but inwardly conceal disbelief or insincerity, emphasizing the gravity of their deception in the sight of Allah.

translation: Except for those who repented, corrected themselves, held fast to Allah, and devoted their religion sincerely to Him—it is they who are with the believers. And Allah will soon give the believers a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transformative power of sincere repentance and righteous action, emphasizing that true faith is not static but requires ongoing commitment to Allah, moral rectitude, and exclusive devotion to Him, ensuring that such individuals are counted among the righteous believers and will ultimately receive Allah's immense reward.

translation: What can Allah gain by punishing you if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is Ever Appreciative and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent justice and mercy of Allah, emphasizing that true gratitude and faith diminish any reason for punishment, as Allah is fully aware of sincerity and rewards it abundantly.

translation: Allah does not like the public mention of evil except by someone who has been wronged. And Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of justice and moderation in speech, even when addressing wrongdoing. It permits speaking out against oppression but emphasizes that such speech should be measured and purposeful, not excessive or vengeful, reflecting Allah's attributes of hearing and knowing all things.

translation: Whether you reveal a good deed or conceal it, or pardon an evil, indeed Allah is Pardoning and Capable.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the virtue of forgiveness and the concealment of good deeds, highlighting Allah's attributes of being Pardoning (Al-'Afuww) and Capable (Qadeer). It encourages believers to adopt a forgiving attitude, even when they have the power to retaliate, and to perform good deeds sincerely, whether publicly or privately, trusting in Allah's recognition and reward.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and wish to discriminate between Allah and His messengers and say, "We believe in some and disbelieve in others," and desire to take a way in between—
interpretation: This verse condemns hypocrisy and partial belief, emphasizing that true faith requires complete acceptance of Allah and all His messengers without discrimination or selective belief, as such an approach is a deviation from true monotheism and leads to spiritual hypocrisy.

translation: It is they who are truly disbelievers. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of true disbelief (kufr) in the sight of Allah, emphasizing that those who reject faith with full knowledge and conviction are the ones who are truly disbelievers. The mention of a 'humiliating punishment' suggests that their rejection is not merely a matter of differing belief but an active and willful opposition to divine truth, which will be met with severe and disgraceful consequences in the Hereafter.

translation: And those who believe in Allah and His messengers and do not discriminate between any of them - to those He will give their rewards. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of believing in all of Allah's messengers without discrimination, highlighting the unity of their message and the necessity of accepting them all as part of the same divine truth.

translation: The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from the heavens. Indeed, they had asked Moses [for] something greater, saying, "Show us Allah outright," so the thunderbolt seized them for their wrongdoing. Then they took the calf [for worship] after clear proofs had come to them, but We pardoned that, and We gave Moses a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse highlights the perpetual skepticism of the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) and their refusal to accept divine guidance without demanding extraordinary proofs, despite having witnessed miracles. It serves as a warning against the dangers of arrogance and the rejection of truth, even when clear signs are presented, as seen in the punishment of those who demanded to see Allah directly and the subsequent idolatry of the calf. The verse also underscores Allah's mercy in pardoning past transgressions while granting clear authority to His messengers as a means of guidance.

translation: And We raised over them the mount for their covenant, and We said to them, 'Enter the gate prostrating,' and We said to them, 'Do not transgress on the Sabbath.' And We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of divine tests and the consequences of failing to uphold one's covenant with Allah. The 'mount raised over them' symbolizes the overwhelming burden of their test, while the command to 'enter the gate prostrating' signifies submission and humility before Allah's commands. The prohibition against transgressing on the Sabbath underscores the importance of adhering to divine laws, and the 'solemn covenant' taken from them emphasizes the gravity of their commitment and the accountability that follows its violation.

translation: But because of their breaking their covenant and their disbelief in the signs of Allah and their killing of the prophets without right and their saying, "Our hearts are wrapped." Rather, Allah has sealed them because of their disbelief, so they do not believe except for a few.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of persistent disbelief and rejection of divine guidance, emphasizing that such attitudes lead to a hardening of the heart, making true faith inaccessible except for those whom Allah guides.

translation: And [for] their disbelief and their saying against Mary a great slander.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of false accusations and the seriousness of defaming an innocent person, particularly in matters of faith and morality.

translation: And [for] their saying, "Indeed, we have killed the Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah." And they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; but [another] was made to resemble him to them. And indeed, those who differ over it are in doubt about it. They have no knowledge of it except the following of assumption. And they did not kill him, for certain.
interpretation: This verse refutes the claim that Jesus (peace be upon him) was crucified and killed, clarifying that Allah protected him from such an end and that the crucifixion was a misperception or a deception by Allah to those who sought to harm him.

translation: Rather, Allah raised him (Jesus) to Himself. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse affirms the divine elevation of Jesus (peace be upon him) to Allah’s presence, rejecting the Christian doctrine of crucifixion while emphasizing Allah’s absolute power and wisdom in determining the fate of His messengers.

translation: And there is none from the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection, he will be a witness against them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of recognizing the truth of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) before their death, either in this life or at the moment of death, as a final testimony to the truth of Islam. It also signifies that Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) will bear witness for or against them on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the accountability of their beliefs and actions.

translation: And for the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been lawful for them [before], and for their averting from the way of Allah many [people],
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of unjust actions and deliberate obstruction of divine guidance, suggesting that moral transgressions and willful deviation from truth can lead to spiritual deprivation and loss of blessings, even when such blessings were previously accessible.

translation: And [for] their taking of usury while they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of the people's wealth unjustly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of transgressing divine prohibitions, specifically the prohibition of usury (riba) and unjustly consuming others' wealth. It highlights the severe consequences awaiting those who persist in such wrongdoing despite clear divine guidance, emphasizing that such actions are not merely social or economic violations but grave moral and spiritual offenses with dire eternal repercussions.

translation: But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], and what was revealed before you. And [particularly] the establishers of prayer and the givers of zakah and [also] the believers in Allah and the Last Day - those We will give a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unwavering faith in all revealed scriptures, not just the Qur'an, and highlights the virtues of those who consistently uphold their religious duties (prayer and charity) and maintain strong belief in the divine and the Hereafter, promising them a magnificent reward as a testament to their steadfastness and piety.

translation: Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Descendants [of Jacob], Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and to David We gave the book [of Psalms].
interpretation: This verse underscores the continuity and unity of divine revelation across all prophets, affirming that the message of Islam is not new but a restoration of the same monotheistic truth preached by all previous messengers, culminating in the finality of prophethood with Muhammad (peace be upon him).

translation: And [We sent] messengers We have mentioned to you, [O Muhammad], before, and messengers We have not mentioned to you. And Allah spoke to Moses with [direct] speech.
interpretation: This verse underscores the comprehensiveness of divine revelation, highlighting that God has sent messengers to various communities throughout history, some of whose stories are known to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and others whose accounts are not recounted in the Qur'an. It also emphasizes the unique and direct communication between God and Moses (peace be upon him), illustrating the special status of certain prophets in divine communication.

translation: Messengers as bearers of good news and as warners, so that mankind will have no excuse before Allah after the messengers. And ever is Allah Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom behind sending messengers to humanity: to provide clear guidance and eliminate any grounds for ignorance or denial as an excuse before Allah on the Day of Judgment. It highlights Allah's justice in ensuring that no one can claim they were unaware of the truth, while also affirming His absolute power and perfect wisdom in His actions and decrees.

translation: But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you—He sent it down with His knowledge—and the angels bear witness. And sufficient is Allah as Witness.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute certainty and divine origin of the revelation (Qur'an) granted to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), affirming that Allah's testimony, along with that of the angels, validates its authenticity and truthfulness, leaving no room for doubt about its divine source.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [others] from the path of Allah - they have strayed far, far away.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of disbelief and obstruction of the path of truth, emphasizing that such actions lead to profound spiritual deviation and distance from divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged—Allah would never forgive them, nor would He guide them to any path.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of Allah’s decree regarding those who persist in disbelief and oppression, emphasizing that their fate is sealed by their own choices, leaving no room for divine mercy or guidance.

translation: Except the path of Hell; they will abide therein forever. And that, for Allah, is [not] difficult.
interpretation: This verse underscores the irreversible and eternal nature of the punishment for those who reject faith, emphasizing that divine justice is absolute and within Allah's power, reflecting the gravity of straying from the righteous path.

translation: O mankind, the Messenger has come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. But if you disbelieve, then to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the universal call to faith in the message brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), emphasizing that belief is the path to true benefit, while disbelief does not diminish Allah's sovereignty or knowledge, as all existence belongs to Him.

translation: O People of the Book, do not exceed the limits in your religion beyond the truth, and do not say about Allah except the truth. The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, is only a messenger of Allah and His word which He conveyed to Mary and a soul from Him. So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say, 'Three.' Stop it; it is better for you. Allah is only One God. Exalted is He above having a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth. And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and rejects any form of exaggeration or falsehood in matters of faith, particularly the Christian doctrine of the Trinity. It affirms the prophethood of Jesus (Isa) as a messenger of Allah, emphasizing his creation through the word of Allah ('Be') and a spirit from Him, while firmly denying any notion of divinity or partnership in worship. The verse serves as a call to monotheism and a warning against associating partners with Allah, highlighting the consequences of such beliefs and the importance of adhering strictly to the truth.

translation: The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels brought near [to Him]. And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant - He will gather them all to Himself.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute submission of all beings to Allah, including Jesus (peace be upon him) and the angels closest to Allah. It highlights that true honor lies in servitude to Allah, and arrogance in rejecting this servitude will lead to divine accountability, as all will ultimately return to Him for judgment.

translation: As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will fully reward them and give them increase out of His bounty. But as for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine principle of justice and mercy, where righteous believers are rewarded abundantly, reflecting God's generosity beyond mere justice, while the arrogant and disdainful face severe punishment, underscoring the absolute sovereignty and justice of Allah without any intermediary to intercede on their behalf.

translation: O mankind, there has come to you a proof from your Lord and We have sent down to you a clear light.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine guidance and clarity provided to humanity through the revelation of the Qur'an, which serves as both a proof of truth and a guiding light out of ignorance and misguidance.

translation: As for those who believe in Allah and hold fast to Him, He will admit them into His mercy and grace, and guide them to Himself on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the reward for true faith and steadfastness in belief, emphasizing that Allah's mercy and guidance are the ultimate outcomes for those who sincerely hold onto Him, leading them to a direct and unobstructed path to Him.

translation: They ask you for a ruling. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning one having neither descendants nor ascendants [as heirs]. If a man dies leaving no children but has a sister, she shall have half of what he leaves. And he is her heir if she has no children. If there are two sisters, they shall have two-thirds of what he leaves. If the siblings are male and female, the male shall have the share of two females." Allah makes clear for you [His law], lest you go astray. And Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Islamic inheritance laws to ensure fair distribution of wealth among heirs, emphasizing the principle of justice where male heirs receive twice the share of female heirs due to their financial responsibilities in Islam. It also highlights Allah’s mercy in providing clear guidance to prevent confusion or injustice in matters of inheritance.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. O you who have believed, fulfill [all] contracts. Lawful for you is the grazing livestock except what is recited to you [as unlawful], so do not violate the rites of Allah while you are in the state of ihram. Indeed, Allah ordains what He intends.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling commitments and contracts, highlighting that Allah's laws are absolute and must be respected, especially during sacred rites like the state of ihram (a state of consecration during Hajj or Umrah). It underscores the balance between divine commandments and human actions, reminding believers that Allah's will governs all matters, and His rulings are not subject to personal interpretation or circumvention.

translation: O you who have believed, do not violate the symbols of Allah or [the sanctity of] the sacred month or [neglect the offering of] the sacrificial animals or the garlands [marking them], nor those coming to the Sacred House seeking bounty from their Lord and [His] approval. But when you come out of ihram, then [you may] hunt. And do not let the hatred of a people who obstructed you from al-Masjid al-Haram lead you to transgress. And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sanctity of religious rites and the importance of maintaining moral boundaries even in times of conflict, emphasizing that personal grievances should not justify transgression or retaliation beyond justice.

translation: Prohibited to you are dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah, and [those animals] killed by strangling or by a violent blow or by a head-long fall or by the goring of horns, and those from which a wild animal has eaten, except what you [are able to] slaughter [before its death]; and [prohibited is] what has been slaughtered on stone altars, and [prohibited is] that you seek decision through divining arrows. That is grave disobedience. This day those who disbelieve have despaired of [defeating] your religion; so fear them not, but fear Me. This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you and have approved for you Islam as religion. But whoever is forced by severe hunger with no inclination to sin - then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the completion of Islam as a comprehensive way of life, marking a pivotal moment in the establishment of divine guidance. It signifies the finality of the religion, eliminating any doubt about its authenticity and sufficiency, while also emphasizing the importance of adhering to its laws without compromise. The permission granted in cases of necessity reflects Allah's mercy and understanding of human frailty, ensuring that His laws remain practical and humane even in extreme circumstances.

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], what has been made lawful for them. Say, "Lawful for you are [all] good and pure foods, and [game caught by] what you have trained of hunting animals which you train as Allah has taught you. So eat of what they catch for you, and mention the name of Allah upon it, and fear Allah." Indeed, Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permissibility of consuming lawful and wholesome foods, including meat obtained through lawful hunting with trained animals, provided that the name of Allah is invoked over it, ensuring gratitude and mindfulness of divine commandments.

translation: Today all good and pure foods have been made lawful for you. The food of the People of the Book is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them. Also lawful for you are chaste women from the believers and chaste women from those who were given the Book before you, provided you give them their dowries, desiring chastity, not lustfully or as secret lovers. Whoever rejects faith, his deeds will come to nothing, and in the Hereafter he will be among the losers.
interpretation: This verse establishes permissibility and mutual recognition of dietary and marital laws between Muslims and the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), reflecting a principle of shared ethical and legal foundations in matters of sustenance and relationships. It emphasizes the importance of chastity and lawful conduct in marriage, while warning against disbelief, which nullifies good deeds and leads to loss in the Hereafter.

translation: O you who have believed, when you rise to [perform] prayer, wash your faces and your forearms to the elbows and wipe over your heads and wash your feet to the ankles. And if you are in a state of janabah, then purify yourselves. But if you are ill or on a journey or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself or you have contacted women and do not find water, then seek clean earth and wipe over your faces and hands with it. Allah does not intend to make difficulty for you, but He intends to purify you and complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of spiritual and physical purification (Taharah) as a prerequisite for the act of prayer, emphasizing that such rituals are not meant to burden believers but to elevate their spiritual state and foster gratitude towards Allah.

translation: And remember the favor of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, 'We hear and we obey.' And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude for Allah's blessings and the significance of fulfilling one's covenants with Him, as exemplified by the initial pledge of the believers. It also serves as a reminder of Allah's omniscience, encouraging believers to maintain sincerity and mindfulness of their intentions and actions.

translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice and fairness, even in the face of personal animosity or bias. It instructs believers to uphold justice purely for the sake of Allah, without allowing hatred or ill-will toward others to influence their actions, as true justice is a fundamental aspect of righteousness and piety.

translation: Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds [that] for them there is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine principle that true faith must be accompanied by righteous actions, and that Allah’s promise of forgiveness and immense reward is contingent upon this combination, reflecting the balance between divine grace and human responsibility.

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs—those are the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequence of rejecting faith and the truth of divine revelation, emphasizing that persistent denial of God's signs leads to eternal punishment in Hell, highlighting the gravity of disbelief and the importance of recognizing divine guidance.

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when a people determined to extend against you [their] hands, but He withheld their hands from you. And fear Allah; and upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of gratitude for divine protection and the necessity of placing trust in Allah, especially in times of potential harm or adversity.

translation: And Allah had already taken a covenant from the Children of Israel, and We raised among them twelve leaders. And Allah said, 'I am with you. If you establish prayer, give zakah, believe in My messengers, support them, and lend Allah a goodly loan, I will surely remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But whoever among you disbelieves after that - he has certainly strayed from the soundness of the way.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of steadfast commitment to faith and righteous deeds, highlighting that divine reward is contingent upon fulfilling obligations such as prayer, charity, and support for God's messengers, while warning against apostasy as a deviation from the path of truth.

translation: But because of their breaking of their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their [proper] places and have forgotten a portion of that with which they were reminded. And you will still observe deceit from them, except a few of them. But pardon them and overlook [their misdeeds]. Indeed, Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of breaking divine covenants and the moral decay that follows, such as hardness of heart and distortion of truth. It also emphasizes the importance of forgiveness and overlooking faults, reflecting Allah's mercy toward those who strive to do good, even when faced with persistent deceit from others.

translation: And from those who say, "We are Christians," We took their covenant; then they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. So We caused among them animosity and hatred until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah is going to inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of breaking divine covenants and neglecting divine reminders, leading to internal strife and conflict among those who claim to follow a faith but deviate from its true teachings.

translation: O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, revealing to you much of what you used to conceal of the Scripture, and overlooking much. There has come to you from Allah a light and a clear Book.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in clarifying truths from the previously revealed scriptures that had been distorted or concealed by some among the People of the Book (Jews and Christians). It also emphasizes Allah's mercy in overlooking certain matters while establishing the Quran as a clear and illuminating guidance, surpassing the earlier revelations in its clarity and preservation.

translation: Allah guides by it (the Qur'an) those who follow His pleasure to the ways of peace and brings them out from darknesses into the light, by His permission, and guides them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Qur'an's role as a divine guide that leads those who seek Allah's pleasure away from confusion and misguidance toward clarity, righteousness, and the path of peace, emphasizing that true guidance is only possible through Allah's will and mercy.

translation: Indeed, they have disbelieved those who say, "Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary." Say, "Then who could prevent Allah at all if He had intended to destroy the Messiah, son of Mary, and his mother, and everyone on earth entirely?" And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them. He creates what He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse refutes the Christian belief in the divinity of Jesus (Isa) by highlighting the absolute sovereignty of Allah, who alone possesses the power to create, sustain, and destroy all existence. It underscores the futility of attributing divine attributes to any created being, including Jesus and his mother, as Allah's will is supreme and unchallenged.

translation: The Jews and the Christians say, "We are the children of Allah and His beloved ones." Say, "Then why does He punish you for your sins? Rather, you are human beings from among those He has created. He forgives whom He wills and punishes whom He wills. And to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and to Him is the [final] destination."
interpretation: This verse refutes the exclusivist claims of the Jews and Christians that they are uniquely favored by Allah, emphasizing that all humans are equal in their creation and subject to Allah's will in matters of forgiveness and punishment, highlighting the absolute sovereignty and justice of Allah over all creation.

translation: O People of the Book, Our Messenger has come to you, clarifying for you after a pause between messengers, lest you say, 'There has come to us no bringer of good tidings or warner.' But there has come to you a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the continuity of divine guidance through messengers, emphasizing that Allah’s mercy is constant, even if there is a temporal gap between prophets. It refutes any excuse of ignorance or lack of warning, as the final messenger (Muhammad ﷺ) has been sent with clear guidance, fulfilling the role of both a bearer of glad tidings (for the righteous) and a warner (against wrongdoing). The mention of Allah’s omnipotence reinforces the certainty of His decrees and the inevitability of accountability.

translation: And [remember] when Moses said to his people, "O my people, remember the favor of Allah upon you when He appointed among you prophets and made you possessors of power and gave you that which He had not given to any other of the worlds."
