interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude and reflection on divine blessings, emphasizing that true leadership and distinction come from moral and spiritual guidance rather than mere temporal power.

translation: O my people, enter the Holy Land which Allah has assigned for you and do not turn back [from it], becoming losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and trust in divine decrees, warning against abandoning a righteous path or opportunity out of fear or hesitation, as it would lead to loss and regret.

translation: They said, "O Moses, indeed within it are a tyrannical people, and indeed, we will never enter it until they leave it. So if they leave it, then we will enter."
interpretation: This verse reflects the initial hesitation and fear of the Israelites in confronting a powerful and oppressive enemy, highlighting their reluctance to engage in a struggle they perceived as beyond their strength, which ultimately required divine reassurance and guidance to overcome.

translation: Two men of those who feared [the punishment of Allah but to whom Allah had granted favour] said, 'Assault them at the gate; for when you are inside the gate, you will be victorious. So put your trust in Allah if you are believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust in Allah (tawakkul) even in the face of seemingly insurmountable challenges. It demonstrates that true faith requires action coupled with reliance on divine support, rather than passive resignation or fear.

translation: They said, "O Moses, indeed we will never enter it, while they are within it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight. Indeed, we are remaining right here."
interpretation: This verse highlights the extreme reluctance and lack of faith of some of the Israelites, who refused to obey Allah's command to enter the promised land out of fear of the enemy, despite the presence of divine support. Their stance reflects a deeper spiritual weakness—prioritizing worldly fear over trust in Allah's promise and the leadership of His messenger.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed I possess no control except over myself and my brother, so separate us from the wicked people.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the limits of human agency and the necessity of divine intervention in matters beyond one's control, emphasizing reliance on God's justice and wisdom in separating the righteous from the corrupt.

translation: So indeed, it is forbidden for them (the disbelieving generation) to enter the Holy Land for forty years, during which they will wander aimlessly throughout the land. So do not grieve over the defiantly disobedient people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of persistent disobedience and defiance against divine commandments, illustrating that such actions lead to prolonged hardship and estrangement from spiritual or moral guidance, as seen in the wandering of the Israelites for forty years due to their refusal to enter the Holy Land as commanded.

translation: And recite to them the story of the two sons of Adam, in truth, when they both offered a sacrifice [to Allah], and it was accepted from one of them but was not accepted from the other. [The latter] said, "I will surely kill you." [The former] said, "Indeed, Allah only accepts from the righteous [who fear Him]."
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of sincerity and piety in worship, highlighting that acceptance by Allah is not based on the outward form of an action but on the state of the heart. It also serves as a warning against envy and the destructive consequences of unchecked anger, as the rejected sacrifice led to the first murder in human history, illustrating how spiritual deficiency can manifest in moral corruption.

translation: If you should raise your hand against me to kill me, I shall not raise my hand against you to kill you. Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of restraint and the fear of Allah in the face of aggression, demonstrating that true strength lies in self-control and trust in divine justice rather than retaliating with violence.

translation: Indeed, I want you to bear my sin and your sin, so you will be among the companions of the Fire. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of bearing the burden of one's own sins and the sins of others through complicity or encouragement in wrongdoing, warning that such actions lead to severe punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: And his soul inclined him to kill his brother; so he killed him, and he became one of the losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive power of unchecked desires and the grave consequences of succumbing to them, even leading to the loss of one's humanity and eternal reward.

translation: Then Allah sent a crow searching in the ground, to show him how to hide the disgrace of his brother. He said, 'Woe to me! Am I unable to be like this crow and hide the disgrace of my brother?' And he became one of the regretful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of sin and the importance of repentance. The regretful state of the murderer after witnessing the crow bury its companion's body underscores the natural human response to wrongdoing—acknowledging one's faults and seeking to rectify them through remorse and change.

translation: Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul or for corruption [done] in the land - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And Our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, [even] after that, throughout the land, were transgressors.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sanctity of human life in Islam, elevating its preservation to a universal moral duty, regardless of race or creed. It condemns murder as an act that not only destroys an individual but also undermines the moral fabric of society, equating it to the destruction of humanity itself. Conversely, saving a life is framed as an act of profound moral significance, akin to saving all of humanity. The mention of 'corruption in the land' broadens the scope of prohibited violence to include not just physical harm but also societal destabilization through injustice or oppression. The verse also highlights the recurring rejection of divine guidance by many, despite clear signs, as a persistent human failing.

translation: Indeed, the recompense of those who wage war against Allah and His Messenger and strive upon earth [to cause] corruption is [either] that they be killed or crucified or that their hands and feet be cut off from opposite sides or that they be exiled from the land. That is for them a disgrace in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse outlines severe punishments for those who actively oppose Islam and its teachings, engage in violent rebellion against the Muslim community, or spread corruption in the land. The punishments—execution, crucifixion, amputation, or exile—serve as both a deterrent and a means of maintaining justice and order. The emphasis on 'corruption' (فسادا) suggests that the crimes involve not just physical harm but also moral and societal destabilization, such as undermining the rule of law or spreading injustice. The mention of disgrace in this world and a great punishment in the Hereafter underscores the gravity of such actions, framing them as transgressions against divine order.

translation: Except for those who repent before you overpower them. So know that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of repentance and Allah's boundless mercy, emphasizing that even those who have committed grave wrongs can find forgiveness if they sincerely repent before facing the consequences of their actions.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and seek the means [of nearness] to Him and strive in His cause that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of a holistic approach to faith, combining piety, active pursuit of closeness to Allah through righteous deeds, and striving in His path, highlighting that true success lies in this integrated practice.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved—if they had all that is on the earth, and the like of it with it, to ransom themselves from the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, it would not be accepted from them. And for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute futility of attempting to escape divine justice through material means. It highlights the inescapable reality of the Day of Judgment, where no amount of wealth or possessions—no matter how vast—can secure salvation for those who reject faith. The emphasis on the rejection of their ransom reveals the depth of their disbelief and the severity of their punishment, reinforcing the Qur'an's message that true redemption lies only in sincere faith and righteous action.

translation: They wish to get out of the Fire, but never will they get out therefrom; and theirs is an enduring torment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and irreversible nature of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief or wrongdoing, emphasizing that escape from the consequences of their actions is not possible, as divine justice is final and eternal.

translation: As for the thief, both male and female, cut off their hands as a recompense for what they have earned [as way of] deterrent punishment from Allah. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse prescribes a severe punishment for theft, not merely as retribution but as a deterrent measure to uphold societal justice and deter future crimes, reflecting the gravity of the offense in the eyes of divine law.

translation: But whoever repents after his wrongdoing and reforms, indeed, Allah will turn to him in forgiveness. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy of Allah, highlighting that sincere repentance and righteous reform can restore a person's spiritual state, regardless of the severity of their past sins.

translation: Do you not know that to Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth? He punishes whom He wills and forgives whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that His authority to punish or forgive is unchallenged and derived from His perfect wisdom and justice. It serves as a reminder of human dependence on Allah’s mercy while also warning against transgression, as His power is all-encompassing and His decrees are final.

translation: O Messenger! Let not those who hasten into disbelief grieve you—those who say, "We believe" with their mouths, but their hearts do not believe. And [also] from among the Jews are those who listen to falsehood, listening to other people who have not come to you. They distort words from their [proper] places, saying, "If you are given this, take it; but if you are not given it, then beware." And whoever Allah intends to put into trial, you will never possess [power] for him against Allah at all. Those are the ones whose hearts Allah does not intend to purify. For them in this world is disgrace, and for them in the Hereafter is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to remain steadfast in his mission despite the hypocrisy and deceit of those who outwardly claim faith but harbor disbelief in their hearts, as well as the Jews who distort the truth for their own gain. It highlights the futility of trying to sway those whom Allah has decreed to misguide, emphasizing that divine trial (fitnah) is beyond human control. The verse underscores the consequences of such behavior—disgrace in this life and severe punishment in the Hereafter—while affirming Allah’s sovereignty over hearts and destinies.

translation: They are listeners to falsehood, devourers of illicit gain. So if they come to you [O Muhammad], either judge between them or turn away from them. And if you turn away from them, they will not harm you at all. And if you judge, judge between them with justice. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding his dealings with hypocrites or those who spread falsehood and engage in corrupt practices. It instructs him to either judge fairly between disputing parties or to distance himself from them if their presence is harmful, emphasizing that their harm is limited and cannot truly affect him if he adheres to justice. The verse underscores the importance of justice ('Qist') and highlights that Allah loves those who uphold it, reinforcing the moral and ethical standard that must guide interactions with such individuals.

translation: But how do they come to you for judgment while they have the Torah, containing the judgment of Allah? Then they turn away, [even] after that. And those are not [in the least] believers.
interpretation: This verse critiques those who claim belief but reject Allah's commandments when it conflicts with their desires, highlighting the inconsistency between their professed faith and their actions.

translation: Indeed, We sent down the Torah, containing guidance and light. The prophets who submitted [to Allah] judged by it for the Jews, as did the rabbis and scholars by what they were entrusted to preserve of Allah's Book, and they were witnesses thereto. So do not fear the people but fear Me, and do not exchange My verses for a small price. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed—then it is those who are the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and purpose of the Torah as a source of guidance and light, entrusted to prophets, rabbis, and scholars for its preservation and application. It emphasizes the importance of adhering to Allah's commandments without compromise, warning against prioritizing worldly gain over divine truth. The verse also highlights the gravity of rejecting Allah's law, equating such rejection with disbelief.

translation: And We ordained for them therein: a life for a life, an eye for an eye, a nose for a nose, an ear for an ear, a tooth for a tooth, and for wounds equal retaliation. But whoever forgoes it as charity, it is an expiation for him. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed—then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse establishes the principle of *qisas* (just retaliation) as a form of justice in Islamic law, ensuring proportional punishment for harm inflicted. However, it also emphasizes the higher moral virtue of forgiveness and charity, where pardoning the offender serves as an expiation for the wrongdoer’s sins. The verse underscores that rejecting divine justice (by not adhering to Allah’s rulings) is an act of oppression, highlighting the importance of divine law in maintaining equity and righteousness.

translation: And We sent, following in their footsteps, Jesus, the son of Mary, confirming that which came before him of the Torah; and We gave him the Gospel, in which was guidance and light and confirming that which preceded it of the Torah as guidance and instruction for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the continuity of divine revelation, highlighting Jesus (peace be upon him) as a prophet who confirmed the Torah given to Moses (peace be upon him) while bringing the Gospel as a source of guidance, light, and moral instruction for the righteous, reinforcing the unbroken chain of monotheistic teachings.

translation: And the People of the Gospel should judge by what Allah revealed in it. And whoever does not judge by what Allah has revealed—it is they who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse underscores the obligation for followers of the Gospel (Christians) to adhere to the divine guidance revealed in their scripture, emphasizing that deviation from this guidance constitutes a form of rebellion against Allah's commandments.

translation: And We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, confirming that which preceded it of the Scripture and as a criterion over it. So judge between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their inclinations away from what has come to you of the truth. For each of you We have appointed a law and a method. Had Allah willed, He could have made you one nation [united in religion], but [He intended] to test you in what He has given you; so race to [all that is] good. To Allah is your return all together, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an as the final revelation, which confirms previous scriptures while serving as the ultimate criterion for judging between truth and falsehood. It commands adherence to Allah's revelation rather than human desires, emphasizing individual and communal responsibility to follow divine guidance. The diversity of laws and paths among nations is part of Allah's wisdom to test humanity, urging believers to strive for righteousness and unity in goodness, with the ultimate return to Allah for judgment and clarification of disputes.

translation: And judge, [O Muhammad], between them by what Allah has revealed and do not follow their desires while being wary of them lest they tempt you away from some of what Allah has revealed to you. And if they turn away - then know that Allah intends only to afflict them for some of their sins. And indeed, many of the people are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of adhering strictly to divine guidance in judgment and decision-making, resisting external pressures or temptations that may lead one astray from Allah's commands, while recognizing that rejection of divine law may result in consequences for those who persist in wrongdoing.

translation: Do they seek the judgment of the time of ignorance? But who is better than Allah in judgment for a people who are certain [in faith]?
interpretation: This verse critiques those who reject divine guidance in favor of human-made laws or pre-Islamic customs, emphasizing that true justice and wisdom can only be found in Allah’s decrees for those who have unwavering faith.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take the Jews and the Christians as allies. They are [in fact] allies of one another. And whoever is an ally to them among you - then indeed, he is [one] of them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against forming alliances with those who oppose or seek to undermine the faith and values of the Muslim community, particularly when such alliances could lead to compromising one's religious principles or loyalty to Islam.

translation: And you will see those in whose hearts is disease hastening to them, saying, "We fear lest a misfortune should strike us." But it may be that Allah will bring conquest or a command from Him, and they will become regretful over what they concealed within themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those whose faith is weak or insincere, as they outwardly express fear of misfortune while secretly harboring doubt or opposition to the truth. It underscores the inevitability of divine justice, where hidden intentions will ultimately be exposed, leading to regret when the truth becomes manifest.

translation: And those who believe say, "Are these the ones who swore by Allah their strongest oaths that indeed they were with you?" Their deeds have become worthless, so they have become losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who falsely claim to be believers while secretly opposing the truth, only to be exposed by their own false oaths. Their deeds are rendered futile because their faith was insincere, and their ultimate loss is a consequence of their deception and lack of true conviction.

translation: O you who have believed, whoever of you should revert from his religion - Allah will bring forth [in your place] a people He will love and who will love Him [who are] humble toward the believers, powerful against the disbelievers; they strive in the way of Allah and do not fear the blame of a critic. That is the favor of Allah; He grants it to whom He wills. And Allah is all-Encompassing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the constancy of divine guidance and the inevitability of Allah's plan, emphasizing that true faith is not merely inherited but must be actively chosen and upheld. It reassures believers that even if some falter, Allah will replace them with a people who embody unwavering devotion, courage in upholding truth, and resilience against opposition, reflecting the transformative power of sincere faith and divine favor.

translation: Indeed, your guardian is none but Allah, His Messenger, and the believers who establish prayer and give zakah while bowing [in worship].
interpretation: This verse highlights the exclusive authority of Allah, His Messenger (peace be upon him), and the true believers in guiding and protecting the Muslim community, with the believers' leadership exemplified by their unwavering devotion to prayer and charity, even in the midst of their acts of worship.

translation: And whoever takes Allah, His Messenger, and those who believe as allies - then indeed, the party of Allah will be the predominant ones.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate victory of those who align themselves with Allah, His Messenger, and the believers, emphasizing that divine support and guidance ensure triumph over adversity, regardless of worldly power or opposition.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take as allies those who took your religion in ridicule and amusement among the People of the Scripture before, nor the disbelievers. And fear Allah, if you should [truly] be believers.
interpretation: This verse cautions believers against forming alliances with those who mock or belittle their faith, whether they are from the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) or disbelievers, as such relationships can undermine the integrity and sincerity of one's faith.

translation: And when you call to prayer, they take it in ridicule and amusement. That is because they are a people who do not use reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of approaching acts of worship, such as prayer, with sincerity and reverence, rather than mockery or frivolity. It underscores the consequences of lacking understanding and reflection in matters of faith, as those who do so fail to grasp the true significance of worship and instead degrade it to mere entertainment.

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, do you resent us except [for the fact] that we have believed in Allah and what was revealed to us and what was revealed before, and that most of you are defiantly disobedient?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) call to the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) to recognize that their objection to Islam stems not from a rational or theological disagreement but from their own persistent disobedience to divine guidance, as evidenced by their deviation from earlier revelations.

translation: Say, 'Shall I inform you of [what is] worse than that as penalty from Allah? [It is of] those whom Allah has cursed and with whom He became angry and made of them apes and pigs and slaves of Taghut. Those are worse in position and further astray from the sound path.'
interpretation: This verse warns against the severe consequences of disbelief and moral corruption, illustrating that those who persist in such states incur Allah's curse, anger, and transformation into the lowest of creatures, symbolizing their spiritual degradation and deviation from the right path.

translation: And when they come to you, they say, 'We believe.' But they have entered with disbelief, and they have certainly left with it. And Allah knows what they were concealing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who outwardly profess faith but inwardly harbor disbelief, demonstrating that true faith must be sincere and not merely performative.

translation: And you see many of them hastening into sin and aggression and consuming [what is] unlawful. How wretched is what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who eagerly engage in sinful acts, oppression, and unjustly consuming forbidden wealth, highlighting the severity of their moral corruption and the consequences of their actions.

translation: If it were not for the fact that Allah would prevent them from doing so, the rabbis and scholars would have consumed the people's wealth through falsehood and prevented them from the way of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and ethical responsibility of religious leaders to guide their communities righteously. It condemns those who, despite their knowledge of divine laws, exploit their positions for personal gain or to obstruct the path of truth, emphasizing that such behavior is not only forbidden but also corrupts both the individual and society.

translation: The Jews say, "Allah's hand is tied up." Their hands are tied up and they are cursed for what they say. Rather, Allah's hands are spread out; He spends however He wills. And what has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. And We have cast enmity and hatred among them until the Day of Resurrection. Whenever they kindle the fire of war, Allah extinguishes it. And they strive throughout the earth [causing] corruption, and Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: This verse addresses the Jewish claim that Allah's power is limited, which reflects a misunderstanding of divine omnipotence. It emphasizes Allah's boundless generosity and sovereignty, contrasting their narrow perception with the reality of His absolute control over all affairs. The verse also highlights the consequences of their rejection and hostility toward divine guidance, leading to increased arrogance and disbelief. Additionally, it underscores the perpetual discord and conflict among them, as well as their futile attempts to incite chaos, which Allah ultimately thwarts. The message serves as a reminder of Allah's justice and the futility of opposing divine will.

translation: And if the People of the Book had believed and feared Allah, We would have removed their evil deeds from them and admitted them into Gardens of Pleasure.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of faith and righteousness, suggesting that true belief and piety can lead to divine forgiveness and ultimate reward, highlighting Allah's mercy and the transformative power of faith.

translation: And if they had upheld the Torah and the Gospel and what was revealed to them from their Lord, they would have eaten from above them and from beneath their feet. Among them is a moderate community, but many of them—what they do is evil.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of adhering to divine guidance—those who truly uphold the teachings of the Torah, Gospel, and the Qur'an would be blessed abundantly, both spiritually and materially. The mention of 'moderate community' refers to those who follow the balanced path of faith, while the majority's deviation leads to moral and spiritual corruption, highlighting the importance of steadfastness in divine commandments.

translation: O Messenger, convey that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed, Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute necessity for the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to convey the entirety of the divine revelation without omission, emphasizing that failure to do so would constitute a negation of his mission. It also reassures the Prophet of divine protection against any harm from people, while simultaneously highlighting the spiritual consequence that Allah does not guide those who persistently reject faith.

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, you are [standing] on nothing until you uphold [the law of] the Torah, the Gospel, and what has been revealed to you from your Lord.' And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord will surely increase many of them in transgression and disbelief. So do not grieve over the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of adhering to divine scriptures in their entirety—Torah, Gospel, and the Qur'an—as the foundation of true guidance. It also highlights the consequence of rejecting this guidance: increased arrogance and disbelief among those who turn away, serving as a reminder not to despair over their rejection, as divine justice will prevail.

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews, and the Sabeans, and the Christians - whoever believed in Allah and the Last Day and did righteousness - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of divine mercy and the importance of sincere faith and righteous deeds over rigid adherence to specific religious labels. It suggests that salvation is not exclusive to any one faith community but is open to all who genuinely believe in Allah and the Hereafter and live righteously.

translation: We took the covenant from the Children of Israel and sent them messengers. Whenever a messenger came to them with what their souls did not desire, a group of them denied [the message], and a group killed [the messengers].
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of rejection and hostility that many prophets faced from their people, despite the clear signs and guidance they brought. It underscores the consequences of arrogance and the refusal to submit to divine truth, even when it is evident.

translation: And they thought there would be no [room for] trial, so they became blind and deaf. Then Allah turned in forgiveness upon them; then [again] many of them became blind and deaf. And Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring cycle of human defiance and divine mercy, illustrating how people may initially reject truth due to arrogance or ignorance, only to later receive forgiveness—yet often revert to their former state of spiritual blindness and deafness, failing to learn from their mistakes.

translation: Certainly they disbelieved those who said, 'Indeed, Allah is the Messiah, the son of Mary,' while the Messiah said, 'O Children of Israel, worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' Indeed, whoever associates others with Allah - Allah has forbidden him Paradise, and his refuge is the Fire. And there are not for the wrongdoers any helpers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and rejects any form of associating partners with Him, including the Christian belief in the divinity of Jesus (Isa) as the son of God. It highlights Jesus' own affirmation of monotheism, directing worship solely to Allah, and warns that shirk (associating partners with Allah) leads to severe consequences, including the deprivation of Paradise and eternal punishment in Hell.

translation: Certainly, those who say, "Allah is the third of three," have disbelieved. And there is no god except the One God. And if they do not desist from what they say, a painful punishment will afflict those of them who disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse addresses the misconception of the Trinity in Christianity, emphasizing the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed). It warns against associating partners with Allah, as such belief constitutes disbelief (kufr). The verse underscores the severity of this error and the consequences for those who persist in it, highlighting the importance of upholding pure monotheism.

translation: Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse calls upon people to turn back to Allah in sincere repentance and seek His forgiveness, emphasizing Allah's attributes of being the Most Forgiving and Most Merciful, thereby encouraging hope in His pardon and grace.

translation: The Messiah, Jesus, the son of Mary, was not but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They both used to eat food. Look how We make clear to them the signs; then look how they are deluded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the humanity and prophethood of Jesus (peace be upon him) and his mother Mary (peace be upon her), countering any exaggerated or divine claims about them. By highlighting that they both ate food, the verse underscores their human nature, rejecting the idea of Jesus being divine or a partner to God. It also serves as a reminder that prophethood is not exclusive to Jesus but has been a recurring theme throughout history, with many messengers sent before him. The verse invites reflection on how people often distort clear signs and proofs, choosing instead to be deluded by falsehood.

translation: Say, 'Do you worship besides Allah that which neither possesses for you any harm nor benefit?' And Allah is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of worshipping anything other than Allah, as such entities lack the power to cause harm or benefit, highlighting the absolute sovereignty and knowledge of Allah alone.

translation: Say, 'O People of the Scripture, do not exceed limits in your religion beyond the truth, nor follow the desires of a people who went astray before and misled many, and strayed from the straight path.'
interpretation: This verse warns against extremism and distortion in religious matters, urging adherence to the true essence of faith rather than following misguided traditions or personal whims that lead people astray from the correct path.

translation: Cursed were those who disbelieved among the Children of Israel by the tongue of David and of Jesus, the son of Mary. That was because they disobeyed and were [habitually] transgressing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine punishment for persistent disobedience and transgression, emphasizing that even prophets like David and Jesus (peace be upon them) conveyed God's condemnation of those who rejected faith and engaged in wrongdoing, underscoring the gravity of defiance against divine commandments.

translation: They used not to forbid one another from wrongdoing that they committed. Wretched indeed was what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse highlights a severe moral failing within a community where individuals not only engage in wrongdoing themselves but also fail to correct or prevent others from committing such acts, thereby perpetuating injustice and corruption.

translation: You see many of them allying themselves with the disbelievers. How evil is what they have sent ahead for themselves—that Allah has become angry with them, and in the punishment they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of forming alliances with those who oppose Allah’s guidance, warning that such actions incur divine wrath and lead to eternal punishment, emphasizing the importance of loyalty to faith over worldly alliances.

translation: And if they had believed in Allah and the Prophet and what was revealed to him, they would not have taken them as allies. But many of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of true faith in Allah and the Prophet (peace be upon him) as the foundation for correct relationships and alliances, warning against forming allegiances with those who reject divine guidance despite their claims of faith.

translation: You will surely find the most intense enmity from the Jews and the polytheists towards the believers, and you will surely find the nearest of them in affection to the believers those who say, "Indeed, we are Christians." That is because among them are priests and monks, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the varying attitudes of different groups toward the believers, emphasizing that while some (like the Jews and polytheists) harbor deep hostility, others (like the Christians mentioned) show greater affinity due to their humility and devotion, exemplified by their religious leaders (priests and monks) who do not exhibit arrogance.

translation: And when they hear what was revealed to the Messenger, you see their eyes overflowing with tears because of the truth they have recognized. They say, "Our Lord, we have believed, so register us among the witnesses."
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound emotional and spiritual response of believers upon hearing the divine revelation, reflecting their deep conviction and humility before the truth, as well as their sincere desire to be acknowledged by Allah as truthful witnesses to their faith.

translation: And why should we not believe in Allah and in the truth that has come to us, while we hope that our Lord will admit us among the righteous people?
interpretation: This verse reflects the natural inclination of a believer to align their faith with divine truth and seek righteousness, emphasizing the importance of sincerity in faith and the hope for divine mercy and guidance.

translation: So Allah rewarded them for what they said with gardens beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. And that is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and recompense, highlighting that Allah rewards those who speak truthfully and act righteously with eternal bliss in Paradise, emphasizing the importance of sincerity and righteousness in both speech and deed.

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs—it is they who will be the companions of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequence for those who persistently reject faith and deny divine guidance, emphasizing that their denial is not merely a personal choice but a rejection of truth that leads to eternal punishment.

translation: O you who have believed, do not prohibit the good things which Allah has made lawful to you and do not transgress. Indeed, Allah does not like transgressors.
interpretation: This verse cautions against imposing unnecessary restrictions on what Allah has permitted, as such actions can lead to extremism or self-imposed hardship, which contradicts the balanced and merciful nature of Islam.

translation: And eat of what Allah has provided for you [which is] lawful and good and fear Allah, in whom you are believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consuming lawful (halal) and pure (tayyib) sustenance as a reflection of one's faith and devotion to Allah, while also reminding believers to maintain taqwa (God-consciousness) in all aspects of their lives, including their dietary choices.

translation: Allah will not call you to account for thoughtlessness in your oaths, but He will call you to account for what your hearts have earned. And the atonement is the feeding of ten needy people from the average of what you feed your own families, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. But whoever cannot find [one of these], then [let him fast for] three days. That is the atonement for your oaths when you have sworn. And guard your oaths. Thus does Allah make clear to you His verses that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the distinction between unintentional (thoughtless) oaths and deliberate ones, emphasizing that accountability is tied to intent and sincerity rather than mere verbal slips. It also highlights the flexibility and mercy in Islam’s legal framework, allowing for expiation through tangible acts of charity, justice, or personal sacrifice when one falls short of their oath, thereby balancing justice with compassion.

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, intoxicants, gambling, [sacrificing on] stone alters [to other than Allah], and divining arrows are but defilement from the work of Satan, so avoid it that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the moral and spiritual corruption inherent in intoxicants, gambling, idolatry, and superstition, categorizing them as abominations that divert believers from righteousness and divine remembrance, thereby obstructing their path to true success in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: The Satan only desires to cause enmity and hatred between you through intoxicants and gambling, and to avert you from the remembrance of Allah and from prayer. So will you not desist?
interpretation: This verse underscores the destructive potential of intoxicants and gambling—not merely as harmful substances or activities, but as tools that Satan exploits to sow discord, weaken communal bonds, and distract believers from their spiritual obligations. The prohibition here is not just about abstaining from these acts but recognizing their capacity to erode faith, unity, and devotion, thereby undermining the very foundations of a righteous life.

translation: And obey Allah and obey the Messenger and beware. And if you turn away, then know that upon Our Messenger is only the clear conveyance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of obedience to Allah and His Messenger while warning against turning away from their guidance, reminding that the Prophet's responsibility is solely to deliver the message clearly, not to enforce belief or compel obedience.

translation: There is no blame upon those who believe and do righteous deeds concerning what they have eaten [in the past] if they fear Allah and believe and do righteous deeds, then fear Allah and believe, then fear Allah and do good. And Allah loves the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's mercy and forgiveness extend to those who repent sincerely and strive to improve their actions, even if they have made past mistakes. It highlights the importance of ongoing piety, faith, and righteous deeds, as well as Allah's love for those who consistently do good.

translation: O you who have believed, Allah will surely test you with something of the game that your hands and spears [can] obtain, that Allah may make evident those who fear Him unseen. And whoever transgresses after that - for him is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and mindfulness of Allah in one's actions, even in permissible matters. It warns against taking advantage of religious exemptions or leniencies for personal gain or without genuine need, as such behavior reveals a lack of true piety and fear of Allah.

translation: O you who have believed, do not kill game while you are in the state of ihram (sacred state for Hajj or Umrah). And whoever of you kills it intentionally, the penalty is an equivalent from sacrificial animals to what he killed, as judged by two just men among you, as an offering (to Allah) delivered to the Ka'bah, or an expiation: the feeding of needy people or the equivalent of that in fasting, that he may taste the consequence of his deed. Allah has pardoned what is past; but whoever returns (to violation), Allah will take retribution from him. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution.
interpretation: This verse establishes a moral and legal boundary for believers during the sacred state of ihram, emphasizing respect for the sanctity of the pilgrimage and the prohibition of hunting. The prescribed penalty for intentional violation reflects a balance between justice and mercy, ensuring accountability while allowing for expiation. The emphasis on 'tasting the consequence of his deed' underscores the spiritual and moral weight of the action, reinforcing the idea that violations of sacred boundaries have real, tangible repercussions. The verse also highlights Allah's initial forbearance ('pardoned what is past') but warns of severe consequences for repeated transgressions, illustrating the balance between divine mercy and justice.

translation: Lawful to you is the pursuit of water-game and its use for food—for the benefit and convenience of yourselves and those who travel; but forbidden is the pursuit of game whilst you are in the sacred precincts or in pilgrim garb. Be conscious of God, to Whom you shall be gathered.
interpretation: This verse establishes the permissibility of hunting and consuming seafood, even while in a state of pilgrimage (ihram), as it is a provision for travelers and a means of sustenance. However, hunting land animals is prohibited during the pilgrimage, emphasizing the sanctity of the sacred precincts and the rites of worship. The directive to 'be conscious of God' underscores the importance of reverence and obedience to divine commands, especially in acts of worship and daily life.

translation: Allah has made the Ka'bah, the Sacred House, standing for the people, and [He has made] the sacred months, and the sacrificial animals and the garlands [by which offerings are identified]. That is so you may know that Allah knows whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and that Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom behind the establishment of the Ka'bah and the associated rituals, highlighting that they serve as a means for people to recognize Allah's omniscience and sovereignty over all creation, reinforcing the importance of submission and devotion in worship.

translation: Know that Allah is severe in punishment and that Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the dual nature of Allah's justice and mercy, urging believers to maintain a balanced approach in their relationship with Him—acknowledging both His rigorous accountability for wrongdoing and His boundless capacity for forgiveness and compassion.

translation: The Messenger's duty is only to convey [the message]. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse underscores the limited role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger—his primary responsibility is to deliver the divine message faithfully, without coercion or alteration. It also highlights Allah's omniscience, emphasizing that nothing is hidden from Him, whether openly expressed or concealed in the heart, reinforcing accountability for intentions and actions.

translation: Say, 'The evil and the good are not equal, even if the abundance of evil pleases you. So fear Allah, O people of understanding, that you may succeed.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral and spiritual distinction between good and evil, asserting that their values cannot be equated regardless of quantity or appearance. It calls for discernment and righteousness, urging believers to prioritize divine guidance over worldly temptations or superficial attractions, as true success lies in piety and adherence to moral integrity.

translation: O you who have believed, do not ask about things which, if they were to be shown to you, would distress you. But if you ask about them while the Qur'an is being revealed, they will be shown to you. Allah has pardoned that. And Allah is Forgiving and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse advises believers to avoid asking unnecessary or prying questions that could lead to distress or confusion, especially when the answers might not be beneficial or when the timing is inappropriate. It highlights Allah's mercy in pardoning such inquiries when made in ignorance, while also reminding believers of Allah's attributes of forgiveness and forbearance.

translation: Indeed, a people before you had asked about it (the Qur'an), then they became disbelievers in it.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who doubt or reject the Qur'an, indicating that previous nations also questioned divine revelations but ultimately rejected them, leading to their downfall.

translation: Allah has not made (any of that which He has forbidden) a Bahirah, or a Sa’ibah, or a Wasilah, or a Ham. But those who disbelieve invent lies against Allah, and most of them have no understanding.
interpretation: This verse refutes superstitious and pagan practices of the pre-Islamic Arabs, who had invented arbitrary rules for their livestock, attributing them to divine will without any basis in revelation. It underscores the folly of those who fabricate falsehoods about Allah, highlighting their lack of reason and true understanding of divine law.

translation: And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," they say, "Sufficient for us is that upon which we found our fathers." Even though their fathers knew nothing, nor were they guided?
interpretation: This verse critiques blind imitation of ancestral traditions without examining their validity in light of divine guidance, emphasizing the importance of seeking truth through reason and revelation rather than mere habit or cultural inheritance.

translation: O you who have believed, upon you is [your responsibility for] yourselves. Those who have gone astray will not harm you when you have been guided. To Allah is your return, all together, and He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability and the importance of individual guidance, while also highlighting that one's righteousness cannot be compromised by the misguidance of others. It reassures believers that ultimate justice and recompense lie with Allah, who will fully disclose their deeds.

translation: O you who have believed, testimony [must be taken] among you when death approaches one of you at the time of bequest - [that of] two just men from among you or two others from outside yourselves, if you are traveling through the land and the calamity of death strikes you. Detain them after the prayer and let them both swear by Allah if you are doubtful, [saying], 'We will not exchange our oath for a price, even if he [i.e., the deceased] is a near relative, and we will not withhold the testimony of Allah. Indeed, we would then be among the sinful.'
interpretation: This verse establishes a legal and moral framework for ensuring the integrity of testimonies in matters of inheritance and bequests, particularly in situations where the witnesses may not be from the same community or family as the deceased. It emphasizes the importance of justice, impartiality, and the avoidance of bribery or favoritism, even in the face of familial ties or worldly temptations. The requirement to detain witnesses after prayer and have them swear an oath underscores the seriousness of bearing witness truthfully, as false testimony is equated with sinfulness.

translation: But if it is found that those two have been guilty of sin, let two others stand forth in their place from among those who have the best claim against the two former, and let them swear by Allah, 'Our testimony is truer than that of the two, for we have come forward without sin, and if we are false, then behold, we are among the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of false testimony and the measures taken to ensure justice, even if it means replacing witnesses who may have erred or acted unjustly. It highlights the importance of integrity in bearing witness, as those who swear must do so truthfully, knowing that falsehood would make them wrongdoers themselves.

translation: That is more likely that they will come with their testimony in its proper form, or they will fear that their oaths will be rebutted after their oaths. And be conscious of Allah and listen. And Allah does not guide the corrupt people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of truthfulness and integrity in testimony, warning against perjury or false oaths. It highlights the moral and spiritual consequences of dishonesty, emphasizing that Allah does not guide those who persist in corruption or deceit.

translation: The Day Allah will gather the messengers and say, "What was the response you received?" They will say, "We have no knowledge. Indeed, it is You who is Knower of all unseen."
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and omniscience of Allah, highlighting that even the prophets, despite their elevated status, possess no independent knowledge or authority. Their role is purely to convey divine messages, and all true understanding and judgment belong solely to Allah, who alone comprehends the unseen and the unseen realities of creation.

translation: When Allah said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, remember My favor upon you and upon your mother when I supported you with the Pure Spirit (Gabriel). You spoke to the people in the cradle and in maturity. And when I taught you the Book and wisdom, the Torah and the Gospel. And when you created from clay the likeness of a bird by My permission, then you breathed into it, and it became a bird by My permission. And you healed the blind and the leper by My permission, and when you brought forth the dead by My permission. And when I restrained the Children of Israel from [harming] you when you came to them with clear proofs, and those who disbelieved among them said, 'This is not but obvious magic.'"
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favors bestowed upon Jesus (peace be upon him), emphasizing his miraculous birth, his ability to perform extraordinary acts by Allah's permission, and his role as a messenger to the Children of Israel. It underscores the rejection Jesus faced despite the clear signs he brought, illustrating the recurring theme in the Qur'an of human skepticism towards divine signs and the consequences of such disbelief.

translation: And [remember] when I inspired the disciples [of Jesus] to believe in Me and My Messenger, they said, "We have believed, and bear witness that we are Muslims [submitting to Allah]."
interpretation: This verse highlights the innate human capacity to recognize and submit to divine truth when it is clearly presented, as demonstrated by the disciples' immediate acceptance of faith and their acknowledgment of their submission to Allah, reflecting the purity of their hearts and the absence of arrogance or resistance to divine guidance.

translation: When the disciples said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, can your Lord send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven?" [Jesus] said, "Fear Allah, if you should be believers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith and trust in Allah's wisdom and power, rather than seeking signs or miracles as a condition for belief. Jesus (peace be upon him) reminds the disciples that true faith requires submission to Allah's will, not demands for material proofs.

translation: They said, "We wish to eat from it (the food from heaven) and satisfy our hearts, and know that you have indeed told us the truth, and be among the witnesses (to its truth)."
interpretation: This verse reflects the demand for tangible proof to strengthen faith and certainty, illustrating the human tendency to seek empirical evidence to validate spiritual truths, while also highlighting the balance between divine signs and the free will to believe.

translation: And [remember] when Jesus, the son of Mary, said, "O Allah, our Lord, send down to us a table [spread with food] from the heaven to be for us a festival for the first of us and the last of us and a sign from You. And provide for us, for You are the best of providers."
interpretation: This supplication by Jesus (peace be upon him) reflects his humility and reliance on Allah, acknowledging that true sustenance and provision come solely from Allah, the best of providers. It also highlights the purpose of divine signs—not merely for material benefit but to strengthen faith and serve as a reminder of Allah’s power and mercy across generations.

translation: Allah said, 'Indeed, I am going to send it down to you, but whoever among you disbelieves thereafter, then I will punish him with a punishment by which I have not punished anyone among the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of apostasy after accepting faith, highlighting that such an act is a severe transgression warranting a unique and severe punishment from Allah, distinct from punishments meted out to others in the world.

translation: And [remember] when Allah said, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as deities besides Allah'?" He said, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say that to which I have no right. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is within myself, and I do not know what is within Yourself. Indeed, You are Knower of the unseen."
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute transcendence of Allah and the limitations of human knowledge, even that of prophets. Jesus (peace be upon him) denies any claim to divinity, affirming that such an assertion would be beyond his right or capacity. It highlights the distinction between the Creator and creation, emphasizing that only Allah possesses perfect knowledge of the unseen, reinforcing the core Islamic belief in tawhid (the oneness of Allah).

translation: I did not say to them except what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' And I was a witness over them as long as I was among them; but when You took me, You were the Observer over them, and You are, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) unwavering obedience to Allah's commands, even in conveying the message to others. It also underscores the limits of human responsibility—while the Prophet was a witness to the actions of his people during his lifetime, ultimate accountability rests with Allah, who remains fully aware of all deeds after the Prophet's departure.

translation: If You punish them, they are Your servants; and if You forgive them, indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and mercy of Allah, highlighting that His decisions—whether punishment or forgiveness—are rooted in His supreme wisdom and power, and that all beings are ultimately subject to His will.

translation: Allah has said, "This is a Day when the truthful will benefit from their truthfulness. For them are gardens [in Paradise] beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. That is the great attainment."
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate reward for those who embody sincerity and truthfulness in their faith and actions, emphasizing that their steadfast commitment to truth in this life will be the key to their eternal success and divine approval in the Hereafter.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is within them, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and power over all creation, asserting that nothing exists outside His control or ability to manage, demonstrating His unchallenged authority and the futility of seeking protection or power outside His dominion.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. [All] praise is [due] to Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and made the darkness and the light. Then those who disbelieve equate [others] with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse underscores the foundational Islamic belief in the oneness of Allah (Tawhid) by highlighting His exclusive role as the Creator of all existence—both the physical universe (heavens and earth) and the metaphysical realities (light and darkness). The mention of 'those who disbelieve' equating others with Allah (shirk) serves as a stark contrast, emphasizing the gravity of associating partners with Him, which is the gravest sin in Islam. The verse thus reinforces the absolute sovereignty and uniqueness of Allah in creation and worship.

translation: It is He who created you from clay; then He decreed a term, and there is a specified term with Him; yet you doubt.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and wisdom of Allah in creating humans from clay and determining their lifespans, emphasizing that despite the certainty of these divine decrees, human beings still harbor doubts—a reminder of their limited understanding and the need for faith in Allah's perfect plan.

translation: And He is Allah, [the only deity] in the heavens and on the earth. He knows your secret and what you declare, and He knows what you earn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute knowledge and presence in all realms, asserting that nothing is hidden from Him—whether hidden intentions, outward declarations, or actions—highlighting His omniscience and the accountability of human beings for their deeds.

translation: And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the persistent refusal of those who reject faith to acknowledge or reflect upon the divine signs (evidence of God's existence and power) presented to them, highlighting the depth of their stubbornness and the consequences of their denial.

translation: For they denied the truth when it came to them, so the news of what they used to ridicule will soon come to them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine justice and the consequences of mocking divine truths; those who reject the truth will inevitably face the reality of their denial.

translation: Have they not considered how many generations We have destroyed before them, whom We had established upon the earth more than We have established you? And We sent [rain from] the sky upon them in abundance and made rivers flow beneath them; then We destroyed them for their sins and brought forth after them another generation.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning against arrogance and complacency, emphasizing that divine favor and material prosperity are not guarantees of security or permanence. It underscores the transient nature of worldly power and the inevitability of divine accountability, urging reflection on the consequences of moral and spiritual neglect.

translation: And if We had sent down to you, [O Muhammad], a written Book on a parchment and they had touched it with their hands, the disbelievers would have said, 'This is not but obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the intransigence of those who reject the truth despite overwhelming evidence. It suggests that even if a tangible, written revelation were presented to them—something they could physically handle—their skepticism would persist, and they would dismiss it as mere trickery. This highlights the deeper issue of the heart's resistance to faith, where no amount of external proof can penetrate a willfully closed mind.

translation: And they say, 'Why has an angel not been sent down to him?' But had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and then they would not be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who demanded a supernatural sign, such as an angel, to validate the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). The interpretation highlights the irony in their demand: if an angel were sent, the divine judgment would be swift and final, leaving no room for further denial or delay, thus underscoring the seriousness of faith and the consequences of rejecting divine guidance.

translation: And if We had made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them in what they confuse themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom behind Allah's choice of sending a human messenger (the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ) rather than an angel. It underscores that even if an angel were sent in human form, people would still find excuses to doubt or reject the message, just as they do with human messengers. The verse emphasizes the test of faith and the tendency of people to seek reasons to avoid belief, regardless of the form in which the message is conveyed.

translation: And indeed, messengers before you were ridiculed, but those who mocked them were afflicted by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning that mocking the truth or the messengers of God will ultimately lead to divine retribution, demonstrating the futility of arrogance and disbelief in the face of divine guidance.

translation: Say, 'Travel through the earth and observe how was the end of those who denied (the truth).'
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on historical consequences of rejecting divine guidance, urging believers to learn from past civilizations that faced destruction due to their disbelief and arrogance.

translation: Say, 'To whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'To Allah.' He has decreed upon Himself mercy. He will surely gather you to the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. It is those who have lost themselves [by disbelief] who will not believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all existence and His inherent attribute of mercy, which He has decreed for Himself. The Day of Resurrection is a certainty, and those who reject faith do so at their own peril, as their disbelief leads to their ultimate loss.

translation: To Him belongs whatever rests in the night and the day. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty over all existence, whether it is the dynamic activity of the day or the quiet stillness of the night, highlighting His encompassing knowledge and awareness of all things.

translation: Say, 'Is it other than Allah I should take as a protector, Originator of the heavens and the earth, who feeds and is not fed?' Say, 'Indeed, I have been commanded to be the first [among you] to submit [to Allah], and [also told], "Do not ever be of the polytheists."'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute uniqueness of Allah in creation, sustenance, and sovereignty, rejecting any notion of associating partners with Him. It also highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) uncompromising monotheistic mission, emphasizing his role as the first Muslim in the line of prophets and a model for submission to Allah alone, while warning against the grave sin of shirk (polytheism).

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of disobeying Allah and the severe consequences that await on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) and obedience to divine commands.

translation: He from whom it is averted on that Day, [Allah] has surely had mercy upon him. And that is the clear attainment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of the Day of Judgment, where divine mercy is the ultimate determinant of salvation. It implies that being spared from punishment on that Day is not merely an act of avoidance but a manifestation of Allah's mercy, highlighting that true success lies in securing that mercy, which is the most evident and undeniable triumph.

translation: And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He touches you with good - then He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all circumstances, emphasizing that no one can avert harm or bring benefit except by His will, reinforcing complete reliance on Him in all affairs.

translation: And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He is the Wise, the Acquainted [with all].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute dominion and control over all of creation, highlighting His unchallenged authority and power over His servants. The attributes 'Wise' and 'Acquainted' underscore that His rule is not arbitrary but governed by divine wisdom and perfect knowledge of all things, ensuring justice and purpose in His decrees.

translation: Say, 'What is the greatest testimony?' Say, 'Allah is witness between me and you. And this Qur'an was revealed to me that I may warn you thereby and whomever it reaches. Do you [then] testify that with Allah there are other deities?' Say, 'I do not testify [to that].' Say, 'He is but one God, and indeed I am free from what you associate [with Him].'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and rejects any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him, emphasizing that true testimony in Islam is to affirm the uniqueness and sovereignty of Allah alone.

translation: Those to whom We have given the Book recognize him [i.e., the Prophet] as they recognize their own sons. Those who have lost themselves [by their disbelief]—they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep familiarity that the People of the Book (Jews and Christians) had with the descriptions of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in their scriptures, akin to recognizing their own children. Yet, despite this recognition, their arrogance, pride, or attachment to worldly interests led them to reject the truth, resulting in their own spiritual ruin. The verse underscores the tragedy of rejecting clear guidance despite overwhelming evidence, as well as the self-inflicted consequences of such rejection.

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about Allah or denies His signs? Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of attributing falsehood to Allah or rejecting His revelations, emphasizing that such actions stem from injustice and will ultimately lead to failure, as divine justice prevails over all.

translation: And [mention] the Day We will gather them all together - then We will say to those who associated others with Allah, 'Where are your 'partners' that you used to claim [for yourselves]?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate accountability of human beings before Allah, where all will be gathered on the Day of Judgment. It highlights the falsehood of associating partners with Allah, as those who did so will be called to account for their claims, and their supposed partners will not be able to intercede or provide any assistance, exposing the futility of their polytheistic beliefs.

translation: Yet their only contention was that they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not idolaters."
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and denial of those who claim to believe in Allah yet secretly associate partners with Him, as their actions contradict their words, revealing their true disbelief despite their claims.

translation: See how they lied against themselves, and how what they used to invent has vanished from them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the self-deception of those who deny the truth, showing that their falsehoods ultimately fail them, leaving them exposed and devoid of their fabricated excuses or claims when confronted with reality.

translation: And among them are those who listen to you [O Muhammad]. But Allah has placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. Until, when they come to you [O Muhammad] to argue with you, the disbelievers say, "This is not but tales of the former peoples."
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and intellectual barriers that prevent certain individuals from accepting the truth, despite hearing it. The mention of 'coverings' over their hearts symbolizes divine preordination or their own hardened hearts that prevent understanding, while 'deafness' in their ears signifies their refusal to listen with an open mind. The persistence of disbelief, even in the face of clear signs, underscores the futility of arguments with those who are spiritually blind and deaf to the truth, as their rejection stems from deep-seated arrogance or preconceived notions rather than a genuine search for guidance.

translation: And they forbid [others] from it and avoid it themselves; but they do not harm [anyone] except themselves, and they do not perceive it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who outwardly condemn a certain action or belief but secretly engage in it themselves, thereby deceiving only themselves while causing no real harm to others.

translation: And if you could but see when they are made to stand before the Fire, they will say, "Oh, would that we could be returned [to life on earth] and never deny the signs of our Lord and be among the believers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound regret of those who denied the truth in this life when they face the consequences of their disbelief in the Hereafter, underscoring the irreversible nature of their choices and the futility of their pleas for a second chance.

translation: But what they used to conceal before has now become clear to them. And if they were returned [to earth], they would certainly return to what they were forbidden, for they are indeed liars.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inescapable reality of divine accountability, where hidden truths—whether deeds, intentions, or hypocrisy—are inevitably exposed. It also highlights the paradox of human nature: even when warned against wrongdoing, some persist in it, revealing the depth of their deceit and defiance against divine commandments.

translation: And they say, "There is not but our worldly life; we will not be resurrected."
interpretation: This verse reflects the denial of the Hereafter by those who are heedless of divine truth, attributing reality solely to the transient pleasures of this world and rejecting the concept of resurrection and accountability, thereby exposing their arrogance and rejection of divine justice.

translation: And if you could but see when they are made to stand before their Lord! He will say, "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord!" He will say, "Then taste the punishment because you used to disbelieve."
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the undeniable truth of Allah's existence and Oneness, which even the disbelievers will acknowledge at the moment of reckoning, though their acknowledgment will be of no avail to them.

translation: Indeed, those who deny the meeting with Allah will have lost. [So lost] that when the Hour comes upon them suddenly, they will say, "Oh, [how great is] our regret over what we neglected concerning it!" And they will bear their burdens on their backs. Unquestionably, evil is that which they bear.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe regret and realization of loss that will afflict those who denied the Hereafter and the meeting with Allah, only when it is too late—when the Hour (Day of Judgment) arrives unexpectedly. Their regret is futile, as their neglect of righteous deeds cannot be undone, and they will bear the full weight of their sins, highlighting the gravity of their disbelief and the consequences of their heedlessness.

translation: And the life of this world is not but amusement and diversion, but the Home of the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah. Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient and superficial nature of worldly life compared to the eternal and profound reality of the Hereafter, urging believers to prioritize spiritual growth and God-consciousness over material pursuits.

translation: We certainly know that it grieves you (O Muhammad) what they say. But they do not deny you (in truth); rather, it is the wrongdoers who deny the signs of Allah.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that the hurt he feels from the rejection and false accusations of his people is understandable, but it clarifies that their denial is not a personal rejection of him—rather, it stems from their rejection of Allah’s signs, reflecting their own arrogance and injustice.

translation: And certainly were messengers denied before you, but they were patient over [the effects of] denial, and they were harmed until Our victory came to them. And nothing can change the words of Allah. And there has certainly come to you some information about the [previous] messengers.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers that rejection and harm from opponents are not unique to their time but were experienced by previous messengers as well. It encourages steadfastness in the face of adversity, affirming that divine victory will ultimately prevail, as Allah’s promises and decrees are unchangeable and will be fulfilled.

translation: And if their aversion is distressful for you, then if you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a ladder into the sky to bring them a sign, do so. But if Allah had willed, He could have gathered them all upon guidance. So do not be among the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse underscores the limits of human influence in guiding others, emphasizing that true guidance comes solely from Allah’s will. It cautions against frustration when people reject divine guidance, reminding the believer that their role is to convey the message, not to force acceptance.

translation: Indeed, only those who listen respond. But the dead—Allah will resurrect them, then to Him they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who are spiritually alive (those who listen and respond to guidance) and those who are spiritually dead (those who remain heedless). It underscores that true responsiveness comes from a heart that is alive to divine truth, while even the spiritually dead will ultimately be resurrected and held accountable before Allah, emphasizing divine justice and the inevitability of the Hereafter.

translation: And they say, 'Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'Indeed, Allah is Able to send down a sign, but most of them do not know.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of the disbelievers who demanded miraculous signs from the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as proof of his prophethood. The verse affirms Allah's absolute power to send such signs but highlights the deeper issue: their refusal to believe stems not from a lack of evidence but from their own ignorance and arrogance, as true guidance requires humility and acceptance of divine wisdom rather than mere spectacle.
