translation: And there is no creature on earth and no bird that flies with its wings except [that they are] communities like you. We have not neglected in the Register a thing. Then unto their Lord they will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of creation under Allah's governance, highlighting that all beings—human and otherwise—are subject to divine order and accountability, as nothing is omitted from Allah's perfect knowledge and record.

translation: But those who deny Our signs are deaf and dumb, blotted out in darkness. Whomever Allah wills to send astray, He leaves astray; and whomever He wills, He sets him on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of rejecting divine guidance, illustrating a spiritual hardening of the heart that leads to misguidance, while also affirming Allah's absolute sovereignty over guidance and misguidance.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if the punishment of Allah comes to you or the Hour [i.e., the Day of Judgment] comes to you, will you invoke others besides Allah, if you should be truthful? [in your claim of associating partners with Him]?'
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to reflect on their true reliance in times of extreme distress, exposing the futility of invoking false deities when faced with divine punishment or the inevitability of the Hour, thereby affirming the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and the absurdity of associating partners with Him.

translation: But it is Him alone that you invoke, and He removes the distress you invoke Him for, if He wills, and you forget what you associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah in responding to human supplications, while also highlighting the futility and forgetfulness of associating partners with Him, as such partners cannot independently alleviate distress or fulfill needs.

translation: And We have already sent [messengers] to nations before you, then We seized them with hardship and affliction that they might humble themselves [to Us].
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine pattern of testing communities through adversity to evoke humility and repentance, highlighting that trials are not arbitrary but purposeful, designed to steer humanity back to submission and reliance on Allah.

translation: So why, when Our punishment came to them, did they not humble themselves? But their hearts hardened, and Satan made what they were doing seem fair-seeming to them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to remain in denial and arrogance even when faced with clear signs of divine retribution, illustrating how hardened hearts can lead to self-deception and the acceptance of wrongdoing as justified.

translation: But when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the doors of every [good] thing, until, when they rejoiced in what they were given, We seized them suddenly, and they were [then] in despair.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against ingratitude and arrogance in the face of blessings, illustrating that material or worldly success can be a test rather than a sign of divine favor. It highlights the fleeting nature of such blessings when they are not accompanied by gratitude or recognition of their true source, leading to sudden and irreversible consequences.

translation: So the roots of the people who did wrong were cut off. And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice, where the consequences of persistent oppression and wrongdoing lead to the complete eradication of the oppressors' legacy, while affirming the sovereignty and supremacy of Allah as the ultimate sustainer and judge of all creation.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah should take away your hearing and your sight and set a seal upon your hearts, which god other than Allah could bring them back for you?' Look how We diversify the signs; then they [still] turn away.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute dependence of human faculties and spiritual perception on Allah, emphasizing that no other power can restore what He has decreed to be taken away. The 'diversification of signs' refers to the varied ways Allah presents evidence of His existence and unity, yet despite this, people persistently reject or ignore these signs, demonstrating their free will to turn away from the truth.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered? If the punishment of Allah comes upon you suddenly or openly, will anyone be destroyed except the wrongdoing people?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice, emphasizing that punishment or calamity is not arbitrary but specifically targets those who persist in oppression and injustice, serving as both a warning and a reminder of accountability.

translation: And We send not the messengers except as bringers of good tidings and as warners. So whoever believes and reforms - there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse underscores the fundamental purpose of prophethood: to guide humanity toward righteousness and warn against deviation. It reassures believers that faith coupled with righteous action absolves them of existential fear and sorrow, as divine mercy supersedes punishment for those who sincerely repent and reform.

translation: But those who deny Our verses—torment will touch them for their defiance.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of rejecting divine guidance, emphasizing that persistent defiance of truth leads to spiritual and moral corruption, which in turn invites divine retribution as a form of justice.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'I do not tell you that I have the depositories [containing the provision] of Allah, nor [do I claim to] know the unseen, nor do I tell you that I am an angel. I only follow what is revealed to me.' Say, 'Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Then will you not give thought?''
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute submission of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to divine revelation, rejecting any claims of possessing supernatural knowledge or authority beyond what Allah has ordained. It also serves as a rhetorical challenge to humanity, emphasizing the stark contrast between those who are spiritually blind (unaware of divine guidance) and those who are guided, urging reflection on the consequences of such a divide.

translation: And warn with it (the Qur'an) those who fear that they will be gathered before their Lord - for them besides Him there will be no protector and no intercessor - that they may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting that true fear of divine accountability should drive one to righteousness, as no intermediary can intervene on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord morning and evening, seeking His Face. You are not accountable for them in any way, nor are they accountable for you in any way. So if you drive them away, you would be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of humility, tolerance, and inclusivity in religious matters, emphasizing that one should not reject or exclude sincere believers—even if they differ in certain practices—so long as they are devoted to Allah and seek His pleasure.

translation: And thus We have tested some of them through others, that they may say, "Are these the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among us?" Is Allah not most knowing of the grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the trials and tribulations that people face, which may lead others to question why certain individuals are favored by Allah. It serves as a reminder that Allah's knowledge encompasses all things, including the true nature of gratitude and the inner state of individuals, which may not be apparent to others.

translation: And when those who believe in Our verses come to you, say, 'Peace be upon you.' Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy: that whoever does wrong out of ignorance and then repents after that and reforms, indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the boundless mercy of Allah, emphasizing that no sin is beyond His forgiveness if one sincerely repents and mends their ways, highlighting the importance of repentance and reform as pathways to divine mercy.

translation: And thus do We detail the verses, and so may the way of the criminals become clear.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and distinctiveness of the signs (verses) in the Qur'an, which serve to expose the truth and make the path of those who persist in wrongdoing unmistakable, leaving no excuse for their misguidance.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah.' Say, 'I do not follow your desires, for then I would have gone astray, and I would not be of the [rightly] guided.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of unwavering commitment to monotheism (Tawhid) and rejecting any form of associationism (Shirk). It highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) refusal to compromise his faith or follow the misguided desires of others, even if it meant facing opposition. The verse serves as a reminder to believers to remain steadfast in their devotion to Allah alone, avoiding the pitfalls of societal pressures or personal inclinations that contradict divine guidance.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I am on clear evidence from my Lord, but you deny it. What you seek to hasten is not in my power. The judgment is only for Allah. He relates the truth, and He is the best of judges.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) unwavering conviction in the divine truth he was sent with, despite the rejection of his people. It also highlights the limits of his authority—he cannot hasten divine punishment or judgment, as that rests solely with Allah. The verse emphasizes Allah's role as the ultimate arbiter of truth, whose decrees are just and decisive, contrasting with human impatience or denial.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "If I had what you are hastening for, the matter would have been decided between me and you, but Allah is most knowing of the wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom behind the delay of punishment or the fulfillment of promises, emphasizing that Allah alone possesses perfect knowledge of justice and wrongdoing, and His timing is always just, even if it appears delayed from a human perspective.

translation: And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. And He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it. And no grain is there in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything wet or dry, but that it is [written] in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and exclusive knowledge of Allah over all aspects of the unseen, including the keys to unseen matters which are beyond human comprehension. It highlights His omniscience over all creation, no matter how minute or hidden, emphasizing that nothing in the universe occurs without His knowledge, as everything is meticulously recorded in His divine decree.

translation: And it is He who takes your souls by night and knows what you have committed by day; then He revives you therein that a specified term may be fulfilled. Then to Him will be your return; then He will inform you of what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute knowledge and control over life and death, as well as the accountability of human actions. It highlights the transient nature of worldly life, where deeds—whether committed openly or in secret—are recorded and will be recompensed in full on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing divine justice and the inevitability of resurrection.

translation: And He is the Subduer over His servants, and He sends over you guardian-angels. Then when death comes to one of you, Our messengers take him in death, and they are not neglectful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and control over all of creation, including human life and death. The mention of guardian-angels highlights the meticulous recording of deeds and the divine oversight of human affairs, underscoring the inevitability of divine justice and the precision with which Allah governs the affairs of His servants.

translation: Then they will be returned to Allah, their true Master. Unquestionably, His is the judgment, and He is the swiftest of accountants.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority and justice of Allah in the Hereafter, where all beings will ultimately return to Him for final judgment. The phrase 'He is the swiftest of accountants' emphasizes that Allah’s reckoning is not delayed or hindered by any process—it is immediate, precise, and just, reflecting His perfect knowledge and power over all things.

translation: Say, 'Who rescues you from the darkness of the land and sea, [to whom] you call humbly and secretly, [saying], "If He saves us from this, we will surely be among the grateful?"
interpretation: This verse underscores the innate human tendency to turn to Allah in moments of distress, invoking Him sincerely and privately, while acknowledging that true gratitude is demonstrated through consistent devotion and acknowledgment of His blessings beyond the immediate relief.

translation: Say, 'Allah rescues you from it and from every distress.' Yet you associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse underscores the irony of human nature, where despite Allah's exclusive power to relieve all hardships, people still turn to false deities or idols for help, thereby committing the grave sin of shirk (associating partners with Allah). It serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute sovereignty and the futility of seeking aid from anything or anyone besides Him.

translation: Say, 'He is the One able to send upon you a punishment from above you or from beneath your feet, or to confuse you [into separate] factions and make you taste the violence of one another.' Look how We diversify the signs, that they might understand.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power of Allah to manifest His punishment in various forms, whether through natural disasters, societal upheaval, or internal strife, as a means to awaken humanity to the consequences of their actions and the urgency of repentance.

translation: And your people denied it while it is the truth. Say, 'I am not a guardian over you.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a warner and bearer of truth, not as a coercive authority over people's faith or actions. It emphasizes that guidance is a matter between individuals and Allah, and the Prophet's duty is to convey the message, not to enforce belief or compel obedience.

translation: For every prophecy there is a fixed time, and you will come to know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of divine decrees and prophecies, assuring that what has been foretold will inevitably come to pass at its appointed time, beyond which there is no delay or alteration.

translation: And when you see those who engage in discourse about Our verses, then turn away from them until they engage in discourse about other than it. And if Satan causes you to forget, then do not sit after the reminder with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to disengage from futile and harmful discussions about the Qur'an's verses, especially when such discourse is used to mock or distort their meanings, and to seek more beneficial conversations instead. It also warns against being led astray by Satan's whispers, emphasizing the importance of remembering divine guidance and avoiding the company of those who persist in wrongdoing.

translation: And there is no responsibility upon the righteous for any account [on the Day of Judgment], except [that they will be] a reminder, so that they may fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the righteous believers will not face any reckoning for their sins in the Hereafter, as their good deeds have already secured their salvation. The phrase 'except a reminder' suggests that their example serves as a lesson for others, urging them to strive for righteousness and God-consciousness.

translation: And leave those who take their religion as amusement and play, and whom the worldly life has deluded. But remind with the Qur'an that whoever does wrong will not be recompensed except by its like; and he will not find besides Allah a protector or a helper. And [yet], he will not be recompensed except for what he was doing. Those are the ones who have lost what they have earned, for them will be a drink of scalding water and a painful punishment because of their disbelief.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning against prioritizing worldly pleasures and distractions over the pursuit of spiritual truth, emphasizing that such a choice will lead to irreversible loss and severe punishment. It underscores the absolute justice of divine recompense, where one's deeds are met with consequences that cannot be mitigated by external intercession or compensation, highlighting the futility of seeking alternatives to divine justice.

translation: Say, 'Shall we invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits us nor harms us, and turn back on our heels after Allah has guided us, like one whom the devils have lured away into bewilderment in the earth, though he has companions who call him to guidance, saying, "Come to us"?' Say, 'Indeed, the guidance of Allah is the [only] true guidance. And we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of seeking guidance from anything other than Allah, emphasizing that true guidance can only come from Him. It also highlights the steadfastness required in faith, comparing those who abandon divine guidance to someone lost and confused, despite the calls of companions to the right path. The verse reinforces the absolute necessity of submitting to Allah, the Lord of all creation, as the sole source of true guidance and salvation.

translation: And establish prayer and fear Him. And it is He to whom you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual obligations of fulfilling one's religious duties (prayer) and maintaining consciousness of God (taqwa), while also reminding believers of the ultimate accountability and return to God on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in truth. And the Day He says, "Be," and it is. His word is the truth. And His is the dominion on the Day the Horn is blown. [He is] Knower of the unseen and the witnessed; and He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah in creation and resurrection, emphasizing that His command alone brings existence into being ('Be, and it is'). It highlights the truthfulness of His word and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, where His knowledge encompasses all that is hidden and manifest. The mention of His wisdom and awareness serves to reassure believers of His perfect justice and control over all affairs.

translation: And [mention] when Abraham said to his father Azar, 'Do you take idols as deities? Indeed, I see you and your people in manifest error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral courage and unwavering commitment to monotheism of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) as he confronts his father and community for their idolatrous practices, emphasizing the stark contrast between truth and falsehood.

translation: And thus did We show Abraham the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and that he might be of those possessing certainty.
interpretation: This verse highlights that true certainty in faith comes from direct divine revelation and observation of the signs of God's power in creation, rather than mere hearsay or tradition.

translation: So when the night covered him over, he saw a planet. He said, "This is my Lord." But when it set, he said, "I do not like those that disappear."
interpretation: This verse highlights the intellectual journey of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) as he questioned the nature of worship and the divine. His initial attribution of divinity to a celestial body reflects the human tendency to seek meaning in the observable world, but his subsequent rejection of it upon its disappearance demonstrates the futility of worshiping transient and impermanent entities, guiding him—and humanity—to seek the Eternal, the Unseen, which does not fade or perish.

translation: So when he saw the moon rising, he said, "This is my lord." But when it set, he said, "If my Lord does not guide me, I will surely be of the people astray."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the intellectual journey of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) from polytheism to monotheism, demonstrating the importance of seeking true guidance from Allah rather than attributing divinity to created entities like the moon, sun, or stars.

translation: So when he saw the sun rising, he said, "This is my Lord! This is greater." And when it set, he said, "O my people, indeed I am free from what you associate [with Allah]."
interpretation: This verse illustrates Prophet Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) rejection of idolatry and his logical demonstration of Allah's oneness. By observing the sun's rise and fall, he refuted the false notion that celestial bodies could be divine, affirming instead that Allah alone is the Creator and Sustainer of all.

translation: Indeed, I have turned my face toward He who originated the heavens and the earth, inclining toward truth, and I am not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse reflects the essence of monotheistic devotion, emphasizing the believer's exclusive focus on the Creator, rejecting any form of idolatry or association of partners with Allah, and affirming a pure, uncompromising faith in the oneness of God.

translation: And he disputed with his people. He said, 'Do you argue with me concerning Allah while He has guided me? And I fear not what you associate with Him [and will not be harmed by it] unless my Lord wills something. My Lord encompasses all things in knowledge. Then will you not be reminded?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) in the absolute oneness and power of Allah, despite the arguments of his people who associated partners with Allah. It underscores the futility of disputing with those who reject divine guidance, as true guidance comes solely from Allah, and no harm can befall a believer unless Allah wills it. The verse also emphasizes Allah's all-encompassing knowledge, reminding humans of their limited understanding and the need to reflect on Allah's signs.

translation: How can I fear what you associate [with Allah] when you fear not having associated with Allah that for which He has not sent down to you any authority? Then which of the two parties is more worthy of security, if you should know?
interpretation: This verse critiques the hypocrisy of those who associate partners with Allah (shirk) while claiming to be believers, questioning their selective fear—fearing false deities but not the consequences of their own disbelief. It challenges them to reflect on which group is truly deserving of security: those who uphold tawhid (monotheism) or those who distort it.

translation: It is those who believe and do not mix their faith with injustice—it is they who will have security, and they are rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of pure and untainted faith, emphasizing that true believers must maintain their trust in God without allowing any form of injustice or wrongdoing to corrupt their devotion, as such purity is the path to true security and divine guidance.

translation: And that was Our proof which We gave to Abraham against his people. We raise by degrees whom We will. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in elevating individuals to higher ranks of understanding, guidance, or spiritual status based on His will, as demonstrated in the case of Abraham (peace be upon him) who was granted clear proof to refute his people's falsehood.

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob; each [of them] We guided. And Noah, We had guided before; and among his descendants, David and Solomon and Job and Joseph and Moses and Aaron. Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine guidance bestowed upon multiple prophets and righteous individuals across generations, emphasizing that guidance is a recurring divine favor rather than a one-time event, and that God rewards those who strive for righteousness.

translation: And [mention] Zakariya and Yahya and Isa and Ilyas - all were of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine selection and favor bestowed upon these prophets, emphasizing that their righteousness was the defining characteristic that elevated them in the sight of Allah, serving as a model for believers to emulate in their own spiritual journeys.

translation: And [mention] Ishmael, Elisha, Jonah, and Lot - and each [of them] We preferred over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon these prophets, emphasizing that their spiritual excellence and moral uprightness were recognized and elevated by Allah above all other beings in their respective times, underscoring the principle that true honor lies in piety and submission to God.

translation: And [We selected] from among their forefathers, their descendants, and their brothers; and We chose them and guided them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine selection and guidance, emphasizing that Allah's favor is not limited to a single generation but extends across families and lineages, provided they uphold righteousness and remain on the path of truth.

translation: That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whomever He wills of His servants. But if they had associated [anything with Allah], whatever they were doing would have become worthless.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah in guiding whom He wills, emphasizing that guidance is a divine gift, not earned by human effort alone. It also serves as a warning that associating partners with Allah (shirk) nullifies all righteous deeds, highlighting the critical importance of pure monotheism (tawhid) in Islam.

translation: Those to whom We gave the Book, the wisdom, and prophethood. If these [people] disbelieve in it, We have already entrusted it to a people who are not disbelievers in it.
interpretation: This verse reassures that the divine guidance and prophethood are preserved and entrusted to a people who will uphold and believe in it, regardless of the disbelief of others, ensuring the continuity of truth and guidance.

translation: It is those whom Allah has guided, so follow their guidance. Say, [O Muhammad], "I ask you for no reward for it; it is not but a reminder for the worlds."
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of following divine guidance as exemplified by those who have been rightly guided, while emphasizing the Prophet's (peace be upon him) selflessness in conveying the message, as he seeks no personal reward—only the guidance serves as a universal reminder for all of humanity.

translation: And they have not appraised Allah with [His] true appraisal when they say, "Allah did not reveal to a human being anything." Say, "Who revealed the Book which Moses brought, a light and guidance for the people? You make it into pages, which you display while concealing much. And you were taught that which you knew not—neither you nor your forefathers." Say, "Allah [revealed it]." Then leave them in their discourse, playing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who deny divine revelation, particularly the claim that Allah has not sent down any scripture to humanity. It highlights the hypocrisy of those who selectively accept parts of the Torah (the Book of Moses) while concealing its true guidance, despite its evident light and wisdom. The verse underscores the importance of recognizing Allah’s role as the ultimate source of all revelation and the folly of dismissing divine knowledge while clinging to superficial or partial understanding.

translation: And this is a Book We have sent down, blessed and confirming what was before it, that you may warn the Mother of Cities (Makkah) and whoever is around it. And those who believe in the Hereafter believe in it, and they are maintaining their prayers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin and purpose of the Qur'an: it is a blessed revelation that confirms the truth of previous scriptures, serving as a warning to Makkah and its surrounding areas. The verse also emphasizes the connection between belief in the Hereafter and acceptance of the Qur'an, while underscoring the importance of steadfastness in prayer as a sign of true faith.

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about Allah or says, 'It has been inspired to me,' while nothing has been inspired to him, and [he] who says, 'I will bring down [a revelation] like what Allah revealed'? If you could but see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming grasp of death while the angels extend their hands, [saying], 'Discharge your souls! Today you will be awarded the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth and [for] being, toward His signs, arrogant.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of falsely attributing words to Allah, whether through fabricating lies, claiming divine inspiration without evidence, or arrogantly challenging the authenticity of Allah’s revelations. It highlights the ultimate accountability of such actions, particularly in the face of death, where the wrongdoers are confronted by angels with no escape, emphasizing that their punishment is a direct consequence of their deliberate defiance and arrogance toward divine truth.

translation: And certainly, you have come to Us alone, just as We created you the first time, and you have left behind what We bestowed upon you behind your backs. And We do not see with you your intercessors whom you claimed were partners [with Allah] in you. Indeed, all ties between you have been severed, and what you used to claim has perished from you.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute accountability of individuals on the Day of Judgment, where no external support—whether from false deities, intercessors, or worldly attachments—can aid them. It highlights the futility of idolatry and misplaced trust, emphasizing that one’s ultimate return is to Allah alone, stripped of all pretenses and false dependencies.

translation: Indeed, Allah is the cleaver of the grain and the date-seed. He brings forth the living from the dead, and He brings forth the dead from the living. That is Allah; so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power over life and death, highlighting the cyclical nature of existence as a sign of divine unity and control, thereby calling humanity to reflect on their misplaced devotion and return to the truth.

translation: He causes the dawn to break; He has made the night for rest, and the sun and the moon for reckoning. That is the determining of the Almighty, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the natural order of creation, where each celestial body and phenomenon serves a distinct purpose—dawn brings light, night provides rest, and the sun and moon regulate time—demonstrating Allah’s supreme power and precise knowledge in orchestrating the universe.

translation: And it is He who has made the stars for you so that you may be guided by them in the darkness of land and sea. We have detailed the signs for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in creating celestial bodies like stars, which serve as navigational aids in the darkness of both land and sea, illustrating Allah's guidance and the signs He has provided for those who reflect and possess true knowledge.

translation: And it is He who created you from one soul and [gave you] a place of dwelling and a place of storage [i.e., the womb and the earth]. We have certainly detailed the signs for a people who understand.
interpretation: This verse underscores the unity of human origin and the divine wisdom in the stages of life, from conception to death, highlighting Allah's meticulous planning and the importance of reflecting on these signs for those who seek true understanding.

translation: And it is He who sends down from the heavens rain, and We bring forth thereby the growth of all things. We bring forth from it greenery from which We bring forth grains arranged in layers. And from the palm trees—of their spathe come forth clusters hanging low. And [We produce] gardens of grapevines and olives and pomegranates, similar [in kind] and different [in variety]. Look at its fruit when it yields and its ripeness. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate and diverse signs of Allah’s creation, emphasizing the need for reflection and belief. The mention of different fruits—some similar in kind yet varied in form—serves as a reminder of the unity of the Creator amidst the diversity of His signs, urging believers to recognize the wisdom and power behind creation as a basis for faith.

translation: And they have attributed to Allah partners from among the jinn, while He created them, and they have fabricated for Him sons and daughters without any knowledge. Exalted is He and high above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse condemns the pre-Islamic Arabian polytheistic belief that associated the jinn with Allah as partners and attributed to Him offspring (sons and daughters) without any divine revelation or rational basis. It emphasizes Allah's absolute transcendence and purity from such false and ignorant attributions, affirming His uniqueness and supremacy in creation and divinity.

translation: Originator of the heavens and the earth. How could He have a son when He does not have a wife? And He created all things, and He is, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute Oneness and uniqueness of Allah (Tawheed), negating any anthropomorphic or human-like qualities attributed to Him, such as having offspring, which would imply a need for a partner or imperfection.

translation: Such is Allah, your Lord; there is no god except Him, the Creator of all things, so worship Him. And He is, over all things, a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah, asserting that He alone is the true God and the Creator of everything, thereby negating any other deity or power. It commands exclusive worship of Allah, highlighting that all affairs are entrusted to His will and control, reinforcing the concept of tawheed (monotheism) in both belief and practice.

translation: No vision can grasp Him, but His grasp is over all vision. He is the Most Subtle, the All-Aware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence of Allah beyond human perception and comprehension, while affirming His perfect knowledge and awareness of all things, including what lies beyond the reach of human sight.

translation: There has come to you enlightenment from your Lord. So whoever sees, it is for his own benefit; and whoever is blind, it is to his own detriment. And I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of individual responsibility in Islam, emphasizing that divine guidance is clear and accessible to all, but each person must choose to recognize and follow it. The consequences of one's choices—whether to accept or reject the truth—are borne solely by the individual, not imposed by external forces or intermediaries.

translation: And thus do We diversify the verses so that they may say, "You have studied," and so that We may make it clear for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in presenting the Qur'anic verses in varied forms—some clear and some allegorical—so that those who are sincere and knowledgeable may discern the truth, while others, out of arrogance or ignorance, may dismiss it as mere human contrivance.

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord. There is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him, and turn away from the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to divine revelation and monotheism, while also instructing the Prophet to distance himself from those who associate partners with Allah, highlighting the necessity of maintaining purity in faith and avoiding compromise with idolatry.

translation: And if Allah had willed, they would not have associated [anything]. And We have not made you over them a guardian, and you are not a manager over them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of free will and divine justice, affirming that Allah does not force anyone to believe or associate partners with Him. Instead, He allows people to make their own choices, and they will be held accountable for those choices on the Day of Judgment. The role of the Prophet (peace be upon him) is not to compel belief but to convey the message, as guidance is ultimately in Allah’s hands.

translation: And do not insult those they invoke besides Allah, lest they insult Allah in enmity without knowledge. Thus We have made pleasing to every community their deeds. Then to their Lord is their return, and He will inform them of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of respectful dialogue and restraint in matters of faith, warning against provoking others in ways that could lead to blasphemy or deeper enmity. It highlights the divine wisdom in allowing diverse paths to unfold, while ultimately emphasizing that all actions will be accounted for by Allah, who alone has perfect knowledge and justice.

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them, they would surely believe in it. Say, 'The signs are only with Allah.' And what makes you know that even if a sign came, they would not believe?
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and stubbornness of those who demand miracles or signs as a condition for faith, while their hearts are already closed to the truth. It underscores that true belief is not contingent on external proofs but on the sincerity of the heart and submission to Allah's will.

translation: And We turn their hearts and their sight aside, as they did not believe in it the first time, and We leave them in their transgression, blundering blindly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hardening of hearts and the blinding of sight as a consequence of persistent disbelief and arrogance, illustrating the divine response to those who reject the truth despite clear signs, leaving them in a state of confusion and moral decline.

translation: And even if We had sent down to them the angels, and the dead had spoken to them, and We had gathered all things before them, they would not have believed unless Allah had willed. But most of them are ignorant.
interpretation: This verse underscores the fundamental principle in Islamic theology that faith is ultimately a matter of divine will and not merely the result of empirical evidence or supernatural signs. It highlights the limits of human perception and the sovereignty of Allah’s decree, while also critiquing the arrogance of those who demand proof as a condition for belief, despite their persistent rejection of guidance.

translation: And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy - devils from mankind and jinn, inspiring one another with adorned speech by way of deception. But if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they invent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind allowing evil forces and deceivers to exist, despite their harmful intentions, as a test of faith and a means to distinguish truth from falsehood for humanity.

translation: And so that the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter may incline to it, and that they may be pleased with it, and that they may commit what they are committing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inclination of disbelievers towards worldly desires and their rejection of the Hereafter, which leads them to persist in their sinful actions, as they are content with their choices and find no need for accountability in the afterlife.

translation: Shall I seek a judge other than Allah when it is He who has sent down to you the Book fully detailed? Those to whom We gave the Book know it is sent down from your Lord in truth, so never be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority of Allah as the sole source of divine guidance and judgment, rejecting any alternative or human-derived systems that claim to supersede His revealed law. It affirms the Qur'an's completeness and veracity, calling upon those who possess prior scriptures to recognize its divine origin, thereby urging believers to reject doubt and place unwavering trust in Allah's revelation.

translation: And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice. None can alter His words, and He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute certainty and unchangeable nature of Allah's decrees and promises, emphasizing that His words are the embodiment of truth and justice, immune to alteration or distortion, reflecting His perfect knowledge and wisdom.

translation: And if you obey most of those on earth, they will lead you astray from the way of Allah. They follow nothing but assumption, and they are not but falsifying.
interpretation: This verse warns against blindly following the majority or popular opinion, especially when it contradicts divine guidance, as people often rely on conjecture rather than truth. It highlights the danger of deviation from the path of Allah due to human whims and baseless claims.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His path, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's perfect knowledge of human guidance and misguidance, affirming that He alone possesses absolute awareness of who follows the truth and who deviates from it, underscoring the importance of sincere intention and divine guidance in one's path.

translation: So eat of that [meat] over which the name of Allah has been mentioned, if you are believers in His signs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permissibility of consuming lawful food that has been dedicated to Allah through the mention of His name, reinforcing the importance of faith in divine signs and the sanctity of halal provisions in a believer's life.

translation: And why should you not eat of that upon which the name of Allah has been mentioned, when He has explained in detail to you what He has forbidden to you, except what you are compelled to [eat]? And indeed, many lead [others] astray through their [own] inclinations without knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of recognizing divine guidance over human desires, warning against the distortion of religious rulings driven by personal whims rather than divine knowledge, and affirming Allah’s ultimate awareness of those who transgress His limits.

translation: And leave what is apparent of sin and what is concealed. Indeed, those who commit sin will be recompensed for what they used to commit.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of avoiding both outward and hidden sins, highlighting that all actions, whether seen or unseen by others, will be accounted for in the Hereafter.

translation: And do not eat from that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned, for indeed, it is grave disobedience. And indeed, the devils inspire their allies [to dispute] with you. And if you obey them, indeed, you would be associators [of others with Allah].
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of invoking Allah's name before partaking in food, signifying that even mundane acts should be sanctified by remembrance of the Divine. It also warns against heeding the whispers of Satan, who seeks to mislead believers into associating partners with Allah by following corrupt influences, thereby compromising their monotheistic faith.

translation: Is he who was dead and We gave him life and made for him a light by which he walks among the people, like one who is in darkness, never to emerge from it? Thus it is made pleasing to the disbelievers what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the spiritual awakening of a believer, who is guided by divine light, with the spiritual blindness of a disbeliever, who remains trapped in ignorance and sin, unable to escape its consequences.

translation: And thus We have placed within every city the most prominent of its criminals, that they might conspire therein. But they conspire not except against themselves, and they perceive it not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the self-destructive nature of evil plots and conspiracies. Those who engage in such behavior often believe they are outsmarting others, but in reality, their actions only harm themselves, both in this world and the Hereafter, without their even realizing the gravity of their misdeeds.

translation: And when a sign comes to them, they say, "We will not believe until we are given like that which was given to the messengers of Allah." Allah is most knowing of where He places His message. There will afflict those who committed crimes debasement before Allah and a severe punishment for what they used to conspire.
interpretation: This verse critiques the arrogance and skepticism of those who demand miracles or proofs to believe, comparing their stance to the divine wisdom in selecting messengers. It highlights that disbelief often stems from arrogance and conspiracy against truth, warning that such attitudes lead to humiliation and severe punishment in the sight of Allah.

translation: So whoever Allah wants to guide - He expands his breast to [accept] Islam; and whoever He wants to send astray - He makes his breast tight and constricted, as though he is climbing into the sky. Thus does Allah place defilement upon those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the concept of divine guidance and misguidance, emphasizing that Allah's will is the ultimate determinant of whether a person finds guidance or straying. The metaphor of a constricted chest symbolizes the psychological and spiritual distress of those who reject faith, highlighting the internal struggle and discomfort that comes from being distant from divine truth.

translation: And this is the straight path of your Lord. We have detailed the signs for people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and straightforwardness of the path set by Allah, which is Islam. The detailed explanation of the signs (verses) is meant to guide those who are mindful and contemplative, encouraging them to reflect deeply on the guidance provided to attain true understanding and righteousness.

translation: For them will be the Home of Peace (Paradise) with their Lord. And He will be their Protecting Friend because of [the good] they used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate reward for the righteous—eternal peace and security in Paradise, granted by Allah as a direct consequence of their righteous deeds, highlighting divine justice and mercy in rewarding good actions.

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will gather them all together, [and He will say], "O company of jinn, you have [mis]appropriated much of mankind." And their allies among mankind will say, "Our Lord, we benefited from one another, but now give us more time until a specified term." [Allah] will say, "The Fire is your accommodation, wherein you will abide eternally, except what Allah wills. Indeed, your Lord is Wise and Knowing."
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate accountability of both humans and jinn for their mutual exploitation in this world, emphasizing that their temporary alliances and benefits will not spare them from divine justice. The exception mentioned ('except what Allah wills') underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty and mercy, reminding that even in punishment, His wisdom prevails.

translation: And thus We let some of the wrongdoers have power over others because of what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine justice, where Allah allows oppressors to face the consequences of their own actions, either in this life or the Hereafter, as part of a greater moral and spiritual balance.

translation: O company of jinn and mankind, did there not come to you messengers from among you, relating to you My verses and warning you of the encounter of this Day of yours?
interpretation: This verse underscores the accountability of both humans and jinn, emphasizing that divine guidance was conveyed to them through messengers from their own kind, yet many were deceived by the fleeting allure of worldly life, leading to their denial and self-imposed condemnation.

translation: That is because your Lord would not destroy the towns unjustly while their people were heedless.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, affirming that Allah does not punish communities without cause, especially when they are unaware or neglectful of their wrongdoings. It highlights the balance between accountability and mercy in divine judgment.

translation: And for all there are degrees [of reward and punishment] for what they have done. And your Lord is not unaware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, affirming that every individual will be recompensed according to their deeds, with no injustice or oversight from Allah. It serves as a reminder of accountability, emphasizing that actions—whether good or evil—are meticulously recorded and will be justly rewarded or punished in the Hereafter.

translation: And your Lord is the Free of need, the Owner of Mercy. If He wills, He can do away with you and replace you with whomever He wills, just as He produced you from the descendants of another people.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty and independence from His creation, emphasizing that human existence is entirely dependent on His will. It serves as a reminder of human humility and the transient nature of life, cautioning against arrogance or assuming permanence in this world.

translation: Indeed, what you are promised will come to pass, and you cannot escape it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine retribution or reward, emphasizing that no one can evade the consequences of their actions as decreed by Allah.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. And you are going to know who will have the final and lasting abode. Indeed, it is the wrongdoers who will not succeed.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the consequences of one's actions. It serves as a reminder that no matter the disparity in worldly power or influence, ultimate success lies with those who uphold righteousness and refrain from oppression, as divine justice will prevail in the end.

translation: And they assign to Allah a share of the crops and cattle which He has created, and they say, 'This is for Allah,' according to their claim, 'and this is for our partners [idols].' But what is for their partners does not reach Allah, and what is for Allah reaches their partners. Evil is their judgment.
interpretation: This verse critiques the hypocritical and self-serving religious practices of those who claim to worship Allah but allocate portions of their wealth to idols or false deities, believing these allocations will benefit their idols. The verse exposes the absurdity of their logic, as they deny their idols the share Allah provides while expecting Allah to accept what they withhold from Him. It highlights the inconsistency and injustice in their approach, where they manipulate religious obligations to serve their own interests rather than submitting sincerely to Allah.

translation: And thus it has been made appealing to many of the polytheists the killing of their children, [a practice] shared by their partners [in idolatry], so that they may ruin them and confuse their religion. And if Allah had willed, they would not have done so. So leave them and what they invent.
interpretation: This verse addresses the pre-Islamic Arab practice of female infanticide, often justified by superstitious beliefs or societal pressures. It highlights how false deities (shuraka')—whom the polytheists associated with Allah—encouraged such heinous acts, distorting their moral and religious compass. The verse underscores Allah’s absolute power: had He willed, such practices would not have occurred, emphasizing that human deviation from divine guidance stems from their own choices, not Allah’s decree. The command to 'leave them and what they invent' reflects divine patience, allowing wrongdoers to face the consequences of their actions while affirming Allah’s justice.

translation: And they say, 'These are cattle and crops forbidden [for sacrifice]—none may eat them except whom We will,' by their claim. And [they declare] cattle to be forbidden to ride, and cattle upon which the name of Allah is not mentioned—they invent a lie against Him. He will punish them for what they were inventing.
interpretation: This verse critiques those who falsely attribute restrictions to Allah's law, claiming certain animals or crops are forbidden for consumption or use without divine sanction, or inventing prohibitions on riding certain animals or invoking Allah's name on them. It highlights the gravity of fabricating lies against Allah, warning of divine retribution for such deceit.

translation: And they say, 'What is within the wombs of these livestock is exclusively for our males and forbidden to our wives. But if it is a stillbirth, then all are partners in it.' He will punish them for their description. Indeed, He is Wise and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the superstitious and unjust practices of some pre-Islamic Arabs who imposed arbitrary restrictions on livestock, claiming that certain offspring were exclusively for men while denying women any share, even in cases of stillbirth where all would logically share the loss. The verse condemns such discriminatory and illogical rulings, affirming that Allah will justly recompense people for their false claims and unjust divisions, as He is fully aware of their intentions and actions.

translation: Indeed, they have lost who killed their children in foolishness without knowledge and forbade what Allah had provided for them, inventing a lie against Allah. They have certainly gone astray, and they were not [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse condemns the pre-Islamic practice of killing children, particularly daughters, out of ignorance and superstition, as well as the false attribution of prohibitions on lawful provisions from Allah, reflecting a distortion of divine guidance driven by cultural or personal whims rather than divine command.

translation: And it is He who produces gardens trellised and untrellised, and the palm trees, and crops of different kinds, and olives, and pomegranates, similar and dissimilar. Eat of its fruit when it yields, and give its due on the day of harvest, and do not waste. Indeed, He does not like the wasteful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom in creating diverse forms of sustenance, encouraging gratitude and moderation in consumption, while reminding humans of their duty to share their blessings with others.

translation: And [He created] the grazing livestock - some for carrying loads and others for [mere] slaughter. Eat what Allah has provided for you [which is lawful] and do not follow the footsteps of Satan. Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the lawful and unlawful in sustenance, distinguishing between what is permissible for consumption (like grazing livestock) and what is not, while warning against following the deceptive paths of Satan, who seeks to lead people astray from divine guidance.

translation: Eight pairs: of the sheep, two; and of the goats, two. Say, "Has He forbidden the two males or the two females or that which the wombs of the two females contain? Inform me with knowledge, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges the arbitrary and baseless prohibitions imposed by the pre-Islamic Arabs on certain livestock, particularly regarding gender and offspring, which lacked any rational or divine justification. It calls into question the legitimacy of such prohibitions by demanding evidence for their claims, thereby exposing the irrationality and superstition underlying their practices.

translation: And from the camels, two; and from the cattle, two. Say, "Is it the two males He has forbidden or the two females, or what the wombs of the two females contain? Or were you witnesses when Allah charged you with this? Then who could be more unjust than he who invents a lie against Allah to lead people astray without knowledge? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse challenges the arbitrary and baseless restrictions imposed by some people on permissible and impermissible food, attributing these restrictions to Allah without divine revelation or sound reasoning. It underscores the gravity of falsely attributing lies to Allah, as such actions mislead people without knowledge, highlighting the severe injustice of those who do so.

translation: Say, 'I do not find within what has been revealed to me [anything] forbidden to one who would eat it unless it be a dead animal, or blood spilled out, or the flesh of swine - for indeed, it is impure - or it be [that slaughtered in] disobedience, dedicated to other than Allah.' But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse establishes the general principles of permissible and forbidden food in Islam, emphasizing that prohibitions are based on divine revelation rather than human whim. The exceptions granted under necessity highlight Allah's mercy and understanding of human frailty, ensuring that survival does not become a source of sin when one is compelled by circumstances beyond their control.

translation: And to those who are Jews, We have forbidden every animal with claws, and of the cattle and the sheep, We have forbidden them their fat, except what adheres to their backs or the entrails, or what is mixed with bone. Thus did We recompense them for their rebellion. Indeed, We are Truthful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of transgression and rebellion against divine commandments, illustrating that God's decrees are just and that disobedience leads to specific prohibitions as a form of punishment or purification.

translation: But if they deny you, [O Muhammad], say, "Your Lord is a possessor of extensive mercy, but His punishment cannot be repelled from the people who commit crimes."
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah's mercy is vast and encompassing, but it also serves as a warning that divine punishment is inevitable for those who persist in injustice and denial, emphasizing the balance between Allah's mercy and justice.

translation: Those who associate others with Allah will say, "If Allah had willed, we would not have associated (anything with Him), nor would our fathers, nor would we have forbidden anything." Likewise, those before them denied until they tasted Our punishment. Say, "Do you have any knowledge you can produce for us? You follow nothing but assumption, and you are only making conjectures."
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of blaming divine decree for one's own misguided actions, as it highlights the persistent denial of truth by those who associate partners with Allah, despite clear evidence and warnings. It serves as a reminder that divine will does not absolve humans of responsibility for their choices, and that reliance on conjecture or false assumptions—rather than divine guidance—leads to ruin.

translation: Say, 'For Allah is the conclusive argument. If He had willed, He would have guided you all.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that divine guidance is ultimately in Allah's hands, and the responsibility of humans is to present the truth clearly, not to force acceptance. It underscores the sovereignty of Allah's will in matters of guidance and the limits of human agency in determining the faith of others.

translation: Say, 'Bring forward your witnesses who can testify that Allah has forbidden this.' Then if they testify, do not testify with them. And do not follow the desires of those who deny Our verses and those who do not believe in the Hereafter, while they ascribe equals to their Lord.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of adhering to divine commandments over personal desires or societal pressures, even when faced with false testimony or denial of truth. It warns against aligning with those who reject divine signs and prioritize worldly desires over faith in the Hereafter, emphasizing the need for steadfastness in truth and divine justice.

translation: Say, 'Come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden to you. [He commands] that you not associate anything with Him, and to parents, good treatment, and do not kill your children out of poverty; We will provide for you and them. And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed. And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [to be killed] except by [legal] right.' This is what He has instructed you that you might use reason.
interpretation: This verse encapsulates foundational ethical and moral principles in Islam, emphasizing monotheism, filial piety, the sanctity of life, and the avoidance of sin. It underscores the idea that human life, including that of children, is sacred and not to be taken without just cause, while also highlighting Allah's role as the ultimate Provider. The command to avoid immoralities, whether overt or hidden, reflects a holistic approach to moral conduct, ensuring both outward actions and inward intentions are aligned with divine guidance.

translation: And do not approach the property of an orphan, except in the best manner, until he reaches his maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice. We do not burden any soul beyond its capacity. And when you speak, be just, even if [it concerns] a near relative. And fulfill the covenant of Allah. That is what He has enjoined upon you so that you may remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice, fairness, and ethical conduct in financial and social dealings, particularly concerning the most vulnerable in society, such as orphans. It underscores that one must act in the best interest of others, even in seemingly minor matters like speech, and uphold commitments made to Allah. The overarching message is that true faith is reflected in how one treats others and fulfills their duties with integrity and compassion.

translation: And this is My path, straight, so follow it; and do not follow [other] ways, lest they scatter you from His way. That is what He has enjoined upon you, that you may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering strictly to the straight path of Islam, as prescribed by Allah, and warns against deviating into alternative paths or ideologies that may lead to confusion, division, or loss of the true guidance.

translation: Then We gave Moses the Book, perfect for the one who does good, and detailing all things, and as guidance and mercy, that they might believe in the encounter with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine perfection and comprehensiveness of the guidance provided through revelation, emphasizing that true goodness is rewarded with clarity and mercy, and that the ultimate purpose of this guidance is to foster unwavering faith in the Hereafter and the meeting with Allah.

translation: And this is a blessed Book which We have sent down, so follow it and fear Allah (have taqwa), that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and blessed nature of the Qur'an, urging believers to adhere to its guidance and live in conscious awareness of Allah (taqwa) as a means to attain His mercy.

translation: Lest you say, "The Book was only revealed to two groups before us, and we were unaware of their studies."
interpretation: This verse warns against the arrogance of believing that divine guidance is exclusively for certain groups while others are left in ignorance, emphasizing that God's message is universal and accessible to all who seek it with sincerity.

translation: Or [do they say], "If only a Book had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than they." But there has come to you a clear evidence from your Lord, a guidance and a mercy. So who is more unjust than he who denies the signs of Allah and turns away from them? We will recompense those who turn away from Our signs with the worst punishment for their turning away.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of demanding additional divine signs as proof when clear guidance has already been provided, and it warns against the arrogance of claiming superiority over others while rejecting Allah's signs.

translation: Do they await except that the angels come to them or your Lord comes, or that some of the signs of your Lord come? The day some of the signs of your Lord come, it will not benefit a soul to believe then, nor will it be accepted from it if it had believed before and did good deeds. Say, 'Wait, for indeed we are waiting.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute certainty of divine accountability and the finality of judgment, emphasizing that faith and righteous deeds must precede the signs of the Hour; once these signs manifest, it will be too late for repentance or acceptance of faith, as the opportunity for meaningful action will have passed.

translation: Indeed, those who have divided their religion and become sects, you [O Muhammad] have nothing to do with them. Their affair is only [left] to Allah; then He will inform them about what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of divisiveness within the faith and the futility of sectarianism, emphasizing that such fragmentation is contrary to the unity and purity of true monotheistic submission (Islam). It serves as a warning against creating divisions based on differing interpretations or personal desires, as ultimate accountability lies with Allah alone, who will judge all actions with absolute justice.

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like, and whoever comes with an evil deed will not be recompensed except with its equivalent—they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and mercy, where good deeds are multiplied manifold while evil deeds are met with just recompense, ensuring no injustice is done to anyone.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord has guided me to a straight path—a correct religion, the way of Abraham, inclining toward truth. And he was not of those who associate others with Allah.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism (Tawheed) and the rejection of associating partners with Allah, highlighting Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) as a model of pure faith and devotion to the one true God.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my prayer, my rites of sacrifice, my living and my dying are for Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute devotion and submission of a believer to Allah alone, encompassing all aspects of life—worship, rituals, daily activities, and even death—affirming that nothing is done except for His sake and under His sovereignty.

translation: There is no partner with Him. And to this I have been commanded, and I am the first of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah (Tawheed), rejecting any form of association or partnership with Him. It also highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) submission to this fundamental principle and his role as the first Muslim, setting an example for all believers to follow.

translation: Say, 'Shall I seek a lord other than Allah while He is the Lord of all things? And every soul earns not [anything] except against itself, nor does any bearer of burdens bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you concerning that over which you used to differ.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah, rejecting any association of partners with Him. It underscores individual accountability, where each person is responsible for their own deeds and cannot bear the burden of another's sins. The return to Allah on the Day of Judgment ensures that all disputes and differences will be resolved with divine justice, revealing the truth behind past disagreements.

translation: And it is He who has made you successors upon the earth and has raised some of you above others in degrees [of rank] that He may test you through what He has provided you. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty, but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom behind the natural hierarchy and diversity in human society, emphasizing that such distinctions are tests of responsibility and character, not grounds for arrogance or oppression, while reminding that divine justice is both swift in accountability and boundless in mercy.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Alif, Lam, Meem, Sad.
interpretation: The opening of this surah (chapter) begins with the basmala, affirming Allah's attributes of mercy and compassion, followed by the mention of certain Arabic letters (Alif, Lam, Meem, Sad). These letters, known as 'muqatta'at' (disjointed letters), appear at the beginning of several surahs and serve as a reminder of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, challenging humanity to produce something similar while also indicating that the true meaning of these letters is known only to Allah.

translation: This is a Book revealed to you, so let there be no burden in your chest from it, that you may warn thereby and [it is] a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that the Qur'an is a divine revelation meant to guide humanity, and he should not feel burdened by its responsibility, as its primary purpose is to serve as a warning to those who disbelieve and a source of guidance and remembrance for the believers.

translation: Follow what has been revealed to you from your Lord and do not follow other than Him any allies. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of adhering strictly to divine guidance as the ultimate source of truth and authority, warning against seeking support or guidance from anything or anyone besides Allah, as doing so reflects a lack of remembrance of His sovereignty and wisdom.

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed, so Our punishment came to it by night or while they were taking their midday rest.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the inevitability of divine retribution for those who persist in disbelief and defiance of God's guidance, emphasizing that punishment can strike unexpectedly, regardless of the time or circumstances.

translation: But their cry was only that they said, "Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the belated acknowledgment of wrongdoing by those who faced divine punishment, emphasizing that true repentance must precede the onset of punishment, not follow it as a desperate reaction.

translation: So let us ask those to whom [the message] was sent, and [let us] ask the messengers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of accountability and the certainty of divine justice, implying that both the recipients of the message and the messengers themselves will be questioned about their roles and responses, reinforcing the inevitability of divine judgment.

translation: We will certainly relate to them [Our message] with knowledge, and We were not absent [from them].
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's complete awareness and meticulous recording of all human actions and events, ensuring that nothing escapes His knowledge or justice, reinforcing the inevitability of accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: And the weighing [of deeds] that Day is the truth. So whoever's scales are heavy, those are the successful ones.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of the Divine Judgment, where every individual's deeds are weighed with perfect accuracy. The 'heaviness' of the scales symbolizes the preponderance of righteous deeds and sincerity in faith, which lead to ultimate success in the Hereafter.

translation: But whoever's scales are light - it is they who have lost themselves, for they wronged Our signs.
interpretation: This verse warns against the consequences of disregarding divine guidance and the signs of truth, emphasizing that those who reject or distort them will face spiritual ruin and eternal loss.

translation: And We have certainly established you upon the earth and made for you therein ways of livelihood. Little do you thank [Me].
interpretation: This verse highlights humanity's ungratefulness despite being granted sustenance, resources, and opportunities for prosperity on Earth. It underscores the importance of recognizing divine blessings and expressing gratitude, as ingratitude is a fundamental flaw in human nature.

translation: And We have certainly created you, [O mankind], and given you [human] form. Then We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He was not of those who prostrated.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between divine command and human free will, illustrating the consequences of arrogance and disobedience. Iblees' refusal to prostrate, despite the clear command, underscores the peril of prioritizing personal pride over submission to Allah's will, serving as a timeless warning against the dangers of spiritual rebellion.

translation: Allah said, 'What prevented you from prostrating when I commanded you?' [Satan] said, 'I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the root of arrogance and disobedience, where Satan's refusal to prostrate to Adam stemmed from his self-perceived superiority based on his origin (fire) over Adam's (clay). It underscores the danger of judging others by worldly standards rather than divine command, revealing how pride can lead to rebellion against Allah's will.

translation: He said, "Descend from it! It is not for you to be arrogant therein. So get out; indeed, you are of the debased."
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of arrogance and disobedience to divine command, illustrating that such traits lead to humiliation and expulsion from divine favor.

translation: He said, "Grant me respite until the Day they are raised up."
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and defiance of Iblis (Satan) towards Allah's command, seeking an extension of time to mislead humanity until the Day of Resurrection, demonstrating his rebellion and the extent of his enmity towards mankind.

translation: Indeed, you are of those given respite.
interpretation: This verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly life and the illusion of security, reminding that no one, not even the most arrogant or defiant, is exempt from the eventual return to Allah and the accountability of their deeds.

translation: He said, 'Then by Your misguidance of me, I will surely sit in wait for them on Your straight path.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the cunning and deceitful strategy of Iblis (Satan) to mislead humans away from the path of righteousness, exploiting their weaknesses and vulnerabilities after their creation.

translation: Then I will come to them from before them and from behind them and from their right and from their left, and You will not find most of them grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent and multifaceted nature of Satan's (Iblis) efforts to mislead humanity, as he attempts to approach people from all directions—front, back, left, and right—to divert them from the path of truth and gratitude to Allah. The mention of most people not being grateful underscores the challenge of maintaining steadfastness and recognition of Allah's blessings in the face of constant temptation and distraction.

translation: He said, 'Go out of it, despised and banished. As for those of them who follow you, I will surely fill Hell with you all.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the eternal consequence of defiance against divine command, highlighting the irrevocable punishment for those who persist in rebellion and lead others astray, emphasizing the severity of divine justice and the finality of the consequences for such actions.

translation: And [O Muhammad], tell them the story of] O Adam, dwell, you and your wife, in Paradise and eat from wherever you will but do not approach this tree, lest you be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of free will within divinely ordained boundaries, illustrating that while humans are granted considerable latitude in their choices, transgressing explicit divine limits leads to moral and spiritual consequences, as seen in the fall of Adam and Eve from their state of grace.

translation: Then Satan whispered to them to make apparent to them that which was concealed from them of their private parts. He said, "Your Lord did not forbid you this tree except that you become angels or become of the immortal."
