interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive tactics of Satan, who exploits human vulnerability and desire for power to lead them astray. It underscores the idea that temptation often preys on our aspirations and insecurities, presenting false promises (like immortality or elevated status) to justify disobedience, thereby revealing the destructive nature of deception and the importance of steadfastness in faith.

translation: And I swear by Allah, I am indeed one of the sincere advisors to both of you.
interpretation: This verse reflects the deceptive nature of Iblis (Satan) as he outwardly presents himself as a well-wisher while concealing his true malicious intent, highlighting the importance of discernment and not being misled by appearances.

translation: So Satan misled them by deception. And when they both tasted the tree, their shameful parts became apparent to them, and they began to fasten upon themselves the leaves of Paradise. And their Lord called out to them, "Did I not forbid you from that tree, and did I not say to you that Satan is to you a clear enemy?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of succumbing to deception and disobedience to divine commandments. It underscores the loss of innocence and the onset of shame and self-consciousness as a result of yielding to temptation, while also emphasizing the role of Satan as a persistent and clear enemy of humanity.

translation: They said, "Our Lord, we have wronged ourselves, and if You do not forgive us and have mercy upon us, we will surely be among the losers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the essence of repentance and the acknowledgment of one's own faults before Allah, coupled with a plea for His mercy and forgiveness. It underscores the human condition of fallibility and the necessity of seeking divine pardon, as well as the dire consequences of failing to do so.

translation: He said, "Go down, being to one another enemies. And for you on the earth is a place of settlement and provision for a time."
interpretation: This verse underscores the dual nature of human existence after the fall of Adam (peace be upon him)—a life marked by both enmity and struggle (due to the influence of Satan) and a temporary abode where humans must strive for sustenance and moral growth until the appointed time of their return to Allah.

translation: From it (the earth) you are brought to life, in it you die, and from it you will be raised.
interpretation: This verse underscores the cyclical nature of human existence—birth, death, and resurrection—all tied to the earth as the origin and final resting place of humanity, emphasizing divine power over life and death.

translation: O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your shame and as an adornment; but the clothing of righteousness - that is best. That is one of the signs of Allah so that they may be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and righteousness as fundamental aspects of human dignity and spiritual well-being, highlighting that true adornment lies not in outward appearances but in inner virtue.

translation: O children of Adam, let not Satan deceive you as he brought your parents out of Paradise, stripping them of their clothing to expose their shame to them. Indeed, he sees you—he and his tribe—from where you do not see them. Indeed, We have made the devils allies to those who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against the deceptive tactics of Satan, who seeks to mislead humanity by exploiting their vulnerabilities, just as he did with Adam and Eve. It highlights Satan's persistent enmity toward humans and his ability to influence those who are spiritually weak or lack faith. The verse also underscores the unseen nature of Satan's influence, emphasizing the need for vigilance and reliance on faith to resist his temptations.

translation: And when they commit an immorality, they say, 'We found our fathers doing it, and Allah has ordered us to do it.' Say, 'Indeed, Allah does not order immorality. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?',
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of justifying sinful actions by blindly following ancestral traditions without questioning their validity in light of divine guidance, emphasizing that Allah does not command immorality and that attributing such orders to Him is a grave falsehood.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'My Lord has ordered justice. And [He orders] that you maintain yourselves upon [every] mosque, and invoke Him, being sincere to Him in religion.' Just as He originated you, you will return [to Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute necessity of justice ('qist') as a divine command, underscoring that justice is not merely a moral virtue but a fundamental obligation in worship and daily life. It also highlights the importance of sincerity ('ikhlas') in worship, directing believers to purify their intentions solely for Allah, without associating partners or ulterior motives. The reminder of returning to Allah ('ta'udun') serves as a profound call to accountability, urging constant mindfulness of the Hereafter in all actions.

translation: As for the guided group, they are guided for a purpose, and as for the misguided group, misguidance is their due. Indeed, they have taken the devils as allies instead of Allah while thinking that they are guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who are truly guided by divine truth and those who are led astray by their own choices or the influence of evil forces. It underscores the accountability of individuals for their beliefs and actions, as well as the deceptive nature of misguidance, where people may falsely believe they are on the right path while being ensnared by falsehood.

translation: O children of Adam, take your adornment at every place of prayer, and eat and drink, but do not be excessive. Indeed, He does not like those who are excessive.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes moderation in all aspects of life, including worship, sustenance, and personal conduct, while discouraging extravagance and wastefulness, as they are contrary to the values of balance and gratitude.

translation: Say, 'Who has forbidden the adornment of Allah which He has produced for His servants and the good things of provision?' Say, 'They are for those who believe during the life of this world, [and] exclusively [for them] on the Day of Resurrection.' Thus do We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse underscores the permissibility of enjoying the adornments and provisions that Allah has created for His servants, emphasizing that these blessings are lawful and pure for believers in this world and will be exclusively theirs in the Hereafter, highlighting the distinction between the righteous and others.

translation: Say, 'My Lord has only forbidden immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed - and sin, and oppression without right, and that you associate with Allah that for which He has not sent down authority, and that you say about Allah what you do not know.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute prohibition of major sins and transgressions, emphasizing that divine law encompasses both overt and hidden forms of wrongdoing, including idolatry, false accusations against Allah, and unjust oppression. It highlights the importance of adhering strictly to revealed guidance and avoiding assumptions or fabrications about Allah’s commands.

translation: And for every community is a [specified] term. And when their time has come, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over time and the predetermined fate of all nations, emphasizing that no individual or community can alter the appointed time of their end, whether by hastening or delaying it.

translation: O children of Adam, if there come to you messengers from among yourselves, reciting to you My verses, then whoever is righteous and reforms—there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of heeding divine guidance when it is presented by righteous messengers, highlighting that righteous conduct and reform lead to spiritual security and freedom from fear and sorrow.

translation: But those who denied Our signs and were arrogant toward them - those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequence of rejecting divine guidance due to arrogance or disbelief, emphasizing that such defiance leads to eternal punishment in Hell, highlighting the gravity of rejecting truth when it is clearly presented.

translation: So who is more unjust than one who invents a lie about Allah or denies His signs? Those will have their share [of punishment] decreed for them until when Our messengers come to them to take them in death, they will say, "Where are those you used to invoke besides Allah?" They will say, "They have strayed from us," and they will bear witness against themselves that they were disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate injustice of attributing falsehood to Allah or rejecting His signs, warning that such denial leads to a state of spiritual blindness where even the intercessors one once invoked are abandoned, and the truth of one's disbelief becomes undeniable in the face of divine justice.

translation: It was said, "Enter the nations before you of jinn and mankind into the Fire." Every time a nation entered, it cursed its sister until, when they had all gathered therein, the later of them said to the former, "Our Lord, these led us astray, so give them a double punishment of the Fire." He said, "For each is a double, but you do not know."
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of divine punishment, where each individual bears responsibility only for their own deeds, yet the mutual influence of wrongdoing among people is acknowledged. The 'double punishment' does not imply that one person's sins are literally doubled onto another, but rather highlights the compounded consequences of leading others astray, as both the misleader and the misled will face their own just recompense. The verse also subtly warns against the dangers of blindly following others without personal accountability.

translation: And the first of them said to the last of them, 'There is no favor for you over us, so taste the punishment for what you used to earn.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment in the Hereafter when the arrogant and oppressive leaders of the past, who had misled others, disclaim any responsibility for their followers, asserting that their followers' suffering is solely due to their own deeds, not the leaders' influence. It underscores the absolute justice of Allah, where no one bears the burden of another's sins, and individuals are held accountable only for their own actions.

translation: Indeed, those who deny Our verses and are arrogant toward them - the gates of the heavens will not be opened for them, nor will they enter Paradise until a camel enters into the eye of a needle. And thus do We recompense the criminals.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of rejecting divine truth and arrogance toward God's signs, illustrating the impossibility of the wicked attaining Paradise through their own merit, just as a camel cannot pass through the eye of a needle—a metaphor for the absolute impossibility of their entry into Heaven.

translation: For them will be a bed of Hellfire and over them coverings (of fire). Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of punishment for the wrongdoers (الظالمين), illustrating that their torment is all-encompassing—both beneath and above them—leaving no escape from divine justice, reflecting the absolute and inescapable nature of Allah’s retribution for those who persist in oppression and injustice.

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds—We charge no soul except [within] its capacity—they are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's justice and mercy, ensuring that no one is burdened beyond their capacity, while highlighting the eternal reward of Paradise for the believers who strive to do good deeds.

translation: And We will remove whatever rancor is in their breasts; streams will flow beneath them. And they will say, 'Praise to Allah, who has guided us to this. We would never have been guided if Allah had not guided us. Certainly, the messengers of our Lord came with the truth.' And it will be proclaimed to them, 'This is Paradise, which you have been made to inherit for what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the transformative power of divine guidance and the ultimate justice of Allah, where He purifies the believers' hearts from any ill feelings, such as envy or resentment, and rewards them with Paradise based on their righteous deeds, underscoring the necessity of divine guidance in attaining true guidance and the certainty of Allah's justice.

translation: And the companions of Paradise will call out to the companions of the Fire, 'We have found what our Lord promised us to be true. Have you [companions of the Fire] found what your Lord promised to be true?' They will say, 'Yes.' Then a herald will announce among them, 'The curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers,'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute certainty of divine justice and the fulfillment of Allah’s promises, contrasting the rewards of the righteous with the punishment of the wrongdoers, and highlighting the unbridgeable divide between Paradise and Hell.

translation: Those who hinder [others] from the way of Allah and seek to make it [seem] crooked, while they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who actively obstruct the path of truth and righteousness, distorting its true nature, and reject the concept of accountability in the Hereafter, demonstrating their disbelief in divine justice and the ultimate consequences of their actions.

translation: And between them will be a barrier. And on the A'raf will be men who recognize each of them by their mark. They will call out to the companions of Paradise, 'Peace be upon you.' They have not [yet] entered it, but they long for it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine justice and the recognition of individuals based on their deeds, as those on the A'raf (a boundary between Paradise and Hell) are able to identify others by their 'marks'—symbolic of their righteous or wicked deeds—demonstrating that actions in this life leave an indelible imprint on the soul.

translation: And when their eyes are turned toward the companions of the Fire, they say, "Our Lord, do not place us with the wrongdoing people."
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of realization for the inhabitants of Paradise when they see the dwellers of Hell, prompting them to express gratitude and seek refuge in Allah from being among the oppressors, underscoring the stark contrast between the two groups and the consequences of their actions.

translation: And the companions of the Heights will call out to men [whom they recognize] by their marks, saying, "What did your gathering and your arrogance avail you?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of realization and regret for those who were arrogant and unjust in the worldly life, as they witness the consequences of their actions and the futility of their previous pride and alliances when it is too late to change their fate.

translation: Are these the ones upon whom you swore that Allah would never grant them mercy? [Enter and stay in] Paradise; you will have no fear, nor will you grieve.
interpretation: This verse serves as a rebuke to those who arrogantly assume that certain people are beyond Allah’s mercy, highlighting the folly of such judgments and affirming that Allah’s mercy encompasses whom He wills, often in ways beyond human perception. It also underscores the ultimate justice and generosity of Paradise, where believers are granted eternal security and freedom from sorrow.

translation: And the companions of the Fire will call to the companions of Paradise, 'Pour upon us some water or from whatever Allah has provided you.' They will say, 'Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the irreversible nature of divine justice in the Hereafter, where the gates of Paradise are permanently closed to the disbelievers, and their pleas for relief are met with the unchanging decree of Allah's justice, emphasizing that salvation is tied to faith and righteousness in this life.

translation: Those who took their religion as amusement and play, and whom the worldly life deluded—so today We will forget them just as they forgot the meeting of this Day of theirs, and [just as] they used to reject Our signs.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against those who treat their faith with frivolity and prioritize worldly pleasures over their spiritual obligations. It highlights the consequences of such neglect, emphasizing that God will reciprocate their indifference by disregarding them on the Day of Judgment, just as they disregarded the signs of God in this life.

translation: And We have certainly brought them a Book which We detailed by knowledge - as guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing its meticulous structure and clarity, which are manifestations of Allah's perfect knowledge. It serves as a guide and a source of mercy specifically for those who embrace faith, highlighting the Qur'an's role in illuminating the path to righteousness and spiritual salvation.

translation: Do they await except its interpretation? The Day its interpretation comes those who had forgotten it before will say, 'Certainly the messengers of our Lord had come with the truth, so will we have any intercessors to intercede for us? Or could we be sent back so we would do other than what we used to do?' They will have lost themselves, and what they used to invent will have departed from them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the finality of the consequences of one's actions. It highlights the human tendency to seek excuses or intercessors when faced with the truth of their deeds, but ultimately, no intercession will avail those who have strayed from righteousness, as their own actions have already determined their fate.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is Allah, who created the heavens and the earth in six days and then established Himself above the Throne. He covers the night with the day, [which] it swiftly pursues, and [He created] the sun, the moon, and the stars, subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and the command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and control over all creation, highlighting His power to bring about the alternation of night and day, the movement of celestial bodies, and the entire order of the universe, all of which serve His divine will and purpose.

translation: Call upon your Lord with humility and in secret. Indeed, He does not like transgressors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere and humble supplication to Allah, away from ostentation and excess. It discourages any form of arrogance or transgression in one's approach to Allah, reminding believers that their prayers should be marked by sincerity, modesty, and a deep sense of submission.

translation: And do not corrupt on earth after its reformation. And call upon Him in fear and hope. Indeed, the mercy of Allah is near to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of maintaining the balance and harmony established by divine order on Earth, warning against actions that disrupt this balance. It also highlights the dual approach to worship—combining reverence (fear of divine displeasure) and aspiration (hope for divine mercy)—as a means to draw closer to Allah, particularly for those who strive to do good.

translation: And it is He who sends the winds as good tidings before His mercy, until when they have carried heavy rainclouds, We drive them to a dead land and send down rain thereby and bring forth thereby [some] of all the fruits. Thus will We bring forth the dead; perhaps you may be reminded.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the power and mercy of Allah in reviving barren land through rain, drawing a parallel to the resurrection of the dead on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing Allah's ability to bring life to what was lifeless as a sign for reflection and remembrance of His ultimate power.

translation: And [as for] the good land, its vegetation emerges by permission of its Lord; but [as for] the bad, nothing emerges except sparsely. Thus do We diversify the signs for a people who are grateful.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the contrast between a receptive heart and a hardened one, using the metaphor of fertile and barren soil to emphasize that divine guidance and blessings flourish only in hearts open to faith and gratitude, while those resistant to truth remain spiritually stagnant.

translation: We sent Noah to his people, so he said: 'O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great Day.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and the urgency of worshipping Him alone, as associating partners with Him (Shirk) is the gravest sin in Islam. Noah's (peace be upon him) message serves as a warning against the consequences of disbelief and disobedience, emphasizing the reality of divine accountability on the Day of Judgment.

translation: The eminent among his people said, "Indeed, we see you in manifest error."
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and stubbornness of the elite who dismiss the truth outright, failing to engage with the message on its merits and instead resorting to personal attacks against the messenger.

translation: He said, 'O my people, there is no error in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) unwavering conviction in his divine mission, affirming his moral uprightness and the authenticity of his message as a direct communication from Allah, not a product of human error or delusion.

translation: I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I advise you, and I know from Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: This verse underscores the prophetic role of conveying divine guidance, offering sincere advice, and possessing knowledge granted by Allah that surpasses human understanding, highlighting the Prophet's (peace be upon him) unique position as a messenger and a source of divine wisdom.

translation: Do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you, to warn you, and that you may fear Allah, so that you may receive mercy?
interpretation: This verse addresses the natural human tendency to question or be skeptical of divine messages delivered through familiar or ordinary means, such as a prophet from their own community. It highlights the purpose of such reminders: to serve as a warning for accountability, to encourage righteousness (taqwa), and ultimately to guide humanity toward divine mercy.

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship, and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a blind people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and the mercy shown to those who believe, while the disbelievers face destruction despite clear signs.

translation: And to the 'Aad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear Him?"
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and the rejection of any form of idolatry, emphasizing that true devotion and fear should be directed solely to Him, as He is the only true deity worthy of worship.

translation: The eminent leaders of his people who disbelieved said, "Indeed, we see you in foolishness, and indeed, we think you are of the liars."
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and closed-mindedness of those who reject truth due to their own biases, attributing foolishness and deceit to the messenger rather than acknowledging the divine guidance he brought.

translation: He said, 'O my people, there is no madness in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet's (peace be upon him) assertion of his sanity and divine mission, rejecting any accusations of madness while affirming his role as a messenger conveying the truth from Allah.

translation: I convey to you the messages of my Lord, and I am to you a sincere advisor.
interpretation: This verse underscores the dual role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as both a conveyor of divine revelation and a sincere advisor to his people, emphasizing his honesty and goodwill in guiding them toward truth and righteousness.

translation: Do you wonder that a reminder has come to you from your Lord through a man from among you, to warn you? And remember when He made you successors after the people of Noah and increased you in creation extensively. So remember the favors of Allah that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of recognizing divine guidance as a mercy rather than an oddity, emphasizing that Allah’s reminders come through chosen messengers to guide humanity. It also highlights the continuity of divine favor, as Allah elevated the status of later generations (like the Children of Israel) after previous nations (like the people of Noah), urging reflection on His blessings to attain success.

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us to worship Allah alone and forsake what our forefathers used to worship? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you are one of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth despite clear evidence, demanding miracles as a condition for belief rather than submitting to divine guidance out of sincere conviction.

translation: He has already revealed to you from your Lord what pollutes [your hearts], and [what causes] wrath. Do you argue with me about names you and your forefathers have invented, for which Allah has sent down no authority? Wait, then, I am waiting with you.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of humanly invented religious practices or names that lack divine sanction, warning against substituting personal or ancestral traditions for revealed truth, and affirming the certainty of divine accountability.

translation: So We saved him and those with him by a mercy from Us, and We destroyed the last remnant of those who denied Our signs. And they were not believers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine mercy extended to the righteous while highlighting the inevitable consequences of persistent disbelief in God's signs, emphasizing that true faith is not merely verbal but must be accompanied by sincere conviction and righteous action.

translation: And to the Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has come to you clear evidence from your Lord. This is the she-camel of Allah [sent] to you as a sign. So leave her to eat within Allah's land and do not touch her with harm, or you will be seized by a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of recognizing divine signs and the consequences of rejecting them, emphasizing the need for humility and obedience to Allah's commands.

translation: And remember when He made you successors after the people of 'Ad and settled you in the land, [granting you] the ability to construct palaces on its plains and to carve homes out of the mountains. Then remember the favors of Allah and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of power and the importance of gratitude and ethical conduct. It highlights that human achievements, no matter how grand, are granted by Allah and should be used responsibly, not for arrogance or oppression, but in acknowledgment of divine favors and in service to justice and balance.

translation: The eminent ones who were arrogant among his people said to those who were oppressed - to those who had believed among them: 'Do you know that Salih (Saleh) has been sent by his Lord?' They said, 'Indeed, we believe in what he has been sent with.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between arrogance and submission to truth. The oppressors' question is not one of genuine inquiry but of mockery, exposing their disbelief despite clear evidence. Meanwhile, the oppressed believers affirm their faith unshaken by the arrogance of the powerful, demonstrating that true conviction is rooted in divine guidance rather than social status or coercion.

translation: Those who were arrogant said, "Indeed, we disbelieve in what you have believed."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who reject faith out of pride rather than genuine conviction, showing that their rejection is rooted in ego rather than truth.

translation: So they hamstrung the she-camel and defied the command of their Lord, saying, 'O Ṣāliḥ, bring us what you threaten us with, if you are truly one of the messengers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the extreme arrogance and defiance of those who reject divine signs despite clear evidence, demanding punishment as a challenge rather than heeding the warning, which reflects a hardened heart that refuses to believe even when confronted with the truth.

translation: So the earthquake seized them, and they became motionless in their homes.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the sudden and overwhelming nature of divine punishment, emphasizing that it can strike swiftly and without warning, leaving no chance for repentance or escape once it has been decreed.

translation: So he turned away from them and said, "O my people, I have certainly conveyed to you the message of my Lord and advised you, but you do not like advisors."
interpretation: This verse highlights the frustration of a prophet when his people reject his guidance despite his sincere efforts to convey God's message and advise them for their own good. It underscores the theme of divine responsibility in delivering the message, while the ultimate choice to accept or reject it lies with the people, despite the prophet's earnest warnings.

translation: And [mention] Lot, when he said to his people, 'Do you commit immorality while you are seeing [its evil]? No people have done it before you from among the worlds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of engaging in immoral acts, particularly those that defy natural law and societal norms, by highlighting that such behavior was unprecedented and condemned even in Lot's time.

translation: Indeed, you approach men with desire instead of women. Rather, you are a people who exceed all bounds.
interpretation: This verse condemns the act of homosexuality as a transgression beyond natural bounds, emphasizing that such behavior is excessive and contrary to the divine order established for human relationships.

translation: And his people's only response was that they said, 'Drive them out of your town! Indeed, they are people who keep themselves pure.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and arrogance of those who reject divine guidance, as they falsely accuse the righteous of arrogance while masking their own envy and rejection of truth under the guise of moral superiority.

translation: So We saved him and his family, except his wife; she was of those who remained behind.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of actions and the importance of faith and obedience to divine commands. The wife's fate serves as a lesson about the irreversibility of choices made in the face of divine warnings, emphasizing that salvation is tied to belief and adherence to righteousness.

translation: And We rained upon them a rain [of destruction]. Then observe how was the end of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine retribution for those who persist in wrongdoing, serving as a stark reminder that no transgression goes unpunished, and that the consequences of injustice are both severe and irreversible.

translation: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord. So give full measure and weight and do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of justice, honesty, and ethical conduct in economic transactions, warning against exploitation and corruption, which are seen as moral and spiritual failings that disrupt societal harmony and divine order.

translation: And do not sit on every path, threatening and obstructing from the way of Allah those who believe in Him, seeking to make it crooked. And remember when you were few, then He increased you. And see how was the end of the corruptors.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who obstruct the path of truth and faith, using deception or intimidation to lead others astray, while forgetting their own small beginnings and the blessings of growth bestowed upon them by Allah.

translation: And if a group of you believed in what I have been sent with, and another group did not believe, then be patient until Allah judges between us, and He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of patience and trust in Allah's divine judgment when faced with differing beliefs or opposition to the truth. It reassures believers that ultimate justice and resolution lie with Allah, who is the most just and wise in His decrees.

translation: The arrogant elite among his people said, 'We will surely drive you out, O Shu'ayb, and those who have believed with you from our town, or you must return to our religion.' He said, 'Even if we were unwilling? '
interpretation: This verse highlights the defiance of truth by those who are arrogant and resistant to guidance. Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) and the believers are given an ultimatum to either abandon their faith or conform to the corrupt practices of their society. Shu'ayb's response underscores the unwavering commitment to monotheism and righteousness, even in the face of coercion, emphasizing that true faith cannot be imposed but must be chosen freely.

translation: We would indeed have fabricated a lie against Allah if we were to return to your religion after Allah has saved us from it. It is not for us to return to it except by the will of Allah, our Lord. Our Lord comprehends all things in knowledge. Upon Allah we rely. Our Lord, decide between us and our people in truth, and You are the best of those who decide.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute rejection of idolatry or false beliefs after having been guided to the truth, emphasizing that such a return would be tantamount to a grave lie against Allah. It highlights the believer's reliance on Allah's will and wisdom, acknowledging that guidance and deviation are entirely in His hands. The supplication reflects a plea for divine justice and intervention, trusting in Allah's ultimate authority to judge rightly between truth and falsehood.

translation: And the eminent ones who disbelieved among his people said, "If you follow Shu'ayb, indeed you will then be losers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and defiance of the disbelieving leaders who sought to intimidate and dissuade the people from following the truth by threatening them with loss and ruin, revealing their own insecurity and fear of losing their influence and power.

translation: So the earthquake seized them, and they became motionless in their homes.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sudden and severe consequences of divine punishment for those who persist in defiance and arrogance against Allah's signs and messengers, emphasizing the swift and inescapable nature of Allah's justice.

translation: Those who denied Shu'ayb became as though they had never dwelt in it. Those who denied Shu'ayb—it is they who were the losers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the irreversible consequences of rejecting divine guidance and the prophets. The phrase 'as though they had never dwelt in it' signifies that their denial erased any trace of their existence in the land, symbolizing both physical and spiritual annihilation. The emphasis on 'the losers' highlights that their rejection led to total loss—both in this world and the Hereafter—demonstrating that defiance of truth results in eternal ruin.

translation: So he turned away from them and said, 'O my people, I have already conveyed to you the messages of my Lord and advised you. So how can I grieve over a disbelieving people?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophet's duty to deliver the divine message and his detachment from the consequences of people's rejection of the truth, emphasizing that guidance is from Allah alone, and the messenger's role is to convey, not to force belief.

translation: And We sent to no city a prophet [who was not persecuted] except that We seized its people with hardship and adversity so that they might humble themselves [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine test of human resilience and the purpose behind tribulations—namely, to evoke humility, repentance, and a return to faith when faced with adversity, rather than succumbing to despair or defiance.

translation: Then We changed their misfortune into prosperity until they multiplied [in number] and said, "Afflictions and hardships have touched our forefathers," so We seized them suddenly while they were unaware.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly conditions and the consequences of ingratitude and arrogance. Despite Allah's blessings and mercy, people often attribute their prosperity to their own strength or past merits, forgetting that these are temporary tests from Allah. The sudden punishment serves as a reminder that true security and blessings come only from Allah, and that human arrogance in attributing success solely to oneself invites divine retribution.

translation: And if the people of the cities had believed and feared Allah, We would have opened upon them blessings from the heaven and the earth; but they denied [the messengers], so We seized them for what they were earning.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle that divine blessings and sustenance are not merely material but contingent upon faith and righteousness. It suggests that material prosperity alone is not a sign of divine favor if it is not accompanied by spiritual and moral integrity, and that rejection of truth, even in the face of abundance, leads to accountability and consequence.

translation: Did the people of the towns feel secure that Our punishment would not come to them by night while they were asleep?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against complacency and heedlessness in the face of divine justice, emphasizing that divine retribution can strike unexpectedly, regardless of one's state of unawareness or security.

translation: Or did the people of the cities feel secure that Our punishment would not come to them at dawn while they were at play?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against complacency and heedlessness in the face of divine justice, emphasizing that sudden and unexpected punishment can befall those who neglect their duties and indulge in frivolity despite clear signs and reminders.

translation: Do they feel secure from the plan of Allah? But no one feels secure from the plan of Allah except the losing people.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against arrogance and complacency in the face of divine justice, emphasizing that Allah's plans are inescapable and that those who disregard this reality are doomed to failure.

translation: Have they not been guided by those who inherited the earth after its former inhabitants, that if We willed, We could have struck them for their sins? And We seal their hearts so they do not hear?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of divine justice and the consequences of persistent wrongdoing, emphasizing that God has the power to punish wrongdoers but may delay it to allow for reflection and repentance. The sealing of hearts signifies a spiritual hardening that results from continuous rejection of truth and moral transgression.

translation: We relate to you from their news some of the accounts of those [communities]. Their messengers had come to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in what they had denied before. Thus does Allah seal over the hearts of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the persistent rejection of truth by those who have hardened their hearts against divine guidance, illustrating that Allah seals their hearts as a consequence of their willful disbelief, not as an arbitrary punishment.

translation: And We did not find for most of them any commitment to an agreement; but indeed, We found most of them defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rarity of true commitment to divine covenants among people, emphasizing that despite God's clear signs and guidance, most people persist in rebellion and disobedience, rejecting the moral and spiritual obligations placed upon them.

translation: Then We sent after them Moses with Our signs to Pharaoh and his nobles, but they wronged them. So observe how was the end of the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning about the consequences of arrogance and oppression in the face of divine guidance; those who reject truth and persist in wrongdoing will ultimately face ruin, illustrating the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: And Moses said, 'O Pharaoh, indeed I am a messenger from the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and authority of Moses' mission, emphasizing that his message is not his own but comes from the Creator of all existence, thereby establishing the truth and inevitability of his call to Pharaoh.

translation: It is incumbent upon me that I should not say anything about Allah except the truth. I have come to you with a clear proof from your Lord, so send with me the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of truthfulness in matters of faith and divine revelation, emphasizing that any message attributed to Allah must be absolute and untainted by falsehood or personal interpretation.

translation: He said, "If you have come with a sign, then bring it forth, if you are of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who falsely claim to possess divine authority or truth to demonstrate their claims through tangible proof, thereby exposing their deceit and reinforcing the authenticity of divine revelation.

translation: So he threw his staff, and behold, it was a manifest serpent.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the divine power of Allah to transform the ordinary into the extraordinary as a sign of truth, demonstrating that what may seem mundane can become a clear proof when willed by Allah.

translation: And he drew out his hand [from his cloak], and behold, it was white for the observers.
interpretation: This verse signifies the manifestation of a miraculous sign by Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) as a proof of his prophethood, demonstrating divine power to the people of Pharaoh, who demanded tangible evidence of his mission.

translation: The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said, "Indeed, this is a knowledgeable enchanter."
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and denial of the ruling elite of Pharaoh's court, who dismiss the message of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) by labeling him as a 'knowledgeable enchanter'—a term meant to undermine his divine mission and portray him as a mere sorcerer using human cunning rather than a messenger of God.

translation: He wants to drive you out of your land. So what do you command?
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of defiance and resolve in the face of adversity, where the speaker seeks the counsel of their people on how to respond to an oppressive force attempting to displace them, highlighting the importance of unity and decisive action in protecting one's home and faith.

translation: They said, "Delay him and his brother, and send among the cities gatherers",
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and defiance of the oppressors who, despite witnessing divine signs, sought to delay the message of truth and suppress its messengers by mobilizing forces against them.

translation: They will bring you every learned magician.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of truth prevailing over deception, suggesting that no matter how cunning or knowledgeable falsehood may appear, it will ultimately be exposed and defeated by divine justice.

translation: And the magicians came to Pharaoh. They said, "Indeed, for us is a reward if we are the ones who prevail."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and worldly ambition of the magicians who approached Pharaoh, seeking reward for their potential victory in a contest of magic. It reflects a transactional mindset, where their faith and loyalty are contingent upon worldly gain rather than divine truth or moral integrity.

translation: He said, "Yes, and indeed you are among the nearest [to me]."
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of divine favor and closeness, where a supplicant's request is granted, and they are assured of a special status in proximity to Allah or His mercy.

translation: They said, "O Moses, either you throw [your staff] or we will be the ones to throw [first]."
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and defiance of the sorcerers or magicians who challenged Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) in the court of Pharaoh. Their demand to throw first was an attempt to intimidate him, showing their disbelief in his divine mission and their reliance on their own perceived magical superiority.

translation: He said, 'Throw,' so when they threw, they bewitched the eyes of the people and struck terror into them, presenting a great magic.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive power of magic, which can manipulate perception and instill fear, but it is ultimately a temporary illusion that cannot withstand the truth.

translation: And We inspired to Moses, 'Throw your staff,' and at once it devoured what they were falsifying.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine power and truth of Moses' miracle, contrasting it with the falsehood of the sorcerers' tricks, thereby affirming the supremacy of God's signs over human deception.

translation: So the truth came to pass, and false was what they were doing.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood, emphasizing that no matter how deeply entrenched or persistent falsehood may seem, it is destined to perish in the face of truth's inevitable victory.

translation: So they were defeated there and turned back in humiliation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of arrogance and defiance against divine will, illustrating how those who reject truth and persist in wrongdoing ultimately face defeat and disgrace, serving as a warning to uphold humility and submission to God.

translation: And the magicians fell down prostrate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immediate and overwhelming impact of divine truth on those who witness it, demonstrating that sincere conviction leads to submission and humility before the divine, even in the face of worldly power or status.

translation: They said, "We believe in the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse reflects a declaration of faith and submission to the absolute sovereignty and lordship of Allah, acknowledging His authority over all creation, which signifies the acceptance of divine unity (tawhid) and the rejection of all false deities or systems of belief that claim lordship or divinity.

translation: Lord of Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: This phrase highlights the divine authority and power of Allah, emphasizing that He is the sustainer and guide of all prophets, including Musa (Moses) and Harun (Aaron), affirming His role as the ultimate Lord over all creation and messengers.

translation: Pharaoh said, 'Do you believe in him before I give you permission? Indeed, this is a plot you have conspired in the city to drive out its people. You will surely come to know.'
interpretation: Pharaoh accuses Moses and his followers of plotting against him and his people, framing their belief in Moses' message as a premeditated act to destabilize his rule and expel the Egyptians. His words reveal his arrogance and refusal to acknowledge divine truth, instead attributing their faith to deception and rebellion.

translation: I will surely cut off your hands and feet from opposite sides; then I will surely crucify you all together.
interpretation: This verse conveys a severe warning of divine punishment for those who commit grave crimes, such as waging war against Allah and His Messenger, spreading corruption on earth, or unjustly killing believers. The punishment described—amputation and crucifixion—reflects the gravity of the offense and serves as a deterrent, emphasizing the sanctity of life, security, and faith in Islam. It also underscores the principle of justice in Islamic law, where severe crimes demand severe consequences.

translation: They said, 'Indeed, we are turning back to our Lord.'
interpretation: This statement reflects a profound realization of divine accountability and the ultimate return to Allah, signifying repentance and submission to His will in the face of impending consequences.

translation: And you [O people] blame us only for our belief in the signs of our Lord when they came to us. Our Lord, pour upon us patience and cause us to die as Muslims [in submission to You].
interpretation: This verse reflects the steadfastness of believers in the face of adversity, acknowledging that their only 'crime' is their unwavering faith in divine revelation. The plea for patience and a Muslim death underscores the human struggle between faith and hardship, seeking divine support to remain resolute and die in a state of submission to God.

translation: And the chiefs of Pharaoh's people said, 'Will you leave Moses and his people to cause corruption in the land and abandon you and your gods?' He said, 'We will kill their sons and keep their women alive; and indeed, we are subjugators over them.'
interpretation: This verse reveals the arrogance and tyranny of Pharaoh's elite, who prioritize their own power and false deities over justice and truth, demonstrating their willingness to commit atrocities to maintain control.

translation: Moses said to his people, 'Seek help in Allah and be patient. Indeed, the earth belongs to Allah; He grants it as an inheritance to whom He wills of His servants. And the [best] outcome is for the righteous.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of relying on Allah in times of hardship and exercising patience, as ultimate control and authority belong to Him. It reassures believers that divine justice will prevail, and those who uphold righteousness will ultimately triumph, even if the immediate circumstances seem unfavorable.

translation: They said, 'We have been harmed before you came to us and after you have come to us.' He said, 'Perhaps your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, so that He may see how you will act.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the patience and steadfastness required in the face of adversity, emphasizing that trials are tests from Allah to observe human conduct and response, ultimately leading to divine justice and the opportunity for believers to prove their faith through righteous actions.

translation: And We did certainly afflict the people of Pharaoh with years of drought and a deficiency in fruits, that they might be reminded.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine method of guiding people through hardships, demonstrating that even in adversity, God's signs are present to prompt reflection and remembrance of His power and the consequences of turning away from His guidance.

translation: But when good comes to them, they say, "This is for us." And if evil afflicts them, they blame Moses and those with him. Unquestionably, their fate is decreed by Allah, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and ingratitude of those who attribute blessings to themselves while blaming others for misfortunes, failing to recognize that all outcomes are ultimately decreed by Allah, though many remain oblivious to this divine truth.

translation: And they said, "No matter what sign you bring us to bewitch us with, we will never believe in you."
interpretation: This verse reflects the hardened disbelief and arrogance of those who reject the truth despite clear evidence, illustrating how some hearts become so closed to guidance that no amount of proof can penetrate their stubbornness.

translation: So We sent upon them the flood and locusts and lice and frogs and blood as distinct signs, but they were arrogant and were a criminal people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of arrogance and persistent wrongdoing, demonstrating that divine signs, even when clear and distinct, may be ignored or dismissed by those who refuse to humble themselves before the truth.

translation: And when the punishment fell upon them, they said, "O Moses, invoke for us your Lord by what He has promised you. If you [remove] the punishment from us, we will surely believe in you and will send with you the Children of Israel."
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and conditional faith of those who only turn to God and His messengers when faced with hardship or punishment, promising obedience and belief in exchange for relief, rather than having sincere faith and devotion.

translation: But when We removed the punishment from them until a term which they were to reach, behold! they broke their word.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness of human nature, particularly when people turn away from divine blessings or guidance once their immediate hardship is lifted, reverting to their old habits of disbelief or ingratitude.

translation: So We took retribution from them, and We drowned them in the sea because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: This verse highlights divine justice in response to persistent denial and neglect of divine signs, demonstrating that rejection of truth, when coupled with arrogance and heedlessness, leads to severe consequences.

translation: And We caused the people who had been oppressed to inherit the eastern regions and the western ones which We had blessed. And the goodly word of your Lord was fulfilled for the Children of Israel because of what they had patiently endured. And We destroyed what Pharaoh and his people had done, and what they had built.
interpretation: This verse highlights divine justice and the fulfillment of God's promise to the oppressed, demonstrating that those who endure trials with patience will ultimately be rewarded, while tyrants and their works will be destroyed.

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came upon a people devoted [at the moment] to their idols. They said, "O Moses, make for us a god just as they have gods." [Moses] said, "Indeed, you are a people behaving ignorantly."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to seek external symbols of faith when confronted with unfamiliar or challenging circumstances, rather than relying on the guidance already provided. It also underscores the folly of demanding proof or substitutes for divine truth when one already possesses it, reflecting a lack of trust and gratitude.

translation: Indeed, these [polytheists] are in clear error, and false is what they have been doing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility and misguidance of associating partners with Allah (shirk) and engaging in actions devoid of truth and righteousness, emphasizing that such beliefs and deeds are baseless and lead to perdition.

translation: Shall I seek a god other than Allah while He has favored you over the worlds?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of seeking any deity besides Allah, emphasizing that true devotion should be directed solely to Him, especially when one acknowledges His unique favor and superiority over all creation.

translation: And [remember] when We saved you from the people of Pharaoh, who afflicted you with the worst torment, killing your sons and keeping your women alive. And in that was a great trial from your Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe persecution faced by the Children of Israel under Pharaoh's rule, emphasizing the divine test of faith and patience that preceded their deliverance, underscoring that trials from Allah are often followed by relief and mercy.

translation: And We appointed with Moses thirty nights and completed them by [adding] ten, so the appointment of his Lord was completed as forty nights. And Moses said to his brother Aaron, 'Take my place among my people, do good, and do not follow the way of the corrupters.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of fulfilling commitments and the trust placed in leaders to maintain righteousness among their people during their absence, emphasizing the balance between personal devotion and communal responsibility.

translation: And when Moses came at Our appointed time and his Lord spoke to him, he said, 'My Lord, show me [Yourself] that I may look at You.' [Allah] said, 'You will not see Me, but look at the mountain; if it should remain in place, then you will see Me.' But when his Lord appeared to the mountain, He rendered it level, and Moses fell unconscious. And when he awoke, he said, 'Exalted are You! I have repented to You, and I am the first of the believers.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute transcendence and incomprehensibility of Allah to human perception, even for a prophet like Moses. The divine response—'You will not see Me'—serves as a profound lesson in humility and the limits of human understanding, while the mountain’s collapse illustrates the overwhelming power of Allah’s presence, which no created entity can withstand. Moses’ immediate repentance and declaration of faith reflect the awe and submission that should accompany any encounter with the divine, emphasizing that true belief is rooted in recognizing one’s own limitations in comprehending Allah’s essence.

translation: He said, 'O Moses, indeed I have chosen you over the people with My messages and My words. So take what I have given you and be among the grateful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine selection and favor bestowed upon Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) over others, emphasizing that his distinction comes from his direct communication with Allah and the responsibilities entrusted to him. It underscores the importance of recognizing divine grace and responding with gratitude and obedience.

translation: And We inscribed for him on the tablets [something] of all things - an admonition and a detailed explanation of all things. So take them with determination and command your people to adopt the best of it. I will show you the home of the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine guidance with resolve and wisdom, while also warning against the consequences of defiance and disobedience, highlighting the stark contrast between the paths of righteousness and corruption.

translation: I will turn away from My signs those who are arrogant upon the earth without right; and [even] if they see every sign, they will not believe in it. And if they see the path of guidance, they will not adopt it as a path; but if they see the path of error, they will adopt it as a path. That is because they denied Our signs and were heedless of them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject divine guidance despite clear signs. Their refusal to follow the truth stems not from a lack of evidence but from their own defiance and neglect of divine signs, reinforcing the idea that true guidance requires humility and openness to truth.

translation: But those who deny Our signs and the meeting in the Hereafter—their deeds have become worthless. Will they be rewarded except for what they used to do?
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of actions performed without faith or sincerity, particularly those that reject divine truth and the accountability of the Hereafter, emphasizing that such deeds are devoid of lasting value and will not be rewarded beyond their temporal consequences.

translation: And the people of Moses, after [his departure], made from their ornaments a calf—a lifeless form with a lowing sound. Did they not see that it could neither speak to them nor guide them to any way? They took it [as an object of worship], and they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the folly of idolatry, highlighting the absurdity of worshiping an inanimate object incapable of any benefit or guidance, while the true Creator—Allah—was the one who had delivered them from oppression. It serves as a timeless lesson on the dangers of misplaced devotion and the moral consequences of injustice.

translation: And when they fell into their hands and saw that they had gone astray, they said, 'If our Lord does not have mercy on us and forgive us, we will surely be among the losers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the desperation and regret of those who realize their mistake too late, emphasizing the importance of seeking Allah's mercy and forgiveness before it is beyond reach.

translation: And when Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved, he said, 'What an evil thing you have done in my absence after me! Did you hasten the command of your Lord?' And he threw down the Tablets and seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward him. [Aaron] said, 'O son of my mother, indeed the people overpowered me and were about to kill me, so do not cause the enemies to rejoice over me, nor place me among the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tension between Musa (Moses) and his people upon his return, reflecting his deep disappointment and anger at their deviation from divine guidance during his absence. It also underscores the importance of patience and unity within the community, as Musa's reaction, though understandable, risks fracturing the bond between him and his brother Aaron (Harun). Aaron's plea emphasizes the vulnerability of leadership and the need for mutual support, warning against actions that could lead to further division or external triumph over the community.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and my brother and admit us into Your mercy, for You are the most merciful of the merciful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound act of humility and forgiveness, where the speaker seeks divine mercy not only for themselves but also for their sibling, demonstrating the virtue of compassion and the importance of familial bonds in seeking God's forgiveness.

translation: Indeed, those who took the calf [for worship] will be overcome with anger from their Lord and [will be subjected to] disgrace in the life of this world. And thus do We recompense the fabricators [of falsehood].
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences for those who deliberately fabricate falsehoods or associate partners with Allah, as seen in the example of the Israelites who worshipped the calf. The 'anger' and 'disgrace' mentioned are not merely temporal punishments but also reflect the moral and spiritual corruption that stems from idolatry and deviation from divine truth. The recompense is a divine principle: those who distort faith or truth will face both worldly humiliation and divine displeasure, serving as a warning against intellectual or spiritual dishonesty.

translation: But those who committed misdeeds and then repented after that and believed—indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless mercy of Allah, emphasizing that sincere repentance and faith can erase past wrongdoings, demonstrating that divine forgiveness is always within reach for those who turn to Him with a contrite heart.

translation: And when the anger subsided in Moses, he took up the Tablets. And in their inscription was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of controlling one's emotions, as Moses did when his anger subsided, allowing him to receive divine guidance. The Tablets symbolize the clarity and mercy that come from divine revelation, accessible only to those who maintain reverence and fear of Allah.

translation: And Moses chose from his people seventy men for Our appointment. Then the earthquake seized them, and he said, "My Lord, if You had willed, You could have destroyed them before and [even] me. Would You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done? This is not but Your trial - You send astray with it whom You will and guide whom You will. You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy upon us; and You are the best of forgivers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the tension between divine justice and mercy, illustrating how human suffering can lead to repentance and supplication. Moses' plea reflects the human struggle to reconcile divine omnipotence with the apparent injustice of collective punishment, ultimately affirming that guidance and misguidance are in God's hands, and that true refuge lies in seeking His forgiveness and mercy.

translation: And decree for us good in this world and good in the Hereafter. Indeed, we have turned to You.' [Allah] said, 'My punishment - I afflict with it whom I will, but My mercy encompasses all things.' So I will decree it [especially] for those who fear Me and give zakah and those who believe in Our signs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the balance between divine justice and mercy, emphasizing that Allah's mercy encompasses all things but is specifically granted to those who embody piety (taqwa), fulfill their obligations (such as zakah), and have faith in divine signs—underscoring that righteous actions and sincere repentance are pathways to Allah's favor.

translation: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered prophet, whom they find written [about] in what they have of the Torah and the Gospel, who enjoins upon them what is right and forbids them what is wrong and makes lawful for them the good things and prohibits for them the evil and relieves them of their burden and the shackles which were upon them. So those who believe in him, honor him, support him and follow the light which has been sent down with him - it is those who will be the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a universal guide whose teachings align with the divine revelations of the Torah and the Gospel. It emphasizes his mission to purify and uplift believers by removing their burdens (both spiritual and societal) and guiding them toward righteousness. The verse underscores the importance of supporting and following the Prophet, associating success with those who accept his message, honor him, and adhere to the divine light (the Qur'an) revealed through him.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, [the Messenger] to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him; He gives life and causes death.' So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the unlettered prophet, who believes in Allah and His words, and follow him that you may be guided.
interpretation: This verse underscores the universality of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) message, emphasizing that his mission is not limited to a specific group but is directed to all of humanity. It highlights the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed), affirming His exclusive right to worship and His power over life and death. The call to believe in Allah and His Messenger, and to follow the Prophet's guidance, is framed as a path to true guidance and enlightenment, reinforcing the idea that submission to Allah's will is the ultimate purpose of human existence.

translation: And from the people of Moses is a community which guides by the truth and thereby establishes justice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the existence of a righteous group within the followers of Moses who not only adhere to the truth but also actively uphold justice in their actions and judgments, serving as a model of moral integrity and fairness.

translation: And We divided them into twelve tribes, [as] nations. And We inspired to Moses when his people implored him, "Strike the stone with your staff." Then twelve springs gushed forth from it; every people knew their drinking place. And We shaded them with clouds and sent down upon them manna and quails, [saying], "Eat from the good things with which We have provided you." And they wronged Us not, but they were [only] wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine organization and sustenance granted to the Children of Israel, emphasizing Allah's mercy and provision, while also underscoring the consequences of human ingratitude and self-inflicted harm through disobedience.

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when it was said to them, "Dwell in this city and eat from it wherever you will and say, 'Relief [from sins],' and enter the gate bowing [in humility]; We will [then] forgive you your sins. We will increase [reward for] the doers of good."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincere repentance and submission to Allah's commands, where true obedience and humility are rewarded with forgiveness and increased grace.

translation: But those who did wrong among them changed [the word] other than what had been said to them, so We sent upon them a punishment from the sky because they were wronging.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of altering divine commandments or distorting them for personal or corrupt interests, which leads to divine punishment as a form of justice for oppression and transgression.

translation: And ask them about the town that was by the sea, when they transgressed on the Sabbath, when their fish came to them openly on their Sabbath day, and the day they did not observe the Sabbath, they did not come to them. Thus We test them for their defiance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of deliberate defiance of divine commandments, illustrating how such defiance can lead to spiritual and material loss as a test of faith and obedience.

translation: And [mention] when a party of them said, "Why do you advise [or warn] a people whom Allah is [about] to destroy or to punish with a severe punishment?" They said, "To be absolved before your Lord, and perhaps they may fear Allah."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of fulfilling one's duty to advise and remind others of moral and spiritual obligations, even when the outcome seems uncertain or the recipients appear resistant. It underscores that the act of advising is a form of accountability before Allah, driven by compassion and hope for reform, rather than a guarantee of immediate change.

translation: But when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We saved those who had forbidden evil, and We seized the wrongdoers with a severe punishment because they were defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine principle of justice and accountability, where those who actively uphold righteousness and prevent evil are protected, while those who persist in oppression and defiance face severe consequences, emphasizing the importance of moral responsibility and the consequences of neglecting divine guidance.

translation: But when they persisted in what they were forbidden from, We said to them, "Be apes, despised and rejected."
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences of defying divine commandments despite clear warnings, illustrating that persistent disobedience can lead to a transformation of one's nature as a form of punishment, reflecting both justice and a lesson for others.

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when your Lord declared that He would surely send upon them [i.e., the oppressors] until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with the worst torment. Indeed, your Lord is swift in penalty; but indeed, He is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the balance between divine justice and mercy, warning that while Allah may delay punishment to test or give respite to wrongdoers, He will ultimately enforce justice swiftly and severely against persistent oppression, yet remains ready to forgive those who repent.

translation: And We divided them throughout the earth into nations. Of them are the righteous, and of them are [others] less than that. And We tested them with good things and bad things so that they might return [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity within human societies, where individuals vary in their moral and spiritual states. The mention of 'good and bad' tests signifies that life's trials—whether prosperity or adversity—are divine means to guide people back to faith and righteousness, emphasizing Allah's mercy in providing opportunities for repentance and reform.

translation: But there succeeded them a posterity who inherited the Book [i.e., the Taurat (Torah)], taking the goods of this low life (without any right) and saying, 'It will be forgiven for us.' And if similar goods come to them, they will take them. Was not the covenant of the Book taken from them that they would not say about Allah anything but the truth? And they have studied what is in it. And the home of the Hereafter is better for those who are pious. Do you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse critiques those who prioritize worldly gains over spiritual integrity, even when they have knowledge of divine scripture. It highlights the hypocrisy of claiming divine forgiveness while knowingly violating divine commands for material benefit, contrasting their short-sightedness with the eternal reward reserved for the God-conscious.

translation: And those who hold fast to the Book and establish prayer—indeed, We will not waste the reward of the reformers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of adhering to divine guidance (the Book) and fulfilling religious obligations (prayer) as a means to attain divine reward, emphasizing that Allah does not disregard the efforts of those who strive to reform themselves and society.

translation: And [remember] when We raised the mountain above them as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was about to fall upon them. [We said], 'Take what We have given you with determination and remember what is in it that you may become righteous.',
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of divine commandments and the consequences of failing to uphold them, illustrating how God's signs—even those as imposing as a mountain—serve as a reminder of His power and the importance of obedience to His guidance.

translation: And [mention] when your Lord took from the children of Adam - from their loins - their descendants and made them testify of themselves, [saying], 'Am I not your Lord?' They said, 'Yes, we have testified.' [This was] lest you should say on the Day of Resurrection, 'Indeed, we were of this unaware.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the pre-eternal covenant between Allah and the human soul, affirming the innate recognition of monotheism (Tawhid) within every person. It highlights that every human being, regardless of time or place, inherently knows and acknowledges Allah as their Lord, a truth they may suppress or forget in this world but cannot deny on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Or [lest] you say, 'It was only that our forefathers associated others in worship before, and we were but descendants after them. So, will You destroy us for what the falsifiers did?'
interpretation: This verse cautions against the human tendency to justify one's own wrongdoing by blaming the actions of previous generations, emphasizing personal accountability in faith and deeds rather than relying on inherited traditions or the misdeeds of ancestors.

translation: And thus We explain the verses in detail, so that they may return [to the truth].
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine method of explaining the Qur'anic verses with clarity and detail, aiming to guide people back to the path of truth and righteousness through understanding and reflection.

translation: And recite to them the story of the one to whom We gave Our signs, but he detached himself from them, so Satan pursued him, and he became of the misguided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the danger of rejecting divine guidance after having been granted it, illustrating how such a choice can lead to spiritual ruin and being misled by Satan.

translation: And if We had willed, We could have elevated him thereby, but he adhered to the earth and followed his desire. So his example is like that of the dog: if you chase it, it pants, or if you leave it, it pants. That is the example of the people who denied Our signs. So relate the stories that they may reflect.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility of rejecting divine guidance despite having the capacity to understand it, comparing such individuals to a dog that pants regardless of external actions, symbolizing their persistent denial and heedlessness of truth.

translation: Evil is the example of the people who denied Our signs and wronged themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting divine guidance and engaging in oppression against one's own soul by denying truth, emphasizing that such actions lead to moral and spiritual ruin.
