translation: Whoever Allah guides - he is the [rightly] guided; and whoever He sends astray - those are the losers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over guidance and misguidance, highlighting that true guidance is a divine gift, while straying is a consequence of rejecting that guidance.

translation: And We have certainly created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. Those are like livestock; rather, they are more astray. It is they who are the heedless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual blindness and deafness of those who, despite having the faculties of intellect, perception, and hearing, fail to use them in recognizing the truth or heeding divine guidance, leading them to a state of moral and spiritual degradation worse than that of animals.

translation: And to Allah belong the best names, so invoke Him by them. And leave [the company of] those who practice deviation concerning His names. They will be recompensed for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of using Allah's beautiful names in supplication, as they reflect His perfect attributes, and warns against distorting or misrepresenting these names, which is a form of disbelief or deviation that will incur divine punishment.

translation: And among those We have created is a community which guides by the truth and thereby establishes justice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the existence of a righteous group within humanity who, by divine guidance, uphold truth and justice, serving as a model for others to follow in rectifying moral and societal imbalances.

translation: And those who deny Our signs, We will progressively lead them from where they do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse warns that Allah may allow those who reject His signs to continue in their disbelief, but in a way that gradually increases their misguidance and distance from truth, without them realizing the trap they are falling into.

translation: And I will give them time. Indeed, My plan is firm.
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's divine wisdom in allowing wrongdoers to persist temporarily, as part of His perfect plan, which will ultimately lead to their just punishment or repentance.

translation: Have they not pondered? There is no madness in their companion (Muhammad). He is but a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of reflection and critical thinking, urging people to examine the signs around them rather than dismissing truth out of prejudice or haste. It also affirms the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) by affirming his sanity and clarity, countering the accusations of madness leveled against him by his detractors.

translation: Have they not looked within the dominion of the heavens and the earth and all that Allah has created, and considered that perhaps their appointed time has drawn near? In what discourse hereafter will they, then, believe?
interpretation: This verse critiques those who remain heedless of the signs of Allah's creation and the inevitability of the Hour, questioning their stubborn refusal to believe in divine truth despite overwhelming evidence in the natural world and the certainty of their own mortality.

translation: Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him. And He leaves them in their transgression, blindly wandering.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine guidance and misguidance, emphasizing that Allah's decision to leave someone astray is final and cannot be overturned by any other guidance. It underscores the importance of seeking Allah's guidance through faith and righteous deeds, as straying from this path leads to spiritual blindness and confusion.

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the Hour: 'When is its arrival?' Say, 'Its knowledge is only with my Lord. None will reveal its time except Him. It lays heavy upon the heavens and the earth. It will not come upon you except unexpectedly.' They ask you as if you are familiar with it. Say, 'Its knowledge is only with Allah, but most of the people do not know.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the timing of the Day of Judgment (the Hour), emphasizing that its knowledge is exclusively His and will not be disclosed to anyone, not even the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. The heaviness of the Hour's knowledge in the heavens and earth signifies its overwhelming significance and the inability of creation to comprehend it. The suddenness of its arrival serves as a reminder of the unpredictability of death and the Hereafter, urging believers to remain steadfast in faith and preparedness.

translation: Say, 'I possess no power to benefit myself or ward off harm except what Allah wills. And if I had known the unseen, I would have acquired much wealth, and no harm would have touched me. I am only a warner and bringer of good tidings to a people who believe.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute dependence of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) on Allah's will, rejecting any notion of his own power or knowledge beyond what Allah grants. It highlights the limits of human agency and the futility of seeking worldly gains through supernatural means, reinforcing the message that true guidance and protection come solely from Allah. The verse also emphasizes the Prophet's role as a messenger tasked with warning and guiding those who believe, rather than possessing any inherent power or divine knowledge.

translation: It is He who created you from one soul and made from it its mate that you may dwell in tranquility with her. And when he covers her, she carries a light burden and continues therein. And when she grows heavy, they both invoke Allah, their Lord, 'If You should give us a good [child], we will surely be among the grateful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural and spiritual bond between spouses, emphasizing that their union is a divine arrangement for mutual tranquility and companionship. The mention of invoking Allah during the anticipation of a child reflects the recognition of divine providence in human life and the importance of gratitude in fulfilling one's responsibilities as a parent.

translation: But when Allah granted them a righteous child, they ascribed partners to Him regarding what He had granted them. Exalted is Allah above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to attribute blessings—even those granted by Allah—to other causes or beings, such as idols, luck, or their own efforts, thereby committing shirk (associating partners with Allah). It underscores the importance of recognizing that all blessings come solely from Allah and should not be shared with any false deities or intermediaries.

translation: Do they attribute to partners that which creates nothing and they themselves are created?
interpretation: This verse critiques the act of associating false deities with Allah, highlighting the absurdity of worshipping idols or beings that lack creative power, unlike Allah who is the sole Creator of all things.

translation: And they will not be able to help them, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute inability of false deities, idols, or any created beings to provide support or assistance to those who worship them, reinforcing the concept of Allah's exclusive power and sovereignty.

translation: And if you invite them to guidance, they will not follow you. It is the same for you whether you invite them or you are silent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the reality that true guidance comes from Allah alone, and no amount of human effort—whether in calling others to the truth or remaining silent—can compel someone to accept it if their hearts are not receptive. It highlights the limits of human influence in matters of faith and the importance of relying on divine wisdom rather than personal persuasion.

translation: Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah are servants like you. So invoke them, and let them respond to you, if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of worshipping or supplicating to anything or anyone other than Allah, as such entities are mere created beings with no power to respond or grant requests, highlighting the absolute uniqueness and supremacy of Allah in all aspects of worship and reliance.

translation: Have they feet to walk with? Or hands to grasp? Or eyes to see? Or ears to hear? Say: 'Call upon your partners, then plot against me, and give me no respite.
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to demonstrate the efficacy of their false deities by invoking them for aid, implying that these idols are powerless to respond or intervene, underscoring the absolute oneness and supremacy of Allah.

translation: Indeed, my protector is Allah, who has sent down the Book; and He protects the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute guardianship of Allah over those who adhere to His guidance, affirming that true protection and support come from Him alone, not from any worldly power or influence.

translation: And those you invoke besides Him cannot help you, nor can they help themselves.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute incapacity of anything or anyone other than Allah to provide assistance or benefit, emphasizing the futility of seeking help or support from false deities, idols, or any created beings, as they possess no power or control over their own affairs, let alone the affairs of others.

translation: And if you invite them to guidance, they do not hear; and you see them looking at you, while they do not see.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual blindness of those who reject guidance despite clear signs, emphasizing that their inability to perceive truth is not due to a lack of evidence but a willful resistance to acknowledge it.

translation: Show forgiveness, enjoin what is good, and turn away from the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to respond to ignorance and wrongdoing with patience, wisdom, and moral integrity rather than engaging in futile arguments or harsh reactions.

translation: But if an incitement from Satan should provoke you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse teaches the believer to turn to Allah in moments of temptation or negative influence, recognizing that Allah is fully aware of all things and can protect from harm.

translation: Indeed, those who fear Allah, when a suggestion touches them from Satan, they remember [it], and then they are seeing [clearly].
interpretation: This verse highlights the power of remembrance (dhikr) and mindfulness of Allah in dispelling the whispers of Satan, restoring clarity and guidance to the believer.

translation: And their brothers aid them in error, then they do not cease.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistence of those who lead others astray, showing no remorse or cessation in their harmful actions, reinforcing the gravity of misleading others from the truth.

translation: And when you do not bring them a sign, they say, 'Why have you not composed it?' Say, 'I only follow what is revealed to me from my Lord. This [Qur'an] is enlightenment from your Lord and guidance and mercy for a people who believe.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an and the Prophet Muhammad's role as a recipient, not an originator, of its message, emphasizing that the Qur'an's guidance and mercy are for those who embrace faith, while its rejection stems from a lack of belief rather than a deficiency in the message itself.

translation: And when the Qur'an is recited, then listen to it and pay attention, that you may receive mercy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of attentive listening and reflection when the Qur'an is recited, suggesting that such engagement fosters spiritual receptivity and divine mercy.

translation: And remember your Lord within yourself, in humility and fear, without loudness in speech—morning and evening—and do not be among the heedless.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere and private remembrance of Allah, combining humility and reverence, while avoiding ostentation or excessive loudness, and underscores the need for consistent devotion, particularly during the early morning and late afternoon, as a means to remain spiritually vigilant and avoid negligence.

translation: Indeed, those who are near your Lord (the angels) do not disdain to worship Him, and they glorify Him, and to Him they prostrate.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute submission and humility of the angels before Allah, highlighting that true servitude and devotion are inherent in their nature, devoid of any arrogance or resistance, serving as a model for human beings in their worship and surrender to the Divine.

translation: They ask you, [O Muhammad], about the bounties [of war]. Say, "The bounties are for Allah and the Messenger." So fear Allah and amend that between yourselves and obey Allah and His Messenger, if you should be believers.
interpretation: This verse establishes that all worldly gains, including spoils of war, ultimately belong to Allah and His Messenger, who distributes them according to divine wisdom. It also serves as a reminder that true faith requires not only submission to Allah and His Messenger but also righteous conduct and reconciliation among believers, emphasizing the priority of spiritual and moral integrity over material concerns.

translation: The believers are only those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, and when His verses are recited to them, it increases them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound impact of faith on a believer's heart and mind, illustrating that true faith is not merely a passive belief but an active, transformative force that evokes awe, deepens conviction, and fosters complete trust in Allah.

translation: Who establish prayer and spend out of what We have provided for them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual obligations of steadfast devotion to Allah through prayer and active gratitude through charitable spending, reflecting a balanced spiritual and social life.

translation: It is those who are truly believers. They will have [degrees of] high status in the sight of their Lord, and forgiveness, and noble provision.
interpretation: This verse underscores the distinction between superficial belief and true faith, emphasizing that genuine believers are distinguished by their elevated status with Allah, which reflects their righteous deeds and sincere devotion, alongside divine forgiveness and honorable sustenance as rewards for their unwavering commitment.

translation: Just as your Lord brought you forth from your home with the truth, while a group of the believers were averse to it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind events that may initially seem unfavorable to human desires, emphasizing that what may be disliked by some believers can ultimately be a source of truth and righteousness ordained by Allah.

translation: They argue with you about the truth after it has become clear, as if they were being driven to death while they look on.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and denial of those who persist in disputing the truth despite its evident clarity, as if they are already condemned to destruction and can see it unfolding before them.

translation: And [remember] when Allah promised you [victory in] one of the two groups - that it would be yours; and you wished that the unarmed one would be yours. But Allah intends to establish the truth by His words and to eliminate the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between human desires and divine wisdom, emphasizing that Allah's plans supersede human preferences to achieve a higher purpose—establishing truth and justice, even if it contradicts immediate human inclinations.

translation: So that the truth may prevail and falsehood may be nullified, even if the wrongdoers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of truth prevailing over falsehood, emphasizing divine justice and the ultimate triumph of righteousness, regardless of the resistance or disdain from those who perpetrate injustice.

translation: When you appealed to your Lord for help, He answered you, 'I am going to reinforce you with a thousand angels, following one after another.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the immediacy and power of divine response to sincere supplication, illustrating that Allah not only hears but actively aids believers in their times of need, often in ways beyond human expectation or comprehension.

translation: And Allah did not make it (the Qur'an) except as good tidings and so that your hearts may thereby be at rest. And victory is not except from Allah. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine purpose behind the revelation of the Qur'an: to bring good news to believers and to reassure their hearts, while also reminding them that ultimate success and victory come solely from Allah, not from their own strength or resources. It highlights Allah's supreme power and wisdom in orchestrating events, encouraging believers to place their trust in Him rather than in worldly means.

translation: When He overwhelms you with drowsiness, as a reassurance from Him, and sends down rain from the sky to purify you thereby and to remove the defilement of Satan from you, and to strengthen your hearts and make firm your steps.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and care for believers in times of hardship, providing spiritual and physical purification, as well as emotional and physical steadfastness to overcome challenges.

translation: When your Lord inspired to the angels, 'I am with you, so strengthen those who have believed.' I will cast terror into the hearts of those who disbelieved, so strike [their] necks and strike from them every fingertip.
interpretation: This verse underscores divine support for believers in times of trial, emphasizing that Allah's assistance is ever-present and that steadfastness in faith will be rewarded with strength and victory. It also highlights the severe consequences for those who reject truth, illustrating the stark contrast between divine mercy for the faithful and divine justice for the defiant.

translation: That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger. And whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger - then indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of opposing divine commandments and the authority of the Messenger, warning that such defiance incurs severe divine retribution.

translation: That is what you will taste, and for the disbelievers is the punishment of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith, emphasizing that their denial will lead to the inescapable and severe consequences of Hellfire, underscoring the justice of divine retribution.

translation: O you who have believed, when you meet those who disbelieved in a battle formation, do not turn your backs to them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of steadfastness and courage in the face of adversity, particularly in battle, as a test of faith and resolve. It warns against fleeing from the enemy, which would not only endanger one's life but also undermine the collective strength and morale of the Muslim community.

translation: And whoever turns his back to them on that Day except as a man turning away to fight or retreating to join a company, has indeed incurred wrath from Allah, and his abode is Hell—and what an evil destination!
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of abandoning the battlefield without valid justification, emphasizing that such an act incurs divine wrath and leads to eternal punishment, unless it is part of a strategic maneuver for defense or regrouping.

translation: So you did not kill them, but it was Allah who killed them. And you did not throw when you threw, but it was Allah who threw, that He might test the believers with a good test. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine sovereignty in human actions, emphasizing that ultimate control and power belong to Allah alone. It reminds believers that their efforts and achievements are only possible through Allah's will and support, and that their successes are tests from Him to evaluate their faith and submission.

translation: That is so. And Allah will weaken the plot of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute power to dismantle the schemes of those who reject faith, affirming that no plot against the truth can ultimately succeed because divine will prevails over human deception.

translation: If you [truly] seek victory, then victory has certainly come to you. And if you cease [from evil], it is better for you. But if you return [to hostility], We will return [to punishment], and your multitude will not avail you anything, even if it has increased. And Allah is with the believers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of worldly power and the ultimate sovereignty of divine justice. It warns against arrogance in strength or victory, reminding that true success lies in righteousness and cessation of wrongdoing. The promise of divine support is conditional on faith and moral conduct, not numerical or material superiority.

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and His Messenger and do not turn away from him while you hear [him speak].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute necessity of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, highlighting that true faith requires submission to divine guidance. It warns against turning away from the Prophet's teachings, even when one is fully aware of them, underscoring the importance of attentiveness and commitment to the message of Islam.

translation: And do not be like those who said, 'We hear,' while they do not hear.
interpretation: This verse cautions against hypocrisy and superficial compliance with faith, emphasizing the importance of sincere and attentive submission to divine guidance rather than mere lip service.

translation: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are the deaf and dumb who do not use reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and intellectual deficiency of those who are willfully blind and deaf to the signs of Allah, refusing to reflect upon the truth or heed divine guidance, despite their capacity to do so.

translation: And if Allah had known any good in them, He would have made them hear; and [even] if He had made them hear, they would [surely] have turned away, being averse.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine knowledge and free will, suggesting that Allah's guidance is not forced upon anyone; rather, it is a matter of choice and receptivity. Even if Allah were to grant them the ability to hear the truth, their hearts' aversion would prevent them from accepting it.

translation: O you who have believed, respond to Allah and the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a person and his heart, and that to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of heeding divine and prophetic guidance as the source of true life—spiritual and moral vitality—while also affirming Allah’s absolute sovereignty over human intentions and ultimate accountability before Him.

translation: And fear a trial that will not afflict those who have wronged among you exclusively. And know that Allah is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse warns against the collective punishment that befalls entire communities due to the sins of some individuals, emphasizing that wrongdoers should not assume they will escape divine retribution solely because they are part of a larger group.

translation: And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people might capture you, but He sheltered you, supported you with His victory, and provided you with good things so that you might be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's divine protection and favor upon the early Muslims when they were few, vulnerable, and persecuted in Makkah. It underscores the idea that Allah's help comes at the most critical times, turning weakness into strength and fear into security, all to cultivate gratitude and reliance on Him.

translation: O you who have believed, do not betray Allah and the Messenger or betray your trusts while you know [the consequence].
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of betrayal, particularly in matters of faith and trust, and warns believers against hypocrisy or deceit in their dealings with Allah, His Messenger, and the trusts (amanat) entrusted to them, emphasizing that such actions are done with full awareness of their wrongfulness and consequences.

translation: And know that your wealth and your children are but a trial, and that with Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that worldly possessions and family ties are tests of faith and devotion, designed to challenge one's priorities and submission to Allah; the 'great reward' refers to the eternal blessings and closeness to Allah that believers earn by enduring these trials with patience and righteousness, rather than being distracted by them.

translation: O you who have believed, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion, remove from you your misdeeds, and forgive you. And Allah is the Possessor of great bounty.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transformative power of taqwa (God-consciousness) in the life of a believer, promising divine guidance ('a criterion' to distinguish right from wrong), purification from sins, and forgiveness, thereby highlighting the boundless mercy and favor of Allah toward those who strive to uphold righteousness.

translation: And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you, or kill you, or expel you [from Makkah]. And they were planning, and Allah was planning, and Allah is the best of planners.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine protection and wisdom in thwarting the plots of the disbelievers, emphasizing that Allah’s plans ultimately prevail over human schemes, even when they appear formidable.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to them, they say, "We have heard. If we willed, we could say [words] like this; this is not but legends of the former peoples."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who reject divine guidance despite its clarity, attributing the Qur'an to mere human fabrication rather than acknowledging its divine origin.

translation: And [remember] when they said, 'O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the heaven or bring us a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and defiance of those who reject the truth despite clear evidence, demanding immediate punishment as a challenge to divine authority, thereby exposing their own disbelief and the hardness of their hearts.

translation: And Allah would not punish them while you are among them. And Allah would not punish them as they seek forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and forbearance of Allah, indicating that His punishment is not inevitable as long as there is a chance for repentance and seeking forgiveness, especially in the presence of a guide or prophet.

translation: And why should Allah not punish them while they obstruct [people] from al-Masjid al-Haram and they were not its guardians? Its guardians are none but the righteous, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and arrogance of those who obstruct others from the sacred precincts of the Masjid al-Haram, despite their lack of true piety or rightful claim to its guardianship. It underscores that true guardianship of the House of Allah belongs only to the God-conscious (Muttaqin), who embody righteousness and devotion, not to those who merely claim authority without genuine faith or moral integrity.

translation: And their prayer at the House was not but whistling and clapping of hands. So taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse critiques the superficial and insincere acts of worship performed by certain groups, emphasizing that true devotion requires inward faith and sincerity, not mere outward rituals devoid of meaning or submission.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve spend their wealth to avert [people] from the way of Allah. They will spend it; then it will become for them a regret; then they will be overcome. And those who disbelieved will be gathered toward Hell.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of the disbelievers' efforts to obstruct the spread of Islam and the truth. Their spending is ultimately in vain, leading only to regret and defeat, both in this world and the Hereafter, where they will face divine punishment.

translation: Allah distinguishes the wicked from the good, then He heaps the wicked together and casts them into Hell. It is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah’s absolute justice in separating the righteous from the corrupt in this life and the Hereafter, ensuring that the wicked face their just punishment in Hell, while the righteous are rewarded in Paradise.

translation: Say to those who disbelieve, if they cease [from disbelief], what has preceded will be forgiven for them; but if they return [to disbelief], then the precedent of the former [unbelievers] has already passed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the possibility of forgiveness for past sins if one repents and abandons disbelief, while warning that persistence in disbelief will lead to the same consequences as those faced by previous disbelievers in history.

translation: And fight them until there is no fitnah and [until] the religion, all of it, is for Allah. And if they cease - then indeed, Allah is Seeing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the necessity of combating oppression and injustice (fitnah) until the worship and sovereignty belong solely to Allah, free from any association or corruption, and not for the sake of worldly conquest or domination.

translation: But if they turn away, then know that Allah is your protector - an excellent protector and an excellent helper.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that even if others turn away from the truth or reject guidance, Allah remains their ultimate supporter and defender, emphasizing His unparalleled role as the best protector and helper in all matters.

translation: And know that whatever you acquire as spoils of war, one-fifth of it is for Allah, and for the Messenger, and for the near relatives, and the orphans, and the needy, and the wayfarer, if you have believed in Allah and what We sent down to Our servant on the Day of Criterion, the day when the two armies met. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse establishes the distribution of war spoils (ghanima) in Islam, emphasizing that a portion belongs to Allah and His Messenger, symbolizing dedication to the divine cause, while the rest is allocated to the needy and vulnerable in society, reflecting the ethical and social justice principles of Islam.

translation: When you were on the nearer bank (of the valley), and they were on the farther bank, and the caravan was below you. And if you had made an appointment to meet, you would have differed in the appointment, but (it happened) so that Allah might accomplish a matter already ordained, that those who were to be destroyed might be destroyed after a clear evidence, and those who were to be saved might be saved after a clear evidence. And indeed, Allah is All-Hearer, All-Knower.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine decree and the unfolding of events according to Allah's preordained plan, even when human actions and intentions seem to suggest otherwise. It underscores that Allah's wisdom governs all outcomes, ensuring that truth and falsehood are clearly distinguished, and that individuals are judged based on their choices and the evidence presented to them.

translation: When Allah showed them to you in your dream as few. And if He had shown them to you as many, you would have lost courage and would have differed in the matter, but Allah saved [you]. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and wisdom in preventing the believers from being overwhelmed by fear or discord in a critical moment, demonstrating that divine intervention often comes in ways that preserve steadfastness and unity among the faithful.

translation: And [remember] when you saw the enemy as few in your eyes, and they saw you as few in their eyes, so that Allah might accomplish a matter already destined. And to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of human perception and the ultimate sovereignty of Allah over all outcomes. It teaches that what may appear insignificant or overwhelming to humans is under Allah's control, and His plans will prevail regardless of human estimations.

translation: O you who have believed, when you encounter a [mighty] company, stand firm and remember Allah much that you may be successful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of steadfastness and remembrance of Allah in times of confrontation or adversity, emphasizing that true success lies not only in physical resilience but also in spiritual fortitude and reliance on divine support.

translation: And obey Allah and His Messenger, and do not dispute and [thus] lose courage and [then] your strength would depart; and be patient. Indeed, Allah is with the patient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unity and steadfastness in the face of challenges. It warns against internal discord, which can weaken resolve and diminish collective strength, while encouraging patience and perseverance, with the assurance that divine support accompanies those who endure difficulties with faith and resilience.

translation: And do not be like those who left their homes proudly and to show off to the people, and hinder [others] from the way of Allah. And Allah is encompassing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse cautions against arrogance, ostentation, and obstructing the path of truth and righteousness, emphasizing that Allah is fully aware of all actions, intentions, and motivations, even those hidden from others.

translation: And [remember] when Satan made their deeds pleasing to them and said, "No one can overcome you today from among the people, and indeed, I am your supporter." But when the two armies came into sight of each other, he turned on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am disassociated from you. Indeed, I see what you do not see; indeed, I fear Allah. And Allah is severe in penalty."
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of Satan's deception and the ultimate futility of relying on him, as true support and victory come only from Allah. It highlights the importance of recognizing the limits of human perception and trusting in divine justice, as Satan's promises are hollow and his warnings of divine retribution are a stark reminder of the consequences of misplaced trust.

translation: When the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease say, "These people are deluded in their religion." But whoever relies upon Allah, then Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and doubt cast by hypocrites and those with weak faith toward the sincerity and conviction of believers. It reassures the believers that true reliance is upon Allah alone, as He is the One with ultimate power and wisdom, and those who trust in Him are protected from such doubts and misguidance.

translation: And if you could see when the angels take the souls of those who disbelieved, striking their faces and their backs, [saying], "Taste the punishment of the Burning Fire."
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity and inevitability of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief, emphasizing that even in their final moments, they are met with harsh reckoning rather than mercy.

translation: This is because of what your hands have earned. And indeed, Allah is not unjust to [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, affirming that Allah does not wrong anyone, as every individual is held accountable for their own actions. The consequences one faces are a direct result of their deeds, emphasizing personal responsibility and the fairness of Allah's judgment.

translation: Like the way of the people of Pharaoh and those before them. They rejected the signs of Allah, so Allah seized them for their sins. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the signs of Allah, drawing a parallel between the fate of past nations like the people of Pharaoh and the consequences of disbelief. It emphasizes Allah's justice and power, highlighting that denial of divine truth leads to severe punishment, underscoring the importance of faith and obedience to Allah's commands.

translation: That is because Allah would not change a favor which He had bestowed upon a people until they change what is within themselves. And indeed, Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of reciprocity in divine favor—Allah’s blessings are sustained by human gratitude and righteousness, but they may be withdrawn if people become ungrateful or corrupt in their hearts and actions.

translation: Like the fate of the people of Pharaoh and those before them, they denied the signs of their Lord, so We destroyed them for their sins, and We drowned the people of Pharaoh—all were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against persistent denial of divine signs and the consequences of oppression, illustrating that historical patterns of disbelief and tyranny lead to divine punishment, emphasizing the inevitability of accountability for those who reject truth and oppress others.

translation: Indeed, the worst of living creatures in the sight of Allah are those who disbelieve; they will not [ever] believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of disbelief (kufr) in the sight of Allah, emphasizing that those who reject faith are not merely misguided but are described as the 'worst of living creatures,' indicating a profound spiritual deficiency that impedes their ability to accept truth, even when confronted with it.

translation: Those with whom you made a covenant, then they break their covenant every time, and they do not fear Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the treachery and lack of moral integrity of those who repeatedly violate their agreements despite knowing the consequences, showing their disregard for divine accountability.

translation: But if you fear treachery from a people, throw them back to their place [of safety] until the threat of treachery has passed and (until) Allah has made clear to you [what is hidden from you]; and indeed, Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to address betrayal with measured and strategic responses, emphasizing the importance of ensuring justice and security before taking further action, while trusting in Allah's ultimate wisdom and knowledge of all affairs.

translation: But if you fear treachery from a people, throw back (their covenant) to them, (putting you) on equal terms: for Allah does not love the treacherous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of reciprocity and fairness in dealings with others, even in the face of betrayal, while emphasizing that Allah detests treachery and expects believers to uphold justice and integrity in all their interactions.

translation: And those who disbelieve think they will never be overtaken. They will never escape.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that no matter how powerful or cunning the disbelievers may seem in their opposition to the truth, they are not beyond the reach of divine justice or the consequences of their actions. Their perceived 'success' is temporary and illusory, as they cannot evade accountability in the sight of Allah.

translation: And prepare against them whatever you are able of power and of steeds of war by which you may terrify the enemy of Allah and your enemy and others besides them whom you do not know [but] whom Allah knows. And whatever you spend in the cause of Allah will be fully repaid to you, and you will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of preparedness and strength in the face of adversaries, not only those known but also those unknown to the believers. It underscores that true power lies in both physical and spiritual readiness, and that any sacrifice made in the path of Allah will be justly rewarded without any injustice.

translation: But if they incline to peace, then incline to it [also] and rely upon Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to respond to peace initiatives from opponents with reciprocity, emphasizing the importance of seeking peace while placing trust in Allah's wisdom and knowledge of all affairs.

translation: And if they intend to deceive you, then sufficient for you is Allah. He it is Who supported you with His help and with the believers.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah is his ultimate protector and supporter, regardless of the deceitful intentions of others. It highlights Allah's role as the ultimate guardian against harm and deception, while also acknowledging the collective support of the believers as a means of divine aid.

translation: And unite their hearts. Had you spent all that is in the earth, you could not have united their hearts, but Allah has united them. Indeed, He is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the limitations of human efforts in achieving unity and harmony among people, emphasizing that true unity can only come from divine intervention, as it transcends human capabilities and is a manifestation of Allah's power and wisdom.

translation: O Prophet, sufficient for you is Allah and [for] those who follow you among the believers.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers that Allah's support and protection are enough for them against any adversaries or challenges they may face, emphasizing reliance on divine providence rather than human strength or alliances.

translation: O Prophet, urge the believers to fight. If there are among you twenty steadfast [ones], they will overcome two hundred. And if there are among you a hundred, they will overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they are a people who do not understand.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine support being proportional to faith and resolve rather than numerical strength alone, emphasizing that true success in struggle comes from steadfastness and trust in God's aid, not mere numbers.

translation: Now Allah has lightened [the hardship] for you, and He knows that there is weakness in you. So if there are among you a hundred steadfast [soldiers], they will overcome two hundred; and if there are among you a thousand, they will overcome two hundred thousand by Allah's permission. And Allah is with the steadfast.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of patience and perseverance in the face of overwhelming odds, reassuring believers that divine support is proportional to their steadfastness, not the raw numbers or strength they possess.

translation: It is not for a prophet to have captives [of war] until he has fought extensively in the land. You desire the commodities of this world, while Allah desires [for you] the Hereafter. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse addresses the moral and strategic priorities in times of war, emphasizing that worldly gains should not distract from higher spiritual and long-term objectives. It highlights the importance of perseverance and patience in fulfilling a greater purpose, rather than seeking immediate material rewards.

translation: If not for a decree from Allah that had already gone forth, there would have been a great punishment for you because of what you took.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine mercy and preordained decree of Allah, which intervenes to avert punishment despite human transgressions, highlighting the balance between justice and mercy in Islamic theology.

translation: So eat of what you have obtained of war booty [being lawful and lawful and good], and fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the permissibility of consuming lawful and wholesome provisions, including war booty, while reminding believers to maintain taqwa (God-consciousness) and to seek forgiveness for any shortcomings, as Allah is the Most Forgiving and Most Merciful.

translation: O Prophet, say to whoever is in your possession of the captives, 'If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you, and He will forgive you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) regarding the treatment of captives, emphasizing that Allah judges the hearts and intentions of individuals. It reassures that if there is any good in their hearts, Allah will reward them with something better than what was taken from them and forgive their past actions, highlighting Allah's boundless mercy and forgiveness.

translation: And if they intend to deceive you, then they have already deceived Allah before, so He gave [you] power over them. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the idea that betrayal is a recurring trait among those who plot against the truth, and it reassures the believer that Allah is fully aware of such deceit and will ultimately empower the righteous to overcome it.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed, migrated, and striven with their wealth and lives in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and aided [them], those are allies of one another. But those who believed but did not migrate—you are not obligated to protect them until they migrate. If they seek your help in the religion, then it is your duty to help them, except against a people with whom you have a treaty. And Allah is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse establishes the concept of mutual support and alliance among believers, emphasizing that migration (hijrah) is a fundamental aspect of faith and solidarity in Islam. It also highlights the principle of reciprocity in aiding fellow Muslims, conditional upon their commitment to the faith and adherence to its obligations, while respecting existing treaties with non-Muslim entities.

translation: And those who disbelieve are allies of one another. If you do not do so, there will be fitnah on earth and great corruption.
interpretation: This verse underscores the natural alliance among disbelievers due to their shared rejection of truth, and it warns believers that failing to unite against such forces will lead to societal turmoil and moral decay, emphasizing the necessity of unity and vigilance in upholding faith.

translation: But those who have believed, migrated, and striven in the cause of Allah, and those who gave shelter and aided - it is they who are the true believers. They will have forgiveness and an honorable provision.
interpretation: This verse underscores the essence of true faith, which is not merely belief in words but is demonstrated through action and sacrifice. It highlights the interconnectedness of faith and good deeds, emphasizing that true believers are those who actively support and uphold their faith, even at personal cost, and in doing so, they embody the highest form of devotion and earn divine reward.

translation: But those who believed after [the initial emigration] and migrated and fought with you - they are of you. And those of [close] relationship are more entitled [to inheritance] in the decree of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity and mutual responsibility of the Muslim community (Ummah), extending inclusion to those who later embrace Islam, migrate for its sake, and strive alongside the early believers. It also highlights the principle of blood relations having a greater claim to inheritance, as ordained by Allah, reinforcing the importance of familial bonds within the Islamic legal framework.

translation: A declaration of disavowal from Allah and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you had made a treaty.
interpretation: This verse signifies the abrogation of treaties with polytheistic groups who violated their agreements, demonstrating that divine justice and the sanctity of faith take precedence over political or social obligations when they conflict with the principles of Islam.

translation: Travel freely in the land for four months and know that you cannot escape Allah, and that Allah will disgrace the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the temporary freedom granted to non-believers during a specific period, emphasizing that their perceived security is not absolute. It serves as a reminder of Allah's ultimate power to humiliate and overcome those who reject faith, reinforcing the transient nature of worldly power and the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: And [this is] an announcement from Allah and His Messenger to the people on the day of the greater pilgrimage that Allah is free from [association with] the polytheists, and [so is] His Messenger. So if you repent, that is best for you; but if you turn away, then know that you will not cause failure to Allah. And give tidings to those who disbelieve of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah and the finality of His Messenger's message, emphasizing that repentance is the only path to salvation, while rejection leads to inevitable divine accountability.

translation: Excepted are those with whom you made a treaty among the polytheists and then they have not been deficient toward you in anything or supported anyone against you; so complete their treaty until their term [has ended]. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling treaties and agreements with those who remain faithful to their word and do not betray or harm the believers, even if they are from opposing groups. It highlights the moral and religious duty to uphold justice and integrity in dealings, reflecting Allah's approval of those who exhibit piety and steadfastness in their commitments.

translation: But when the sacred months have passed, then kill the polytheists wherever you find them and capture them and besiege them and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush. But if they should repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then leave their way free. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse outlines the permissibility of fighting against polytheists who are actively hostile towards Muslims, but it also sets clear conditions for cessation of hostilities, emphasizing the importance of repentance, adherence to prayer, and payment of zakah as signs of genuine reconciliation and acceptance of Islamic principles.

translation: And if any one of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection so that he may hear the words of Allah. Then escort him to a place of safety. That is because they are a people who do not know.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of extending hospitality and protection to those who seek it, even among those who do not share the same faith, as a means to expose them to the message of Islam. It reflects a principle of tolerance and dialogue, allowing others the space to hear and understand before making judgments, while also ensuring their safety in a potentially unfamiliar or hostile environment.

translation: How can the polytheists have a covenant with Allah and with His Messenger, except for those with whom you made a covenant near the Sacred Mosque? Then, as long as they are upright for you, be upright for them. Indeed, Allah loves the righteous.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrisy of the polytheists who claimed to have a covenant with Allah and His Messenger, while simultaneously violating their agreements. It highlights the conditional nature of treaties with non-believers, emphasizing that Muslims must reciprocate only when the other party fulfills their obligations, reflecting the principle of justice and righteousness in dealings.

translation: But if they gain dominance over you, they will not observe towards you any pact or obligation. They may please you with their words, but their hearts will refuse; and most of them are defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse warns against placing trust in those who may outwardly appear to comply with agreements or show kindness but harbor ill intentions in their hearts, emphasizing the importance of discerning true loyalty from hypocrisy and deception.

translation: They have exchanged the signs of Allah for a small price and averted [people] from His way. Indeed, it is they who are the worst in what they do.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who prioritize worldly gains over the divine guidance of Allah, actively obstructing others from following His path for their own selfish interests, reflecting a profound moral and spiritual corruption.

translation: They do not respect any bond or obligation towards a believer, and it is those who are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe condemnation of those who betray the trust and violate the sanctity of a believer's life, honor, or rights, despite any prior agreements or obligations. It underscores the gravity of breaking such bonds, as it is an act of aggression and oppression, placing the perpetrators firmly in the category of wrongdoers.

translation: But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakah, then they are your brothers in religion. And We detail the verses for a people who know.
interpretation: This verse underscores the possibility of reconciliation and unity within the Islamic faith, emphasizing that true brotherhood in religion is contingent upon repentance, consistent worship (prayer), and charitable giving (zakah), which reflect sincere submission to Allah and adherence to Islamic principles.

translation: But if they break their oaths after their treaty and defame your religion, then fight the leaders of disbelief - indeed, they have no [honest] commitment - so that they may cease.
interpretation: This verse addresses the breaking of treaties by hostile parties and their subsequent aggression against the Muslim community, particularly through verbal attacks on Islam. It permits defensive warfare against those who violate their agreements and actively oppose the faith, with the ultimate goal of deterring further hostility and restoring peace.

translation: Do you not fight a people who broke their oaths and determined to expel the Messenger, and they were the first to attack you? Do you fear them? But Allah has more right that you should fear Him, if you are [true] believers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the moral and religious obligation to uphold justice and defend against aggression, even when faced with those who have violated treaties, as true faith demands prioritizing devotion to Allah over fear of human adversaries.

translation: Fight them; Allah will punish them by your hands and will disgrace them and will give you victory over them and heal the breasts of a believing people.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine support granted to believers in their struggle against oppression, promising both worldly victory and spiritual healing, while underscoring that ultimate justice and retribution belong to Allah.

translation: And He will remove the anger of their hearts. And Allah turns in forgiveness to whom He wills. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and wisdom in forgiving those whom He wills, even after their hearts have been purified of negative emotions like anger. It underscores that forgiveness is a divine prerogative, granted not merely on the basis of human effort but through Allah's infinite knowledge and wisdom.

translation: Do you think that you will be left [without being tested] while Allah has not yet made evident those who strive among you and [those who] do not take besides Allah, His Messenger, and the believers as allies? And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the necessity of genuine faith being tested through action, particularly through striving (jihad) in the path of Allah. It also warns against forming secret alliances with those outside the fold of true believers, as such allegiances contradict sincere devotion to Allah, His Messenger, and the Muslim community.

translation: It is not for the polytheists to maintain the mosques of Allah while they witness against themselves with disbelief. Those - their deeds have become worthless, and in the Fire they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse underscores the incompatibility of polytheism with the sanctity of Allah's houses of worship, emphasizing that true faith is a prerequisite for any meaningful connection to these sacred spaces. It also serves as a stark warning that deeds performed without sincere faith are rendered futile, highlighting the eternal consequences of rejecting divine truth.

translation: The mosques of Allah are only to be maintained by those who believe in Allah and the Last Day, establish prayer, give zakah, and fear none except Allah. It is expected that those will be of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true devotion and maintenance of places of worship are not merely about physical upkeep but are deeply tied to sincere faith, righteous deeds, and unwavering trust in Allah alone. It underscores that guidance is a consequence of aligning one's actions with these principles, highlighting the inseparable link between belief, worship, and moral conduct in Islam.

translation: Do you consider the providing of water to the pilgrims and the maintenance of al-Masjid al-Haram as equivalent to [the deeds of] those who have believed in Allah and the Last Day and strived in the cause of Allah? They are not equal in the sight of Allah. And Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the distinction between actions performed out of mere ritual or social duty and those rooted in sincere faith and active devotion to Allah. It highlights that true worth in the sight of Allah is determined by the sincerity, intention, and commitment behind one's actions, not merely their outward appearance or communal recognition.

translation: But those who have believed, migrated, and striven for the cause of Allah with their wealth and lives are far higher in rank in the sight of Allah. And it is they who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the supreme status of believers who not only have faith but also act upon it through sacrifice and struggle (jihad) for the sake of Allah, both materially and physically. Their dedication elevates them in rank with Allah, emphasizing that true success lies in active commitment to faith beyond mere belief.

translation: Their Lord gives them good tidings of mercy from Himself and approval and gardens for them wherein is enduring pleasure.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for the righteous—divine mercy, acceptance by Allah, and eternal bliss in Paradise, emphasizing that true success lies in Allah’s pleasure and the everlasting joy of the Hereafter.

translation: Abiding therein forever. Indeed, with Allah is a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward for those who remain steadfast in faith and righteous deeds, highlighting that Allah's reward is not only just but also boundless in its magnitude and permanence.

translation: O you who have believed, do not take your fathers or your brothers as allies if they prefer disbelief over belief. And whoever of you takes them as allies - then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the primacy of faith over familial ties when they conflict with Islamic principles, warning believers against prioritizing blood relations over their commitment to Islam, and emphasizing that true loyalty is to God and His guidance.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "If your fathers, your sons, your brothers, your wives, your relatives, the wealth you have acquired, commerce in which you fear a decline, and dwellings you love are more beloved to you than Allah and His Messenger and jihad in His cause, then wait until Allah executes His command. And Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people."
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against prioritizing worldly attachments—such as family, wealth, and comfort—over faith and the obligations of Islam, including striving in the path of Allah. It underscores the severity of such a choice, implying that those who value these attachments more than their commitment to Allah and His Messenger are in grave spiritual peril, as they are defiantly disobedient to divine guidance.

translation: Allah has helped you (believers) on many occasions, and (especially) on the Day of Hunayn, when your great numbers impressed you, but they availed you nothing, and the earth, for all its vastness, became constricted for you, then you turned back in retreat.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of the limits of human power and the necessity of relying solely on divine support, regardless of apparent numerical or material strength. It highlights the transient nature of worldly advantages and the humbling reality that true victory comes only through faith and divine decree, not through sheer numbers or resources.

translation: Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and upon the believers and sent down forces which you did not see, and punished those who disbelieved. And that is the recompense of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's divine support for His Messenger and the believers, demonstrating that victory and success come from Him alone, not merely from human effort or strategy. The unseen forces (angels) sent by Allah signify His unseen assistance in battles and trials, reinforcing the concept of tawakkul (reliance on Allah). The punishment of the disbelievers serves as a reminder of divine justice, where the consequences of disbelief are met with commensurate recompense, underscoring the accountability of human actions in the sight of Allah.

translation: Then Allah will accept repentance after that for whom He wills. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute sovereignty in accepting repentance, emphasizing that His forgiveness is not automatic but granted according to His will, reflecting both His justice and boundless mercy.

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, the polytheists are unclean, so they should not approach al-Masjid al-Haram after this year of theirs. And if you fear privation, Allah will enrich you from His bounty if He wills. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the spiritual and ritual purity required to enter the sacred precincts of the Masjid al-Haram, emphasizing that those who associate partners with Allah (mushrikun) are spiritually impure and thus unfit to approach it. It also reassures believers that their obedience to Allah’s commands—such as prohibiting the polytheists from the mosque—will not lead to hardship but will instead be rewarded with divine sustenance, as Allah is the ultimate provider and possessor of wisdom in His decrees.

translation: Fight those who do not believe in Allah or the Last Day, nor comply with what Allah and His Messenger have forbidden, nor embrace the religion of truth from among those who were given the Scripture, until they pay the jizyah willingly while humbled.
interpretation: This verse outlines the conditions under which fighting is permitted against certain non-Muslim groups, specifically those who reject faith in Allah and the Hereafter, do not adhere to divine prohibitions, and refuse to accept the truth of Islam. The requirement to pay the jizyah (a tax) is framed as a sign of submission and acknowledgment of Muslim authority, not as an act of humiliation for the believers but as a means for non-Muslims to live under Islamic rule in a state of dhimmi (protected) status, with their rights and obligations clearly defined.

translation: The Jews say, "Ezra is the son of Allah," and the Christians say, "The Messiah is the son of Allah." That is their statement from their mouths; they [merely] imitate the saying of those who disbelieved before. May Allah destroy them; how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse condemns the attribution of divine parentage to human figures like Ezra or Jesus (peace be upon them), emphasizing that such claims stem from blind imitation of earlier disbelievers rather than divine revelation, and it highlights the absurdity and deviation of such beliefs.

translation: They have taken their scholars and monks as lords besides Allah, and [also] the Messiah, the son of Mary. And they were not commanded except to worship one God; there is no deity except Him. Exalted is He above whatever they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse critiques the tendency of people to elevate religious leaders or figures to a status that rivals or surpasses the worship due to Allah alone, even when those figures themselves did not command such devotion. It underscores the principle of *tawhid* (absolute monotheism) and condemns the act of associating partners with Allah, whether in the form of idols, human leaders, or other intermediaries, as this contradicts the core Islamic belief in the oneness of God.

translation: They want to extinguish the light of Allah with their mouths, but Allah refuses except to perfect His light, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine truth prevailing despite the efforts of its detractors to suppress it, highlighting Allah's unwavering commitment to completing and manifesting His light (guidance) regardless of the resistance or displeasure of those who reject faith.

translation: It is He who sent His Messenger with guidance and the religion of truth to manifest it over all religion, although they dislike the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine guarantee that the message of Islam, brought by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), will ultimately prevail over all other systems and beliefs, despite the resistance of those who associate partners with Allah. It highlights the inevitability of Islam's triumph due to its divine origin and the truth it embodies, regardless of human opposition or disbelief.

translation: O you who have believed, indeed, many of the rabbis and monks devour the wealth of people unjustly and avert [them] from the way of Allah. And those who hoard gold and silver and spend it not in the way of Allah - give them tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against the exploitation of religious authority for personal gain and the hoarding of wealth without fulfilling one's obligations to society and faith, emphasizing the moral duty to use resources for the greater good rather than selfish accumulation.

translation: On the Day when it will be heated in the fire of Hell and with it will be branded their foreheads, their flanks, and their backs, (and it will be said to them): "This is what you hoarded up for yourselves, so taste what you used to hoard."
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning against greed and hoarding of wealth or resources, emphasizing the severe consequences of such actions in the Hereafter, where the very objects of one's greed will become instruments of punishment.

translation: Indeed, the number of months with Allah is twelve [lunar] months in the register of Allah [from] the day He created the heavens and the earth; of these, four are sacred. That is the correct religion, so do not wrong yourselves during them. And fight the polytheists all together as they fight you all together. And know that Allah is with the righteous.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine ordainment of the lunar calendar and highlights the sanctity of four specific months, during which engaging in wrongdoing is particularly condemned. The command to fight the polytheists is framed within the context of reciprocity, emphasizing that the struggle is mutual and just. The concluding reminder of Allah's support for the righteous underscores the moral and spiritual foundation of the struggle, framing it not merely as a physical or political conflict but as a test of faith and piety.

translation: Indeed, the postponement [of a sacred month] is an increase in disbelief by which those who have disbelieved are led [further] astray. They make it lawful one year and unlawful another year to correspond to the count of what Allah has forbidden, [thus] making lawful what Allah has forbidden. Made pleasing to them is the evil of their deeds; and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse condemns the practice of *Nasi’* (postponing sacred months) by the pagan Arabs, who manipulated the lunar calendar to evade the prohibitions of Allah, such as warfare during sacred months. The deeper meaning highlights the deceptive nature of human attempts to justify sin by altering divine timings or rulings, emphasizing that such actions stem from arrogance and disbelief, leading only to further moral corruption.

translation: O you who have believed, what is [the matter] with you that, when you are asked to spend in the cause of Allah, you hold back? Have you preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter? But what is the enjoyment of worldly life compared to the Hereafter except a [very] little.
interpretation: This verse addresses the believers' reluctance to engage in jihad (struggle) for the sake of Allah, highlighting their attachment to worldly comforts and neglect of the greater reward in the Hereafter. It serves as a reminder that the fleeting pleasures of this life are insignificant compared to the eternal blessings promised in the next, urging them to prioritize their faith and devotion over material concerns.

translation: If you do not march forth (to fight in the cause of Allah), He will punish you with a painful punishment and will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. And Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of striving in the path of Allah, warning that neglecting this duty may lead to divine punishment and the replacement of the community by others who are more steadfast and obedient. It also reassures that such a shift would not diminish Allah's power or perfection, as He is entirely self-sufficient and capable of fulfilling His will without any loss to Himself.

translation: If you do not aid him [Prophet Muhammad], then Allah certainly aided him when those who disbelieved expelled him, being the second of two, when they were in the cave, when he said to his companion, 'Do not grieve; indeed, Allah is with us.' Then Allah sent down His tranquility upon him and supported him with unseen forces and made the word of those who disbelieved the lowest, while the word of Allah is the highest. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah in aiding His messengers and believers, emphasizing that divine support transcends human limitations and material means, as seen in the unseen forces that aided the Prophet (ﷺ) during his greatest trial.

translation: March forth, whether light or heavy, and strive with your wealth and your lives in the cause of Allah. That is better for you, if you but knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving in the path of Allah, regardless of one's physical or material capabilities, and highlights that such striving is ultimately beneficial for the believer, provided they have true knowledge and understanding of its value.

translation: If it had been an easy gain and a moderate trip, they would have followed you, but the distance was too great for them. And they will swear by Allah, 'If we were able, we would have gone out with you,' destroying themselves [by testifying to falsehood], and Allah knows that indeed they are liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to be believers but abandon the struggle (jihad) when it requires genuine sacrifice. Their excuses and oaths are empty, revealing their true lack of faith, as Allah exposes their falsehood.

translation: May Allah forgive you. Why did you give them permission [to stay behind] before it became clear to you who were truthful and [before] you knew the liars?
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of discernment and verification in leadership and decision-making, especially when dealing with matters of trust and integrity. It suggests that hasty decisions or concessions without thorough assessment can lead to unintended consequences, and emphasizes the need for leaders to rely on clear evidence and wisdom before granting permissions or making judgments.

translation: Those who believe in Allah and the Last Day do not ask your permission to strive with their wealth and their lives. And Allah is Knowing of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inherent readiness of true believers to sacrifice their wealth and lives in the path of Allah without hesitation, reflecting their deep faith and trust in divine reward. It also subtly critiques those who may hesitate or seek excuses, contrasting them with the unwavering commitment of the righteous.

translation: Only those who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day and whose hearts are in doubt ask your leave (not to fight). Thus, in their doubt, they waver.
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and hesitation of those whose faith is weak or nonexistent, particularly in matters requiring commitment or action, such as jihad. Their lack of conviction manifests as indecision and reluctance, reflecting the instability of their beliefs.

translation: And if they had intended to go forth, they would have prepared for it [some] preparation. But Allah disliked their being sent, so He kept them back, and it was said [to them], "Remain [behind] with those who remain."
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrites' lack of sincerity and genuine commitment to the cause of faith, as their reluctance to participate in jihad (struggle) stems from their inner aversion rather than any legitimate excuse, reflecting Allah's displeasure with their cowardice and the divine decree that they remain behind with those who are physically or spiritually unable to strive.

translation: If they were to go out with you, they would only increase you in corruption, and they would hasten throughout [your lands] seeking [to cause] you fitnah (tribulation), while among you are those who listen to them. And Allah is Knowing of the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive influence of hypocrites who, despite outward affiliation, secretly work to undermine the community from within, exploiting any opportunity to sow discord and corruption.

translation: They sought to cause discord before, and they turned things upside down for you until the truth came and Allah's command prevailed, though they disliked it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the persistent efforts of adversaries to sow discord and disrupt the divine mission, but their schemes ultimately fail when truth prevails, highlighting the inevitability of divine justice and the triumph of righteousness over malice.

translation: And among them is he who says, 'Give me leave (to be excused) and do not put me to the test.' Indeed, they have already fallen into trial. And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who seek to avoid responsibility while secretly harboring doubt or reluctance in their faith. Their plea for exemption ('do not put me to the test') is exposed as insincere, as their actions reveal they have already succumbed to the trial of disbelief. The warning that Hell encompasses the disbelievers underscores the severity of their spiritual failure and the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: If good befalls you, it grieves them; but if a misfortune overtakes you, they say, 'We had already taken our precaution beforehand,' and turn away, rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocritical nature of those who only align themselves with success and abandon others in times of hardship, revealing their true disloyalty and lack of genuine faith.

translation: Say, 'Never will we be struck except by what Allah has decreed for us; He is our protector.' And upon Allah let the believers rely.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of predestination (Qadr) in Islam, teaching that all events, good or bad, occur by Allah's will and decree. It encourages believers to trust in Allah's plan and rely on Him completely, as He is the ultimate protector and sustainer.

translation: Say, 'Do you await for us except one of the two best things? While we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Himself or at our hands. So wait; indeed, we are awaiting with you.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a stance of unwavering faith and trust in divine justice, coupled with readiness to face trials with patience and resolve. It underscores the believers' confidence in Allah's support, whether through victory or martyrdom, while warning the adversaries of impending divine or worldly consequences for their actions.

translation: Say, 'Spend willingly or unwillingly; it will not be accepted from you. Indeed, you have been a defiantly disobedient people.'
