interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering trust in divine decree despite opposition, emphasizing that true reliance on Allah grants a believer the courage to face adversity with conviction, even when confronting a hostile majority.

translation: But if you turn away, then I have not asked you for any reward. My reward is only from Allah, and I have been commanded to be of those who submit (to Allah).
interpretation: This verse underscores the unconditional nature of the messenger's mission—his duty is to convey the message without seeking personal gain, as his ultimate accountability rests with Allah. It also highlights the voluntary nature of faith; guidance is a divine gift, and rejection does not diminish the messenger's responsibility or the truth of the message.

translation: But they denied him, so We saved him and those with him in the ship, and made them successors (on the earth), and We drowned those who denied Our signs. Then see how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and the mercy of Allah in granting respite to the righteous while punishing the obstinate disbelievers, serving as a lesson in divine justice and the inevitability of accountability.

translation: Then We sent after him messengers to their peoples, and they came to them with clear proofs, but they were not to believe in what they had denied before. Thus do We seal over the hearts of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent rejection of divine guidance by those who are steeped in transgression and arrogance. It underscores the idea that when people repeatedly deny the truth despite clear evidence, their hearts become hardened, and they are deprived of the ability to accept guidance—a consequence of their own defiance and injustice.

translation: Then We sent after them Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh and his chiefs with Our signs, but they behaved arrogantly and were a sinful people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of human arrogance and defiance in the face of divine guidance, despite clear signs and miracles, leading to their own moral corruption and downfall.

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Indeed, this is obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to dismiss divine truth when it challenges their preconceived notions or interests, attributing it instead to deception or trickery.

translation: Moses said, 'Do you say about the truth when it has come to you, "Is this magic?" And magicians will not succeed.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and denial of truth by those who refuse to acknowledge divine guidance when it is presented to them, instead resorting to dismissive labels like 'magic' to avoid confronting the reality of the message.

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us to turn us away from what we found our fathers following, and that the two of you might possess greatness in the land? And we are not going to believe in you two.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubbornness and arrogance of those who refuse to abandon their inherited traditions and beliefs, even when presented with truth. It highlights the human tendency to cling to familiar ways and resist change, especially when it challenges established norms or threatens one's status or pride.

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'Bring to me every skilled magician.'
interpretation: This verse reflects Pharaoh's arrogance and his reliance on worldly power and deception to counter divine truth, demonstrating his refusal to acknowledge the signs of God and his determination to suppress them through any means, including magic.

translation: So when the magicians came, Moses said to them, 'Cast whatever you are going to cast.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Moses' challenge to the magicians, demonstrating his confidence in divine truth over their illusions, and setting the stage for a decisive confrontation between truth and falsehood.

translation: But when they threw, Moses said, "What you have brought is [mere] magic. Allah will surely invalidate it. Indeed, Allah does not amend the work of corrupters."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine power to nullify falsehood and deception, affirming that Allah ultimately thwarts the schemes of those who spread corruption and mislead others through deceitful means.

translation: And Allah confirms the truth by His words, even if the criminals dislike it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute certainty and inviolability of divine truth, which Allah establishes and upholds through His own words. It conveys that no matter how much the wrongdoers or those who reject the truth may oppose or resent it, the truth will prevail because it is sanctioned by Allah Himself. The mention of 'criminals' (المجرمون) here likely refers to those who persist in injustice, disbelief, or opposition to divine guidance, emphasizing that their rejection does not diminish the truth but rather highlights their own defiance against Allah's will.

translation: But none believed in Moses except [some] offspring of his people, for fear of Pharaoh and his establishment, that they would persecute them. And indeed, Pharaoh was arrogant in the land, and he was of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the selective belief of a few among Moses' people, driven by fear of persecution rather than sincere conviction, while Pharaoh's arrogance and oppression are condemned as transgressive acts against divine guidance.

translation: And Moses said, 'O my people, if you have believed in Allah, then rely upon Him, if you should be Muslims [in submission to Him].'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete trust and reliance on Allah after affirming faith in Him, highlighting that true submission (Islam) requires placing one's trust entirely in Allah's will and decree.

translation: So we said, 'Upon Allah we rely. Our Lord, do not make us a trial for the oppressive people.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the believers' plea to Allah for protection from being a means of temptation or trial for wrongdoers, ensuring their faith remains steadfast and unshaken by the oppression they face.

translation: And we saved you by My mercy from the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine intervention and mercy that saved the believers from destruction by the hands of their disbelieving oppressors, emphasizing that ultimate victory and salvation come from Allah alone.

translation: And We inspired to Moses and his brother, 'Settle your people in Egypt in houses and make your houses a direction [for prayer], and establish prayer. And give good tidings to the believers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine command to establish a spiritual foundation amidst a challenging environment, emphasizing the importance of creating a space for worship and prayer even in adverse circumstances, while also encouraging steadfastness and hope for the believers.

translation: And Moses said, 'Our Lord, indeed You have given Pharaoh and his establishment splendor and wealth in the life of this world, our Lord, that they may lead [mankind] astray from Your way. Our Lord, obliterate their wealth and harden their hearts so that they will not believe until they see the painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound theological tension between divine justice and human free will, where Moses appeals to God to counteract the corrupting influence of wealth and power, which are often used to mislead people from the path of truth, ultimately invoking divine intervention to expose the consequences of their disbelief.

translation: He said, "Your prayer has been answered, so stand firm [in your devotion] and do not follow the way of those who do not know."
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of steadfastness in faith and righteousness after receiving divine guidance or answers to supplication, warning against emulating the ignorant who act without knowledge or divine direction.

translation: And We took the Children of Israel across the sea, and Pharaoh and his soldiers pursued them in tyranny and enmity until, when drowning overcame him, he said, "I believe that there is no deity except the One in whom the Children of Israel believe, and I am of the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate futility of false pride and oppression when faced with divine truth. Pharaoh's last-minute declaration of faith, driven by desperation rather than genuine conviction, underscores the Quranic principle that true faith must be rooted in sincerity and submission to Allah, not coerced or self-serving. It also serves as a warning against delaying repentance until the point of no return, emphasizing the importance of recognizing truth before it is too late.

translation: Now you have disobeyed before and were among the corrupters.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of past disobedience and the consequences of being among those who spread corruption, highlighting the importance of repentance and reform to avoid divine punishment.

translation: So today We will save you in your body so that you may be a sign for those after you. And indeed, many of the people are heedless of Our signs.
interpretation: This verse underscores the eternal significance of divine signs and the consequences of human neglect. It highlights that some signs are preserved in the physical world (like Pharaoh's body) to serve as enduring proof of God's power and truth, yet many people remain oblivious to these profound reminders.

translation: And We had settled the Children of Israel in a goodly settlement and provided them with good things. But they did not differ until knowledge came to them. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the initial blessings and stability granted to the Children of Israel, followed by their subsequent divisions after receiving divine knowledge. It underscores the importance of unity in faith and the consequences of discord, while affirming divine justice in resolving disputes on the Day of Judgment.

translation: But if you are in doubt about what We have revealed to you, then ask those who have been reading the Book before you. The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord, so never be among the doubters.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers that the Qur'an is the true revelation from Allah, and any doubts about it can be resolved by consulting the People of the Book (Jews and Christians), who possess scriptures that preceded the Qur'an. It encourages seeking knowledge and verification from those with prior scriptural knowledge, while firmly establishing the authenticity of the divine message.

translation: And do not be among those who deny the signs of Allah, lest you become among the losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against rejecting the truth of Allah's signs—whether they are in the form of divine revelations, natural phenomena, or moral guidance—emphasizing that denial leads to spiritual loss and ruin.

translation: Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been decreed will not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute certainty of divine decree, indicating that some people are so entrenched in their disbelief that even clear signs and guidance will not sway them, as their hearts are sealed by divine wisdom.

translation: And even if every sign comes to them, until they see the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the stubbornness and disbelief of those who refuse to accept the truth despite overwhelming evidence, suggesting that some people's hearts are so hardened that no amount of proof or divine signs will guide them to faith.

translation: Then why was there not a single town that believed so its faith benefited it? [We saved it from Our punishment,] except the people of Jonah? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the worldly life and gave them enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse underscores the unique and exceptional nature of divine mercy, which is not bound by human expectations or norms. It highlights that faith alone, without prior merit or collective righteousness, can invoke God's favor, as seen in the case of the people of Jonah, whose sincere repentance led to immediate relief from punishment and temporary prosperity. It serves as a reminder that divine justice is not rigidly transactional but is ultimately rooted in mercy and the potential for redemption, even in the face of grave sins.

translation: And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed - all of them entirely. Then, [O Muhammad], would you compel the people until they become believers?
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of free will in matters of faith, emphasizing that belief must come from genuine conviction rather than coercion or external pressure.

translation: And it is not for a soul to believe except by permission of Allah, and He places defilement upon those who do not use reason.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over faith and disbelief, emphasizing that belief is a divine gift granted only to those whom Allah permits, while those who reject faith do so due to their own intellectual and moral deficiencies, as they fail to recognize the signs of truth.

translation: Say, 'Observe what is in the heavens and the earth.' But the signs and warnings do not benefit a people who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of divine signs and warnings for those whose hearts are hardened against faith, emphasizing that even clear evidence of Allah’s existence and power will not sway those who refuse to believe.

translation: Do they await except the like of the days of those who passed on before them? Say, 'Then wait; indeed, I am with you among those who wait.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth, implying that their fate will mirror the consequences faced by previous nations who denied their messengers. It reassures the Prophet (peace be upon him) and believers that divine justice will prevail, and they should remain patient in the face of opposition, trusting in Allah's timing and plan.

translation: Then We save Our messengers and those who believe. Thus, it is incumbent upon Us to save the believers.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's unwavering commitment to protecting and delivering His messengers and those who have faith in Him, reflecting His divine justice and mercy.

translation: Say, 'O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion - then I do not worship those you worship besides Allah; but [I worship] Allah alone, who causes you to die. And I have been commanded to be of the believers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute monotheism of Islam, rejecting any form of polytheism or association of partners with Allah. It emphasizes the inevitability of death and the accountability to Allah alone, reinforcing the call to sincere faith and submission to Him.

translation: And set your face toward the religion, inclining to truth, and never be of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining unwavering devotion to monotheism (Tawheed) and rejecting any form of polytheism or associating partners with Allah. It calls for sincerity in faith and steadfastness in following the straight path of Islam, free from deviation or compromise with false deities.

translation: And do not invoke besides Allah that which neither benefits you nor harms you, for if you did, then indeed you would be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute exclusivity of worship and devotion to Allah alone, warning against associating anything or anyone with Him in acts of worship, as such association constitutes injustice (ظلم) against the divine right of Allah to be worshipped exclusively.

translation: And if Allah should touch you with adversity, there is no remover of it except Him. And if He intends for you good, then there is no repeller of His bounty. He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants. And He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all affairs, emphasizing that no one can avert harm or bring benefit except by His will, highlighting His complete control over destiny and His boundless mercy in bestowing favors upon whom He pleases.

translation: Say, 'O mankind, the truth has come to you from your Lord. So whoever is guided - it is only for [the benefit of] his soul; and whoever goes astray - it is only against it. And I am not over you a manager.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the individual responsibility of each person in their spiritual journey; guidance or misguidance is a personal matter with consequences borne solely by the individual, not by the Prophet (peace be upon him) who is merely a warner and bearer of the divine message.

translation: And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah gives His judgment. And He is the best of judges.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine revelation and exercising patience in the face of adversity, trusting that Allah's ultimate judgment is the most just and beneficial.

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book whose verses are perfected and then distinguished from [their] detail by [one who is] Wise and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and perfection of the Qur'an, highlighting its coherence, clarity, and detailed guidance, all emanating from Allah's infinite wisdom and knowledge.

translation: Worship none but Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and the exclusive right of Allah to be worshipped, while also highlighting the dual role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as both a warner against divine punishment for disbelief and a bearer of glad tidings for those who submit to Allah.

translation: And seek forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful. And turn to Him in repentance that your reward may be bestowed in full and that you may be given a goodly provision; and if you turn away, then I truly fear for you the punishment of a Great Day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking Allah's forgiveness and turning to Him in repentance, as it leads to divine mercy, sustenance, and reward in this life and the Hereafter. It also serves as a warning against turning away from Allah, as it may result in severe punishment on the Day of Judgment.

translation: To Allah is your return, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate accountability of all human actions and the absolute power of Allah to recompense or judge accordingly, emphasizing that nothing escapes His knowledge or authority.

translation: Behold! They fold up their bosoms to hide themselves from Him. Behold! When they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He is the Knower of the innermost thoughts.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of attempting to hide one's true intentions or deeds from Allah, as He is fully aware of what is concealed in the hearts and what is openly displayed.

translation: And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and place of storage. All is in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute knowledge and control over the sustenance and existence of all creatures, emphasizing that provision is divinely ordained and meticulously recorded, reinforcing trust in Allah's wisdom and plan.

translation: And it is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days—and His Throne was upon water—so that He might test you [to see] which of you is best in deed. And if you say, 'Indeed, you will be resurrected after death,' those who disbelieve will surely say, 'This is not but obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine purpose behind creation and the test of human deeds, while also highlighting the skepticism of those who reject the Hereafter, dismissing its reality as mere illusion or deception.

translation: And if We delay the punishment for them until a counted time, they will surely say, "What is holding it back?" Look, the Day it comes to them will not be turned away from them, and what they used to ridicule will surround them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the folly of those who mock or doubt it. The delay of punishment is not an indication of its absence but rather a test of human patience and faith; those who question it will ultimately face the inescapable reality of their actions, as divine justice will prevail on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And if We give man a taste of mercy from Us and then withdraw it from him, indeed, he is despairing and ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to lose hope and become ungrateful when faced with adversity after experiencing blessings, underscoring the importance of patience and gratitude in faith.

translation: And if We let him taste [a taste of] favor after hardship has touched him, he will surely say, "Bad times have passed away from me." Indeed, he is happy and boastful.
interpretation: This verse critiques the human tendency to attribute blessings solely to their own merit or past struggles, ignoring divine favor, while also highlighting the fleeting and superficial nature of such pride when it arises from temporary worldly comforts rather than true gratitude or recognition of Allah's grace.

translation: Except for those who are patient and do righteous deeds; they will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of patience and righteous actions, emphasizing that those who endure hardships with steadfastness and perform good deeds will be granted divine forgiveness and a substantial reward in the Hereafter.

translation: Perhaps, [O Muhammad], you would leave aside some of what is revealed to you, and your breast feels straitened by it because they say, "Why has a treasure not been sent down for him, or an angel not come with him?" But you are only a warner. And Allah is over all things a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that his role is solely to convey the divine message as a warner, not to fulfill the demands of the disbelievers for miracles or material signs. It underscores Allah's sovereignty and His complete control over all affairs, reminding the Prophet to remain steadfast in his mission regardless of the people's skepticism or expectations.

translation: Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Say, "Then bring ten fabricated surahs like it and call upon whoever you can besides Allah, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse challenges those who deny the divine origin of the Qur'an to produce something similar in eloquence, coherence, and depth, even if only in ten surahs. It underscores the Qur'an's unparalleled literary and spiritual excellence, which cannot be replicated by human effort alone, thereby affirming its authenticity as a revelation from Allah.

translation: But if they do not respond to you, then know that it was sent down with the knowledge of Allah, and that there is no god except Him. So, will you then submit?
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah in revelation and guidance, emphasizing that divine knowledge encompasses all things, and that true submission (Islam) is to Him alone, regardless of human responses or rejection.

translation: Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornments, We will give them their full reward for their deeds in it, and they will not be deprived [of their due] therein.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against prioritizing worldly gains over spiritual growth, emphasizing that God will fulfill the desires of those who seek only worldly pleasures but will not reward them in the Hereafter, as their intentions were not aligned with righteousness.

translation: It is those for whom there is nothing but the Fire in the Hereafter. And [as for] what they had done, it has become worthless, and [all] what they used to do has become futile.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequence for those who reject faith and persist in wrongdoing, emphasizing that their deeds in this life hold no weight or benefit in the Hereafter, rendering all their efforts meaningless.

translation: Then is he who had a clear proof from his Lord, and a witness from Him follows him, and before him is the Book of Moses as a guide and mercy? They believe in it. But whoever disbelieves in it from the factions—the Fire is his promised destination. So be not in doubt about it. Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord, but most of the people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity of divine guidance and the certainty of its truth, urging the listener to trust in the revealed message rather than doubt it, while also warning that rejection of this truth leads to severe consequences.

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about Allah? Those will be presented before their Lord, and the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord." Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of attributing falsehood to Allah, emphasizing that such an act is the epitome of injustice. It highlights the accountability of those who fabricate lies about divine matters, as they will face divine judgment and eternal condemnation, illustrating the severe consequences of falsehood against Allah.

translation: Those who hinder [others] from the path of Allah and seek to make it [seem] crooked, while they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who actively obstruct others from following the straight path of Islam, distorting its teachings or presenting it in a misleading manner, and warns that such people will ultimately reject faith in the Hereafter.

translation: It is not in their power to avert (punishment) from the earth, nor have they any protectors besides Allah. Their punishment will be doubled. They could not hear, nor could they see.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute inability of those who reject faith to evade divine punishment or find any true allies outside of Allah. Their rejection blinds them to the truth, rendering them incapable of perceiving guidance, and their punishment is intensified due to their persistent denial and defiance.

translation: It is they who have lost their own souls: all their inventions will leave them in the lurch.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate loss and regret of those who, through their own choices and actions, have strayed from the truth and divine guidance, only to find that their false beliefs and fabricated excuses are of no avail in the face of divine justice and reality.

translation: Indeed, they will be the greatest losers in the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe and irreversible loss that awaits those who reject faith and righteousness, emphasizing that their regret and loss in the Hereafter will be absolute and unmatched.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves to their Lord - those are the companions of Paradise; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith is not merely a declaration but is proven through righteous actions and humility before Allah. The combination of belief, righteous deeds, and sincere humility is the key to attaining Paradise, highlighting that a balanced spiritual and moral life is essential for salvation.

translation: The example of the two parties is like the blind and deaf, and the seeing and hearing. Are they equal in comparison? Then, will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who are spiritually blind and deaf to the truth (those who reject faith despite clear signs) and those who are spiritually perceptive and receptive (those who acknowledge and follow divine guidance). The rhetorical question underscores the absurdity of equating the two, emphasizing that true guidance and misguidance are fundamentally incomparable, and urging reflection on this disparity.

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, [saying], 'Indeed, I am to you a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of Prophets as divine messengers tasked with warning their people against deviation and inviting them to the truth, emphasizing the clarity and transparency of their message despite potential rejection or ridicule.

translation: That you worship none but Allah. Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful Day.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and warns against associating partners with Him, emphasizing the severe consequences of such disbelief or idolatry in the Hereafter.

translation: So the eminent ones who disbelieved among his people said, "We do not see you, [O Noah], except as a man like ourselves, and we do not see the followers of yours except as those who are the lowest of us in judgment, and we do not see for you any merit over us. Rather, we think you are liars."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and denial of the disbelieving elite who dismissed Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and his followers based on superficial judgments, rejecting divine guidance due to their own pride and prejudice.

translation: He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has granted me a mercy from Himself, [so much so that] it has been obscured from you, should we compel you to accept it while you are averse to it?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tension between divine guidance and human free will, emphasizing that true faith cannot be forced upon anyone, even if the evidence is clear and the messenger is granted divine mercy.

translation: And O my people, I do not ask you for any wealth for it. My reward is only from Allah. And I am not the one to drive away those who believe. Indeed, they will meet their Lord, but I see you as a people who are ignorant.
interpretation: This verse underscores the Prophet's unwavering commitment to his mission, emphasizing that his sole purpose is to convey the message of Islam without seeking personal gain or material reward. It also highlights his compassion and respect for believers, affirming that their faith is between them and Allah, and that he does not have the authority or intention to reject or drive them away. The verse further critiques the people's ignorance, suggesting that their rejection of the message stems from a lack of understanding or wisdom rather than any fault on the part of the believers.

translation: And O my people, who would protect me from Allah if I drove them out? Will you not then be mindful?
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet's call to his people, acknowledging that if he were to reject them for their disbelief, he would still be in need of Allah's protection, emphasizing the futility of opposing divine will and the importance of remembering Allah's sovereignty.

translation: And I do not say to you that I possess the treasures of Allah, nor do I claim knowledge of the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel. Nor do I say to those whom your eyes look down upon that Allah will never grant them any good. Allah knows best what is within their souls. If I were to say such a thing, I would indeed be among the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) absolute humility and submission to Allah's will, rejecting any claims of divine authority, knowledge of the unseen, or superiority over others. It highlights the importance of refraining from arrogance and judgment, as only Allah possesses true knowledge of people's hearts and destinies.

translation: They said, "O Noah, you have disputed with us and prolonged the dispute with us, so bring us what you promise us, if you should be of the truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and defiance of the disbelievers who challenge the messenger (Noah) despite his repeated warnings and calls to truth, demanding immediate proof of his message as a condition for their belief, reflecting their refusal to accept guidance unless it conforms to their demands.

translation: It is only that Allah brings it to you if He wills, and you cannot prevent [it].
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all events and outcomes, emphasizing that nothing occurs except by His will. It serves as a reminder of human limitation and the inability to thwart Allah's decrees, reinforcing reliance on divine will and the futility of opposing His plans.

translation: And my advice will not benefit you, [O my people,] if I should desire to advise you, if Allah intends to keep you astray. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine will and human free will, highlighting that guidance ultimately comes from Allah alone. It serves as a reminder that no matter how sincere the advice or effort of a well-wisher, true guidance is a matter of Allah's decree. It also emphasizes accountability, as all will return to Allah for judgment.

translation: Or do they say, 'He has fabricated it?' Say, 'If I have fabricated it, upon me is my crime, and I am innocent of what you commit.'
interpretation: This verse addresses accusations of fabrication against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by disbelievers, affirming his truthfulness while rejecting their false claims and distancing himself from their unjust accusations.

translation: And it was revealed to Noah, 'No one of your people will believe except those who have already believed, so do not grieve over what they used to do.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the face of rejection and opposition, teaching believers to remain steadfast in their mission despite the ingratitude or hostility of others, trusting in Allah's plan and timing.

translation: And construct the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and do not address Me concerning those who wronged—for indeed, they are [to be] drowned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of divine guidance and obedience in fulfilling a divinely ordained task, while also highlighting the inevitability of divine justice for the wrongdoers, emphasizing that their fate is sealed and not subject to intercession.

translation: And he constructed the ship, and whenever a group of his people passed by him, they ridiculed him. He said, 'If you ridicule us, then we will ridicule you just as you ridicule us.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the steadfastness of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) in the face of mockery and ridicule from his people while he was engaged in the seemingly impossible task of building the ark. It underscores the importance of perseverance in fulfilling divine commands despite opposition, and the certainty of divine retribution against those who mock the truth and its followers.

translation: And you will surely know who it is that will be afflicted by a disgraceful punishment, and upon whom a lasting punishment will descend.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth, indicating that divine punishment will inevitably come to those who persist in their disbelief, bringing both humiliation in this life and an enduring torment in the Hereafter.

translation: Until, when Our command came and the oven overflowed, We said, "Load upon the ship of every kind [of creature] two mates, and your family—except those against whom the word has already passed—and whoever has believed." And none had believed with him except a few.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine command to Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) to gather pairs of all creatures and his family onto the Ark, except those already decreed for destruction. The mention of 'the oven overflowing' symbolizes the imminent flood as a sign of God's decisive judgment. The scarcity of believers with Noah underscores the rarity of true faith in the face of widespread disbelief, emphasizing that salvation is granted only to those who heed divine warnings.

translation: And he said, 'Embark in it! In the name of Allah is its course and its anchorage. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of seeking divine guidance and blessings before embarking on any significant journey or endeavor, as well as the assurance of Allah's forgiveness and mercy in all affairs.

translation: And the ship sailed with them through waves like mountains, and Noah called out to his son, who had kept apart, 'O my son, come aboard with us and do not be with the disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the urgency of divine guidance and the consequences of rejecting it, even when it comes from a close family member. Noah’s plea to his son reflects the tension between familial bonds and moral responsibility, emphasizing that faith and salvation transcend personal relationships when faced with divine judgment.

translation: I will seek refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water.' Allah said, 'There is no protector today except for whom He has mercy upon.' And the waves came between them, and he was among those drowned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation and the futility of seeking refuge in anything other than Him, even in seemingly insurmountable circumstances. It highlights that divine mercy is the only true protection, and no worldly means—no matter how strong—can avert Allah’s decree when He intends to manifest His will.

translation: And it was said, 'O earth, swallow your water, and O sky, withhold [your rain].' And the water subsided, and the matter was accomplished, and the ship came to rest on the [mountain of] Judiyy. And it was said, 'Away with the wrongdoing people.'
interpretation: This verse illustrates the culmination of divine justice, where the earth and sky respond to God's command to end a period of trial, symbolizing the end of punishment for the oppressors and the salvation of the righteous. The 'wrongdoing people' are condemned to perish, highlighting the inevitability of divine retribution for injustice.

translation: And Noah called upon his Lord and said, 'My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tension between human emotions and divine justice. Noah appeals to Allah based on familial ties ('my son is of my family') and the certainty of Allah's promise ('Your promise is true'), yet he also acknowledges Allah's ultimate authority and wisdom ('You are the most just of judges'). It underscores the idea that divine decrees transcend personal attachments and must be accepted with submission, even when they conflict with human desires.

translation: Allah said, "O Noah, indeed he is not of your family; indeed, he is [one whose] work was other than righteous, so do not ask Me that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, I advise you, lest you be of the ignorant."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of adhering to divine commandments and the dangers of interceding for those who persist in wrongdoing, even if they are close family members. It also underscores the prohibition of seeking knowledge beyond what is permitted, as such inquiries can lead to ignorance and deviation.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed I seek refuge in You from asking You for what I have no knowledge of. And unless You forgive me and have mercy upon me, I will be among the losers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the humility and submission of the supplicant before Allah's infinite knowledge and wisdom. It underscores the recognition that human understanding is limited, and that seeking knowledge beyond one's capacity or questioning Allah's decrees without proper understanding can lead to loss. The plea for forgiveness and mercy highlights the need for divine guidance and protection from arrogance or ignorance, emphasizing reliance on Allah's grace rather than human intellect alone.

translation: It was said, "O Noah, disembark in peace from Us and blessings upon you and upon the communities [to come] from those with you." And [other] communities We will grant enjoyment [of worldly pleasures], but then there will touch them from Us a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine mercy granted to Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and his followers, symbolizing spiritual salvation and divine favor. Simultaneously, it serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly prosperity for those who reject guidance, foreshadowing their inevitable punishment as a consequence of their defiance.

translation: This is from the tidings of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad]. You did not know it, [neither] you nor your people, before this. So be patient. Indeed, the [best] outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing that its knowledge was not accessible to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) or his people prior to its revelation, highlighting the miraculous nature of the Qur'an as a source of unseen knowledge. The command to 'be patient' serves as a reminder that divine wisdom unfolds in its own time, and ultimate success belongs to those who remain steadfast in their faith and righteousness.

translation: And to the 'Aad [We sent] their brother Hud. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. You are not but inventors [of falsehood]."
interpretation: This verse underscores the core message of monotheism (Tawhid) and the rejection of idolatry, emphasizing that Allah is the only true deity worthy of worship. It also highlights the moral responsibility of individuals to reject falsehood and uphold truth, as the people of 'Aad were accused of fabricating lies by associating partners with Allah.

translation: O my people, I do not ask you for any reward for it. My reward is only from the One who created me. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse underscores the sincerity and selflessness of the messenger's mission, emphasizing that their sole motivation is divine accountability rather than worldly gain, while also inviting reflection on the deeper purpose of their message.

translation: And O my people, seek forgiveness from your Lord and repent to Him. He will send [rain from] the sky upon you in showers and increase you in strength [added] to your strength, and do not turn away as criminals.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of repentance (tawba) as a means to attain Allah's mercy and blessings. By seeking forgiveness and turning back to Him, a community can expect divine sustenance (symbolized by rain) and an increase in strength, both materially and spiritually. The warning against turning away 'as criminals' suggests that rejecting this call to repentance will lead to moral and spiritual decline, akin to the state of wrongdoers.

translation: They said, "O Hūd, you have not brought us any clear evidence, and we are not about to abandon our gods at your word. Nor are we believers in you."
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth despite clear signs, prioritizing their traditions and idols over divine guidance.

translation: All they say is, 'Some of our gods have afflicted you with evil.' He said, 'I call God to witness—and you bear witness—that I am free of what you associate [with Him].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) unwavering stance against polytheism and his complete dissociation from the false deities worshipped by the disbelievers. It underscores the futility of attributing misfortune to other than Allah and the importance of absolute monotheism (Tawhid) in Islam.

translation: Instead of Him, so all of you plot against me, then do not give me respite.
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to those who reject the truth, urging them to gather all their efforts and schemes against the truth, but assuring that divine justice will prevail without delay.

translation: Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. There is no creature but that He holds its forelock [in His grasp]. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes absolute trust in Allah's power and control over all creation, asserting that no creature can escape His dominion. It reassures the believer that Allah's governance is just and guided by the 'straight path,' implying unwavering justice, wisdom, and righteousness in His decrees and actions.

translation: But if they turn away, then I have already conveyed to you what I was sent with to you. And my Lord will replace you with another people, and you will not harm Him at all. Indeed, my Lord is, over all things, Guardian.
interpretation: This verse underscores the accountability of messengers to deliver their message and the ultimate authority of Allah in replacing those who reject guidance, emphasizing that divine will prevails regardless of human resistance.

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us, and We saved them from a harsh punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine principle of mercy and salvation for the righteous, contrasting it with the severe punishment for those who reject faith, emphasizing that deliverance is a manifestation of God's grace bestowed upon the faithful.

translation: And [We destroyed] the people of 'Aad. They denied the signs of their Lord, disobeyed His messengers, and followed the command of every obstinate tyrant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and the dangers of blindly following tyrannical leaders who oppose truth and justice.

translation: And they incurred in this world a curse and [also] on the Day of Resurrection. Unquestionably, the people of 'Ad denied their Lord. Then, away with the people of 'Ad — the people of Hud.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences of rejecting divine guidance and the warnings of the prophets, as seen in the fate of the 'Ad people who denied their Lord Hud. It highlights that disbelief not only leads to worldly and spiritual ruin but also eternal damnation, serving as a stark reminder of the importance of heeding divine messages and the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: And to the Thamud [We sent] their brother Salih. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. He initiated you from the earth and settled you in it, so ask forgiveness of Him and repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is near and responsive."
interpretation: This verse underscores the exclusive worship of Allah, emphasizing His sole authority as the Creator and Sustainer, while calling for repentance and seeking forgiveness due to His proximity and responsiveness to His servants.

translation: They said, 'O Salih, you were among us a source of hope before this. Do you forbid us from worshiping what our forefathers worshiped? And indeed, we are in doubt about what you are calling us to—doubtful.',
interpretation: This verse highlights the tension between tradition and reform, illustrating how people often cling to inherited beliefs out of comfort or fear of change, even when confronted with moral or spiritual truth.

translation: He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has granted me a mercy from Himself, who could protect me from Allah if I were to disobey Him? Then you would only increase me in loss.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of seeking help from others when one has divine guidance and mercy, as disobedience to Allah leads to ultimate loss regardless of worldly support.

translation: And O my people, this is the she-camel of Allah - to you a sign. So leave her to eat in Allah's earth and do not touch her with harm, or an imminent punishment will seize you.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of respecting divine signs and the consequences of transgressing against them, highlighting the need for obedience and reverence toward Allah's commands and symbols.

translation: So they hamstrung her, and he said, 'Enjoy yourselves in your homes for three days. That is a promise not to be denied.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of defying divine commandments and the importance of heeding warnings, as the people who hamstrung the she-camel faced imminent punishment within a specified timeframe, emphasizing that Allah's decrees are absolute and inescapable.

translation: So when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him, by a mercy from Us, and [saved them] from the disgrace of that day. Indeed, your Lord is the Powerful, the Mighty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mercy and justice that distinguishes between the righteous and the wicked. The 'disgrace of that day' refers to the punishment that befell the disbelieving people of Thamud, while Salih and the believers were spared due to Allah's mercy. It underscores that true salvation is a result of faith and divine favor, and that Allah's power and might are absolute, ensuring justice is served.

translation: And the wrongdoers were seized by the punishment, so they became motionless in their homes.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sudden and inescapable nature of divine retribution for those who persist in oppression and injustice, highlighting that their downfall is swift and irreversible, leaving them helpless in the very places where they once exercised power.

translation: As if they had never prospered therein. Indeed, the Thamud disbelieved in their Lord. So away with the Thamud!
interpretation: This verse underscores the irreversible consequences of rejecting divine guidance and the fleeting nature of worldly success when devoid of faith, serving as a stark warning against arrogance and ingratitude toward Allah's signs and blessings.

translation: And Our messengers came to Abraham with good tidings; they said, "Peace." He said, "Peace." And soon he brought [them] a roasted calf.
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's (peace be upon him) exemplary hospitality and his immediate recognition of the divine nature of the visitors, despite their angelic form, by responding to their greeting with warmth and urgency to serve them.

translation: So when he saw their hands not reaching for it, he doubted them and felt a fear of them. They said, "Do not fear; indeed, we have been sent to the people of Lot."
interpretation: This verse highlights the initial distrust and fear of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) when he perceived the angels sent to him as strangers whose intentions were unclear, as their hands did not reach for the food he offered. His reaction underscores the natural human instinct to be cautious in unfamiliar situations, even when the visitors are divine messengers. The angels' reassurance that they were sent to a specific people (the people of Lot) serves to clarify their mission and alleviate his fear, demonstrating that divine communication often comes with signs to guide and comfort the recipient.

translation: And his wife was standing by, so she laughed. Then We gave her good tidings of Isaac and after Isaac, Jacob.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of the birth of Isaac (and later Jacob) to a barren woman (Sarah) and an elderly man (Abraham), demonstrating Allah's power to fulfill His promises despite seemingly impossible circumstances, and underscoring the importance of trust in divine decree.

translation: She said, "Woe to me! Shall I bear a child while I am an old woman, and this is my husband an old man? Indeed, this is an amazing thing!"
interpretation: This verse reflects Sarah's initial disbelief and astonishment at the news of her impending pregnancy in her old age, highlighting the miraculous nature of divine intervention and the fulfillment of God's promise, which underscores themes of faith, patience, and the power of God's will.

translation: They said, 'Do you wonder at the decree of Allah? The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the Household. Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing Allah's decree (Qadr) with faith and acceptance, rather than questioning it with amazement or doubt. It also underscores the special status and blessings of the Ahl al-Bayt (the Household of the Prophet), emphasizing that their honor and mercy come from Allah, who is ultimately Praiseworthy (Hameed) and Glorious (Majeed) in all His actions and attributes.

translation: So when the awe had left Abraham and the good tidings had reached him, he began to plead with Us concerning the people of Lot.
interpretation: This verse highlights Abraham's deep concern for justice and mercy, even in the face of divine decree, as he intercedes for the people of Lot despite their wrongdoing, reflecting the balance between divine justice and human compassion.

translation: Indeed, Abraham was forbearing, compassionate, and repentant.
interpretation: This verse highlights three key virtues of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him): forbearance (ḥalīm) in the face of hardship and trials, deep compassion (awwāh) toward others, and constant repentance (munīb) to Allah, reflecting his unwavering devotion and moral excellence.

translation: O Ibrahim, cease from this! Indeed, the command of your Lord has come, and indeed, they are coming to them a punishment that will not be turned back.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority and inevitability of divine decree, emphasizing that no intercession or plea can alter what Allah has decreed. It also highlights the urgency of submission to Allah’s command, as seen in the immediate cessation of Ibrahim’s (peace be upon him) action, symbolizing unwavering faith and obedience in the face of divine will.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt straitened for them, and said, 'This is a difficult day.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the emotional and moral conflict faced by Prophet Lot (peace be upon him) when he saw his people's hostility toward the divine messengers, reflecting his deep sense of responsibility and the burden of his mission in the face of overwhelming opposition.

translation: And his people came rushing to him, and before that they used to commit evil deeds. He said, 'O my people, these are my daughters—they are purer for you. So fear Allah and do not disgrace me concerning my guests. Is there not among you a single right-minded man?',
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral duty of hospitality and the rejection of societal norms that lead to sin, as Lot (peace be upon him) prioritizes the protection of his guests over the corrupt desires of his people, while also questioning their lack of reason and decency.

translation: They said, 'You know well we have no right over your daughters, and indeed, you know what we desire.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the hypocrisy and hidden intentions of the people of Lot (peace be upon him), who demanded his daughters while secretly seeking illicit relationships with the men of his community. It highlights the contrast between their outward claims of righteousness and their inward corruption.

translation: He said, 'If only I had power over you or could take refuge in a strong support!',
interpretation: This verse reflects the desperation and helplessness of someone who feels powerless against a perceived threat or adversity, seeking refuge in strength or support that they lack. It underscores the human tendency to rely on external power or protection when faced with overwhelming challenges.

translation: They said, 'O Lot, indeed we are messengers of your Lord; [they] will never reach you. So set out with your family during a portion of the night and let none of you look back except your wife; indeed, she will be struck by what strikes them. Indeed, their appointment is [for] the morning. Is not the morning near?',
interpretation: This verse underscores the urgency of divine intervention and the importance of absolute obedience to divine commandments, even in the face of impending destruction. It highlights the severity of divine punishment for those who persist in their transgressions, while also illustrating God's mercy in providing a clear path to salvation for the righteous.

translation: So when Our command came, We made its highest part lowest and rained upon them stones of layered hard clay.
interpretation: This verse signifies the irreversible and decisive nature of divine punishment, where the destruction is so complete that even the loftiest structures are reduced to rubble, and the punishment is meticulously prepared and executed, leaving no room for escape or doubt about its source.

translation: Marked by your Lord; and they are not far from the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine justice, implying that no action—good or evil—goes unnoticed by Allah, and that the consequences of wrongdoing, while possibly delayed, are inevitable and will be meted out with perfect justice.

translation: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. And do not decrease the measure or the weight. Indeed, I see you in prosperity, but indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a Day encompassing."
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of justice and fairness in economic dealings, warning against exploitation through fraudulent measures or weights, while also reminding the people of their moral duty to worship Allah alone and the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.

translation: And O my people, give full measure and weight in justice and do not deprive people of their due and do not commit abuse on earth, spreading corruption.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral and ethical responsibility of individuals and societies to uphold justice in trade and transactions, ensuring fairness and honesty while avoiding exploitation or corruption.

translation: Allah is the Best Protector for you, if you are believers. And I am not a guardian over you.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that Allah's protection and care are far superior to any human oversight, emphasizing reliance on divine guardianship rather than human authority or intervention.

translation: They said, 'O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we leave what our fathers worshipped or that we do with our wealth what we please? Indeed, you are the forbearing, the discerning.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of the people of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) in rejecting his message. They mock his guidance, implying that his faith restricts their freedom to worship as they please or manage their wealth as they desire, while also ironically acknowledging his wisdom and patience—qualities they refuse to accept.

translation: He said, 'O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord and He has provided me with a good provision [from Himself], and I do not intend to differ from you in what I forbid you [from doing]? I only desire reform as much as I am able. And my success is not but through Allah. Upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn penitent.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the sincerity and humility of a prophet (likely Shu'ayb) in conveying his message, emphasizing that his actions are solely for the sake of Allah and the reform of his people, not for personal gain or opposition to them.

translation: And O my people, let not your dissension from me lead the punishment to befall you like that which befell the people of Noah or the people of Hud or the people of Salih. And the people of Lot are not far from you.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against persistent rejection of truth and defiance of divine guidance, cautioning that the consequences of such behavior can be severe and historically documented, as seen in the destruction of past nations who similarly denied their prophets.

translation: And seek forgiveness from your Lord and repent to Him. Indeed, my Lord is Merciful and Loving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness (istighfar) and repentance (tawbah) as a continuous spiritual practice, highlighting Allah's boundless mercy and love as the foundation for this relationship.

translation: They said, "O Shu'ayb, we do not understand much of what you say, and indeed, we see you as weak among us. Were it not for your clan, we would have stoned you. And you are not a person of honor to us."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and dismissal of truth by those who reject guidance. Despite Shu'ayb's (peace be upon him) clear message, they belittle him, showing their own weakness in understanding divine truth and their reliance on tribal protection rather than moral integrity.

translation: He said, "O my people, is my kinship with you more beloved to you than Allah? And you have taken Him as a [means of] abandonment behind your backs. Indeed, my Lord is encompassing of what you do."
interpretation: This verse reflects the prophet Hud's (peace be upon him) reproach to his people for prioritizing tribal loyalty and worldly ties over their duty to worship and obey Allah, highlighting the folly of rejecting divine guidance in favor of transient allegiances.

translation: And O my people! Act according to your position; indeed, I am acting. Soon you will know who it is upon whom will come a punishment that will disgrace him, and who is a liar. And watch, for indeed I am watching with you.
interpretation: This verse reflects the resolute stance of a prophet or messenger in the face of opposition, asserting that their actions are guided by truth and divine purpose, while warning the people that their defiance will lead to a humiliating punishment if they persist in falsehood. The call to 'watch' underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the certainty of accountability for one's deeds.

translation: And when Our command came, We saved Shu'ayb and those who believed with him, by Our mercy. And the shriek seized the wrongdoers, so they became motionless in their homes.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice and mercy, illustrating that those who uphold faith and righteousness are ultimately saved, while the oppressors face swift and decisive punishment, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly power and the inevitability of divine retribution.

translation: As if they had never prospered there. Indeed, away with [the people of] Madyan, just as Thamud was taken away [in destruction].
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences of rejecting divine guidance and persisting in disbelief and oppression, serving as a stark warning that those who defy Allah’s commands will face annihilation, regardless of their past prosperity or power.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mission of Moses (peace be upon him) as a prophet, emphasizing that he was sent with both miraculous signs (evidence of his prophethood) and a clear, unmistakable proof of his divine authority to guide the Children of Israel and challenge the oppressive Pharaoh.

translation: To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they followed the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was not right-minded.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dangers of blind obedience to tyrannical leaders, emphasizing that following unjust commands without discernment leads to moral and spiritual ruin, as exemplified by Pharaoh's followers who were misguided by his oppressive and unrighteous rule.

translation: Their people will be led forth on the Day of Resurrection, and they will be made to enter the Fire. And evil is the arrival to which they are led.
interpretation: This verse serves as a severe warning against leading others astray, particularly in matters of faith, by prioritizing worldly desires or falsehood over divine guidance. It underscores the gravity of responsibility for those in positions of influence—whether leaders, scholars, or elders—who misguide their followers, as their ultimate destination will be the Fire, highlighting the eternal consequences of such betrayal.

translation: And they will be followed by the curse in this [life] and on the Day of Resurrection. What an evil gift it is!
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe and lasting consequences of following misguidance or wrongdoing, emphasizing that such a path leads not only to immediate condemnation in this world but also to eternal damnation in the Hereafter, highlighting the gravity of the choices one makes.

translation: That is from the news of the towns which We relate to you. Some of them are still standing, and some are mown down.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly life and the varying states of nations and civilizations, some of which endure while others are destroyed, serving as a reminder of divine justice and the consequences of human actions.

translation: And We did not wrong them, but they wronged themselves. So their gods which they invoked besides Allah did not avail them at all when the command of your Lord came. And they did not increase them [in anything] except in loss.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of personal accountability in divine justice, emphasizing that human suffering is not due to God's injustice but rather a consequence of their own choices and actions.

translation: And thus has your Lord taken to punishment when the inhabitants of the cities were wrongdoers. Indeed, His punishment is painful and severe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine retribution for persistent injustice and oppression, emphasizing that divine punishment, while delayed, is ultimately severe and inescapable for those who transgress against moral and ethical boundaries.

translation: Indeed in that is a sign for whoever fears the punishment of the Hereafter. That is a Day when all the people will be gathered, and that is a Day that will be witnessed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the accountability of all humanity before Allah, emphasizing that the signs of divine power and justice are evident for those who reflect upon the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.

translation: And We delay it only for a specified term.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom in the timing of events, particularly the Day of Judgment, which is delayed not arbitrarily but for a precise and predetermined purpose, allowing humanity time for reflection, repentance, and preparation.

translation: The Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission. Then among them will be the wretched and the blessed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and authority of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where even the power of speech is subject to His will, highlighting the gravity of accountability and the predetermined fate of individuals based on their deeds.

translation: But as for those who were [utterly] wretched, they will be in the Fire. For them therein is [only] a heavy breathing and roaring.
interpretation: This verse highlights the eternal punishment of the disbelievers and the wicked in the Hereafter, emphasizing the severity of their suffering through vivid auditory imagery—'heavy breathing' and 'roaring'—to underscore the inescapable and agonizing nature of their fate, devoid of any mercy or relief.

translation: They will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. Indeed, your Lord is All-Doer of what He intends.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and will of Allah, emphasizing that His decrees—whether in punishment, mercy, or the duration of existence—are final and beyond human comprehension, yet perfectly aligned with His infinite wisdom and justice.

translation: But as for those who were [destined to be] prosperous, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills. [It is] a bounty uninterrupted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of Paradise for the righteous, highlighting that their reward is not merely temporary but everlasting, contingent only upon the will of Allah, which underscores the boundless and uninterrupted nature of divine grace.

translation: So do not be in doubt, [O Muhammad], as to what these [polytheists] worship. They worship only as their forefathers worshipped before. And indeed, We will give them their share undiminished.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the believers that the false deities worshipped by the polytheists hold no real power or legitimacy, as their worship is merely a blind imitation of their ancestors without any divine basis. It also serves as a reminder that Allah will ultimately fulfill His promise to the believers by granting them their rightful reward in full, while the disbelievers will receive their due portion in this world without any reduction, though it may not be a reward of the same nature.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, but there came to be differing over it. And if it were not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been concluded between them. And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in allowing differing opinions among people regarding religious matters, as it serves as a test of their faith and a means to distinguish between those who seek truth and those who are obstinate. The 'word that preceded from your Lord' refers to Allah's decree of free will and the postponement of judgment until the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing His mercy and justice in deferring final judgment.

translation: And indeed, to each of them your Lord will fully repay their deeds. Indeed, He is All-Aware of what they do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of Allah in recompensing every individual for their deeds, emphasizing that nothing escapes His knowledge or is overlooked in His accounting.

translation: So remain on a right course as you have been commanded, [you] and whoever has turned back with you [to Allah], and do not transgress. Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and righteousness, urging both the individual and the community to adhere unwaveringly to the path of truth and justice. It also serves as a reminder that God is fully aware of all actions, thereby encouraging accountability and moral integrity in all dealings.

translation: And do not incline towards those who do wrong, lest the Fire should touch you; and you have no protectors besides Allah, nor shall you be helped.
interpretation: This verse warns against forming alliances or alliances with oppressors and wrongdoers, as their wrongdoing can lead to divine punishment. It emphasizes that seeking protection or support from such individuals is futile, as true protection and assistance come only from Allah.

translation: And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the early hours of the night. Indeed, good deeds do away with misdeeds. That is a reminder for those who remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of regular prayer and the purifying effect of good deeds on one's sins, highlighting the mercy and forgiveness of Allah for those who strive to remember and repent.

translation: And be patient, for indeed, Allah does not waste the reward of those who do good.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of patience in the face of hardship or adversity, assuring believers that their perseverance and righteous deeds will not go unnoticed or unrewarded by Allah. It serves as a reminder that divine justice ensures that every act of goodness is accounted for and recompensed in due time.

translation: Why were there not among the generations before you those possessing wisdom forbidding corruption on Earth, except for a few of those We saved from them? But the wrongdoers pursued what they were indulged in, and they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse critiques the moral and spiritual decline of past societies, emphasizing that divine punishment often comes when the majority abandon righteousness, even if a few righteous individuals remain. It warns against the dangers of collective moral failure and the consequences of unchecked corruption, while also highlighting Allah's mercy in saving those who remain steadfast in faith.

translation: And your Lord would never destroy the towns wrongfully while their people are reforming.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, asserting that Allah does not punish communities unjustly if their inhabitants are striving for righteousness and reform. It implies that divine retribution is contingent upon persistent wrongdoing and corruption, not merely the passage of time or the mere existence of a community.

translation: And if your Lord had willed, He could have made the people [of this world] one community; but they will not cease to differ [among themselves],
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in allowing human diversity and differing opinions, as it serves as a test of free will and a means for spiritual growth through trial and reflection.

translation: Except whom your Lord has mercy on. And for that did He create them. And the word of your Lord is fulfilled: "I will surely fill Hell with jinn and mankind all together."
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute sovereignty of Allah in both mercy and justice. While Allah's mercy encompasses all things, His justice demands that those who reject His guidance and persist in wrongdoing will inevitably face the consequences in Hell. The creation of humans and jinn is thus a test of their free will, with the ultimate outcome determined by their choices.

translation: And each [story] of the messengers We relate to you, [O Muhammad], is a means by which We strengthen your heart. And in this has come to you the truth and an admonition and a reminder for the believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose of recounting the stories of past prophets: to reinforce the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) resolve and faith, while also serving as a source of truth, guidance, and moral lessons for believers, reminding them of the consistency of divine messages across time.

translation: And say to those who disbelieve, 'Work according to your position; indeed, we are working [as well].'
interpretation: This verse is a challenge to the disbelievers, asserting that their efforts to oppose or undermine the truth will not go unanswered by Allah. It implies that divine justice will prevail, and their actions will be met with corresponding consequences, reinforcing the certainty of accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: And wait, indeed we are waiting.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine justice and the certainty of accountability. It serves as a reminder that while humans may perceive delays or injustices in the world, Allah’s timing is perfect, and He will ultimately deliver justice. It also implies a challenge to those who oppose the truth, asserting that their reckoning is imminent, and their waiting will not be in vain.

translation: To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and to Him will be returned all matters. So worship Him and rely upon Him. And your Lord is not unaware of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all that is unseen and known, and underscores the necessity of complete devotion and trust in Him alone, while reassuring that Allah is fully aware of all human actions, thus encouraging righteous conduct.

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. These are the verses of the clear Book.
interpretation: The opening of this surah (Yusuf) introduces its divine origin and clarity, establishing the Qur'an as a source of guidance and truth, distinct from human fabrication or ambiguity.

translation: Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an that you might understand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and accessibility of the Qur'an's message, ensuring that its guidance is presented in a language (Arabic) that the people of its time could comprehend, thereby making its teachings directly intelligible to them.

translation: We relate to you, [O Muhammad], the best of stories in what We have revealed to you of this Qur'an although you were, before it, among the unaware.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and unparalleled excellence of the Qur'an's narratives, affirming that its stories are the most truthful and profound, even though the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was previously unaware of them, highlighting the transformative power of revelation.

translation: When Joseph said to his father, 'O my father, indeed I have seen [in a dream] eleven stars and the sun and the moon; I saw them prostrating to me.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine gift of dreams as a means of conveying important messages or prophecies, and it highlights the importance of humility and submission to Allah, as even celestial bodies—symbols of grandeur—prostrate before the righteous servant of Allah.

translation: He said, 'O my son, do not relate your vision to your brothers, lest they contrive against you a plan. Indeed, Satan, to man, is a manifest enemy.'
