interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of discretion and the potential for envy or harm from others, even within one's own family. It also underscores the need to be wary of Satan's influence, as he seeks to sow discord and misfortune.

translation: And thus will your Lord choose you and teach you the interpretation of narratives and complete His favor upon you and upon the family of Jacob as He completed it upon your fathers before, Abraham and Isaac. Indeed, your Lord is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine selection and favor bestowed upon the recipient, emphasizing God's role in guiding and educating them in wisdom and understanding, as well as the completion of His blessings, paralleling the favor shown to earlier prophets like Abraham and Isaac. It underscores the importance of divine knowledge and wisdom in the recipient's life and mission.

translation: Certainly, in Joseph and his brothers, there are signs for those who ask.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound lessons and moral lessons embedded in the story of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) and his brothers, which serve as guidance and reflection for those who seek wisdom and understanding.

translation: When they said, 'Surely Yusuf and his brother are dearer to our father than we are, though we are a group of strong men. Indeed, our father is in plain error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive nature of jealousy and the tendency to belittle one's own worth in comparison to others, leading to misguided accusations and familial discord.

translation: Kill Joseph or cast him out to some (unknown) land, that the favor of your father may be given to you alone; and after that you will be a righteous people.
interpretation: This verse reflects the destructive consequences of jealousy and the lengths to which envy can drive people, even among close family members. It highlights the moral decay that arises when individuals prioritize their own desires over familial bonds and divine guidance, ultimately leading to a loss of righteousness and spiritual integrity.

translation: One of them said, "Do not kill Joseph, but throw him into the depths of the well; some travelers may pick him up, if you must act."
interpretation: This verse reflects the initial hesitation and moral conflict among Joseph's brothers regarding their plan to eliminate him out of jealousy, ultimately choosing a less severe course of action to rid themselves of him while leaving room for divine intervention or unexpected mercy.

translation: They said, "O our father, why do you not trust us with Joseph while indeed we are his sincere well-wishers?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the brothers' attempt to manipulate their father's trust by appealing to their perceived sincerity and concern for Joseph, masking their hidden jealousy and ill intentions.

translation: Send him with us tomorrow so he may enjoy himself and play, and indeed we will take good care of him.
interpretation: This verse reflects the initial deceptive plan of Yusuf's (Joseph) brothers to temporarily remove him from their father's care, under the guise of allowing him to enjoy himself, while secretly intending to harm or abandon him.

translation: He said, 'Indeed, it grieves me that you should take him away, and I fear lest the wolf should devour him while you are heedless of him.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep emotional concern and fear of a parent (Ya'qub, peace be upon him) for the safety of his son (Yusuf, peace be upon him), highlighting the vulnerability of a child left unprotected and the natural instinct to prioritize their well-being above all else.

translation: They said, 'If the wolf devours him while we are a group, then indeed we would be losers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep-seated jealousy and fear of loss among the brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph), which led them to plot against him despite their collective strength. It underscores the destructive nature of envy and the lengths to which it can drive people, even those who are supposed to be united.

translation: So when they took him [Joseph] away and agreed to put him into the bottom of the well. And We revealed to him, "You will surely inform them of this affair of theirs while they perceive not."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in preserving Joseph (Yusuf) and ensuring his eventual rise to a position of power and honor. It underscores that Allah’s plans unfold in ways beyond human comprehension, often through trials and tribulations, ultimately leading to justice and the fulfillment of His decrees.

translation: And they came to their father in the evening, weeping.
interpretation: This verse highlights the emotional and psychological impact of truth and justice, where the brothers of Yusuf (Joseph) are forced to confront the consequences of their past actions, leading them to repentance and distress in front of their father Yaqub (Jacob).

translation: They said, 'O our father, indeed we went racing and left Joseph with our possessions, and a wolf ate him. But you will not believe us, even if we should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of the brothers' claim, revealing their premeditated lie to cover up their betrayal of Joseph. Their attempt to manipulate their father's emotions by fabricating a story underscores the depths of their jealousy and moral corruption, as they prioritize their own desires over familial bonds and truth.

translation: And they brought his shirt stained with false blood. He said, 'Rather, your souls have enticed you to commit something [evil]. So [my course is] beautiful patience. And Allah is the One sought for help against what you describe.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the deception of human nature and the importance of patience in the face of false accusations. It teaches that when faced with injustice or slander, one should respond with patience and trust in Allah's help rather than succumbing to anger or despair.

translation: And there came a caravan, and they sent their water-drawer, and he let down his bucket. [The ruler of Egypt said], 'Good news! Here is a boy.' And they hid him as merchandise, and Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind seemingly ordinary events, as the arrival of the caravan and the discovery of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) by the water-drawer were part of Allah's plan to reunite him with his family and fulfill his destiny as a prophet.

translation: And they sold him for a cheap price—just a few dirhams—and they were indifferent to him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral depravity of those who prioritize material gain over justice and compassion, showing how the value of a human life can be diminished in the eyes of those consumed by greed and indifference.

translation: And the one who bought him from Egypt said to his wife, 'Make his stay comfortable; perhaps he will benefit us or we may adopt him as a son.' And thus We established Joseph in the land to teach him the interpretation of events, and Allah has full power over His affair, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine destiny and the unseen wisdom behind events. Despite the apparent circumstances—Joseph being sold into slavery—Allah’s plan unfolds in a way that elevates him to a position of influence and knowledge. It underscores that human actions, though they may seem insignificant or even harmful, are part of a greater divine scheme that serves a higher purpose, often beyond human comprehension.

translation: And when he reached his full strength and maturity, We gave him wisdom and knowledge. And thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights that divine rewards, such as wisdom and knowledge, are granted to those who demonstrate patience, perseverance, and righteousness in their development and actions, emphasizing that spiritual and intellectual growth are tied to moral excellence and divine favor.

translation: And the woman in whose house he was, sought to seduce him, and she closed the doors and said, 'Come to me.' He said, 'Allah forbid! Indeed, he is my master, who has made my stay pleasant. Indeed, the wrongdoers will not succeed.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of resisting temptation and upholding moral integrity, even in the face of persistent and enticing pressure. It highlights the believer's reliance on Allah and the acknowledgment of His blessings, while also serving as a warning that those who engage in wrongdoing will ultimately fail.

translation: And indeed, he (Joseph) sought to seduce her, and she sought to seduce him, but he would have succeeded had he not seen the proof of his Lord. Thus [it was] that We should avert evil and indecency from him. Indeed, he was of Our chosen servants.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine protection granted to those who are sincere in their faith and devotion. It highlights that true righteousness is not merely the absence of temptation but the strength to resist it through divine guidance and moral integrity.

translation: And they raced to the door, and she tore his shirt from the back. And they found her husband at the door. She said, 'What is the punishment for one who intended evil against your wife except imprisonment or a painful punishment?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of justice and the consequences of false accusations. The woman's immediate response to protect herself and her honor, while also seeking justice, demonstrates the societal expectation that wrongdoers should face appropriate punishment. It also underscores the gravity of false allegations, as the man's actions—though misunderstood—could have led to severe consequences for the woman if not for the truth being revealed.

translation: She said, 'It was he who tried to seduce me.' A witness from her household testified, 'If his shirt is torn from the front, then she has told the truth, and he is the liar.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of physical evidence in resolving disputes, suggesting that actions and tangible proof are more reliable than verbal accusations alone. It also underscores the principle of justice, where even in personal matters, objective evidence must be considered to establish the truth.

translation: But if his shirt is torn from the back, then she has lied, and he is of the truthful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of examining evidence carefully in matters of accusation or dispute, as outward appearances can be deceiving. It underscores the need for truthfulness and the consequences of falsehood, as well as the reliability of the truthful party when evidence aligns with their account.

translation: So when he saw his shirt torn from the back, he said, 'Indeed, it is of the deception of you women. Indeed, your deception is great.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and guarding against subtle, deceptive tactics, particularly those employed by women in this context, which can lead even righteous individuals astray. It underscores the need for vigilance and wisdom in discerning hidden motives and the potential for great harm in such deceptions.

translation: Joseph, turn away from this. And ask forgiveness for your sin. Indeed, you were of the sinful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and turning away from sin, even in moments of temptation or moral struggle. It underscores the acknowledgment of human fallibility and the necessity of repentance to maintain spiritual purity.

translation: And women in the city said, 'The wife of the Aziz is seeking to seduce her young man; indeed, she has been consumed by love for him. Indeed, we see her in manifest error.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the societal judgment and moral scrutiny faced by women, particularly in positions of power or influence, where their actions are magnified and misconstrued. It underscores the theme of hypocrisy and the tendency to vilify women based on rumors rather than facts, as seen in the exaggerated claims about the Aziz's wife, which later prove to be false when Yusuf (Joseph) is proven innocent.

translation: So when she heard of their scheming, she sent for them and prepared for them a banquet, and gave each one of them a knife. Then she said, 'Come out before them.' And when they saw him, they were stunned [by his beauty], and cut their hands, and said, 'How perfect is Allah! This is not a human. This is none but a noble angel.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the power of divine beauty and grace, which can overwhelm even the most cunning hearts and cause them to recognize truths beyond their usual perceptions. It also underscores the idea that divine signs—whether in the form of beauty, wisdom, or miracles—can shatter preconceived notions and lead to genuine spiritual awakening.

translation: She said, 'That is the one about whom you blamed me. And I did indeed seek to seduce him, but he firmly refused. And if he does not do what I order him to, he will surely be imprisoned, and he will be among the humiliated.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the struggle between resisting temptation and succumbing to societal pressure or personal desires, emphasizing the importance of moral integrity and steadfastness in faith.

translation: My Lord, prison is more beloved to me than what they invite me to. And if You do not avert their plan from me, I will incline toward them and be of the ignorant.
interpretation: This verse reflects Prophet Yusuf's (Joseph) unwavering commitment to his faith and moral integrity, prioritizing divine obedience over worldly temptation. His plea to Allah demonstrates deep trust in divine wisdom, acknowledging that without Allah's protection, human weakness could lead to deviation.

translation: So his Lord answered him and turned away their plot. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine response to sincere supplication and the protection granted to those who are steadfast in faith, demonstrating Allah's responsiveness to the prayers of His servants and His omniscient awareness of all affairs, including the hidden plots of adversaries.

translation: Then it became clear to them after they had seen the signs that they should imprison him for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the delayed realization of truth despite clear evidence, reflecting human tendency to acknowledge divine signs only after prolonged resistance or suffering, underscoring the interplay between divine signs and human perception.

translation: And there entered the prison with him two young men. One of them said, 'Indeed, I saw myself [in a dream] pressing wine.' And the other said, 'Indeed, I saw myself carrying upon my head [some] bread from which the birds were eating. Inform us of its interpretation; indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking righteous counsel and the power of divine interpretation. The two dreams symbolize different outcomes—one of hardship (carrying bread for birds, which may imply scarcity or servitude) and one of prosperity (pressing wine, which could represent abundance or joy). Their request to Joseph (peace be upon him) underscores the human need for guidance, even in matters of interpretation, and reflects their trust in his righteousness. It also foreshadows Joseph’s God-given ability to interpret dreams, a sign of his prophethood and divine favor.

translation: He said, "You will not receive any food which you are given, but I will surely inform you about its interpretation before it comes to you. That is from what my Lord has taught me. Indeed, I have abandoned the religion of a people who do not believe in Allah, and they, in the Hereafter, are disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Yusuf's (Joseph) unique ability granted by Allah to interpret dreams and unseen matters, demonstrating divine favor and wisdom bestowed upon him. It also underscores his rejection of the faith of his people, who denied Allah and the Hereafter, reflecting his unwavering commitment to monotheism and the truth.

translation: And I followed the religion of my fathers, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. It was not for us to associate anything with Allah. That is from the grace of Allah upon us and upon the people, but most people are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of monotheism (Tawhid) and the rejection of associating partners with Allah, which is a fundamental principle in Islam. It also underscores the idea that true guidance is a divine favor, not something earned by human effort alone. The mention of gratitude serves as a reminder that recognizing Allah's blessings is a moral duty, yet many fail to do so, reflecting a broader spiritual negligence.

translation: O [my fellow] prison companions! Are separate lords better, or Allah, the One, the Prevailing?
interpretation: This verse challenges polytheistic beliefs by questioning the efficacy of multiple deities compared to the absolute oneness and supreme power of Allah, emphasizing that true sovereignty and control belong solely to Him.

translation: You worship besides Him only [mere] names you have named - you and your forefathers - for which Allah has sent down no authority. Legislation is not but for Allah. He has commanded that you worship not except Him. That is the correct religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of worshipping anything other than Allah, emphasizing that such practices lack divine sanction and are merely human inventions. It asserts the absolute authority of Allah in legislation and worship, highlighting the uniqueness of monotheism (Tawhid) as the only true and correct path, while critiquing the ignorance of those who deviate from it.

translation: O [you two] companions of the prison! As for one of you, he will pour wine for his master to drink; and as for the other, he will be crucified, and the birds will eat from his head. The matter about which you inquired has been decreed against you.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine decree and the irrevocability of Allah’s judgment, as the dreams of the two prisoners are interpreted with absolute precision, leaving no room for alteration or delay.

translation: And he said to the one whom he thought would be saved from both [them], 'Mention me to your master.' But Satan caused him to forget the mention [to] his master, so he remained in prison for several years.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of relying on human intermediaries or forgetting divine remembrance due to the influence of Satan, emphasizing the importance of direct reliance on Allah rather than seeking help through others.

translation: And the king said, 'Indeed, I saw [in a dream] seven fat cows being eaten by seven [that were] lean, and seven green spikes [of grain] and others [that were] dry. O eminent ones, advise me in my vision, if you should interpret visions.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking wisdom and counsel from those knowledgeable and capable of providing insight, even in matters of dreams and visions, as they may hold significant meanings or guidance.

translation: They said, "[You are merely telling] false dreams, and we are not knowledgeable in the interpretation of dreams."
interpretation: This verse highlights the dismissive attitude of the people of Pharaoh toward Prophet Yusuf's (Joseph's) interpretation of dreams, reflecting their skepticism and refusal to recognize divine signs or the wisdom in his words.

translation: But the one who was saved from both of them (Joseph and the king) remembered after a time, 'I will inform you about its interpretation, so send me forth.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of patience and the importance of remembering one's duty to convey beneficial knowledge, even after a delay. It also underscores the concept of divine timing, where Allah's wisdom unfolds in ways that test faith and trust in His plan.

translation: Joseph, O truthful one, explain to us [the meaning of] seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones and seven green spikes and others [dried] so that I may return to the people; perhaps they will know [the interpretation].
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking knowledge and wisdom from those who possess it, as the king turned to Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him), recognizing his truthfulness and righteousness, to interpret his dream. It underscores the virtue of consulting experts in their fields and the humility required to acknowledge one's limitations in understanding complex matters.

translation: You will plant for seven years consecutively, so whatever you harvest, leave it in its ear except a little of which you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of prudent planning and sustainable resource management, emphasizing that one should not consume all of their harvest but instead preserve the majority for future needs, reflecting divine wisdom in provision and preparation for lean periods.

translation: Then there will come after that seven intense (years of drought), which will devour what you have laid up for them, except a little of what you have stored away.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly provisions and the importance of humility and reliance on divine will, as even the most diligent preparations can be rendered insignificant in the face of greater, divinely ordained trials.

translation: Then there comes after that a year in which the people are given rain and in which they press [olives and grapes].
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine cycle of provision and hardship, reminding humanity that sustenance and trials are part of a greater, purposeful pattern ordained by Allah, intended to test faith, gratitude, and resilience.

translation: And the king said, 'Bring him to me.' So when the messenger came to him, he said, 'Return to your lord and ask him what is the case of the women who cut their hands. Indeed, my Lord is fully Aware of their deception.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the king's realization of Yusuf's (Joseph's) innocence and the deceitfulness of the women who falsely accused him. It underscores the divine knowledge of Allah, who is aware of all hidden truths and deceptions, reinforcing the theme of divine justice and the ultimate exposure of falsehood.

translation: He said, 'What was your business when you sought to seduce Joseph?' They said, 'God forbid! We know nothing evil of him.' The wife of the governor said, 'Now the truth has come to light. It was I who sought to seduce him, and he is indeed of the truthful ones.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the moral integrity of Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him) and the hypocrisy of those who falsely accused him. It highlights that truth ultimately prevails, even when falsehood is initially propagated, and that the righteous are vindicated by their steadfastness in faith and virtue.

translation: That is so that [Pharaoh] may know that I did not betray him in secret, and that Allah does not guide the deceitful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of sincerity and integrity in one's actions, even when dealing with adversaries, as Allah ultimately exposes deceit and guides the righteous.

translation: And I do not absolve myself, for indeed the soul is prone to evil, except what my Lord has mercy upon. Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent human struggle with the soul's inclination toward wrongdoing and sin, while also emphasizing the necessity of divine mercy and forgiveness to overcome this tendency.

translation: And the king said, 'Bring him to me; I will take him exclusively for myself.' So when he spoke with him, he said, 'Indeed, today you are with us established [in position] and trusted.',
interpretation: This verse highlights the recognition of Joseph's (Yusuf's) exceptional qualities by a powerful figure, demonstrating that trust and competence can be acknowledged even by those outside one's immediate circle, leading to elevated status and responsibility.

translation: He said, 'Appoint me over the storehouses of the land. Indeed, I am a knowledgeable guardian.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trustworthiness and competence in leadership, as the speaker seeks a position of responsibility to manage resources wisely, reflecting a divine principle of appointing qualified individuals to positions of authority.

translation: And thus We established Joseph in the land, to settle therein wherever he willed. We bestow Our mercy upon whom We will, and We do not waste the reward of the good-doers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine decree and the reward for righteousness, emphasizing that Allah's mercy is granted according to His will, and those who strive for goodness will never have their efforts go unrewarded.

translation: And indeed, the reward of the Hereafter is better for those who believe and are conscious of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true believers, who live with piety and mindfulness of Allah, will ultimately receive a superior and everlasting reward in the Hereafter compared to the fleeting pleasures of this world.

translation: And Joseph's brothers came and entered upon him, and he recognized them, but they did not recognize him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and foresight of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) in concealing his identity from his brothers, despite recognizing them, to test their character and prepare the ground for eventual reconciliation and forgiveness.

translation: And when he had furnished them with their provisions, he said, 'Bring me a brother of yours from your father. Do you not see that I give full measure and that I am the best of hosts?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trustworthiness and generosity in dealings, as well as the wisdom in recognizing and rewarding good behavior, even in challenging circumstances.

translation: But if you do not bring it to me, there will be no measure [of grain] for you with me, nor will you [ever] come near [me].
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of failing to fulfill a covenant or obligation, implying that the consequences are not merely material but extend to spiritual and relational estrangement, emphasizing the severity of trustworthiness in divine or moral agreements.

translation: They said, "We will try to persuade his father about him, and indeed, we will succeed."
interpretation: This verse reflects the determination of a group of people to influence or manipulate a situation to their advantage, even if it involves deceit or coercion, highlighting the potential for human cunning and the need for divine guidance to overcome such challenges.

translation: And he said to his young men, "Make their merchandise their luggage, so they might recognize it when they return to their people; perhaps they will come back."
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of moral integrity and trustworthiness, where Yusuf (Joseph) secretly arranges for the return of the merchandise to his brothers' bags, hoping they would realize their innocence and return to him, demonstrating both generosity and strategic foresight.

translation: So when they returned to their father, they said, "O our father, we have been denied the measure (of grain), so send our brother with us so that we may obtain the measure, and indeed we will take care of him."
interpretation: This verse highlights the brothers' cunning deception, where they manipulate their father by fabricating a loss of provisions to justify taking Benjamin with them, despite their prior wrongdoing against Joseph. It underscores the theme of betrayal and the lengths to which envy and guilt can drive people to lie, even to their own family.

translation: He said, 'Shall I entrust him to you except as I entrusted his brother to you before? But Allah is the best Protector, and He is the Most Merciful of the merciful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the wisdom of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) in his measured response to his brothers' request to entrust Binyamin (Benjamin) to them, drawing a parallel to their past betrayal regarding Yusuf himself. It underscores the balance between trust and caution, while affirming complete reliance on Allah’s protection and mercy, as ultimate safeguards against human frailty and deception.

translation: And when they opened their baggage, they found their merchandise returned to them. They said, "O our father, what more could we desire? This is our merchandise returned to us. We will [now] provide [for] our people and protect our brother and obtain an increase of a camel's load; that is an easy measurement."
interpretation: This verse highlights the brothers' realization of divine justice and mercy, as their lost merchandise is unexpectedly returned to them, demonstrating that their earlier actions were flawed and that Allah's plan is beyond human comprehension. Their statement reflects humility and gratitude, acknowledging that their needs are already met, which contrasts with their past arrogance and deceit.

translation: He said, 'I will not send him with you until you give me a sure pledge from Allah to bring him back to me, unless you are surrounded by an enemy.' So when they gave him their pledge, he said, 'Allah is a witness over what we say.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust and accountability in human dealings, even in matters of great consequence. It shows that Prophet Yaqub (Jacob) (peace be upon him) took precautions to ensure the safe return of his son Yusuf (Joseph) (peace be upon him), demonstrating wisdom and foresight in his actions.

translation: And he said, 'O my sons, do not enter from one gate but enter from gates dispersed among you. And I cannot avail you against Allah at all. Indeed, the decision is only for Allah; upon Him I have relied, and upon Him let the reliant rely.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of divine decree and reliance on Allah, emphasizing that human efforts alone cannot alter Allah's will, and true security lies in trusting in Him.

translation: And when they entered from where their father had ordered them, it did not avail them against Allah at all except [it was] a need within the soul of Jacob which he satisfied. And indeed, he was a possessor of knowledge because of what We had taught him, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the limited power of human planning and strategy when faced with divine decree, emphasizing that ultimate control lies with Allah alone. It also underscores the importance of divine knowledge granted to certain individuals, like the Prophet Jacob (peace be upon him), which sets them apart from the majority who remain unaware of such spiritual truths.

translation: And when they entered upon Joseph, he took his brother to himself and said, 'Indeed, I am your brother, so do not grieve over what they used to do.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound mercy and forgiveness of Joseph (Yusuf) towards his brothers despite their past wrongdoings, illustrating the Islamic virtue of pardoning others and the transformative power of reconciliation.

translation: So when he had furnished them with their provisions, he put the king’s bowl into his brother’s saddlebag. Then an announcer called out, 'O caravan! Indeed, you are thieves!',
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust and integrity in human interactions, even in seemingly mundane or opportunistic situations. It suggests that true morality is not merely about outward compliance with rules but is rooted in an inner sense of justice and honesty, as demonstrated by the protagonist's proactive measure to test his brothers' honesty rather than passively allowing circumstances to unfold.

translation: They said, turning to them, 'What is it you are missing?'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of confrontation and questioning, where the tone suggests a mix of curiosity, challenge, or even mockery, as the speakers address a group they are confronting, implying that the latter's presence or actions are unexpected or out of place.

translation: They said, 'We are missing the king's measure, and whoever brings it shall have a camel's load [of grain], and I am responsible for it.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a situation where a group of people, likely officials or servants, are investigating the loss of a valuable item (the king's measure) and setting a reward for its return, demonstrating both a sense of justice in accountability and a practical approach to resolving the matter through incentive.

translation: They said, "By Allah, you have certainly known that we did not come to cause corruption in the land or [that] we have been thieves."
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea of innocence and denial of wrongdoing, where the accused assert their moral integrity and distance themselves from the accusations, invoking divine witness to emphasize their truthfulness.

translation: They said, "So what should be his punishment if you are lying?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the challenge posed by the opponents of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to the divine origin of the Qur'an. They demanded a punishment if the message brought by the Prophet was false, demonstrating their arrogance and refusal to accept the truth despite its clear signs.

translation: They said, "His penalty is that he in whose bag it is found shall be its penalty." Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of personal accountability in justice, where punishment is commensurate with the crime and applied strictly to the wrongdoer, reflecting divine justice that is both precise and impartial.

translation: So he [Joseph] began with their bags before the bag of his brother; then he extracted it from the bag of his brother. Thus did We plan for Joseph. He could not have taken his brother within the king's religion except that Allah willed. We raise in degrees whom We will, and over every possessor of knowledge is one [more] knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind seemingly coincidental or orchestrated events, emphasizing that Allah's plan transcends human understanding. It underscores the principle of *tawakkul* (reliance on Allah) while also illustrating how apparent trials or tests can serve a greater purpose in the divine scheme, ultimately leading to elevated ranks for those chosen by Allah.

translation: They said, 'If he steals, a brother of his has stolen before.' So Joseph kept it to himself and did not reveal it to them. He said, 'You are in a worse position, and Allah is most knowing of what you describe.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and flawed judgment of Joseph's brothers, who accuse him of theft despite their own past wrongdoing. Joseph's response reflects his wisdom in not immediately defending himself, trusting in Allah's knowledge and justice, while subtly exposing their moral inconsistency.

translation: They said, "O Aziz, indeed, he has a father, an old man. So take one of us in his place. Indeed, we see you as one of the good-doers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the brothers' attempt to manipulate Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) by appealing to his sense of justice and mercy, exploiting his known righteousness to persuade him to show leniency toward their brother Binyamin (Benjamin). It highlights the tension between their deceitful intentions and their outward display of respect, revealing their hypocrisy while underscoring Yusuf's moral integrity.

translation: Said [Prophet] 'Allah forbid that we should take [your brother] except from the one at whose place we found our goods. Indeed, we would then be wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Joseph's (peace be upon him) commitment to justice and fairness, even in a personal matter. It underscores the principle that no one should be held accountable or punished for a crime unless there is clear evidence against them, demonstrating the importance of due process and the prohibition of injustice in Islamic ethics.

translation: So when they lost hope in him, they conferred privately. The eldest of them said, "Do you not know that your father has taken a promise from you in Allah's name, and before that you failed regarding Joseph? So I will not leave this land until my father permits me or Allah judges for me, and He is the best of judges."
interpretation: This verse highlights the tension between human resolve and divine decree. The elder brother’s declaration reflects a shift from despair to determination, rooted in a mix of guilt (for past failures) and faith (in Allah’s justice). It underscores the idea that while humans may act out of necessity or regret, ultimate resolution lies with Allah’s wisdom and timing, as He is the 'best of judges'—a reminder of submission to divine will even in moments of human struggle.

translation: Go back to your father and say, 'O our father, indeed your son has stolen, and we did not testify except to what we knew. And we were not, [to be] guardians over the unseen.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of honesty and the limitations of human knowledge. The brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) admit their testimony is based solely on what they witnessed, acknowledging they cannot claim knowledge of hidden matters, thus emphasizing humility and the boundaries of human perception.

translation: And ask the town where we were, and the caravan with which we came, [and they will testify]. And indeed, we are truthful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of corroborating evidence in establishing truth, suggesting that even inanimate witnesses (like a town or caravan) can serve as proof when necessary, reinforcing the gravity of the speaker's claim of innocence.

translation: Nay, but you have tempted yourselves with a vain desire; so patience is most fitting. It may be that Allah will bring them all to me; surely He is the Knowing, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Yusuf's (Joseph) unwavering trust in Allah's wisdom and justice despite the hardships he faced. It highlights the virtue of patience in the face of temptation and adversity, and the belief that Allah's plan, though unseen, is ultimately beneficial and just.

translation: And he turned away from them and said, 'Alas, my sorrow over Yusuf!' And his eyes turned white from grief, and he was filled with sorrow.
interpretation: This verse highlights the depth of Prophet Yaqub's (Jacob's) emotional pain and grief over the loss of his beloved son Yusuf (Joseph), to the point of overwhelming sorrow that manifests physically in his eyes turning white and his heart being crushed with grief.

translation: They said, "By Allah, you will not cease remembering Joseph until you become fatally ill or perish."
interpretation: This verse reveals the depth of the brothers' jealousy and their inability to tolerate their father's constant mention of Joseph, reflecting how unchecked envy can lead to extreme and harmful reactions against the object of one's resentment.

translation: Indeed, I complain of my suffering and sorrow only to Allah, and I know from Allah what you do not know.
interpretation: This verse reflects the depth of Prophet Yaqub's (Jacob) reliance and trust in Allah during times of hardship, emphasizing that true solace and resolution come from Allah alone, beyond human understanding.

translation: O my sons, go and seek news of Joseph and his brother, and do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, no one despairs of the mercy of Allah except the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse encourages steadfastness and hope in Allah’s mercy even in the face of seemingly insurmountable difficulties, emphasizing that despair is a trait of those who reject faith.

translation: So when they came to him, they said, "O Aziz, hardship has touched us and our family, and we have come with goods of little value. So give us full measure and be charitable to us. Indeed, Allah rewards the charitable."
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and desperation of the people who approached Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) during a time of famine, acknowledging their need and appealing to his sense of justice and charity, while also reminding him of Allah's reward for those who give.

translation: Did you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were unaware?
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing past wrongdoings, even if committed in ignorance, and the necessity of seeking forgiveness and rectifying one's actions.

translation: They said, 'Are you indeed Joseph?' He said, 'I am Joseph, and this is my brother. Allah has certainly conferred favor upon us. Indeed, he who fears Allah and is patient - then Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of patience and piety in the face of hardship and adversity. It underscores that those who remain steadfast in their faith and righteousness, trusting in Allah's plan, will ultimately be rewarded, as their efforts and perseverance are never in vain in the sight of Allah.

translation: They said, 'By Allah, Allah has certainly preferred you over us, and we were indeed sinners.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the acknowledgment of a divine favor bestowed upon someone, coupled with a confession of one's own shortcomings or sins, highlighting humility and recognition of God's grace.

translation: He said, "No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you; and He is the most Merciful of the merciful."
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound mercy and forgiveness of Allah, emphasizing that sincere repentance and turning back to Him erases past wrongs, offering hope and relief to those seeking redemption.

translation: Go with this shirt of mine and cast it over my father's face, he will regain his sight. And bring me all your family members.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power of faith and the divine connection between a prophet and his family. It signifies that spiritual purity and divine favor can restore physical and spiritual sight, emphasizing the importance of trust in Allah's plan and the intercession of righteous individuals.

translation: And when the caravan departed, their father said, 'Indeed, I find the scent of Joseph, except you think I am delusional.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep emotional bond between Prophet Yaqub (Jacob) and his son Yusuf (Joseph). It demonstrates the strength of a father's love and intuition, even in the face of separation and adversity, as well as the pain of longing and hope for reunion.

translation: They said, "By Allah, indeed you are in your old error."
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubbornness and denial of the disbelievers who refuse to accept the truth despite clear evidence. Their statement reveals their deep-seated arrogance and refusal to acknowledge the guidance presented to them, clinging instead to their long-held false beliefs.

translation: But when the bearer of good news arrived, he cast it on his face, and he became seeing. He said, 'Did I not say to you that I know from Allah what you do not know?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of trust in divine knowledge and the consequences of doubt. The bearer of good news, through his unwavering faith and submission to Allah's will, regains his sight—a metaphor for spiritual enlightenment—while those who doubted are reminded of the limitations of their own understanding compared to the certainty of divine wisdom.

translation: They said, "O our father, ask for forgiveness for our sins, indeed we have been sinners."
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and repentance of the brothers of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) when they sought forgiveness from their father, Prophet Yaqub (Jacob), acknowledging their past wrongdoings and seeking his intercession for divine mercy.

translation: He said, 'I will ask forgiveness for you from my Lord. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet's (peace be upon him) intercession and his reliance on Allah's mercy, demonstrating the importance of seeking forgiveness and the boundless compassion of Allah, even for those who may have wronged others.

translation: So when they entered upon Joseph, he took his parents to him and said, "Enter Egypt, Allah willing, safe and secure."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine fulfillment of a promise and the importance of trust in Allah's plan. Joseph's invitation to his family to enter Egypt, with the phrase 'Insha'Allah' (if Allah wills), reflects his humility and acknowledgment that all affairs are subject to Allah's decree, emphasizing reliance on Him rather than arrogance or presumption of control.

translation: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they fell down before him in prostration. And he said, 'O my father, this is the interpretation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it a reality. And He was good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you from the desert after Satan had sown discord between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, He is the Knowing, the Wise.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and gratitude of Prophet Yusuf (Joseph) towards Allah. Despite his high status in Egypt, he acknowledges that his dreams' fulfillment and his family's reunion are solely due to Allah's grace and wisdom. It underscores the importance of recognizing divine intervention in one's life and the power of Allah's subtle and wise plans, even in seemingly impossible situations.

translation: My Lord, You have granted me some sovereignty and taught me the interpretation of events. Creator of the heavens and the earth, You are my Protector in this world and the Hereafter. Cause me to die a Muslim and join me with the righteous.
interpretation: This supplication reflects the humility and gratitude of the speaker, acknowledging Allah's supreme authority and wisdom in granting knowledge and power. It underscores the believer's reliance on Allah as their ultimate protector and guide, seeking a righteous end and companionship with the righteous in the Hereafter.

translation: This is from the news of the unseen which We reveal to you, [O Muhammad]. And you were not with them when they put together their plan and were scheming.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing that its knowledge of past events—particularly those unseen by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him)—is a sign of its authenticity as revelation from Allah, not human fabrication.

translation: And most of the people, even if you desire it, will not be believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent free will of individuals and the limits of human influence in matters of faith, emphasizing that true belief is a matter of the heart and divine guidance rather than mere human persuasion.

translation: And you do not ask them for any payment for it; it is but a reminder for the worlds.
interpretation: The verse underscores the pure, selfless nature of the Prophet's mission—he does not seek personal gain or reward for delivering the divine message, as its purpose is solely to serve as a universal guidance and reminder for all of humanity.

translation: And how many a sign is there in the heavens and the earth which they pass by, while they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of people who witness the signs of Allah's existence and power in the natural world yet deliberately ignore them, showing ingratitude and heedlessness toward divine signs.

translation: And most of them believe in Allah only while they associate others with Him [in worship].
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and superficial faith of many people who claim to believe in Allah but still engage in polytheistic practices, such as associating partners with Him in worship, seeking intercession from others, or attributing divine attributes to creation.

translation: Do they feel secure that a overwhelming punishment from Allah will not come upon them, or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they perceive not?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against complacency and false security in the face of divine justice. It underscores the sudden and inevitable nature of Allah's punishment or the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that no one can escape accountability, regardless of their perceived safety or ignorance.

translation: Say, 'This is my way; I invite to Allah with insight, I and those who follow me. And exalted is Allah; and I am not of those who associate others with Him.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of calling to Allah with clarity, knowledge, and conviction, while also affirming the exclusivity of worship to Him alone. It underscores the responsibility of the caller to Islam to be grounded in understanding and to distance themselves from any form of shirk (associating partners with Allah).

translation: And We sent not before you, [O Muhammad], except men to whom We revealed [Our message]. So ask the people of the former scriptures if you do not know. And We did not make the former people of disbelievers possessors of the earth, and We have not sent them before you except as deliverers of good tidings and warners. And those who disbelieved say, "This is not but a lie he invented, and another people have aided him in it." But they have come with wrongdoing and manifest falsehood. And they say, "None will enter Paradise except one who is a Jew or a Christian." That is [their] wish. Say, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse underscores the consistency of divine revelation across different eras, emphasizing that prophets before Muhammad (peace be upon him) were also human beings from their respective communities, not supernatural beings. It challenges the people of Makkah to reflect on the fate of past nations who rejected their prophets, implying that their own fate could similarly be dire if they persist in disbelief. The verse also highlights the superiority of the Hereafter for the God-conscious, contrasting worldly life with the eternal rewards of the righteous. The rhetorical questions invite reflection and reason, urging the audience to use their intellect to recognize the truth rather than clinging to baseless claims or prejudices.

translation: Until, when the messengers despaired and were certain that they had been denied [by their people], there came to them Our victory, and whoever We willed was saved. And Our punishment cannot be repelled from the people who are criminals.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the ultimate triumph of truth, even when it appears that falsehood has prevailed. It reassures believers that divine aid is certain to arrive at the appointed time, and that no amount of despair or denial can alter the course of justice. The verse also serves as a warning to oppressors that their crimes will not go unpunished, reinforcing the moral order of the universe.

translation: There was certainly a lesson in the stories of those before them for those of understanding. The Qur'an is not a fabricated tale, but rather a confirmation of what came before it, a detailed explanation of all things, and a guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the Qur'an's divine origin and its purpose as a source of guidance and mercy, not a human invention. It highlights that the stories of previous prophets and nations serve as lessons for those who reflect deeply (Ulil Albab), emphasizing the continuity of divine revelation and the importance of recognizing truth through intellectual and spiritual discernment.

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book whose verses are perfected and then presented in detail from [one who is] Wise and Acquainted. [Say], 'Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days and attribute to Him equals? That is the Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and perfection of the Qur'an, emphasizing that its verses are meticulously structured and detailed, reflecting the wisdom and knowledge of Allah. It challenges the disbelievers to reflect on the creation of the earth in two days as a sign of Allah's power, urging them to reject the false attribution of equals to Him, which is a fundamental aspect of monotheism (Tawhid).

translation: It is Allah who created the heavens without pillars that you can see; then He established Himself above the Throne. And He subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. He arranges [each] matter; He details the signs that you might, of the meeting with your Lord, be certain.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over all creation, highlighting His ability to govern the universe without visible support, demonstrating His transcendence and control over cosmic order.

translation: And it is He who spread the earth and placed in it firm mountains and rivers; and from all fruits He made in it pairs two by two. He causes the night to cover the day. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate design and balance in creation, inviting reflection on the signs of Allah's power and wisdom in the natural world, encouraging believers to ponder and recognize divine order.

translation: And in the earth are diverse regions (close) together, and gardens of grapes, and crops, and date-palms, growing from one root or from distinct roots, watered with the same water. Yet some We make to excel others in fruit. Verily, in that are signs for people who understand.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity and interconnectedness of life on Earth, demonstrating how different plants, though sharing the same environment and resources, produce varying fruits and benefits, reflecting a deliberate design that invites reflection on the wisdom and power of the Creator.

translation: And if you are amazed, then amazing is their saying, 'When we are dust, will we indeed be in a new creation?' Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, and those will have shackles around their necks, and those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of those who reject the concept of resurrection and the Hereafter, questioning how they could be recreated after becoming dust. It underscores the severity of their denial, equating their disbelief to a form of spiritual bondage, and warns of the eternal punishment that awaits them in Hell.

translation: And they urge you to hasten the evil [i.e., punishment] before the good [i.e., mercy], while there have already occurred before them similar punishments. Indeed, your Lord is Forgiving and Merciful to the people despite their wrongdoing, and indeed, your Lord is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse underscores the impatience of those who demand immediate punishment for their wrongdoing while ignoring Allah's mercy and the opportunity for repentance, reminding them of the consequences faced by past nations who rejected divine warnings.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" You are only a warner, and for every people is a guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism of the disbelievers who demand miraculous signs as proof of prophethood, while affirming the role of the Prophet (peace be upon him) as a warner and acknowledging that guidance comes from Allah for each community through its appointed guide or prophet.

translation: Allah knows what every female carries and what the wombs contract and what they expand. And every matter is with Him according to a measure.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute knowledge and control over all aspects of creation, including the unseen processes within the wombs and the precise measurement of all things, affirming His divine wisdom and sovereignty over life's intricacies.

translation: The Knower of the unseen and the seen, the Most Great, the Most High.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute knowledge encompassing all that is hidden and manifest, and His supreme majesty and exalted status above all creation, affirming His unparalleled sovereignty and transcendence.

translation: Whether one of you conceals the speech or publicizes it, and whether one is hidden by night or goes forth by day.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah is fully aware of all actions, whether they are done in secret or openly, at night or during the day, highlighting the all-encompassing knowledge and presence of Allah over all human deeds.

translation: For each soul, there are successive guardians before and behind it, protecting it by Allah's command. Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is within themselves. And when Allah intends for a people ill, there is no repelling it. And there is not for them besides Him any protector.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the concept of divine decree and human agency, highlighting that while Allah has decreed certain outcomes for individuals and communities, these outcomes are not arbitrary but are tied to the moral and spiritual state of those people. It underscores the principle of accountability and the power of self-reformation, implying that change must begin within before it manifests externally.

translation: It is He who shows you the lightning, [causing] fear and aspiration, and produces the heavy clouds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of divine signs—how they evoke both fear and hope in human hearts, reflecting the balance between divine warnings (like lightning as a sign of punishment) and divine mercy (like rain as a sign of sustenance), thereby underscoring Allah's absolute control over creation and the need for human reflection and reliance on Him.

translation: And the thunder exalts [Allah] with His praise, and the angels [as well] from fear of Him. And He sends thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills while they dispute about Allah - and He is severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power and majesty of Allah, emphasizing that even natural phenomena like thunder glorify Him, while angels tremble in awe of His might. It underscores the futility of human disputes about Allah’s nature or authority, as His decrees are unchallengeable and His punishment severe for those who reject His signs.

translation: To Him alone belongs the supplication of truth. Those whom they invoke besides Him do not respond to them at all, just as a person stretches out his hands towards water, desiring it to reach his mouth, but it never does. The supplications of the disbelievers are only in vain.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of invoking anything or anyone other than Allah, as He alone possesses the power to respond to supplications. The imagery of stretching out hands towards water that never reaches the mouth vividly illustrates the helplessness and ineffectiveness of seeking help from false deities or intermediaries, emphasizing that such efforts are inherently misguided and devoid of true benefit.

translation: To Allah prostrates whoever is within the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, and [so do] their shadows in the mornings and the evenings.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that even those who may reject Him in their hearts are compelled to acknowledge His dominion through the natural order of existence. The mention of shadows prostrating in the mornings and evenings symbolizes the inevitability of submission to Allah’s will, as the movement of the sun dictates the passage of time and the cycle of day and night, reflecting a universal and unchanging truth.

translation: Say, 'Who is Lord of the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Then have you taken besides Him allies who do not possess [even] for themselves any benefit or harm?' Say, 'Is the blind equivalent to the seeing? Or is darkness equivalent to light? Or have they attributed to Allah partners who created like His creation so that the creation seemed similar to them?' Say, 'Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Prevailing.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness (Tawheed) of Allah and refutes the notion of associating partners with Him. It highlights the futility of worshipping false deities who have no power to benefit or harm, contrasting them with Allah, the sole Creator and Sustainer of all things. The rhetorical questions underscore the inherent disparity between truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, and the uniqueness of Allah's creative power.

translation: He sends down from the sky, water, and the valleys flow according to their measure, but the flood carries a rising foam. And from that which they kindle in the fire, seeking adornment or utensils, is foam like it. Thus does Allah present the truth and falsehood. As for the foam, it vanishes, [being] cast off; but as for that which benefits the people, it remains on the earth. Thus does Allah present examples.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the transient nature of falsehood and the enduring value of truth. Just as foam from a flood or molten metal quickly dissipates, so too does falsehood ultimately fade away, leaving no lasting impact. In contrast, truth—like the beneficial elements carried by the water or the refined metal—endures and provides lasting benefit to humanity, reflecting its intrinsic value and permanence in the divine plan.

translation: For those who responded to their Lord is the best [reward]. But as for those who did not respond to Him, if they had all that is in the earth, all of it, and the like of it with it, they would offer it for ransom. It is those who will have the worst reckoning, and their refuge is Hell—and how wretched is that destination.
interpretation: This verse underscores the stark contrast between the recompense of those who heed their Lord’s call and those who reject it. The latter’s attachment to worldly wealth is so profound that even an equivalent of all earthly treasures would not suffice to save them from divine accountability, highlighting the futility of materialism in the face of ultimate justice. Their punishment is severe, and their abode is Hell—a place of profound misery, emphasizing the gravity of rejecting divine guidance.

translation: Then is he who knows that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth like he who is blind? Only those of understanding will pay heed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those who recognize and accept the divine truth revealed in the Qur'an and those who remain spiritually blind to it, emphasizing that true understanding and reflection are gifts granted only to those with sound intellect and awareness.

translation: Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the promise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of keeping one's word and fulfilling commitments made to Allah, highlighting the virtue of trustworthiness and integrity in one's dealings with the Divine and, by extension, with others.

translation: And [they are] those who join what Allah has ordered to be joined and fear their Lord and are afraid of the evil of [their] account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of maintaining ties of kinship and righteous relationships as commanded by Allah, while also emphasizing the believer's consciousness of Allah's commandments and the accountability of their deeds on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord, and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, and repel evil with good - it is they who will have the final attainment of the [eternal] home.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of true believers who embody patience, devotion, and righteousness. Their actions are driven by sincere faith and a desire for Allah's pleasure, not worldly recognition. By repelling evil with good, they demonstrate moral strength and spiritual maturity, ultimately securing a blessed and eternal abode in Paradise.

translation: They will enter Gardens of perpetual residence, which the Most Merciful has promised to His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise has ever been coming. They will not hear therein any ill speech - only [greetings of] peace - and they will have their sustenance therein, morning and afternoon.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exclusivity and generosity of Allah's promise of Paradise, emphasizing that entry is not solely based on individual righteousness but extends to righteous family members, demonstrating the importance of familial piety and the communal aspect of salvation in Islam.

translation: Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.
interpretation: This verse acknowledges and rewards the steadfastness and perseverance of believers in the face of hardship, emphasizing that patience in this world leads to a blessed and ultimate abode in the Hereafter.

translation: But those who break the covenant of Allah after its confirmation and sever what Allah has ordered to be joined and spread corruption on earth - for them is the curse, and they will have the worst of homes.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of breaking solemn promises made with Allah, particularly those that involve severing ties of kinship or righteous conduct, and engaging in corruption. It serves as a stern warning against betrayal of divine trust and moral decay, emphasizing that such actions lead to divine displeasure and a wretched end in the Hereafter.

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. And they rejoiced in the life of the world, while the life of the world is, compared to the Hereafter, not but a brief enjoyment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom behind the distribution of sustenance, reminding believers that material prosperity in this world is temporary and insignificant when measured against the eternal life to come, urging detachment from worldly attachments and trust in Allah's decree.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him from his Lord?" Say, "Indeed, Allah leaves astray whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back [to Him]."
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of the disbelievers who demand miraculous signs as proof of prophethood, highlighting Allah's absolute sovereignty over guidance and misguidance, which is based on His infinite wisdom and the free will of individuals to turn to Him.

translation: Those who have believed, and whose hearts find reassurance in the remembrance of Allah. Unquestionably, by the remembrance of Allah do hearts find reassurance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound spiritual tranquility that comes from remembering Allah, emphasizing that true faith is not just a cognitive belief but also a heartfelt connection that brings inner peace and contentment.

translation: Those who believe and do righteous deeds—excellent is their reward and good is their final destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine promise of ultimate success and felicity for believers who combine faith with righteous actions, emphasizing that true prosperity lies not only in worldly rewards but in the eternal, blissful return to Allah.

translation: Thus We have sent you (O Muhammad) to a community before whom other communities have passed away, in order that you might recite to them what We have revealed to you, while they disbelieve in the Most Beneficent (Allah). Say: "He is my Lord, there is no god but He. In Him I put my trust, and to Him will be my return (for resurrection)."
interpretation: This verse underscores the prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger to a people who, like previous nations, reject the message of Tawhid (the Oneness of Allah). It emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah, the necessity of placing trust in Him alone, and the ultimate return to Him for judgment, reinforcing the themes of divine unity, accountability, and reliance on Allah.

translation: And if there were a Qur'an with which mountains could be moved, or the earth could be split asunder, or the dead could be made to speak (it would not have been other than this Qur'an), but to Allah belongs the Command altogether. Do the believers not see that if Allah had willed, He could have guided all mankind? And never will the disbelievers receive a calamity for what they have earned, or will it settle near their homes until the promise of Allah comes. Indeed, Allah does not fail in [His] promise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation and the limits of human will in the face of divine decree. It rejects the notion that guidance is solely dependent on miraculous signs or coercive proof, emphasizing instead that faith is a matter of the heart and divine wisdom. The verse also serves as a reminder of divine justice, affirming that Allah’s promises are certain and that the disbelievers’ rejection will ultimately lead to their just recompense, without delay or favor.

translation: And certainly were messengers mocked before you, but I prolonged enjoyment for those who disbelieved; then I seized them, and how [terrible] was My penalty.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who mock or reject the messengers of God, illustrating that past nations who did so faced severe divine punishment despite temporary worldly prosperity, emphasizing the inevitability and justice of God's retribution for persistent disbelief.

translation: Is He who takes account of each soul for what it has earned? Yet they associate others with Allah. Say, 'Name them! Or do you inform Him of something He does not know on earth, or of some word of conjecture?' Rather, their machinations have been made to seem fair to the disbelievers, and they have been obstructed from the path. And whoever Allah leaves astray has no guide.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute accountability of every individual for their actions, highlighting Allah's omniscience and sovereignty. The rhetorical questions challenge the polytheists' attribution of partners to Allah, exposing the absurdity of their claims and the lack of evidence for such associations. The verse also reveals the deceptive nature of disbelief, where misguidance is made to appear attractive, leading people away from the truth, and emphasizing that divine guidance is the only path to righteousness.

translation: For them is a punishment in the life of this world, and indeed, the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe. And for them, there is no protector against Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief or transgression, emphasizing that their suffering is not only deferred to the Hereafter but also manifests in worldly consequences, which serve as a reminder of their misdeeds.

translation: The example of Paradise which the righteous have been promised is [that] beneath it rivers flow. Its food is eternal and its shade. That is the consequence for the righteous, and the consequence for the disbelievers is the Fire.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the eternal and unchanging nature of Paradise as a reward for the righteous, contrasting it with the Fire as the inevitable consequence for the disbelievers, emphasizing divine justice and the permanence of the Hereafter.

translation: And those to whom We gave the Book rejoice in what has been revealed to you, [O Muhammad], while [some] factions disbelieve in part of it. Say, "I have only been commanded to worship Allah and not associate anything with Him. To Him I invite, and to Him is my return."
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who recognize the truth of divine revelation and those who reject it partially or entirely. It emphasizes the exclusive worship of Allah, rejecting any form of idolatry or association, and underscores the ultimate return to Allah, reinforcing the accountability of all actions.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic legislation. And if you should follow their desires after what has come to you of knowledge, you will not have against Allah any ally or protector.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and unchangeable nature of the Qur'an's guidance, emphasizing that deviating from its teachings—especially to appease human desires or societal pressures—will leave one without divine support or protection, highlighting the absolute authority of Allah's commandments over personal inclinations.

translation: And We have already sent messengers before you and assigned to them wives and descendants. And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah. For every term is a decree.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom behind the humanization of prophets—highlighting that they were not exempt from natural human experiences like marriage and family life—while simultaneously affirming that any miraculous signs they brought were solely by Allah’s command, not their own power. It also emphasizes the predetermined nature of all events, reinforcing the concept of divine decree (*qadar*) and the fixed timeline (*ajal*) for all matters.

translation: Allah erases what He wills and confirms, and with Him is the Mother of the Book.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute sovereignty over all affairs, including the ability to alter or confirm events, decrees, or records as He wills. The 'Mother of the Book' (Umm al-Kitab) refers to the preserved, eternal knowledge of Allah, which encompasses all divine decrees and realities, serving as the ultimate source of truth and certainty.

translation: And [whether] We show you some of what We promise them, or [whether] We take you [in death], indeed, it is for you [only] to convey [the message], and upon Us is the account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) responsibility to convey the divine message without coercion or guarantee of its immediate acceptance, while reassuring him that the ultimate accountability for the response of the people rests with Allah alone.

translation: Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges? And Allah judges; none can reverse His judgment. And He is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine decree and the futility of resisting it. The 'reduction of the land from its edges' symbolizes the gradual but certain fulfillment of Allah's will, whether through natural processes, historical events, or the decline of civilizations. The verse serves as a reminder that Allah's judgment is absolute and irreversible, and that all actions will be swiftly accounted for, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly power and the permanence of divine justice.

translation: And those before them had already plotted, but Allah [took away] their plot entirely. He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will come to know for whom is the final destination of the abode.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah’s absolute power to thwart the schemes of those who plot against His guidance, emphasizing that no deception can ultimately succeed against divine will. It also serves as a warning to disbelievers that their actions—no matter how cunning—will be fully accounted for, and the consequences of their deeds will manifest in the Hereafter, where the true outcome of their efforts will be revealed.

translation: And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Sufficient is Allah as a witness between me and you, and whoever has knowledge of the Book."
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine validation of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) mission, asserting that even those who reject his prophethood cannot deny the truth when confronted with the knowledge of those who possess divine scripture, such as the People of the Book (Jews and Christians). It highlights that true understanding of scripture would lead to recognition of the Prophet's truthfulness, as Allah's signs are evident in both revelation and creation.

translation: Alif, Lam, Ra. [This is] a Book which We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], that you might bring mankind out of darknesses into the light by permission of their Lord - to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and purpose of the Qur'an as a source of guidance, emphasizing its role in illuminating the path from ignorance and misguidance ('darknesses') to truth and righteousness ('light') through Allah's permission, leading to the recognition of His absolute power ('Exalted in Might') and boundless praise ('Praiseworthy').

translation: Allah is He besides Whom there is no god, the Owner of all things in the heavens and the earth; and woe to the disbelievers because of a severe punishment;
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all existence, emphasizing that there is no deity worthy of worship except Him. The warning of 'woe' to the disbelievers signifies the severe consequences of rejecting divine truth, highlighting the gravity of disbelief in the face of Allah's unassailable authority and the inevitability of His just punishment.

translation: Those who prefer the life of this world over the Hereafter and avert [people] from the way of Allah, seeking to make it [seem] deviant - they are in extreme error.
interpretation: This verse warns against prioritizing worldly desires over spiritual obligations, highlighting the danger of leading others astray by distorting the path of truth for selfish or corrupt motives.

translation: And We sent not a messenger except [speaking] in the language of his people to clarify for them, and Allah sends astray [thereby] whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
