The mention of the earth swallowing them or punishment striking unexpectedly highlights the sudden and inescapable nature of Allah's justice, which operates beyond human perception and control.

translation: Or He may seize them during their (daily) movements, and there is none to prevent Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and control over all things, including the movements and actions of people. It serves as a reminder that no one can escape or evade Allah's grasp, as He has the ability to seize or punish whenever He wills, without any power to resist or escape.

translation: Or He may seize them during their fear (of an impending calamity). Indeed, your Lord is Most Kind and Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and compassion, even in moments of fear or impending hardship, reminding believers that divine punishment is not arbitrary but tempered by His boundless mercy.

translation: Do they not see that Allah, Who created all things, causes the shadows to incline to the right and to the left, prostrating to Allah while they are humble?
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural order and submission of all creation to Allah, contrasting the deliberate disobedience of those who refuse to recognize this divine sign, thereby emphasizing the universality of Allah's sovereignty and the futility of human arrogance.

translation: To Allah prostrates whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, including all creatures, and the angels, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that every entity—whether in the heavens, on earth, or among the angels—submits to His will through prostration, a symbol of humility and obedience. The mention of angels not being arrogant highlights that true submission is not a sign of weakness but of profound recognition of divine authority and wisdom.

translation: They fear their Lord above them, and they do what they are commanded.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound reverence and awe that the angels have for Allah, recognizing His absolute authority and power above them, while simultaneously demonstrating their unwavering obedience to His commands without hesitation or deviation.

translation: And Allah has said, 'Do not take two deities. Indeed, He is only One God. So fear only Me.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and prohibits associating any partners with Him, warning against polytheism and commanding exclusive devotion and reverence toward Allah alone.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and to Him is due [all] religion, [throughout] the upright [times]. Then is it other than Allah you fear?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation and the exclusivity of His right to worship and obedience, critiquing any deviation from this principle as misplaced fear or devotion.

translation: And whatever favor you have is from Allah; then when harm touches you, to Him you cry for help.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute dependence of human beings on Allah for all blessings and assistance, emphasizing that even in times of distress, the only true source of relief and support is Him.

translation: But when He removes the harm from you, at once a party of you associates others with their Lord [in worship],
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness of human nature, particularly in times of distress and relief. It suggests that when people face hardship, they may turn to Allah sincerely, but upon being relieved of that hardship, some revert to associating partners with Allah, demonstrating a lack of true faith and gratitude.

translation: So they may deny what We have granted them. So enjoy yourselves. Soon you will know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the blessings and guidance from Allah, reminding them that their denial will not go unanswered and that they will face consequences for their disbelief.

translation: And they assign to what they do not know a share of the sustenance We have provided them. By Allah, you will surely be questioned about what you used to fabricate.
interpretation: This verse highlights the folly of attributing divine qualities or powers to false deities or fabricated beliefs, as people often allocate a portion of their blessings to things they do not truly understand or acknowledge as worthy of worship. The warning underscores the accountability for false claims and attributions, emphasizing that such fabrications will be scrutinized in the Hereafter.

translation: And they attribute to Allah daughters—exalted is He—and for themselves is whatever they desire.
interpretation: This verse critiques the pre-Islamic Arab practice of demeaning daughters by associating them with Allah while arrogantly claiming superiority through their own desires, highlighting the hypocrisy of assigning divine attributes to what they consider inferior.

translation: And when one of them is given the glad tidings of [the birth of] a female, his face becomes dark and he suppresses [his] resentment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep-seated societal prejudice against women in pre-Islamic Arabia, where the birth of a daughter was often met with disappointment and shame, reflecting a distorted sense of honor tied to male lineage.

translation: There will hide from the people the evil of which they are informed: Will he keep it on (suffering) contemptuously, or bury it in the dust? Behold, evil is what they judge.
interpretation: This verse reflects the moral cowardice of those who conceal the truth or suppress justice when faced with evil, choosing instead to endure humiliation or bury the truth rather than confront it openly, revealing the flawed nature of their judgment.

translation: For those who do not believe in the Hereafter, the example is like the evil, and for Allah is the highest example. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the perception of those who deny the Hereafter and the true nature of Allah. It underscores that the disbelief in the Hereafter leads to a flawed and negative understanding of existence, akin to 'evil' or futility, while Allah's attributes—perfect, supreme, and beyond human limitations—are the ultimate reality. The verse also serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute power and wisdom, which believers acknowledge and disbelievers fail to grasp.

translation: And if Allah were to impose blame on the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon the earth a single creature, but He defers them for a specified term. And when their term comes, they will not remain behind an hour, nor will they precede [it].
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's boundless mercy and forbearance, as He does not immediately punish people for their injustices, allowing them time to repent and reform. It also highlights the inevitability of divine justice, where every soul will face the consequences of its actions at the appointed time, without delay or haste.

translation: And they attribute to Allah what they dislike, while their tongues describe falsehood as if for them is the best [reward]. Assuredly, for them is the Fire, and they will be [rightly] abandoned.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who falsely attribute to Allah what He dislikes or dislikes Him to be associated with, while hypocritically portraying their falsehoods as virtuous or beneficial for themselves. It highlights the moral corruption of such individuals, who distort truth to serve their own interests, and warns of their inevitable punishment in the Hereafter for their deceit and arrogance.

translation: By Allah, We did send Messengers to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds fair-seeming to them; so he is their patron today, and they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the recurring pattern of human history where Satan deceives people into justifying their wrongdoings, leading them astray from divine guidance, and ultimately resulting in their downfall and punishment.

translation: And We have not sent down to you the Book, [O Muhammad], except for you to make clear to them that wherein they have differed and as guidance and mercy for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the primary purpose of the Qur'an: to resolve disputes among people regarding matters of faith and guidance, while also serving as a source of divine mercy and guidance for those who embrace belief, reinforcing the idea that the Qur'an is a clarifying and merciful revelation meant to guide believers through their spiritual and moral challenges.

translation: And Allah sends down from the sky, water, and with it He revives the earth after its death. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power of Allah in reviving the dead earth through rain, serving as a metaphor for spiritual revival and the importance of heeding divine signs and guidance.

translation: And indeed, in the cattle there is a lesson for you. We give you drink from what is in their bellies - between excretion and blood - pure milk, palatable for drinkers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate design in creation, demonstrating Allah's power to produce pure sustenance (milk) from seemingly impure sources (the mixture of food, blood, and waste in the stomach), underscoring the concept of divine wisdom and the signs of Allah's existence in the natural world.

translation: And from the fruits of date-palms and grapevines you derive intoxicants and good provision. Indeed, in that is a sign for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of certain fruits—like dates and grapes—from which both harmful intoxicants (such as wine) and beneficial provisions (such as food) can be derived, emphasizing the importance of wisdom and discernment in distinguishing between what is beneficial and what is harmful for humanity.

translation: And your Lord inspired to the bee, 'Take for yourself, from the mountains, houses, and from the trees, and [also] what they construct.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in creating and guiding even the smallest creatures, like bees, to utilize their environment effectively for survival and productivity, underscoring the broader principle of divine providence and the intricate balance in creation.

translation: Then eat from all the fruits and follow the ways of your Lord laid down [for you]. There emerges from their bellies a drink, varying in colors, in which there is healing for people. Indeed in that is a sign for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing divine signs in nature, encouraging reflection and gratitude for the sustenance provided by Allah. The mention of diverse fruits and their healing properties highlights the wisdom and mercy in creation, urging believers to ponder over the signs to strengthen their faith and understanding of Allah's power.

translation: And Allah created you; then He will take your souls at death. And among you is he who is brought back to the most decrepit [old] age so that he will not know, after [having had] knowledge, a thing. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of human life and the inevitability of death, emphasizing that no matter how long one lives, the decline of old age can strip away knowledge and faculties, underscoring the absolute power and knowledge of Allah in controlling the lifespan and conditions of His creation.

translation: And Allah has favored some of you over others in [worldly] provision. But those who were favored would not give their provision to those whom their right hands possess so they would be equal thereby. Then is it the favor of Allah they reject?
interpretation: This verse critiques the human tendency to hoard blessings from Allah and deny others their due, despite acknowledging that all provision ultimately comes from Him. It highlights the hypocrisy of those who enjoy Allah’s favors but refuse to share them equitably, even with those under their care, while still claiming to believe in His grace. The verse underscores the moral obligation to recognize Allah’s blessings as a test of gratitude and generosity, not a license for selfishness or exploitation.

translation: And Allah has made for you from yourselves mates, and has made for you from your mates children and grandchildren, and has provided for you from the good things. Then is it the falsehood that they believe in, and [yet], it is the favor of Allah they disbelieve in?
interpretation: This verse underscores the natural order and divine blessings in human life, contrasting the acknowledgment of Allah's favors with the irrationality of preferring falsehood over them, highlighting ingratitude as a moral failing.

translation: And they worship besides Allah that which can neither provide them any provision from the heavens or the earth, nor can they do anything.
interpretation: This verse condemns the worship of anything other than Allah, emphasizing that such objects or beings lack the power to provide sustenance or influence any aspect of existence, highlighting the futility and irrationality of associating partners with Allah.

translation: So do not set up any similitudes for Allah. Indeed, Allah knows while you do not know.
interpretation: This verse warns against likening Allah to His creation or attempting to define Him through human analogies, emphasizing the limits of human knowledge and the absolute transcendence of Allah.

translation: Allah presents an example: a slave owned by another, who has no power over anything, and someone to whom We have granted good provision from Us, so he spends from it secretly and openly. Can they be equal? Praise be to Allah. But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the helplessness of a slave who owns nothing with the blessed capacity of a free believer who, having been granted sustenance by Allah, spends it in all circumstances—openly and in secret—thus demonstrating gratitude and moral agency, which elevate him above the helpless slave.

translation: And Allah presents an example: two men, one of them mute, unable to do anything, a burden upon his master—wherever he directs him, he brings no good. Is he equal to one who commands justice and is on a straight path?
interpretation: This verse contrasts a helpless, dependent individual who brings no benefit to anyone with a person who actively upholds justice and follows the right path, emphasizing that true worth lies in moral responsibility and righteous action rather than mere existence or dependency.

translation: And to Allah belongs the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. And the command of the Hour is not but as a glance of the eye or even nearer. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty over all that is unseen in the heavens and the earth, emphasizing His unparalleled power and control over the universe. The mention of the Hour (Day of Judgment) being as swift as the blink of an eye or even faster highlights the suddenness and inevitability of divine decrees, reinforcing the idea that Allah's will is instantaneous and beyond human comprehension, yet perfectly executed according to His wisdom.

translation: And Allah has brought you forth from the wombs of your mothers while you knew nothing, and He gave you hearing, vision, and intellect that perhaps you would be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine endowment of human beings with faculties of perception and reasoning, emphasizing that these intellectual and sensory capabilities are not merely for survival but are intended as means to recognize and acknowledge the blessings of Allah, fostering gratitude and submission to Him.

translation: Do they not see the birds controlled in the atmosphere of the sky? None holds them except Allah. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute power and control of Allah over all creation, even the flight of birds, which serves as a reminder of His sovereignty and the need for faith and reflection in His signs.

translation: And Allah has made for you from your homes a place of rest and made for you from the hides of livestock tents which you find light on your day of travel and your day of settlement. And from their wool, fur, and hair, He has made for you comforts and provisions for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and provision by emphasizing how He has designed various aspects of life to serve humanity's needs, ensuring comfort, utility, and adaptability in different circumstances, whether in settled living or during travel.

translation: And Allah has made for you, from what He has created, shades, and has made for you, from the mountains, shelters, and has made for you garments which protect you from the heat, and garments which protect you from your [enemy in] battle. Thus does He complete His favor upon you, so that you may submit [to Him].
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's meticulous care and provision for human well-being, both in physical and spiritual dimensions. The mention of shades, shelters, and protective garments symbolizes Allah's encompassing mercy and guidance, ensuring human comfort, security, and preparedness for life's challenges. The ultimate purpose of these blessings is to foster gratitude and submission to Allah, reinforcing the idea that all provisions are divine favors aimed at guiding humanity toward faith and reliance on Him.

translation: But if they turn away, then upon you is only the clear conveyance [of the message].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the responsibility of the messenger (in this context, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ) to deliver the message of Islam clearly and unambiguously, while acknowledging that the ultimate guidance or rejection lies with the recipients of the message. It underscores that the duty of the messenger is to convey the truth without coercion, and that the consequences of acceptance or rejection are not within their control.

translation: They recognize the favors of Allah; then they deny them, and most of them are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to acknowledge divine blessings yet still reject faith, often due to arrogance or ingratitude, which leads to disbelief despite clear evidence of God's favors.

translation: And [mention] the Day when We will bring from every nation a witness, and it will not be permitted for the disbelievers [to remain], nor will they be asked to apologize.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice on the Day of Judgment, where every community will have a witness—often understood as their own prophets or scriptures—testifying against their disbelief, leaving no room for excuses or apologies from those who rejected faith.

translation: And when those who wronged see the punishment, it will not be lightened for them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and irreversible nature of divine justice, emphasizing that the punishment for wrongdoing is final and inescapable, with no possibility of mitigation or delay.

translation: And when those who associated others with Allah see their 'partners,' they will say, 'Our Lord, these are our partners [whom] we used to invoke besides You.' But they will throw back at them the statement, 'Indeed, you are liars.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate rejection and falsehood of associating partners with Allah, as even those partners will disown their worshippers on the Day of Judgment, exposing the futility of idolatry and the inevitability of accountability for one's beliefs and actions.

translation: And they will submit to Allah that Day, and what they used to invent will depart from them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of submission to Allah on the Day of Judgment, where all falsehoods and deceptions that people clung to in this world will be exposed and rendered powerless, revealing the absolute truth of divine justice.

translation: For those who disbelieved and obstructed [others] from the path of Allah, We will increase them in punishment over the punishment [they were already destined for], because they were causing corruption.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of divine justice, where the punishment for disbelief and obstruction of truth is intensified not merely for disbelief itself, but for the active corruption and harm caused by such actions. It underscores that wrongdoing compounds accountability, and that divine retribution is proportional to the extent of mischief wrought in the world.

translation: And [mention] the Day when We will raise among every nation a witness over them from themselves. And We have brought you, [O Muhammad], as a witness over these [people]. And We have sent down to you the Book as clarification for all things and as guidance and mercy and good tidings for the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse underscores the universal accountability of all nations on the Day of Judgment, where each community will have a witness from among themselves to testify to their deeds. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is designated as a witness over his nation, highlighting his pivotal role in conveying the divine message. The revelation of the Qur'an is framed as a comprehensive guide, mercy, and glad tidings for Muslims, emphasizing its timeless relevance and transformative power in guiding humanity toward righteousness and salvation.

translation: Indeed, Allah commands justice, good conduct, and giving to relatives, and He forbids immorality, bad conduct, and oppression. He admonishes you so that you may take heed.
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundational moral and ethical principles in Islam, emphasizing that true faith must manifest in actions—justice, kindness, and generosity toward family—while actively rejecting all forms of corruption, injustice, and transgression. It underscores that divine guidance is not merely theoretical but a practical framework for a balanced and righteous life.

translation: And fulfill the covenant of Allah when you have taken it, and do not break [your] oaths after their confirmation while you have made Allah, over you, a witness. Indeed, Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the sanctity of commitments made in the name of Allah, urging believers to honor their promises and not to break them after affirming them, as Allah is a witness to all such pledges. It underscores the moral and religious duty to uphold one's word, reflecting the broader Qur'anic principle of trustworthiness and integrity in all dealings.

translation: And do not be like the woman who unravels her yarn, breaking it into pieces after it has been firmly spun, taking your oaths as a means of deceit among yourselves, so that one party may become superior to another. Allah only tests you with this, and on the Day of Resurrection, He will surely make clear to you what you used to differ about.
interpretation: This verse condemns hypocrisy and the misuse of oaths to deceive others for personal or factional gain, emphasizing that such behavior is a test from Allah to expose true intentions and will be judged accordingly on the Day of Resurrection.

translation: And if Allah had willed, He could have made you [of] one religion, but He lets astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. And you will surely be questioned about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine principle of free will within the bounds of Allah's will, emphasizing that guidance and misguidance are ultimately determined by Him, yet humans are still held accountable for their choices and actions.

translation: And do not use your oaths to deceive one another, lest your foot slip after it has been firm, and you taste evil for barring [people] from the way of Allah. And for you is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against using oaths insincerely or manipulatively to gain advantage over others, as such behavior undermines trust and harms both individuals and society. It emphasizes the gravity of obstructing people from the path of truth and righteousness, equating such actions with moral and spiritual corruption, and underscores the severe consequences of such deeds in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And do not exchange the covenant of Allah for a small price. Indeed, what is with Allah is better for you, if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse warns against prioritizing worldly gains or temporary benefits over the divine covenant and obedience to Allah, emphasizing that true and lasting good lies in fulfilling one's commitment to Allah rather than seeking fleeting material rewards.

translation: What is with you will perish, and what is with Allah will remain. And We will surely reward those who were patient with their best deeds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of worldly possessions and the eternal value of good deeds in the sight of Allah, emphasizing that true success lies in patience and righteous actions rewarded by Allah.

translation: Whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while he is a believer - We will surely cause him to live a good life, and We will surely reward them their reward [in Paradise] according to the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith and righteous deeds—regardless of gender—are the foundation for a blessed life in this world and the Hereafter, with divine justice ensuring that no good deed goes unrewarded.

translation: So when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge with Allah from Satan, the expelled [from His mercy].
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to seek divine protection from the influence of Satan before reciting the Qur'an, emphasizing the importance of spiritual purity and focus to fully benefit from its guidance.

translation: Indeed, he (Satan) has no authority over those who believe and place their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that their faith and reliance on Allah (SWT) protect them from the deceptions and influences of Satan, emphasizing the power of true faith and trust in divine providence.

translation: Indeed, his authority is only over those who take him as a ally and those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse clarifies the limited scope of Satan's influence, restricting it to those who willingly ally themselves with him or engage in shirk (associating partners with Allah). It emphasizes that true believers, who remain steadfast in their faith and avoid such associations, are beyond his reach.

translation: And when We substitute a verse in place of a verse - and Allah is most knowing of what He sends down - they say, "You, [O Muhammad], are but an inventor [of lies]." But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and resistance faced by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from those who rejected the divine origin of the Qur'an. It underscores the deeper truth that human beings often dismiss what they do not understand or refuse to accept, reflecting their own limitations rather than the validity of the message.

translation: Say, 'The Holy Spirit has brought it down from your Lord in truth, to strengthen those who believe, and as guidance and good tidings for the Muslims.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and purpose of the Qur'an's revelation, highlighting its role in fortifying the faith of believers, providing them with guidance, and offering glad tidings of success and salvation to those who submit to God.

translation: And We certainly know that they say, 'It is only a human being who teaches him.' The tongue of the one they refer to is foreign, while this Qur'an is [in] a clear Arabic language.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of the Quraysh who claimed the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was being taught by a foreigner, likely referring to a freed slave named Salman al-Farsi. The verse refutes this claim by highlighting the linguistic purity and eloquence of the Qur'an, which is in clear Arabic—a language the Prophet (peace be upon him) was born into and mastered, making such an accusation absurd.

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the signs of Allah - Allah will not guide them, and for them is a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle that guidance from Allah is contingent upon sincere belief in His signs (evidence of His existence, power, and truth). Those who reject these signs out of arrogance or willful denial close the door to divine guidance, and their rejection leads them to a state of spiritual blindness, for which they will face severe consequences in the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, those who invent falsehood about Allah are the ones who do not believe in His verses, and it is they who are the liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and spiritual consequences of disbelief, suggesting that the act of denying Allah's signs or falsely attributing lies to Him stems from a fundamental lack of faith, which in turn corrupts one's integrity and truthfulness.

translation: Whoever disbelieves in Allah after his belief—except for someone who is compelled while his heart is content with faith—but whoever opens his chest to disbelief, upon them is the wrath of Allah, and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between forced disbelief and genuine conviction, emphasizing that true faith is a matter of the heart, not external pressure, while warning against the dangers of willingly embracing disbelief after recognizing the truth.

translation: That is because they preferred the life of this world over the Hereafter, and Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual choice of prioritizing worldly desires over the eternal rewards of the Hereafter, which leads to a rejection of divine guidance due to the hardening of the heart against truth.

translation: It is those upon whose hearts, hearing, and sight Allah has set a seal. And it is they who are heedless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual hardening of those who persistently reject faith and truth, leading to divine sealing of their hearts, ears, and eyes, rendering them incapable of recognizing guidance, despite the signs around them.

translation: Indeed, it is certain that they in the Hereafter will be the losers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of loss for those who persist in disbelief or wrongdoing, emphasizing the irreversible consequences of their choices in the Hereafter.

translation: Then, indeed, your Lord, to those who emigrated after they had been afflicted and then strove [for Allah] and were patient - indeed, your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the profound mercy and forgiveness of Allah towards those who endure hardship, migrate for the sake of faith, and persist in their struggle and patience in the path of righteousness. It highlights that Allah's forgiveness and mercy are not merely conditional but are extended to those who demonstrate unwavering commitment and resilience in their faith, even after facing trials and tribulations.

translation: The Day every soul will come to plead for itself, and every soul will be fully compensated for what it did. And they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where every individual will be held accountable for their deeds without any injustice or favoritism, emphasizing the inevitability of divine recompense.

translation: And Allah presents an example: a town that was safe and secure, its livelihood coming to it in abundance from every place, but it denied the favors of Allah. So Allah made it taste the envelopment of hunger and fear for what they had been doing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against ingratitude and complacency, illustrating how divine blessings—security, abundance, and stability—can be revoked when a people fail to recognize and acknowledge God's favors, instead choosing disbelief and transgression.

translation: And certainly, there came to them a Messenger from among themselves, but they denied him, so the punishment seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance brought by a prophet from their own people, emphasizing that divine punishment is a just response to persistent injustice and denial of truth.

translation: So eat of what Allah has provided for you [which is] lawful and good and be grateful for the favor of Allah if it is [indeed] Him that you worship.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of recognizing the blessings of Allah by consuming what is lawful and wholesome, and expressing gratitude through worship, highlighting that true servitude to Allah involves both adherence to His law and appreciation of His provisions.

translation: He has only forbidden to you dead animals, blood, the flesh of swine, and that which has been dedicated to other than Allah. But whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit], then indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the permissibility of consuming otherwise prohibited foods under dire necessity, emphasizing that Allah's mercy and forgiveness extend even in situations of extreme hardship, provided the person is not acting out of desire or exceeding the limits of necessity.

translation: And do not say about what your tongues falsely describe, 'This is lawful,' and 'This is unlawful,' to invent a lie about Allah. Indeed, those who invent a lie about Allah will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse condemns the act of attributing false rulings to Allah regarding what is lawful or unlawful without divine authority, emphasizing that such deception will lead to failure in the Hereafter.

translation: A brief enjoyment; but they will have a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient and ultimately deceptive nature of worldly pleasures, warning that those who prioritize them over spiritual accountability will face severe and lasting consequences.

translation: And to those who are Jews, We have forbidden what We related to you before. And We did not wrong them, but they were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and personal accountability, emphasizing that wrongdoing stems from one's own actions rather than external oppression, and that divine prohibitions are not arbitrary but rooted in justice and wisdom.

translation: But indeed, your Lord - to those who do wrong in ignorance and then repent after that and reform, indeed, your Lord is after that Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy of Allah towards those who sincerely repent from their wrongdoings, even if they were committed out of ignorance, and then actively strive to rectify their actions. It underscores that repentance and reformation are pathways to divine forgiveness, highlighting Allah’s compassion and willingness to pardon those who turn to Him with genuine remorse.

translation: Indeed, Abraham was a [comprehensive] leader, devoted to Allah, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute monotheism and unwavering devotion of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) to Allah, emphasizing his role as a model of righteousness and his rejection of idolatry or associating partners with Allah.

translation: Grateful for His favors. He chose him and guided him to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and being thankful for God's blessings, as well as acknowledging His guidance and the selection of individuals for a righteous path.

translation: And We gave him in this world goodness, and indeed, in the Hereafter he is among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine reward in both this life and the Hereafter for those who remain steadfast in faith and righteousness, emphasizing that true success encompasses both worldly blessings and eternal salvation.

translation: Then We inspired you, [O Muhammad], to follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth; and He was not of those who associate with Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine command to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to adhere to the pure monotheistic tradition of Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham), free from any form of idolatry or associationism, emphasizing the unbroken chain of prophetic guidance that rejects all forms of shirk (associating partners with Allah).

translation: Indeed, the Sabbath was only appointed for those who differed over it. And indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse underscores that divine rulings, such as the Sabbath, are not arbitrary but are tied to the context and circumstances of the people they were given to, highlighting God's justice in addressing disputes among them.

translation: Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in a way that is best. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the [rightly] guided.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of propagating faith with gentleness, wisdom, and patience, avoiding harshness or coercion. It encourages using the most effective and respectful methods of dialogue, recognizing that true guidance comes from Allah alone, who alone knows the hearts of people.

translation: And if you punish [an enemy, O believers], punish with an amount equivalent to the wrong that has been done to you. But if you are patient, it is certainly better for the patient.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of proportional justice in retaliation while highlighting the virtue of patience and forbearance as a higher moral choice, rewarding the patient with divine favor and spiritual strength.

translation: And be patient, for indeed, your patience is not but through Allah. And do not grieve over them, nor be distressed by what they plot.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of relying solely on Allah for strength and patience in the face of adversity, reminding the believer that true patience is only possible with Allah's help. It also instructs the believer not to be overwhelmed by grief for those who reject the truth or by the harm caused by their plots, as ultimate justice and victory belong to Allah.

translation: Indeed, Allah is with those who fear Him [with reverence] and those who are doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah's support, guidance, and closeness are granted to those who cultivate piety (taqwa) and actively engage in righteous deeds, highlighting the interconnectedness of faith and righteous action in attaining divine proximity.

translation: Glory to He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa, whose surroundings We have blessed, to show him of Our signs. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine power and majesty of Allah, emphasizing His ability to transcend the laws of nature and time, as evidenced by the miraculous Night Journey (Isra) and Ascension (Mi'raj) of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It also highlights the sanctity of both the Masjid al-Haram in Mecca and the Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem, framing them as blessed places chosen by Allah for profound spiritual significance. The verse serves as a reminder of Allah's omniscience and omnipotence, reinforcing the believer's trust in His signs and wisdom.

translation: And We gave Moses the Scripture and made it a guidance for the Children of Israel, [commanding them], 'Take not other than Me as a guardian or helper.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the exclusive right of Allah to be the sole source of guidance and protection, rejecting any form of association or reliance on intermediaries or false deities for divine support or direction.

translation: A posterity of those We carried with Noah. Indeed, he was a grateful servant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity of divine guidance and the importance of gratitude to Allah, as exemplified by Prophet Noah (peace be upon him), whose righteousness and thankfulness earned him and his descendants divine favor and protection.

translation: And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture: 'You will surely cause corruption on the earth twice, and you will surely reach [a degree of] great transgression.'
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to the Children of Israel about their recurring tendencies toward moral corruption and arrogance, despite their divine guidance. It highlights the cyclical nature of their deviations, suggesting that their actions will escalate to a level of severe transgression, warranting divine intervention or consequences.

translation: So when the promise of the first of them came, We sent against you servants of Ours possessing great might, and they probed throughout the dwellings, and it was a promise fulfilled.
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability of divine retribution when a people persist in their transgressions, as it reflects God's justice in fulfilling His warnings through historical events, emphasizing that no promise from Allah is left unfulfilled.

translation: Then We turned you back to them, and We reinforced you with wealth and sons and made you more numerous in manpower.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's favor upon the believers by granting them material and numerical strength after a setback, emphasizing that true success lies in divine support rather than mere numerical or material superiority.

translation: If you do good, you do good for yourselves; and if you do evil, it is for them (your souls). Then when the promise of the Hereafter comes, (it will be) to disgrace your faces and to enter the mosque as they entered it the first time, and to destroy what they took over with total destruction.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of personal accountability in both good and evil deeds, emphasizing that righteous actions benefit the doer while wrongdoing harms the soul. The latter part warns of a future reckoning where wrongdoers will face humiliation and destruction, symbolizing divine justice and the consequences of defiance against God's commands.

translation: Perhaps your Lord will have mercy upon you. But if you return [to sin], We will return [to punishment]. And We have made Hell, for the disbelievers, a prison.
interpretation: This verse underscores the balance between divine mercy and justice, emphasizing that Allah’s mercy is always available to those who repent and seek forgiveness, but it is not unconditional. It serves as a reminder that while Allah is Most Merciful, He is also Just, and those who persist in disbelief or sin without repentance will face the consequences of their actions.

translation: Indeed, this Qur'an guides to that which is most upright and gives good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Qur'an's role as a divine guide, leading humanity to the most righteous path, while also emphasizing the importance of faith and righteous actions, promising immense reward for believers who embody these virtues.

translation: And for those who do not believe in the Hereafter, We have prepared a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences awaiting those who reject the concept of the Hereafter, emphasizing that their disbelief will be met with divine retribution in the form of a painful punishment, underscoring the gravity of denying the accountability and justice of the afterlife.

translation: And man prays for evil as he prays for good, and man is ever hasty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the flawed nature of human beings, who often act impulsively and fail to consider the consequences of their actions, even when seeking good or evil.

translation: And We have made the night and the day as two signs. Then We have made the sign of the night dark and made the sign of the day enlightening, that you may seek bounty from your Lord and may know the number of years and the account. And everything We have detailed in a clear manner.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in the alternation of night and day, which serves as signs for human beings to recognize the passage of time, seek sustenance, and reflect on the order of creation, ultimately guiding them to acknowledge the power and knowledge of their Lord.

translation: And every soul We have bound to its fate in its neck; and on the Day of Resurrection, We will bring forth for it a record which it will find spread open.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inescapable accountability of every individual for their deeds, as each person's actions are recorded meticulously and presented openly on the Day of Judgment, leaving no room for denial or escape from divine justice.

translation: Read your record. Sufficient is your own self this Day as an accountant against you.
interpretation: This verse underscores the individual accountability of every person on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that each soul will be held responsible for its own deeds without the intercession of others, highlighting the absolute justice and personal responsibility inherent in divine judgment.

translation: Whoever is guided is only guided for [the benefit of] his soul. And whoever goes astray only goes astray to its detriment. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And We had not been going to punish [any people] until We sent a messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability in the Hereafter, where each individual is responsible for their own deeds and will face the consequences thereof. It also underscores the justice and mercy of Allah in sending messengers to guide humanity, providing them with clear guidance before any punishment is decreed.

translation: And when We intend to destroy a city, We command its affluent ones, but they defy therein, so the decree against it becomes due, and We destroy it with complete destruction.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of divine justice, where God's punishment is not arbitrary but follows a pattern of warning and accountability; it is a reminder that societal destruction is often preceded by moral corruption and oppression by the powerful, and that divine retribution is a response to persistent injustice rather than an indiscriminate act.

translation: And how many generations We have destroyed after Noah! And sufficient is your Lord concerning the sins of His servants as All-Aware, All-Seer.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine retribution for persistent wrongdoing, emphasizing Allah's comprehensive knowledge of human sins and His decisive power to punish or preserve as He wills.

translation: Whoever desires the immediate [transitory enjoyment of this world], We hasten for him from it what We will to whom We intend. Then We make for him Hell, which he will [enter to] burn, censured and banished.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against the pursuit of worldly desires at the expense of spiritual well-being, emphasizing that Allah's justice ensures that those who prioritize transient gains without regard for the Hereafter will face severe consequences, including humiliation and eternal punishment in Hell.

translation: But whoever desires the Hereafter and exerts the effort due to it while he is a believer - it is those whose effort is ever appreciated [by Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere intention and diligent effort in seeking the Hereafter, highlighting that such efforts are not only recognized but also rewarded by Allah when accompanied by true faith.

translation: Nay, We extend provision for these and for those from the bounty of your Lord. And never has the bounty of your Lord been restricted.
interpretation: This verse underscores the boundless generosity of Allah’s provision, which encompasses all—both believers and non-believers—without restriction, emphasizing that divine favor is not limited by human merit or disbelief.

translation: See how We have favored some of them over others. But the Hereafter is greater in degrees and greater in favor.
interpretation: This verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly distinctions and privileges, emphasizing that the true and lasting superiority lies in the Hereafter, where divine justice and merit will be fully realized.

translation: Do not set up with Allah any other god, or you will sit down reproached and forsaken.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and warns against associating partners with Him, which is a grave sin in Islam. It highlights the consequences of shirk (idolatry) in this world—being despised and abandoned by both Allah and people—and in the Hereafter, severe punishment. The verse serves as a reminder of the importance of pure monotheism and the futility of relying on anything or anyone besides Allah.

translation: And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to parents. Whether one or both of them attain old age in your life, say not to them a word of contempt, nor repel them, but address them in terms of honor.
interpretation: This verse establishes the fundamental principle of monotheism while simultaneously emphasizing the paramount duty of kindness and respect toward parents, even when their presence becomes burdensome due to old age or infirmity. It underscores the balance between spiritual devotion and moral conduct, teaching that true servitude to God is reflected in compassionate treatment of one's parents, regardless of their behavior or the personal sacrifices required.

translation: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, 'My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small.'
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to show humility, respect, and kindness towards their parents, especially in their old age, as a form of gratitude for their upbringing and sacrifices. It emphasizes the duty of children to pray for their parents' mercy and forgiveness, drawing a parallel between the parents' nurturing in childhood and the child's obligation to care for them in return.

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of what is within yourselves. If you should be righteous [in intention], then indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful to those who return [to Him].
interpretation: This verse highlights the omniscience of Allah regarding the hidden intentions and states of the heart, emphasizing that true righteousness stems from sincere intention rather than outward appearance. It reassures believers that Allah’s forgiveness and mercy are readily available to those who repent and turn back to Him with genuine remorse and a commitment to rectify their actions.

translation: And give the relative his right, and the needy, and the wayfarer. And do not spend wastefully.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fulfilling one's obligations towards family, the poor, and travelers, while also warning against extravagance and wastefulness in spending, promoting a balanced approach to charity and financial responsibility.

translation: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and ever has Satan been to his Lord ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the moral and spiritual gravity of extravagance and wastefulness, equating such behavior with the actions of the devils (Shayatin), who are inherently rebellious and ungrateful to Allah. It serves as a stark warning against excessive indulgence in worldly pleasures or resources, emphasizing that such conduct not only reflects a lack of gratitude to Allah but also aligns one's character with the corrupt and destructive nature of Satan.

translation: But if you turn away from them seeking mercy from your Lord which you expect, then speak to them a gentle word.
interpretation: This verse advises believers to respond with kindness and gentleness when they are unable to fulfill a request or obligation, especially when motivated by the hope of divine reward or mercy, rather than harshness or rejection.

translation: And do not keep your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it completely, so you become blameworthy and regretful.
interpretation: This verse advises moderation in spending and charity, warning against both extreme miserliness and excessive generosity that could lead to financial ruin or dependency on others.

translation: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed, He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute sovereignty over sustenance and provision, emphasizing that He grants or withholds according to His wisdom and knowledge of His servants' needs and circumstances, without injustice or oversight.

translation: And do not kill your children for fear of poverty. We provide for them and for you. Indeed, their killing is ever a great sin.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sanctity of life and prohibits the killing of children, even in times of hardship, as it is a grave sin. It reassures that sustenance is guaranteed by Allah, and thus, fear of poverty should not lead to such an act, emphasizing trust in divine provision and the moral imperative to protect the innocent.

translation: And do not approach unlawful sexual intercourse. Indeed, it is an immorality and is evil as a way.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of engaging in unlawful sexual relations, not only as an act of immorality but also as a path that leads to broader moral and societal corruption, emphasizing the importance of maintaining chastity and upholding ethical boundaries in human relationships.

translation: And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right. And whoever is killed unjustly - We have given his heir authority, so let him not exceed limits in [the matter of] taking life. Indeed, he has been supported [by the law].
interpretation: This verse establishes the sanctity of human life and prohibits murder without just cause, emphasizing that even in cases of just retribution, the right of the heir must be balanced with divine justice, preventing excessive or unjust retaliation.

translation: And do not approach the property of an orphan except in the best manner until he reaches his maturity. And fulfill the covenant, for the covenant will be questioned about.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ethical treatment of orphans' wealth, mandating that it be managed or used only in ways that are beneficial to them, not exploited or misused. It also underscores the importance of fulfilling promises and commitments, as they will be held to account in the Hereafter, reflecting the Qur'an's emphasis on justice, trustworthiness, and responsibility in all dealings.

translation: And give full measure when you measure out, and weigh with a true balance. That is better and fairer in conclusion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of fairness and honesty in trade and transactions, urging believers to uphold justice in all dealings, as it leads to the best and most equitable outcomes.

translation: And do not pursue that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking knowledge and acting upon verified information rather than indulging in conjecture or unfounded assumptions. It warns against blindly following hearsay or unverified claims, as every individual will be held accountable for their actions, including what they choose to believe or spread.

translation: And do not walk upon the earth arrogantly, for you will never tear the earth [apart] and you will never reach the mountains in height.
interpretation: This verse warns against arrogance and excessive pride in one's abilities or status, reminding humans of their limitations and the transient nature of worldly power.

translation: All of that—its evil is hated by your Lord.
interpretation: This verse underscores the moral and spiritual gravity of sin and disobedience in the sight of Allah, emphasizing that such actions are not merely disliked but deeply abhorrent to Him, reflecting His absolute justice and purity.

translation: This is [part] of what your Lord has revealed to you of wisdom. And do not set up with Allah another god, or you will be thrown into Hell, blamed and rejected.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheism and warns against associating partners with Allah, as it leads to severe punishment in the Hereafter, highlighting the gravity of shirk (idolatry) in Islam.

translation: Has your Lord favored you [with sons] and taken from the angels females? Indeed, you say a grave saying.
interpretation: This verse challenges the pre-Islamic Arabian practice of preferring male children over females, as well as the erroneous belief that angels, being servants of God, could be female—a notion that reflects a distorted understanding of divine unity and the nature of angels.

translation: And We have certainly diversified in this Qur'an for them that they may be reminded, but it increases them only in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the paradoxical effect of the Qur'an on different people: while it is a source of guidance and remembrance for those who are receptive, it can also deepen the aversion and rejection of those whose hearts are hardened or who are predisposed to disbelief.

translation: Say, 'If there were with Him [other] gods, as they say, then they would have sought a way to [the Lord of] the Throne.'
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheistic belief in multiple deities by highlighting the logical inconsistency of such a claim. If there were multiple gods, they would have to coordinate and compete for power, leading to chaos rather than harmony in the universe. The verse implies that the existence of a single, supreme God is the only coherent explanation for the order and unity observed in creation.

translation: Exalted and far above what they say is a great transcendence.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute purity and majesty of Allah, declaring Him free from any falsehood or imperfection attributed to Him by those who deny His oneness or distort His attributes.

translation: The seven heavens and the earth and all that is within them glorify Him. There is not a single thing but glorifies Him with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse underscores the universal and constant glorification of Allah by all creation, even if humans are unable to comprehend or perceive it. It highlights Allah's boundless mercy and patience, as He continues to sustain and forgive despite the limited understanding of His creatures.

translation: And when you [O Muhammad] recite the Qur'an, We place between you and those who do not believe in the Hereafter a concealed barrier.
interpretation: This verse highlights the protective and isolating nature of divine revelation, suggesting that the Qur'an itself acts as a spiritual and moral barrier between the believer and the disbeliever, preventing the latter from fully comprehending or accepting its truths due to their rejection of the Hereafter.

translation: And We have placed over their hearts coverings, lest they understand it, and in their ears deafness. And when you mention your Lord alone in the Qur'an, they turn their backs in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and psychological barriers that prevent people from accepting the truth of the Qur'an. The 'coverings' and 'deafness' symbolize the hardening of hearts and the refusal to listen, which arise from arrogance, prejudice, or deep-seated disbelief. The turning away in aversion when the Qur'an emphasizes the oneness of Allah (Tawheed) reflects a rejection of divine truth, rooted in a preference for worldly desires or misguided ideologies over submission to Allah.

translation: We know best what they listen for, as they listen to you [O Prophet], and [We know] when they are in private conversation, when the wrongdoers say, 'You follow only a man bewitched.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's deep awareness of the hidden intentions and secret discussions of the disbelievers, even as they plot against the Prophet (peace be upon him) in private. The phrase 'a man bewitched' reflects their denial of the divine origin of the Qur'an, attributing it to sorcery or madness, which underscores their refusal to accept the truth despite its clarity.

translation: Have you not considered how they strike comparisons for you [O Muhammad], so they go astray and cannot find a way?
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of those who attempt to discredit the truth by drawing false analogies or comparisons, emphasizing that their misguidance leaves them incapable of finding the right path or truth.

translation: And they say, 'When we are bones and crumbled remains, will we really be resurrected as a new creation?''
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and denial of the disbelievers who question the possibility of resurrection after their bodies have decomposed, highlighting their stubbornness in rejecting the truth despite clear signs of Allah's power.

translation: Say, 'Be you stones or iron'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and will of Allah, emphasizing that human resistance or defiance is ultimately futile in the face of divine decree, as even the most unyielding of materials—stones or iron—would submit to His command.

translation: Or [do they think that] they will be created anew in a manner different from their first creation? Yet they are in confusion about the possibility of their rebirth. Say, "He who created you the first time will bring you back." Then they will nod their heads at you and say, "When will that be?" Say, "It may well be near."
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who deny resurrection after death, questioning how they could be recreated. The response emphasizes Allah's absolute power to recreate what He initially created, reassuring that the timing of resurrection is known only to Him but will certainly occur, possibly sooner than they expect.

translation: The Day when He will call you and you will respond with His praise, and you will think that you had remained [in the world] but a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the brevity of worldly life compared to the eternal Hereafter, emphasizing that on the Day of Judgment, people will realize how fleeting their time in this world was, despite its perceived length during their earthly existence.

translation: And tell My servants to say that which is best. Indeed, Satan sows discord among them. Indeed, Satan is ever, to mankind, a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of using kind and respectful language, even in disagreements, as harsh words can exacerbate conflicts and play into the hands of Satan, who seeks to sow discord and division among people.

translation: Your Lord is most knowing of you. If He wills, He will have mercy upon you; or if He wills, He will punish you. And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], over them as a manager.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over human fate, emphasizing that His mercy or punishment is entirely within His discretion, not subject to human control or intercession. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reminded that his role is not to enforce divine justice or coerce belief but to convey the message, leaving the response and consequences to Allah alone.

translation: And your Lord knows best whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others, and We gave David the book [of Psalms].
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's perfect knowledge of all creation, emphasizing that He is fully aware of every being in the heavens and the earth. The second part underscores the divine wisdom in elevating some prophets above others in rank and granting them specific scriptures, such as the Psalms given to Prophet David, to fulfill His greater plan for guidance and mercy.

translation: Say, 'Call upon those you claim [to be gods] besides Him, so they will never be able to remove harm from you or avert it.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute incapacity of any entity other than Allah to influence or alter the decrees of the universe, emphasizing that no intercessor or deity possesses the power to change one's fate or alleviate suffering without Allah's permission, thereby negating any form of shirk (associating partners with Allah).

translation: It is those who invoke Allah, seeking the means [of nearness] to their Lord, [asking] which of them are nearest, and hope for His mercy and fear His punishment. Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is ever feared.
interpretation: This verse highlights the balanced approach of true believers in their relationship with Allah, combining hope in His mercy with fear of His punishment, while also emphasizing the importance of seeking closeness to Him through righteous actions and devotion.

translation: And there is no city but that We will destroy it before the Day of Resurrection or punish it with a severe punishment. That has ever been in the Register inscribed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over life and death, emphasizing that no community is exempt from divine accountability. It conveys that divine punishment or destruction is not arbitrary but follows a predetermined decree ('in the Book'), reflecting Allah's justice and the inevitability of consequences for persistent disbelief or oppression.

translation: And We did not prevent the sending of signs except that the former peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a clear sign, but they wronged her. And We send not the signs except as a deterrent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the historical pattern where divine signs (or miracles) were sent to previous nations, but they were rejected due to their disbelief. The example of the she-camel given to the Thamud people is cited as a clear sign, yet they transgressed against it, leading to their destruction. The verse underscores that signs are sent not merely as proofs but as warnings and deterrents to encourage reflection and obedience, with the ultimate purpose of guiding humanity toward righteousness.

translation: And [remember] when We said to you, 'Indeed, your Lord has encompassed the people.' And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people, and [also] the accursed tree in the Qur'an. And We warn them, but it only increases them in great transgression.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose behind certain divine tests and warnings in the Qur'an, such as the vision granted to the Prophet (peace be upon him) and the mention of the accursed tree. These are not meant to mislead but to serve as trials to distinguish between those who submit to Allah's will and those who persist in arrogance and defiance, thereby deepening their rebellion.

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate before Adam'; so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He said, 'Should I prostrate before one You created from clay?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of arrogance and disobedience to divine command. Iblees' refusal to prostrate before Adam, despite the clear order, stems from his pride in his creation from fire, contrasting Adam's creation from clay, and reflects the destructive nature of rejecting God's will due to personal vanity.

translation: Have you seen this one whom You have honored above me? If You delay me until the Day of Resurrection, I will surely destroy his descendants, except for a few.
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and envy of Iblis (Satan) towards Adam (peace be upon him) and his descendants, as he vows to mislead and corrupt them, except for those whom Allah protects by His grace. It highlights the ongoing struggle between truth and falsehood, and the importance of seeking Allah's refuge from the whispers of Satan.

translation: He said, 'Go forth; then whoever follows you among them - indeed, Hell will be the recompense of you all, an ample recompense.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and uncompromising nature of divine justice, where following misguidance leads to a severe and just punishment, emphasizing that no one will escape accountability for their choices.

translation: And incite [to senselessness] whoever you can among them with your voice and mobilize against them your cavalry and infantry and become a partner in their wealth and children and promise them.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believers to be vigilant against the deceptive tactics of Satan, who seeks to mislead people through false promises, material temptations, and the allure of wealth and progeny. It emphasizes the importance of recognizing Satan's whisperings and not being swayed by his empty enticements, as they lead only to ruin and deception.

translation: Indeed, My servants—you have no authority over them. And sufficient is your Lord as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that no external force, including Satan or his allies, can truly control or misguide them without their own consent, as ultimate authority and guardianship rest solely with Allah, who is the perfect Protector and Manager of all affairs.

translation: Your Lord is He Who drives the ships for you through the sea, that you may seek of His Bounty. Indeed, He is Ever Merciful to you.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's continuous mercy and provision for humanity, demonstrating His control over natural forces to facilitate human sustenance and progress, while emphasizing the importance of seeking His bounty through lawful means.

translation: And when harm touches you at sea, those you invoke are lost except Him. But when He delivers you to the shore, you turn away. And ever is man ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn to Allah sincerely only in times of distress and forget Him when comfort and safety are restored, reflecting a lack of consistent gratitude and recognition of divine power.

translation: Do you feel secure that He will not cause the side of the land to swallow you up, or send against you a storm of stones, then you would find no guardian for yourselves?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against arrogance and complacency in the face of divine power, reminding humanity of its vulnerability and the need for humility and reliance on Allah, rather than feeling secure in one's own strength or resources.

translation: Or do you feel secure that He will not send you back into it [the sea] another time and send upon you a storm of wind, and drown you for what you have disbelieved? Then you would not find for yourselves against Us any helper.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against arrogance and ingratitude toward Allah’s signs and blessings, emphasizing that divine justice may manifest in unexpected ways if humanity persists in disbelief or defiance of moral and spiritual boundaries.

translation: And We have certainly honored the Children of Adam and carried them on the land and sea and provided for them of the good things and preferred them over much of what We have created, with [definite] preference.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent dignity and honor bestowed upon humanity by Allah, elevating them above many other creations. It underscores the responsibility that comes with this honor, including the stewardship of the earth and its resources, as well as the moral and ethical obligations to use these blessings in a manner pleasing to Allah.

translation: The Day We will call forth every people with their record [of deeds]; then whoever is given his record in his right hand - those will read their records, and they will not be wronged, [even] as much as a thread [inside a date seed].
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where every individual will be held accountable for their deeds with no injustice whatsoever, no matter how small the deed may be.

translation: And whoever is blind in this [life], will be blind in the Hereafter, and more astray in [his] way.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of spiritual blindness in this life, which leads to greater deviation and loss in the Hereafter, emphasizing the importance of seeking guidance and awareness of divine truth.

translation: And indeed, they were about to tempt you away from what We revealed to you, to fabricate something else against Us, and then they would have taken you as a close friend.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense opposition faced by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from those who sought to distort his message or lure him away from his divine mission, revealing the depth of their enmity and the lengths they would go to undermine his prophethood.

translation: And if it were not that We had firmly established you [O Muhammad], you were about to incline towards them a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine protection granted to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) from being swayed by the desires or pressures of others, even in moments of personal weakness, underscoring the importance of steadfastness in faith and the grace of Allah's support in preserving the integrity of His message.

translation: Then We would have made you taste double [punishment] in life and double [after] death. Then you would not find for yourself against Us any helper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and unchallengeable authority of Allah in meting out justice, emphasizing that no one can escape His punishment or find protection against His decree, regardless of their status or power in this life or the Hereafter.

translation: And [remember, O Muhammad] when they were about to drive you out of the land [of Makkah] so that they might expel you therefrom; but [in fact,] they will not remain after you except for a little while.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that the efforts of his opponents to expel him from Makkah would ultimately fail, and their power would be short-lived. It underscores the transient nature of worldly opposition to divine missions and the eventual triumph of truth.

translation: The tradition of those We sent before you from among Our messengers; and you will not find in Our tradition any alteration.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers that the divine method of dealing with nations—through sending messengers and testing people with trials—is consistent throughout history and will not change. It underscores the certainty of Allah’s decrees and the inevitability of His established patterns in guiding or punishing nations based on their response to guidance.

translation: Establish prayer from the decline of the sun to the darkness of the night, and [also] the Qur'an of dawn. Indeed, the recitation of dawn is ever witnessed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of regular and timely prayer, highlighting the dawn prayer (Fajr) as particularly significant due to its witnessing by angels, underscoring its spiritual weight and the need for devotion and attentiveness in its observance.

translation: And during the night, stand (in prayer) for it is a voluntary act for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a station of praise and glory.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the spiritual and personal benefits of voluntary night prayers (Tahajjud), suggesting that such devotion can elevate one's status in the sight of Allah, granting them a station of honor and praise, which may include intercession or a special closeness to Allah.

translation: And say, 'My Lord, enable me to enter where I must enter with truth, and enable me to exit where I must exit with truth, and grant me from Yourself a supporting authority.'
interpretation: This supplication reflects a plea for divine guidance and support in all matters of life, seeking truthfulness in actions and decisions, and requesting strength and authority from Allah to uphold justice and righteousness.

translation: And say, 'The truth has come, and falsehood has perished. Indeed, falsehood is [by nature] bound to perish.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of truth prevailing over falsehood, emphasizing that falsehood, by its very nature, is transient and will ultimately be eradicated, while truth is eternal and unassailable.

translation: And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and mercy for the believers, but it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss.
interpretation: This verse underscores the dual nature of the Qur'an's impact: it serves as a source of spiritual healing and divine mercy for those who believe and approach it with sincerity and faith, while for those who persist in injustice and reject its guidance, it only deepens their misguidance and ultimate loss in the Hereafter.

translation: And when We bestow favor upon man, he turns away and distances himself; and when evil touches him, he is despairing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural human tendency to become distant from Allah and ungrateful when blessed with prosperity, while succumbing to despair during hardship, reflecting a lack of steadfastness and trust in divine wisdom.

translation: Say, 'Every one acts in accordance with his own disposition; your Lord knows best who is best guided on the path.'
