interpretation: This verse emphasizes the oneness of God (Tawhid) and calls all people to worship Allah alone, rejecting any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him, as the path to true guidance and salvation.

translation: But the factions differed among themselves. So woe to those who disbelieved from the [coming] punishment of a tremendous Day.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the consequences of disbelief, highlighting that even in the face of clear signs, those who reject the truth will face severe punishment, emphasizing the gravity of their denial and the certainty of accountability.

translation: They will come to Us with their hearing, their sight, and their skins testifying against them about what they used to do. But the wrongdoers today are in clear error.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of accountability in the Hereafter, where every faculty of the wrongdoers—even their own bodies—will bear witness against them, highlighting the inescapable nature of divine justice and the futility of their denial.

translation: And warn them of the Day of Regret, when the matter will be decided, while they are in heedlessness and they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of heeding warnings about the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that those who neglect their duties and live in disbelief will face regret when it is too late to change their fate.

translation: Indeed, it is We who will inherit the earth and whoever is on it, and to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's ultimate ownership and control over all of creation, reminding humanity of their temporary existence and the certainty of their return to Him for judgment.

translation: And mention in the Book, Abraham. Indeed, he was a devoted friend [to Allah], a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique status of Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) as a beloved friend of Allah, emphasizing his unwavering devotion and close relationship with the Divine, which serves as a model for believers in their own spiritual journey.

translation: When he said to his father, 'O my father, why do you worship that which does not hear, nor see, nor avail you anything?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of worshipping only that which has true power and ability, contrasting the futility of idol worship with the omnipotence of Allah, who alone possesses the attributes of hearing, seeing, and providing benefit.

translation: O my father, indeed I have come to me knowledge which did not come to you, so follow me; I will guide you to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse reflects the tension between personal conviction and familial duty, highlighting the challenge of conveying truth to those who may not initially accept it, even when motivated by sincere guidance.

translation: O my father, do not worship Satan. Indeed, Satan has ever been, to the Most Merciful, disobedient.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility and danger of following Satan, whose inherent disobedience to Allah renders him unworthy of worship. It serves as a warning to prioritize devotion to Allah alone, as Satan’s rebellion against divine authority makes him a flawed and unreliable guide.

translation: O my father, indeed I fear that a punishment from the Most Merciful will afflict you, so you will become a companion of Satan.
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep concern and love of a son for his father, warning him against the consequences of associating with falsehood or disbelief, which would lead him to follow Satan's path.

translation: He said, 'Are you [truly] disavowing my gods, O Abraham? If you do not desist, I will surely stone you. So leave me for a [long] time.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between Abraham (peace be upon him) and his people, particularly the idolatrous rejection of his monotheistic message. The speaker's threat reflects the arrogance and hostility of those who cling to false deities, while the command to 'leave me' underscores Abraham's patience and wisdom in disengaging from futile arguments, trusting in divine justice rather than force.

translation: Peace be upon you. I will ask my Lord to forgive you; indeed, He has ever been gracious to me.
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) supplication for forgiveness on behalf of others, demonstrating his humility and reliance on Allah's mercy, while also acknowledging Allah's favor and grace upon him.

translation: And I will leave you and whatever you invoke besides Allah, and I will invoke my Lord. Perhaps I will not be among the wretched in invoking my Lord.
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) unwavering commitment to monotheism and his rejection of idolatry, even at the risk of personal hardship. It demonstrates his patience, trust in Allah, and determination to follow the truth, even if it leads to isolation or difficulty.

translation: So when he (Ibrahim) had separated himself from them and what they worshipped besides Allah, We granted him Ishaq and Yaqub, and each We made a Prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincere devotion to Allah alone, demonstrating that true faith requires complete detachment from false deities and worldly distractions. It also underscores Allah's favor in rewarding such devotion with blessings—here, the birth of Ishaq (Isaac) and Yaqub (Jacob)—and elevating individuals to the rank of Prophethood, signifying a spiritual legacy that transcends generations.

translation: And We granted them out of Our mercy, and We made for them a renowned and upright reputation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor and mercy bestowed upon certain individuals, elevating their status and granting them lasting honor and praise in the eyes of others.

translation: And mention in the Book, Moses. Indeed, he was chosen, and he was a messenger, a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique status of Moses (peace be upon him) as a chosen servant of Allah, distinguished by his unwavering devotion and direct communication with the Divine. His roles as a messenger and prophet underscore his pivotal mission to guide his people and convey Allah's commands, serving as a model of righteousness and submission to Allah's will.

translation: And We called him from the right side of the mount, and We drew him near in communion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intimate and direct communication between Allah and His chosen servant, emphasizing the exclusivity and honor of the divine dialogue, where proximity signifies a special status and favor.

translation: And We granted him out of Our mercy his brother Aaron, a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor and mercy bestowed upon Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) by appointing his brother Aaron (peace be upon him) as a prophet to support him in his mission, demonstrating that Allah's mercy often manifests through familial bonds and practical assistance in fulfilling one's duties.

translation: And mention in the Book, Ishmael. Indeed, he was true to his promise, and he was a messenger [and] a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of trustworthiness and integrity, emphasizing that Ishmael (peace be upon him) was steadfast in fulfilling his promises, which is a commendable trait for all believers to emulate in their dealings with others.

translation: And he used to enjoin upon his family prayer and charity, and he was pleasing to his Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of establishing consistent acts of worship and righteousness, not only for oneself but also for one's family, as a means of earning divine pleasure and guidance.

translation: And mention in the Book, Idrees. Indeed, he was a man of truth and a prophet.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remembering and honoring the righteous servants of Allah, even if they are not as widely known as other prophets, emphasizing that sincerity and truthfulness in faith are what truly matter.

translation: And We raised him to a high station.
interpretation: This verse refers to the exaltation and elevation of the Prophet Idris (Enoch) or the Prophet Jesus (Isa) in spiritual rank and status by Allah, signifying their closeness to Him and their elevated position in the sight of Allah.

translation: These are the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from the prophets of the descendants of Adam, and of those We carried [in the ship] with Noah, and from the descendants of Abraham and Israel, and from those whom We guided and chose. When the verses of the Most Merciful were recited to them, they fell down in prostration and wept.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound humility and emotional response of the righteous servants of Allah when they encounter divine guidance. It underscores that true faith is not merely intellectual assent but a transformative experience that evokes deep submission, reverence, and tears of devotion, reflecting a heart fully surrendered to Allah's mercy and truth.

translation: But there succeeded them a posterity who wasted the prayer and followed lusts. So they will meet perdition.
interpretation: This verse warns against the abandonment of religious obligations and the pursuit of worldly desires, which leads to moral and spiritual ruin, emphasizing the consequences of straying from divine guidance.

translation: Except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds—it is they who will enter Paradise, and they will not be wronged at all.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless mercy of Allah, emphasizing that sincere repentance, true faith, and righteous actions can erase past sins and secure entry into Paradise without any injustice or deprivation of reward.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence which the Most Merciful has promised to His servants in the unseen. Indeed, His promise has ever been an obligation [upon Him].
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty and inevitability of divine promises, particularly the reward of Paradise for the righteous, which is guaranteed by Allah's own nature and will, not contingent on human merit alone.

translation: They will not hear therein any ill speech, but only [greetings of] peace. And they will have their provision therein, morning and afternoon.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purity and tranquility of Paradise, where no harmful or vain words exist, only peace and serenity, reflecting the absolute perfection of the believers' reward.

translation: That is the Paradise which We give as an inheritance to those of Our servants who were righteous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine reward based on righteousness and piety, emphasizing that Paradise is not merely a place of reward but a rightful inheritance granted by Allah to those who embody taqwa (God-consciousness and righteousness) in their lives.

translation: And We (angels) do not descend except by the command of your Lord. To Him belongs what is before us and what is behind us and whatever is between that. And your Lord is never forgetful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and control of Allah over all matters, including the revelation of divine messages. It underscores that even the angels, who deliver revelation, act only by Allah's command, highlighting the structured and purposeful nature of divine decrees. The mention of 'what is before us and what is behind us' signifies Allah's encompassing knowledge and authority over all times—past, present, and future—while the assurance that 'your Lord is never forgetful' reassures believers of Allah's unfailing remembrance and justice.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, so worship Him and be steadfast in His worship. Do you know of any equivalent to Him?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute uniqueness and sovereignty of Allah, commanding exclusive worship and steadfast devotion to Him alone, while rejecting any notion of partners or equals in His divinity.

translation: And man says, 'When I have died, will I indeed be brought to life?',
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and denial of some people regarding the possibility of resurrection after death, reflecting their lack of faith in the Hereafter and the power of Allah to bring life to the dead.

translation: Does man not remember that We created him before, when he was nothing?
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah in creation, reminding humanity of its humble origins—from non-existence to existence—thereby emphasizing the necessity of humility, gratitude, and reliance on Allah rather than arrogance or self-sufficiency.

translation: Indeed, for your Lord We will surely gather them and the devils; then We will bring them to be present around Hell, humbled on their knees.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the accountability of all beings—human and jinn—before Allah. It highlights the humbling and submissive state of the disbelievers and their allies (including the devils) on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the absolute power of Allah to gather and judge His creation with perfect justice.

translation: Then We will surely extract from every sect which of them was most severe against the Most Merciful in defiance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the eventual accountability of those who, despite knowing the truth, persistently oppose and defy the mercy and guidance of Allah with arrogance and obstinacy, emphasizing that their defiance will not go unpunished.

translation: Then We certainly know best who are most worthy of burning therein.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute knowledge and justice, indicating that He is fully aware of those who truly deserve punishment, as opposed to those who may merely appear to deserve it. It underscores the precision of divine judgment, where only those who are truly deserving of Hellfire will be subjected to it, reflecting Allah's perfect wisdom and mercy in His decrees.

translation: And there is not one of you but shall come to it (Hell). This is to your Lord (Allah) a Decree which must be accomplished.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of every individual facing the consequences of their deeds in the Hereafter, emphasizing divine justice and the certainty of accountability for one's actions.

translation: Then We will save those who feared Allah and leave the wrongdoers within it, on their knees.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine justice and mercy, where the righteous are granted salvation and protection, while the oppressors face punishment, illustrating the consequences of one's deeds in the Hereafter.

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, those who disbelieve say to those who believe, 'Which of the two parties [i.e., the believers or the disbelievers] is better in position and more excellent in assembly?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and defiance of the disbelievers, who challenge the believers by questioning the superiority of their faith and community, despite the clear evidence of truth in the Qur'an. It underscores the futility of their skepticism and the ultimate triumph of truth over falsehood.

translation: And how many a generation We have destroyed before them who were better in possessions and [outward] appearance?
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly power, wealth, and beauty, emphasizing that Allah’s decree of destruction is not based on material superiority but on moral and spiritual accountability.

translation: Say, 'Whoever is in error, the Most Gracious will extend for him an extension [of life] until, when they see what they were promised—either the punishment or the Hour [of Judgment]—they will come to know who is worst in position and weaker in soldiers.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the temporary nature of worldly life and the inevitability of accountability in the Hereafter, warning that prolonged respite does not equate to divine approval but rather a test of patience and opportunity for repentance.

translation: And Allah increases those who are guided in guidance. And the enduring good deeds are better with your Lord for reward and better for return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of divine reciprocity—those who sincerely seek guidance are granted increasing clarity and steadfastness in their faith, while righteous actions (like charity, knowledge, or acts of worship) yield the highest recompense in this life and the Hereafter, far surpassing any temporary worldly gains.

translation: Have you seen the one who denies Our signs and says, "I will surely be given wealth and children"?
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and delusion of those who reject divine signs while boasting about worldly gains, implying that true success is not measured by material wealth or progeny but by faith and righteousness.

translation: Does he know the unseen, or has he taken from the Most Merciful a promise?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of anyone claiming knowledge of the unseen or having a special covenant with Allah that grants exclusive access to hidden knowledge, emphasizing the absolute sovereignty and exclusivity of Allah’s knowledge and authority.

translation: Nay! We will record what he says and extend for him the punishment extensively.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine retribution for those who persist in disbelief or arrogance, emphasizing that every word and action will be meticulously recorded and met with commensurate punishment, reflecting the absolute justice and omniscience of Allah.

translation: And We will inherit from him what he says, and he will come to Us alone.
interpretation: This verse underscores the accountability of every individual for their words and deeds, emphasizing that no one can escape the consequences of their actions, as all will ultimately stand alone before Allah on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And they have taken besides Allah [false] deities to be for them a source of power.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of seeking power and security from anything other than Allah, as false deities—whether idols, worldly systems, or even human constructs—cannot provide true strength or protection. It underscores the inherent weakness of associating partners with Allah, as only He possesses true power and authority.

translation: Nay, but they will deny their worship and become their adversaries.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate futility of idolatrous worship, as those who engage in it will eventually deny their false deities and turn against them, revealing the baselessness of their devotion.

translation: Have you not considered that We sent the devils upon the disbelievers to incite them to fury?
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual struggle between divine guidance and the forces of evil, illustrating how disbelief can leave individuals vulnerable to the deceptive whispers of Satan, which drive them toward destructive behavior and intensified hostility against truth.

translation: So do not hasten against them. Indeed, We are preparing for them a punishment.
interpretation: This verse advises patience and restraint in dealing with those who oppose or harm believers, as divine justice will ultimately prevail without the need for premature or unjust retaliation.

translation: The Day We will gather the righteous to the Most Merciful as a delegation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the honor and distinction granted to the righteous on the Day of Judgment, where they will be presented before Allah as honored guests, underscoring their closeness to Him and the special treatment they receive due to their piety and devotion.

translation: And We will drive the criminals to Hell, [as a place of] return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of divine justice, where those who persist in wrongdoing and reject guidance will face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter, emphasizing the certainty of retribution for their deeds.

translation: They possess no power of intercession, except for those who have taken a covenant with the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah in matters of intercession, emphasizing that no one can intercede on behalf of another unless granted explicit permission by Allah, symbolized here by 'taking a covenant'—a metaphor for divine acceptance and favor.

translation: And they say, 'The Most Merciful has taken a son.'
interpretation: This verse refutes the false claim of those who attribute offspring to Allah, emphasizing the absolute oneness and transcendence of Allah, who is beyond any human-like attributes such as having children.

translation: You have come with something monstrous.
interpretation: This verse is a strong rebuke, indicating that the action or statement being referred to is so grave and unacceptable that it is likened to a monstrous or horrifying deed, suggesting extreme disapproval and condemnation from a moral and spiritual perspective.

translation: The heavens almost rupture from above them, and the earth splits open, and the mountains collapse
interpretation: This verse illustrates the overwhelming magnitude and awe-inspiring power of divine signs or events, emphasizing that certain phenomena are so profound that they could shatter the heavens, split the earth, and crumble mountains, underscoring the absolute sovereignty and unmatched might of Allah.

translation: It is not appropriate for the Most Merciful [Allah] to have a son.
interpretation: This verse refutes the false claim that Allah has a son, emphasizing the absolute oneness (Tawheed) of Allah and rejecting any anthropomorphic or polytheistic notions about Him.

translation: And it is not appropriate for the Most Gracious (Allah) to take a son.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute transcendence and uniqueness of Allah, rejecting any anthropomorphic notions of Him having offspring or familial relationships, as such concepts are beneath His divine majesty and perfection.

translation: And there is not one in the heavens and the earth but comes to the Most Gracious as a servant.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah, emphasizing that all creation—whether in the heavens or on earth—exists solely to serve and submit to Him, highlighting the inherent servitude and humility of all beings before their Creator.

translation: He has enumerated them and counted them precisely.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute knowledge and meticulous record of every individual's deeds, actions, and even hidden intentions, leaving no aspect unaccounted for in His divine reckoning.

translation: And all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute uniqueness of Allah's relationship with each individual on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that no one will intercede or accompany another, as each soul stands directly accountable before Allah without any intermediary or support.

translation: Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds - the Most Merciful will appoint for them affection.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine reward for true faith and righteous actions, emphasizing that Allah's mercy will instill love and closeness in the hearts of believers, both towards Him and among themselves, as a consequence of their devotion and good deeds.

translation: And thus We have made it easy in your tongue, so that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a people who are stubborn.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accessibility of the Qur'an's message in the language of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), ensuring it reaches both those who will heed its guidance (the righteous) and those who persistently reject it (the stubborn), thereby fulfilling the dual purpose of mercy and accountability.

translation: How many generations have We destroyed before them! Do you perceive a single one of them or hear even a whisper of them?
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and inevitability of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief and defiance, serving as a stark reminder of the fleeting nature of worldly power and the certainty of divine justice.

translation: Ta-Ha.
interpretation: The opening of this chapter, 'Ta-Ha,' is a combination of two Arabic letters that carry no explicit meaning on their own. This is a common stylistic feature in the Qur'an, where certain chapters begin with such letters, known as 'Muqatta'at.' These letters often serve as a reminder of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, inviting reflection on the divine origin of the message, as their precise meaning remains known only to Allah.

translation: We have not sent down the Qur'an to you (O Muhammad) to cause you distress.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that the revelation of the Qur'an is not meant to burden him with hardship or difficulty, but rather to guide humanity and convey divine guidance.

translation: Except as a reminder for those who fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose of divine revelation: to serve as a reminder and guidance for those who are conscious of Allah and strive to follow His commands, indicating that true guidance is only beneficial to those who are receptive and mindful of their spiritual accountability.

translation: A revelation from [Allah], the One who created the earth and the high heavens.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin of the Qur'an by attributing its revelation to Allah, the Creator of the entire universe, thereby establishing the Qur'an's authority as a message from the One who has power over all creation.

translation: The Most Merciful [who is] above the Throne established Himself.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and transcendence over all creation, while also affirming His nearness and mercy to His servants. The phrase 'established Himself' (استوى) is interpreted by Ahl al-Sunnah as a divine attribute that befits Allah's majesty without likening Him to His creation, avoiding both anthropomorphism and negation of His attributes.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is under the soil.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and ownership of Allah over all existence, from the heavens to the earth and everything in between, including what lies beneath the surface, highlighting His comprehensive control and dominion over all creation.

translation: And if you speak aloud, [He hears it]; and He knows the secret and what is even more hidden.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute knowledge of all forms of speech and thought, whether openly expressed or concealed in the deepest recesses of the heart, emphasizing His omniscience and the futility of attempting to hide anything from Him.

translation: Allah - there is no deity except Him. He has the most beautiful names.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and emphasizes that all divine attributes and perfections belong solely to Him, rejecting any association or comparison with creation.

translation: Has there come to you the story of Moses?
interpretation: This verse introduces the narrative of Moses (peace be upon him) as a reminder and a lesson for the listener or reader, emphasizing the importance of reflecting on the stories of past prophets to draw wisdom and guidance for their own lives.

translation: When he saw a fire, he said to his family, 'Stay here; indeed, I have perceived a fire, perhaps I can bring you a burning brand therefrom or find guidance by the fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the initial spark of revelation and guidance, where Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) is drawn to a fire in the darkness, symbolizing the beginning of divine communication and the path to guidance for his people.

translation: So when he came to it, he was called, 'O Moses!
interpretation: This verse marks a pivotal moment of divine communication, where Allah directly addresses Musa (Moses), signifying the commencement of a sacred mission or revelation, emphasizing the exclusivity and intimacy of this encounter.

translation: Indeed, I am your Lord, so remove your sandals. Indeed, you are in the sacred valley of Tuwa.
interpretation: This verse signifies a moment of divine calling and consecration, where God commands Moses to remove his sandals as a sign of reverence and humility before the sacred ground, highlighting the sanctity of the encounter and the need for spiritual purity in divine presence.

translation: And I have chosen you, so listen to what is revealed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine selection and mission of a prophet, emphasizing the importance of attentiveness to revelation as a means of guidance and purpose.

translation: Indeed, I am Allah. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Me, so worship Me and establish prayer for My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse establishes the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and commands exclusive worship of Him alone, while also emphasizing the importance of prayer as a means of remembering and connecting with Allah.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming—almost I conceal it—so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives for.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, which Allah has chosen to keep hidden from creation to ensure that every individual is held accountable for their deeds without prior knowledge, thereby emphasizing the sincerity and purity of their intentions and actions.

translation: So let not those who believe not in it (the Qur'an) and follow their own desires, divert you from it, lest you perish.
interpretation: This verse warns against being swayed by the disbelief or worldly desires of those who reject the Qur'an, emphasizing the importance of remaining steadfast in faith and not compromising one's beliefs due to external pressures or temptations.

translation: And what is that in your right hand, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse reflects Allah's subtle and merciful approach in addressing Prophet Moses (peace be upon him), inviting him to reflect on the seemingly ordinary object in his hand—his staff—while preparing him for a greater sign of divine power.

translation: He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I beat down leaves with it for my sheep, and I have therein other uses."
interpretation: This verse highlights the practical wisdom of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) in justifying his request for a sign to Allah. It demonstrates his humility and acknowledgment of his needs, showing that reliance on Allah does not negate the use of permissible means to fulfill one's necessities.

translation: He said, 'Cast it down, O Moses.'
interpretation: This command from Allah to Moses (peace be upon him) signifies the divine empowerment of an individual to act in a seemingly impossible or challenging situation, trusting in Allah's support and the ultimate triumph of truth and justice.

translation: Then he threw it down, and behold, it was a snake, moving swiftly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transformative power of divine signs, where a simple act of obedience to Allah’s command results in a miraculous and awe-inspiring manifestation of His will, demonstrating that true authority and change come from Allah alone.

translation: He said, 'Take it and do not fear. We will restore it to its former state.'
interpretation: This verse reflects divine reassurance and the power of restoration, suggesting that God can return things to their original state or condition, whether it be a physical object, a situation, or even a person's spirit, after a period of loss, hardship, or transformation.

translation: And draw your hand to your side; it will come out white without any disease, as another sign.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of divine signs—both as proof of truth and as a means to address the doubts of those who challenge it, demonstrating that Allah's power encompasses both the seen and the unseen.

translation: So that We may show you some of Our greatest signs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that certain experiences or events are not merely coincidental but are deliberate manifestations of divine power and signs meant to guide and strengthen the faith of the believer.

translation: Go to Pharaoh; indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of conveying divine guidance and justice even to those in positions of power who have become arrogant and oppressive, emphasizing the duty to address tyranny with wisdom and resolve.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, expand for me my breast.'
interpretation: This supplication reflects a profound spiritual request for inner peace, clarity, and the capacity to bear the weight of divine responsibility, as exemplified by Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) when he sought strength and receptivity to fulfill his mission.

translation: And make my affair easy for me.
interpretation: This supplication reflects a plea for divine assistance in overcoming difficulties and achieving success in one's endeavors, seeking God's guidance and facilitation in all matters.

translation: And remove the knot from my tongue
interpretation: This supplication reflects a plea for clarity and eloquence in speech, seeking divine assistance to overcome any impediment or difficulty in expressing oneself effectively and truthfully.

translation: So that they may understand my speech.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of clear communication and comprehension in conveying the message, highlighting the need for listeners to engage deeply with the words being spoken to grasp their true meaning and intent.

translation: And appoint for me a minister from my family
interpretation: This supplication reflects a request for support and assistance in fulfilling a significant responsibility, emphasizing the need for divine help and guidance in one's endeavors.

translation: Aaron is my brother.
interpretation: This statement reflects the close relationship and shared mission between the speaker (Moses) and Aaron, highlighting their unity in purpose and divine assignment, where Aaron is chosen to support Moses in conveying God's message to Pharaoh and the Israelites.

translation: Strengthen through him my back.
interpretation: This supplication seeks divine assistance and empowerment through the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to bear the burdens of faith, responsibility, and the challenges of life with steadfastness and resilience.

translation: And associate him (Pharaoh) with me in my affair.
interpretation: This verse reflects the supplication of Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) to Allah, seeking divine support and strength in his mission to confront Pharaoh. It demonstrates the humility and reliance of a prophet on Allah, acknowledging that success in any endeavor ultimately comes from Him alone.

translation: So that we may glorify You much
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of continuous remembrance and glorification of Allah, highlighting the believer's duty to praise Him abundantly in all circumstances.

translation: And we remember You much.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of constant remembrance of Allah, emphasizing that frequent invocation and mindfulness of Him is a virtuous act that strengthens one's connection with the Divine.

translation: Indeed, You have been ever Seeing of us.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's continuous awareness and oversight of all matters concerning the believers, emphasizing His deep knowledge and attentiveness to their needs, struggles, and circumstances.

translation: He said, 'You have been granted your request, O Moses.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the acceptance of Prophet Moses' (peace be upon him) supplication by Allah, demonstrating that sincere prayers are answered by the Almighty, and divine decrees are fulfilled in ways that align with His wisdom and timing.

translation: And We certainly conferred favor upon you another time.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's repeated blessings and favors upon the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), emphasizing that divine grace is continuous and not limited to a single instance, reinforcing the idea of ongoing support and guidance from Allah.

translation: When We inspired to your mother what We inspired.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine communication and guidance bestowed upon the mother of the Prophet Moses (peace be upon him), emphasizing the profound spiritual connection and protection granted to her during a critical moment in her life.

translation: Throw him into the chest, then cast him into the river; the river will cast him ashore, where he will be taken by an enemy of Mine and his. And I cast upon you a love from Me, so that you may be brought up under My watchful eye.
interpretation: This verse highlights divine protection and predestination, where Allah's plan unfolds despite human actions, ensuring the safety and upbringing of a chosen individual under His care.

translation: When your sister was walking, she said, 'Shall I guide you to someone who will nurse him?' So We returned you to your mother, that her eye may be cooled and she may not grieve. And you killed a soul, but We saved you from distress and tested you with various trials. Then you stayed for years among the people of Madyan, then you came at the appointed time, O Moses.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's divine protection and guidance over Prophet Moses (peace be upon him), demonstrating how Allah intervenes in human affairs to fulfill His plans and preserve His chosen servants from harm, even when they are unaware of His support.

translation: And I have chosen you for Myself.
interpretation: This verse signifies Allah's special selection and favor upon a person or a group, indicating a unique purpose or mission assigned to them by divine will.

translation: Go, you and your brother, with My signs, and do not slacken in My remembrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and perseverance in fulfilling one's mission, even when faced with challenges or opposition. It also highlights the necessity of constant remembrance of Allah to maintain faith and resolve in the face of adversity.

translation: Go, both of you, to Pharaoh. Indeed, he has transgressed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of conveying divine guidance and justice to those in positions of power, even when they have become arrogant and oppressive, as Pharaoh had. It serves as a reminder that no one, regardless of their status, is above accountability for their actions, and that the duty to uphold truth and righteousness is paramount.

translation: So speak to him kindly, perhaps he will be reminded or fear [Allah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gentle and respectful communication, even with those who may be hostile or opposed to the message, in the hope that kindness will soften their hearts and lead them to reflection or reverence.

translation: They said, "Our Lord, indeed we fear that he will hasten [punishment] against us or that he will transgress."
interpretation: This supplication reflects a deep sense of humility and fear before divine justice, acknowledging human frailty and the potential for divine wrath to manifest swiftly or excessively, highlighting the need for mercy and protection.

translation: He said, "Fear not. Indeed, I am with you both, hearing and seeing."
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that Allah is always present and aware of their circumstances, providing comfort and support in times of fear or uncertainty.

translation: So they came to him and said, 'Indeed, we are messengers of your Lord. So send with us the Children of Israel and do not torment them. We have come to you with a sign from your Lord, and peace be upon whoever follows the guidance.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of conveying God's message with clarity and respect, even when addressing those in positions of power or opposition, as the messengers approached Pharaoh with a balance of firmness and diplomacy, emphasizing both their divine mission and the consequences of rejecting guidance.

translation: Indeed, it has been revealed to us that the punishment will be upon whoever denies and turns away.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine retribution for those who reject the truth and persistently turn away from it, highlighting the accountability of individuals for their disbelief and defiance.

translation: So who is the Lord of you two, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of recognizing and acknowledging the true Lord and Creator, challenging individuals to reflect on their beliefs and submit to the divine authority of Allah.

translation: Our Lord is the One who gave everything its creation and then guided [it].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's comprehensive role as the Creator and Sustainer, who not only brings all things into existence but also provides them with the innate guidance necessary for their existence and purpose, reflecting a divine order and wisdom in all of creation.

translation: So what is the case with the earlier generations?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the fate of past civilizations that rejected divine guidance, warning against the consequences of arrogance and disbelief, and urging humanity to heed the lessons of history to avoid repeating their downfall.

translation: Its knowledge is only with my Lord. In a Book. My Lord neither errs nor forgets.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute certainty and infallibility of divine knowledge, emphasizing that Allah’s decrees and records are perfect and free from error or forgetting, contrasting with human limitations.

translation: Who has made the earth a resting place for you and made for you roads therein and sent down from the sky water, then We brought forth with it pairs of various plants.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's meticulous design in creating the earth for human habitation, providing stability (as a 'resting place'), guidance (through 'roads'), and sustenance (via water that produces diverse vegetation), underscoring His role as the Sustainer and Provider for all life.

translation: Eat and pasture your livestock. Indeed, in that are signs for people of understanding.
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the natural world and the sustenance provided by Allah, urging believers to observe and appreciate the signs of divine wisdom in the provision of food and the sustenance of livestock, which serve as reminders of Allah's power and mercy.

translation: From it [the earth] We created you, and into it We will return you, and from it We will bring you forth another time.
interpretation: This verse underscores the cyclical nature of human existence and the divine power over life, death, and resurrection, emphasizing humanity's origin, return to Allah, and eventual revival for the Hereafter.

translation: And We certainly showed him all Our signs, but he denied and refused.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth despite clear evidence, illustrating the consequences of rejecting divine signs out of pride or disbelief.

translation: Did you come to us to drive us out of our land with your magic, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and defiance of those who reject divine guidance, attributing the miracles of a prophet to mere sorcery rather than recognizing them as signs from God.

translation: So we will bring you magic like it, so set for us a meeting time, which neither we nor you will fail to keep, at a place of your choosing.
interpretation: This verse reflects a challenge posed by those who doubted the divine origin of the Qur'an, demanding that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) produce something similar in its eloquence and power. The challenge underscores the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, which, despite being revealed to an unlettered man, remains unmatched in its linguistic and spiritual excellence.

translation: Your appointment is the Day of the Festival, and that the people will be gathered at mid-morning.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment, where the people will be resurrected and gathered for reckoning, emphasizing the certainty and timing of this event as a divine appointment.

translation: So Pharaoh turned away, plotted, and then came [to Musa (Moses)].
interpretation: This verse illustrates the deceptive and manipulative nature of Pharaoh's response to the truth brought by Prophet Moses (peace be upon him). Instead of engaging with the message in good faith, Pharaoh resorted to plotting and scheming, demonstrating a refusal to acknowledge the divine signs and a determination to oppose them through worldly power and cunning.

translation: Moses said to them, "Woe to you! Do not fabricate a lie against Allah, lest He destroy you with a punishment. And indeed, he has failed who fabricates [a lie]."
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of attributing falsehood to Allah, warning against the severe consequences of such an act, both in this world and the Hereafter, while highlighting the ultimate failure of those who engage in deception against divine truth.

translation: So they disputed among themselves their affair and [while] they concealed [their] private conversation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the internal discord and hidden scheming among a group, reflecting how disputes and secret deliberations can lead to confusion and misdirection, ultimately undermining unity and purpose.

translation: They said, "Indeed, these two are but magicians who want to drive you out from your land with their magic and do away with your most exemplary way."
interpretation: This verse reflects the resistance of the people of Moses (peace be upon him) to the truth brought by him and Aaron (peace be upon them), attributing their message to sorcery rather than divine guidance. It highlights how people often reject truth when it challenges their established norms or threatens their power, resorting to false accusations to justify their opposition.

translation: So resolve upon your plan, and then come [forward] in straight ranks; and today will be the day of victory for the one who prevails.
interpretation: This verse encourages unity and strategic planning among believers in the face of adversity, emphasizing that success comes to those who stand firm and united in their faith and resolve.

translation: They said, "O Moses, either you throw [your staff] or we will be the first to throw [our staffes]."
interpretation: This verse reflects the defiance and arrogance of the magicians of Pharaoh who challenged Moses (peace be upon him) to a contest, attempting to undermine his divine mission by asserting their own power first, thereby showing their disbelief and hostility toward the truth.

translation: Nay, they said: "Only put the spell (on us), then behold, their ropes and their staffs, it seemed to him from their magic as though they were moving fast."
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive power of magic, where the magicians' ropes and staffs appeared to move on their own due to their enchantment, illustrating how falsehood can temporarily mimic truth, but ultimately, divine truth prevails.

translation: So Moses conceived a fear within himself.
interpretation: This verse reflects the initial human reaction of fear and apprehension when faced with the overwhelming presence of divine revelation or an extraordinary encounter, highlighting the humility and vulnerability of even the greatest prophets before the majesty of Allah.

translation: We said, 'Do not fear, for indeed you are the most exalted.'
interpretation: This verse reassures the believer of divine protection and empowerment, affirming that God elevates those who trust in Him, dispelling fear and instilling confidence in their spiritual and moral superiority over worldly challenges.

translation: And throw what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have made. They have only made the deception of a magician, and the magician will not succeed wherever he is.
interpretation: This verse highlights the power of divine truth over human deception, illustrating that Allah's signs and miracles will always prevail over the illusions and tricks of those who oppose the truth, no matter how cunning their schemes may appear.

translation: So the magicians fell down in prostration. They said, "We have believed in the Lord of Aaron and Moses."
interpretation: This verse highlights the transformative power of truth and divine signs, as even the most hardened skeptics (the magicians) are compelled to submit to the truth when faced with undeniable evidence, demonstrating that genuine faith arises from recognizing and yielding to the signs of Allah.

translation: Did you believe in him before I gave you permission? Indeed, he is your chief who has taught you magic. So I will surely cut off your hands and feet from opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees, and you will surely know which of us is more severe in punishment and more lasting.
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of confrontation where authority (likely Pharaoh) asserts control over belief, implying that faith must be sanctioned by power rather than divine truth. The harsh punishment described underscores the oppressive nature of the ruler's response to dissent, where dissent is framed as rebellion against both political and religious order, and the severity of the punishment is meant to serve as a deterrent to others.

translation: They said, "We will never prefer you over the clear proofs that have come to us, and over He who created us. So decree whatever you are to decree. You can only decree [regarding] this worldly life."
interpretation: This verse reflects the steadfastness of believers in their faith and their refusal to compromise their beliefs, even under pressure. It highlights their unwavering commitment to divine truth and their acknowledgment that worldly decrees hold no power over the eternal truths revealed by God.

translation: Indeed, we have believed in our Lord so that He may forgive us our sins and what you (Pharaoh) forced us to do of magic. And Allah is the Best and the Most Lasting.
interpretation: This verse reflects the unwavering faith of the believers in Allah's mercy and justice, even in the face of coercion and oppression. It underscores the belief that true faith is not diminished by external pressures or forced actions, as Allah's forgiveness encompasses both sincere belief and unintended or coerced deeds. The mention of 'magic' here symbolizes the oppressive demands of Pharaoh, highlighting that Allah's power and permanence transcend all worldly forces.

translation: Indeed, whoever comes to his Lord as a criminal - then indeed, for him is Hell. He will neither die therein nor live.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and irreversible nature of divine justice, emphasizing that those who meet their Lord burdened with sin will face eternal punishment without any hope of escape or relief, highlighting the gravity of moral accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: But whoever comes to Him as a believer who has done righteous deeds—it is they who will have the highest degrees [of Paradise],
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere faith and righteous actions in attaining closeness to Allah and the highest ranks in Paradise, highlighting that both belief and good deeds are essential for ultimate success.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. And that is the reward of whoever purifies himself.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true purification of the self—through righteous deeds, repentance, and adherence to divine guidance—leads to an eternal reward in Paradise, characterized by unending bliss and closeness to Allah.

translation: And We inspired Moses, saying: 'Take away My slaves by night, surely you shall be followed.' Then Pharaoh sent callers to [all] cities, [ordered]: 'Indeed, these are indeed but a small band, and indeed, they are enraged against us, and indeed, we are all on guard.' So We brought out the people of Pharaoh from gardens and springs, and treasures and a splendid station. Thus. And We caused the people of Israel to inherit them. So the sun rose upon them at the time when the people of Pharaoh were [left] dead, [lying] cast out, as if they had not remained there for even an hour of a day. Thus do We expose those who are criminals.
interpretation: This verse underscores divine intervention in human affairs, illustrating how Allah orchestrates events to fulfill His will and protect His righteous servants. It highlights the futility of human arrogance and power when confronted with divine decree, as seen in the downfall of Pharaoh despite his perceived invincibility. The narrative serves as a reminder of Allah's justice and the transient nature of worldly might, reinforcing the importance of faith and submission to divine authority.

translation: So Pharaoh pursued them with his armies, and the sea overwhelmed them completely.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of arrogance and defiance against divine command, as Pharaoh's pursuit of the Israelites, despite clear signs of God's power, led to his ultimate destruction, serving as a lesson in the futility of opposing divine will.

translation: And Pharaoh led his people astray and did not guide them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive role of a leader who misguides his people instead of guiding them toward truth and righteousness, emphasizing the moral responsibility of leadership.

translation: O Children of Israel, We delivered you from your enemy, and We made a covenant with you at the right side of the mount [Tur], and We sent down upon you the manna and the quails.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's favors and covenants with the Children of Israel, emphasizing His mercy in delivering them from their enemies and providing them with sustenance (manna and quails) as a sign of His ongoing care and the consequences of their covenant with Him.

translation: Eat of the good things We have provided for you and do not transgress [or exceed] therein, lest My anger should descend upon you. And he upon whom My anger descends has certainly perished.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the balance between enjoying the permissible blessings of Allah and avoiding excess or injustice, which can invoke divine displeasure. It warns against overindulgence or oppression in the use of Allah's provisions, emphasizing that such behavior can lead to spiritual ruin and divine punishment.

translation: And indeed, I am the Perpetual Forgiver of those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds, and then remain upon guidance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless mercy of Allah, emphasizing that sincere repentance, faith, and righteous actions are the keys to forgiveness, even after committing sins.

translation: And what made you hasten from your people, O Moses?
interpretation: This verse highlights a moment of divine reassurance to Moses (peace be upon him) after he left his people in haste, possibly due to his distress or confusion, indicating that Allah's plan is unfolding with perfect timing and wisdom.

translation: They said, 'These are following me, and I hastened to You, my Lord, so that You may be pleased.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of deep spiritual urgency and devotion, where the supplicant seeks to align themselves with divine will, expressing both their commitment to follow guidance and their eagerness to attain divine satisfaction.

translation: He said, "So indeed, We have tested your people after you [departed], and the Samiri has led them astray."
interpretation: This verse highlights the vulnerability of communities to deviation and misguidance after the departure of a righteous leader, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness in faith and the need for constant vigilance against false influences.

translation: So Moses returned to his people, angry and grieved. He said, 'O my people, did your Lord not make you a good promise? Then, was the time prolonged for you, or did you intend that wrath from your Lord should descend upon you, so you broke your promise to me?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the tension between divine promises and human accountability, illustrating how delay in fulfillment does not negate the certainty of the promise but underscores the importance of steadfastness and trust in divine timing.

translation: They said, "We did not break our promise to you by our own will, but we were made to carry the burdens of the ornaments of the people, then we threw them away, and thus did the Samiri suggest."
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of humans to rationalize their mistakes by blaming external factors or circumstances rather than taking full responsibility for their actions, as seen in the excuses made by the people who followed the Samiri.

translation: So he brought out for them a calf—a lifeless body that had a lowing sound. They said, "This is your god and the god of Moses, but he forgot."
interpretation: This verse critiques the Israelites' idolatry and their hasty abandonment of monotheism, illustrating the human tendency to revert to material and tangible objects of worship when divine guidance is absent, and the folly of attributing forgetfulness to God.

translation: Do they not see that they cannot return a word [of supplication] to them, nor do they possess for them any harm or benefit?
interpretation: This verse highlights the powerlessness of idols and false deities to respond to prayers or provide any benefit or harm to their worshippers, underscoring the futility of associating partners with Allah and the absolute sovereignty of Allah alone.

translation: And Aaron had already said to them before [the return of Moses], 'O my people, you are only being tested by this, and indeed, your Lord is the Most Merciful, so follow me and obey my order.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of a prophet in guiding their people back to the truth when they are misled, emphasizing that trials and tests are part of human existence, but the ultimate mercy and guidance come from Allah, urging obedience to divine leadership.

translation: They said, "We will never cease being devoted to it until Moses returns to us."
interpretation: This verse reflects the Israelites' steadfastness in their devotion to the golden calf they had made during Moses' absence, demonstrating their lack of patience and trust in Allah's guidance, as well as their susceptibility to deviation when left without proper leadership.

translation: He (Moses) said, "O Aaron, what prevented you when you saw them going astray?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of standing firm in faith and taking a stand against wrongdoing, even when others falter. It underscores the responsibility of leaders and those in positions of guidance to correct deviations with wisdom and resolve.

translation: Will you not follow [my command]? Then have you disobeyed My order?
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of obedience to divine commandments and serves as a gentle rebuke for any deviation from them, highlighting the consequences of defiance and the need for repentance and realignment with the path of righteousness.

translation: He said, 'O son of my mother, do not seize [me] by my beard or [by] my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, "You have caused division among the Children of Israel and did not observe [i.e., wait for] my word."'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of patience and respect in resolving conflicts, even among close associates. It also underscores the need to consider the consequences of one's actions and words, ensuring they do not lead to division or harm to others.

translation: He said, 'Then what is your case, O Samiri?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moment of confrontation where Moses questions Samiri about his role in leading the Israelites into idolatry, emphasizing accountability for misleading others.

translation: I perceived what they did not perceive, so I took a handful of the trace of the Messenger and cast it away. And thus my soul enticed me.
interpretation: This verse highlights the internal struggle between faith and temptation, where one may momentarily grasp the guidance of truth (symbolized by the 'trace of the Messenger') but then succumb to the deceptions of their own desires, leading to regret and rejection of that guidance.

translation: He said, "Then go, for indeed, for you in the life [a state] is that you will say, 'No contact.' And indeed, for you [there is] an appointment which you will not fail to keep. And look at your god which you remained devoted to—we will burn it, then we will scatter it into the sea, utterly scattering."
interpretation: This verse illustrates the rejection of false deities and the consequences of idolatry, emphasizing the futility of worshipping anything other than the One True God. It also highlights the certainty of divine appointment (the Day of Judgment) and the ultimate power of Allah to destroy false objects of worship, symbolizing the eradication of disbelief and the triumph of truth.

translation: Your god is but Allah, besides whom there is no god, the All-Knowing, the All-Encompassing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah (Tawheed), rejecting any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him. It also highlights Allah's infinite knowledge and encompassing power over all things, reinforcing the idea that true worship and reliance should be directed solely to Him.

translation: Thus have We narrated unto thee some of the stories of what happened before: and We have given thee from Ourselves a Reminder (this Qur'an).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and purpose of the Qur'an, presenting it as a reminder and a source of guidance, distinct from mere historical narration, while affirming its role as a continuation of God's communication with humanity through revelation.

translation: But whoever turns away from it (the Qur'an) will indeed bear a heavy burden on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe consequence of rejecting the guidance of the Qur'an, indicating that such rejection will result in a heavy burden of sin and accountability on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Abiding therein forever, and wretched will be for them on the Day of Resurrection the burden.
interpretation: This verse underscores the eternal nature of the punishment for those who reject faith, emphasizing the unrelenting severity of their fate and the immense burden of their sins on the Day of Judgment.

translation: The Day the Trumpet is blown, and We will gather the criminals that Day, blue-eyed (with terror).
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the accountability of human actions, emphasizing divine justice where even the most hardened criminals will face the consequences of their deeds, depicted here in a state of overwhelming fear and helplessness.

translation: They whisper to one another, saying, 'You stayed no longer than ten nights.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the brevity and transient nature of worldly life, emphasizing how people, in their disbelief or denial, underestimate the significance of their time in this world, reducing its importance to mere fleeting moments.

translation: We know best what they say when the most eloquent of them speaks: 'You have tarried but a day.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's deep awareness of human speech and deception, even when it is cleverly disguised as truth. It underscores the transient nature of worldly life compared to the eternal reality of the Hereafter, where all deeds will be fully accounted for.

translation: And they ask you about the mountains, so say, 'My Lord will blow them away completely.'
interpretation: This verse signifies the absolute power of Allah over all creation, demonstrating that even the most seemingly permanent and formidable structures, like mountains, are subject to His command and can be utterly destroyed at His will, reflecting the transient nature of the material world and the ultimate sovereignty of Allah over all existence.

translation: And leave it as a level, barren plain.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power of Allah to reduce even the most prosperous and bustling places to a state of desolation and emptiness, highlighting the transient nature of worldly life and the inevitability of divine judgment.

translation: You will not see in it any crookedness or deviation.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the perfection and flawlessness of the Qur'an, highlighting that its guidance is absolute and free from any inconsistency, contradiction, or deviation from truth.

translation: On that Day, they will follow the caller [with] no deviation therefrom, and humbled will be the voices to the Most Merciful, so you will not hear except a whisper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute submission and inevitability of divine judgment on the Day of Resurrection, where all creation will unresistingly follow the call to account without deviation, and the awe-inspiring majesty of Allah will silence all voices except for the faintest, reverent whispers, reflecting the overwhelming humility and submission of all beings before their Creator.

translation: On that Day, no intercession will avail except [that of] one to whom the Most Merciful has given permission and has accepted his word.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where even intercession is only granted by His permission and acceptance, highlighting the exclusivity of His authority and the futility of any intercession without His divine approval.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they do not encompass Him with knowledge.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and unknowable nature of Allah's essence and knowledge, emphasizing that human comprehension is limited and cannot fully grasp the divine, which transcends all boundaries and encompasses all things.

translation: And [all] faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all existence. And he will have failed who carries injustice [as a burden].
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and eternal nature of Allah, before whom all creation will ultimately submit in humility. The second part warns that those who persist in oppression or injustice, whether against others or themselves, will face ruin, as their burden of sin will lead to their downfall, emphasizing divine justice and the consequences of moral transgression.

translation: And whoever does righteous deeds, being a believer, will not fear injustice or deprivation.
interpretation: This verse assures believers that their righteous actions, coupled with faith, will not be diminished or unjustly treated by Allah; their deeds will be fully rewarded without any reduction or oppression.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an and have diversified within it the warnings, so that they may fear Allah or it may produce a reminder for them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purposeful design of the Qur'an's revelation in Arabic, with its repeated warnings and varied expressions, to evoke God-consciousness (taqwa) in the hearts of listeners or to serve as a reminder that sparks reflection and spiritual awakening.

translation: So exalted is Allah, the True King. Do not hasten with [recitation of] the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you, and say, 'My Lord, increase me in knowledge.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of patience and divine timing in receiving and understanding revelation, while also emphasizing the pursuit of knowledge as a lifelong endeavor guided by Allah.

translation: And We had already taken a covenant from Adam before, but he forgot; and We found not in him a firm resolve.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent human tendency to forget divine commands and the struggle to maintain steadfastness in faith, even for the first human, Adam, despite his direct covenant with God.

translation: And [mention] when We said to the angels, 'Prostrate to Adam,' so they prostrated, except for Iblees. He refused.
interpretation: This verse highlights the first act of defiance against the divine command, illustrating the consequences of arrogance and disobedience. Iblees' refusal to prostrate, despite the explicit order, stems from his self-perceived superiority over Adam, whom he deemed inferior due to his creation from clay rather than fire. This act of defiance marks the origin of pride and its destructive potential, serving as a cautionary example of how unchecked arrogance can lead to spiritual ruin and eternal loss.

translation: So We said, 'O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife. Then let him not drive you both out of Paradise so you suffer.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the deceptive nature of Satan (Iblis) and the importance of remaining vigilant against his whispers, as he seeks to lead humans astray from the path of obedience to Allah, even if it means causing them hardship and deprivation of divine blessings.

translation: Indeed, you will not go hungry therein or be unclothed.
interpretation: This verse assures the believer of divine providence and care in the Hereafter, guaranteeing freedom from basic human needs like hunger and lack of clothing, symbolizing complete fulfillment and contentment in Paradise.

translation: And you will not be thirsty therein, nor will you be exposed to the sun.
interpretation: This verse signifies the eternal comfort and relief from hardships that believers will experience in Paradise, where all worldly sufferings—such as thirst and exposure to harsh elements—will cease to exist.

translation: Then Satan whispered to him, [saying], "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and possession that does not deteriorate?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan, who tempts humans by promising eternal benefits and appealing to their desires for permanence and power, ultimately leading them away from obedience to God.

translation: But they both ate from it, and thus their shameful parts became exposed to them, and they began to fasten upon themselves some of the leaves of Paradise. And Adam disobeyed his Lord and thus erred.
interpretation: This verse highlights the immediate consequence of human transgression against divine command, illustrating the loss of innocence and the onset of shame, as well as the human instinct to conceal vulnerability. It also underscores the concept of disobedience leading to error, emphasizing the moral accountability inherent in human nature.

translation: Then his Lord chose him, turned to him in forgiveness, and guided him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor and mercy bestowed upon a person, emphasizing that despite human shortcomings, God's grace can lead to repentance, guidance, and ultimate redemption.

translation: He said, "Go down from it, all of you, [and] some of you will be enemies to others. Then if there comes to you guidance from Me, whoever follows My guidance will not go astray [in the world] nor suffer [in the Hereafter]."
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of human choice and the guidance provided by divine revelation. It highlights that while enmity and conflict are inherent in human nature due to differing paths, those who adhere to divine guidance will be protected from spiritual deviation and ultimate loss, emphasizing the importance of following righteousness as a safeguard against misguidance and despair.

translation: But whoever turns away from My remembrance will have a life of narrowness, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of neglecting the remembrance of Allah (dhikr), indicating that such neglect leads to a life of hardship and spiritual deprivation in this world, while also resulting in a state of blindness and loss on the Day of Judgment, symbolizing both spiritual and physical deprivation.

translation: He will say, 'My Lord, why have You raised me blind while I was seeing?''
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound regret and realization of someone who had been granted sight in this world but failed to use it to recognize the truth of Allah and His signs, leading to spiritual blindness in the Hereafter.

translation: Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them, so today you are forgotten.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of reciprocity in divine justice—how one treats the signs of Allah determines how they will be treated in return. Forgetting or neglecting the guidance sent by Allah leads to being forgotten by Him in a state of loss and abandonment.

translation: And thus do We recompense he who transgresses and does not believe in the signs of his Lord. And indeed, the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe and more enduring.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, where those who exceed the bounds of righteousness and reject the signs of Allah (i.e., His guidance and revelations) will face severe and lasting consequences in the Hereafter. It highlights the gravity of ingratitude toward divine blessings and the rejection of moral and spiritual boundaries, emphasizing that such actions are met with a punishment that is both harsher and more permanent than any worldly retribution.

translation: Have they not been guided by the many We destroyed before them—generations who walked in the dwellings of those they now inhabit? Indeed, in that are signs for people of intellect.
interpretation: This verse underscores the historical precedent of divine punishment for past nations who persisted in disbelief and defiance, despite witnessing the remnants of their destroyed civilizations. It serves as a warning to contemporary people, urging reflection on the consequences of arrogance and rejection of divine guidance, while emphasizing the importance of intellectual discernment in recognizing God's signs.

translation: And if not for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been obligatory [to punish them] and [they would have been given] a specified term.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and forbearance, as He delays punishment for wrongdoers despite their sins, giving them respite until an appointed time, demonstrating His justice and the opportunity for repentance.

translation: So be patient over what they say and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord before the rising of the sun and before its setting; and during periods of the night [exalt Him], and at the ends of the day, that you may be satisfied.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience in the face of adversity and opposition, while also highlighting the significance of constant remembrance and praise of Allah. The call to glorify Allah before sunrise, sunset, during the night, and at the ends of the day underscores the need for a continuous and unwavering connection with the Divine, which ultimately leads to inner contentment and satisfaction.

translation: And do not extend your eyes toward that by which We have diversified the mates of the worldly life, [its being but] a temporary enjoyment of this world, that We may test them thereby. And your Lord's provision is better and more lasting.
interpretation: This verse cautions against excessive attachment to the fleeting pleasures and luxuries of this world, reminding believers that such distractions are temporary trials meant to test humanity. True and lasting sustenance, both material and spiritual, comes from Allah, which is superior in quality and permanence compared to the transient enjoyments of this life.

translation: And enjoin prayer upon your family [and yourself] and be steadfast therein. We ask you not for provision; We provide for you, and the [best] outcome is for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consistency and perseverance in fulfilling one's religious duties, particularly prayer, as a means of guidance and righteousness for oneself and one's family. It reassures that reliance on Allah's provision is sufficient, as He is the ultimate sustainer, and that the true success lies in piety and devotion to Him.

translation: And they say, "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?" Has there not come to them evidence of what was in the former scriptures?
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism of the disbelievers who demand miraculous signs as proof of the Prophet's (peace be upon him) message, while ignoring the clear signs already present in the divine scriptures of the past.

translation: And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it (the Qur'an), they would surely have said: 'Our Lord, why did You not send to us a Messenger so that we might have followed Your verses before we were humbled and disgraced?',
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom behind the gradual revelation of divine guidance and the delay of punishment, as it provides humanity with the opportunity to reflect, repent, and follow the truth before facing divine retribution, thereby demonstrating Allah's mercy and justice.

translation: Say, 'Each is waiting, so wait. You will soon know who are the people of the straight path and who has been guided.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine justice and the accountability of all actions; it serves as a warning to those who oppose the truth that their fate will be revealed in due time, while affirming that guidance is in the hands of Allah alone.

translation: The account of mankind has drawn near to them, while they are in heedlessness turning away.
