interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning about the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing humanity's tendency to remain oblivious to this ultimate reality despite its proximity, often distracted by worldly pursuits and turning away from moral and spiritual accountability.

translation: No mention from their Lord comes to them but they listen to it while they are at play.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between the divine message and the frivolous attitude of those who hear it, indicating that they are so engrossed in worldly distractions that they fail to reflect on the profound guidance being conveyed to them.

translation: Their hearts are distracted. And the wrongdoers conspired in private, saying, "Is this [Prophet] not but a man like you? So will you follow magic while you perceive [the truth]?"
interpretation: This verse critiques those who dismiss the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by reducing his message to mere human invention, despite their own awareness of the truth. It highlights the hypocrisy of people who recognize the Prophet's humanity yet reject his divine mission out of arrogance or stubbornness, while their hearts remain distracted from the deeper spiritual reality.

translation: My Lord knows whatever is said in the heavens and the earth; and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's omniscience and awareness of all speech, whether in the heavens or the earth, emphasizing that nothing is hidden from His knowledge, and He is fully capable of hearing and comprehending all that is said.

translation: Nay, they say: '[Muhammad's revelations are but] confused dreams; nay, he has invented it himself; nay, he is a poet. Let him, then, bring us a sign just as the earlier [prophets] were sent [with signs].'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and refusal of the disbelievers to accept the divine origin of the Qur'an, attributing it instead to human fabrication or poetic inspiration, while demanding miraculous proofs similar to those given to past prophets—a challenge that underscores their hardened hearts and rejection of faith despite the clear signs already presented.

translation: No nation before them believed that We destroyed. Will they then believe?
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of expecting faith from those who persist in disbelief despite clear signs and warnings, as history shows that nations that rejected guidance were ultimately destroyed.

translation: And We sent not before you [O Muhammad] except men to whom We revealed [Our message]. So ask the people of the remembrance if you do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that prophethood is not exclusive to any particular race or lineage but is granted by Allah to whom He wills, and all messengers were human beings who received divine revelation.

translation: And We did not grant them (the angels) bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal.
interpretation: This verse refutes the pre-Islamic Arabian belief that angels were immortal beings who did not require sustenance, emphasizing that angels, like humans, are created beings with limitations, subject to Allah's will and not divine in nature.

translation: Then We fulfilled for them the promise, and We saved them and whom We willed, and We destroyed the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine principle of justice and mercy, where Allah fulfills His promises to the righteous while punishing those who exceed bounds in disbelief or oppression. It underscores the balance between divine grace and accountability, reminding humanity of the consequences of their actions.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you a Book containing your mention. Will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Qur'an's role as a source of guidance and remembrance for humanity, urging people to reflect upon its teachings rather than merely recite it passively.

translation: And how many a town have We destroyed that was given to wrongdoing, and set up after it another people!
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice, illustrating that oppressive societies are not spared from destruction, while new communities are raised in their place, often embodying the consequences of past injustices or the mercy of Allah in granting new opportunities for reform and righteousness.

translation: But when they felt Our punishment, behold, they began to flee from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of attempting to escape divine punishment once it has been decreed, as the fleeing itself becomes a sign of their acknowledgment of their wrongdoing and the inevitability of their fate.

translation: Do not run away, but return to that which you were given luxury and to your dwellings, so that you may be questioned.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against fleeing from accountability or responsibility, urging individuals to face the consequences of their actions rather than evading them, as all will ultimately be held to account for their deeds.

translation: They will say, "O woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the realization of wrongdoing and regret in the Hereafter, where people will acknowledge their past injustices as they face the consequences of their actions.

translation: And so their cry continued until We made them like a harvested field, silent and still.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the finality of divine punishment, emphasizing that persistent denial and defiance of truth ultimately lead to complete annihilation and irreversible loss, leaving no trace or resistance behind.

translation: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them in play.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purposeful and meaningful creation of the universe by Allah, rejecting any notion of creation as mere amusement or without significance.

translation: Had We wished to take a pastime, We could have taken it from Ourselves, if We were ever to do (such a thing).
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute transcendence and uniqueness of Allah, emphasizing that He is beyond any need for amusement or diversion, as these are attributes of creation. It serves as a rebuke to those who attribute human-like qualities or limitations to Allah, affirming His perfection and self-sufficiency.

translation: But We cast the truth against falsehood, so it destroys it, and behold, falsehood perishes. And woe to you for what you attribute [to Allah]!
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitable defeat of falsehood when confronted by the truth, emphasizing that falsehood cannot withstand the power of truth, which is a divine attribute. The warning 'woe to you for what you attribute [to Allah]' serves as a reproach to those who falsely ascribe lies or imperfections to Allah, highlighting the grave consequences of such slander.

translation: To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth. And those near Him are not prevented by arrogance from worshipping Him, nor do they tire.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, highlighting that every being in the heavens and the earth is subservient to Him. The second part underscores the humility and unwavering devotion of the angels or those close to Allah, who do not hesitate or grow weary in their worship and service to Him, serving as a model of perfect submission and devotion for all believers.

translation: They glorify Allah night and day, never ceasing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the perpetual and unwavering devotion of certain beings—often understood in Islamic tradition as angels—to the worship and glorification of Allah, emphasizing their tireless and unflagging commitment to this act of worship without any interruption or fatigue.

translation: Or have they taken for themselves gods from the earth who resurrect [the dead]?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of associating partners with Allah by questioning whether anyone could possibly derive divinity from the earth itself—something created and subservient—let alone claim the power to resurrect the dead, which is an exclusive attribute of Allah alone.

translation: If there were within the heavens and the earth gods besides Allah, they both would be ruined. So exalted is Allah, Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness and supremacy of Allah (Tawheed), emphasizing that the existence of multiple deities would lead to chaos and disorder in the universe, as their conflicting wills and powers would disrupt the harmony of creation.

translation: He is not questioned about what He does, but they will be questioned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and unquestionable authority of Allah, emphasizing that His actions are beyond human comprehension or judgment, while humans will be held accountable for their deeds on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Or have they taken gods besides Him? Say, [O Muhammad], 'Produce your proof. This [Qur'an] is the message for those with me and the message of those before me.' But most of them do not know the truth, so they are turning away.
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to provide evidence for their false deities while affirming the truth of the Qur'an, which aligns with the divine messages of the past. It highlights the ignorance and stubbornness of those who reject the truth despite its clarity.

translation: And We sent not before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of God (Tawheed) and the core message of all prophets, which is to worship Allah alone without associating any partners with Him. It serves as a reminder that the fundamental purpose of human existence is to submit to Allah and acknowledge His exclusive right to worship.

translation: And they say, 'The Most Merciful has taken a son.' Exalted is He! Rather, they are [but] honored servants.
interpretation: This verse refutes the false claim of divine filiation attributed to Allah, emphasizing His absolute transcendence and purity from such anthropomorphic notions, while affirming the elevated status of righteous servants who are honored by their closeness to Allah through obedience and servitude.

translation: They do not precede Him in speech, and they act by His command.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute submission and obedience of the angels to Allah's will, highlighting their perfect alignment with His commands without any deviation or initiative of their own.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they cannot intercede except for those with whom He is pleased, and they stand in awe of His majesty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute knowledge and sovereignty, highlighting that intercession is only granted by His permission, underscoring the humility and reverence of the angels in His presence.

translation: And whoever among them says, 'I am a god besides Him,' such We will recompense with Hell. Thus do We recompense the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of God (Tawheed) and warns against associating partners with Him, which is a grave sin in Islam. It highlights the severe punishment for those who claim divinity for themselves or others, affirming that such arrogance and falsehood will be met with divine justice in the Hereafter.

translation: Have not those who disbelieve known that the heavens and the earth were a joined entity, and We separated them? And We made from water every living thing. Will they not then believe?
interpretation: This verse underscores the signs of Allah's power and wisdom in the creation of the universe, challenging the disbelievers to reflect on the evidentiary nature of these signs to guide them toward faith.

translation: And We placed on the earth firm mountains, lest it should shake with them, and We placed therein wide paths for them to travel, that they may be guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's wisdom in creating the earth with stability and guidance, emphasizing that divine design serves both physical and spiritual purposes.

translation: And We made the sky a protected ceiling, but they turn away from its signs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the majesty and protection of the heavens, which serve as a sign of Allah's power and wisdom, yet many people remain heedless of these profound signs.

translation: And it is He who created the night and the day and the sun and the moon; all [of them] in an orbit are swimming.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine order and precision in the creation of celestial bodies, emphasizing that each follows a predetermined path (orbit) in perfect harmony, reflecting Allah's absolute control and wisdom in the universe.

translation: And We did not grant to any man before you eternity [on earth]; so if you die, would they be the immortal ones?
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of death for all humans, including the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), and refutes the notion that anyone, even a prophet, can escape it. It serves as a reminder of human mortality and the transient nature of worldly life, directing attention to the eternal life of the Hereafter.

translation: Every soul will taste death. And We test you with evil and with good as trial; and to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of death for every human being, serving as a reminder of life's transient nature. The subsequent mention of trials through both hardship and ease highlights that these experiences are tests from Allah, designed to purify and refine the believer's faith and character. The ultimate return to Allah signifies that all deeds, whether in times of difficulty or prosperity, will be accounted for, emphasizing accountability and the transient nature of worldly life.

translation: And when those who disbelieve see you, [O Muhammad], they take you not except in ridicule, [saying], "Is this the one who mentions your gods?" And they are, at the mention of the Most Merciful, disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mockery and disbelief of the polytheists towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the message of monotheism he brought. It underscores their rejection of the truth, even when confronted with the remembrance of Allah, the Most Merciful, demonstrating their deep-seated arrogance and stubbornness in their disbelief.

translation: Man was created hasty. I will show you My signs, so do not impatiently demand them.
interpretation: This verse cautions against human impatience and emphasizes the importance of trust in Allah's timing, reminding us that divine wisdom unfolds in its own perfect measure.

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of those who deny the truth, challenging believers to hasten the fulfillment of divine promises or warnings, thereby testing their faith and resolve.

translation: If only those who disbelieve could know the time when they will not be able to ward off the Fire from their faces, nor from their backs, and they will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse underscores the helplessness and despair of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that their disbelief will leave them utterly powerless against divine punishment, with no refuge or intercession to save them.

translation: Nay, it will come upon them suddenly and stupefy them, and they will not be able to ward it off, nor will they have any respite.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability and suddenness of divine retribution or the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that it will catch people unprepared, leaving them powerless to resist or delay it, highlighting the absolute sovereignty and finality of God's decree.

translation: And indeed, messengers before you were ridiculed, but those who mocked them were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning that mockery of divine messengers and their messages will ultimately lead to divine retribution, demonstrating the consequences of arrogance and disbelief in the face of truth.

translation: Say, 'Who can protect you by night and day from the Most Merciful?' Yet they turn away from the remembrance of their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of relying on anything or anyone other than Allah for protection and sustenance, as He alone is the ultimate Guardian (Al-Hafeez). The mention of 'night and day' emphasizes His constant and unceasing care over His creation. The second part underscores the ingratitude and heedlessness of those who reject or ignore the remembrance of Allah, despite His continuous blessings and protection.

translation: Or do they have gods other than Us that can protect them? They cannot help themselves, nor can they be defended against Us.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah, emphasizing that no other deity or power can provide protection or assistance against His will. It refutes the notion of associating partners with Allah, as such false gods are utterly powerless to defend themselves, let alone their worshippers, and are entirely dependent on Allah's decree.

translation: Nay, We gave these and their fathers enjoyment until life grew long for them. Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its edges? Is it they who will prevail?
interpretation: This verse critiques the arrogance of those who deny divine truth despite witnessing the signs of Allah’s power in the natural world, such as the gradual decline of their lands, which symbolizes the inevitability of divine judgment and the transient nature of worldly dominance.

translation: Say, 'I only warn you by revelation.' But the deaf do not hear the call when they are warned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the limited efficacy of warnings when the recipients are spiritually or intellectually deaf—unable or unwilling to perceive the truth even when it is presented to them clearly.

translation: And if a breath of your Lord's punishment touches them, they will surely say, 'Woe to us! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the delayed realization of wrongdoing by those who persist in injustice, emphasizing that acknowledgment of error comes only when punishment is imminent, underscoring the futility of repentance at the last moment.

translation: And We place the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, so no soul will be treated unjustly at all. And if there should be the weight of a mustard seed of good, We will bring it forth. And sufficient are We as accountants.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where every individual's deeds, no matter how small, will be weighed with perfect accuracy, ensuring no injustice occurs in the reckoning.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses and Aaron the criterion [i.e., the Torah] and a light and a reminder for the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon the prophets Moses and Aaron (peace be upon them) by granting them the Torah as a source of guidance, light to illuminate the truth, and a reminder for those who strive to be conscious of Allah and live righteously.

translation: Those who fear their Lord unseen and are apprehensive of the Hour.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound consciousness of God (taqwa) in the hearts of the believers, even when no one else is watching, and their deep awareness of the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, which instills in them a sense of urgency and reverence in their actions and devotion.

translation: And this is a blessed Reminder which We have sent down: will you then deny it?
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and sanctity of the Qur'an, challenging those who reject its truth to reconsider their stance, as it is a source of guidance and blessing.

translation: And We had already given Abraham his guidance before, and We were fully aware of him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine recognition of Prophet Ibrahim's (Abraham) righteousness and guidance, emphasizing that Allah's knowledge of His servants is comprehensive and precedes their actions, reflecting His wisdom in selecting and guiding prophets.

translation: When he said to his father and his people, 'What are these statues to which you are devoted?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophetic tradition of questioning falsehood and idolatry, even within one's own family, to guide them toward the truth and monotheism.

translation: They said, "We found our forefathers worshipping them."
interpretation: This verse reflects the tendency of people to follow inherited traditions blindly, even when those traditions lead to deviation from the truth. It highlights the human inclination to cling to ancestral practices without questioning their validity, which can result in misguidance if those practices contradict divine guidance.

translation: He said, "Indeed, you and your forefathers have been in manifest error."
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of deviation from the truth, emphasizing that error can persist across generations if not corrected by divine guidance. It serves as a warning against blindly following ancestral traditions that contradict the path of righteousness.

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us with the truth, or are you one of the jesters?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and mockery of those who refuse to accept the truth when it challenges their beliefs or lifestyles, often dismissing it as mere amusement or deception rather than acknowledging its divine origin.

translation: Nay, but [say], "My Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, Who originated them, and I am a witness to this [truth]."
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness and supremacy of Allah as the Creator and Sustainer of the heavens and the earth, rejecting any association of partners with Him, while affirming the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a witness to this fundamental truth.

translation: And by Allah, I will surely plan against your idols after you turn and leave.
interpretation: This verse reflects the determination of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) to dismantle the false deities worshipped by his people, symbolizing the rejection of idolatry and the affirmation of monotheism (Tawhid). It underscores the courage to confront falsehood and the steadfastness in upholding truth, even in the face of opposition.

translation: So he made them into fragments except a great one for them, that they might return to it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth despite clear signs, as they refuse to acknowledge the power and oneness of Allah even when confronted with undeniable evidence.

translation: They said, 'Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the immediate reaction of disbelief and accusation when faced with the destruction of their idols, revealing their deep attachment to false deities and their quickness to blame others without evidence, highlighting the contrast between their ignorance and the truth they refuse to acknowledge.

translation: They said, "We heard a young man talking about them, called Ibrāhīm (Abraham)."
interpretation: This verse highlights the initial reaction of the people to the message of Prophet Ibrāhīm (Abraham), emphasizing their acknowledgment of his call to monotheism, even if they later rejected it.

translation: They said, 'Bring him before the eyes of the people, that they may witness [it].'
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and defiance of those who reject the truth, demanding a public spectacle to witness what they believe will be their triumph over the divine message, rather than seeking sincere reflection or guidance.

translation: They said, 'Is it you who has done this to our gods, O Abraham?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the confrontation between Prophet Ibrahim (AS) and his people after he destroyed their idols, challenging their false beliefs and exposing the powerlessness of their deities.

translation: Nay, but this was their chief who did it; so ask them, if they can speak.
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to acknowledge the absurdity of their idols by pointing out that their greatest idol—the one they revere most—was incapable of speaking or acting, thus exposing the futility of worshiping inanimate objects.

translation: Then they turned to themselves and said, 'Indeed, it is you who are the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of self-realization and accountability, where individuals recognize their own wrongdoing after initially blaming others or external factors. It underscores the moral and spiritual awakening that comes from introspection, leading to an acknowledgment of personal responsibility for one's actions.

translation: Then they turned back with their heads lowered; indeed, you knew what they were saying.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who outwardly appear to submit but inwardly harbor disbelief, as their actions and hidden intentions contradict their apparent compliance.

translation: Do you worship besides Allah what neither benefits you in anything nor harms you?
interpretation: This verse challenges the practice of worshipping idols or anything other than Allah, emphasizing the futility of such worship since these objects cannot provide any benefit or cause any harm, highlighting the absolute power and uniqueness of Allah in creation and sustenance.

translation: Woe to you and woe to what you worship besides Allah! Do you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse conveys a strong rebuke to those who associate partners with Allah, emphasizing the futility and misguidance of worshipping false deities. It underscores the importance of reason and intellect in recognizing the oneness of Allah, as true understanding should lead one to reject idolatry and submit to the truth.

translation: They said, "Burn him and support your gods if you are going to do anything!"
interpretation: This verse reflects the desperation and irrationality of those who oppose divine truth, resorting to destruction and violence rather than engaging in reasoned discourse or acknowledging the futility of their false deities.

translation: We said, 'O fire, be coolness and safety upon Abraham.'
interpretation: This verse demonstrates the miraculous intervention of Allah in protecting His prophets, where the natural laws were temporarily suspended to preserve the sanctity of His chosen servant, Ibrahim (AS). It also signifies that divine power can override physical laws when necessary for a higher purpose, reflecting Allah's absolute control over all creation.

translation: And they intended to harm him, so We made them the greatest losers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate failure of those who plot against the truth and the righteous, emphasizing that divine justice will prevail over all schemes, no matter how cunning they may be.

translation: And We delivered him [Lot] and Lot to the land which We had blessed for all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mercy and justice in delivering the righteous (Lot and his followers) while punishing the wrongdoers, demonstrating that guidance and salvation are granted to those who uphold moral integrity, even in the face of societal corruption.

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob as a gift, and each We made righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor of granting offspring to the prophets, emphasizing that their progeny were not only blessed with worldly existence but also endowed with righteousness, a testament to Allah's mercy and the fulfillment of His promises to the righteous.

translation: And We made them leaders guiding by Our command, and We inspired to them the doing of good deeds, and the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah; and they were to Us worshippers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine appointment of certain individuals as leaders who guide others according to God's command, emphasizing their role in promoting righteous deeds, maintaining religious observances, and fostering sincere worship, all of which reflect their unwavering devotion and submission to God.

translation: And to Lot We gave judgment and knowledge, and We saved him from the town that was committing evil deeds. Indeed, they were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine grace of bestowing wisdom and discernment upon Prophet Lot (peace be upon him), while also emphasizing the moral corruption of his people, who were deeply entrenched in sinful and transgressive behavior. It underscores the importance of divine guidance in navigating moral decay and the necessity of divine intervention to protect the righteous from societal corruption.

translation: And We admitted him into Our mercy. Indeed, he was of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine reward for those who strive to live righteously, emphasizing that righteousness is the key to attaining Allah's mercy and favor.

translation: And [mention] Noah, when he called [to Us] before [the others], so We responded to him and saved him and his family from the great affliction.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of sincere supplication (du'a) and divine responsiveness, highlighting that Allah answers the prayers of those who call upon Him with true devotion, even if the supplicant is alone in their faith or facing immense hardship.

translation: And We delivered him and those with him, from the people who denied Our signs. Indeed, they were a people of evil, so We drowned them all.
interpretation: This verse underscores divine justice and mercy, where those who persistently reject truth and engage in wickedness face consequences, while the righteous are saved. It highlights the balance between divine punishment for the corrupt and salvation for the faithful, emphasizing that divine intervention is both just and merciful.

translation: And [mention] David and Solomon, when they judged concerning the field when the sheep of a people strayed into it at night, and We were witnesses to their judgment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the wisdom and justice of the prophets David and Solomon, demonstrating that divine guidance enables even the most complex disputes to be resolved with fairness, and underscores the importance of divine oversight in matters of judgment.

translation: And We caused the understanding of it to reach Solomon, and to each [of them] We gave judgment and knowledge. And We subjected the mountains and the birds to exalt [Allah] with David, and We were, of course, the doers [of all things].
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine favor granted to Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him) in understanding the speech of birds and other creatures, highlighting the unique wisdom and knowledge bestowed upon him. It also emphasizes Allah's absolute power to subject nature—mountains and birds—to the service of His prophets, demonstrating that all creation submits to His will, reinforcing the concept of divine omnipotence and the subservience of the natural world to Allah's command.

translation: And We taught him the craft of making garments for you, to protect you from your violence. So, will you be grateful?
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine gift of knowledge and skill, in this case, the art of crafting protective armor, which serves as a means of safeguarding against harm. It underscores the importance of recognizing and appreciating the blessings bestowed upon humanity, urging reflection on the source of such abilities and the responsibility to express gratitude for them.

translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind, blowing forcefully, proceeding by his command toward the land which We had blessed. And We are ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute control over natural phenomena, demonstrating His omnipotence by subjecting the wind to Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him) as a sign of divine favor and wisdom. It also underscores the concept of divine knowledge ('kullu shay'in 'alīmun'), affirming that Allah's command encompasses all things, even those beyond human perception or control.

translation: And [also] from the devils were those who dived for him [Solomon] and did work other than that. And We were, for them, observers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extent of Solomon's (peace be upon him) dominion and the subjugation of even the jinn (supernatural beings) to his will, as a sign of Allah's favor. It also underscores Allah's omniscience and control over all creation, including the unseen, as He was a watchful guardian over the devils, ensuring they did not exceed their bounds or harm anyone.

translation: And [mention] Job, when he called to his Lord, 'Indeed, adversity has touched me, and You are the Most Merciful of the merciful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the depth of Prophet Job's (Ayyub) faith and trust in Allah's mercy, even in the face of immense suffering. It teaches that sincere supplication to Allah, coupled with patience and unwavering belief in His compassion, is a powerful form of worship and a means to seek relief from hardship.

translation: So We answered his prayer, lifted the suffering that afflicted him, restored his family to him and gave them twice as many—all as a mercy from Us and a lesson for the worshippers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine response to sincere supplication and the restoration of blessings as a test of gratitude and remembrance of Allah, demonstrating that trials are followed by relief when one turns to Allah in faith and patience.

translation: And [mention] Ishmael, Enoch, and Dhul-Kifl—all were of the patient ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of patience as a shared trait among multiple Prophets, emphasizing that steadfastness in faith and perseverance through trials is a mark of divine favor and a path to righteousness.

translation: And We admitted them into Our mercy. Indeed, they were of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward of the righteous—entry into Allah’s mercy, which encompasses Paradise and divine favor, underscoring that their righteousness in this life was the key to their eternal salvation.

translation: And [mention] the man of the fish (Jonah), when he went off in anger and thought that We would not restrict him. Then he called out in the darknesses, 'There is no deity except You; You are far exalted above all imperfections. Indeed, I have been among the wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the humility and repentance of Prophet Jonah (peace be upon him) when he realized his mistake in abandoning his mission out of frustration. It teaches that even the righteous can falter, but sincere repentance and turning back to Allah in humility are always accepted, regardless of the depth of one's error.

translation: So We answered him and saved him from the distress. And thus do We save the believers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine principle that Allah responds to the sincere supplications of those who turn to Him in times of hardship, particularly the believers who maintain faith and trust in His mercy and justice.

translation: And [mention] when Zechariah called upon his Lord, saying, 'My Lord, do not leave me alone [with no heir], while You are the best of inheritors.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound humility and trust in Allah's decree, where Zechariah, despite his old age and barren wife, turns to Allah in supplication, acknowledging Allah's ultimate power over inheritance and progeny, and placing his hope entirely in Allah's wisdom and mercy.

translation: So We answered his prayer, granted him Yahya (John), and cured his wife (Sarah) of barrenness. Indeed, they used to vie with one another in good deeds, call upon Us with hope and fear, and were humble before Us.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine response to sincere supplication and the virtue of steadfastness in faith, demonstrating that Allah rewards those who persistently strive for righteousness with both spiritual and worldly blessings. It also underscores the importance of balancing hope and fear in worship, as well as humility in one's relationship with Allah.

translation: And [We blessed] her who guarded her chastity, so We breathed into her of Our spirit, and made her and her son a sign for all worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine intervention and sanctity bestowed upon Maryam (Mary), emphasizing her purity and the miraculous birth of Isa (Jesus), which serves as a profound sign of Allah's power and mercy across all creation.

translation: Indeed, this your community is one community, and I am your Lord, so worship Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the human community under the worship of one God, rejecting polytheism and affirming the exclusive right of Allah to be worshipped.

translation: And they divided their affair among themselves, [but] all to Us they will return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of human division and disunity in matters of faith and guidance, emphasizing that despite their disagreements, all will ultimately return to Allah for judgment, underscoring the accountability of every individual for their choices.

translation: But whoever does righteous deeds, while he is a believer—indeed, We will not allow to be lost the reward of one who does good, and indeed, We are recording it for him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of divine reward for righteous actions performed with true faith, highlighting Allah's justice and the meticulous recording of deeds, which serves as both a motivation for believers and a reminder of accountability.

translation: And it is forbidden upon a town which We have destroyed that they should return.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality of divine punishment for a people who persistently reject guidance and transgress against Allah's commandments. Once a community is destroyed due to its defiance and corruption, it is decreed by Allah that they will not be resurrected in this worldly form again, serving as a warning against similar transgressions in other times or places.

translation: Until, when [the dam of] Gog and Magog is opened, and they, from every elevated place, descend rapidly.
interpretation: This verse signifies a pivotal moment in the end times when the barriers holding back the destructive forces of Gog and Magog are removed, allowing them to spread across the earth with unprecedented speed and force, signaling widespread chaos and trial.

translation: And the true promise drew near. Then the eyes of those who disbelieved will be fixed [in horror], [saying], "O woe to us! We had been in neglect of this; rather, we were wrongdoers."
interpretation: This verse underscores the sudden and overwhelming realization of the truth at the time of judgment, when the consequences of disbelief and injustice become undeniable, leading to despair and self-condemnation.

translation: Indeed, you [disbelievers] and whatever you worship other than Allah are fuel for Hell. You will all enter it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and the futility of worshipping anything besides Him. It warns that all forms of idolatry—whether in the form of false deities, material objects, or even misplaced devotion—will lead to damnation in Hell. The verse also implies that those who associate partners with Allah share the same fate as their misguided objects of worship, emphasizing the severity of shirk (associating partners with Allah).

translation: If these (beings and objects) were gods besides Him, they would not have come to them. And all are abiding eternally therein.
interpretation: This verse refutes the polytheistic belief that deities other than Allah exist. It argues that if there were multiple gods, they would have come to each other's realms, implying a lack of divine order and hierarchy. The mention of all beings abiding eternally in their respective places underscores the unity of Allah's dominion and the impossibility of multiple independent deities coexisting.

translation: For them in it is a gasping breath, and they will not hear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the finality and utter helplessness of the inhabitants of Hell (Jahannam). The 'gasping breath' signifies their extreme suffering and agony, while their inability to hear underscores their complete isolation from any mercy or hope, emphasizing the irreversible nature of their punishment.

translation: Indeed, those for whom the best [reward] has already been decreed from Us will be removed far from it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice and mercy of Allah, indicating that those who are already destined for Paradise will not be subjected to the trials of the Hereafter, as they are already secured in their eternal reward.

translation: They will not hear its slightest sound, and they will abide forever in what their souls desire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute tranquility and eternal bliss of the inhabitants of Paradise, where even the faintest disturbance is absent, and their desires are perpetually fulfilled without end.

translation: They will not be grieved by the greatest terror, and the angels will receive them, [saying], "This is your Day which you were promised."
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that on the Day of Judgment, they will not be overwhelmed by the greatest fear or terror, as they will be greeted by angels with the glad tidings of their promised Day, signifying divine mercy and protection for the righteous.

translation: The Day We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] scroll for the records. As We began the first creation, We will bring it back. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and control of Allah over all creation, highlighting the inevitability of the Day of Judgment. It underscores the promise of resurrection and accountability, reassuring believers that Allah’s decrees are certain and will be fulfilled, as He has the power to recreate and recompense all deeds.

translation: And We have already written in the Zabur [Psalms] after the [previous] mention that My righteous servants will inherit the earth.
interpretation: This verse signifies that divine justice will ultimately prevail, and those who remain steadfast in faith and righteousness will be granted authority and dominion over the earth, replacing oppressive and corrupt systems.

translation: Indeed, in this is a message for people who worship [Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Qur'an's guidance and lessons are specifically intended for those who are sincere in their worship and devotion to Allah, implying that true understanding and benefit come to those with a heart inclined toward submission and faith.

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the universal and benevolent purpose of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) mission, emphasizing that his guidance and teachings are intended to bring mercy, guidance, and spiritual upliftment to all of humanity and creation, transcending boundaries of race, culture, or time.

translation: Say, 'It has been revealed to me that your god is but one God. So will you submit [to Him]?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of God (Tawheed) and calls upon humanity to recognize and submit to this fundamental truth, rejecting any form of polytheism or association of partners with Allah.

translation: But if they turn away, then say, 'I have announced to you all alike. And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of clear communication and fairness in conveying the message of Islam, regardless of the response. It also highlights the uncertainty of the timing of divine promises or warnings, reminding the believer that ultimate knowledge rests with Allah alone.

translation: He knows what is declared of speech, and He knows what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute knowledge of Allah, which encompasses not only our outward actions and words but also our innermost thoughts and hidden intentions, reminding us of the necessity for sincerity and mindfulness in all aspects of our lives.

translation: And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and a enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse suggests that certain events or circumstances may serve as tests or trials for believers, testing their faith and patience, while also providing temporary worldly benefits or enjoyment for a limited period.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, judge [between us] in truth. And our Lord is the Most Merciful, the one sought for help against what you describe.'
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea for divine justice and mercy in the face of false accusations or oppression, invoking Allah's attributes of justice ('al-Haqq') and mercy ('ar-Rahman'), while seeking His protection from the harm caused by others' false claims.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. O mankind, fear your Lord. Indeed, the earthquake of the Hour is a tremendous thing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of the transient nature of worldly life and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the need for constant mindfulness of Allah and righteous conduct to prepare for the ultimate accountability.

translation: The Day you see it, every nursing mother will forget her nursling, and every pregnant woman will drop her load, and you will see the people drunk, but they are not drunk—rather, the punishment of Allah is severe.
interpretation: This verse describes the overwhelming shock and disorientation of the Day of Judgment, where the intensity of the event will be so profound that natural human instincts and states—such as a mother’s care for her child or the state of pregnancy—will be completely overshadowed by the sheer magnitude of the event. The mention of people appearing 'drunk' but not actually being so symbolizes the confusion and bewilderment that will engulf humanity, highlighting that the true source of their state is not intoxication but the terrifying reality of divine retribution.

translation: And among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge and follows every rebellious devil.
interpretation: This verse highlights the danger of engaging in baseless arguments about Allah, which stems from ignorance and leads to following the whispers of Satan, who incites misguidance and rebellion against divine truth.

translation: Upon him it is written that whoever takes him as a protector, he will surely mislead him and guide him to the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan (or evil influences) in leading people astray from the path of truth and righteousness, ultimately leading them to severe punishment.

translation: O mankind, if you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then indeed We created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then from a clinging clot, then from a lump of flesh, formed and unformed - that We may show you. And We settle in the wombs whom We will for a specified term, then We bring you out as a child, then [We develop you] that you may reach your [time of] maturity. And among you is he who is taken in [early] death, and among you is he who is returned to the most decrepit [old] age so that he knows, after [once having] knowledge, nothing. And you see the earth barren, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and swells and grows of every beautiful kind.
interpretation: This verse addresses human skepticism about the Day of Resurrection by tracing the stages of human creation—from dust to embryo—highlighting Allah’s power to bring life from the lifeless. It underscores the transient nature of life, where some die young while others live to extreme old age, losing their faculties, thus emphasizing the inevitability of divine accountability. The barren earth’s revival with rain symbolizes Allah’s ability to resurrect the dead, reinforcing the certainty of the Hereafter.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and because He gives life to the dead, and because He has power over all things.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truthfulness of Allah, His power to resurrect the dead, and His supreme authority over all creation, reinforcing the believer's trust in divine justice and the inevitability of resurrection and accountability.

translation: And the Hour is coming—no doubt about it—and Allah will resurrect those in the graves.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the resurrection of all beings, emphasizing divine justice and accountability, where every individual will be recompensed according to their deeds.

translation: And among the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and arrogance of disputing about Allah without proper knowledge, guidance, or divine revelation, emphasizing the importance of seeking truth through authentic sources rather than baseless arguments.

translation: He seeks to lead astray from the way of Allah, for him is disgrace in this world, and We will make him taste on the Day of Resurrection the punishment of the burning fire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility and ultimate downfall of those who actively oppose or misguide others from the path of truth and divine guidance, emphasizing that their efforts will not only fail but will also bring them humiliation in this life and severe punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: This is because of what your own hands have sent forth, and verily, Allah is not unjust to His servants.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of personal accountability, emphasizing that individuals are responsible for their own actions and will face consequences that are just and fair, as Allah does not wrong anyone.

translation: And among the people is he who worships Allah on an edge. If good befalls him, he is satisfied thereby; but if a trial befalls him, he turns back on his face [to disbelief], losing [this] world and the Hereafter. That is the manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fragility of faith when it is not deeply rooted in sincerity and conviction. It warns against a superficial or conditional worship that depends on external circumstances—such as prosperity or ease—rather than being steadfast in devotion regardless of life's trials. True faith is tested in adversity, and those who abandon their beliefs when faced with hardship demonstrate a loss that extends beyond the temporal world into the eternal Hereafter.

translation: He calls upon, besides Allah, such as can neither harm nor benefit him. That is the farthest straying.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of invoking or worshiping anything other than Allah, as such entities lack the power to cause harm or provide benefit. It highlights the depth of misguidance in associating partners with Allah, as true harm and benefit lie solely in His hands.

translation: He calls [one] to whom harm is closer than benefit. Wretched is the ally and wretched is the companion.
interpretation: This verse warns against forming alliances or seeking help from those whose influence is more harmful than beneficial, emphasizing the importance of choosing righteous companions and allies who guide one toward goodness rather than destruction.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. Allah does what He intends.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine justice and mercy of Allah, emphasizing that true faith must be accompanied by righteous actions, and that Allah's will is sovereign in granting Paradise to those who meet His criteria.

translation: Whoever thinks that Allah will never help him in this world and the Hereafter, let him extend a rope to the sky, then cut it, and let him see whether his plan removes what angers him.
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance and disbelief of those who doubt Allah's power and support, urging them to reflect on the futility of their schemes when compared to Allah's ultimate control over all affairs.

translation: And thus We have sent it down as clear verses. And Allah guides whom He wills.
interpretation: This verse underscores the clarity and evident nature of the Qur'anic revelations, emphasizing that divine guidance is bestowed upon whom Allah intends, highlighting both the accessibility of truth and the sovereignty of Allah's will in granting spiritual guidance.

translation: Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews, the Sabians, the Christians, the Magians, and those who associated others with Allah - Allah will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, Allah is, over all things, Witness.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and accountability, affirming that Allah will judge all people fairly on the Day of Resurrection, regardless of their religious affiliation or beliefs in this world. It rejects any notion of partiality or favoritism in Allah's judgment, emphasizing that all actions and intentions will be weighed with absolute justice.

translation: Do you not see that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is in the earth, the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the moving creatures and many of mankind? But upon many the punishment is justified. And he whom Allah humiliates - for him there is no bestower of honor. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, demonstrating that even inanimate entities and celestial bodies submit to His will through their inherent nature. The mention of 'many of mankind' prostrating highlights the voluntary submission of believers, while 'many upon whom the punishment is justified' refers to those who reject this submission, facing divine justice. The final clause reaffirms that Allah’s actions are unconstrained by any external force, emphasizing His omnipotence and the futility of opposing His will.

translation: These are two adversaries who have disputed concerning their Lord. But those who disbelieved will have garments of fire cut out for them, and boiling water will be poured over their heads.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the believers and the disbelievers in their relationship with Allah. The 'two adversaries' symbolize the opposing paths of faith and disbelief, where the latter leads to severe punishment—symbolized by garments of fire and boiling water—reflecting the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and divine justice.

translation: With it, He melts what is in their bellies and [their] skins.
interpretation: This verse describes the severe and excruciating pain that the disbelievers will endure in Hellfire, where their internal organs and skins will be melted by the scorching fire, emphasizing the unbearable torment awaiting them as a consequence of their disbelief and sins.

translation: And for them are iron maces.
interpretation: This verse describes a severe punishment for the wrongdoers in the Hereafter, where they will be struck with iron maces, symbolizing the intensity and unbearable nature of their torment.

translation: Whenever they try to escape from it in distress, they will be returned to it, and it will be said to them: 'Taste the punishment of the Fire!',
interpretation: This verse underscores the inescapable and eternal nature of the punishment for those who reject faith, emphasizing that their attempts to flee from the torment of Hell will be futile, and they will be repeatedly subjected to its agony as a definitive consequence of their disbelief.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for believers who combine faith with righteous actions, emphasizing both material and spiritual blessings in Paradise, where their adornments and attire reflect divine generosity and honor.

translation: And they have been guided to the good and pure speech, and guided to the path of the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine guidance that leads people to both righteous speech and the right path—indicating that true guidance encompasses both moral conduct in words and righteous action in deeds, culminating in the ultimate praise of Allah.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [people] from the way of Allah and from al-Masjid al-Haram, which We made for the people - both the resident and the traveler - and whoever intends therein [to cause] harm unjustly, We will make him taste of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of obstructing others from the path of truth and faith, particularly in the sacred precincts of the Ka'bah, which is a universal place of worship. It warns that deliberate harm or deviation from divine guidance within this sacred space will incur severe divine retribution, emphasizing the sanctity of both faith and its symbols.

translation: And [mention] when We positioned the House for Abraham, [saying], "Do not associate anything with Me and purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who stand [in prayer] and those who bow and prostrate."
interpretation: This verse underscores the monotheistic foundation of the Ka'bah, emphasizing absolute devotion to Allah alone and the sanctity of the House as a place of pure worship, free from any association of partners or idols, while also highlighting the diverse forms of worship performed there.

translation: And proclaim to the people the Hajj [pilgrimage]; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel; they will come from every distant pass
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal call to Hajj, highlighting its obligatory nature for all capable Muslims, regardless of their physical or geographical limitations, underscoring the unity and equality of believers in their submission to Allah.

translation: That they may witness benefits for themselves and mention the name of Allah on known days over what He has provided for them of [sacrificial] animals. So eat of them and feed the miserable and the poor.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the communal and spiritual benefits of the Hajj pilgrimage, where believers witness the blessings of Allah and engage in acts of worship, including the sacrifice of livestock. The instruction to eat from the sacrifice and feed the poor highlights the concept of sharing blessings with those in need, reinforcing social welfare and gratitude to Allah for His provisions.

translation: Then let them complete their prescribed duties, fulfill their vows, and perform Tawaf around the ancient House (the Ka'bah).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the completion of religious rites with sincerity and devotion, highlighting the importance of fulfilling one's obligations to Allah, whether through acts of worship like Tawaf or personal vows made during Hajj or Umrah.

translation: That [is so]. And whoever honors the sacred ordinances of Allah - it is best for him in the sight of his Lord. And lawful to you are the grazing livestock, except what is recited to you [as unlawful], so avoid the uncleanness of idols and avoid false speech.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting and upholding the sanctities ordained by Allah, as doing so is a means of attaining goodness in the sight of Allah. It also highlights the distinction between what is lawfully permitted (such as grazing livestock) and what has been explicitly prohibited, urging believers to steer clear of idolatrous practices and dishonest speech, which are spiritually and morally corrupting.

translation: Being upright for Allah, not associating anything with Him. And whoever associates others with Allah - it is as if he had fallen from the sky and was snatched by the birds or the wind carried him down to a far-off place.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and warns against associating partners with Him. The vivid imagery of falling from the sky and being snatched by birds or carried away by the wind to a distant place symbolizes the spiritual peril of shirk (associating partners with Allah). It implies that those who commit shirk are spiritually lost, disconnected from divine guidance, and in a state of extreme vulnerability and ruin, akin to a helpless fall from a great height.

translation: That [is so]. And whoever honors the symbols of Allah - indeed, it is from the piety of hearts.
interpretation: This verse underscores that reverence for the symbols of Allah, such as rituals, sacred places, and rites of worship, is a manifestation of the deep-rooted piety and sincerity within a person's heart, reflecting their true devotion and consciousness of Allah.

translation: For you in them [the sacrificial animals] are benefits until a specified time, then their place of sacrifice is to the Ancient House [the Ka'bah].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the temporary worldly benefits of sacrificial animals, such as their meat, milk, and wool, which are permitted for human use until a predetermined time, after which their primary purpose shifts to being sacrificed and dedicated to Allah at the Ka'bah in Makkah. It underscores the balance between permissible worldly enjoyment and the ultimate act of worship and devotion.

translation: And for every community, We have appointed a rite of sacrifice that they may mention the Name of Allah over what He has provided for them of [sacrificial] animals from the grazing livestock. So your god is one God; therefore to Him submit [in Islam]. And give good tidings to the humble [before their Lord],
interpretation: This verse underscores the universality of divine worship, emphasizing that all communities have been guided to a form of ritual sacrifice as a means of acknowledging Allah's blessings and affirming His oneness. The mention of 'one God' reinforces the absolute monotheism (Tawhid) central to Islam, rejecting any form of idolatry or association of partners with Allah. The call to submit to Him is a reminder of the core Islamic principle of surrender to Allah's will. The reference to the 'humble' highlights the virtue of humility in worship, suggesting that true submission is marked by a heartfelt recognition of Allah's supremacy and a sincere, unpretentious devotion to Him.

translation: Those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble with fear, and [who] endure what afflicts them with patience, and who establish prayer, and who spend from what We have provided for them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of the truly righteous believers, emphasizing their deep reverence for Allah, patience in adversity, commitment to worship, and generosity in charity, reflecting a holistic submission to divine will.

translation: And the sacrificial animals We have made for you as among the symbols of Allah; therein you have goodness. So mention the name of Allah upon them as they stand in line (for sacrifice). Then, when they collapse on their sides, eat from them and feed the content one and the supplicant. Thus We have subjected them to you so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the act of sacrifice as an expression of gratitude and devotion to Allah, highlighting the ethical and communal dimensions of sharing the meat with both those who are content with what they receive and those who ask for it, thereby fostering social welfare and thankfulness.

translation: Never does Allah receive [as sacrifice] from it [the animal's] meat or blood, but rather He receives from you the fear of Him. Thus has He subjected them to you so that you may proclaim Allah's greatness for His guidance to you, and give glad tidings to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse underscores that the true essence of sacrifice is not the physical offering of meat or blood, but the spiritual devotion and piety (taqwa) that accompanies it. It reminds believers that Allah is not in need of their sacrifices but seeks their sincere submission and gratitude for the guidance He has provided.

translation: Indeed, Allah defends those who have believed. Indeed, Allah does not like every treacherous and ungrateful person.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's protection and support for believers who remain steadfast in their faith, while also highlighting the divine disapproval of those who betray their trust and are ungrateful, emphasizing the moral and ethical standards that Allah upholds.

translation: Permission [to fight] has been given to those who are being fought, because they were wronged. And indeed, Allah is competent to give them victory.
interpretation: This verse establishes the moral and legal justification for defensive warfare in Islam, emphasizing that those who are oppressed have the right to resist and seek justice, and that divine support is guaranteed for the righteous cause.

translation: Those who were expelled from their homes without right—only because they said, "Our Lord is Allah." And if not for Allah's repelling [some] people by means of others, destroyed would have been monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned. And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine principle of protecting religious freedom and the sanctity of places of worship, even in the face of persecution. It highlights that Allah's intervention in human affairs often manifests through the actions of people who uphold justice and defend the oppressed. The verse also emphasizes the reciprocal relationship between Allah and believers: those who stand for Allah’s cause will find divine support, reflecting the theme of divine justice and the preservation of faith.

translation: Those who, if We give them authority in the land, establish prayer, give zakah, enjoin what is right and forbid what is wrong. And to Allah belongs the outcome of [all] matters.
interpretation: This verse highlights the responsibilities of those entrusted with power and authority in society. It emphasizes that true leadership is not merely about control but about establishing justice, practicing charity, and promoting moral and ethical behavior. It underscores the importance of collective responsibility in upholding righteousness and combating wrongdoing, reminding that all actions ultimately return to Allah, who is the final arbiter of justice and outcomes.

translation: And if they deny you, then already before them denied the people of Noah, and 'Aad, and Thamud.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that the rejection of divine messengers is not a new phenomenon; rather, it is a recurring pattern throughout history where previous nations also denied their prophets, leading to their eventual destruction as a consequence of their disbelief and defiance.

translation: And the people of Ibrahim and the people of Lut.
interpretation: This verse highlights the historical significance of the prophets Ibrahim (Abraham) and Lut (Lot), emphasizing their missions to their respective communities. It serves as a reminder of divine justice, where the people who rejected their messages faced severe consequences, underscoring the importance of heeding divine guidance and the consequences of disbelief and disobedience.

translation: And the people of Madyan (Midian) denied (the messengers). And Moses denied (was rejected by Pharaoh and his people), so I granted respite to the disbelievers; then I seized them, and how (severe) was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance and the temporary nature of worldly respite granted to the disbelievers, which ultimately leads to severe punishment as a manifestation of divine justice.

translation: How many a city We have destroyed while it was unjust, so it lies in ruins, with abandoned wells and lofty palaces!
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning about the consequences of oppression and injustice, illustrating that no civilization, no matter how grand or fortified, is immune to divine retribution if it persists in wrongdoing. The imagery of ruined cities—empty wells and deserted palaces—symbolizes the irreversible collapse of societal structures built on tyranny, emphasizing that material power and wealth are fleeting when divorced from moral and ethical integrity.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land so that they may have hearts with which to reason, or ears with which to hear? Indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but it is the hearts within the chests that grow blind.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of reflection and active engagement with the signs of God in the world. It criticizes those who do not use their intellect or spiritual faculties to recognize the truth, emphasizing that true blindness is not physical but a willful refusal to perceive and understand the divine guidance present in creation and revelation.

translation: And they urge you to hasten the punishment. But Allah will never fail in His promise. And indeed, a Day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the relativity of time in the sight of Allah, contrasting human impatience with the absolute certainty of divine timing.

translation: And how many a city have I given respite to while it was wrongdoing, then I seized it; and to Me is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse underscores the temporary nature of worldly power and prosperity, warning that divine punishment is inevitable for those who persist in oppression and injustice, regardless of their temporal success.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the prophetic role of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger sent to warn humanity of the consequences of their actions, guiding them toward righteousness and away from deviation, without imposing compulsion or forcing belief.

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds—for them is forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine principle that true faith is inseparable from righteous action, and that Allah’s mercy and sustenance are the reward for those who embody both, reflecting the Qur’an’s emphasis on the unity of belief and ethical conduct.

translation: But those who strive against Our verses to frustrate them—it is they who will have the punishment of the Blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences for those who actively oppose or seek to invalidate the divine signs and revelations of Allah, emphasizing that their defiance will lead them to the torment of Hellfire as a just retribution for their arrogance and rejection of truth.

translation: And We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he recited [his scripture], Satan threw into it [some misunderstanding] by his recitation; but Allah abolishes that which Satan throws in. Then Allah makes precise His verses. And Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's protection over His divine messages from any corruption or distortion, even when Satan attempts to interfere. It reassures that Allah's final word and verses are always preserved in their true form, demonstrating His ultimate wisdom and authority in safeguarding the purity of revelation.

translation: That He may make what Satan throws in a trial for those within whose hearts is disease and those hard of heart. And indeed, the wrongdoers are in extreme dissension.
interpretation: This verse highlights how Satan's whispers and deceptions serve as a test for those with weak faith or hardened hearts, exposing their inner vulnerabilities and leading them further into misguidance and conflict.

translation: And so that those who have been given knowledge may know that it is the truth from your Lord and believe in it, and their hearts humble themselves to Him. And indeed, Allah is the Guide of those who believe to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of knowledge and faith in recognizing divine truth, highlighting that true understanding leads to humility and submission to Allah. It also underscores Allah's guidance for believers, directing them to the straight path—a path of righteousness and unwavering faith.

translation: But those who disbelieve remain in doubt about it [the Qur'an] until the Hour comes upon them suddenly or there comes to them the punishment of a barren day.
interpretation: This verse underscores the persistent skepticism of the disbelievers toward the truth of the Qur'an and its divine origin, despite clear signs and warnings. Their doubt is so entrenched that they will only acknowledge its truth when it is too late—either at the sudden onset of the Day of Judgment or when they face an irreversible and decisive punishment, symbolized by 'a barren day' (a day devoid of mercy or hope). It highlights the futility of their denial in the face of divine inevitability.

translation: The dominion on that Day will be Allah's; He will judge between them. So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in gardens of pleasure.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where He alone will render final judgment between people based on their faith and deeds, emphasizing divine justice and the eternal reward for the righteous.

translation: But those who disbelieved and denied Our signs—it is they who will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences for those who reject faith outright and deny the divine signs (evidence of truth) presented to them. The 'humiliating punishment' implies not just physical torment but also the degradation of their status and dignity in the Hereafter, reflecting divine justice that aligns with their choice to reject truth.

translation: And those who emigrated for the sake of Allah and then were killed or died - Allah will surely provide for them a good provision. And indeed, it is Allah who is the best of providers.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that those who sacrifice their lives or homes for the sake of Allah will be rewarded abundantly in the Hereafter, emphasizing divine justice and the certainty of Allah's provision, as He is the best of providers.

translation: He will admit them to an entrance that they will be pleased with. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse assures believers that Allah will guide them to a state or place of ultimate satisfaction and contentment, reflecting His deep knowledge of their hearts and His forbearance in granting them what is best, even if they may not immediately recognize it as such.

translation: That [is what We have decreed]. And whoever retaliates with the like of what he was harmed with, and then is oppressed again, Allah will surely aid him. Indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of justice and divine support for those who endure oppression. It highlights that Allah aids those who respond to harm proportionally and then face further injustice, demonstrating that divine justice prevails over human transgressions. The mention of Allah being 'Pardoning and Forgiving' suggests that while justice is served, there is also room for mercy and forgiveness in the face of continued oppression.

translation: That is because Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, and Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute power and control over the natural cycles of time and light, demonstrating His sovereignty over all creation, while also emphasizing His awareness of all things, as He is the All-Hearing and All-Seeing.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute truth of Allah and the futility of idolatry, asserting that any deity other than Allah is baseless and devoid of reality. It also highlights Allah's supreme status and unmatched greatness, reinforcing the idea that true worship and reliance should be directed solely toward Him.

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the heavens, and the earth becomes green? Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power and wisdom in transforming the earth through rain, demonstrating His subtle yet profound control over all things, as well as His deep awareness of all creation's needs and states.

translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and self-sufficiency of Allah, emphasizing that all existence—whether in the heavens or on earth—is entirely under His dominion and control. The mention of Allah being 'the Free of need' (Al-Ghani) highlights His independence from all creation, while 'the Praiseworthy' (Al-Hameed) signifies that all praise and gratitude are ultimately directed to Him, as He is the source of all blessings and perfections.

translation: Do you not see that Allah has subjected to your use whatever is in the earth and the ships which sail through the sea by His command? And He holds the sky from falling to the earth unless by His permission. Indeed, Allah, to the people, is Kind and Merciful.
