interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute sovereignty over all creation, demonstrating His power and mercy by subjecting the earth and the heavens to human benefit while maintaining their order and stability—an order that reflects divine wisdom and care for humanity.

translation: And it is He who gave you life, then causes you to die, then will [again] give you life. Indeed, man is ungrateful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the cyclical nature of life and death, emphasizing Allah's absolute power over creation and resurrection, while also highlighting humanity's inherent tendency to deny or forget divine favors despite witnessing such profound signs.

translation: For every community We have appointed a whole system of worship they follow; so do not let them dispute with you in this matter. And invite [people] to your Lord. Indeed, you are on a straight guidance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universality of divine guidance, asserting that all communities have been given their own prescribed ways of worship, which are valid in their own contexts. It instructs the Prophet (peace be upon him) not to engage in disputes over differing religious practices but to remain steadfast in his own guidance, which is straight and true, and to continue inviting people to the worship of Allah alone.

translation: But if they argue with you, say, "Allah is most knowing of what you do."
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to respond to disputations with divine authority, emphasizing that ultimate knowledge and judgment belong to Allah alone, thereby discouraging reliance on human reasoning or opposition in matters of faith.

translation: Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which you used to differ.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority of Allah in resolving disputes and rendering final judgments on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that human disagreements in this world will ultimately be settled by divine justice.

translation: Do you not know that Allah knows what is in the heaven and the earth? Indeed, that is in a Book. Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute knowledge and awareness of all things, both in the heavens and the earth, which is recorded in the Preserved Book (al-Lawh al-Mahfooz). It serves as a reminder of Allah's omnipotence and the inevitability of His decree, emphasizing that nothing escapes His knowledge or control.

translation: And they worship besides Allah that for which He has not sent down any authority and that of which they have no knowledge. And there will not be for the wrongdoers any helper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility and ignorance of associating partners with Allah in worship, emphasizing that such practices lack any divine sanction or true understanding, while also affirming that the oppressors (those who commit shirk) will ultimately find no support or salvation on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, you will recognize in the faces of those who disbelieve denial. They almost assault those who recite Our verses to them. Say, 'Shall I inform you of [what is] worse than that?' The Fire—Allah has promised it to those who disbelieve—and wretched is the destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense hostility of the disbelievers toward the truth and its conveyors, illustrating their refusal to accept divine guidance despite its clarity, and underscores the severity of their punishment in the Hereafter as a consequence of their arrogance and rejection.

translation: O mankind, an example is presented, so listen to it. Indeed, those you invoke besides Allah will never create [as much as] a fly, even if they gathered together for that purpose. And if the fly should take away from them a [tiny] thing, they could not recover it from it. Weak indeed is the one who seeks and the one who is sought.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute incapacity of anything other than Allah to create, sustain, or even protect the smallest of things, highlighting the stark contrast between the Creator and the created. It serves as a profound reminder of Allah's unparalleled power and the futility of directing worship or reliance toward false deities, which are utterly powerless in comparison.

translation: They have not honored Allah with true honor. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
interpretation: This verse underscores the failure of humans to recognize Allah’s true greatness, power, and majesty, despite His absolute sovereignty and strength. It serves as a reminder of the limits of human perception and the necessity of humbling oneself before Allah’s unparalleled authority.

translation: Allah chooses from the angels messengers and from the people. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute sovereignty in selecting whom He wills for His divine missions, whether from the angels or among humans, emphasizing His comprehensive knowledge and awareness of all things.

translation: He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and to Allah all matters return.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's omniscience and absolute sovereignty over all things, emphasizing that nothing escapes His knowledge—past, present, or future—and that all affairs ultimately return to Him for final judgment and resolution.

translation: O you who have believed, bow, prostrate, and worship your Lord and do good - that you may succeed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of both outward acts of worship (such as prayer) and inward righteousness (such as doing good deeds), linking spiritual devotion to moral conduct as the path to true success in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And strive for Allah with the striving due to Him. He has chosen you and has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty. [It is] the religion of your father, Abraham. Allah named you 'Muslims' before [in former scriptures] and in this [Quran], that the Messenger may be a witness over you and you may be witnesses over the people. So establish prayer and give zakah and hold fast to Allah. He is your protector; and excellent is the protector, and excellent is the helper.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere devotion to Allah, highlighting that true faith is not burdensome but a path of ease and guidance. It underscores the continuity of monotheistic tradition from Abraham to the final revelation, affirming the role of Muslims as witnesses to truth in the world. The call to establish prayer, give charity, and hold fast to Allah reflects the practical expression of this devotion, ensuring a balanced life of worship, social responsibility, and reliance on divine support.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. There has certainly succeeded the believers.
interpretation: This verse introduces a declaration of success and triumph for the believers, emphasizing that true success is not merely material or worldly but is rooted in faith, righteousness, and adherence to divine guidance. It sets the tone for the subsequent verses, which elaborate on the qualities and actions that lead to this success.

translation: Those who are humble and submissive in their prayers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of true concentration and humility in prayer, emphasizing that it is not merely a ritualistic act but a profound act of devotion and submission to Allah, where the heart and mind are fully engaged.

translation: And those who turn away from ill speech
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of those who avoid engaging in vain or harmful talk, demonstrating their mindfulness of the purity of their speech and their commitment to meaningful and beneficial communication.

translation: And who are active in [paying] the zakah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of actively fulfilling one's religious obligations, particularly the duty of zakah (obligatory charity), which is not just a financial transaction but an act of worship and social responsibility that purifies wealth and benefits the community.

translation: And those who guard their private parts (from illegal sexual intercourse).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of chastity and self-restraint, highlighting the moral and spiritual duty of believers to protect their modesty and avoid sexual misconduct, reflecting a broader commitment to righteousness and piety.

translation: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not to be blamed.
interpretation: This verse clarifies the boundaries of permissible intimacy for believers, emphasizing that sexual relations are lawful only within the sanctity of marriage or with those lawfully acquired as concubines, thereby upholding moral and social order while acknowledging the realities of human nature.

translation: But whoever seeks beyond that, it is they who are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse warns against seeking anything beyond the permissible limits set by Allah, emphasizing that those who do so are committing an act of transgression, thereby crossing the boundaries of what is lawful and just.

translation: And those who are faithfully observant of their trusts and their covenants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and ethical responsibility of believers to honor their commitments and fulfill their obligations with integrity, emphasizing the importance of trustworthiness in personal and communal relationships.

translation: And those who carefully maintain their prayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of consistency and devotion in performing the obligatory prayers, highlighting that true believers are distinguished by their unwavering commitment to their religious duties, which reflects their deep faith and mindfulness of Allah.

translation: It is they who are the inheritors.
interpretation: This verse signifies that the righteous believers are the true heirs of Paradise, inheriting eternal bliss and divine reward as a result of their faith, righteous deeds, and steadfastness in the path of Allah.

translation: It is those who will inherit the Garden (Paradise); they will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal and unchanging nature of the reward for the righteous believers, highlighting that Paradise is not a temporary state but a permanent abode where they will dwell forever, free from any end or alteration.

translation: And indeed We created man from an extract of clay.
interpretation: This verse underscores the humble and earthly origin of human beings, emphasizing that despite their potential for greatness, humans are fundamentally connected to the material world from which they were created, reminding them of their dependence on Allah and their place within the natural order.

translation: Then We made him a sperm-drop in a firm lodging.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous and intricate process of human creation, emphasizing Allah's power and wisdom in forming life from a seemingly insignificant beginning, thereby underscoring the sanctity and purpose of human existence.

translation: Then We made the sperm-drop into a clinging clot, and We made the clot into a lump [of flesh], and We made [from] the lump, bones, and We covered the bones with flesh; then We developed him into another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators.
interpretation: This verse highlights the meticulous and gradual process of human creation, emphasizing Allah's supreme power and wisdom in transforming a simple sperm-drop into a fully formed human being, underscoring the divine origin and sanctity of human life.

translation: Then indeed, after that you will surely die.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark reminder of the inevitability of death for all human beings, emphasizing the transient nature of worldly life and the certainty of the Hereafter, urging reflection on one's deeds and preparation for the afterlife.

translation: Then indeed, you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of the Hereafter and the final resurrection, affirming that all human beings will be raised from the dead to stand before Allah for judgment, where deeds will be accounted for.

translation: And We have created above you seven heavens, and never were We of creation unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's meticulous and comprehensive knowledge of His creation, implying that nothing in the heavens or the earth escapes His awareness or control.

translation: And We sent down from the sky water in due measure, and We gave it a place to stay in the earth, and indeed, We are Able to take it away.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute control over natural resources, particularly water, which is essential for life. It highlights the balance in the distribution and sustenance of water, reminding humans of their dependence on divine provision and the transient nature of worldly blessings, as Allah can alter or withdraw them at any time.

translation: And We have produced for you thereby gardens of palm trees and grapevines in which there is much fruit for you to eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine blessing of sustenance and provision, demonstrating Allah's mercy in creating diverse and abundant sources of nourishment for humanity, encouraging gratitude and reflection on the signs of creation.

translation: And a tree that grows on Mount Sinai, which produces oil and is a relish for the eaters.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically highlights the blessedness and unique qualities of a tree that grows in a sacred and elevated place (Mount Sinai), symbolizing divine favor and sustenance that is both nourishing and delightful for those who partake of it.

translation: And indeed, in livestock there is a lesson for you. We give you drink from what is in their bellies, and for you in them are numerous benefits, and from them you eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate design and multifaceted utility of livestock, serving as a sign of divine providence and wisdom, urging reflection on the Creator's power and the interconnectedness of all creation.

translation: And upon it (the earth) and upon the ships you are carried.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine facilitation of human transportation and travel, both on land and by sea, underscoring Allah's power to provide means for human sustenance and movement.

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, [and he said], "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear Him?"
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and calls upon humanity to recognize and worship Him alone, devoid of any partners or associates, as the sole source of guidance and fear.

translation: The elite who disbelieved from his people said, "This is not but a human being like you who wishes to take precedence over you. Had Allah willed, He would have sent down angels. We have not heard of this among our forefathers of old."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and disbelief of the elite among Prophet Saleh's people, who dismissed him as merely a human like them, refusing to acknowledge his divine mission. Their argument that Allah could have sent angels instead reveals their stubbornness and rejection of prophethood, as well as their reliance on tradition over divine guidance.

translation: He is naught but a man possessed by madness, so wait and watch him for a time.
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and ridicule of the disbelievers toward the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), attributing his message to madness rather than divine revelation.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, help me because they deny me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the supplication of a prophet (likely Noah, as referenced in the broader context of the surah) seeking divine assistance against those who reject his message and oppose him, highlighting the struggle between truth and falsehood and the believer's reliance on Allah's support in the face of adversity.

translation: Then We inspired to him, 'Construct the ship under Our observation, and Our inspiration, and when Our command comes and the oven overflows, bring into it of every kind a pair [of creatures] from your family, except those against whom the word has already gone, and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of divine command and the inevitability of God's decree, emphasizing that human efforts must align with divine will, and that divine justice is absolute and unquestionable.

translation: But when you have boarded the ship, you and those with you, then say: 'Praise be to Allah who has saved us from the unjust people.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of gratitude to Allah for deliverance from harm or oppression, emphasizing that such gratitude should be expressed immediately upon safety, as it acknowledges divine intervention and reinforces humility and reliance on Allah.

translation: And say, 'My Lord, enable me to settle in a blessed place, and You are the best of those who grant [a place of] settlement.'
interpretation: This supplication reflects a deep sense of reliance on Allah and a request for divine favor in finding a place of residence that is blessed, secure, and conducive to spiritual and worldly well-being. It acknowledges Allah's supreme power and wisdom in providing the best outcome for the supplicant.

translation: Indeed, in that are signs, and indeed We are ever testing [Our servants].
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom behind trials and tribulations, indicating that they serve as tests to reveal the true nature of faith and submission in individuals, thereby purifying their hearts and strengthening their reliance on Allah.

translation: Then We produced after them another generation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine succession and the continuous cycle of human generations, emphasizing that Allah's power and authority extend beyond any particular era or people, ensuring the continuity of His message and the accountability of each generation for their deeds.

translation: So We sent among them a messenger from themselves, [saying], "Worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him. Then will you not fear Him?"
interpretation: This verse underscores the fundamental Islamic principle of Tawhid (monotheism), emphasizing that Allah is the only true deity worthy of worship, and it calls upon people to reflect on their accountability to Him, urging them to abandon false deities and idolatry out of reverence and fear of divine judgment.

translation: And the eminent ones among his people who disbelieved and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, while We had granted them luxury in the life of this world, said, 'This is not but a man like yourselves. He eats what you eat and drinks what you drink.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and denial of the disbelievers who, despite their worldly privileges, refuse to acknowledge the truth due to their disbelief in the Hereafter and their inability to recognize the divine origin of the message brought by the Prophet (peace be upon him). Their focus on superficial similarities (eating and drinking) reflects their rejection of the spiritual and moral dimensions of prophethood.

translation: And if you obey a human being like yourselves, then indeed you will be losers.
interpretation: This verse cautions against blindly following human leaders or individuals who are similar to oneself in nature, as doing so can lead to deviation and ultimate loss in both this life and the Hereafter.

translation: Does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones, you will be brought forth?
interpretation: This verse challenges the skepticism of those who doubt the possibility of resurrection after death, questioning their denial of divine power to restore life to decomposed matter, thereby affirming the Qur'an's core message of the Hereafter as an inevitable reality.

translation: Far, far is what you are promised!
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine retribution and the stark contrast between human perception of time and the certainty of Allah's promises, urging reflection on the transient nature of worldly life and the permanence of the Hereafter.

translation: There is not but our worldly life; we die and live, and we will not be resurrected.
interpretation: This verse reflects a common misconception among those who deny the Hereafter, suggesting that life is cyclical and finite, with no accountability or eternal existence beyond this world.

translation: He is but a man who has fabricated a lie about Allah, and we are not believers in him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection of false claims made against Allah by an individual, emphasizing the importance of truth and the rejection of fabricated lies in matters of faith.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, grant me victory over them for they have denied me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the supplication of a prophet or messenger seeking divine assistance against those who reject and oppose the truth he has brought, emphasizing reliance on God's power and justice in the face of adversity.

translation: In a little while, they will become regretful.
interpretation: This verse warns of the swift and inevitable consequences of defiance against divine commandments, suggesting that those who oppose or mock divine guidance will soon face regret when the truth becomes undeniable.

translation: So the blast seized them in truth, and We made them as rubbish (scattered debris). So away with the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice, illustrating that those who persist in oppression and wrongdoing will face sudden and decisive destruction, leaving no lasting legacy or influence, serving as a stark warning against tyranny and injustice.

translation: Then We produced after them other generations.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of human civilizations and the inevitability of their rise and fall, serving as a reminder of divine power and the transient nature of worldly power and glory.

translation: No nation can hasten its term, nor can they delay it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the timing of events, including the lifespan of nations or individuals, emphasizing that human efforts cannot alter divinely ordained decrees.

translation: Then We sent Our messengers in succession. Every time an ummah rejected its messenger, We made them follow one another [to ruin], and We made them as a tale [in the peoples' mouths]. So away with a people who do not believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the recurring pattern of human rejection of divine guidance, highlighting the consequences of such disbelief. It emphasizes that rejecting truth, despite repeated warnings, leads to the downfall of communities, serving as a historical lesson for those who persist in unbelief.

translation: Then We sent Moses and his brother Aaron with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mission entrusted to Moses and Aaron, emphasizing that their authority was not merely political or personal but derived from God's signs (miracles) and a clear proof of their prophethood, underscoring the legitimacy of their message against the tyranny of Pharaoh.

translation: To Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they behaved arrogantly and were a haughty people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive nature of arrogance and defiance against divine guidance, showing how it leads to ruin for both individuals and societies.

translation: They said, 'Shall we believe in two humans like ourselves while their people are subservient to us?'.
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and denial of truth by those who refuse to accept the message of the prophets due to their own inflated sense of superiority and attachment to worldly power.

translation: But they denied them, so they became among the destroyed.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting divine guidance and the messengers of Allah. It serves as a warning against arrogance and disbelief, emphasizing that those who reject the truth will face destruction, illustrating the importance of humility and acceptance of divine guidance.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture that they might be guided.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purpose of revelation: guidance. It underscores that divine scriptures, like the Torah given to Moses, are sent to lead humanity from error to truth, from darkness to light, and from misguidance to the straight path.

translation: And We made the son of Mary and his mother a sign, and We sheltered them in a high place of rest and flowing water.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine protection and miraculous nature of Jesus (Isa) and his mother Mary (Maryam), emphasizing that their story is a sign of Allah's power and mercy, and that they were provided with a secure and blessed refuge.

translation: O Messengers, eat from the good foods and work righteousness. Indeed, I am Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of maintaining purity and integrity in both sustenance and actions, reminding messengers—and by extension all believers—that their deeds are under divine scrutiny, urging them to align their worldly consumption with righteous conduct.

translation: And indeed, this your community is one community, and I am your Lord, so fear Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of the Muslim community (Ummah) and the exclusive worship of Allah, reminding believers of their shared faith and the necessity of taqwa (God-consciousness) in all aspects of life.

translation: Then they divided their affair among themselves into sects, each party rejoicing in what they have.
interpretation: This verse critiques the divisive tendencies within communities, where people fragment into opposing groups based on differing beliefs or interests, each clinging to their own perspective with unwarranted satisfaction, often leading to conflict and discord rather than unity and mutual understanding.

translation: So leave them in their confusion for a time.
interpretation: This verse advises patience and restraint in the face of persistent disbelief or opposition, indicating that divine justice will ultimately prevail without the need for immediate intervention.

translation: Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children
interpretation: This verse highlights the delusion of those who believe that their material prosperity and abundance of offspring are signs of divine favor or proof of their righteousness, when in reality, such blessings may be a test or a delay of accountability for their actions.

translation: We hasten to them with good things? Nay, they perceive not.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to assume that blessings or good fortune are granted as a result of their own actions or worthiness, while in reality, such favors are purely from Allah’s grace and timing, which humans often fail to recognize or appreciate.

translation: Indeed, those who are apprehensive from [the punishment of] their Lord
interpretation: This verse highlights the emotional and spiritual state of believers who are deeply conscious of Allah's majesty and the consequences of their actions, leading them to live in constant awareness and reverence.

translation: And those who believe in the verses of their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of unwavering faith in the divine signs (ayat) of Allah, which include the Qur'an, the natural world, and the signs within oneself, as a fundamental aspect of true belief and submission to Allah.

translation: And [they are] those who associate nothing with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of God (Tawheed) and the rejection of any form of polytheism or associating partners with Allah, highlighting the purity of faith in the hearts of the believers.

translation: And [they are] those who give what they give while their hearts are fearful because they will return to their Lord—
interpretation: This verse highlights the internal struggle of believers who, despite their acts of charity, remain conscious of their ultimate return to Allah and the accountability that follows, emphasizing sincerity and humility in worship.

translation: It is these who hasten to do good deeds, and they are the foremost in them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the proactive nature of true believers in performing righteous deeds, emphasizing their eagerness and priority in doing good, setting an example for others to follow.

translation: And We do not charge any soul except within its capacity. And with Us is a Book that speaks the truth; and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's justice and mercy, ensuring that no individual is burdened beyond their capacity to bear. It reassures that divine accountability is based on fairness, and no soul will be treated unjustly, as all deeds are meticulously recorded in the 'Book' (presumably the Preserved Tablet or records of deeds), which will speak the truth on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Nay, but their hearts are hardened by this (the Qur'an); and they have deeds besides that which they are working at.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual blindness and arrogance of those who reject the Qur'an despite its clear guidance, as their hearts remain veiled by their own preoccupation with worldly pursuits and misguided actions.

translation: Until, when We seize the affluent among them with punishment, behold, they start crying for help.
interpretation: This verse highlights the delayed but inevitable nature of divine punishment for those who indulge in luxury and oppression while ignoring moral and spiritual responsibilities, emphasizing that their eventual cries for mercy will be unheeded.

translation: Do not raise your voices today; indeed, you will not be helped against Us.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of seeking help or refuge from Allah’s punishment on the Day of Judgment, as no one can avert it, and all appeals will be in vain.

translation: My verses were recited to you, but you turned on your heels,
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection of divine guidance despite its clear presentation, emphasizing the stubbornness and ingratitude of those who were given the opportunity to accept the truth but chose to turn away from it.

translation: And you turn away from it, being arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and rejection of truth by those who turn away from divine guidance, despite its clarity and truthfulness, due to their pride and self-exaltation.

translation: Have they not then pondered over the Word (of Allah), or has there come to them what had not come to their forefathers of old?
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers to reflect deeply on the divine message rather than dismissing it outright, implying that their rejection is not based on reason or evidence but on blind imitation of their ancestors.

translation: Or do they not recognize their Messenger? So they deny him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by those who were familiar with him, despite his truthfulness and integrity, reflecting a deeper spiritual blindness and ingratitude.

translation: Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, so you are not to be among the deniers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who reject the Qur'an, attributing its revelation to fabrication rather than divine origin. It affirms the Qur'an's truthfulness as a divine message and highlights the common human resistance to accepting truth, especially when it challenges preconceived notions or worldly interests.

translation: And if the truth had followed their desires, the heavens and the earth and whoever is in them would have been ruined. Rather, We have brought them their reminder, but they are turning away from their reminder.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of divine truth over human whims and desires, asserting that if truth were subject to personal inclinations, cosmic order would collapse—highlighting the necessity of submitting to objective divine guidance rather than subjective desires.

translation: Or do they ask you for a reward? But the reward of your Lord is better, and He is the best of providers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of seeking worldly compensation for conveying divine guidance, as the true reward comes from Allah, who is the ultimate and most generous Provider, far surpassing any material or temporary gains.

translation: And indeed, you [O Muhammad] invite them to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse underscores the clarity and unerring nature of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) call to Islam, likening it to a 'straight path'—free from deviation, ambiguity, or compromise—which is the path of monotheism (Tawhid) and righteousness.

translation: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter are deviating from the path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and spiritual consequences of rejecting the belief in the Hereafter, suggesting that such disbelief leads individuals away from the righteous path and distorts their moral compass, as their actions are no longer guided by the accountability of the Hereafter.

translation: And if We had mercy upon them and removed what afflicted them of adversity, they would persist in their transgression, wandering blindly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the nature of human ingratitude and stubbornness; even when granted relief from hardship, people often fail to reflect or repent, instead persisting in their rebelliousness and heedlessness.

translation: And We had seized them with punishment, but they did not humble themselves to their Lord, nor did they supplicate [to Him] with humility.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance despite clear signs and punishments, illustrating the stubbornness of those who refuse to submit to Allah's will even in the face of adversity.

translation: Until, when We open for them a gate of severe punishment, at once they are in despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sudden and overwhelming realization of those who persist in disbelief or defiance against divine guidance, as they face the consequences of their actions in a manner that leaves them utterly helpless and devoid of hope.

translation: And it is He who has created for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine endowment of human faculties—hearing, sight, and insight (hearts)—as signs of Allah’s mercy and wisdom, yet it laments humanity’s frequent failure to recognize and express gratitude for these blessings, highlighting ingratitude as a moral and spiritual deficiency.

translation: And it is He who has dispersed you [mankind] upon the earth and to Him you will be gathered.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty over human existence, from our initial creation and distribution across the earth to our ultimate return to Him for judgment, emphasizing divine control over life's beginning and end.

translation: And it is He who gives life and causes death, and [it is] He who alternates the night and the day. Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power of Allah in sustaining and controlling life, death, and the natural cycles of the universe, urging humanity to reflect on these signs to recognize His oneness and wisdom.

translation: Nay, they say the like of what the former people said.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent nature of human denial and skepticism towards divine guidance, showing that people often repeat the same objections and disbelief as those who came before them, despite clear signs and warnings.

translation: They say, 'When we have died and become dust and bones, will we really be resurrected?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism of those who deny resurrection after death, questioning the possibility of life after complete decomposition, thereby challenging the concept of divine justice and accountability.

translation: We and our forefathers were promised this before. This is nothing but tales of the ancients.
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and dismissal of divine messages by those who reject the truth, attributing it to baseless myths rather than recognizing it as a legitimate revelation from Allah.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'To whom belongs the earth and whoever is in it, if you should know?''
interpretation: This verse challenges humanity to reflect on the ultimate ownership of the earth and all that exists within it, emphasizing that true sovereignty belongs to Allah alone, regardless of human claims or perceptions of possession.

translation: They will say, "[It belongs] to Allah." Say, "Then will you not remember?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to attribute all power and control to Allah in times of distress or need, yet they often forget Him in times of ease and forgetfulness, failing to acknowledge His blessings and maintain gratitude.

translation: Say, 'Who is the Lord of the seven heavens and the Lord of the Great Throne?'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and uniqueness of Allah, challenging the listener to recognize the Creator of the heavens and the earth, thereby affirming His unparalleled authority and power over all existence.

translation: They will say, "[It belongs] to Allah." Say, "Then will you not fear Him?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the hypocrisy of those who claim to acknowledge Allah's absolute ownership and authority yet fail to act with the reverence and obedience that such acknowledgment demands, highlighting the disconnect between lip service and true faith.

translation: Say, 'Who is it that holds in His hand the dominion of all things, while He protects [all], and none can protect against Him, if you should know?',
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and unmatched power of Allah, emphasizing that all authority and protection ultimately belong to Him alone, and no one can challenge or override His will.

translation: They will say, "[It belongs] to Allah." Say, "Then how are you deluded?"
interpretation: This verse challenges the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe in Allah yet act in ways that contradict His commands, exposing their self-deception and the inconsistency between their professed faith and their actions.

translation: But We have brought them the truth, and indeed they are liars.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an as the absolute truth, contrasting it with the falsehood propagated by those who deny it, thereby highlighting the futility of their denials in the face of undeniable truth.

translation: Allah has not taken any son, nor has there been with Him any god. [If there had been], then each god would have taken what he created, and some of them would have overcome others. Exalted is Allah above what they describe [concerning Him].
interpretation: This verse refutes the polytheistic beliefs that ascribe partners or offspring to Allah, emphasizing His absolute oneness and uniqueness. It highlights the logical inconsistency of associating partners with Allah, as such a scenario would lead to chaos and conflict among the supposed gods, undermining the harmony and order observed in creation.

translation: Knower of the unseen and the seen, exalted is He above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute knowledge and sovereignty over all existence—both the hidden and the manifest—while affirming His transcendence above any false partners or associations attributed to Him by those who commit shirk (idolatry).

translation: Say, 'My Lord, if You should show me what they are promised'
interpretation: This verse reflects a plea for patience and trust in Allah's timing, acknowledging human limitations in comprehending divine justice and the ultimate fulfillment of promises.

translation: My Lord, so do not place me among the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This supplication reflects a plea for divine protection from being associated with those who commit injustice, emphasizing the believer's desire to remain steadfast in righteousness and avoid moral corruption.

translation: And indeed, We are surely able to show you what We promise them.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that Allah's promises of punishment or reward for the disbelievers will certainly come to pass, and Allah has the power to fulfill His decrees in due time.

translation: Repel evil with what is better. We are most knowing of what they attribute [to Us].
interpretation: This verse encourages responding to harm or evil with kindness and patience, trusting that Allah is fully aware of the accusations and falsehoods people spread, and that He will ultimately judge with justice.

translation: And say, 'My Lord, I seek refuge in You from the evil suggestions of the devils.'
interpretation: This verse teaches the believer to actively seek divine protection from the whispers and deceptions of Satan, emphasizing reliance on Allah and the importance of invoking His help to ward off spiritual harm.

translation: And I seek refuge in You, my Lord, lest they come near me.
interpretation: This supplication reflects a plea for divine protection from the presence or influence of harmful individuals or evil forces, emphasizing the believer's reliance on Allah's safeguarding power.

translation: Until when death comes to one of them, he says, "My Lord, send me back"
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to desire a second chance when faced with the inevitability of death, reflecting regret for past actions and a desire to amend one's deeds, which underscores the importance of living a righteous life in the present rather than postponing repentance and good deeds until it is too late.

translation: Perhaps I should do righteous deeds in what I have left behind.' By no means! It is but a word he utters; and before them is a barrier until the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality of death and the absolute inability of the deceased to alter their fate or return to the world to perform good deeds. The 'word' refers to the deceased's regretful wish to return, which is futile because the opportunity has passed, and their fate is sealed until the Day of Resurrection.

translation: And when the Horn is blown, that Day there will be no kinship among them, nor will they ask about one another.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and irreversible transformation of human relationships on the Day of Judgment, where worldly ties—no matter how deep or sacred—will dissolve entirely before the overwhelming reality of divine justice and accountability.

translation: But as for he whose scales are heavy, it is they who will be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true success in the Hereafter is determined by the weight of one's good deeds, as measured by Allah's justice, rather than worldly wealth or status. It underscores the importance of righteous actions and moral integrity in securing eternal felicity.

translation: But whoever's scales are light - it is they who have lost themselves, [and will] abide eternally in Hell.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of moral accountability in the Hereafter, emphasizing that even minor deficiencies in righteous deeds, when weighed against divine justice, can lead to eternal loss, highlighting the necessity of sincere faith and righteous conduct.

translation: The Fire will burn their faces, and they will be gloomy therein.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe and irreversible consequences of disbelief and wrongdoing, where the Fire of Hell will visibly mark the faces of the condemned, leaving them disfigured and in a state of perpetual gloom, reflecting the justice and finality of divine punishment.

translation: Were My verses not recited to you, so you used to deny them?
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of rejecting divine guidance despite its clear presentation and recitation, highlighting the consequences of such denial in both worldly and spiritual realms.

translation: They said, "Our Lord, our wretchedness overcame us, and we were a people astray."
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound regret and realization of people who, in the Hereafter, acknowledge that their own destructive choices and heedlessness led them to ruin, rather than attributing their fate to external forces or divine injustice.

translation: Our Lord, bring us out of this [city]; for if we return [to disbelief], we will indeed be wrongdoers.
interpretation: This supplication reflects a profound acknowledgment of human weakness and the need for divine guidance to resist temptation and maintain faith. It underscores the believer's recognition that returning to oppression or disbelief would constitute a grave injustice against their own souls, as they would be betraying the truth they have come to know.

translation: ‘Be you condemned to it! Do not speak!’
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality and irrevocable nature of the punishment for the disbelievers in the Hereafter, stripping them of any opportunity to plead, negotiate, or even speak in their defense, emphasizing the absolute justice and decisiveness of Allah’s judgment.

translation: Indeed, there was a group of My servants who would say, 'Our Lord, we have believed, so forgive us and have mercy upon us, and You are the best of the merciful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking forgiveness and mercy from Allah with sincerity and trust in His boundless compassion, emphasizing that true faith is accompanied by humility and reliance on divine grace.

translation: So you took them in mockery until they made you forget My remembrance, and you used to laugh at them.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against mocking or belittling others, as such behavior can lead to a loss of focus on one's own faith and spiritual duties, ultimately causing one to forget the remembrance of Allah.

translation: Indeed, I have rewarded them today for their patience. It is they who are the victorious.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice and recompense for steadfastness in faith and righteous deeds, affirming that patience in the face of hardship is ultimately rewarded with eternal success and victory in the Hereafter.

translation: He will say, "How long did you remain on earth? A number of years."
interpretation: This verse reflects the questioning of the deceased in the grave by the angels Munkar and Nakir, probing the duration of their worldly life to assess their awareness of the transient nature of their existence before the Hereafter.

translation: They said, "We remained a day or part of a day. Ask those who keep count."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to underestimate the passage of time, especially in relation to the Hereafter, suggesting a lack of awareness or denial of the true magnitude of divine reckoning.

translation: He said, "You have remained only a little - if only you had known."
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of worldly life and the urgency of preparing for the Hereafter, as the limited time spent in this world contrasts sharply with the eternal consequences of one's actions.

translation: Did you think that We created you in vain and that you would not return to Us?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of a purposeless existence, affirming that human life is not without meaning or consequence, and that all will ultimately return to Allah for judgment.

translation: So Exalted is Allah, the True King. There is no deity except Him, the Lord of the Noble Throne.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and uniqueness of Allah, declaring Him as the only true King and Lord, whose authority and majesty are unparalleled and beyond any comparison.

translation: And whoever invokes besides Allah another god for which he has no proof, his reckoning is only with his Lord. Indeed, the disbelievers will not succeed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility and spiritual peril of associating partners with Allah (shirk) without any rational or divine justification. It asserts that those who engage in such polytheism will ultimately face accountability before Allah alone, and their denial of truth ensures their failure in both this life and the Hereafter.

translation: And say, 'My Lord, forgive and have mercy, for You are the best of those who show mercy.'
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to seek Allah's forgiveness and mercy through supplication, acknowledging His ultimate mercy and superiority over all creation in granting it.

translation: It is a Book We have sent down to you, set apart for you, and sent down in it are clear verses, so that you may remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and clarity of the Qur'an, highlighting its purpose as a guidance for remembrance and reflection, ensuring that its teachings are accessible and understandable to humanity.

translation: The adulteress and the adulterer—flog each of them with a hundred lashes. And let no pity for them seize you in the religion of Allah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute nature of divine justice, where punishment is administered without personal bias or emotional influence, reflecting the sovereignty of Allah’s law over human sentiment.

translation: The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or an idolatress, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or an idolater. And that has been made unlawful for the believers.
interpretation: This verse establishes a moral boundary for believers by prohibiting marriage between a chaste Muslim and an adulterer or idolater, reflecting the Qur'an's emphasis on righteousness and purity in personal relationships.

translation: And those who accuse chaste women [of adultery] and then do not produce four witnesses—flog them with eighty lashes and do not accept their testimony ever after. And it is they who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse establishes a strict legal and moral standard for accusations of adultery, requiring definitive evidence (four witnesses) to avoid false accusations that could ruin reputations and lives. It underscores the gravity of such claims in Islam, where honor and integrity are highly valued, and it imposes severe consequences—both corporal punishment for the accusers and permanent disqualification from giving testimony—on those who fail to meet this burden of proof, thereby protecting the innocent from slander.

translation: Except for those who repent after that and correct themselves, for indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless mercy of Allah, emphasizing that sincere repentance and righteous correction can restore a person’s spiritual standing, regardless of past sins, as long as the repentance is genuine and followed by righteous deeds.

translation: And those who accuse their wives [of adultery] and have no witnesses except themselves - then the testimony of one of them [is required] by swearing four times by Allah that he is indeed truthful,
interpretation: This verse establishes a legal procedure for husbands who accuse their wives of adultery but lack external witnesses. It requires the husband to solemnly swear four times by Allah, affirming his accusation, thereby binding himself to the truthfulness of his claim under divine oath, which carries significant moral and spiritual weight.

translation: And the fifth [oath] is that the curse of Allah be upon him if he [Muhammad] is among the liars.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of falsehood, particularly in matters of divine revelation, by invoking Allah's curse upon anyone who falsely attributes lies to Him or His Messenger, emphasizing the gravity of such an act in Islamic belief.

translation: And it will be warded off from her punishment that she testifies four times by Allah, [saying], 'Indeed, I am of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of false accusations in Islamic law, particularly regarding charges of adultery (zina). It establishes a stringent requirement for the accuser to provide four testimonies under oath to substantiate their claim, thereby deterring frivolous or malicious accusations and emphasizing the gravity of bearing false witness.

translation: And the fifth (oath) is that the wrath of Allah will be upon her if he is among the truthful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of making false accusations, particularly in matters of grave consequence, as it invokes divine punishment upon the accuser if they are not truthful.

translation: And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, and indeed Allah is Accepting of repentance, Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the indispensability of Allah's grace and mercy in human life, emphasizing that without them, guidance and salvation would be unattainable. It also highlights Allah's attributes of being 'Tawwab' (the One who accepts repentance) and 'Hakim' (the Wise), suggesting that no matter how far one strays, the door to repentance and forgiveness is always open, provided one turns back to Him with sincere remorse.

translation: Indeed, those who came with the slander [against 'A'ishah] are a group among you. Do not think it an evil for you; rather, it is good for you. For each person among them will be what he has earned of sin, and he who took upon himself the greater part thereof - for him is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse addresses the incident of the slander against 'A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her), highlighting that such trials, though seemingly harmful, can ultimately bring about greater good for the believers, such as increased faith, unity, and purification of the community, while also serving as a warning of severe consequences for those who propagate or take a leading role in spreading falsehood.

translation: Why did the believing men and women not think good of one another when you heard it [i.e., the slander] and say, 'This is an obvious falsehood'?
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of maintaining trust and positive assumptions among believers, especially in the face of accusations or rumors. It criticizes the delay in responding with righteousness and discernment, urging believers to immediately reject falsehood and uphold justice rather than harboring doubts or suspicions.

translation: Why did they [not] bring four witnesses against her? But since they did not bring the witnesses, then it is they, in the sight of Allah, who are the liars.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of false accusations, particularly in matters of honor and morality, by emphasizing that accusers must provide credible evidence—here, four witnesses—to substantiate their claims. Failure to do so exposes them as liars in the sight of Allah, highlighting divine justice in protecting individuals from slander and upholding truth through stringent standards of proof.

translation: And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, in this world and the Hereafter, there would have struck you a great punishment for what you indulged in.
interpretation: This verse underscores the indispensability of Allah's grace and mercy in averting punishment for human shortcomings, both in this life and the Hereafter, highlighting the peril of overstepping divine boundaries without repentance or rectification.

translation: When you received it on your tongues and spoke with your mouths what you had no knowledge of, and you thought it was a trivial matter while it was, in the sight of Allah, grave.
interpretation: This verse cautions against spreading or believing in unverified information, especially when it concerns others, as such actions can cause significant harm and are considered grave in the sight of Allah, regardless of how trivial they may seem to the speaker.

translation: And why, when you heard it, did you not say, 'It is not for us to speak of this. Exalted are You [O Allah]; this is a great slander.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of exercising restraint and wisdom in speech, especially when confronted with false or harmful allegations. It highlights the moral duty to reject falsehood and uphold truth, even in the face of provocative or damaging statements.

translation: Allah admonishes you concerning this [conduct] that you return to it never [again], if you should be believers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of returning to sinful behavior after recognizing its wrongfulness, emphasizing that true faith necessitates sincere repentance and a firm commitment to avoid such actions permanently.

translation: And Allah makes clear to you the verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's role in providing clear guidance through the Qur'anic verses, highlighting His deep knowledge and wisdom in conveying truths and laws that are both profound and practical for human life.

translation: Indeed, those who desire that immorality should spread among the believers will have a painful punishment in this world and the Hereafter. And Allah knows, while you do not know.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who seek to spread immorality or scandal within the Muslim community, emphasizing that such actions will incur severe divine punishment in both this life and the Hereafter, highlighting the gravity of slander and corruption in society.

translation: And [you would not have been guided] had it not been for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy. Indeed, Allah is Compassionate and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute dependence of humanity on Allah's grace and mercy for guidance and success, emphasizing that any good in this world or the Hereafter is solely a result of His benevolence, not human merit alone.

translation: O you who have believed, do not follow the footsteps of Satan. And whoever follows the footsteps of Satan - indeed, he orders [improper] conduct and wrongdoing. And if not for the favor of Allah upon you and His mercy, not one of you would be purified ever; but Allah purifies whom He wills. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against the influence of Satan, emphasizing that following his path leads to moral corruption. It highlights the necessity of divine guidance and mercy for spiritual purification, reminding believers that their righteousness is not self-achieved but granted by Allah, who alone has the power to cleanse hearts and grant purity.

translation: And let not those of virtue among you and the wealthy swear not to give [aid] to their relatives and the needy and those who emigrated for the sake of Allah. And let them pardon and overlook. Would you not love for Allah to forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of generosity and forgiveness, urging those who are financially stable or morally upright to support their relatives, the poor, and those who have sacrificed for their faith, without hesitation or resentment. It highlights that overlooking others' faults and showing mercy can lead to divine forgiveness, reinforcing the reciprocal nature of compassion in Islam.

translation: Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unaware and believing women of immorality are cursed in this world and the Hereafter; and for them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of false accusations against chaste women, emphasizing that such slander is not only a grave sin but also carries severe consequences in both this life and the Hereafter, reflecting the Qur'an's emphasis on justice, honor, and the protection of individual dignity.

translation: The Day when their tongues, their hands, and their feet will bear witness against them as to what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute accountability of every individual on the Day of Judgment, where even the parts of the body that were used to commit sins will testify against their owner, highlighting the inescapable reality of divine justice and the thoroughness of Allah's knowledge of human actions.

translation: On that Day, Allah will pay them their due in full, and they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine justice and the ultimate truth of Allah's existence, emphasizing that on the Day of Judgment, all accounts will be settled with absolute fairness, leaving no doubt about Allah's sovereignty and veracity.

translation: Evil women are for evil men, and evil men are for evil women. And good women are for good men, and good men are for good women. Those are acquitted of what they say. For them is forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and moral reciprocity, emphasizing that individuals are paired with counterparts who share their moral character—whether good or evil. The acquittal mentioned refers to the false accusations of the hypocrites, affirming that the righteous are purified from such slander, and their righteousness is rewarded with forgiveness and honor in the Hereafter.

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter houses other than your own houses until you have announced your presence and greeted their inhabitants. That is best for you; perhaps you will be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of respecting others' privacy and personal boundaries, even in matters as seemingly trivial as entering someone's home. It teaches Muslims to be considerate of others' space and to seek permission before entering, fostering a culture of mutual respect and mindfulness in social interactions.

translation: But if you do not find anyone in them, do not enter them until permission has been given to you. And if you are told, 'Go back,' then go back. It is purer for you. And Allah is Knowing of what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking permission before entering private spaces and respecting boundaries, highlighting that such conduct leads to greater purity and righteousness in one's actions.

translation: There is no blame upon you for entering houses not inhabited in which there is convenience for you. And Allah knows what you reveal and what you conceal.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that they are not held accountable for utilitarian or necessary entry into uninhabited dwellings where they may find benefit, while emphasizing Allah's omniscience regarding both outward actions and hidden intentions.

translation: Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and self-restraint in matters of physical and visual purity, underscoring that such conduct is spiritually elevating and aligned with divine awareness.

translation: And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their private parts and not display their adornments except what is apparent of it, and to draw their head-coverings over their chests, and not display their adornments except to their husbands, their fathers, their husbands' fathers, their sons, their husbands' sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, their women, that which their right hands possess, or those male attendants having no physical desire, or children who are not yet aware of the private aspects of women. And let them not stamp their feet to make known what they conceal of their adornments. And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you might succeed.
interpretation: This verse outlines the Islamic code of modesty and privacy for women, emphasizing both external conduct (such as lowering the gaze and covering adornments) and internal virtue (guarding chastity). It specifies permissible relationships where modest dress and behavior may be relaxed, while also prohibiting actions that draw attention to hidden adornments. The broader lesson is the importance of modesty as a safeguard for personal dignity and societal harmony, encouraging believers to seek repentance and spiritual refinement.

translation: And marry the unmarried among you and the righteous among your male and female slaves. If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is all-Encompassing, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse encourages marriage for those who are unmarried, including the righteous among one's slaves, and reassures that Allah can provide for them even if they are poor, emphasizing Allah's boundless generosity and knowledge.

translation: And let those who cannot find a marriage keep themselves chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty. And [as for] those who seek a contract [for emancipation] from among those whom your right hands possess, then make a contract with them if you know there is good in them; and give them from the wealth of Allah which He has given you. And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, to seek the temporary gains of this worldly life. And if someone compels them, then indeed, Allah is, after their compulsion, Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of chastity and ethical conduct, whether for those unable to marry or for those in servitude. It encourages providing opportunities for emancipation and financial support to those seeking freedom, while also protecting vulnerable individuals from exploitation, particularly women in servitude, by prohibiting forced prostitution and affirming divine mercy for those who are coerced.

translation: And We have certainly sent down to you verses clear in meaning, and an example from [the stories of] those who passed on before you, and an admonition for the God-fearing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and guidance of the Qur'an, using historical examples of past nations as lessons for the righteous, highlighting the continuity of divine guidance and the importance of heeding warnings to attain piety.

translation: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The example of His light is like a niche within which is a lamp, the lamp is within glass, the glass as if it were a pearly [white] star lit from [the oil of] a blessed olive tree, neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow even if untouched by fire. Light upon light. Allah guides to His light whom He wills. And Allah presents examples for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describes Allah’s guidance as an illuminating light that dispels spiritual darkness, emanating from a source of divine wisdom (the 'blessed olive tree')—symbolizing purity and universality, unconfined by temporal or spatial limitations. The 'pearly star' imagery suggests that true guidance is radiant, constant, and accessible to those whom Allah wills to guide, transcending human constructs of direction or exclusivity.

translation: In houses which Allah has ordered to be raised and in which His name is mentioned; there glorify Him, morning and evening:
interpretation: This verse highlights the sanctity and elevated status of houses of worship—particularly mosques—where Allah’s name is invoked regularly. The mention of 'morning and evening' signifies constant remembrance and devotion, emphasizing that such places are centers of spiritual elevation, purity, and divine connection, fostering an environment of peace, reflection, and unwavering faith.

translation: Men whom neither commerce nor business distracts from the remembrance of Allah, and from establishing prayer and giving zakah. They fear a Day in which the hearts and eyes will [flicker] intensely.
interpretation: This verse highlights the priority of spiritual obligations over worldly engagements, emphasizing that true believers remain steadfast in their devotion to Allah, even amidst their worldly pursuits. It also underscores the profound awe and anticipation of the Day of Judgment, where the certainty of accountability will cause hearts and eyes to tremble in fear.

translation: So Allah will reward them [in Paradise] for what they did and increase them from His bounty. And Allah provides for whom He wills without account.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah’s boundless generosity and justice, emphasizing that He rewards deeds not only with justice but also with additional bounty beyond measure, demonstrating that His mercy and favor are not constrained by calculation or limitation.

translation: But the deeds of those who disbelieve are like a mirage in a lowland which a thirsty one thinks is water until, when he comes to it, he finds it is nothing; and he finds Allah with him, and He will pay him in full his account. And Allah is swift in account.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the futility and emptiness of worldly pursuits pursued by those who reject faith, likening their efforts to a mirage that deceives the seeker. It emphasizes that ultimate justice and recompense come from Allah alone, who sees all deeds and will account for them without delay, contrasting the fleeting nature of human perception with the absolute certainty of divine justice.

translation: Or [they are] like darknesses within an unfathomable sea which is covered by waves, upon which are waves, over which are clouds - darknesses, some of them upon others. When one puts out his hand [therein], he can hardly see it. And he to whom Allah has not granted light - for him there is no light.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the depth of spiritual blindness and confusion experienced by those who reject divine guidance, likening their state to the impenetrable darkness of an abyssal sea obscured by multiple layers of waves and clouds, where even the slightest attempt to perceive is futile without light. It emphasizes that true guidance (light) comes solely from Allah, and without it, one remains in profound darkness, unable to discern truth from falsehood.

translation: Do you not see that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth and the birds with wings spread? Each has known its [mode of] prayer and exultation. And Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal submission of all creation to Allah, highlighting that even the natural world—birds in flight, celestial bodies, and earthly beings—engages in a form of worship (prostration, prayer, and glorification) that reflects divine order and purpose. It underscores the inherent harmony and obedience of creation to Allah’s will, suggesting that human beings, too, are called to recognize and align themselves with this natural submission.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah is the return.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that everything in the heavens and the earth is under His control and ownership. The mention of 'return' highlights the ultimate accountability of all beings to Allah, affirming the Day of Judgment where every soul will answer for its deeds.

translation: Do you not see that Allah drives clouds, then composes them, then makes them a mass, and you see the rain coming forth from within it? And He sends down from the sky, from [mountains in] the sky, hail, and strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills. The flash of its lightning almost takes away the eyesight.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah's absolute sovereignty and control over natural phenomena, emphasizing His power to direct blessings or withhold them as He wills, serving as a reminder of His dominion over all creation and the unpredictability of divine decree.

translation: Allah alternates the night and the day. Indeed, in that is a lesson for those who possess insight.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom in the natural cycles of night and day, which serve as a constant reminder of Allah's power and the inevitability of change, urging believers to reflect on these signs and draw lessons for their own lives.

translation: And Allah has created every living creature from water. And of them are those that move on their bellies, and of them are those that move on two legs, and of them are those that move on four. Allah creates what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute power and wisdom in creation, highlighting the diversity of life forms and their unique modes of movement as a testament to His boundless creativity and control over all things.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down clear signs. And Allah guides whom He wills to a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and unambiguous nature of the divine revelations (Qur'anic verses) as a means of guidance, while also highlighting Allah's sovereign will in directing whom He chooses to the path of truth and righteousness.

translation: And they say, "We believe in Allah and in the Messenger and we obey," then a party of them turn away after that. And those are not believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between verbal affirmation and true faith, emphasizing that genuine belief is demonstrated through consistent obedience and unwavering commitment, not merely by outward declarations.

translation: And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them, at once a party of them turns aside.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to follow the guidance of Allah and His Messenger but deliberately avoid submitting to divine judgment when it conflicts with their personal interests or desires, revealing their true allegiance to worldly inclinations over spiritual truth.

translation: And if the truth is theirs, they will come to it submissively.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of truth prevailing and the natural submission of those who recognize it, highlighting the futility of resistance when confronted with genuine evidence or right.

translation: Is it [that there is] a disease in their hearts? Or did they doubt? Or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them? Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who harbor hidden doubts, skepticism, or ill intentions toward Islam and its teachings. It highlights their inner turmoil—whether due to unresolved doubts, fear of divine justice, or a sense of injustice toward themselves—while affirming that their true flaw is their oppression of truth through denial and hypocrisy.

translation: The only statement of the believers when they are called to Allah and His Messenger to judge between them is that they say, 'We hear and we obey.' And it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the essence of true faith and submission to divine authority, emphasizing that genuine believers respond to Allah's and His Messenger's guidance with immediate acceptance and obedience, not with hesitation or dispute, as this is the path to true success and salvation.

translation: And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger and fears Allah and is conscious of Him, it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse underscores that true success in the sight of Allah is attained not merely by outward obedience or ritualistic acts, but by a combination of sincere devotion, reverence for Allah, and mindfulness of His commands in both intention and action.

translation: And they swear by Allah their strongest oaths that if you ordered them, they would surely go forth. Say, 'Do not swear. [Such] obedience is known. Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with that which you do.'
interpretation: This verse addresses hypocrites who falsely pledge absolute obedience to the Prophet (peace be upon him) but in reality, their commitment is insincere. It highlights the importance of genuine faith and action, warning against superficial or deceptive claims, as Allah is fully aware of true intentions and deeds.

translation: Say, 'Obey Allah and obey the Messenger.' But if they turn away, then upon him [Muhammad] is only what he is charged with, and upon you is what you are charged with. And if you obey him, you will be [rightly] guided. And upon the Messenger is only the [duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility in following divine guidance: while individuals must strive to obey Allah and His Messenger, ultimate accountability rests with each person for their own choices, and the Prophet's role is solely to convey the message clearly.

translation: Allah has promised those who believe among you and do righteous deeds that He will surely make them successors (khulafa) upon the earth just as He made those before them successors, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has chosen for them, and He will surely substitute for them, after their fear, security. They will worship Me, not associating anything with Me. But whoever disbelieves after that, it is those who are the defiantly disobedient.
interpretation: This verse outlines a divine promise to the believers who uphold righteousness, assuring them of a future where they will inherit leadership and authority on earth, much like previous generations. It guarantees the establishment and dominance of their faith, replacing fear with security, and ensuring their exclusive worship of Allah without any association of partners.
