It reassures them that God has provided a secure sanctuary (likely Mecca) where they are blessed with sustenance and protection, yet their lack of awareness prevents them from recognizing this divine favor.

translation: And how many a city have We destroyed whose inhabitants were wrongdoers, so that it lies in ruins. So are its empty dwellings—We have but rarely inhabited them after them. And it is We who are the inheritors.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of worldly power and the inevitability of divine retribution against oppressive societies. It serves as a warning that arrogance and injustice, if unchecked, lead to destruction, with God ultimately taking control of all that remains, emphasizing His sovereignty over the fate of nations.

translation: And your Lord would not destroy the cities unjustly while their people were reformers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, emphasizing that Allah does not punish communities without first sending a messenger to guide them and warn them of their transgressions. It highlights the necessity of accountability and the opportunity for repentance before any divine retribution is enacted, reinforcing the idea that destruction is only justified when a people persist in oppression and injustice despite clear guidance.

translation: And whatever you have been given is [only for] the enjoyment of the worldly life and its adornment. But what is with Allah is better and more lasting. Then will you not reason?
interpretation: This verse cautions against becoming overly attached to the temporary pleasures and material gains of this world, emphasizing that the true and lasting good lies in what Allah has prepared for the believers in the Hereafter, urging reflection on the transient nature of worldly life compared to the eternal.

translation: Then is he whom We have promised a good promise which he will meet [in the Hereafter] like he whom We provided enjoyment of worldly life and then he is, on the Day of Resurrection, among those presented [for punishment]?
interpretation: This verse underscores the stark contrast between the ultimate fate of those who heed divine promises and those who indulge in transient worldly pleasures without regard for the Hereafter, emphasizing that the latter will face accountability and punishment on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And [mention] the Day He will call them, saying, 'Where are My 'partners' which you used to claim?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate power and singularity of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where all false claims of partnership with Him will be exposed and rendered meaningless, affirming the absolute oneness (Tawheed) of Allah and the futility of associating partners with Him.

translation: Those against whom the word has been justified will say, "Our Lord, these are the ones we led astray. We led them astray just as we were led astray. We declare our disassociation from You; it was not us they worshipped."
interpretation: This verse reflects the regret and denial of accountability by those who were misguided and led others astray. It highlights the human tendency to shift blame and absolve oneself of responsibility by attributing their actions to external influences, while simultaneously disassociating from the consequences of their deeds. The verse underscores the importance of personal accountability and the futility of blaming others or circumstances for one's own choices.

translation: And it will be said, 'Call upon your 'partners' [i.e., false deities],' so they will call upon them, but they will not respond to them, and they will see the punishment. If only they had been guided!
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute futility of associating partners with Allah in worship, as even those false deities will disown their worshippers on the Day of Judgment when they are in dire need of help, revealing the depth of their misguidance and the consequences of their deviation from true guidance.

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will call them and say, 'What did you answer the messengers?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the accountability of individuals on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that every person will be questioned about their response to the divine messages conveyed by the prophets, highlighting the gravity of rejecting or heeding those messages.

translation: And the tidings were obscured from them on that Day, so they will not ask one another.
interpretation: This verse highlights the overwhelming nature of the Day of Judgment, where the severity of the events will be so intense that people will be unable to comprehend or discuss the situation with one another, reflecting a state of shock and helplessness.

translation: But as for he who repented, believed, and did righteousness, perhaps he will be among the successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of sincere repentance, faith, and righteous deeds, suggesting that such a combination is the path to ultimate success in the sight of Allah, regardless of past misdeeds.

translation: And your Lord creates what He wills and chooses; not for them was the choice. Exalted is Allah and high above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah in creation and choice, affirming that His will and selection are unchallenged and supreme, while human beings have no independent power to dictate or alter divine decree.

translation: And your Lord knows what their breasts conceal and what they declare.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's omniscience and awareness of both the hidden intentions and the outward actions of people, emphasizing that nothing escapes His knowledge, whether concealed in the heart or openly expressed.

translation: And He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him is praise in the first and the last, and His is the judgment, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and His exclusive right to all praise, both in this world and the Hereafter, while also affirming that all matters of judgment and return ultimately belong to Him.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah made for you the night perpetual until the Day of Resurrection, is there a god other than Allah who could bring you light? Will you not then hear? [i.e., listen and heed]'
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheistic beliefs of the time by highlighting the absolute uniqueness of Allah’s power. It underscores that no other deity—real or imagined—could sustain or alter the natural order, such as the alternation of night and day, which is a sign of Allah’s sole sovereignty over creation. The rhetorical question invites reflection on the absurdity of associating partners with Allah, as no other being possesses the ability to provide light or govern the cosmic order.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah made for you the day continuous until the Day of Resurrection, is there a god other than Allah who could bring you a night in which you could rest? Will you not then see?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute uniqueness and power of Allah by highlighting the natural balance He has established in creation—such as the alternation of day and night—which serves as a sign of His oneness and wisdom, and challenges humans to reflect on their inability to alter or replace this divine order.

translation: And out of His mercy, He made for you the night and the day so that you may rest in it and seek from His bounty, and so that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the creation of night and day, emphasizing that they serve as a balance for human life—providing rest and sustenance—so that people may reflect on Allah’s blessings and express gratitude.

translation: And [mention] the Day He will call them, [saying], "Where are My 'partners' that you used to claim?"
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate futility of associating partners with Allah, as on the Day of Judgment, those false deities will be powerless to respond or aid their worshippers, exposing the falsehood of their claims.

translation: And We have taken witnesses from every nation, then We said, "Produce your proof, if you should be truthful." So they knew that the truth belongs to Allah, and what they used to invent has strayed from them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality of divine truth and the futility of human fabrication in matters of faith. It conveys that God has established clear evidence (witnesses) for every community, and when the truth is presented, those who had deviated through falsehoods realize the supremacy of God’s truth, while their baseless claims collapse under the weight of divine proof.

translation: Indeed, Qarun was from the people of Moses, but he tyrannized over them. And We gave him of treasures whose keys would burden a strong band of people, when his people said to him, 'Do not exult. Indeed, Allah does not like those who exult [in their riches].'
interpretation: This verse serves as a cautionary tale against arrogance and ingratitude, highlighting that wealth and power are not inherently virtuous but are tests from Allah. True success lies in humility, gratitude, and using one's blessings for the benefit of others rather than for self-aggrandizement.

translation: But seek, through that which Allah has given you, the home of the Hereafter; and [yet], do not forget your share of the world. And do good as Allah has done good to you. And desire not corruption in the land. Indeed, Allah does not like corrupters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes a balanced approach to life, urging believers to prioritize the pursuit of the Hereafter while also fulfilling their legitimate worldly needs and responsibilities. It encourages gratitude and reciprocity in goodness, as well as active engagement in improving society, but strictly prohibits any form of corruption or mischief, highlighting that such actions are contrary to Allah's will.

translation: He said, "I was only given it because of knowledge I have." Did he not know that Allah had destroyed before him generations of those who were greater than him in power and had gathered more wealth? But the criminals are not asked about their sins.
interpretation: This verse critiques the arrogance of those who attribute their success or wealth solely to their own knowledge or effort, ignoring the divine will and the fate of previous nations who were destroyed despite their power and resources, highlighting the folly of attributing ultimate control to human means rather than recognizing Allah's sovereignty over all outcomes.

translation: So he came out before his people in his adornment. Those who desired the life of this world said, 'If only we had like what Qarun has been given! Indeed, he is one of great fortune.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to covet the material wealth and status of others, often overlooking the transient nature of worldly possessions and the potential consequences of such desires.

translation: And those who were given knowledge said, "Woe to you! The reward of Allah is better for he who believes and does righteousness." And none are granted it except the patient.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between worldly temptations and the eternal reward of Allah for the believers who remain steadfast in their faith and righteous deeds. It emphasizes that true success lies in patience and trust in Allah's promise, rather than fleeting worldly gains.

translation: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling-place. Then he had no party to help him against Allah, nor was he of those who could save themselves.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power of Allah and the futility of seeking protection or salvation outside of Him, as demonstrated by the divine punishment of a tyrant who defied Allah's commands—highlighting that no earthly power or alliance can avert Allah's decree.

translation: And those who had longed for his position the day before began saying, "Indeed, it is Allah who extends provision to whom He wills of His servants and restricts it. If it were not for Allah’s favor upon us, He would have caused the earth to swallow us! Indeed, it is evident that the disbelievers will never succeed."
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and ingratitude of those who envied the elevated status of a righteous person, only to later realize the divine wisdom behind Allah’s distribution of provision and trials. Their sudden acknowledgment of Allah’s absolute power over sustenance and punishment reflects a moment of forced humility, yet their underlying disbelief remains exposed, as they still associate failure with disbelief rather than recognizing Allah’s greater plan.

translation: But the Home of the Hereafter We assign to those who seek neither high-handedness nor mischief on earth. And the end is best for the God-conscious.
interpretation: This verse underscores that the ultimate reward in the Hereafter is reserved for those who avoid arrogance and oppression in this world, instead embodying piety and righteousness, as their conduct aligns with divine principles rather than worldly power or corruption.

translation: Whoever comes with a good deed will have [a reward] better than it; and whoever comes with an evil deed - then those who did evil deeds will not be recompensed except [with that] which they used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and mercy, emphasizing that good deeds are rewarded with greater good, reflecting Allah's generosity, while evil deeds are met with commensurate consequences, highlighting the accountability of human actions.

translation: Indeed, He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an will bring you back to a place of return. Say, 'My Lord is most knowing of who brings the guidance and who is in manifest error.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine justice and the accountability of all individuals. It reassures the Prophet (peace be upon him) that Allah, who has entrusted him with the Qur'an, will ultimately guide him to the truth and justice, while those who reject the guidance will face clear and undeniable error. It also serves as a reminder that Allah alone possesses perfect knowledge of who is rightly guided and who is astray, emphasizing human dependence on divine wisdom.

translation: And you were not expecting that the Book would be given to you except as a mercy from your Lord. So never be a supporter of the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and purpose of the Qur'an as a mercy from Allah, emphasizing that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) did not seek or anticipate this revelation for personal gain or worldly motives. It warns against aligning with or supporting those who reject faith, as their rejection contradicts the very essence of the Qur'an's message of guidance and mercy.

translation: And let not those who disbelieve divert you from the verses of Allah after they have been revealed to you. But invite to your Lord and be not of those who associate others with Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a directive to remain steadfast in faith and purpose, resisting any external influences that may deter one from adhering to the divine guidance. It emphasizes the importance of unwavering commitment to monotheism and the propagation of faith, while cautioning against the pitfalls of idolatry and associating partners with Allah.

translation: And do not invoke with Allah any other god. There is no god except Him. Everything will perish except His Face. To Him belongs the command, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and warns against associating any partners with Him, which is the gravest sin in Islam (shirk). It also highlights the transient nature of worldly existence compared to the eternal nature of Allah's essence ('His Face'), reinforcing the concept of divine sovereignty and the ultimate return of all creation to Him for judgment.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.
interpretation: This verse introduces the Qur'an as a divine revelation, emphasizing Allah's attributes of mercy and compassion, which are foundational to understanding the subsequent guidance and teachings within the text.

translation: Do the people think that they will be left alone because they say, "We believe," and they will not be tested?
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of trials and tribulations in the life of a believer, even after professing faith. It serves as a reminder that true faith is not merely a verbal declaration but is proven through patience, perseverance, and steadfastness in the face of hardships. The verse implies that trials are a means of purification and a test of sincerity, distinguishing between those who truly believe and those who do not.

translation: And We have certainly tested those before them, so Allah will surely make evident those who are truthful and He will surely make evident the liars.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of trials and tests in life as a means for Allah to distinguish between the sincere and the insincere in their faith and commitment.

translation: Do the evildoers think they can escape Us? How wretched is their judgment!
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against arrogance and complacency in wrongdoing, asserting that no one can evade divine justice regardless of their perceived power or cunning. It underscores the folly of those who believe they can outmaneuver God’s decree, emphasizing the ultimate accountability of all actions in the Hereafter.

translation: Whoever expects to meet Allah, then the appointed time of Allah is surely coming. And He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of the Day of Judgment and the inevitability of meeting Allah, encouraging believers to live with the awareness of accountability and divine justice, while reminding them that Allah is fully aware of all intentions and deeds.

translation: And whoever strives (in the cause of Allah), strives only for himself. Indeed, Allah is free from need of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that acts of worship, righteousness, and striving in the path of Allah are ultimately for the benefit of the individual's own soul and spiritual growth, not because Allah needs them. It underscores Allah's absolute self-sufficiency and independence from all creation, while highlighting the personal responsibility of each person to seek righteousness and closeness to Allah.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will surely remove from them their misdeeds and will surely reward them the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mercy and justice that accompanies true faith and righteous action, ensuring that believers are purified of their sins and rewarded abundantly for their good deeds, reflecting Allah's boundless generosity and the transformative power of sincere devotion.

translation: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. To Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of kindness and respect toward parents while establishing a clear boundary when their demands conflict with the fundamental tenets of faith. It teaches that devotion to God takes precedence over parental wishes, even if those wishes are well-intentioned, and that ultimate accountability rests with God alone.

translation: And [as for] those who believe and do righteous deeds, We will surely admit them among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle that true faith is inseparable from righteous action; it is not merely a matter of belief in the heart but must be demonstrated through deeds that align with divine guidance. The promise of admission among the righteous reflects Allah's justice and mercy, rewarding those who embody both faith and righteous conduct with eternal companionship in the highest ranks of Paradise.

translation: And among the people are those who say, "We believe in Allah," but when they are harmed for [the sake of] Allah, they consider the trial of the people as [if it were] the punishment of Allah. But if victory comes from your Lord, they will surely say, "Indeed, we were with you." Is not Allah most knowing of what is within the hearts of all creatures?
interpretation: This verse critiques the hypocrites who claim faith but abandon it when faced with hardship, only to reaffirm their loyalty when success arises, exposing their insincerity and the true state of their hearts.

translation: And Allah will surely make evident those who believe, and He will surely make evident the hypocrites.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's ultimate knowledge and the eventual manifestation of truth, where genuine faith and hidden hypocrisy will be clearly distinguished, often through trials or decisive events.

translation: And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, 'Follow our way, and we will bear your sins.' But they will not bear anything of their sins. Indeed, they are liars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and deceitfulness of the disbelievers who falsely promise to take on the sins of believers if they follow their path, while in reality, no one can bear the burden of another's sins except by Allah's will, as stated in the Qur'an (e.g., 53:38). It underscores the futility of their claims and the moral corruption of their offer, revealing their true intention to mislead others away from the truth.

translation: And [then] they will surely carry their own burdens and [other] burdens along with their burdens, and they will surely be questioned on the Day of Resurrection about what they used to invent.
interpretation: This verse warns against the grave sin of attributing falsehood to Allah or fabricating lies in His name, as those who do so will bear not only their own sins but also the burden of their falsehoods, which will be exposed and questioned on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And We certainly sent Noah to his people, and he remained among them for a thousand years minus fifty years, and the flood seized them while they were wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of persistent wrongdoing and the limits of divine forbearance. Despite Noah's prolonged efforts to guide his people, their refusal to heed his message led to their destruction, illustrating that divine punishment is a response to sustained injustice rather than an arbitrary act.

translation: So We saved him and those with him in the ship, and made it a sign for all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine intervention in the story of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) and his followers, emphasizing God's power to save the righteous and establish a lasting sign (the Ark) as a reminder of His mercy and justice for all people across time.

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Abraham said to his people, 'Worship Allah and fear Him. That is best for you, if you should know.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the fundamental call of all prophets: the worship of Allah alone and the avoidance of associating partners with Him, while emphasizing that true guidance and benefit lie in submitting to Allah's commandments out of reverence and awareness of His sovereignty.

translation: You worship only idols besides Allah, and you invent falsehood. Indeed, those you worship besides Allah do not possess the provision for you, so seek provision from Allah and worship Him and be grateful to Him. To Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of worshipping anything other than Allah, as such objects or beings lack the power to provide sustenance or any true benefit. It calls for sincere monotheism (tawhid), directing believers to seek their sustenance and ultimate return only to Allah, emphasizing gratitude as a fundamental aspect of worship.

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already before them denied nations. And upon the Messenger is only [the duty of] clear notification.
interpretation: This verse underscores the historical precedent of rejection faced by previous messengers, emphasizing that denial of the truth is not unique to the current audience but has been a recurring pattern throughout human history, while reaffirming the prophetic role as one of conveying the message clearly rather than coercing belief.

translation: Have they not seen how Allah originates the creation, then repeats it? Indeed, that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute power and control over all existence, emphasizing that just as He effortlessly initiates creation, He can just as effortlessly resurrect it on the Day of Judgment, serving as a reminder of divine omnipotence and the inevitability of resurrection.

translation: Say, 'Travel throughout the earth and observe how Allah began creation.' Then Allah will bring about the final creation. Indeed Allah, over all things, is competent.
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on the signs of Allah in the natural world as a means to affirm His power and wisdom, particularly regarding the resurrection and the Hereafter, by drawing an analogy between the initial creation and its recreation.

translation: He punishes whom He wills and has mercy upon whom He wills. And to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over both punishment and mercy, emphasizing that these are not arbitrary but based on His infinite wisdom and justice. It serves as a reminder of human accountability and the ultimate return to Allah, where true justice and recompense will be fully realized.

translation: And you will never escape [from Allah] in the earth or in the sky. And besides Allah, you have no protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah, emphasizing that no one can evade His grasp or control, whether on earth or in the heavens. It also highlights the futility of seeking protection or assistance from anything or anyone other than Allah, as He alone possesses true guardianship and support.

translation: But those who disbelieved in the signs of Allah and in [their] meeting with Him - those have despaired of My mercy, and it is for them a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality of despair for those who reject divine signs and deny the inevitability of meeting Allah, emphasizing that such rejection severs all hope of mercy and ensures a severe, inescapable punishment.

translation: But the only answer of his people was that they said, "Kill him or burn him." But Allah saved him from the fire. Indeed in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith and divine protection granted to those who remain steadfast in their belief despite facing severe persecution and adversity. It underscores the idea that true believers are tested, but their trust in Allah's plan ultimately prevails, serving as a lesson in perseverance and divine justice for those who reflect on such signs.

translation: And they say, 'Indeed, we have taken besides Allah idols for affection between us in the life of this world.' But on the Day of Resurrection, they will deny one another and curse one another, and their refuge will be the Fire, and they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of placing love and devotion in anything other than Allah, as such attachments will ultimately lead to betrayal and denial on the Day of Judgment, resulting in eternal loss and punishment.

translation: So Lot believed in him (Abraham). And he said, 'Indeed, I will emigrate to my Lord. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith and trust of Prophet Lot (Lut) in Prophet Abraham (Ibrahim) and in the divine plan. It also underscores the concept of migration (hijrah) for the sake of faith, demonstrating submission to Allah's command and seeking refuge in His power and wisdom.

translation: And We gave him Isaac and Jacob and placed in his descendants prophethood and scripture, and We gave him his reward in this world, and indeed, he is in the Hereafter among the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon the Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him), emphasizing the continuity of prophethood and divine guidance through his lineage, culminating in the final prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him). It also underscores the concept of divine justice, where righteousness in this world is rewarded with ultimate success in the Hereafter.

translation: And [We sent] Lot when he said to his people, 'Indeed, you commit such immorality as no one has preceded you with from the worlds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of Lot's people's transgression, highlighting that their sin of homosexuality was unprecedented in human history, thereby emphasizing its extreme depravity and the necessity of divine intervention to punish such grave moral corruption.

translation: Do you indeed approach men and cut off the road and commit outrages in your assemblies?' There was no other answer from his people except that they said, 'Bring us the punishment of Allah if you should be of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral depravity of a people who engage in unnatural and harmful acts, disrupt societal order, and openly defy divine commandments, yet demand immediate punishment for those who expose their wrongdoing, revealing their arrogance and refusal to repent.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, grant me victory over the corrupt people.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the supplication of a righteous servant seeking divine intervention against those who spread corruption and injustice in the world, highlighting the believer's reliance on Allah's power to overcome oppression and restore justice.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Abraham with the good tidings, they said, 'Indeed, we are going to destroy the people of this town, for its people have been wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice where wrongdoers are given fair warning before punishment, and it underscores the principle that divine intervention is a response to persistent injustice rather than arbitrary action.

translation: He said, 'Indeed, in it is Lot.' They said, 'We are more knowing of who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she is of those who remain behind.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between divine knowledge and human presumption. Despite the angels' clear indication that Lot (peace be upon him) was among those to be saved, the people of Lot arrogantly claimed superior knowledge, only to be proven wrong when divine decree spared Lot and his household (except his wife, who perished due to her disbelief). It underscores the futility of human arrogance in the face of God's will and the importance of humility in recognizing divine authority.

translation: And when Our messengers came to Lot, he was distressed for them and felt straitened for them. And they said, 'Fear not, nor grieve. Indeed, we will save you and your family, except your wife; she is of those who remain behind.',
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine protection granted to the righteous while emphasizing the consequences of disbelief. Lot's distress reflects his righteous concern for his people's wrongdoing, but the angels reassure him of salvation for him and his family, excluding his wife, who is condemned for her association with the wrongdoers. This underscores the principle that divine mercy is tied to faith and righteousness, not lineage or familial ties.

translation: Indeed, We are going to bring down upon the people of this city a punishment from the sky because of their defiance.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine principle of accountability, where persistent defiance against God's commands and moral transgressions invite severe consequences, serving as both a warning and a reminder of the importance of righteousness and submission to divine will.

translation: And We have left of it a clear sign for people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and contemplation over blind imitation, urging believers to seek understanding and wisdom in the signs left by Allah in creation and revelation.

translation: And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb. He said, 'O my people, worship Allah and expect the Last Day and do not commit abuse on the earth, spreading corruption.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of monotheistic worship and the accountability of the Hereafter, while warning against societal corruption and injustice, highlighting the moral and spiritual duties of individuals towards both God and their community.

translation: But they denied him, so the earthquake seized them, and they became motionless in their homes.
interpretation: This verse underscores the swift and decisive nature of divine punishment for those who reject the truth despite clear signs, serving as a warning against arrogance and ingratitude.

translation: And [We destroyed] 'Aad and Thamud, and it has become clear to you from their dwellings. Satan made their deeds appealing to them and thus averted them from the [right] way, even though they were perceptive.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against the destructive consequences of succumbing to the temptations of Satan, even when one possesses the ability to discern right from wrong. It highlights the peril of allowing misguided desires to obstruct the path of truth, emphasizing that such a choice can lead to ruin, despite initial clarity and insight.

translation: And [We destroyed] Qarun, Pharaoh, and Haman. And Moses had come to them with clear signs, but they were arrogant in the land, and they were not outpacing [Us].
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of human arrogance and defiance in the face of divine signs and warnings. Despite the clear evidence presented to them—through Moses (peace be upon him)—Pharaoh, Qarun, and Haman refused to humble themselves, believing their power and status made them invincible. Their downfall serves as a reminder that no amount of worldly might or arrogance can shield one from the consequences of rejecting truth or opposing divine will. It highlights the transient nature of human power and the ultimate authority of Allah over all affairs.

translation: So each [of the previous nations] We seized for his sin. And among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones, and among them were those whom the blast seized, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned. And Allah would not have wronged them, but it was they who were wronging themselves.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, where punishment is meted out in direct proportion to the sins committed by individuals or nations. It highlights that God does not wrong anyone, but rather, people wrong themselves by their own actions, leading to their downfall. The varied forms of punishment mentioned serve as a reminder of the consequences of transgression and the inevitability of accountability in the divine scheme.

translation: The example of those who take allies other than Allah is like the example of the spider who takes a house. And indeed, the weakest of houses is the house of the spider. If they only knew.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically highlights the fragility and ultimate failure of relying on anything or anyone other than Allah for protection, support, or salvation. Just as a spider's web is delicate and easily destroyed, so too are the alliances or idols people worship instead of Allah—doomed to disappointment and collapse when tested. The verse underscores the futility of such dependence and calls for recognizing Allah as the only true source of strength and security.

translation: Indeed, Allah knows whatever they invoke besides Him. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute knowledge and sovereignty, affirming that nothing escapes His awareness, not even the false deities or objects of worship that people invoke besides Him. The attributes 'Exalted in Might' and 'Wise' highlight His unmatched power and perfect wisdom, reinforcing the futility of associating partners with Him and the necessity of directing all worship solely to Him.

translation: And these examples We present to the people, but none will understand them except those of knowledge.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of deep understanding and wisdom in comprehending the divine signs and parables in the Qur'an, implying that true comprehension is a gift granted to those who possess knowledge and reflection.

translation: Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth. Indeed, in that is a sign for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and purposeful design of creation, serving as a clear proof of Allah's existence and power for those who reflect with faith.

translation: Recite what has been revealed to you of the Book and establish prayer. Indeed, prayer prohibits immorality and wrongdoing, and the remembrance of Allah is greater. And Allah knows what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of both reciting and living by the Qur'an, as well as the transformative power of prayer in purifying one's character. It highlights that true remembrance of Allah elevates the believer above mere ritual, fostering a consciousness of divine presence that naturally deters moral corruption.

translation: And do not argue with the People of the Book except in the best manner, unless it is with those who wronged among them. And say, "We believe in what was revealed to us and what was revealed to you. And our God and your God is One, and to Him we submit."
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of engaging in dialogue with followers of other Abrahamic faiths (People of the Book) in a manner that is respectful, just, and based on common ground, while also drawing a clear boundary against those who act unjustly or aggressively. It underscores the shared belief in the oneness of God and the submission to Him, highlighting the unity of divine origin in religious teachings.

translation: And thus We have sent down to you the Book [i.e., the Qur'an]. So those to whom We have given the Book believe in it, and among these [i.e., the Arabs] are some who believe in it. And none deny Our signs except the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual response to the Qur'an: those who were already recipients of divine scriptures (like the People of the Book) recognize its truth, while some among the Arabs also affirm it. However, the rejection of Allah's signs is a trait exclusive to the disbelievers, emphasizing that denial stems from arrogance or willful ignorance rather than genuine intellectual or spiritual deficiency.

translation: And you, [O Muhammad], were not a reader of any scripture before it, nor did you write it with your right hand. Otherwise, the falsifiers would have had [cause for] doubt.
interpretation: This verse underscores the miraculous nature of the Qur'an, emphasizing that its revelation is beyond human capability, thereby affirming its divine origin and the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) without any possibility of fabrication or human intervention.

translation: Nay, but they are clear revelations in the hearts of those who have been given knowledge. And none deny Our revelations save the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound impact of divine revelations on those who possess true knowledge and understanding, suggesting that such revelations resonate deeply within their hearts, affirming their truth. Conversely, it underscores that denial of these signs is not due to a lack of evidence but stems from a deliberate rejection rooted in injustice and arrogance, as only the wrongdoers persist in such denial despite the clarity of the signs.

translation: And they say, 'Why has not a sign been sent down to him from his Lord?' Say, 'The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the misconception that divine signs alone can compel belief, while the true purpose of revelation is to guide those who seek truth and to warn those who reject it, emphasizing that the authority of the message lies with Allah, not in the demand for miracles.

translation: Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book which is recited to them? Indeed, in that is a mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound mercy and guidance of the Qur'an, emphasizing that its revelation alone is a sufficient sign of Allah's favor and a reminder for those who have faith, underscoring the importance of belief in recognizing divine blessings.

translation: Say, 'Sufficient is Allah between me and you as a witness. He knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth.' And those who believe in falsehood and disbelieve in Allah—it is they who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and omniscience of Allah, emphasizing that no falsehood or disbelief can escape His knowledge or justice. It serves as a warning to those who reject the truth, affirming that their denial does not diminish Allah’s authority but instead seals their fate as losers in the ultimate reckoning.

translation: And they urge you to hasten the punishment. And if not for a specified term, the punishment would have already come to them. But it will surely come to them suddenly while they perceive not.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom in delaying punishment, highlighting that Allah's timing is precise and inevitable, contrasting human impatience and the suddenness of divine reckoning that catches people unprepared.

translation: They urge you to hasten the punishment. And indeed, Hell will encompass the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the disbelievers' impatience and arrogance in demanding immediate punishment for their disbelief, while ignoring the inevitability of their eventual reckoning in Hell, which will fully encompass them as a consequence of their rejection of faith.

translation: The Day the punishment will overwhelm them from above them and from beneath their feet, and He will say, "Taste what you used to do."
interpretation: This verse underscores the inescapable and comprehensive nature of divine punishment on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that no aspect of a person's life or existence will be beyond the reach of accountability, as even their most hidden actions will be exposed and reckoned.

translation: O My servants who have believed, indeed My earth is spacious, so worship only Me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless mercy and opportunity for spiritual growth granted by Allah, urging believers to remain steadfast in their faith and devotion despite any hardships or constraints they may perceive, as true worship is not limited by physical or worldly limitations.

translation: Every soul will taste death. Then to Us you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of death for all beings and the ultimate return to Allah for judgment, emphasizing accountability and the transient nature of worldly life.

translation: But those who believe and do righteous deeds—We will surely lodge them in chambers of Paradise, beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide eternally. Excellent is the reward of the workers [of good].
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine recompense for true faith and righteous action, emphasizing that Paradise is not merely a reward but a permanent, elevated abode of eternal bliss, where the righteous are granted honor and proximity to Allah’s mercy, reflecting the ultimate fulfillment of their devotion and deeds.

translation: They are those who endure with patience and put their trust in their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights two fundamental qualities of the righteous: steadfast perseverance in the face of trials and unwavering reliance on Allah alone, recognizing that ultimate control and support lie with Him.

translation: And how many a creature carries not its own provision. Allah provides for it and for you. And He is the Hearing, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute control over sustenance and provision, emphasizing that all beings—regardless of their ability to provide for themselves—are ultimately dependent on Allah's mercy and wisdom in granting their needs.

translation: And if you ask them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth and subjected the sun and the moon?' they will surely say, 'Allah.' Then how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent human recognition of Allah's absolute power and authority in creation, despite the persistent denial and deviation of those who associate partners with Him, underscoring the irony of their refusal to submit to the One who is undeniably the Creator.

translation: Allah extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts it for him. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of all things.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute sovereignty over sustenance (rizq), emphasizing that He grants or withholds provision according to His wisdom and knowledge, which encompasses all things. It serves as a reminder of divine justice and the importance of trust in Allah's decree, regardless of apparent circumstances.

translation: And if you ask them, 'Who sends down rain from the sky, giving life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness?' they will surely say, 'Allah.' Say, [O Muhammad], 'Praise to Allah'; but most of them do not reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of human nature—acknowledging Allah’s power in creation yet failing to reflect on His signs or submit to His guidance, demonstrating a disconnect between intellectual acknowledgment and spiritual submission.

translation: And this worldly life is not but diversion and play, while the Hereafter is indeed the [eternal] abode. If they only knew.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient and superficial nature of worldly life compared to the eternal and meaningful reality of the Hereafter, urging reflection on the fleeting nature of earthly pursuits.

translation: But when they board a ship, they call upon Allah, sincere in their devotion to Him. But when He delivers them to the land, behold, they associate others with Him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness of human nature, particularly in times of distress versus times of ease. It underscores the tendency of people to turn to Allah sincerely only when they are in dire need, such as during a perilous journey, but to revert to associating partners with Allah or neglecting their devotion when their immediate fears are alleviated and they return to a state of comfort or security.

translation: So they may deny what We have given them, and enjoy themselves. But they will come to know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly enjoyment and the eventual realization of truth for those who reject divine blessings out of ingratitude, arrogance, or disbelief.

translation: Have they not seen that We have made [Makkah] a safe sanctuary, while people are being taken away around them? Then in falsehood they believe, and in the favor of Allah they disbelieve?
interpretation: This verse critiques those who fail to recognize the divine protection and blessings of Allah, instead clinging to falsehood and rejecting His favors despite clear evidence of His grace in their midst.

translation: And who is more unjust than he who invents a lie about Allah or denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not a dwelling in Hell for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of falsely attributing lies to Allah or rejecting divine truth when it is presented, emphasizing that such actions are not only unjust but also warrant severe punishment in the Hereafter, specifically in Hell.

translation: And those who strive for Us, We will surely guide them to Our ways. And indeed, Allah is with the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of divine reciprocity—sustained effort and struggle in the path of faith and righteousness are met with Allah’s guidance and support, reflecting a covenantal relationship where divine assistance is proportional to human commitment and sincerity.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: The opening verse establishes the divine source of the Qur'an and sets the tone for its recitation, invoking Allah's mercy as a foundation for understanding and guidance. The disconnected letters (Alif, Lam, Meem) are a phenomenon in the Qur'an whose meaning is known only to Allah, though some scholars suggest they may signify the miraculous nature of the Qur'an or serve as a reminder of the divine origin of the revelation.

translation: The Byzantines have been defeated.
interpretation: This verse refers to a historical event where the Byzantine Empire suffered a military defeat, which was seen as a sign of divine intervention and a test of faith for the early Muslims, as the Persians, who were then dominant, were not traditionally seen as a major world power in the same way as the Byzantines.

translation: In the nearest land, and they, after their defeat, will overcome.
interpretation: This verse refers to a historical event where a small group of believers, despite initial defeat, will ultimately achieve victory, highlighting divine support and the eventual triumph of truth over falsehood.

translation: In a few years. For Allah is the command before and after. And on that Day the believers will rejoice.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all affairs, past, present, and future, and reassures the believers that their ultimate triumph and joy are guaranteed by divine decree, regardless of the immediate circumstances they may face.

translation: With the help of Allah. He helps whom He wills. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah in granting victory and assistance, emphasizing that divine aid is a matter of His will and wisdom, not human entitlement or effort alone.

translation: Allah has promised, and Allah never breaks His promise, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute certainty and inviolability of Allah’s promises, contrasting it with the limited understanding and awareness of human beings, who often doubt or overlook divine guarantees due to their lack of knowledge.

translation: They know only the outward aspect of the life of this world, while of the Hereafter they are heedless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to focus excessively on the material and superficial aspects of worldly life, often neglecting the deeper, spiritual realities and the ultimate purpose of existence, which is the Hereafter.

translation: Do they not reflect within themselves? Allah created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them only in truth and for a specified term. And indeed, many of the people, of the meeting with their Lord, are disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of reflection and contemplation on the signs of Allah in the universe, which are clear evidence of His existence, power, and wisdom. The 'specified term' refers to the fixed duration of the universe’s existence, culminating in the Day of Judgment. The mention of many people being 'disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord' highlights the irony that despite the overwhelming signs of truth, some persist in denial, neglecting to recognize the inevitability of accountability before Allah.

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and left more traces on the earth, and they cultivated it more than they have cultivated it. And their messengers came to them with clear proofs. And Allah would not have been unjust to them, but it was they who were unjust to themselves.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of reflecting on historical precedents as a means of understanding divine justice and the consequences of human actions. It highlights that Allah does not wrong people by punishing them without cause; rather, their own injustices and transgressions against truth and morality lead to their downfall.

translation: Then the end of those who did evil was that they denied the signs of Allah and used to ridicule them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate consequence of persistent wrongdoing and arrogance: the rejection of divine guidance and mockery of truth, leading to spiritual blindness and divine punishment.

translation: Allah originates the creation, then He repeats it, then to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over all creation, highlighting His ability to bring existence from non-existence and to resurrect the dead, underscoring the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the return of all beings to Allah for ultimate accountability.

translation: And on the Day the Hour [of resurrection] comes, the criminals will be disgraced.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate accountability and divine justice, where the wrongdoers will face public humiliation and disgrace in the Hereafter, stripped of their power and arrogance, as their true deeds are exposed and they are held to account before Allah.

translation: And they will have no intercessors from their [false] gods, and they will be deniers of their [false] gods.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of associating partners with Allah, as these false deities will neither intercede on behalf of their worshippers nor acknowledge them, revealing the ultimate deception of shirk (associating partners with Allah).

translation: And [remember] the Day when the Hour will be established - that Day they will be separated [in groups],
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of the Day of Judgment and the absolute separation that will occur on that Day, where people will be divided based on their deeds and faith, emphasizing divine justice and the final reckoning.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will be in a garden, delighted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate reward for believers who combine faith with righteous actions, highlighting that their reward is not merely spiritual but also a state of profound joy and contentment in Paradise.

translation: But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our signs and the meeting of the Hereafter, they will be brought into the punishment [in full force].
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequence for those who reject faith outright, deny divine signs, and disbelieve in the Hereafter, emphasizing that their punishment is not merely theoretical but an inevitable reality they will face.

translation: So exalted is Allah when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the constant and unwavering praise and glorification of Allah, highlighting that His transcendence and perfection should be acknowledged at all times—both at the start and end of each day, underscoring the cyclical nature of time and the perpetual need for remembrance of the Divine.

translation: And to Him belongs praise in the heavens and the earth, and at the evening and when you appear [i.e., at midday].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the comprehensive and perpetual nature of Allah's praise, which encompasses all creation in the heavens and the earth, and is continuously offered at all times—morning, evening, and midday—highlighting the timeless and all-encompassing sovereignty and majesty of Allah.

translation: He brings forth the living from the dead, and brings forth the dead from the living, and He revives the earth after its death. So will you be brought forth.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power of Allah in creation and resurrection, highlighting the cyclical nature of life and death as a sign of divine omnipotence and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment.

translation: And of His signs is that He created you from dust; then, suddenly you were human beings dispersing [throughout the earth].
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of human creation from humble origins (dust) and the subsequent divine power that transforms it into a living, sentient being capable of spreading across the earth, emphasizing Allah's sovereignty over life and existence.

translation: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates that you may find tranquility in them; and He placed between you affection and mercy. Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural bond and harmony between spouses, emphasizing that their relationship is not merely physical but rooted in emotional and spiritual connection, designed to foster peace, love, and compassion—qualities that reflect divine wisdom and serve as a reminder for those who ponder the signs of Allah.

translation: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the diversity of your languages and colors. Indeed in that are signs for those of knowledge.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity in human languages and colors as a deliberate sign of Allah's power and wisdom, emphasizing that such variations are not random but serve as proofs of divine design, inviting reflection and appreciation of the natural order.

translation: And of His signs is your sleep by night and by day, and your seeking of His bounty. Indeed in that are signs for a people who listen.
interpretation: This verse highlights the signs of Allah's power and mercy in the natural rhythms of human life, such as sleep and the pursuit of sustenance, which serve as reminders for those who reflect and heed divine guidance.

translation: And of His signs is [that] He shows you the lightning [causing] fear and aspiration, and He sends down rain from the sky by which He revives the earth after its death. Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of divine signs—how they evoke both fear and hope, reflecting the human response to divine power and mercy, and underscoring the importance of reflection and reason in recognizing God's signs in the natural world.

translation: And of His signs is that the heavens and the earth stand firm by His command. Then when He calls you with a single call, from the earth you will emerge.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and control of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that the heavens and the earth exist and function solely by His command, demonstrating His sovereignty and the inevitability of resurrection and the Day of Judgment.

translation: To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are obedient to Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over all creation, highlighting that every entity in the heavens and the earth submits to His will, whether consciously or by the natural order He has established.

translation: And He is the One who begins creation; then He repeats it, and it is [even] easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest attribute in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and wisdom, highlighting that the act of recreating what He has already created is trivial for Him, underscoring His omnipotence and the ease with which He can bring about resurrection and recompense, while also affirming His supreme attributes that transcend all creation.

translation: Allah presents an example from yourselves. Do you have among those whom your right hands possess any partners in what We have provided for you so that you are equal in it [and] you would fear them as your fear each other? Thus do We detail the verses for a people who use reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absurdity of associating partners with Allah by drawing a parallel to human relationships. It questions whether a master would share his wealth or authority equally with his slaves to the point of fearing them as he fears his peers, which is inherently illogical. The verse underscores the uniqueness and supremacy of Allah’s oneness (Tawheed) and serves as a rational argument against shirk (associating partners with Allah), emphasizing that such a notion is as irrational as a master treating his slaves as equals in power and fear.

translation: But those who wronged followed their own desires without knowledge. So who can guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And they will have no helpers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of following one's desires blindly without seeking true knowledge or guidance, emphasizing that such a path leads to spiritual deviation, and only Allah can guide or misguide as part of His divine wisdom.

translation: So set you your face to the straight and right religion, the natural way of Allah upon which He has created mankind. There is no altering in Allah’s creation. That is the straight religion, but most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the innate human disposition (fitrah) towards monotheism and moral uprightness, which is the natural state in which Allah created humanity. It underscores the unchangeable nature of this divine design and the correctness of the straight path (Islam), while lamenting the widespread ignorance or deviation from this primordial truth.

translation: Turning to Him in repentance, fear Him, establish prayer, and do not be among the polytheists.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere repentance, God-consciousness, and consistent worship while warning against associating partners with Allah, highlighting the core principles of monotheism and devotion.

translation: Have you seen he who has made his religion [seem distinct] and he is divided into factions, each party rejoicing in what it has?
interpretation: This verse critiques those who fragment their religion into sects and factions, each clinging to their own interpretations or beliefs with misplaced pride, failing to recognize the unity and universality of true faith.

translation: And when harm touches the people, they call upon their Lord, turning to Him in repentance. Then when He gives them a taste of mercy, behold, a party of them associate others with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness of human nature in times of distress versus prosperity, illustrating how people often turn to God sincerely in hardship but revert to arrogance or idolatry when blessings are bestowed upon them.

translation: So that they may deny what We have granted them. So enjoy yourselves; you will soon come to know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the blessings and guidance bestowed upon them by Allah, urging them to enjoy their worldly life while it lasts, for they will ultimately face the consequences of their disbelief and ingratitude.

translation: Or have We sent down to them an authority, so it speaks about what they used to associate with Him?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion that idols or false deities have any divine authority or power to speak or act, emphasizing that such associations are baseless and devoid of truth.

translation: And when We give the people a taste of mercy, they rejoice in it; but if evil afflicts them for what their hands have put forth, immediately they despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness of human nature in responding to divine blessings and trials, where people often become arrogant in prosperity and despair in adversity, failing to recognize the deeper purpose behind both.

translation: Do they not see that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the distribution of sustenance, emphasizing that Allah's control over provision is a test of faith and a reminder of His absolute power and justice, urging believers to trust in His decree rather than questioning His wisdom.

translation: And give the relative his right, and the needy, and the wayfarer. That is best for those who desire the countenance of Allah. And it is they who will be successful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the moral and spiritual obligation of providing for one's family, the poor, and travelers, framing such charity as a means to seek Allah's pleasure and attain true success, underscoring that righteousness is measured not by mere ritual but by compassionate action.

translation: And whatever you give for interest to increase within the wealth of people will not increase with Allah. But whatever you give in charity, seeking the countenance of Allah—it is they who will have multiplied [reward],
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of usury (riba) in the sight of Allah, as it does not bring true growth or blessing, while charity (zakat) given sincerely for the sake of Allah is divinely multiplied in reward and spiritual benefit.

translation: It is Allah who created you, then provided for you, then will cause you to die, then will give you life. Is there among your 'partners' any that can do any of that? Exalted is He and high above what they associate [with Him].
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute uniqueness and omnipotence of Allah by highlighting His exclusive control over the fundamental aspects of human existence—creation, sustenance, death, and resurrection—while simultaneously negating the power of any false deities or partners that humans might associate with Him.

translation: Corruption has appeared throughout the land and sea because of what the hands of people have earned, so He may let them taste part of what they have done that they may return [to righteousness].
interpretation: This verse highlights the causal relationship between human actions and the resulting corruption in the world, suggesting that moral and ethical failings lead to societal and environmental decay, urging reflection and repentance.

translation: Say, 'Travel throughout the earth and observe how was the end of those before. Most of them were associators [with Allah].'
interpretation: This verse encourages reflection on historical consequences of disbelief and idolatry, urging believers to learn from past nations who rejected divine guidance, thereby emphasizing the importance of recognizing Allah's oneness and the perils of associating partners with Him.

translation: So set you your face to the straight and upright religion, before there comes from Allah a Day which there is no returning for it. On that Day, they will be divided (in groups).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency of adhering to the true and upright path of Islam, as the Day of Judgment is inevitable and irreversible. It serves as a reminder that one's ultimate fate is determined by their actions and faith, and that there will be no second chances or turning back once that Day arrives.

translation: Whoever disbelieves, it is against their own soul; and whoever does righteousness, it is for their own souls.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility in matters of faith and righteousness, highlighting that one's choices directly impact their own spiritual state rather than affecting others.

translation: So that He may reward those who believe and do righteous deeds out of His bounty. Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Allah’s rewards are granted out of His grace and mercy, not as an obligation, and that true faith is demonstrated through both belief and righteous action. It also underscores Allah’s displeasure with disbelief, highlighting the importance of sincerity in faith and the futility of rejecting divine guidance.

translation: And of His signs is [that] He sends the winds as good tidings and to let you taste His mercy and so the ships may sail at His command and so you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the interconnectedness of divine signs in nature, emphasizing that natural phenomena like winds are not random but purposeful acts of God, designed to guide humanity toward recognizing His mercy, seeking His blessings, and fostering gratitude.

translation: And We have already sent messengers before you to their people, and they came to them with clear proofs; then We took retribution from those who committed crimes. And it is incumbent upon Us to support the believers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine principle that Allah sends messengers with clear signs to guide people, and those who reject the truth and persist in wrongdoing will face just consequences. Meanwhile, Allah’s promise to support the believers signifies that divine aid is guaranteed for those who remain steadfast in faith and righteousness, reinforcing the concept of divine justice and the ultimate triumph of truth.

translation: It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir the clouds and spread them in the sky however He wills, and He makes them fragments so you see the rain emerge from within them. Then when He strikes with it whom He wills of His servants, at once they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute control over natural phenomena as a sign of His power and sovereignty, while also illustrating the duality of divine signs—some bring destruction, others bring mercy, and human response depends on whether the sign is perceived as beneficial or harmful.

translation: And indeed, before it was sent down to them, they were in despair.
interpretation: This verse highlights the despair and hopelessness of the people before the revelation of the Qur'an, emphasizing that their state of mind made them receptive to divine guidance when it finally came.

translation: So observe the effects of Allah's mercy—how He revives the earth after its death. Indeed, He will surely bring the dead to life, and He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the power of Allah to bring life to the barren earth as a metaphor for His ability to resurrect the dead, emphasizing divine omnipotence and the inevitability of resurrection, which serves as a reminder of accountability and the consequences of one's deeds in the Hereafter.

translation: And if We send a wind and they see it turning things yellow, they would still remain ungrateful thereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent nature of human ingratitude and disbelief, even when faced with clear signs of Allah's power and mercy, such as the changing of the seasons or the effects of wind on the environment.

translation: Indeed, you [O Muhammad] cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn their backs retreating.
interpretation: This verse highlights the limits of the Prophet's (peace be upon him) ability to guide those who are spiritually dead (unreceptive to truth) or those who deliberately turn away from guidance, emphasizing that ultimate guidance comes from Allah alone.

translation: And you cannot guide the blind out of their error. You can only make hear those who believe in Our signs, and they are Muslims.
interpretation: This verse underscores the limits of human agency in guiding others—true guidance comes only from divine will, and those who respond are those predisposed to faith.

translation: Allah is the One who created you in a state of weakness, then He made after weakness a strength, then He made after strength a weakness and old age. He creates what He wills, and He is the Knowing, the Capable.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of human life and the stages of development and decline that every individual experiences, from weakness in infancy, to strength in youth, to weakness and old age in later years. It serves as a reminder of Allah's absolute power and wisdom in creating and controlling all aspects of existence, urging humans to reflect on their own mortality and dependence on Allah.

translation: And on the Day the Hour appears, the criminals will swear not that they remained [in the world] except for an hour. Thus they were deluded.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief and denial of the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, where they will falsely claim to have only spent a brief moment in the world, despite the overwhelming evidence of their prolonged lives and deeds, reflecting their rejection of divine truth and the consequences of their actions.

translation: And those who were given knowledge and faith will say, 'You have remained, according to the decree of Allah, until the Day of Resurrection. And this is the Day of Resurrection, but you used to not know.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the certainty of the Day of Resurrection and the accountability of all deeds, emphasizing that divine knowledge and faith reveal truths that remain hidden from those who lack them.

translation: So on that Day, the wrongdoers will not benefit from their excuses, nor will they be allowed to seek forgiveness.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality and irrevocability of divine judgment, emphasizing that no amount of justification or plea for mercy will alter the consequences of one's wrongdoing once the Day of Judgment has arrived.

translation: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example. And if you bring them a sign, those who disbelieve will surely say, "You are but inventors."
interpretation: This verse underscores the persistent skepticism of those who reject divine guidance, highlighting that no amount of evidence or miraculous signs can sway hearts hardened by disbelief, as they will always attribute truth to deception or fabrication.

translation: Thus does Allah seal the hearts of those who do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of willful ignorance or rejection of divine guidance—Allah may seal the hearts of those who persistently turn away from truth, making them unable to recognize or accept it.

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad]. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And let them not disquiet you who are not certain [of the Day of Resurrection].
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that divine justice will prevail in the end, despite the mockery and disbelief of those who deny the Hereafter, urging patience and steadfastness in the face of adversity.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Alif, Lam, Meem.
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundational principle of seeking divine guidance and blessings before engaging in any significant endeavor, emphasizing Allah's boundless mercy and compassion as the source of all good. The Arabic letters 'Alif, Lam, Meem' are among the Quranic 'mystery letters' (muqatta'at), whose meanings are known only to Allah, inviting reflection on the depth and wisdom of the Quran's message.

translation: These are the verses of the Wise Book.
interpretation: This phrase introduces the Qur'anic verses as divine signs that carry profound wisdom, emphasizing their role as a source of guidance and truth, not merely as literary or historical texts.

translation: Guidance and mercy for the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights that the Qur'an serves as a source of divine guidance and mercy specifically for those who strive to do good deeds and embody righteousness in their actions and intentions.

translation: Those who establish prayer and give zakah, and of the Hereafter they are certain.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of steadfastness in worship and charitable giving as fundamental aspects of faith, while also emphasizing the certainty of the Hereafter, which serves as a motivating factor for righteous conduct and accountability in this life.

translation: Those are upon [right] guidance from their Lord, and it is those who are the successful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who follow divine guidance and those who do not, emphasizing that true success lies in adhering to the path set by God, which brings both spiritual and worldly fulfillment.

translation: And of the people is he who buys the amusement of speech to mislead [others] from the way of Allah without knowledge and takes it in ridicule. Those will have a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who exploit distractions or deceptive rhetoric to divert people from the truth of Islam, doing so with arrogance and mockery, thereby incurring severe divine retribution for their deliberate misguidance and disrespect.

translation: And when Our verses are recited to him, he turns away arrogantly as if he did not hear them, as if there were deafness in his ears. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of rejecting divine guidance out of arrogance and pride, emphasizing that such defiance leads to spiritual deafness and ultimate punishment.

translation: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - for them are gardens of pleasure.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reward of Paradise for believers who not only affirm faith in their hearts but also manifest it through righteous actions, highlighting the Qur'anic principle that true faith is inseparable from righteous conduct.

translation: They will abide therein forever. [It is] the promise of Allah [which is] truth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
