interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal nature of the reward for the righteous in the Hereafter, underscoring the absolute certainty of Allah's promise, which is guaranteed by His power and wisdom, thereby reinforcing the believer's hope and trust in divine justice.

translation: He created the heavens without pillars that you can see; and He cast into the earth mountains standing firm, lest it should shake with you, and He dispersed throughout it from every creature. And We sent down from the sky water, and caused to grow thereby all kinds of noble pairs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate design and balance in creation, emphasizing that Allah's power is evident in the heavens and earth, which are sustained without visible support, demonstrating His absolute control and wisdom in maintaining the universe's stability and harmony.

translation: This is Allah's creation. Show Me what those besides Him have created. Nay, the wrongdoers are in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute uniqueness and supremacy of Allah’s creation, challenging the false deities worshipped by others to demonstrate any comparable act of creation, thereby exposing the delusion and misguidance of those who associate partners with Allah.

translation: And We certainly gave Luqman wisdom, [saying], "Be grateful to Allah." And whoever is grateful is grateful for [the benefit of] himself. And whoever denies [His favor] then indeed, Allah is Free of need and Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse underscores the intrinsic value of gratitude to Allah, emphasizing that it is not for Allah's benefit but for the believer's own spiritual growth and well-being. It also highlights Allah's absolute self-sufficiency and perfection, independent of human acknowledgment or denial.

translation: And [mention, O Muhammad], when Luqman said to his son while he was instructing him, 'O my son, do not associate [anything] with Allah. Indeed, associating [anything with Him] is a great injustice.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of shirk (associating partners with Allah) as the ultimate form of injustice, highlighting that true monotheism is the foundation of all righteousness and moral integrity.

translation: And We have enjoined upon man [care] for his parents. His mother carried him, [increasing her] in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning is in two years. Be grateful to Me and to your parents; to Me is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of gratitude and devotion to parents, highlighting the immense sacrifice they make—especially the mother, whose hardship begins from pregnancy and continues through nursing and early childhood. It underscores that true gratitude must be directed toward Allah first, as He is the ultimate source of all blessings, while also acknowledging the role of parents in nurturing and raising a child.

translation: But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them. And accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness, and follow the way of those who turn back to Me [in repentance]. Then to Me is your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the balance between filial piety and the absolute oneness of God (Tawhid). It commands respect and kindness toward parents even if they attempt to lead their child into idolatry or sin, but draws a clear boundary: obedience to them must never supersede obedience to God. The instruction to 'follow the way of those who turn back to Me' suggests that true guidance comes from those who repent and submit to God, not from those who lead others astray. The verse ultimately reminds believers that their actions will be accounted for on the Day of Judgment, reinforcing accountability and the primacy of divine will.

translation: O my sons, if you were to be [buried] even as small as a mustard seed, and were it in a rock or [anywhere] in the heavens or in the earth, Allah would bring it forth. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute knowledge and power to resurrect and account for every minute detail, no matter how hidden or insignificant it may seem to human perception.

translation: O my son, establish prayer, enjoin what is right, forbid what is wrong, and be patient over what befalls you. Indeed, [all] that is of the matters [requiring] determination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness in faith and righteous conduct, urging perseverance in prayer, promoting good, preventing evil, and enduring hardships with patience, as these actions require strong resolve and commitment to one's beliefs.

translation: And do not turn your cheek away from people, nor walk through the earth arrogantly. Indeed, Allah does not like whoever is arrogant and boastful.
interpretation: This verse warns against arrogance and disdainful behavior toward others, emphasizing humility and respect in social interactions.

translation: And be moderate in your pace and lower your voice; indeed, the most disagreeable of sounds is the voice of donkeys.
interpretation: This verse advises moderation in all aspects of life, including speech and behavior, as extremes are discouraged in Islam. The comparison to the voice of donkeys serves as a stark reminder of the importance of maintaining a respectful and measured tone, especially in communication, to avoid causing annoyance or discord.

translation: Do you not see that Allah has made subject to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and amply bestowed upon you His favors, [both] apparent and unapparent? But of the people is he who disputes about Allah without knowledge or guidance or an enlightening Book.
interpretation: This verse underscores the vastness of Allah's blessings and the extent of His control over all creation, yet it also highlights the folly of those who engage in baseless disputes about Allah without proper knowledge, guidance, or divine revelation, emphasizing the importance of seeking truth through legitimate means.

translation: And when it is said to them, 'Follow what Allah has revealed,' they say, 'Rather, we will follow what we found our fathers doing.' Even though the devil invites them to the punishment of the Blaze?
interpretation: This verse critiques the blind following of ancestral traditions without examining their validity in light of divine guidance, highlighting the danger of prioritizing cultural or familial customs over truth, especially when those customs lead to deviation and punishment.

translation: And whoever submits himself to Allah while being a doer of good has surely grasped the most trustworthy handhold. And to Allah is the outcome of [all] matters.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere submission to Allah (SWT) combined with righteous actions, highlighting that true faith is not merely in words but in deeds. The 'most trustworthy handhold' symbolizes an unshakable connection to Allah, ensuring steadfastness in faith and guidance. It reassures the believer that ultimate success and resolution of all matters rest with Allah, encouraging trust in His decree and wisdom.

translation: And whoever disbelieves, let not their disbelief grieve you. To Us is their return, and We will inform them of what they did. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and believers that they should not be distressed by the disbelief of others, as their ultimate return and accountability lie with Allah. It underscores Allah's omniscience and the certainty of divine justice, reminding us that no action, whether hidden or manifest, escapes Allah's knowledge.

translation: We let them enjoy for a little while, then We will force them to a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning that worldly comforts and luxuries are temporary and do not guarantee divine favor or protection from ultimate accountability.

translation: And if you ask them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they will surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'All praise is for Allah.' But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of human nature—acknowledging Allah as the Creator yet failing to recognize His right to worship and gratitude, demonstrating a disconnect between intellectual belief and spiritual submission.

translation: To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, Allah is the Self-Sufficient, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute ownership and sovereignty over all existence, highlighting His self-sufficiency (Ghani) and the fact that He is worthy of all praise (Hameed). It underscores the idea that nothing in creation is independent of Him, and all praise and gratitude ultimately belong to Him alone.

translation: And if all the trees on earth were pens and the sea [were ink], replenished thereafter by seven [more] seas, the words of Allah would not be exhausted. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the infinite nature of Allah's knowledge, wisdom, and divine speech, emphasizing that no matter how vast the resources of expression—whether trees as pens or seas as ink—human attempts to capture or convey the entirety of Allah's words are fundamentally limited and inadequate.

translation: He has not created you, nor will He resurrect you, except as a single soul. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of human origin and destiny, underscoring that all of humanity shares the same fundamental nature and will be judged collectively by Allah, who is fully aware of every individual's deeds and circumstances.

translation: Do you not see that Allah causes the night to enter the day and causes the day to enter the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term? And Allah, with what you do, is Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute control over the natural cycles of day and night, as well as the precise and purposeful movement of celestial bodies like the sun and moon, which operate within divinely ordained limits. It serves as a reminder of Allah's omniscience and awareness of human actions, reinforcing the concept of divine governance over all creation and the accountability of human beings for their deeds.

translation: That is because Allah is the Truth, and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood, and because Allah is the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute truth of Allah and the futility of idolatry, emphasizing that all worship and devotion must be directed solely to Him, as He alone possesses ultimate sovereignty and supremacy.

translation: Do you not see that the ships sail through the sea by the favor of Allah that He may show you of His signs? Indeed in that are signs for everyone patient and grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing divine signs in the natural world, urging reflection on Allah's power and benevolence as evidenced by the marvels of creation, such as the movement of ships at sea, which serves as a reminder for those who are steadfast and appreciative in their faith.

translation: And when waves cover them like canopies, they call upon Allah, sincere in their faith in Him. But when He delivers them to the land, some of them become moderate [in faith]. And none reject Our signs except every ungrateful traitor.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to turn to Allah sincerely in times of distress and hardship, seeking His help and mercy. However, once the crisis is over, many people revert to their previous state of moderation or even disbelief, failing to maintain the sincerity and gratitude they displayed during their trials. It underscores the transient nature of human faith and the importance of steadfastness in belief, as well as the consequences of ingratitude and betrayal of one's own principles.

translation: O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when no father will avail his child, nor will a child avail his father at all. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. So let not the worldly life deceive you, nor let the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute accountability of each individual before Allah on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that familial ties and worldly connections will not avail anyone on that Day. It serves as a stark reminder of the transient nature of worldly life and the permanence of divine justice, urging believers to prioritize their relationship with Allah over worldly attachments.

translation: Indeed, Allah [alone] has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs. And no soul perceives what it will earn tomorrow, nor does any soul perceive in what land it will die. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and exclusive knowledge of Allah, emphasizing that human beings lack complete awareness of future events, including their sustenance, lifespan, or place of death. It serves as a reminder of human limitations and the necessity of trusting in Allah's wisdom and divine plan.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Alif, Lam, Mim.
interpretation: The opening of this surah (chapter) begins with the basmala, affirming Allah's attributes of mercy and compassion, which sets the tone for the divine guidance that follows. The disconnected Arabic letters (Alif, Lam, Mim) are a phenomenon known as 'muqatta'at,' whose meaning is known only to Allah, though some scholars suggest they may signify the miraculous nature of the Qur'an itself or serve as a reminder of the divine origin of the revelation.

translation: The revelation of the Book [this Qur'an] in which there is no doubt, is from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine origin of the Qur'an, affirming its absolute truth and authenticity as a revelation from Allah, the Lord of all creation, thereby negating any possibility of doubt or human fabrication in its content.

translation: Or do they say, "He has fabricated it?" Rather, it is the truth from your Lord, so that you may warn a people to whom no warner has come before you, so that they may be guided.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of the disbelievers who accused the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of fabricating the Qur'an. It affirms that the Qur'an is the absolute truth from Allah, sent as a mercy and guidance to humanity, particularly to those who had not received divine guidance before. The verse underscores the Prophet's role as a warner and the Qur'an's purpose in guiding people to the right path.

translation: It is Allah who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days; then He established Himself above the Throne. You have none besides Him as protector or intercessor. Then will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and uniqueness of Allah, highlighting that no one shares His authority or can intercede without His permission, underscoring the importance of remembering and submitting to Him alone.

translation: He arranges [each] matter from the heaven to the earth; then it will ascend to Him in a Day, the extent of which is a thousand years of those which you count.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and control of Allah over all affairs, highlighting the vast difference between divine time and human perception, underscoring the meticulous and encompassing nature of Allah's governance over the universe.

translation: That is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Exalted, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's comprehensive knowledge encompassing all that is hidden and all that is manifest, underscoring His absolute power and mercy, which are intrinsic to His divine nature.

translation: Who perfected everything He created and began the creation of man from clay.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute perfection in His creation, highlighting that every aspect of existence is meticulously designed with wisdom and purpose. The mention of man's creation from clay underscores the humble origin of humanity, reminding us of our dependence on Allah and the transformative power of His will, as He elevates the lowly to a higher purpose.

translation: Then He made his descendants from an extract of a humble fluid.
interpretation: This verse highlights the miraculous nature of human creation, emphasizing that despite the apparent humility and insignificance of the fluid (sperm) from which humans are created, Allah elevates and shapes them with great wisdom and purpose.

translation: Then He proportioned him and breathed into him from His spirit and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique honor bestowed upon humanity by Allah: the infusion of His spirit into Adam, endowing humans with intellect, perception, and emotional depth, yet despite these divine gifts, humans often fail to express gratitude proportionate to these blessings.

translation: And they say, 'When we are lost in the earth, will we indeed be in a new creation?' Rather, they are in [denial of] the meeting with their Lord.
interpretation: This verse addresses the skepticism of those who reject the concept of resurrection and accountability after death, questioning how they could be recreated after being lost in the earth. The deeper meaning highlights their refusal to acknowledge the reality of the Hereafter and the divine justice that awaits them, revealing their ingratitude and denial of Allah's power and wisdom.

translation: Say, 'The Angel of Death who is entrusted with you will take your souls; then to your Lord, you will be returned.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of death and the certainty of return to Allah for judgment, emphasizing human accountability and the transient nature of worldly life.

translation: And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are hanging their heads before their Lord, [saying], 'Our Lord, we have seen and heard, so return us [to the world]; we will work righteousness. Indeed, we are [now] certain.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the profound regret and despair of the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, where they acknowledge their past misdeeds and futilely plead for a second chance, realizing too late the gravity of their actions. It highlights the irreversible nature of the Hereafter and the certainty of divine justice, contrasting their present plea with the absolute finality of their fate.

translation: And if We had willed, We could have given every soul its guidance, but the word from Me has come into effect [that] I will surely fill Hell with jinn and people all together.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah in guiding or misguiding His creation, yet it simultaneously emphasizes His justice—He does not arbitrarily deprive anyone of guidance but fulfills His decree by rewarding the righteous and punishing the unrighteous, as a manifestation of His perfect wisdom and justice.

translation: So taste [the punishment] for having forgotten the meeting of this Day of yours. Indeed, We have [accordingly] forgotten you. And taste the enduring punishment for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine justice and accountability, where the consequence of neglecting one's duties or the remembrance of God in this life is met with a commensurate punishment in the Hereafter, reflecting the absolute justice of Allah's decree.

translation: Only those who believe in Our verses are those who, when they are reminded of them, fall down in prostration and glorify [Allah] with praise of their Lord, and they are not arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the true believers' humility and submission to Allah's signs, demonstrating that genuine faith is accompanied by physical and spiritual humility, devoid of arrogance or resistance to the truth.

translation: Their sides forsake their beds, to pray to their Lord in fear and hope, and they spend out of what We have provided for them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deep spiritual devotion of the believers, who prioritize their relationship with Allah over physical comfort, engaging in worship with a balanced sense of awe (fear of divine punishment) and aspiration (hope for divine reward). Their generosity reflects a recognition that all sustenance comes from Allah, motivating them to spend in His cause selflessly.

translation: No soul knows what has been hidden for them of the comfort of the eyes as a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights the incomprehensible and unparalleled nature of the rewards that await the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing that their ultimate joy and satisfaction—far beyond mere material or sensory pleasures—are divinely ordained as a just recompense for their righteous deeds in this world.

translation: So, is one who was a believer like one who was defiantly disobedient? They are not equal.
interpretation: This verse underscores the fundamental distinction between faith and disobedience, emphasizing that moral and spiritual integrity cannot be equated with rebellion against divine guidance, regardless of superficial similarities.

translation: But as for those who believe and do righteous deeds, they will have the Gardens of Refuge as accommodation for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true faith is inseparable from righteous action, and that the ultimate reward in the Hereafter is directly tied to one's deeds in this life, reflecting divine justice and the principle of accountability.

translation: But as for those who were defiantly disobedient, their refuge is the Fire. Every time they wish to emerge from it, they will be returned to it, and it will be said to them, "Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny."
interpretation: This verse underscores the irreversible and inescapable nature of divine punishment for those who persistently reject faith and righteousness, emphasizing the justice of God's decree and the finality of their fate.

translation: And We will surely let them taste the lesser punishment before the greater punishment, that they might turn back.
interpretation: This verse suggests that Allah may test people with lesser hardships in this life as a reminder or wake-up call, hoping they will repent and return to the right path before facing a greater punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: And who is more unjust than he who is reminded of the verses of his Lord; then he turns away from them? Indeed, We will extract retribution from the criminals.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of rejecting divine guidance after it has been clearly presented, equating such rejection with profound injustice and warning of severe consequences for those who persist in their denial.

translation: And We certainly gave Moses the Scripture, so do not be in doubt about his meeting [with Allah]. And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty of divine revelation and the prophethood of Moses (peace be upon him), urging believers not to doubt his encounter with Allah or the authenticity of the guidance he brought, which was specifically tailored to guide the Children of Israel.

translation: And We made from among them leaders guiding by Our command when they were patient and [when] they were certain of Our signs.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine selection of patient and steadfast believers as leaders who guide others with divine wisdom, emphasizing that true leadership stems from unwavering faith in Allah's signs and steadfastness in trials.

translation: Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority of Allah in resolving disputes and rendering final judgments on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that human disagreements, no matter how contentious, will ultimately be settled by divine wisdom and justice.

translation: Have they not been guided by [the example of] how many generations We destroyed before them, [how they] walked in their dwellings? Indeed in that are signs. Then will they not hear?
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of reflecting on historical consequences as a means of guidance, urging listeners to heed the lessons of past civilizations destroyed for their defiance, rather than remaining heedless of divine signs.

translation: Have they not seen that We drive the water to the barren land and bring forth thereby crops from which their livestock and they themselves eat? Then will they not see?
interpretation: This verse underscores the tangible signs of Allah's power and providence in the natural world, urging reflection on how such evident blessings should lead to recognition of divine authority and gratitude, rather than denial or heedlessness.

translation: And they say, "When will this victory come, if you are truthful?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of the disbelievers towards the promises of divine victory and justice, questioning the timing of its fulfillment despite clear signs and warnings.

translation: Say, [on] the Day of Conquest, the faith of those who disbelieved will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality of judgment and the absolute irrelevance of faith at the moment of truth. It conveys that no amount of belief or adherence to faith in the past will avail the disbelievers when the decisive event (Day of Conquest) arrives, highlighting the irreversible nature of divine justice and the absence of any opportunity for repentance or reprieve at that stage.

translation: So turn away from them and wait; indeed, they are waiting.
interpretation: This verse instructs the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to disengage from those who reject his message and to patiently await the outcome of their actions, trusting in divine justice and timing.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. O Prophet, fear Allah and do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine guidance over worldly influences, emphasizing that even the Prophet (peace be upon him) must prioritize obedience to Allah over the pressures of disbelievers and hypocrites, reinforcing the principle that ultimate wisdom and knowledge belong to Allah alone.

translation: And follow what is revealed to you from your Lord. Indeed, Allah is ever, concerning what you do, Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to divine revelation and guidance, reminding believers that Allah is fully aware of their actions, thus encouraging sincerity and righteousness in their deeds.

translation: And rely upon Allah; and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of placing complete trust in Allah's plan and relying on Him for all matters, as He is the ultimate and sufficient guardian over all affairs.

translation: Allah has not made for any human being two hearts inside his body. Nor has He made your wives, whom you declare to be like your mothers' backs, your [actual] mothers. Nor has He made your adopted sons your [true] sons. That is [merely] your saying by your mouths, while Allah says the truth, and He guides to the way.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute truthfulness of Allah’s commandments and the falsity of human claims that contradict divine wisdom. It rejects the notion that a person can have two hearts or that mere declarations (like those in pre-Islamic adoption customs) can alter reality or divine rulings, emphasizing that Allah’s words are the ultimate truth and the only true guidance.

translation: Call them by [the names of] their fathers; it is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in faith and your clients. And there is no blame upon you for that in which you have erred by mistake, but [only for] what your hearts have intended. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of maintaining justice and clarity in social and familial relationships, even in matters of lineage and identity. It highlights that while biological lineage is valued, spiritual kinship (brotherhood in faith) and loyalty (clientship) are also significant in Islam. The verse also distinguishes between unintentional mistakes and deliberate actions, emphasizing accountability only for what is consciously intended, reflecting Allah's mercy and forgiveness.

translation: The Prophet is more entitled [in authority] over the believers than themselves, and his wives are [in the position of] their mothers. And the relatives are more entitled [to inheritance] in the Book of Allah than the believers and the Muhajirun, except that you do what is right towards your friends. That has been decreed in the Book.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) unparalleled authority and precedence over the believers in matters of guidance, leadership, and spiritual welfare, surpassing even their own self-interests. It also elevates his wives to the status of mothers to the believers, emphasizing their sanctity and respect. The verse further clarifies the priority of inheritance rights among relatives in Islamic law (Sharia), overriding the general rule for believers and Muhajirun (migrants), unless one chooses to honor non-relatives through acts of kindness or bequests—a principle that reflects both divine decree and human agency in upholding righteousness and social bonds.

translation: And [recall, O Prophet,] when We took the covenant from the prophets, and from you [O Muhammad], and from Noah, Abraham, Moses, and Jesus, the son of Mary; and We took from them a solemn covenant.
interpretation: This verse underscores the unity of divine revelation and the shared mission of all prophets, emphasizing that their core message—submission to God and moral accountability—was consistent across time, while their specific laws and practices were tailored to their respective communities.

translation: Let them ask the truthful about their truthfulness. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of truthfulness and warns those who reject faith of severe consequences. It also implies that the truthful will be recognized and vindicated, while the disbelievers will face just retribution for their denial.

translation: O you who have believed, remember the favor of Allah upon you when [an enemy] came upon you and We sent against them a wind and armies [of angels] you did not see. And ever is Allah, of what you do, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of gratitude and remembrance of Allah's favors, especially in times of trial or when facing overwhelming odds. It serves as a reminder that divine assistance can come in unexpected forms and from unseen sources, reinforcing trust in Allah's omnipotence and omniscience.

translation: When they came at you from above you and from below you, and when the eyes grew wild and the hearts rose up to the throats, and you were imagining about Allah various assumptions.
interpretation: This verse describes a moment of extreme distress and fear, where the believers faced overwhelming odds from all directions, both physically and psychologically. The mention of 'various assumptions about Allah' suggests that in such dire circumstances, people's faith may waver, leading to doubts or misconceptions about divine justice, power, or mercy. It highlights the fragility of human trust in Allah when confronted with seemingly insurmountable challenges, while also underscoring the importance of steadfastness and reliance on Allah even in the face of overwhelming adversity.

translation: There, the believers were tested and shaken with a severe shaking.
interpretation: This verse highlights the trials and tribulations faced by believers, emphasizing that such hardships are a test of faith and resilience, intended to purify and strengthen their conviction.

translation: And [remember] when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is disease were saying, "Allah and His Messenger did not promise us except delusion."
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and doubt of the hypocrites and those with weak faith, who dismiss the promises of Allah and His Messenger as mere deception, reflecting their lack of trust in divine truth and the Hereafter.

translation: And when a party of them said, "O people of Yathrib, there is no place for you [here], so return [home]." And a group of them asked the Prophet, saying, "Indeed, our houses are exposed." But they were not exposed; they only desired to flee.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and lack of commitment of some individuals during a critical moment in the early Muslim community. Their words and actions reveal a preference for personal safety over the collective struggle for faith and survival, exposing their true intentions of desertion rather than genuine concern for their homes.

translation: And if they had entered upon them from its [surrounding] regions, and they were indeed asked to cause discord, they would have done it; and they would not have delayed it except briefly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent susceptibility of human beings to discord and division, particularly when external pressures or temptations arise. It suggests that if circumstances or influences from all directions were to incite them toward mischief or discord, they would readily succumb, demonstrating the fragility of their resolve unless they are firmly grounded in faith and righteousness.

translation: And they had already promised Allah before [that] they would not turn their backs [to flee]. And ever is the promise to Allah [that for which He will take account].
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of breaking a solemn pledge made to Allah, emphasizing that such a breach is not merely a personal failing but a matter of divine accountability, as Allah holds all promises to the highest standard of responsibility.

translation: Say, 'Flight will not benefit you if you flee from death or killing. Then [if you do flee] you will not be allowed [to enjoy life] except for a little.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine decree and the futility of attempting to escape one's predetermined fate, whether it be death or any other trial. It serves as a reminder that human efforts to evade what has been ordained by Allah are in vain, and that true benefit lies in submitting to His will and seeking refuge in Him rather than in fleeing from it.

translation: Say, 'Who can protect you from Allah if He intends for you harm or intends for you mercy?' And they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and power of Allah over all affairs, emphasizing that no one can avert His decree—whether it be harm or mercy. It serves as a reminder of human helplessness in the face of divine will and the futility of seeking protection or aid outside of Him.

translation: Allah certainly knows those among you who hinder [others], and [also] those who say to their brothers, 'Come to us,' while they come to battle only a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to support the Muslim community but avoid genuine sacrifice or struggle when it matters most, instead urging others to take risks while they themselves remain passive.

translation: They advance upon you from every side, so when fear comes you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling like one overtaken by death. But when the fear departs, they flay you with sharp tongues, avaricious for spoils. Such have not believed, so Allah has made their deeds worthless, and that is ever easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim faith but abandon their principles when faced with hardship or temptation, only to revert to hostility and greed once the immediate threat subsides.

translation: They think the confederates have not withdrawn; but if the confederates should come [again], they would wish they were in the desert among the Bedouins, inquiring [from afar] about your news. And if they were among you, they would fight not except for a little.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy and lack of true commitment of some who claim to be believers. It suggests that in times of hardship or danger, those who are insincere in their faith would prefer to distance themselves from the community of believers, showing their reluctance to engage in genuine struggle or sacrifice for the cause they superficially support.

translation: Certainly, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example for whoever has hope in Allah and the Last Day, and remembers Allah much.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a model of conduct and virtue for all Muslims, particularly those who seek closeness to Allah and strive for the Hereafter, highlighting that emulating his character and actions is a means to attain divine reward.

translation: And when the believers saw the confederates, they said, 'This is what Allah and His Messenger had promised us; and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth.' And it only increased them in faith and submission.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering faith of the believers in the promises of Allah and His Messenger, even in the face of seemingly insurmountable challenges. It underscores the importance of trust in divine decree and the strength that comes from sincere submission to Allah's will, reinforcing that true faith is not shaken by trials but rather grows stronger through them.

translation: Among the believers are men who have been true to their covenant with Allah. Among them are some who have fulfilled their vow [to the death], and some who are still waiting—but they have never changed [their determination] in the least.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unwavering commitment of true believers to their faith and promises to Allah. It distinguishes between those who have fulfilled their obligations, even at the cost of their lives, and those who remain steadfast in their resolve, awaiting the fulfillment of their duties without wavering in their dedication or compromising their principles.

translation: Allah will reward the truthful for their truthfulness and punish the hypocrites if He wills, or accept their repentance. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine justice and mercy, highlighting that truthfulness is rewarded while hypocrisy is met with punishment unless repentance is sought. It also emphasizes Allah's boundless forgiveness and mercy, which are accessible even to those who have strayed, provided they turn to Him in sincere repentance.

translation: Allah repelled the disbelievers in their rage, they did not obtain any good. And Allah sufficed the believers from fighting. And Allah is All-Powerful, All-Mighty.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power to thwart the plans of the disbelievers, ensuring they gain no benefit from their hostility, while simultaneously protecting the believers from the need to engage in combat. It underscores Allah's strength and authority, affirming that He is the ultimate protector and sustainer of those who have faith in Him.

translation: And He brought down those who supported them from the People of the Book from their fortresses and cast terror into their hearts, [some] you killed, and [some] you took captive.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine support granted to the believers in their military engagements against their adversaries, emphasizing that victory is ultimately from Allah. The mention of terror cast into the hearts of the enemy underscores the psychological impact of divine intervention, reinforcing the idea that true power lies in Allah's hands, not merely in human strength or strategy.

translation: And He caused you to inherit their land, their homes, and their wealth, and [also] land which you had not trodden. And Allah is ever, over all things, competent.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute power and control over all affairs, demonstrating that He can grant victory and inheritance to whom He wills, even without prior effort or struggle on their part, as a test of faith and gratitude.

translation: O Prophet, say to your wives, 'If you desire the life of this world and its adornments, then come, I will provide for you and give you a gracious release.'
interpretation: This verse addresses the Prophet Muhammad's wives, offering them a choice between the transient pleasures of this world and the eternal rewards of the Hereafter, while also affirming the Prophet's commitment to justice and fairness in their separation if they so choose.

translation: And if you women desire Allah, His Messenger, and the Home of the Hereafter, then indeed, Allah has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of prioritizing spiritual and eternal goals over worldly desires, and it highlights the reward for those who align their intentions and actions with the path of Allah and His Messenger.

translation: O wives of the Prophet! If any of you were to commit an open indecency, the punishment for her would be doubled twofold, and that is easy for Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the heightened accountability of the Prophet's wives due to their elevated status and responsibility as role models for the Muslim community, emphasizing that their moral conduct carries greater consequences.

translation: But whoever of you devoutly submits to Allah and His Messenger and does righteous deeds, We will grant her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her an honorable provision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the principle of divine justice and generosity, where sincere submission (qunut) to Allah and His Messenger, combined with righteous actions, is rewarded with multiplied blessings—both in this life and the Hereafter—demonstrating Allah’s boundless mercy and the elevated status of those who strive in faith and righteousness.

translation: O wives of the Prophet! You are not like any other women. If you fear Allah, then do not be soft in speech, lest he in whose heart is disease should be moved with desire; but speak in an honorable manner.
interpretation: This verse instructs the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to maintain a dignified and reserved demeanor in their speech and conduct, particularly to avoid any behavior that could be misinterpreted or exploited by those with impure intentions. It emphasizes modesty and self-restraint as a means of protection against temptation and moral corruption.

translation: And abide in your homes, and do not display yourselves as [was] the display of the former times of ignorance. And establish prayer and give zakah and obey Allah and His Messenger. Allah intends only to remove from you the impurity [of sin], O people of the [Prophet's] household, and to purify you with [extensive] purification.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of modesty, piety, and devotion in the lives of the believers, particularly emphasizing the elevated spiritual status of the Prophet's household (Ahl al-Bayt), whose purity and sanctity are divinely ordained as a means of spiritual purification for all Muslims.

translation: And remember what is recited in your houses of the verses of Allah and wisdom. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Acquainted [with all things].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reflecting upon and internalizing the divine guidance and wisdom that is conveyed within the home, highlighting the role of the household as a space for spiritual nourishment and remembrance of Allah.

translation: Indeed, the Muslim men and Muslim women, the believing men and believing women, the obedient men and obedient women, the truthful men and truthful women, the patient men and patient women, the humble men and humble women, the charitable men and charitable women, the fasting men and fasting women, the men who guard their private parts and the women who do so, and the men who remember Allah much and the women who remember Allah much - Allah has prepared for them forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of gender equality in the eyes of Allah, emphasizing that righteousness and piety transcend gender. It highlights that both men and women who embody these virtues—such as faith, sincerity, patience, humility, charity, and devotion—will be rewarded equally in the Hereafter. The mention of diverse acts of worship and moral conduct reflects the holistic nature of Islamic practice, where both internal devotion (like remembrance of Allah) and external actions (like fasting and charity) are equally valued.

translation: And it is not for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, that they should [otherwise] have any choice in their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority of Allah and His Messenger in matters of faith and guidance, emphasizing that true believers must submit to divine and prophetic decrees without reservation, as deviation from this path constitutes clear misguidance.

translation: And [remember] when you said to the one on whom Allah has bestowed favor and you have bestowed favor, 'Keep your wife and fear Allah,' while you concealed within yourself what Allah is to disclose. And you feared the people, while Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you in order that there not be upon the believers any discomfort concerning the wives of their adopted sons when they no longer need them. And ever is the command of Allah accomplished.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of prioritizing divine commandments over human fears or societal pressures, as demonstrated by the Prophet's (peace be upon him) initial hesitation in marrying Zaynab bint Jahsh, the divorced wife of his adopted son Zayd, due to concern about public opinion. It underscores that Allah's will transcends cultural norms and that divine wisdom governs all matters, ensuring that His commands are fulfilled regardless of human reservations.

translation: The Prophet is not responsible for any hardship in what Allah has decreed for him. This is Allah's established way with those who passed away before. And Allah's command is a determined decree.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet (peace be upon him) that any challenges or hardships he faces are part of Allah's divine plan and not a reflection of his own shortcomings or failures. It also emphasizes the consistency of Allah's sunnah (way) throughout history, where previous prophets and righteous people faced trials as part of their divine mission. The verse underscores the absolute decree of Allah, highlighting that what He ordains is final and will inevitably come to pass, regardless of human resistance or understanding.

translation: Those who convey the messages of Allah and fear Him and do not fear [anyone] except Allah. And sufficient is Allah as Accountant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the qualities of true believers who are entrusted with conveying Allah's messages—they do so with unwavering commitment, prioritizing divine approval over the approval of others, and recognizing Allah alone as the ultimate authority over their actions and accountability.

translation: Muhammad is not the father of [anyone] among your men, [but [he is] the Messenger of Allah and last of the prophets. And ever is Allah, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is not biologically the father of any of the believers, despite being a spiritual and moral guide for them, and that his role as a prophet is final and unparalleled, with no prophet to succeed him.

translation: O you who have believed, remember Allah with much remembrance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of constant and abundant remembrance of Allah in the life of a believer, not just in times of ease or ritual acts, but as a continuous state of consciousness and gratitude.

translation: And glorify Him morning and evening.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the constant remembrance and glorification of Allah, encouraging believers to maintain a perpetual state of praise and worship throughout the day, not limiting it to specific times or rituals.

translation: It is He who confers blessing upon you, as do His angels [asking Him to], that He may bring you out from darknesses into the light. And ever is He, to the believers, Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine mercy and care Allah has for believers, highlighting that His blessings and the supplications of the angels are constant, guiding them from spiritual ignorance and sin (darknesses) to enlightenment and righteousness (light). It emphasizes the active role of Allah’s mercy in the lives of believers, ensuring their spiritual growth and protection.

translation: Their greeting on the Day they meet Him will be 'Peace.' And He has prepared for them a generous reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for believers: eternal peace and security in the Hereafter, underscoring the divine promise of tranquility and honor for those who remain steadfast in faith and righteousness.

translation: O Prophet! Indeed, We have sent you as a witness, and a bringer of good tidings, and a warner.
interpretation: This verse establishes the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) universal role as a witness to the truth of Islam, a bearer of glad tidings for the believers, and a warner against disbelief and its consequences, emphasizing his comprehensive mission to all of humanity.

translation: And inviting to Allah, by His permission, and a shining lamp.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as both a caller to the truth of Islam and a guiding light for humanity, illuminating the path to righteousness through divine revelation.

translation: And give good tidings to the believers that they will have from Allah a great bounty.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers of Allah's boundless generosity and the immense rewards awaiting them in this life and the Hereafter, emphasizing the certainty of divine favor as a source of hope and motivation for steadfastness in faith.

translation: And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and disregard their harm, and put your trust in Allah. And sufficient is Allah as a Trustee.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to remain steadfast in their faith and not be swayed by the pressures or deceptions of those who reject the truth (disbelievers) or those who outwardly claim belief but inwardly harbor doubt or malice (hypocrites). It emphasizes the importance of resilience in the face of opposition and the necessity of placing complete trust in Allah’s protection and guidance, rather than seeking validation or compromise with those who seek to undermine faith.

translation: O you who have believed, when you marry believing women and then divorce them before you have touched them, there is no waiting period for you to count concerning them. But give them [a gift of] compensation and send them away in a good manner.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of fairness and kindness in marital relationships, even in cases of divorce, by mandating a generous compensation ('mut'ah') for the wife when the marriage is dissolved before consummation, reflecting Islam's emphasis on justice and compassion in all dealings.

translation: O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives to whom you have given their dowries and what your right hand possesses of those whom Allah has granted you as spoils of war, and the daughters of your paternal uncles, the daughters of your paternal aunts, the daughters of your maternal uncles, and the daughters of your maternal aunts who emigrated with you, and a believing woman if she offers herself to the Prophet and the Prophet wishes to marry her—this [marriage] is exclusively for you, excluding the [other] believers. We certainly know what We have ordained for them regarding their wives and those whom their right hands possess, so that there may be no discomfort for you. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse grants the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) certain unique dispensations in marriage, highlighting his elevated status and the special considerations made for his role in Islam. The exclusivity of these permissions underscores the Prophet's unique position as a model for Muslims, while also emphasizing that such concessions are not extended to others, reflecting the divine wisdom in balancing personal allowance with communal guidance.

translation: You may defer whom you will of them, and take to yourself whom you will. And whomsoever you desire of those whom you had set aside, there is no blame on you. That is more proper that they should be content, and not grieve, and that they should be pleased with what you give them. Allah knows what is in your hearts. And Allah is Knowing, Forbearing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of fairness and consideration in personal relationships, emphasizing that decisions should be made with the well-being and contentment of all parties in mind, while also acknowledging the complexity of human emotions and the need for understanding and patience in such matters.

translation: It is not lawful for you [O Muhammad] to marry other women after [this], nor to replace any of your wives with another, even if her beauty pleases you, except for those whom your right hand possesses. And Allah is ever, over all things, a Watcher.
interpretation: This verse underscores the unique position of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in terms of marriage, granting him specific dispensations not applicable to the general Muslim community, such as the allowance to marry beyond the usual limit of four wives and the prohibition of replacing wives solely for reasons of beauty or preference.

translation: O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet except when you are permitted for a meal, without awaiting its readiness. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without seeking to remain for conversation. Indeed, that [behavior] used to annoy the Prophet, and he would shy away from [telling you] it. But Allah is not shy of the truth. And when you ask [his wives] for something, ask them from behind a partition. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts. And it is not for you to harm the Messenger of Allah or to marry his wives after him, ever. Indeed, that would be in the sight of Allah an enormity.
interpretation: This verse establishes the sanctity and special status of the Prophet Muhammad's household, setting boundaries for respectful interaction with him and his wives to maintain their dignity and privacy. It emphasizes the importance of avoiding actions that could cause discomfort or harm to the Prophet, reflecting the profound reverence due to him. The instruction to seek permission before entering and to maintain modesty in speech and conduct underscores the need for propriety and restraint in relationships with those in positions of spiritual leadership. The prohibition against marrying the Prophet's wives after his death highlights the unique and eternal respect owed to them, elevating their status beyond ordinary social norms.

translation: Whether you disclose a matter or conceal it, indeed Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute knowledge of Allah, emphasizing that nothing—whether hidden or revealed—escapes His awareness, thereby urging sincerity and mindfulness in all actions and intentions.

translation: There is no blame upon them [the wives of the Prophet] regarding their fathers, their sons, their brothers, the sons of their brothers, the sons of their sisters, their women, or what their right hands possess. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is ever, over all things, a Witness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exceptional status of the wives of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), granting them a level of modesty and protection that transcends ordinary social norms, while also reinforcing the importance of taqwa (God-consciousness) in all aspects of life.

translation: Indeed, Allah and His angels send blessings upon the Prophet. O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and salute him with a worthy salutation.
interpretation: This verse establishes a reciprocal relationship between Allah's grace and the believers' duty, emphasizing that invoking blessings upon the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) is not merely a ritual but a means of aligning oneself with divine mercy and the angelic realm, thereby elevating one's spiritual state.

translation: Indeed, those who harm Allah and His Messenger - Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and prepared for them a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of disrespect or harm directed toward Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him), emphasizing that such actions incur divine wrath and severe consequences in both this life and the Hereafter, reflecting the absolute sanctity of Allah and His Messenger in Islamic belief.

translation: And those who harm believing men and believing women without having they committed any wrong—have [indeed] burdened themselves with slander and manifest sin.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of unjustly harming believers, emphasizing that such actions are not merely moral failings but carry severe spiritual consequences, as they involve false accusation and clear transgression against Allah's commandments.

translation: O Prophet, tell your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers to bring down over themselves [part] of their outer garments. That is more appropriate so that they may be recognized and not harassed. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse instructs Muslim women to observe modest dress (hijab) to be recognized as chaste believers and thereby avoid harassment, reflecting a balance between piety and societal respect, while emphasizing Allah's mercy in setting such guidelines.

translation: If the hypocrites and those with disease in their hearts, and the rumor-mongers in the city, do not desist, We will surely incite you against them; then they will not remain your neighbors therein except for a little while.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of persistent hypocrisy, malice, and social disruption, indicating that divine intervention may arise to address such behavior, leading to their eventual removal or marginalization from the community.

translation: Cursed they will be wherever they are found, they will be seized and massacred completely.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe and irreversible consequences of those who persist in disbelief and enmity against the truth, emphasizing that their fate is sealed by divine decree, regardless of their location or power.

translation: This is the way of Allah that has passed for those who came before; and you will not find any change in the way of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unchangeable nature of Allah's laws and decrees, which have consistently applied throughout history to previous nations and generations.

translation: People ask you about the Hour. Say, 'The knowledge of it is only with Allah.' And what may make you perceive? Perhaps the Hour is near.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over the knowledge of the Day of Judgment (the Hour), reminding humanity of their limited understanding and the transient nature of worldly time, urging them to focus on preparation and righteousness rather than speculation about its timing.

translation: Indeed, Allah has cursed the disbelievers and prepared for them a Blaze.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and irreversible nature of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief, emphasizing that their fate is sealed by Allah’s wrath, reflecting the gravity of rejecting faith and the finality of their punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: They will abide therein forever, not finding a protector nor a helper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the eternal and inescapable nature of the consequences for those who reject faith, emphasizing that in the Hereafter, they will have no one to intercede on their behalf or provide them with any form of support or protection.

translation: The Day their faces will be turned about in the Fire, they will say, "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger."
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound regret and remorse of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, as they realize too late the gravity of their rejection of divine guidance and the consequences of their defiance, underscoring the irreversible nature of their choices and the finality of their fate.

translation: And they will say, 'Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our masters and our great ones, and they led us astray from the [right] way.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to blindly follow authority figures without exercising personal judgment or verifying the truth, leading to deviation from the correct path.

translation: Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.
interpretation: This supplication reflects a plea for severe divine retribution against those who oppose or harm the believers, invoking both intensified punishment and a profound curse, emphasizing the gravity of their transgressions in the sight of Allah.

translation: O you who have believed, do not be like those who harmed Moses, but Allah absolved him of what they said. And he was, in the sight of Allah, distinguished.
interpretation: This verse cautions believers against following the example of those who unjustly criticized and harmed Prophet Moses (peace be upon him), despite Allah ultimately vindicating him. It serves as a reminder to uphold justice, refrain from slander, and trust in Allah’s justice, as He exonerates the truthful and holds the malicious accountable.

translation: O you who have believed, fear Allah and speak words of appropriate justice.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of both piety and righteous speech in the life of a believer. It calls for a conscious awareness of Allah's presence and commandments, coupled with the responsibility to communicate with truth, fairness, and wisdom, avoiding deceit, slander, or harmful words.

translation: He will rectify your deeds for you and forgive you your sins. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly attained a great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of obedience to Allah and His Messenger, suggesting that true faith and righteous deeds lead to both spiritual purification and ultimate success in the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they declined to bear it and feared it; but man [undertook to] bear it. Indeed, he was unjust and ignorant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique burden of moral responsibility that humanity bears, unlike the rest of creation. The 'Trust' (Amanah) refers to the moral and spiritual obligations placed upon humans, including free will, accountability, and the capacity to choose between right and wrong. The heavens, earth, and mountains refused this burden due to their inability to comprehend or uphold it, while humans, despite their flaws (being 'unjust and ignorant'), accepted it. This underscores the divine honor granted to humanity, as well as the moral and spiritual challenges that come with it, emphasizing the need for humility, wisdom, and righteousness in fulfilling this trust.

translation: Allah will punish the hypocrites, men and women, and the polytheists, men and women, and Allah will accept repentance from the believers, men and women. And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine justice and mercy, highlighting that Allah's punishment is reserved for those who persist in hypocrisy and polytheism, while His mercy is extended to those who repent and believe, demonstrating the balance between accountability and forgiveness in Islam.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. [All] praise is [due] to Allah, who owns whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth and [who] has praise in the Hereafter. And He is the Wise, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundation of monotheistic belief by affirming Allah's absolute ownership and sovereignty over all existence, both in this world and the Hereafter, while emphasizing that all praise is due to Him alone. The mention of His wisdom (الحكيم) and knowledge (الخبير) underscores that His decrees and actions are perfect, encompassing both the seen and unseen, and that all praise is ultimately directed to Him for His justice, mercy, and ultimate authority over all outcomes.

translation: He knows what penetrates into the earth and what emerges from it, and what descends from the heavens and what ascends therein. And He is the Most Merciful, the Most Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's comprehensive knowledge and power over all aspects of creation, both seen and unseen, highlighting His attributes of mercy and forgiveness as encompassing all things.

translation: But those who disbelieve say, 'The Hour will not come to us.' Say, [O Muhammad], 'Yes, by my Lord, it will surely come to you. [He is] Knower of the unseen.' Not absent from Him is an atom's weight within the heavens or within the earth or [what is] smaller than that or greater, except that it is in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of the Day of Judgment (the Hour) and refutes the denial of the disbelievers who claim it will never come. It emphasizes Allah’s absolute knowledge and awareness of all things, no matter how small or hidden, reinforcing that nothing escapes His divine decree or record.

translation: So that those who believe and do righteous deeds may be rewarded—those will have forgiveness and a noble provision.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine principle of justice and recompense, highlighting that true faith is inseparable from righteous action, and that Allah’s forgiveness and generous provision are the just rewards for those who embody both.

translation: But those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them—it is they for whom there is a painful punishment of wrath.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences for those who actively oppose or seek to undermine the divine signs (evidence, proofs, or revelations) of Allah, not out of ignorance or misunderstanding, but with deliberate defiance and malice. The 'painful punishment of wrath' signifies not just physical torment but also the spiritual and existential despair that results from rejecting truth in the face of clear evidence, highlighting the gravity of such rebellion against divine guidance.

translation: But those who have been given knowledge see that what has been revealed to you from your Lord is the truth and guides to the path of the Exalted in Might, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who possess true knowledge and those who do not, emphasizing that the divine revelation (the Qur'an) is recognized as truth by those with genuine understanding, guiding them to the path of Allah's absolute power and boundless praise.

translation: And those who disbelieved said, "Shall we direct you to a man who tells you that when you have become completely broken down, you will be created anew?"
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism and mockery of the disbelievers toward the concept of resurrection and the Day of Judgment, questioning the possibility of human beings being recreated after complete disintegration, thereby challenging the core Islamic belief in the afterlife and divine power.

translation: Have they fabricated a lie about Allah, or is there madness in him? Rather, it is those who disbelieve in the Hereafter who are in punishment and [in] extreme error.
interpretation: This verse challenges the integrity of those who deny the truth of the Qur'an or the prophethood of Muhammad (peace be upon him) by attributing falsehood to Allah or questioning His divine wisdom. The deeper meaning underscores the severe consequences of disbelief in the Hereafter, which leads to both punishment in the afterlife and a profound spiritual misguidance in this world, highlighting the gravity of rejecting divine guidance.

translation: Have they not looked at what is before them and what is behind them of the heaven and the earth? If We willed, We could cause the earth to swallow them, or let fall upon them fragments from the sky. Indeed in that is a sign for every servant turning back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse underscores the fragility of human existence and the absolute power of Allah over all creation, serving as a reminder of divine accountability and the consequences of turning away from faith.

translation: And We certainly gave David from Us bounty. [We said], "O mountains, repeat [Our] praises with him, and [so did] the birds." And We made pliable for him iron.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special favors bestowed upon the Prophet David (peace be upon him), including the ability to command nature—mountains and birds—to join him in praising Allah, as well as the unique skill to work with iron, which enabled him to craft armor and benefit humanity. It underscores the concept of divine grace and the interconnectedness of all creation in worship and service to Allah.

translation: That I may fashion for you a coat of mail and perfect it, and that you may weave from it fine and coarse (threads) for you. And you will do righteous deeds. Indeed, I am, of what you do, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of both physical and spiritual productivity, emphasizing that sincere effort in any form of work, when combined with righteousness, is recognized and valued by Allah.

translation: And to Solomon [We subjected] the wind - its morning [journey was that of] a month and its afternoon [journey was that of] a month - and We made flow for him a spring of [liquid] copper. And [We subjected] among the jinn those who worked for him by the permission of his Lord. And whoever of them turned away from Our command, We would make him taste of the punishment of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extent of Allah's power and the submission of nature and supernatural beings to His will, as demonstrated through the subjugation of the wind and the jinn to Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him). It underscores the concept of divine decree and the consequences of defiance against Allah's commands, as those who deviate from His will face severe punishment.

translation: They work for him whatever he wills of sanctuaries, statues, bowls like reservoirs, and stationary kettles. [It was said], "Work, O family of David, with gratitude." And few of My servants are grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extraordinary abilities granted to the family of Prophet David (peace be upon him), where even inanimate objects like statues, vessels, and kettles were crafted to serve divine purposes, reflecting a deep harmony between human skill and divine will. The call to 'work with gratitude' underscores that such blessings are not merely for personal or worldly gain but are opportunities to express thankfulness to Allah, reminding humanity that true success lies in recognizing divine favors and using them in ways that align with divine wisdom.

translation: So when We decreed death for him [Sulayman], nothing indicated to them his death except a creature of the earth eating his staff. Then when he fell, it became clear to the jinn that if they had known the unseen, they would not have remained in the humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the limits of knowledge and power, even for beings like the jinn who possess supernatural abilities. It highlights that true knowledge belongs solely to Allah, and no one—whether human, jinn, or otherwise—can claim to possess the unseen (ghayb) without divine revelation. The jinn's prolonged enslavement to Sulayman (peace be upon him) despite their supposed wisdom serves as a lesson in humility and submission to Allah's decree.

translation: There was for [the tribe of] Saba' in their dwelling place a sign: two gardens, on the right and on the left. [They were told], "Eat from the provision of your Lord and be grateful to Him. [You have] a good land and [forgiving] Lord."
interpretation: This verse highlights the blessings and favors bestowed upon the people of Saba', exemplified by their lush gardens and abundant provisions, which were signs of Allah's mercy. The call to gratitude underscores the importance of recognizing divine favors, while the mention of a 'good land' and a 'forgiving Lord' suggests that these blessings are not merely material but also spiritual, contingent upon their acknowledgment and appreciation of Allah's generosity.

translation: But they turned away, so We sent upon them the flood of the dam, and We replaced their two gardens with two gardens of bitter fruit, thorny trees, and a few lote trees.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the consequences of ingratitude and rejection of divine guidance, where material blessings are replaced with hardship as a test of faith and a sign of divine justice.

translation: That is how We recompense those who disbelieve. And would We recompense except the utterly ungrateful?
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, where those who persistently reject faith and deny the truth are recompensed accordingly. The mention of 'the utterly ungrateful' highlights that ingratitude—whether to God’s signs, blessings, or guidance—is the core of disbelief, and thus the recompense is fitting for such a stance.

translation: And We placed between them and the towns which We had blessed [other] towns visible [from one another], and We apportioned the journey between them: 'Travel through them by night and day, secure.'
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and provision of security for travelers, emphasizing that He has made the path between towns not only visible and accessible but also safe for continuous movement, day and night, ensuring peace and protection for those who traverse it.

translation: But they said, 'Our Lord, distance our journeys from one another,' and wronged themselves, so We made them as tales and dispersed them completely. Indeed in that are signs for every patient and grateful one.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of human arrogance and ingratitude, where people demand separation from divine guidance and then face the fragmentation of their unity and legacy, serving as a lesson for those who endure trials with patience and gratitude.

translation: And indeed, Iblees (Satan) confirmed his assumption about them, so they followed him, except for a group of believers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the deceptive nature of Satan, who exploits human weaknesses and expectations to lead people astray, while true faith acts as a shield against his influence.

translation: And he had no authority over them, except that We might test who believes in the Hereafter from who is thereof in doubt. And your Lord, over all things, is Guardian.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the influence of evil or misguidance is only permitted by Allah to test the faith of individuals, distinguishing between those who truly believe in the Hereafter and those who harbor doubts, while affirming Allah's comprehensive knowledge and guardianship over all things.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "Invoke those you claim [to be gods] besides Allah." They do not possess [even] as much as the weight of an atom in the heavens or on the earth, nor do they have any partnership therein, nor is there for them from Him any assistant.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah alone, emphasizing that any deities claimed besides Him are utterly powerless and devoid of any real authority or control over creation.

translation: And intercession will not benefit with Him except for one whom He permits. [They will say], 'When it is removed from the hearts, they will say, "What did your Lord say?" They will say, "The truth." And He is the Most High, the Grand."
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and unchallenged authority of Allah, emphasizing that no intercession can occur without His explicit permission. It highlights the humility and awe of the angels and believers in the presence of Allah’s majesty, where even the truth is conveyed with reverence and submission to His supreme will.

translation: Say, 'Who provides for you from the heavens and the earth?' Say, 'Allah. And indeed, we or you are either upon guidance or in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah in sustaining all creation and challenges both believers and disbelievers to reflect on their paths—whether they are guided by divine truth or lost in manifest error. It invites introspection and recognition that ultimate provision and guidance come solely from Allah, urging humility and submission to His will.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'You will not be asked about what we committed, nor will we be asked about what you do.'
