interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal accountability in the Hereafter, where each individual will answer only for their own deeds, not for the actions of others, underscoring the principle of individual responsibility in Islam.

translation: Our Lord will gather us together and then will judge between us in truth. And He is the One Who judges, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse reassures believers that ultimate justice will prevail in the Hereafter, where Allah will gather all people and judge them with absolute truth and fairness, based on His perfect knowledge of all deeds and intentions.

translation: Say, 'Show me those whom you have claimed [to be partners with Allah].' No! Rather, it is Allah who is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness and supremacy of Allah, rejecting any notion of partners or associates in His divinity. It challenges the polytheists to present any evidence for their claims, affirming that Allah alone possesses true power and wisdom, and that any perceived partners are mere illusions.

translation: And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a universal [messenger] to mankind as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. But most of the people do not know.
interpretation: This verse underscores the universal scope of the Prophet Muhammad's mission, emphasizing that his message is intended for all of humanity, not just a specific group, and serves both as a source of hope (good tidings) and a caution (warning) against deviation.

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of those who deny the truth, challenging the believers to hasten the fulfillment of divine promises or warnings, thereby testing the certainty of their faith.

translation: Say, 'What do you think? If Allah's punishment were to come to you by night or by day, would the guilty wish to hasten it away? Would they then believe when they see it? But (now that it has not come) they call it far off!
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the folly of those who delay repentance, assuming they have ample time to escape accountability. It highlights the human tendency to procrastinate in matters of faith and morality, only to realize the gravity of their situation when it is too late, as the punishment becomes undeniable.

translation: But those who disbelieved say, "We will never believe in this Qur'an nor in what came before it." If you could but see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, hurling reproaches at one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, "If not for you, we would have been believers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate regret and blame that the oppressors (the arrogant) will face from the oppressed (the weak) on the Day of Judgment, when their false claims of superiority are exposed and their role in leading others astray becomes undeniable.

translation: Those who were arrogant said to those whom they had oppressed, 'Was it we who turned you away from the guidance after it had come to you? Rather, it was you [yourselves] who were criminals.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the deflection of responsibility by the arrogant towards the oppressed, attributing their own wrongdoing to others, thereby exposing their hypocrisy and refusal to acknowledge their own sins.

translation: And those who were oppressed said to those who were arrogant, "Nay, but [it is because of] the conspiracy of night and day when you were ordering us to disbelieve in Allah and attribute equals to Him." And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment, and We will place shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Will they be recompensed except for what they used to do?
interpretation: This verse highlights the accountability of individuals for their actions, emphasizing that no one will be punished unjustly; rather, they will face consequences commensurate with their deeds, particularly in matters of faith and disbelief.

translation: And We sent to no city a warner except that its affluent ones said, "Indeed, we, in that with which you were sent, are disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those in positions of wealth and power, who often reject divine guidance due to their complacency and attachment to worldly pleasures, serving as a warning against the dangers of materialism and self-satisfaction.

translation: And they said, 'We are more in wealth and children [than you], and we are not to be punished.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and materialism of those who deny the Hereafter, believing that their worldly prosperity is a sign of Allah's favor and that they are immune from divine accountability, thereby ignoring the transient nature of worldly life and the true purpose of wealth and progeny as tests from Allah.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it], but most of the people do not know.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom behind the distribution of sustenance, reminding us that Allah’s provision is not solely tied to human effort or merit but is part of a greater, often unseen plan, testing faith and patience.

translation: And it is not your wealth or your children that bring you near to Us in position, but whoever believes and does righteousness - for those there will be a double reward for what they did, and they will be in chambers [of Paradise], secure.
interpretation: This verse underscores that true proximity to Allah is not achieved through material or worldly means, but through sincere faith and righteous deeds, which alone secure divine reward and eternal security in Paradise.

translation: And those who strive against Our signs, seeking to hasten [Our punishment], they will be brought into the punishment [in full force].
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of human attempts to evade or hasten divine justice, emphasizing that those who actively oppose or mock Allah's signs will inevitably face the consequences of their defiance in the Hereafter.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord extends provision for whom He wills of His servants and restricts [it] for him. But whatever you spend [in His cause] - He will compensate it; and He is the best of providers.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah over sustenance and provision, reminding believers that their wealth and resources are ultimately in His hands. It encourages trust in Allah's wisdom regarding distribution while urging generosity, as He will replace and multiply any expenditure made in His cause, affirming His unmatched ability to provide and sustain.

translation: And [mention] the Day when He will gather them all together and then say to the angels, 'Did these [people] used to worship you?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate accountability of human beings on the Day of Judgment, where even the false deities they worshipped will be exposed as powerless, and their misplaced devotion will be laid bare before them and the angels.

translation: They said, 'Exalted are You! You are our protector besides them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them were believers in them.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the folly of associating partners with Allah, as the people in question initially recognized Allah's supremacy ('Exalted are You!') but then erroneously turned to other beings (the jinn) for protection and worship, demonstrating a misplaced trust that contradicted their own acknowledgment of Allah's sole authority.

translation: So today no one will have power to benefit or harm another, and We will say to those who wronged, 'Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where all worldly power and influence cease to exist, and only divine justice prevails. The denial of the wrongdoers is met with the fulfillment of what they once mocked, highlighting the certainty of divine retribution and the accountability of every soul for its deeds.

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, they say, "This is not but a man who wants to prevent you from what your fathers worshipped." And they say, "This is not but a fabrication, invented." And those who disbelieved say of the truth when it has come to them, "This is not but obvious magic."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and resistance of those who refuse to accept the truth despite clear evidence. It reflects the tendency of people to dismiss divine guidance when it contradicts their long-held beliefs or desires, attributing it to deception, fabrication, or magic rather than acknowledging its divine origin.

translation: And We did not give them any scriptures which they could study, nor did We send to them before you any warner.
interpretation: This verse highlights the uniqueness of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) mission, emphasizing that the people being addressed had no prior divine scriptures to guide them nor any prophetic warnings sent before him, making his role as a warner and bringer of guidance all the more significant and unprecedented.

translation: And those before them denied (the truth), though they had not attained a tenth of what We had given them. Yet they denied My messengers, so how [severe] was My reproach!
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of rejecting divine guidance despite the overwhelming evidence of Allah's blessings and the consistency of His messengers' messages across time. The comparison to 'a tenth' highlights the vast disparity between human capacity and Allah's infinite generosity, emphasizing that denial is not rooted in reason but in arrogance or willful blindness.

translation: Say, 'I only advise you of one [thing]: that you stand for Allah, [seeking truth] in pairs and individually, then reflect.' There is no madness in your companion [i.e., the Prophet Muhammad]. He is not except a warner to you before [the coming of] a severe punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of personal reflection and seeking truth individually and collectively, while affirming the Prophetic mission of Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a sincere warner against divine punishment, urging people to examine their own hearts and actions rather than dismiss his message as madness.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'Whatever payment I might have asked of you is yours. My [true] reward is only from Allah, and He is, over all things, Witness.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the sincerity of the Prophet Muhammad's mission, emphasizing that his sole motivation is divine reward, not worldly gain, and that Allah is fully aware of all intentions and actions.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, my Lord projects the truth. [He is] the Knower of the unseen.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute knowledge and power to reveal the truth, affirming that He is the only One who possesses complete awareness of all hidden matters, and that His decrees and revelations are based on absolute truth.

translation: Say, 'The truth has come, and falsehood neither originates nor returns.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute and eternal nature of truth (haqq) as brought by divine revelation, contrasting it with falsehood (batil), which is transient and powerless to either initiate or sustain itself against the truth. It underscores the inevitability of truth's triumph and the futility of falsehood in the face of divine guidance.

translation: Say, 'If I should go astray, I would only go astray against myself. But if I am guided, it is by what my Lord reveals to me. Indeed, He is Hearing and near.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the accountability of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) for his own actions and guidance, emphasizing that his guidance comes solely from divine revelation, not from his own will or effort alone. It also highlights the closeness of Allah to His servants, both in His knowledge and responsiveness to their needs.

translation: And if you could see when they are terrified, with no escape, and they are seized from a nearby place.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the inescapability of punishment for those who reject faith, emphasizing that no amount of fleeing or proximity to safety can avert their fate.

translation: And they say, 'We believe in it,' but how can they reach (the truth) from a distant place?
interpretation: This verse critiques those who claim faith superficially or without true conviction, suggesting their belief is weak or insincere, as genuine faith requires sincere effort and proximity to the truth, not mere lip service from afar.

translation: And indeed they disbelieved in it before, and they conjecture about the unseen from a far place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent disbelief of those who reject the truth despite its clarity, suggesting that their rejection is not based on evidence but on arrogance and distance from true understanding, even resorting to baseless speculation about matters beyond their knowledge.

translation: And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done with their kind before. Indeed, they were in a suspicious doubt.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of persistent doubt and skepticism towards divine guidance, suggesting that such doubt can lead to a spiritual separation from the blessings and desires one seeks, mirroring the fate of previous disbelieving communities.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. [All] praise is [due] to Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, [who] made the angels messengers having wings, two or three or four. He increases in creation what He wills. Indeed, Allah is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over all creation, highlighting His ability to create and augment as He wills, including the angels with their varying forms. It underscores the divine origin of praise and the meticulous, purposeful design in creation, reflecting Allah's wisdom and control over every aspect of existence.

translation: Whatever mercy Allah opens for people, none can withhold it; and whatever He withholds, none can release it thereafter. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all provisions, including mercy, sustenance, and blessings. It teaches that Allah's decrees are final and beyond human interference, emphasizing His ultimate power and wisdom in distributing His favors as He wills, without any intermediary or force capable of altering His decisions.

translation: O mankind, remember the favor of Allah upon you. Is there any creator other than Allah who provides for you from the heaven and the earth? There is no deity except Him, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusive right of Allah to be worshipped due to His unique role as the sole Creator and Sustainer of all existence, thereby refuting any false deities or misguided beliefs in alternative sources of provision or power.

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already have messengers before you been denied. And to Allah are [all] matters returned.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that rejection of his message is not unique to his time, as previous messengers also faced denial, and ultimately, all matters—including judgment and justice—are returned to Allah, who is the ultimate arbiter of truth.

translation: O mankind, indeed the promise of Allah is true. So let not the worldly life deceive you, nor let the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a profound reminder of the transient nature of worldly life and the certainty of divine justice. It warns against being lured by the allure of materialism or the deceptions of Satan, emphasizing that ultimate truth and accountability lie with Allah. The verse encourages steadfastness in faith and righteousness, regardless of the fleeting pleasures or trials of this life.

translation: Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy. He only invites his party to be among the companions of the Blaze [Hellfire].
interpretation: This verse underscores the perpetual enmity between humans and Satan, urging believers to recognize and resist his temptations by aligning with righteousness. It highlights Satan's deceitful nature, as he seeks to mislead people into error and damnation, emphasizing the importance of vigilance and steadfastness in faith to avoid his snares.

translation: Indeed, for those who disbelieve is a severe punishment, and for those who believe and do righteous deeds is forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the outcomes of disbelief and faith, emphasizing that true belief is not merely verbal but must be accompanied by righteous actions, which are the foundation for divine forgiveness and immense reward.

translation: Is he whose evil deed is made fair-seeming to him so that he considers it good? Indeed, Allah sends astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills. So do not let yourself perish in regret over them. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that people's perceptions of good and evil can be distorted by their own actions and desires, leading them astray from the truth. It cautions against excessive grief over those who persist in wrongdoing, as their choices are known to Allah, who alone has the wisdom to guide or misguide. The verse underscores the importance of trusting in Allah's justice and wisdom rather than being consumed by despair over the choices of others.

translation: And it is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir the clouds; then We drive them toward a dead land and bring forth thereby water; and We bring forth thereby from the earth every kind of growth. Thus will you be brought forth.
interpretation: This verse illustrates Allah’s power over life and death, using the natural cycle of rain reviving barren land as a metaphor for resurrection, affirming that just as He revives the earth, He will resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Whoever desires honor [through power]—then all honor belongs to Allah. To Him ascends the good word, and the righteous work raises it. But those who plot evil deeds—there is a severe punishment for them, and their plotting will perish.
interpretation: True honor and power come solely from Allah, not from worldly means or oppression. Sincere faith and righteous deeds elevate a person spiritually, while deceitful schemes and evil intentions ultimately lead to ruin, as divine justice ensures their failure.

translation: And Allah created you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then He made you pairs. And no female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. And no living person is granted long life, nor is any part of their life decreased, but it is in a Register. Indeed, that for Allah is easy.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute sovereignty over all stages of human life, from creation to lifespan, emphasizing that nothing occurs without His knowledge and decree, reinforcing the concept of divine predestination (*qadar*) and the meticulous recording of all events in the 'Preserved Tablet' (*Lawh al-Mahfuz*).

translation: And the two bodies of water are not alike—this one is fresh and sweet, pleasant to drink, and this one is salty and bitter. And from each you eat fresh meat and extract ornaments which you wear. And you see the ships plowing through it so you may seek of His bounty, and that you may be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity and balance in creation, illustrating how contrasting elements—like fresh and saltwater—serve distinct yet complementary purposes, all contributing to human sustenance and benefit, thereby underscoring the wisdom and mercy behind divine design.

translation: He merges the night into the day and merges the day into the night, and He has subjected the sun and the moon—each running [its course] for a specified term. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. And those whom you invoke other than Him do not possess [as much as] the membrane of a date seed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that no created being—no matter how revered—possesses even the slightest independent power or authority. The imagery of the night and day merging, along with the sun and moon running their courses, highlights the perfect order and precision in Allah’s creation, which is entirely dependent on Him. The mention of the 'membrane of a date seed' serves as a stark contrast to the grandeur of Allah’s dominion, illustrating the utter helplessness of any other deity or object of worship compared to Him.

translation: If you call them, they do not hear your call; and even if they heard, they would not respond to you. And on the Day of Resurrection, they will reject your association [of them with Allah]. And none informs you like [one] Acquainted [with all].
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of invoking false deities or intermediaries, emphasizing their complete inability to respond or intercede, contrasting the absolute power and responsiveness of Allah. It also highlights the ultimate rejection of such associations on the Day of Judgment, affirming the uniqueness and exclusivity of Allah's authority and the consequences of associating partners with Him.

translation: O mankind, you are those in need of Allah, while Allah is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute dependence of all creation on Allah, highlighting His self-sufficiency and the inherent poverty of human beings in their need for Him, both materially and spiritually.

translation: If He wills, He can do away with you and bring forth a new creation.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over creation, emphasizing that human existence is entirely dependent on His will. It serves as a reminder of human humility and the transient nature of life, while also affirming Allah's ability to replace or renew creation as He pleases, highlighting His unrestricted authority over all things.

translation: And that is not difficult for Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and ease with which Allah accomplishes His will, emphasizing that nothing is beyond His capability, even when it seems impossible to human perception.

translation: And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if someone heavily laden calls [another] to [bear] its load, nothing of it will be carried, even if he should be a close relative. You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen and establish prayer. And whoever purifies himself only purifies himself for [the benefit of] his soul. And to Allah is the [final] destination.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute individual accountability of each person before Allah, rejecting any notion of intercession or shared burden in the Hereafter. It underscores that righteousness and purification are personal responsibilities, with no external force or intercessor able to alleviate one's own sins. The warning is directed at those who embody God-consciousness ('taqwa') and steadfast devotion, highlighting that true guidance is internal and stems from a sincere relationship with the Divine.

translation: And not equal are the blind and the seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental difference between those who are spiritually blind (lacking insight or guidance) and those who possess clarity and awareness (guided by truth and faith). It underscores that the two groups cannot be equated in their perception, actions, or ultimate outcomes, as their paths and destinies diverge based on their choices and beliefs.

translation: Nor the darkness nor the light.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah, highlighting that neither darkness nor light can exist without His command, underscoring that all aspects of creation, both apparent and hidden, are entirely dependent on Him.

translation: Nor the shade nor the scorching heat.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over all natural phenomena, including elements that provide comfort like shade and those that cause discomfort like scorching heat, underscoring that nothing in creation operates independently of divine will.

translation: And the living and the dead are not alike. Indeed, Allah causes to hear whom He wills, but you cannot make hear those in the graves.
interpretation: This verse underscores the fundamental difference between those who are spiritually alive—guided by faith and righteousness—and those who are spiritually dead—devoid of belief and righteous deeds. It also highlights the limits of human influence, as only Allah can guide whom He wills, and no amount of effort can awaken those who are spiritually dead, symbolized by 'those in the graves.'

translation: You are not but a warner.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the limited role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a bearer of divine warning, highlighting that his mission is to convey God's message and admonish people, not to compel or force them into faith.

translation: Indeed, We have sent you, [O Muhammad], with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there is not a nation but a warner has passed among them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the universality of Prophethood and the divine mission of every messenger sent to their respective nations, emphasizing that guidance is a recurring theme in human history, ensuring no people are left without a warning or reminder of the truth.

translation: And if they deny you, [O Muhammad], then already did those before them deny, and they came to them their messengers with clear proofs and written ordinances and the enlightening Scripture.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that denial of his message is not unique to his people; rather, it is a recurring pattern throughout history where previous nations rejected their messengers despite clear evidence and divine scriptures, emphasizing divine justice and the inevitability of accountability.

translation: Then I seized the disbelievers; so how [terrible] was My reproach?
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine retribution for those who persistently reject faith and defy God's signs, emphasizing that their denial does not alter the certainty of their punishment, which is as severe as it is just.

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby fruits of varying colors? And in the mountains are tracts, white and red of varying shades, and extremely black.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity and harmony in Allah's creation, emphasizing how the same natural processes—like rainfall—produce vastly different outcomes in fruits, mountains, and other phenomena, reflecting the wisdom and power of the Creator.

translation: And among people, beasts, and cattle are various colors. Indeed, the only ones who fear Allah among His servants are the scholars. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse underscores that the diversity in creation—whether in humans, animals, or livestock—reflects the boundless power and wisdom of Allah. However, it specifically highlights that true awareness and reverence for Allah’s majesty and authority are most profoundly found among those who possess deep knowledge ('ulama'). This implies that knowledge, particularly of the Qur'an and Sunnah, elevates a person’s understanding of Allah’s signs and commands, fostering a deeper sense of awe and obedience to Him.

translation: Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah, establish prayer, and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and publicly, expect a trade that will never perish.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtuous cycle of faith, devotion, and generosity, emphasizing that true success lies not in fleeting worldly gains but in an eternal, unperishable transaction with Allah—one rooted in sincerity, consistency, and trust in divine reward.

translation: To pay them their rewards in full and give them more out of His bounty. Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's boundless generosity and justice, highlighting that He not only rewards His servants fully for their deeds but also bestows additional favors out of His infinite grace. The mention of Him being 'Forgiving' and 'Appreciative' underscores that even those who fall short are met with mercy and that sincere efforts are acknowledged and rewarded beyond measure.

translation: And what We have revealed to you of the Book is the truth, confirming what was before it. Indeed, Allah is, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and truthfulness of the Qur'an, affirming its consistency with previous scriptures while highlighting Allah's comprehensive knowledge and awareness of His servants' deeds and states.

translation: Then We caused to inherit the Book those We have chosen from among Our servants; and among them is he who wrongs himself, and among them is he who is moderate, and among them is he who is foremost in good deeds, by permission of Allah. That is the great bounty.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diverse spiritual states of believers who inherit the divine guidance (the Book), illustrating that Allah's grace encompasses all, from those who struggle with their faith to those who excel in righteousness, all within the framework of divine permission and mercy.

translation: They will enter Gardens of Eternity, wherein they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their garments therein will be silk.
interpretation: This verse highlights the eternal and luxurious rewards awaiting the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing both material adornment and refined comfort as symbols of divine generosity and the ultimate fulfillment of their faith.

translation: And they will say, "Praise to Allah, who has removed from us [all] sorrow. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative—
interpretation: This verse reflects the gratitude of the inhabitants of Paradise for Allah’s mercy in removing their past hardships and trials, highlighting His attributes of forgiveness and appreciation for their good deeds, which underscores the transformative power of divine grace in erasing suffering and rewarding righteousness.

translation: Who has settled us in the Home of Eternity out of His bounty. No fatigue will touch us therein, nor any weariness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal reward of Paradise, granted by Allah's grace, where believers will experience complete comfort and freedom from any form of hardship or exhaustion, reflecting the ultimate fulfillment of divine mercy.

translation: But those who disbelieved will have the fire of Hell. It will not be decreed for them that they die, nor will its punishment be lightened for them. Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one.
interpretation: This verse underscores the eternal and unrelenting nature of divine punishment for those who persistently reject faith and gratitude to Allah. The absence of death or relief from suffering in Hell signifies the finality of their fate, emphasizing the gravity of their disbelief and ingratitude, which are met with commensurate justice.

translation: And they will cry out therein, 'Our Lord, take us out! We will do righteous work other than what we used to do.' Did We not grant you life long enough for whoever would remember therein to remember, and did the warner come to you? So taste [the punishment], for there is not for the wrongdoers any helper.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality of judgment and the irreversible nature of one's deeds in the Hereafter. The plea of the wrongdoers to be returned to the world to do righteous deeds is met with divine response that their time in the world was sufficient for reflection and repentance, yet they persisted in wrongdoing. It highlights the consequences of rejecting guidance and the absence of any intercession for those who wronged themselves by denying the truth.

translation: Indeed, Allah is Knower of the unseen [aspects] of the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute and encompassing knowledge, which transcends the visible and invisible realms, including the deepest secrets of the human heart, thereby emphasizing His omniscience and the futility of attempting to hide anything from Him.

translation: It is He who has made you successors upon the earth. And whoever disbelieves - upon him will be his disbelief. And it does not increase the disbelievers in anything but disfavor with their Lord. And it does not increase the disbelievers in anything but loss.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of human life and the accountability of individuals for their choices. It highlights that disbelief (kufr) does not harm Allah but rather harms the disbeliever themselves, deepening their estrangement from divine mercy and leading to ultimate loss in the Hereafter.

translation: Say, 'Have you seen your 'partners' whom you invoke besides Allah? Show me what of the earth have they created, or do they have any share in the heavens? Or have We given them a book so they are [standing] on clear evidence from it? [No,] rather, the wrongdoers do not promise each other except delusion.'
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to prove the validity of their false deities by demonstrating any tangible creation or shared authority with Allah, highlighting the baselessness of their claims and the delusion in their mutual assurances of divine partnership.

translation: Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth, lest they cease. And if they were to cease, no one could hold them after Him. Indeed, He is Forbearing and Forgiving.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and unchanging power of Allah in sustaining the universe, emphasizing that His control is constant and beyond any challenge or interruption, reflecting His infinite wisdom and mercy in maintaining creation despite human shortcomings.

translation: And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if a warner came to them, they would surely be more guided than one of the nations. But when a warner came to them, it only increased them in aversion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who refuse to accept the truth despite clear evidence. It underscores the futility of relying on oaths or preconceived notions when faced with divine guidance, as their rejection stems from deep-seated pride and aversion rather than a genuine search for truth.

translation: Out of pride in the land and plotting evil. But evil plotting does not encompass except its own people. Then do they await except the precedent of the former peoples? But you will never find in the way of Allah any change, and you will never find in the way of Allah any alteration.
interpretation: This verse warns against arrogance and deceitful schemes, emphasizing that such actions ultimately harm only their perpetrators, as history has shown that those who engage in evil plotting are inevitably destroyed by their own machinations. It reassures believers that Allah’s decrees are unchangeable and that divine justice will prevail, as seen in the consistent patterns of punishment for past oppressors.

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were stronger than them. But Allah is not such that anything in the heavens or on the earth can frustrate Him. Indeed, He is Knowing and Competent.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that historical patterns of divine retribution against arrogant and oppressive nations are consistent and inevitable, regardless of their power or strength. It underscores Allah’s absolute sovereignty and omniscience, emphasizing that no force—whether in the heavens or the earth—can thwart His will or delay His decrees. The mention of past nations’ destruction despite their strength is a lesson in humility and a warning against arrogance, reinforcing the idea that true power lies with Allah alone.

translation: And if Allah were to impose blame on the people for what they have earned, He would not leave upon the earth a single creature, but He delays them for a specified term. And when their term has come, then indeed, Allah is ever, upon His servants, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's boundless mercy and justice, highlighting that while He is fully aware of human deeds, He grants respite and does not hasten punishment, allowing time for repentance and reflection.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Ya, Seen.
interpretation: This verse begins with the invocation of Allah's names, emphasizing His mercy and compassion, which sets the tone for the divine message that follows. The letters 'Ya, Seen' are among the 'mystery letters' (al-huruf al-muqatta'at) at the beginning of some chapters of the Qur'an, whose meaning is known only to Allah, though they are often understood to invite reflection and contemplation on the miraculous nature of the Qur'an itself.

translation: By the wise Qur'an,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine wisdom and guidance encapsulated within the Qur'an, highlighting its role as a source of profound knowledge and truth for humanity.

translation: Indeed, you are from among the messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms the prophethood and divine mission of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), confirming that he is one of the chosen messengers sent by Allah to guide humanity.

translation: On a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the guidance of Allah as a clear and unwavering path, free from deviation or ambiguity, guiding believers toward righteousness and truth.

translation: A revelation from the Almighty, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This opening phrase of many chapters in the Qur'an establishes the divine origin and authority of the text, emphasizing that its source is the All-Powerful and Compassionate God, thereby setting the tone for the sacred and transformative nature of its message.

translation: That you may warn a people whose forefathers were not warned, so they are heedless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the responsibility of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to convey the message of Islam to a people who have not received prior divine guidance, emphasizing their state of neglect and unawareness of the consequences of their actions.

translation: Indeed, the word has come true against most of them, so they do not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent rejection of truth by many, despite clear signs and warnings, indicating a deep-seated resistance to faith that stems from arrogance or blind adherence to tradition rather than genuine inquiry.

translation: Indeed, We have put shackles around their necks, reaching up to their chins, so they are with heads raised up.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describes the state of those who persistently reject the truth and guidance, illustrating how their arrogance and stubbornness bind them to their own misguidance, preventing them from humbly submitting to the truth even when it is clearly presented to them.

translation: And We placed before them a barrier and behind them a barrier, and thus We covered them, so they do not see.
interpretation: This verse signifies the spiritual and moral blindness that results from persistent rejection of divine guidance, where Allah places barriers around such people, preventing them from seeing or accepting the truth, despite clear signs being presented to them.

translation: And it is all the same for them whether you warn them or do not warn them—they will not believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine foreknowledge and the fixed nature of some people's rejection of faith, indicating that no amount of warning or effort can change their predetermined disbelief.

translation: You can only warn those who follow the Reminder and fear the Most Merciful unseen. So give them good tidings of forgiveness and a noble reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who are receptive to divine guidance and those who are not, emphasizing that true guidance comes from a combination of following the Qur'an (the Reminder) and having a deep, sincere fear of Allah that is not contingent on visible signs or immediate consequences.

translation: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have put forth and what they have left behind. And all things We have enumerated in a clear register.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah’s absolute power over life and death, emphasizing that He is the sole source of resurrection and the reckoner of all human deeds—both actions and their lasting impacts. It also highlights divine omniscience and the meticulous recording of every detail in a manifest record, ensuring justice and accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: And present to them an example: the people of the city, when the messengers came to it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of reflecting on historical events and the consequences faced by those who reject the truth, serving as a reminder of divine justice and the accountability of nations to their messengers.

translation: When We sent to them two [messengers], but they denied them both, so We reinforced them with a third, and they said, "Indeed, we are messengers sent to you."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of divine support in the face of rejection and adversity, demonstrating that Allah strengthens His messengers with additional means when their mission is met with disbelief, emphasizing the inevitability of truth and the temporary nature of opposition.

translation: They said, "You are not but human beings like us, and the Most Merciful has not revealed anything. You are but lying."
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and denial of the disbelievers who refuse to accept the divine origin of the message brought by the prophets, attributing it instead to human fabrication, thereby rejecting the truth outright.

translation: They said, "Our Lord knows that we are indeed messengers sent to you."
interpretation: This verse reflects the prophets' unwavering conviction in their divine mission, asserting that their truthfulness is known to Allah, which serves as a reassurance to both themselves and their people against doubts or accusations.

translation: And our duty is only to convey the clear message.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers as messengers whose primary responsibility is to deliver the divine message clearly and unambiguously, without coercion or imposition, leaving the ultimate response to the guidance to the will and choice of the people.

translation: They said, "Indeed, we consider you a bad omen. If you do not desist, we will surely stone you, and there will surely touch you, from us, a painful punishment."
interpretation: This verse reflects the ignorance and superstition of the disbelievers who attributed their misfortunes to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his followers, rather than acknowledging their own wrongdoing. Their threat of stoning and punishment reveals their arrogance and rejection of divine guidance, ultimately leading to their own destruction.

translation: They said, "Your omen is with you! Is it because you were reminded? Rather, you are a transgressing people."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth despite clear reminders, attributing their misfortune to external factors rather than acknowledging their own wrongdoing.

translation: And there came from the farthest part of the city a man running. He said, "O my people, follow the messengers."
interpretation: This verse highlights the courage and conviction of a lone believer who, despite the potential danger of his city's rejection of the messengers, openly declares his allegiance to them, serving as a model of unwavering faith and moral integrity in the face of adversity.

translation: Follow those who do not ask you for any reward, and they are rightly guided.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to seek guidance from sincere and selfless individuals who do not seek personal gain or reward for their advice or teachings, emphasizing the importance of sincerity and righteousness in leadership and mentorship.

translation: And why should I not worship He who created me, and to Him you will be returned?
interpretation: This verse reflects the fundamental Islamic principle of Tawhid (monotheism), emphasizing the obligation of worshipping Allah alone, the Creator, and acknowledging that all creation will ultimately return to Him for judgment and accountability.

translation: Do I take besides Him other gods? If the Most Compassionate intends harm for me, their intercession will not avail me at all, nor can they save me.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah in His power and ability to affect outcomes, rejecting any notion of associating partners with Him who could intervene or alter His decrees.

translation: Indeed, I am in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of profound self-awareness and humility, where the speaker acknowledges their prior misguidance or deviation from truth, highlighting the importance of recognizing one's own errors as a step toward repentance and correction.

translation: Indeed, I have believed in your Lord, so listen to me.
interpretation: This verse reflects the declaration of faith by a believer in the face of opposition, asserting their conviction in the Lord of the people being addressed, while also calling for their attention and acceptance of the truth.

translation: It was said, "Enter Paradise." He said, "I wish my people could know"
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound regret of a righteous person who has entered Paradise, wishing that his people could witness his reward and thereby be guided to the truth, emphasizing the importance of guidance and the pain of seeing others remain astray.

translation: My Lord has forgiven me and made me one of the honored.
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of profound gratitude and humility, where the speaker acknowledges divine forgiveness and elevation to a status of honor, suggesting a deep spiritual connection and recognition of God's mercy and favor.

translation: And We did not send down upon his people after him any soldiers from the heaven, nor would We ever do so.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah in determining the means and methods of divine intervention, emphasizing that Allah's help or punishment is not bound by human expectations or conventional means, and that His decisions are beyond the constraints of the physical world.

translation: It was but a single shout, and lo! They were extinguished.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sudden and absolute nature of divine punishment, highlighting how a single decisive command from Allah can instantly bring an end to the existence of those who persist in defiance and disbelief, leaving no trace of their former power or presence.

translation: Alas for mankind! Never came a messenger to them but they did mock him.
interpretation: This verse underscores the recurring human tendency to reject divine guidance and ridicule those who bring it, highlighting the tragic irony of dismissing truth despite its clear signs, which often leads to their own downfall.

translation: Have they not seen how many generations We have destroyed before them? They will not return to them.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who deny or doubt the truth of the Qur'an and the Day of Judgment, reminding them of the fate of past nations who were destroyed due to their disbelief and defiance, and emphasizing that no one can escape the consequences of their actions or return to this world to amend them.

translation: And indeed, every one of them, before Us, are to be brought together.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute accountability of every individual in the sight of Allah, emphasizing that no soul will escape the reckoning of their deeds, no matter how hidden or seemingly insignificant they may be.

translation: And a sign for them is the dead earth. We have brought it to life and brought forth from it grain, so they eat from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power to bring life from the lifeless, symbolizing resurrection and divine providence, as He sustains humanity through the earth's resources despite its apparent barrenness.

translation: And We placed therein gardens of palm trees and grapevines and caused to burst forth therefrom springs.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power to create and sustain life in barren lands, transforming them into lush gardens and providing abundant water sources, symbolizing divine generosity and the ability to bring forth blessings from nothingness.

translation: So that they may eat of His fruit and what their hands have put forth. Will they not then be grateful?
interpretation: This verse underscores the natural order of sustenance and the importance of recognizing divine provision, urging reflection on the blessings bestowed upon humanity and the necessity of gratitude to Allah for His favors.

translation: Glory be to the One Who created all pairs from what the earth produces, from themselves, and from what they do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the boundless power of Allah in creating diverse pairs—whether from plants, humans, or even unseen or unknown forms—highlighting His infinite knowledge and creative ability beyond human comprehension.

translation: And a sign for them is the night: We strip from it the day, and behold, they are in darkness.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine power in the natural cycle of day and night, demonstrating Allah's control over creation and the inevitability of His signs, which should lead to reflection and faith.

translation: And the sun runs [on course] toward its stopping point. That is the determination of the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the precise and predetermined order in the universe, highlighting Allah's supreme power and infinite knowledge in regulating the natural laws, ensuring that all creation follows His will without deviation.

translation: And the moon, We have determined it in stages until it returns like an old date stalk.
interpretation: This verse signifies the divine precision and order in the creation of the moon, highlighting its cyclical phases as a sign of Allah's power and the inevitability of His decrees, reflecting the transient yet purposeful nature of all things.

translation: It is not allowable for the sun to reach the moon, nor does the night overtake the day, but each, in an orbit, is swimming.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine order and precision in the cosmic system, where each celestial body moves in its designated path without interference, illustrating the concept of divine governance and the impossibility of any disruption in the natural order.

translation: And there is a sign for them in that We carried their descendants in the laden ship.
interpretation: This verse highlights the mercy and power of Allah in preserving humanity through the great flood, demonstrating His ability to protect and sustain His creation even in the face of destruction.

translation: And We created for them [ mounts] similar to them, so they may ride upon them.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's power to create means of transportation that serve humanity's needs, demonstrating His mercy and provision. It underscores the idea that Allah equips humans with the tools necessary for their livelihood and progress, encouraging gratitude and reliance on Him.

translation: And if We will, We can drown them; then there will be no helper for them, nor will they be rescued.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over all creation, including life and death. It serves as a reminder of human vulnerability and dependence on Allah, emphasizing that no force or entity—whether human, natural, or otherwise—can intervene against Allah's will. The mention of drowning also symbolizes the inevitability of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief or defiance, highlighting the futility of seeking help from false sources of power or protection.

translation: Except as a mercy from Us and as a provision for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the balance between divine mercy and the temporary nature of worldly life, reminding believers that any blessings or respite granted are ultimately from Allah and are meant to serve a purpose in this life before the Hereafter.

translation: And when it is said to them, "Fear what is before you and what is behind you, that you might receive mercy."
interpretation: This verse critiques those who ignore divine warnings and moral accountability, emphasizing the consequences of their actions both in this life and the Hereafter, urging them to seek mercy through righteousness and repentance.

translation: And no sign comes to them from the signs of their Lord except that they turn away from it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent refusal of those who reject faith to acknowledge or reflect upon the signs and proofs of Allah's existence and power, even when they are clearly presented to them. It underscores the depth of their aversion and the hardness of their hearts, as they deliberately avoid recognizing the truth despite overwhelming evidence.

translation: And when it is said to them, "Spend out of what Allah has provided for you," the disbelievers say to the believers, "Shall we feed someone whom Allah, if He willed, could feed? You are only in clear error."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and ingratitude of the disbelievers, who refuse to spend in charity while attributing Allah's power to withhold provision to their own will, thereby denying the believers' guidance and distorting the truth.

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of those who deny the truth, challenging the believers to hasten the fulfillment of divine promises or threats, thereby testing the sincerity of their faith.

translation: They do not await except one Blast, which will seize them while they are disputing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sudden and decisive nature of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that it will arrive without warning, halting all human disputes and activities, and rendering all previous arguments or preparations irrelevant in the face of divine justice.

translation: So they will not be able to make a will, nor will they return to their people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality of death and the inability of the deceased to influence or alter their fate or the affairs of the living, emphasizing the absolute nature of divine decree and the irreversibility of the end of life.

translation: And the Horn will be blown, and at once they will come out of their graves to their Lord, hastening.
interpretation: This verse signifies the sudden and inevitable resurrection of all humanity on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the swift and unquestioning response to Allah's command, where the dead will rise from their graves and hasten towards their Lord without delay or hesitation.

translation: They will say, "O woe to us! Who has raised us from our place of sleep?" [It will be said], "This is what the Most Merciful had promised, and the messengers told the truth."
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment of resurrection when people will be raised from their graves, overwhelmed by the realization of the truth of resurrection and the Day of Judgment, acknowledging that the promises of the Most Merciful (Allah) and the truthfulness of the messengers have been fulfilled.

translation: It was but a single cry, and behold! They are all before Us, arraigned in array.
interpretation: This verse underscores the suddenness and inevitability of divine judgment, emphasizing that no matter how powerful or numerous the wrongdoers may seem, their end is swift and their accountability before Allah is absolute and unavoidable.

translation: So today no soul will be wronged at all, nor will you be recompensed except for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where every individual will be held accountable only for their own deeds without any injustice or favoritism, and their recompense will be precisely commensurate with their actions in this life.

translation: Indeed, the companions of Paradise will be, today, in a state of joyful occupation.
interpretation: This verse highlights the eternal bliss and contentment of the believers in Paradise, where they are engaged in activities that bring them pure joy and fulfillment, free from any toil or burden.

translation: They and their spouses will be in shades, reclining on thrones.
interpretation: This verse describes the ultimate comfort and honor that believers will experience in Paradise, where they will be with their spouses, enjoying eternal peace and luxury in the presence of Allah's mercy.

translation: For them therein is fruit, and for them is whatever they request.
interpretation: This verse highlights the boundless generosity of Allah in Paradise, where believers will not only enjoy the natural bounty of fruit but also have their deepest desires and requests fulfilled, reflecting the ultimate fulfillment of their needs and aspirations in a state of eternal contentment.

translation: A word of peace from a Lord Most Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of peace and mercy, emphasizing that true tranquility and compassion emanate from Allah, who is the ultimate source of all goodness and benevolence.

translation: And [you who believe in Allah and His Messenger] separate yourselves today, O criminals.
interpretation: This verse calls upon believers to distinguish themselves from wrongdoers by adhering to righteousness and righteous deeds, emphasizing the importance of moral and spiritual separation from evil in both belief and action.

translation: Did I not enjoin upon you, O children of Adam, that you worship not Satan? Indeed, he is to you a clear enemy.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the primordial covenant between Allah and humanity, emphasizing the inherent enmity between Satan and mankind, urging believers to reject his influence and remain steadfast in their devotion solely to Allah.

translation: And worship Me. This is a straight path.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusive worship of Allah alone, rejecting any form of idolatry or association, and highlights that true guidance lies in adhering to this monotheistic path without deviation.

translation: And indeed, many jinns from among men and jinns have led astray many. So, do you not reason?
interpretation: This verse highlights the pervasive influence of misguidance and deception in the world, often stemming from both human and supernatural sources. It serves as a reminder to exercise critical thinking and discernment, urging believers to reflect on their choices and not blindly follow the whims of others without considering the consequences.

translation: This is the Hellfire which you were promised.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark reminder of the consequences of one's actions in the Hereafter, emphasizing the reality of divine justice and the fulfillment of God's promises.

translation: Burn them today for what you used to disbelieve.
interpretation: This verse is a stern warning to those who persistently reject the truth and oppose divine guidance, indicating that their denial will lead to severe punishment in the Hereafter, where they will face the consequences of their disbelief.

translation: This Day We will seal up their mouths, and their hands will speak to Us, and their feet will bear witness to what they used to earn.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of divine justice, where even the mute faculties of the body will testify to one's deeds on the Day of Judgment, leaving no room for denial or escape from accountability.

translation: And if We willed, We could surely obliterate their eyes, so they would race to the path, but how could they see?
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over human perception and guidance, suggesting that true sight—both physical and spiritual—is a divine gift, not an inherent human capability.

translation: And if We willed, We could transform them in place, so they would not be able to proceed, nor could they return.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute power to alter or transform creation as He wills, illustrating that human strength, will, or progress are entirely subject to His decree.

translation: And whoever We grant long life, We reverse in creation. Then will they not reason?
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly life and the inevitability of aging and decline, even for those granted longevity, to emphasize the importance of using one's time wisely for spiritual reflection and preparation for the Hereafter.

translation: And We did not teach him [Muhammad] poetry, nor is it befitting for him. It is not but a reminder and a clear Qur'an.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an by distinguishing it from human poetry or literary works, affirming that the Qur'an is not a product of human creativity but a revelation from Allah, meant solely for guidance and remembrance.

translation: That He may warn whoever is alive and justify the word against the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the dual purpose of revelation: to guide those who are spiritually alive and receptive to truth, while simultaneously sealing the fate of those who persist in disbelief, ensuring that divine justice is fulfilled against them.

translation: Have they not seen that We created for them, from what Our hands have wrought, livestock, which they own?
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of human denial of divine power despite clear evidence in creation, as the existence of livestock—created by Allah—serves as a sign of His ability to resurrect the dead.

translation: And We have subjected them to them, so some they ride, and some they eat.
interpretation: This verse highlights the subjugation of certain animals to human benefit, demonstrating Allah's mercy and provision for humanity, while also implying a sense of responsibility and gratitude towards these creatures for their use in sustenance and service.

translation: And for them in it are benefits and drinks. Will they not then be grateful?
interpretation: This verse underscores the ungratefulness of humans despite the clear signs of Allah's blessings and provisions, which are evident in the natural world and daily life, urging reflection on the necessity of gratitude.

translation: And they have taken besides Allah [false] deities that they might be helped.
interpretation: This verse critiques the act of associating partners with Allah (shirk) by worshipping idols or other deities, suggesting that such practice is not only futile but also stems from a misplaced hope in these false gods for assistance or salvation, rather than seeking true help from Allah alone.

translation: They are not able to help themselves, and they are brought forth as an army for them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the helplessness of false deities or idols that people may worship besides Allah. It emphasizes that these objects of worship cannot even aid themselves, let alone their followers, and that they will ultimately be gathered as part of Allah's dominion, underscoring the futility of associating partners with Allah.

translation: So do not be grieved by their speech. Indeed, We know what they conceal and what they reveal.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and believers that Allah is fully aware of both the hidden and apparent actions and intentions of people, so they should not be distressed by the words or opposition of the disbelievers, as divine justice will ultimately prevail.

translation: Does man not consider that We created him from a drop of fluid? Yet behold, he becomes an open adversary.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of human nature, where despite being created from a humble and insignificant origin (a drop of fluid), man often becomes arrogant and hostile, denying the truth and opposing divine guidance.

translation: And he presents for Us an example and forgets his own creation. He says, 'Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the arrogance of those who deny resurrection and the power of Allah, as they overlook their own origin and the evident signs of Allah's creative ability in their own existence.

translation: Say, 'He will give life to them Who created them for the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing.'
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute power and knowledge, affirming that just as He initiated life in creation, He possesses the ability to resurrect the dead on the Day of Judgment, demonstrating His comprehensive awareness of all things.

translation: Who has provided for you from the green tree fire, so that you kindle from it?
interpretation: This verse highlights the power and control of Allah over all creation, demonstrating that even something as ordinary as a green tree can be transformed into fire for human benefit, emphasizing divine omnipotence and the signs of Allah's existence in the natural world.

translation: Is not He who created the heavens and the earth Able to create the likes of them? Yes, [it is so]; and He is the Knowing Creator.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and capability of Allah, emphasizing that if He has already created the vast and complex heavens and earth, then creating something similar or even lesser is certainly within His power. The repetition of 'Yes, [it is so]' affirms the certainty of this truth, while 'the Knowing Creator' highlights Allah's comprehensive knowledge and His role as the originator of all creation.

translation: Indeed, His command when He intends a thing is only that He says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah in creation, emphasizing that His command alone is sufficient to bring about any desired outcome without the need for intermediaries or prolonged processes.

translation: So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and control of Allah over all creation, reminding humanity of their ultimate return to Him for judgment and accountability.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. By those lined up in rows (1)
interpretation: The verse begins by invoking Allah's names of mercy, setting a tone of divine compassion and guidance, before introducing an oath by the angels or celestial beings arranged in ranks, symbolizing order, harmony, and the meticulous execution of divine will.

translation: So [they are] the repellers, repelling with a repelling.
interpretation: This verse refers to the angels who drive away evil and harmful influences, both physical and spiritual, with divine authority. Their repelling is not merely a forceful rejection but a protective measure ordained by Allah to maintain balance and safeguard His creation from corruption or harm.

translation: So the reciters of the Qur'an recite it distinctly.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reciting the Qur'an with clarity and precision, reflecting both the beauty of its linguistic structure and the necessity of understanding its profound meanings.

translation: Indeed, your God is One.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of God, rejecting any form of polytheism or association of partners with Him.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and Lord of the easts.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and dominion of Allah over all creation, including the heavens, the earth, and everything in between, as well as the multiple directions of the rising sun (easts), underscoring His comprehensive and unchallenged authority over all realms of existence.

translation: Indeed, We have adorned the lowest heaven with the adornment of the stars.
interpretation: This verse highlights the grandeur and beauty of the heavens, which Allah has adorned with stars as a sign of His power and creativity, serving as a reminder of His sovereignty over all creation.

translation: And protection from every rebellious devil.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine protection from malevolent forces, emphasizing that Allah's safeguarding encompasses all forms of evil, including those who actively resist truth and righteousness.

translation: They do not listen to the exalted assembly [of angels] and are pelted from every side.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and moral distance between the disbelievers and the divine realm, emphasizing their inability to perceive or benefit from the guidance of the angels or the higher truths of the unseen world.

translation: Driven away, and for them is a lasting punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine retribution for those who persist in defiance and disbelief, emphasizing that their rejection of truth leads to eternal separation from God's mercy and a punishment that is both inescapable and enduring.

translation: Except for one who snatches a fleeting sound, then he is pursued by a piercing flame.
interpretation: This verse refers to the futility of attempting to eavesdrop on the divine realm, as any such effort—no matter how brief—will be met with swift and severe consequences, symbolized by the 'piercing flame'.

translation: Then ask them, [O Muhammad], 'Which of them is stronger in structure or [more durable] in composition?' We created them from sticky clay.
interpretation: This verse challenges the arrogance of those who deny the power of Allah by questioning the strength and durability of their own creation compared to Allah's creation, emphasizing that humans, despite their perceived strength, were originally formed from humble and fragile clay.

translation: Nay, they wonder, and they mock.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief and mockery of those who reject the truth, despite witnessing clear signs, indicating their arrogance and refusal to acknowledge divine guidance.

translation: And when they are reminded, they do not remember.
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of those who, despite being reminded of the truth, deliberately choose to ignore it, demonstrating a hardened heart and a refusal to reflect or act upon guidance.

translation: And when they see a sign, they ridicule it.
interpretation: This verse reflects the attitude of those who dismiss divine signs and miracles out of arrogance or disbelief, treating them as objects of mockery rather than signs of truth, which underscores the hardened hearts of those who reject guidance despite clear evidence.

translation: And they say, 'This is not but obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and denial of the disbelievers who attribute the divine revelations to mere trickery or sorcery, refusing to acknowledge their miraculous and truthful nature.

translation: What! When we have died and become dust and bones, shall we really be resurrected?
interpretation: This verse reflects a common human doubt or denial of the possibility of resurrection after death, challenging the concept of life after death and the power of Allah to restore life to what has decomposed, thereby testing faith in divine omnipotence and the Hereafter.

translation: Or our forefathers of old?
interpretation: This rhetorical question challenges the notion of blindly following ancestral traditions without critical reflection or verification, emphasizing the importance of independent reasoning and adherence to truth over inherited customs.

translation: Say, 'Yes,' and you will be humbled.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine truth and the submission required from those who oppose it, emphasizing that resistance is futile in the face of God's will.

translation: But it will only be a single blast, and then they will all look on.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing the sudden and decisive nature of the final trumpet blast that will signal the end of the world and the beginning of the Hereafter, leaving humanity in awe and realization of the reality of resurrection and judgment.

translation: And they will say, 'O woe to us! This is the Day of Recompense.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the realization of the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, where they acknowledge their regret and despair upon facing the consequences of their actions, recognizing the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: This is the Day of Judgment about which you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of the Day of Judgment, which was previously rejected by the disbelievers. It serves as a reminder of the accountability that awaits all, emphasizing the consequences of one's disbelief and the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: Assemble those who did wrong, their spouses, and whatever they used to worship
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate accountability of individuals and their associations in this life, emphasizing that both the wrongdoers and those they followed or associated with in sinful practices will be gathered together for divine judgment, highlighting the consequences of misguided loyalty and complicity in wrongdoing.

translation: And besides Allah, will you guide them to the path of Hell?
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility and misguidance of seeking guidance or help from anything or anyone other than Allah, as such paths lead to destruction and ruin.

translation: Stop them, for they are to be questioned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of accountability for one's actions, emphasizing that no individual can evade responsibility for their deeds. It serves as a reminder of the Day of Judgment, where every soul will be held to account for their choices and behaviors.

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not help one another?
interpretation: This verse questions the reluctance or failure of people to support each other in times of need or moral duty, highlighting a lack of solidarity and collective responsibility.

translation: Nay, but today they are in submission.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of submission to divine will, highlighting that even those who once rejected or opposed truth will ultimately acknowledge its supremacy—whether in this world or the Hereafter—when faced with the undeniable reality of divine justice and truth.

translation: And they will turn to one another, questioning each other.
interpretation: This verse reflects the intense moment of accountability on the Day of Judgment, where people will urgently seek answers from one another about their deeds and the consequences they now face, highlighting the overwhelming realization of their actions.

translation: They said, "Indeed, you used to come to us from the right."
interpretation: This verse suggests a tone of accusation or mockery, implying that the addressees were perceived as having a consistent, possibly deceptive or misguided, influence or behavior that was seen as coming from a position of power or moral authority ('from the right'). It reflects a sense of entitlement or arrogance in the accusers' tone, as if they believed the addressed party had no right to act as they did.

translation: They will say, "Rather, you were not [at all] believers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the disbelievers' admission in the Hereafter that their denial of the truth was not due to ignorance or lack of evidence, but rather a rejection of faith borne out of arrogance and obstinacy, despite clear signs.

translation: And we had no authority over you; rather, you were a people transgressing [against Allah].
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of human free will and accountability, affirming that no force or coercion from external entities (including divine messengers) can compel belief or righteousness; the choice lies with individuals, whose rejection of truth stems from their own rebelliousness.

translation: So the word of our Lord has come into effect upon us; indeed, we will taste [punishment].
interpretation: This verse reflects the inevitability of divine justice and the certainty of accountability for one's deeds, emphasizing that no soul will escape the consequences of its actions, as decreed by Allah.

translation: So We led you astray, for we ourselves were astray.
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of divine accountability where the wrongdoers attribute their misguidance to Allah, but the context implies that their deviation was a result of their own choices, not divine compulsion.

translation: For indeed, on that Day, they will be in the torment, sharing [it] together.
interpretation: This verse underscores the collective accountability of people in the Hereafter, where wrongdoers will face shared punishment, emphasizing the gravity of their actions and the inescapable justice of divine retribution.

translation: Indeed, thus do We deal with the criminals.
