interpretation: This verse underscores the divine justice that will be meted out to those who persist in wrongdoing and transgression, affirming that their punishment is a just and inevitable consequence of their actions.

translation: Indeed, when it was said to them, 'There is no god except Allah,' they were arrogant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection and arrogance of those who refuse to acknowledge the oneness of Allah despite clear evidence, choosing instead to cling to their pride and false deities.

translation: And they say, 'Is it [indeed] that we would abandon our gods for a mad poet?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and mockery of the disbelievers towards the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and his message, dismissing it as the ravings of a mentally unstable person rather than a divine revelation.

translation: Nay, he has brought the truth and confirms the Messengers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an, affirming that it is not a fabrication but a revelation from Allah, consistent with the messages of previous prophets, thus validating the continuity of monotheistic truth across all messengers.

translation: Indeed, you are going to taste the painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who persist in disbelief or transgression, emphasizing the inevitability of divine retribution for their actions.

translation: And you will not be recompensed except for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, affirming that individuals will be held accountable solely for their own actions, with no burden of another's deeds, nor any injustice in the reckoning.

translation: Except the chosen servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exclusivity of divine mercy and protection, which is granted only to those who are sincere and devoted to Allah with pure intentions, free from any form of hypocrisy or hidden agendas.

translation: For those [the righteous], there is a known provision.
interpretation: This verse assures believers that their sustenance is preordained and guaranteed by Allah, emphasizing divine providence and the certainty of provision for those who follow the path of righteousness.

translation: Fruits. And they will be honored.
interpretation: This verse highlights the honor and dignity that will be bestowed upon the righteous in the Hereafter, where they will be granted not only spiritual rewards but also physical delights, such as fruits, as a symbol of their elevated status and Allah's generosity.

translation: In Gardens of Delight.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ultimate reward and bliss that awaits the righteous believers in Paradise, where they will experience eternal happiness, peace, and fulfillment in the presence of Allah.

translation: On couches facing each other.
interpretation: This verse describes the elevated status of the believers in Paradise, where they will recline in comfort and dignity, facing one another in a state of mutual honor and respect, reflecting the harmony and joy of their eternal abode.

translation: There will be circulated among them a cup from a pure spring.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate reward of the righteous in Paradise, where they will be served with pure, refreshing drinks from the spring of life, symbolizing eternal bliss and divine generosity.

translation: A delight for the drinkers, white and pure.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describes the reward of the righteous in Paradise, where their drink is not only pure and refreshing but also a source of immense joy and satisfaction for those who partake in it, symbolizing the ultimate bliss and divine favor.

translation: Therein (the wine of Paradise) will be no intoxication nor will they suffer any exhaustion from it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purity and perfection of the blessings in Paradise, highlighting that they are free from any negative effects or flaws, ensuring that the believers experience only pure, untainted joy and fulfillment.

translation: And with them will be women of modest gaze, with lowered eyes,
interpretation: This phrase describes the purity and modesty of the believing women in Paradise, highlighting their chastity and dignity, as they do not cast lustful glances nor are they subjected to any indecency, reflecting a state of complete spiritual and moral refinement.

translation: As if they were protected pearls.
interpretation: This verse uses the metaphor of pearls to describe the beauty and purity of the women being referred to, emphasizing their untouched and radiant nature, suggesting a sense of exclusivity and high value.

translation: Then they turned to one another, questioning.
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of intense reflection and mutual inquiry among people, often in the context of the Hereafter, where individuals will turn to each other in bewilderment or realization, seeking answers or confessing their past deeds.

translation: One of them will say, 'Indeed, I had a companion (who misguided me).'
interpretation: This verse reflects the regret and acknowledgment of a person in the Hereafter who realizes that their companion in this world led them astray from the path of truth and righteousness, highlighting the consequences of bad company and the importance of choosing righteous associates.

translation: Do you say that he is indeed one of the truthful?
interpretation: This verse reflects skepticism and doubt towards the truthfulness of a messenger or a claimant of truth, highlighting the challenge of accepting divine messages without evidence or conviction.

translation: What, when we are dead and have become dust and bones, shall we indeed be resurrected?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of resurrection by questioning the possibility of life after complete physical decomposition, highlighting the skepticism of those who deny the Hereafter.

translation: He said, 'Will you then watch?',
interpretation: This verse reflects the challenge posed by Prophet Hud (peace be upon him) to his people, the tribe of 'Aad, to witness the consequences of their rejection of divine guidance and their arrogance, implying that divine retribution is imminent and unavoidable.

translation: Then he looked and saw him in the midst of the blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the certainty of divine justice and the inescapable consequences of one's actions, as the individual is shown the reality of their fate in the Hellfire, a place of unrelenting punishment.

translation: By Allah, I swear that I was about to lead you astray.
interpretation: This verse reflects the speaker's acknowledgment of a momentary temptation or inclination toward misguidance, which they attribute to their own human frailty, but they affirm their ultimate commitment to truth and righteousness by invoking Allah's name.

translation: And if it were not for the favor of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth (to punishment).
interpretation: This verse reflects deep gratitude and humility before divine grace, acknowledging that without God's mercy, one would face inevitable punishment or destruction, underscoring the absolute dependence of humanity on divine benevolence.

translation: So will We not cause them to die?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of human mortality and the inevitability of death, implying that God’s power extends beyond the natural order, suggesting a deeper reality or divine intervention in the cycle of life and death.

translation: Except for our first death, and we will not be punished.
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of disbelief or denial where the speaker dismisses the possibility of resurrection and punishment, suggesting that death is a one-time event and that they will not face accountability for their actions.

translation: Indeed, this is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the ultimate success and salvation that comes from adhering to divine guidance and righteous deeds, highlighting that true victory lies in attaining Allah's pleasure and the Hereafter.

translation: So let the workers work for the like of it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of striving for excellence and perfection in one's deeds, as if they were being judged by the highest standards, encouraging believers to perform their actions with sincerity, dedication, and the utmost effort.

translation: Is that [a] better hospitality or the tree of Zaqqum?
interpretation: This verse challenges the listener to reflect on the stark contrast between the eternal reward of the righteous and the severe punishment of the wicked, using the metaphor of the Zaqqum tree—a symbol of excruciating torment—to underscore the gravity of rejecting divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse highlights that trials and tests are often a consequence of oppression and injustice, serving as a means to expose the true nature of the oppressors and to manifest their disbelief or defiance against divine guidance.

translation: Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the depths of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describes the severe and unbearable torment of Hell, where even the trees are manifestations of its horrors, symbolizing the inescapable and overwhelming nature of divine punishment for the disbelievers and wrongdoers.

translation: Its heads are like the heads of devils.
interpretation: This verse describes a plant or tree with an appearance so twisted and unnatural that it resembles the heads of devils, symbolizing something grotesque, cursed, or utterly repellent in form and nature.

translation: Indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of the consequences of one's actions, highlighting that those who engage in wrongdoing will inevitably face the repercussions, which will be as certain and consuming as the food they eat.

translation: Then indeed, they will have a mixture of scalding water.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of the punishment in the Hereafter, where even the drink offered to the wrongdoers is not pure but mixed with something as painful as scalding water, symbolizing the inescapable torment and the complete loss of comfort or relief.

translation: Then indeed, their return will be to Hell.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice, emphasizing that those who persist in wrongdoing will ultimately face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter, with Hell as their final destination.

translation: Indeed, they have found their forefathers astray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the tendency of people to follow the traditions and beliefs of their ancestors without questioning or verifying their correctness, even if those traditions are misguided or deviant.

translation: They rush after them in haste.
interpretation: This verse implies a blind or reckless following of others without independent thought or reflection, often driven by blind imitation or desire for worldly gains, rather than seeking truth or righteousness.

translation: And indeed, before them, most of the former peoples went astray.
interpretation: This verse serves as a cautionary reminder that deviation from the truth and righteousness is not a new phenomenon but has been a recurring pattern throughout human history, urging believers to remain steadfast in their faith and guidance.

translation: And We have already sent among them warners.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine tradition of sending messengers to guide humanity, emphasizing Allah's mercy and justice in providing clear guidance and warnings to every community.

translation: So observe how was the end of those who were warned.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences faced by those who were given clear warnings but chose to ignore them, implying that divine justice prevails and that rejecting guidance leads to ruin.

translation: Except the chosen servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity of divine mercy and salvation, which is granted only to those who have purified their intentions and actions solely for the sake of Allah, free from any form of shirk (associating partners with Allah) or hypocrisy.

translation: And indeed, Noah called upon Us, so how excellent a Responder [We were]!
interpretation: This verse highlights the responsiveness and mercy of Allah in answering the prayers of His righteous servants, demonstrating His unfailing support for those who turn to Him in faith and devotion.

translation: And We delivered him and his family from the great distress.
interpretation: This verse highlights divine intervention and mercy, demonstrating that those who remain steadfast in faith and righteousness are granted relief from overwhelming hardships, even in seemingly impossible situations.

translation: And We made his descendants the survivors.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the preservation and continuation of the lineage of a righteous servant of God (likely referring to Noah, as mentioned in the broader context of the surah), highlighting divine favor and the perpetuation of their legacy despite overwhelming destruction.

translation: And We left for him among later generations [a message],
interpretation: This verse highlights the enduring legacy of a righteous individual, indicating that their influence and teachings continue to benefit subsequent generations, serving as a reminder of their piety and guidance.

translation: Peace be upon Noah among the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the universal recognition of Prophet Noah's (peace be upon him) righteousness and his elevated status as a messenger of God, whose legacy of faith and perseverance is acknowledged across all realms of existence.

translation: Indeed, thus We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and recompense, affirming that Allah rewards those who perform righteous deeds with goodness, reflecting His perfect justice and mercy.

translation: Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine recognition of a person's faith and devotion, indicating that their belief is acknowledged and valued by Allah, regardless of their worldly status or circumstances.

translation: Then We drowned the others.
interpretation: This verse signifies divine retribution against those who persistently reject the truth and oppress others despite clear warnings, illustrating that Allah's justice will ultimately prevail over injustice.

translation: And indeed, among his (Noah's) followers was Abraham.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual lineage and continuity of guidance, showing that even in the time of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him), there were righteous individuals like Prophet Abraham (peace be upon him) who followed the same monotheistic path, emphasizing the unbroken chain of prophethood and the consistency of divine guidance across generations.

translation: When he came to his Lord with a sound heart.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and purity of intention in one's relationship with Allah. A 'sound heart' (قلب سليم) refers to a heart free from shirk (associating partners with Allah), hypocrisy, malice, and spiritual ailments, embodying complete trust, devotion, and submission to Allah alone.

translation: When he said to his father and his people, 'What do you worship?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the prophetic approach of challenging false beliefs and inviting reflection on the nature of worship, emphasizing the importance of questioning and discerning truth from falsehood in matters of faith.

translation: Do you then seek other than Allah for your god?
interpretation: This verse questions the rationality of worshipping false deities or idols instead of the One True God, emphasizing the absurdity of replacing the Creator with created things that cannot benefit or harm.

translation: Then what is your thought about the Lord of the worlds?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question that underscores the gravity of reflecting upon the nature and attributes of Allah, the Lord of all creation. It serves as a call to ponder deeply about the Creator’s power, wisdom, and authority over the universe, urging humanity to recognize His supremacy and the consequences of their actions in light of His dominion.

translation: Then he looked with a glance at the stars.
interpretation: This verse highlights a moment of reflection or consideration, where the subject pauses to observe the heavens, suggesting a search for meaning, guidance, or divine signs.

translation: So he said, "Indeed, I am [about to be] ill."
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of divine intervention through a seemingly mundane excuse, highlighting how even the most trivial of human actions can be used by Allah to fulfill His greater plan, in this case, exposing the disbelief of the people and preserving the righteousness of the Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

translation: So they turned away from him, fleeing.
interpretation: This verse reflects the rejection and defiance of truth by those who are arrogant or obstinate, choosing to flee from guidance rather than confront it.

translation: Then he turned to their gods and said, 'Will you not eat?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the absurdity and powerlessness of idols, as Ibrahim (AS) sarcastically questions why they do not partake in food, exposing their inability to act or respond, thereby undermining the false notion of their divinity.

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not speak?
interpretation: This verse is a reproach to those who remain silent in the face of truth or injustice, urging them to use their voice and speech for righteousness rather than passivity or fear.

translation: And strike them with your right hand.
interpretation: This verse is often interpreted within the context of disciplining children or correcting wrongdoers with a balanced and measured approach, emphasizing the use of the right hand as a symbol of authority and guidance rather than literal physical harm.

translation: So they came to him joyfully and cheerfully.
interpretation: This verse reflects a moment of collective joy and enthusiasm in response to divine guidance or a positive turn of events, highlighting the natural human inclination to welcome truth and righteousness with open hearts and gladness.

translation: Do you worship what you carve yourselves?
interpretation: This verse condemns the act of worshipping idols that are carved by human hands, emphasizing the absurdity of attributing divinity to objects created by humans rather than the Creator Himself.

translation: And Allah created you and what you do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over all creation, including human actions, which are ultimately subject to His will and decree.

translation: They said, "Construct for him a building, then throw him into the blazing fire."
interpretation: This verse reflects the extreme enmity and malicious intent of those who sought to harm the Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) by devising a cruel plan to burn him alive, demonstrating their rejection of truth and their readiness to commit grave injustices.

translation: But they intended to harm him, so We made them the lowest.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine justice that intervenes when people plot against the righteous, ensuring that their schemes ultimately fail and they are humiliated, emphasizing God's power to protect His chosen ones and the futility of opposing divine will.

translation: And he said, 'Indeed, I am going toward my Lord; He will guide me.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the unwavering trust and submission of a believer in the divine plan, even when facing uncertainty or separation from the familiar. It signifies that true guidance comes from Allah alone, and that one's journey—whether literal or metaphorical—is ultimately in His hands.

translation: My Lord, grant me [a child] from among the righteous.
interpretation: This supplication reflects a deep yearning for righteous progeny, recognizing that children are a blessing from Allah and that their righteousness is a source of comfort and pride for parents in this life and the Hereafter.

translation: So We gave him the good tidings of a forbearing son.
interpretation: This verse highlights the virtue of patience and forbearance, emphasizing that divine rewards are often bestowed upon those who remain steadfast and composed in the face of trials, as exemplified by the son who would later be known for his wisdom and restraint.

translation: And when they had both submitted [to the command of Allah] and he put him down upon his forehead, We called to him, "O Abraham, You have fulfilled the vision. Indeed, We thus reward the doers of good." Indeed, this was the clear trial. And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice,
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate test of faith and submission to Allah's command, demonstrating that true devotion requires complete trust in Allah's wisdom, even in the face of seemingly impossible or painful trials.

translation: So when they had both submitted [to the will of Allah] and he put him down on his forehead [for sacrifice],
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate act of submission and trust in Allah's command, demonstrating that true faith requires complete surrender, even in the face of immense personal sacrifice.

translation: And We called him, 'O Abraham!'
interpretation: This verse highlights the intimate and direct communication between Allah and His chosen servant, Ibrahim (AS). It signifies a moment of divine calling, emphasizing Allah's personal attention and the special status of Ibrahim (AS) as a friend of Allah (Khalilullah). The call is not just a summon but an invitation to a higher purpose, reflecting the deep connection and trust between the servant and his Lord.

translation: The vision was true. Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine promises and rewards for those who strive to do good, affirming that Allah's justice and generosity are manifest in fulfilling His word.

translation: Indeed, this is the manifest trial.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity and undeniable nature of a test or hardship that a believer is facing, highlighting that such trials are a profound and unmistakable part of life's challenges, designed to test faith and resilience.

translation: And We ransomed him with a great sacrifice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate test of faith and submission to Allah, where the willingness to sacrifice what is most precious—even one's own child—demonstrates unwavering trust in divine command.

translation: And We left for him among later generations [the message],
interpretation: This verse highlights the enduring legacy of a righteous individual, indicating that their influence and teachings persist through subsequent generations, serving as a reminder of their virtue and guidance.

translation: Peace be upon Ibrahim (Abraham).
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine acknowledgment of Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) righteousness and his elevated status in the sight of Allah, highlighting the eternal peace and honor bestowed upon him as a reward for his unwavering faith and devotion.

translation: Thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and recompense, affirming that Allah rewards those who perform righteous deeds with goodness, reflecting His perfect justice and mercy.

translation: Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the status of a person as a true believer in the sight of Allah, emphasizing their righteousness and acceptance in the divine presence.

translation: And We gave him the good tidings of Isaac as a prophet, one of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor of granting a righteous child who would also be a prophet, emphasizing the continuity of prophethood through righteous lineage and the fulfillment of Allah's promises.

translation: And We blessed him and Isaac. And among their descendants are doers of good and [also] clearly unjust to themselves.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of human potential within the lineage of Prophets, emphasizing that divine blessings do not guarantee moral perfection but rather provide the opportunity for both righteousness and self-destruction, underscoring the importance of personal accountability.

translation: And We had certainly conferred favor upon Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine grace and favor bestowed upon the prophets Moses (Musa) and Aaron (Harun) by Allah, emphasizing their elevated status and the special support they received in their mission to guide their people.

translation: And We delivered them and their people from the great distress.
interpretation: This verse highlights divine intervention in times of severe hardship, emphasizing that deliverance comes from Allah alone, reinforcing trust in His power and mercy.

translation: And We supported them, so they became the dominant ones.
interpretation: This verse highlights divine intervention and the ultimate triumph of those who are supported by Allah, emphasizing that true victory comes from His aid rather than mere human effort or power.

translation: And We gave them the clear Book.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor of granting a clear and unambiguous scripture to a people, which serves as a guidance and a criterion between right and wrong, emphasizing the importance of divine revelation in distinguishing truth from falsehood.

translation: And We guided them to the straight path.
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah has granted guidance to all of creation, particularly humans, by providing them with the means to recognize and follow the truth, which is the straight path leading to righteousness and ultimate success.

translation: And We left for them (a lesson) among later generations.
interpretation: This verse highlights the enduring legacy and lessons that remain from the stories of past prophets and their nations, serving as a reminder and guidance for future generations.

translation: Peace be upon Moses and Aaron.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor and honor bestowed upon the prophets Moses (Musa) and Aaron (Harun), peace be upon them, by Allah. It signifies the purity and righteousness of their mission and serves as a reminder of Allah's mercy and blessings upon His righteous servants.

translation: Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine principle of reciprocity—Allah rewards those who perform good deeds with commensurate good, reflecting His justice and mercy.

translation: Indeed, they are among Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine recognition and validation of certain individuals as true believers, highlighting Allah's intimate knowledge of their faith and devotion, and affirming their status as part of the righteous community.

translation: And indeed, Elias (Elijah) was one of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse affirms the prophethood of Elias (peace be upon him), placing him among the righteous messengers chosen by Allah to convey His guidance to humanity.

translation: When he said to his people, 'Will you not fear Allah?',
interpretation: This verse highlights the prophetic call to recognize divine authority and moral accountability, urging the listener to reflect on their actions and the consequences of disregarding divine guidance.

translation: Do you call upon Baal and forsake the Best of creators?
interpretation: This verse critiques the act of worshipping false deities or idols while neglecting the worship of Allah, the One True Creator, who is unparalleled in His perfection and excellence.

translation: Allah is your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers of old.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unchanging nature of Allah as the sole Lord and sustainer of all creation, including past generations, affirming His eternal authority and the continuity of divine guidance across time.

translation: But they denied it, so they will be brought [for punishment].
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice, warning those who reject the truth that their denial will not save them from accountability, as they will ultimately face the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.

translation: Except the chosen servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exclusivity of divine mercy and salvation, which is reserved for those who are sincere and devoted to Allah alone, free from any form of idolatry or hypocrisy.

translation: And We left for him among the later generations [a message],
interpretation: This verse highlights the enduring legacy of a righteous individual, indicating that their influence and teachings are perpetuated through subsequent generations, serving as a reminder of their virtue and guidance.

translation: Peace be upon the family of Elias.
interpretation: This verse signifies that divine mercy and peace are bestowed upon the family of the Prophet Elias (Elijah), highlighting their righteousness and spiritual status in the sight of Allah.

translation: Indeed, thus do We reward the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice and recompense, affirming that Allah rewards those who perform good deeds with excellence and sincerity, reflecting His perfect justice and mercy.

translation: Indeed, he was of Our believing servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the status of a person as a true believer, emphasizing their unwavering faith and devotion to God, which is recognized and acknowledged by Allah Himself.

translation: And indeed, Lot was one of the messengers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine selection and prophetic mission of Lot (peace be upon him), affirming his status as a chosen messenger of Allah, tasked with guiding his people despite their rejection and immorality.

translation: When We saved him and all his family.
interpretation: This verse highlights divine mercy and protection granted to a righteous servant of God and his entire household, emphasizing that salvation is a gift of faith and obedience to God's will.

translation: Except an old woman among those who remained behind.
interpretation: This verse refers to the wife of Prophet Lot (peace be upon him), who was an exception among her people—those who persisted in their disbelief and wickedness—because she did not follow them in their transgression but remained steadfast in her faith, though she was ultimately destroyed with them due to her association with them.

translation: Then We destroyed the others.
interpretation: This verse signifies the decisive end of those who persistently rejected the truth and were warned by divine signs but failed to heed them, illustrating the inevitability of divine retribution for defiance and disbelief.

translation: And indeed, you pass by them in the morning
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of human life and the inevitability of encountering divine signs, even in mundane daily routines, urging reflection on the deeper realities beyond the visible world.

translation: And during the night. Will you not then understand?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and contemplation over the signs of Allah in the natural world, such as the alternation of day and night, urging humanity to ponder these signs to recognize divine wisdom and guidance.

translation: And indeed, Jonah was among the messengers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inclusion of Jonah (Yunus) among the prophets sent by Allah, highlighting his status as a chosen messenger despite his temporary lapse in patience, which serves as a lesson in divine mercy and the importance of steadfastness in faith.

translation: When he fled to the laden ship.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Prophet Yunus (Jonah, peace be upon him) fleeing from his people in a state of distress, seeking refuge in a ship that was heavily laden with cargo and passengers, marking the beginning of his journey that would lead to his eventual deliverance by Allah's command.

translation: So he responded, and thus became among those who were refuted.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of opposing divine truth; those who stubbornly reject guidance, despite clear evidence, ultimately face humiliation and defeat, as their arguments are exposed as baseless.

translation: So the fish swallowed him while he was blameworthy.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of one's actions when they go against divine will or moral conduct, as seen in Prophet Yunus's (Jonah) story, where his fleeing from his mission led to his punishment and subsequent remorse.

translation: Then why was he not among those who glorify [Allah]?
interpretation: This verse questions the absence of a person from the ranks of those who consistently remember and praise Allah, implying a reproach for failing to uphold the spiritual duty of dhikr (remembrance of Allah) despite being aware of its importance.

translation: To dwell in his belly until the Day they are resurrected.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe and inescapable punishment of those who consume the wealth of orphans unjustly, comparing their fate to being trapped in the belly of a beast until the Day of Resurrection—a vivid metaphor for the inevitability and horror of divine retribution.

translation: But We cast him onto the open shore, and he was ill.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of divine rejection and the humbling of those who defy God's will, even when they appear to have been favored by temporary success.

translation: And We caused to grow, on top of him, a plant of gourd.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and care even in the most dire of circumstances, demonstrating that He can provide sustenance and relief in ways that are beyond human expectation or conventional means.

translation: And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more.
interpretation: This verse highlights the magnitude of Prophet Jonah's (Yunus) mission, emphasizing that his call to repentance reached an exceptionally large audience, demonstrating Allah's mercy and the vastness of His guidance.

translation: So they believed; then We granted them enjoyment for a time.
interpretation: This verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly blessings and the importance of faith as the true source of lasting benefit. It serves as a reminder that material prosperity is not a definitive sign of divine favor, nor is hardship a sign of displeasure, as both are tests for humanity.

translation: Then ask them: 'Is your Lord the One Who has daughters while they have sons?'
interpretation: This verse challenges the pre-Islamic Arabian society's irrational preference for male children over female children, highlighting the inconsistency in their beliefs about divine attribution and human lineage.

translation: Or did We create the angels as females, while they are witnesses?
interpretation: This verse challenges the pre-Islamic Arabian belief that angels were female, ascribing to them a gender that contradicts their true nature as genderless, spiritual beings created by Allah. It underscores the absurdity of such claims by highlighting the angels' own witness to Allah's creative power, which does not involve such distortions.

translation: Behold, they utter a lie against Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of falsehood attributed to Allah, emphasizing that such claims are not merely erroneous but constitute a grave sin and a deliberate distortion of truth.

translation: They say, "Allah has begotten a son," but they are truly lying.
interpretation: This verse refutes the false claim that Allah has a son, emphasizing that such an assertion is a lie and contradicts the absolute oneness and transcendence of Allah.

translation: Has He chosen daughters over sons?
interpretation: This rhetorical question is used to challenge the pre-Islamic Arabian practice of preferring male children over females, highlighting the injustice and ignorance of such discrimination, while affirming Allah's perfect and just choice in creation.

translation: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This verse is a reproach to those who make unfair or unjust judgments, implying that their reasoning is flawed or their moral compass is misaligned, as they fail to uphold truth and justice in their rulings.

translation: Then will you not remember?
interpretation: This verse serves as a rhetorical question, urging reflection on the signs of Allah's existence and power in the universe, encouraging the listener to ponder and recognize the truth.

translation: Or do you have a clear authority (or proof)?
interpretation: This verse challenges those who reject the truth without valid evidence or reasoning, implying that their denial is baseless and lacks any legitimate support.

translation: Then bring your book, if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who deny the truth to present their own scripture or evidence to support their claims, implying that their inability to do so underscores the authenticity and divine origin of the Qur'an.

translation: And they have attributed to Him [partners] from among His creation, while the creation will surely be brought before Him.
interpretation: This verse condemns the attribution of partners or equals to Allah, emphasizing that all creation, including those who commit shirk (associationism), will ultimately be presented before Him for judgment, underscoring the absolute oneness (Tawheed) of Allah and the accountability of all beings.

translation: Exalted is Allah above what they describe [i.e., attribute to Him].
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute transcendence of Allah from any imperfections, false attributes, or anthropomorphic descriptions that people may ascribe to Him, affirming His purity and uniqueness beyond human comprehension or comparison.

translation: Except the chosen servants of Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exclusivity of divine mercy and salvation, emphasizing that only those who are truly sincere and devoted to Allah, free from any form of hypocrisy or hidden agenda, will be granted His special protection and favor.

translation: Indeed, you [disbelievers] and whatever you worship
interpretation: This verse addresses the disbelievers of the Quraysh tribe, challenging their false deities and affirming the exclusivity of Allah's worship, as their objects of worship hold no power or reality in comparison to the One True God.

translation: You will not be able to entice anyone away from what they are upon.
interpretation: This verse underscores the steadfastness of people in their beliefs or paths, suggesting that no external influence or temptation can sway them from their core convictions if they are firmly rooted in truth and righteousness.

translation: Except those destined for Hell.
interpretation: This phrase underscores the absolute justice and divine decree of Allah, indicating that some individuals are predestined for Hell due to their persistent rejection of faith and wrongdoing, as a consequence of their own choices and actions.

translation: And there is not one of us but has a known appointed place.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine decree and the predetermined stages of existence assigned to every individual, whether human or jinn, highlighting the inevitability of their roles and fates within the cosmic order.

translation: And indeed, it is We who are the arrangers [of revelation],
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute control over the revelation of the Qur'an, highlighting that He alone orchestrates its preservation, arrangement, and transmission, ensuring its authenticity and divine origin.

translation: And indeed, it is We who are the glorifiers [of Allah] and the praisers [of Him].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusive right of Allah alone to be glorified and praised, affirming His absolute sovereignty and uniqueness in all forms of worship, including tasbeeh (glorification) and praise.

translation: And indeed, they used to say
interpretation: This phrase introduces a statement or claim made by a group of people, often implying that their words were habitual or persistent, suggesting a pattern of behavior or belief that may be challenged or corrected in the subsequent context.

translation: If only We had a reminder from the earlier peoples.
interpretation: This verse expresses a profound sense of regret and missed opportunity, highlighting the human tendency to wish for past guidance or warnings that were not heeded, emphasizing the importance of learning from history and divine messages.

translation: But we are the sincere servants of Allah.
interpretation: This phrase emphasizes the exclusivity and sincerity of one's devotion to Allah, rejecting any association of partners or impure motives in worship, and affirming that true servitude belongs solely to Him.

translation: But they disbelieved in it, so they will come to know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth despite clear evidence, indicating that their denial will lead to a realization of the consequences in the Hereafter, where they will face the reality of their disbelief.

translation: And Our word has already gone forth to Our servants the messengers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and finality of Allah's decree, particularly concerning the success of His messengers and their followers, despite the trials they face in conveying the truth.

translation: Indeed, they are the victorious ones.
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that despite the apparent struggles and hardships they may face in the world, they are ultimately on the path of triumph and success in the sight of Allah, as their efforts are aligned with divine truth and justice.

translation: And indeed, Our soldiers are the ones who will prevail.
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that divine support and victory belong to them, as God's forces—whether angelic, historical, or spiritual—are ultimately triumphant against oppression and falsehood, regardless of apparent worldly setbacks.

translation: So turn away from them for a while
interpretation: This verse instructs patience and forbearance in the face of adversity or opposition, suggesting a temporary disengagement from conflict to allow for reflection or a shift in circumstances.

translation: And they will see [their deeds], and soon they will see [the consequences].
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine justice, where every action will be fully witnessed and accounted for in the Hereafter, leaving no room for denial or escape from the consequences of one's deeds.

translation: Do they challenge Our punishment by seeking to hasten it?
interpretation: This verse underscores the arrogance and disbelief of those who challenge Allah's divine wisdom by demanding the immediate realization of His punishment, failing to recognize the mercy and patience He extends before any reckoning.

translation: But when it descends upon their outskirts, woe to the warned ones in the morning.
interpretation: This verse warns of the sudden and unexpected arrival of divine punishment or a severe calamity, emphasizing the regret and despair that will afflict those who were warned but did not heed the warnings or take them seriously.

translation: And turn away from them for a while.
interpretation: This verse instructs patience and restraint in the face of adversity or opposition, suggesting a temporary disengagement rather than immediate confrontation, allowing time for reflection or divine resolution.

translation: And see! Soon they will see.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who deny the truth or oppose divine guidance, indicating that they will eventually come to recognize the reality of their situation, whether in this life or the Hereafter, when it will be too late for repentance or benefit.

translation: Glory be to your Lord, the Lord of Majesty and Honour, above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence of Allah from any imperfections or false attributes that people may ascribe to Him, affirming His absolute perfection and majesty.

translation: And peace be upon the messengers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine recognition and honor bestowed upon all the prophets and messengers sent by Allah, affirming their status as bearers of truth and mercy, and invoking blessings and tranquility upon them as a testament to their unwavering commitment to delivering Allah's message.

translation: And all praise is due to Allah, the Lord of all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse establishes the foundational principle of gratitude and recognition of Allah's sovereignty over all creation, emphasizing that every form of praise inherently belongs to Him alone.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Saad. By the Qur'an containing the reminder (or the one who is reminded).
interpretation: This verse begins with the basmala, affirming divine mercy and grace, followed by the letter 'Saad' whose precise meaning is known only to Allah, and then emphasizes the Qur'an as a source of profound remembrance and guidance, highlighting its role in reminding humanity of divine truths and moral responsibilities.

translation: Nay, but those who disbelieve are in [a state of] arrogance and defiance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the spiritual and moral state of those who reject faith, describing their condition as one of arrogance and defiance against divine truth, which blinds them to guidance and leads to their downfall.

translation: How many generations We have destroyed before them! They called out when there was no longer time for escape.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief and defiance, emphasizing that repentance and escape are no longer possible once God's decree has been issued.

translation: And they wondered that a warner had come to them from among themselves. And the disbelievers said, "This is a magician, a liar."
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to dismiss truth when it comes from familiar sources, often attributing noble or divine messages to mundane or deceitful motives when they challenge one's preconceived notions or interests.

translation: Will they set up another god besides Allah? Indeed, that would be a tremendous thing.
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of associating partners with Allah, emphasizing the absurdity and impossibility of such an idea, as it contradicts the fundamental principle of monotheism (Tawhid) in Islam.

translation: And the eminent ones among them set out, [saying], "Go forth and persist steadfastly in [worship of] your gods. Indeed, this [Quran] is something intended [to be thwarted]."
interpretation: This verse reflects the arrogance and defiance of the polytheistic leaders of Makkah who, despite witnessing the signs of truth in the Quran, chose to reject it out of pride and attachment to their false deities. Their call to persist in idolatry reveals their deep-seated resistance to divine truth, rooted in fear of losing their social and religious influence.

translation: We have not heard of this in the former faith: this is nothing but a forgery.
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and denial of the disbelievers towards the message of the Qur'an, dismissing it as a fabrication rather than divine revelation, highlighting their refusal to accept truth despite its clarity.

translation: Has the Remembrance been sent down to him from among us? Rather, they are in doubt about My Remembrance. Rather, they have not yet tasted My punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and denial of those who reject divine guidance, questioning why revelation would come to someone among them rather than to themselves, reflecting their misplaced sense of superiority and lack of humility before God.

translation: Or do they possess the treasures of the mercy of your Lord, the Exalted in Might, the Bestower?
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers who reject the signs and guidance of Allah, questioning whether they have exclusive access to divine mercy or possess the keys to Allah's treasures of grace and provision, which they can dispense at their own will.

translation: Or do they possess the dominion of the heavens and the earth and what is between them? Then let them ascend through [any] means.
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers' arrogance and false claims of power, questioning whether they truly possess any authority over the heavens, the earth, and everything in between. The call to 'ascend through [any] means' is a rhetorical challenge, implying that even if they had such power, they would be incapable of achieving anything beyond their limited understanding, as true dominion belongs solely to Allah.

translation: The confederate forces were routed, and they could not achieve their goal.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of human alliances and schemes when they are formed against divine will, highlighting that no power can withstand God's decree.

translation: Before them, the people of Noah, 'Aad, and Pharaoh of the stakes denied (the messengers).
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth, highlighting that previous nations who denied their messengers faced severe consequences, emphasizing the inevitability of divine retribution for persistent disbelief.

translation: And the Thamud, and the people of Lot, and the Dwellers of the Wood—those were the factions.
interpretation: This verse highlights the historical consequences faced by past nations and communities that rejected divine guidance, serving as a reminder of the fate that awaits those who persist in disbelief or defiance of moral and spiritual truths.

translation: There is none among them but that they have denied the messengers, so My punishment is justified.
interpretation: This verse underscores the recurring pattern of human rejection of divine messengers throughout history, emphasizing that denial of truth is met with just consequences, reinforcing the principle of accountability in divine justice.

translation: And these [disbelievers] await nothing except a single blast [of the Horn]; there will be no second one.
interpretation: This verse underscores the sudden and irreversible nature of divine judgment, emphasizing that the disbelievers' denial will be met with an abrupt and decisive end, leaving no room for repentance or delay.

translation: And they say, 'Our Lord, hasten for us our share before the Day of Judgment.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the impatience and arrogance of those who demand immediate punishment for the righteous, challenging divine wisdom and timing, thereby exposing their own disbelief and disregard for the divine plan.

translation: Be patient over what they say, and remember Our servant David, the possessor of strength; indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder that patience in the face of adversity and mockery is a virtue, and that turning to Allah in repentance and devotion is a path to strength and guidance, as exemplified by the Prophet David (peace be upon him).

translation: Indeed, We subjected the mountains [to praise] along with him, exalting [Allah] in the evening and at dawn.
interpretation: This verse highlights the harmony between all elements of creation in glorifying Allah, emphasizing that even inanimate entities like mountains are made to participate in this universal act of worship, underscoring the interconnectedness of all existence in divine praise.

translation: And the birds gathered in flocks—each one turns to Allah in devotion.
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural inclination of all creatures, including birds, toward recognizing and submitting to their Creator, emphasizing the universal pattern of divine guidance and the innate disposition (fitrah) of all beings to turn to Allah.

translation: And We strengthened his kingdom and gave him wisdom and decisive speech.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon a prophet (likely Solomon, peace be upon him) by granting him not only political and military strength but also profound wisdom and the ability to articulate truth with clarity and justice.

translation: Has the story of the dispute come to you, when they climbed over the wall into the private chamber?
interpretation: This verse refers to a profound test of faith and divine justice, illustrating how Allah tests His servants through seemingly insurmountable trials, yet ultimately delivers them through His wisdom and power when they place their trust in Him.

translation: When they came to David and he was startled by them, they said, "Fear not! [We are] two adversaries: one of us has wronged the other, so judge between us with truth and do not exceed [in injustice], and guide us to the right path."
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of justice and impartiality in judgment, even when faced with unexpected or intimidating situations. It also underscores the role of a just ruler or leader in resolving disputes fairly and guiding people toward the truth and the right path.

translation: Indeed, this brother of mine has ninety-nine ewes, and I have one ewe only. So he said, 'Entrust her to me,' and he overpowered me in speech.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the use of persuasive speech to unjustly claim something that belongs to another, highlighting the importance of fairness and integrity in dealings, even in matters of negotiation or dialogue.

translation: He said, 'Indeed, he has wronged you in demanding your ewe [in addition] to his ewes. And indeed, many associates oppress one another, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds—and few are they.' And David became certain that We had tried him, so he asked forgiveness of his Lord and fell down bowing [in prostration] and turned in repentance [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and spiritual distinction between those who prioritize justice and righteousness (embodied by the few who believe and do good) and those who succumb to greed and oppression (like the majority of associates). It also underscores the humility and repentance of Prophet David (peace be upon him) when he realized his mistake, demonstrating that even righteous individuals may falter but can seek forgiveness and return to Allah with sincere repentance.

translation: So We forgave him for that; and indeed, he has nearness to Us and an excellent place of return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine mercy and forgiveness granted to a righteous servant, emphasizing that true proximity to Allah is attained through repentance, righteousness, and steadfastness in faith, leading to an ultimate return to Him in the Hereafter.

translation: O David, indeed We have made you a vicegerent upon the earth, so judge between the people in truth and do not follow [your own] desire, as it will lead you astray from the way of Allah. Indeed, those who are led astray from the way of Allah will have a severe punishment for forgetting the Day of Account.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of leadership and the moral responsibility that comes with authority. It warns against the corruption of power when personal desires or biases influence judgment, emphasizing that true justice must be rooted in divine truth rather than human inclination. The severe punishment mentioned for straying from Allah’s path serves as a reminder of the accountability that leaders—and all people—will face on the Day of Judgment, reinforcing the necessity of integrity and adherence to divine guidance in all decisions.

translation: And We did not create the heaven and the earth and what is between them without purpose. That is the assumption of those who disbelieve, so woe to those who disbelieve from the Fire.
interpretation: This verse refutes the notion that the creation of the universe is without purpose or meaning, a belief held by those who deny the existence of Allah and the Hereafter. It emphasizes that the creation of the heavens, the earth, and everything in between is purposeful and deliberate, serving as a sign of Allah's wisdom, power, and the reality of the Day of Judgment.

translation: Or should we treat those who believe and do righteous deeds the same as those who spread corruption on earth? Or should We treat the righteous the same as the wicked?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of moral equivalence, emphasizing that Allah does not judge believers and righteous people the same as those who engage in corruption or wrongdoing, as divine justice inherently distinguishes between good and evil.

translation: A Book which We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], full of blessing, that they may ponder over its verses and that men of understanding may remember.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and the profound blessings of the Qur'an, urging believers to deeply reflect on its verses and to derive wisdom and guidance from it, rather than merely reciting it passively.

translation: And We gave David, Solomon. An excellent servant, indeed he was one who repeatedly turned back [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor bestowed upon Solomon, the son of David, and emphasizes his exceptional devotion to Allah, characterized by constant repentance and return to Him.

translation: When they were presented to him at the time of the afternoon, the swift, high-stepping horses.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of recognizing and appreciating the beauty and strength of Allah's creation, as well as the fleeting nature of worldly distractions when compared to the remembrance of Allah.

translation: And he said, 'Indeed, I have preferred the love of good things over the remembrance of my Lord until [the sun] disappeared behind the curtain [of the horizon].'
interpretation: This verse highlights the temporary nature of worldly attachments and the importance of prioritizing spiritual obligations over material desires, even when one is deeply engrossed in them.

translation: So they returned to them. And [the hoopoe] struck [their legs and necks] with its wings.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the swift and decisive action taken against those who oppose divine truth, emphasizing that resistance is met with overwhelming force, leaving no room for doubt or defiance.

translation: And We certainly tested Solomon and placed on his throne a body; then he repented.
interpretation: This verse highlights a trial or test that Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him) faced, where his authority or throne was temporarily altered or challenged, possibly as a means of testing his faith or humility. The 'body' placed on his throne could symbolize a test of his patience, reliance on Allah, or a reminder of the transient nature of worldly power. His subsequent repentance signifies his return to Allah, acknowledging his dependence on Him and seeking forgiveness, which underscores the importance of humility and repentance in the face of trials.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, forgive me and grant me a dominion not permitted to anyone after me. Indeed, You are the Bestower.'
interpretation: This supplication reflects a moment of human vulnerability and the desire for divine favor, while also highlighting the importance of seeking forgiveness and recognizing Allah's ultimate generosity. It underscores the transient nature of worldly power and the need for humility before the Almighty.

translation: So We subjected the wind to his (Solomon's) command, which blew gently wherever he directed it.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine power granted to Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him) as a sign of Allah's favor and the fulfillment of His promise, demonstrating that true authority and control over nature come only through submission to Allah's will.

translation: And [We subjected] the devils, every builder and diver [of the sea],
interpretation: This verse highlights the subjugation of jinn (often referred to as 'devils' or 'shayatin' in this context) by Allah to serve the Prophet Solomon (peace be upon him), demonstrating Allah's absolute power over all creation, including beings beyond human perception, and their forced obedience to divine will for the fulfillment of a higher purpose.

translation: And others bound together in shackles.
interpretation: This verse refers to those who will be punished in the Hereafter, bound together in chains as a sign of their disbelief and defiance against Allah's commands, illustrating the severity of their punishment.

translation: This is Our bounty, so bestow it (as you will), or withhold it, without account.
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute sovereignty of Allah over His favors and blessings, emphasizing that humans are merely entrusted with them and must use them in accordance with divine will, whether through generosity or restraint, without pride or accountability to others.

translation: And indeed, he has nearness to Us and an excellent final return.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status and closeness to Allah that a righteous servant of God attains in the Hereafter, emphasizing that their ultimate return to Him is in the most excellent and honorable manner.

translation: And remember Our servant Job, when he called out to his Lord, 'Satan has afflicted me with hardship and pain.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of turning to Allah in times of distress and recognizing the role of trials in spiritual growth, even when the source of affliction is attributed to external forces like Satan.

translation: Run with your leg [to the river]. This is a cool washing place and a drink.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically instructs the believer to take decisive action (symbolized by 'running') to purify themselves (through repentance or righteous deeds), which will lead to both spiritual cleansing ('cool washing place') and sustenance ('drink'), reflecting the rewards of faith and righteousness.

translation: And We granted him his family and a like number thereof with them, as a mercy from Us and a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine principle of reciprocity and multiplication of blessings as a manifestation of mercy, specifically rewarding those who remain steadfast in faith and righteousness, while also serving as a lesson for those who reflect deeply on the consequences of their actions and the nature of divine justice.

translation: And take in your hand a bundle of grass and strike with it, and do not break your oath. Indeed, We found him patient, an excellent servant. Indeed, he was one who repeatedly turned [to Allah].
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of fulfilling one's oaths while also demonstrating the virtue of patience and steadfastness in the face of trials. It underscores that true servitude to Allah is marked by unwavering commitment, frequent repentance, and a consistent return to Him, even when faced with difficult circumstances.

translation: And remember Our servants, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob - those of strength and vision.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remembering and reflecting upon the lives of the righteous servants of Allah, who possessed both physical and spiritual strength (symbolized by 'hands') and deep insight and wisdom (symbolized by 'eyes'). It serves as a reminder to emulate their steadfastness, devotion, and clarity of purpose in faith and righteousness.

translation: Indeed, We chose them with [the] exclusive [quality of] remembrance of the Hereafter.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special status of certain individuals chosen by Allah due to their unwavering focus on the Hereafter, demonstrating that true devotion is marked by constant mindfulness of the eternal life to come rather than worldly distractions.

translation: And indeed, they are with Us among the chosen, the excellent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the elevated status of certain individuals in the sight of Allah, emphasizing their selection and excellence, which may refer to prophets, righteous servants, or those granted special favor due to their unwavering faith and righteous deeds.

translation: And remember Ishmael, Elisha, and Dhul-Kifl—all of whom were among the good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of remembering and invoking the blessings of past righteous prophets and figures, not merely as historical figures but as enduring examples of righteousness and devotion to God. It underscores the continuity of divine guidance and the virtue of recalling those who upheld truth and righteousness, serving as a reminder of the path of goodness that believers should emulate.

translation: This is a reminder. And indeed, for the God-conscious there is an excellent place of return.
interpretation: This verse underscores the purpose of the Qur'an as a reminder and a guide, while affirming that those who embody piety and mindfulness of Allah will ultimately attain a sublime and blessed destination in the Hereafter.

translation: Gardens of perpetual residence, whose doors will be opened to them.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate reward of Paradise, where the righteous will be granted eternal bliss in lush gardens, and their entry will be marked by divine honor and welcome, symbolizing Allah's boundless mercy and the fulfillment of His promises to the faithful.

translation: Reclining therein, they will call for abundant fruit and drink.
interpretation: This verse highlights the luxurious and bountiful nature of Paradise, emphasizing the comfort and joy of the believers in their eternal abode, where they are free to enjoy the finest provisions without any scarcity or hardship.

translation: And with them will be women of modest gaze, of equal age.
interpretation: This verse highlights the purity and modesty of the believing women in Paradise, who are described as 'qāṣirāt aṭ-ṭarf' (women of modest gaze), meaning they lower their gaze and are not immodest, and 'atrāb' (of equal age), suggesting harmony and compatibility among them, free from worldly imperfections or disparities.

translation: This is what you are promised for the Day of Recompense.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine justice and the inevitability of the Day of Judgment, where every soul will be recompensed according to its deeds, emphasizing accountability and the fulfillment of divine promises.

translation: Indeed, this is Our provision; it will never run out.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the eternal and boundless nature of Allah's provision (rizq), assuring believers that divine sustenance is not limited by scarcity or depletion, but is everlasting and sufficient for all.

translation: This is so, and indeed for the transgressors is the worst destination.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine justice, warning that those who persistently defy God’s commands and indulge in oppression will face a severe and irreversible punishment in the Hereafter, emphasizing the consequences of arrogance and rebellion against divine guidance.

translation: Hellfire they will enter, so wretched is that resting place.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe and irreversible consequences of rejecting divine guidance, emphasizing the gravity of Hellfire as a destination for those who persist in wrongdoing, serving as a stark warning against moral and spiritual negligence.

translation: So let them taste it: boiling water and scalding pus.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the severe and unbearable punishment awaiting the disbelievers in the Hereafter, using vivid and repulsive imagery to convey the intensity of their suffering as a deterrent against disbelief and moral transgression.

translation: And of His signs is that He created for you from yourselves mates
interpretation: This verse highlights the natural pairing and harmony in creation, emphasizing that the existence of spouses is a divine sign of Allah's wisdom and purpose in human life, reflecting love, companionship, and procreation as part of His perfect design.

translation: This is a host rushing against you. There is no welcome for them. They will burn in the Fire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the severe consequences awaiting those who oppose the truth or act with malice. It serves as a warning that no matter how forcefully or persistently wrongdoers may come against the righteous, their ultimate fate is destruction in the Fire, highlighting the futility of their efforts and the certainty of divine retribution.

translation: They said, 'No welcome for you! You have brought this upon us! How wretched a settlement!''
interpretation: This verse reflects the rejection and condemnation of a group who blame others for their misfortune, showing ingratitude and denial of responsibility, highlighting the consequences of poor choices and the rejection of accountability.

translation: They will say, "Our Lord, whoever prepared this for us, double for him the punishment in the Fire."
interpretation: This verse reflects the despair and regret of the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, where they call upon Allah to intensify the punishment for those who led them astray or facilitated their misguidance, demonstrating their acknowledgment of the severity of their fate and the justice of divine retribution.

translation: And they will say, "Why do we not see men whom we used to count among the wicked?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the regret and bewilderment of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment when they realize the absence of those they once considered powerful or evil, highlighting the reversal of worldly perceptions in the Hereafter.

translation: Did We take them in ridicule, or have their eyes strayed (from the truth)?
interpretation: This verse questions whether the disbelievers' rejection of the truth stems from mockery or from a genuine inability to perceive the signs of Allah's guidance, highlighting the depth of their denial.

translation: Indeed, that is the truth—why the people of the Fire will dispute.
interpretation: This verse highlights the inevitability of the Fire's punishment for the wrongdoers, where even in their state of torment, they will argue and dispute among themselves, acknowledging the justice of their punishment but blaming one another for their downfall, reflecting the depths of their regret and denial.

translation: Say, 'I am only a warner.' And there is no god except Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness and supreme power of Allah, emphasizing that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is merely a messenger tasked with warning humanity, not a deity or source of power himself.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and dominion over all creation, highlighting His unmatched power and authority, while also affirming His boundless mercy and forgiveness, which encompasses all things.

translation: Say, 'It is a great news.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the profound significance of the Qur'anic message, urging believers to recognize its immense importance and divine origin, as it pertains to the core truths of faith, guidance, and the Hereafter.

translation: You are turning away from it (the Qur'an).
interpretation: This verse highlights a deliberate avoidance or rejection of the Qur'an's guidance, implying a conscious turning away from its divine message despite its clarity and truth.

translation: I had no knowledge of the Exalted Assembly when they were disputing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) humility and the fact that his knowledge comes solely from divine revelation, not from any prior or independent source, even among the highest celestial beings.

translation: It is not revealed to me except that I am a clear warner.
interpretation: This verse underscores the limited scope of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) mission, emphasizing that his role is solely to deliver a clear and unambiguous warning to humanity, without introducing any new revelation or doctrine beyond what has been divinely ordained.

translation: When your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I am creating a human being from clay."
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin and purpose of human creation, emphasizing that humanity is a deliberate act of God, fashioned from humble material (clay), yet destined for a lofty role in creation.

translation: Then when I have fashioned him and breathed into him of My spirit, fall down to him in prostration.
interpretation: This verse highlights the unique status of Adam (peace be upon him) as the recipient of divine honor, where Allah commands the angels to prostrate to him, signifying the elevation of human dignity and the distinction granted to him through the infusion of the divine spirit, which elevates him above other creations.

translation: So all the angels prostrated themselves, all together.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and unconditional obedience of the angels to Allah’s command, demonstrating their submission and servitude as a model for humanity to emulate in their own worship and devotion.

translation: Except Iblees (Satan), he refused to be among the prostrators and was among the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive nature of pride and arrogance, as Iblees (Satan) refused to obey Allah's command out of arrogance, leading to his disbelief and eternal damnation.

translation: He said, 'O Iblees, what prevented you from prostrating to that which I created with My hands? Were you arrogant, or were you [already] of the exalted ones?',
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of arrogance and the refusal to submit to divine command, illustrating how pride can lead to disobedience and ultimately to damnation.

translation: He said, "I am better than him. You created me from fire and created him from clay."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and ingratitude of Iblis (Satan) towards Allah's creation, as he boasts about his origin and belittles Adam (peace be upon him) based on their differing compositions, thereby rejecting Allah's command and demonstrating a flawed sense of superiority.

translation: He said, 'Then get out of it; indeed, you are expelled [from mercy].'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and irrevocable decree of Allah regarding the expulsion of Iblis (Satan) from His mercy due to his defiance and arrogance, highlighting the consequences of rebellion against divine authority.

translation: And indeed, upon you is My curse until the Day of Judgment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe and eternal consequences of defiance against divine commandments, highlighting that such rebellion incurs a permanent state of divine displeasure and estrangement.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, then reprieve me until the Day they are resurrected.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the plea of Iblis (Satan) to Allah after being cursed for his refusal to prostrate to Adam, seeking respite until the Day of Resurrection to mislead humanity and lead them astray, demonstrating his arrogance and defiance against Allah's command.

translation: Then, indeed, you are among those granted respite.
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine response to a request for respite or delay in punishment, indicating that the addressee is granted a temporary reprieve rather than immediate punishment, which underscores Allah's mercy and justice in deferring consequences for a specified time.

translation: Until the Day of the Known Time.
interpretation: This phrase refers to the Day of Judgment, a fixed and predetermined time known only to Allah, marking the end of this world and the beginning of the Hereafter, where all souls will be held accountable for their deeds.

translation: He said, 'By Your might, I will surely mislead them all'
interpretation: This verse reflects the declaration of Iblis (Satan) to Allah, expressing his resolve to mislead all of humanity out of arrogance and defiance, despite knowing that Allah's power is absolute and His will prevails.

translation: Except Your devoted servants among them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the exception of those who are truly sincere and devoted to God, emphasizing that divine mercy and protection are granted to those who remain steadfast in their faith and purify their intentions.

translation: So I follow the truth, and I say the truth.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to truth and speaking it openly, even when it may be unpopular or challenging, reflecting a commitment to honesty and integrity in both belief and communication.

translation: I will surely fill Hell with you and whoever follows you among them, all together.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute certainty of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief and actively lead others astray, emphasizing the gravity of their actions and the inevitability of their fate in the Hereafter.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'I do not ask you for any reward for it, nor am I of those who are pretentious.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the sincerity and purity of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) mission, emphasizing that he does not seek personal gain or recognition for conveying the divine message, nor does he engage in false pretenses or deceptive behavior.

translation: It is but a reminder to the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the universal nature of the Qur'an, highlighting that its message is intended not just for a specific group or time, but for all of humanity across all ages.

translation: And you will surely come to know its tidings after a time.
