interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of eventual knowledge and understanding of the truth or outcome of a matter, even if it is delayed. It serves as a reminder of divine justice and the inevitability of revelation, encouraging patience and trust in Allah's wisdom.

translation: This is the revelation of the Book [the Quran] from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse establishes the divine origin of the Quran, attributing its revelation to Allah, who is described with two of His most majestic attributes: 'Al-Aziz' (the Exalted in Might), emphasizing His absolute power and authority, and 'Al-Hakim' (the Wise), underscoring the perfect wisdom and purpose behind the revelation.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, so worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the authenticity and divine origin of the Qur'an, urging the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and all believers to worship Allah exclusively, with pure and undivided devotion, free from any form of idolatry or hypocrisy.

translation: Unquestionably, for Allah is the pure religion. And those who take protectors besides Him [say], "We only worship them that they may bring us nearer to Allah in position." Indeed, Allah will judge between them concerning that over which they differ. Indeed, Allah does not guide he who is a liar and [confirmed] disbeliever.
interpretation: This verse underscores the exclusivity of devotion to Allah alone, rejecting any form of associating partners with Him, even if the intention is to seek closeness to Allah through intermediaries. It highlights the futility of such practices, as true guidance comes only from Allah, who will ultimately judge between truth and falsehood, exposing the hypocrisy of those who claim to worship others while disbelieving in Allah's absolute oneness.

translation: If Allah had intended to take a son, He could have chosen whatever He willed from His creation. Exalted is He! He is Allah, the One, the Prevailing.
interpretation: This verse refutes the polytheistic belief in Allah having offspring or partners, emphasizing His absolute oneness (Tawheed) and sovereignty over all creation. It underscores that Allah is beyond human limitations and that any notion of Him having a son is a fabrication incompatible with His transcendent nature.

translation: He created the heavens and the earth in truth. He wraps the night over the day and wraps the day over the night. And He has subjected the sun and the moon, each running [its course] for a specified term. Unquestionably, He is the Exalted in Might, the Perpetual Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over the universe, demonstrating His ability to create, regulate, and sustain all existence with precision and purpose. The imagery of wrapping night over day and vice versa symbolizes the seamless and unchanging order of cosmic cycles, reinforcing the idea of divine control and inevitability. The mention of the sun and moon's fixed courses highlights the meticulous design in creation, while the titles 'the Exalted in Might' and 'the Perpetual Forgiver' underscore both His majesty and mercy, reminding humanity of His ultimate authority and capacity for forgiveness.

translation: He created you from one soul and then made from it its mate. And He produced for you from the grazing livestock eight mates. He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs dominion. There is no deity except Him; so how are you averted?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the unity of human origin and the divine plan behind creation, highlighting Allah's exclusive sovereignty and the futility of turning away from His guidance despite clear signs of His existence and power.

translation: If you disbelieve, indeed Allah is free from need of you. And He does not approve for His servants disbelief. But if you are grateful, He approves it for you. And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. Then to your Lord is your return, and He will inform you about what you used to do. Indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute independence of Allah from human belief or disbelief, while emphasizing His justice and mercy. It highlights that disbelief is not pleasing to Allah, as it harms only the disbeliever, not Him, and gratitude is a virtue that earns His approval. The verse also reinforces individual accountability, rejecting any notion of intercession or shared burden in the Hereafter, and assures that all actions will be fully disclosed and judged by Allah, who is fully aware of the innermost intentions and secrets of the heart.

translation: And when harm touches man, he calls upon his Lord, turning to Him [in repentance]. Then when He bestows a favor upon him from Himself, he forgets what he was calling upon before and sets up rivals to Allah that he may lead [others] astray from His path. Say, 'Enjoy your disbelief for a little; indeed, you will be among the companions of the Fire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness of human nature in times of distress versus prosperity, illustrating how people often turn to Allah in desperation but forget Him when blessings are bestowed, substituting false deities or distractions for true devotion, thus straying from the path of guidance.

translation: Is one who is devoutly obedient during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing [in prayer], fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord [like one who does not]? Say, 'Are those who know equal to those who do not know?' Only those of understanding are mindful.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who actively engage in sincere worship, reflection, and moral accountability—embodied in the 'qānit' (devoutly obedient)—and those who remain spiritually indifferent. It underscores that true understanding and wisdom are not merely intellectual but manifest in a life of devotion, humility, and pursuit of divine mercy. The rhetorical question challenges the reader to recognize that spiritual awareness and moral integrity elevate a person beyond mere knowledge, making them worthy of divine proximity.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], to those who have believed that they should forgive those who expect not the days of Allah so that He may compensate a people for what they used to earn. It is for Allah alone to recompense (them), and He is the most Swift in account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of patience and forgiveness in the face of adversity, reminding believers that Allah's reward is vast and not limited by human calculations, and that ultimate justice belongs to Allah alone.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'Indeed, I have been commanded to worship Allah, being sincere to Him in religion.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawhid) and the rejection of any form of idolatry or associating partners with Him, even in the sincerest acts of worship. It underscores that true worship must be solely for Allah, devoid of any ulterior motives or hidden intentions that could compromise its purity.

translation: And I have been commanded to be the first of the Muslims.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of prioritizing submission to Allah's will above all else, even if it means being the first to embrace Islam in a given context or time. It reflects a deep sense of humility and devotion, recognizing that true leadership in faith comes from sincere obedience to divine commandments.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I fear, if I disobey my Lord, the punishment of a tremendous Day.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the gravity of disobeying Allah and the severe consequences that follow in the Hereafter, emphasizing the importance of obedience and mindfulness of divine accountability.

translation: Say, 'I worship Allah, being sincere to Him in my religion.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of pure monotheism (Tawhid) and sincerity in worship, directing the believer to affirm their exclusive devotion to Allah alone, free from any form of idolatry or association of partners with Him.

translation: So worship what you will besides Him.' Say, 'Indeed, the losers are those who will lose themselves and their families on the Day of Resurrection.' Unquestionably, that is the manifest loss.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of worshipping anything other than Allah, warning that such misplaced devotion will lead to ultimate loss—not just for the individual but for their entire family on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the severity of associating partners with Allah (shirk) as the gravest form of self-destruction.

translation: For them (the disbelievers) are layers of fire above them and layers of fire below them. That is how Allah instills fear in His servants. So, O My servants, fear Me!
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of divine punishment for those who reject faith, depicting it as an inescapable, multi-layered torment from all directions. The imagery serves as a stark warning to believers to remain conscious of Allah's power and to adhere to righteousness out of reverence and fear of His justice, rather than succumbing to arrogance or disbelief.

translation: But those who avoid Taghut (false deities) by not worshipping them and turn to Allah in repentance for them is good tidings. So give good tidings to My servants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who reject false deities (Taghut) and those who turn sincerely to Allah, emphasizing that true guidance and salvation come from turning away from falsehood and seeking Allah alone.

translation: Those who listen to the word [of Allah] and follow the best of it. Those are the ones whom Allah has guided, and those are the ones possessing intelligence.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of not only hearing divine guidance but actively discerning and adhering to its most excellent and purest interpretation. It underscores that true guidance from Allah is reserved for those who possess deep understanding ('ulu al-albab')—individuals who reflect, reason, and prioritize truth over superficial or distorted interpretations, thereby earning divine direction.

translation: Is he whom the sentence of punishment has become due deserving that you (O Muhammad) should save him from the Fire?
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute justice and inevitability of divine decree, emphasizing that no intercession or effort can alter what Allah has decreed for those deserving of punishment, underscoring the importance of righteous conduct in this life to avoid such a fate.

translation: But those who fear their Lord will have lofty chambers built above one another, beneath which rivers flow. (This is) the promise of Allah. Allah does not fail in His promise.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine reward for the righteous—those who embody taqwa (God-consciousness)—as a promise of eternal, elevated dwellings in Paradise, symbolizing both honor and proximity to Allah, with the imagery of flowing rivers beneath underscoring the perpetual blessings and tranquility awaiting them, a testament to Allah’s unwavering fidelity to His covenants.

translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky, and We produce thereby fruits of varying colors; and in the mountains are tracts, white and red of varying shades and [some] extremely black.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate signs of Allah’s power and wisdom in the natural world, urging reflection on how diverse phenomena—from rainfall to the colors of the earth—serve as reminders for those with understanding and intellect.

translation: So is he whose breast Allah has expanded to [accept] Islam and he is upon a light from his Lord [like one whose heart rejects it]? Then woe to those whose hearts are hardened against the remembrance of Allah. Those are in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the contrast between those whose hearts are open to the guidance of Islam and those whose hearts remain hardened against the remembrance of Allah. It warns that a hardened heart leads to manifest error, emphasizing the importance of spiritual receptivity and the danger of rejecting divine guidance.

translation: Allah has sent down the best statement: a Book (the Quran), its parts resembling each other in goodness and truth, oft-repeated. The skins of those who fear their Lord shiver from it. Then their skins and their hearts soften to the remembrance of Allah. That is the guidance of Allah by which He guides whomever He wills. And whomever Allah sends astray, for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transformative power of the Quran, illustrating how its recitation evokes both awe and reverence in those who truly fear Allah, while simultaneously softening their hearts towards devotion and remembrance of Him. It underscores that guidance is solely in Allah’s hands, emphasizing His sovereignty over the hearts of humanity.

translation: Is he who will confront the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection [like one safe from it]? And it will be said to the wrongdoers, 'Taste what you used to earn.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of accountability for one's actions in the Hereafter, contrasting the fate of the righteous with that of the wrongdoers. It highlights divine justice, where no injustice will go unpunished, and the consequences of one's deeds—whether good or evil—will be fully realized.

translation: Those before them denied, and there came to them the punishment from where they did not perceive.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against arrogance and denial of truth, emphasizing that divine retribution often strikes unexpectedly, catching wrongdoers off guard when they least expect it.

translation: So Allah made them taste disgrace in the life of this world. And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse underscores the temporal nature of worldly punishment for those who reject divine guidance, contrasting it with the far more severe and enduring punishment in the Hereafter, which serves as a reminder of the gravity of their choices and the importance of heeding divine signs.

translation: And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example that they might take heed.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Qur'an's use of diverse parables and examples to convey profound truths, aiming to penetrate the hearts and minds of listeners and encourage reflection and remembrance of Allah's signs and lessons.

translation: An Arabic Qur'an, free from any crookedness, so that they may become righteous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and straightforwardness of the Qur'an's message, designed to guide people toward righteousness and piety by presenting divine guidance in a pure and unambiguous form.

translation: Allah presents an example: a man owned by multiple quarreling partners and a man belonging entirely to one man. Are the two equal in comparison? Praise be to Allah! But most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of associating partners with Allah (shirk) by contrasting a slave owned by multiple conflicting masters—who cannot provide true guidance or unity—with a slave owned by a single, benevolent master who can offer stability and direction. It underscores the uniqueness of Allah’s oneness (tawhid) and the absurdity of equating Him with false deities or idols that cannot provide true benefit or coherence.

translation: Indeed, you [O Muhammad] will die, and indeed, they will die.
interpretation: This verse underscores the universal nature of death, emphasizing that no individual—whether a prophet, leader, or ordinary person—is exempt from it, thereby highlighting the transient nature of worldly life and the inevitability of divine judgment.

translation: Then indeed, you will, on the Day of Resurrection, dispute before your Lord.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of accountability and the final reckoning before Allah on the Day of Judgment, where all disputes and hidden truths will be exposed, emphasizing the absolute justice and divine wisdom in Allah's judgment.

translation: So who is more unjust than he who lies about Allah and denies the truth when it comes to him? Is there not in Hell a [permanent] residence for the disbelievers?
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of attributing falsehood to Allah or rejecting the truth when it is presented clearly, emphasizing that such disbelief leads to an inevitable and eternal punishment in Hell, highlighting the moral and spiritual consequences of such actions.

translation: And [there are] those who have brought the truth and those who believe in it—it is those who are the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual role of truth: both bringing it and affirming it. The righteous are those who not only uphold the truth themselves but also recognize and validate it when it is presented to them, demonstrating integrity in both action and belief.

translation: They will have whatever they desire from their Lord. That is the reward of the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse underscores the concept of divine justice and recompense, emphasizing that those who strive to do good in this life will be granted their heart's desires in the Hereafter as a reward from Allah, reflecting His boundless generosity and the fulfillment of His promises to the righteous.

translation: Allah will efface their worst deeds and recompense them with the best of what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's boundless mercy and justice, indicating that He not only pardons the sins of the righteous but also elevates their good deeds to the highest degree, rewarding them beyond their expectations as a manifestation of His grace and favor.

translation: Is not Allah sufficient for His Servant? Yet they try to frighten you with those [they worship] besides Him. And whoever Allah sends astray, for him there is no guide.
interpretation: This verse reassures the believers that Allah’s protection and guidance are sufficient for them, despite the efforts of those who seek to intimidate them with false deities or distractions. It emphasizes that true guidance comes solely from Allah, and those He allows to stray will find no path back to Him.

translation: And whoever Allah guides - for him there will be no misguider. Is not Allah Exalted in Might and Owner of Retribution?
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah in guidance and misguidance, emphasizing that true guidance comes solely from Him, and once granted, it cannot be revoked by any force. The rhetorical question at the end highlights Allah's supreme power and justice, affirming that He is both Mighty and capable of exacting retribution against those who persist in disbelief or defiance.

translation: And if you ask them, 'Who created the heavens and the earth?' they will surely say, 'Allah.' Say, 'Then have you considered what you invoke besides Allah? If Allah intended harm for me, could they remove His harm? Or if He intended mercy for me, could they withhold His mercy?' Say, 'Sufficient for me is Allah; upon Him rely those who trust.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and exclusive power of Allah in determining outcomes—whether harm or mercy—while highlighting the impotence of false deities or objects of worship besides Him. It serves as a rebuke to those who associate partners with Allah, demonstrating that such entities cannot alter divine decree or provide any real benefit or protection, thereby emphasizing the necessity of placing complete trust in Allah alone.

translation: Say, 'O my people, work according to your position; indeed, I am working. Then you will come to know.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of individual accountability and the inevitability of divine justice. It encourages steadfastness in one's path, whether righteous or otherwise, while affirming that ultimate outcomes will reveal the truth, and divine justice will prevail.

translation: Whoever comes to it (the Fire) will be disgraced, and upon him will descend a lasting punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the irreversible and humiliating nature of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief or wrongdoing, emphasizing both the disgrace they face and the eternal permanence of their suffering.

translation: Indeed, We have sent down to you, [O Muhammad], the Book in truth, so you may judge between the people by that which Allah has shown you. And do not be for the deceitful an advocate.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and purpose of the Qur'an as a source of guidance and justice, while clarifying that the Prophet's role is not to force guidance upon individuals, as each person is responsible for their own choices and will face the consequences accordingly.

translation: It is Allah who takes the souls at the time of their death, and [the souls] of those that do not die [during their] sleep. Then He keeps those for whom He has decreed death and sends the others for a specified term. Indeed, in that are signs for a people who reflect.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute control over life and death, emphasizing that every soul's lifespan is predetermined and that even sleep is a temporary, reversible form of 'death' from which one returns to continue their appointed time.

translation: Or have they taken besides Allah intercessors? Say, 'Even if they possess nothing and do not reason?'
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion of seeking intercession from false deities or intermediaries, emphasizing that such entities lack any real power or understanding, thereby rendering their intercession meaningless.

translation: Say, 'All intercession belongs to Allah. To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. Then to Him you will be returned.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation and the finality of His authority. It rejects any notion of intercession outside His will, emphasizing that all power and authority rest solely with Him, and that ultimate return and accountability are to Him alone.

translation: And when Allah alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who disbelieve in the Hereafter shrink with aversion. But when those [worshipped] other than Him are mentioned, immediately they rejoice.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast in the emotional and spiritual responses of those who reject the Hereafter versus those who do not believe in the oneness of Allah. The aversion to the remembrance of Allah alone reflects a deeper rejection of divine truth and accountability in the Hereafter, while the joy in mentioning other deities reveals their attachment to false gods and worldly distractions, which they prefer over the truth.

translation: Say, 'O Allah, Originator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, You will judge between Your servants concerning that over which they used to differ.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah in all matters, including the resolution of disputes among people, and affirms His comprehensive knowledge of both the seen and unseen realms, which serves as the basis for His just judgment.

translation: And if those who did wrong had all that is on the earth, all of it, and the like of it besides, they would seek to ransom themselves with it from the evil of the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. And there will appear to them from Allah what they had never imagined.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of human efforts to escape divine punishment through worldly means, emphasizing that no amount of wealth or possessions can avert the consequences of injustice and wrongdoing in the Hereafter.

translation: And there will appear to them, from their evil deeds, what they had done, and they will be surrounded by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of facing the consequences of one's actions, particularly those that were dismissed or mocked in disbelief. It serves as a warning that the mockery of divine truths or the rejection of moral accountability will not spare one from the reality of their deeds in the Hereafter, where the consequences of their actions will manifest in full force.

translation: And when harm touches man, he calls upon Us; then when We grant him a favor from Us, he says, "I was given it only due to [my own] knowledge." Rather, it is a trial, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fickleness of human nature in times of adversity and prosperity. When faced with hardship, people turn to Allah in desperation, but upon receiving blessings, they often attribute their success to their own efforts or intellect, failing to acknowledge Allah's role. The verse underscores that worldly blessings are tests from Allah, designed to reveal true human character—whether they remain grateful or become arrogant and ungrateful.

translation: Those before them had already said it, but what they had earned did not avail them at all.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of worldly gains and achievements when they are not accompanied by true faith and righteous deeds, as past nations who rejected divine guidance faced destruction despite their wealth and power.

translation: So they were afflicted by the evil consequences of what they had earned. And [as for] those who wronged among them, there will afflict them the evil consequences of what they had earned, and they will not be able to escape [it].
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, where individuals face the consequences of their actions—both good and bad—without exception. It serves as a warning to those who commit wrongdoing, emphasizing that their misdeeds will inevitably catch up with them, and there is no escape from accountability before God.

translation: Do they not know that Allah extends provision for whom He wills and restricts it? Indeed, in that are signs for a people who believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine wisdom behind the distribution of sustenance, reminding believers that Allah's control over provision is absolute and purposeful, serving as a test of faith and a sign of His sovereignty over all things.

translation: Say, 'O My servants who have transgressed against themselves [by sinning], do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.'
interpretation: This verse offers profound hope and reassurance to those who have strayed from the path of righteousness, emphasizing that Allah's mercy encompasses all sins, no matter how grave, as long as one turns to Him in repentance with sincerity.

translation: And turn to your Lord in repentance and submit to Him before the punishment comes upon you; then you will not be helped.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency of seeking repentance and submitting to Allah before the opportunity for forgiveness and mercy is lost, as divine punishment may arrive without the possibility of escape or assistance.

translation: And follow the best of what has been revealed to you from your Lord before the punishment comes upon you suddenly while you are unaware.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency of adhering to the divine guidance revealed in the Qur'an, as the consequences of neglecting it may manifest unexpectedly, leaving no time for repentance or preparation.

translation: That the soul will say, 'Woe to me! I neglected what is due to Allah, and I was among the mockers.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound regret and self-reproach that will consume a person on the Day of Judgment when they realize the gravity of their past negligence toward their duties to Allah and their mockery of faith, underscoring the irreversible consequences of such actions in the Hereafter.

translation: Or do you say, 'If Allah had guided me, I would have been among the righteous'?
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to attribute guidance solely to divine will while neglecting personal responsibility in seeking righteousness, implying that true guidance requires both divine favor and human effort in striving for righteousness.

translation: Or [do you say] when you see the punishment, 'If only I had another chance, then I would be among the doers of good.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility of regret when faced with divine justice, emphasizing that the time for repentance and good deeds has already passed, and urging proactive righteousness in the present moment.

translation: Yes, My signs came to you, but you denied them and were arrogant, and you were among the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of rejecting divine guidance despite its clarity, highlighting the danger of arrogance in the face of truth, which leads to disbelief and spiritual ruin.

translation: And on the Day of Resurrection you will see those who lied about Allah with their faces blackened. Is there not in Hell a [sufficient] place of refuge for the arrogant?
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences for those who falsely attribute lies to Allah, emphasizing that their deception will be visibly exposed on the Day of Judgment through the blackening of their faces—a symbol of disgrace and punishment. The rhetorical question at the end highlights the inevitability of Hell as the ultimate abode for the arrogant, who reject truth and belittle divine commandments, reinforcing the moral lesson that arrogance and deceit lead to eternal ruin.

translation: Allah will deliver those who fear Him to their place of salvation: no evil shall touch them, nor shall they grieve.
interpretation: This verse assures believers that those who cultivate God-consciousness (taqwa) will be protected from harm and spared from grief in both this life and the Hereafter, highlighting the ultimate security and peace that come from righteousness.

translation: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is, over all things, a Disposer of affairs.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and control over all creation, affirming that He not only brings everything into existence but also sustains, governs, and manages all affairs with perfect wisdom and authority.

translation: To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth. And those who disbelieve in the signs of Allah - it is those who are the losers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that true guidance and ultimate success come only through belief in His signs, while rejection thereof leads to spiritual and existential loss.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'Is it other than Allah I should desire for you to worship, O ignorant ones?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the exclusivity of worship to Allah alone, rejecting any association of partners with Him, and highlights the folly of those who advocate or engage in such practices.

translation: And certainly, it has been revealed to you and to those before you: 'If you associate [anything] with Allah, your deeds will surely become worthless, and you will surely be among the losers.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and warns against associating partners with Him (shirk), which is the gravest sin in Islam. It serves as a reminder that any good deeds performed without true faith and devotion to Allah alone will be rendered null and void, emphasizing the importance of sincere and exclusive worship of Allah.

translation: But worship Allah and be among the grateful.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of exclusive devotion to Allah and the cultivation of gratitude as a fundamental aspect of faith, indicating that true worship is inseparable from a heart that acknowledges and appreciates Allah's blessings.

translation: And they have not honored Allah with true honor, while the entire earth will be within His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be folded in His right hand. Exalted is He and high above what they associate with Him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah, contrasting the limited perception of those who associate partners with Him. It underscores that Allah's true greatness is beyond human comprehension or adequate appreciation, as He holds the entire universe in His grasp with ease, while the false deities people worship are powerless and non-existent.

translation: And the Horn will be blown, so whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills. Then it will be blown again, and at once they will be standing, looking on.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over life and death, emphasizing that resurrection and judgment are solely in His hands. The exception of 'whom Allah wills' highlights His mercy and wisdom, as only He knows the true state of hearts and deeds. The second blowing of the Horn signifies the resurrection of all beings, where they will witness the consequences of their worldly actions, reflecting divine justice and the inevitability of the Hereafter.

translation: And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the Book will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, emphasizing divine justice and the accountability of all beings. The 'light of its Lord' symbolizes the revelation and truth that will illuminate the earth, while the 'Book' represents the record of deeds. The 'prophets and witnesses' highlight the truthfulness of divine justice, ensuring that no one is wronged in the final judgment.

translation: And every soul will be fully compensated [for] what it did, and He is most knowing of what they do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of Allah in recompensing every individual for their deeds, emphasizing that nothing escapes His knowledge or goes unaccounted for.

translation: And those who disbelieved will be driven to Hell in groups until, when they reach it, its gates will be opened, and its keepers will say to them, "Did there not come to you messengers from among yourselves, reciting to you the verses of your Lord and warning you of the meeting of this Day of yours?" They will say, "Yes, but the word [i.e., decree] of punishment has come into effect against the disbelievers."
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice for those who persistently reject the truth despite clear warnings from Allah's messengers. The mention of the 'word of punishment' signifies that Allah's decree against the disbelievers is final and unchangeable, emphasizing that their fate is a consequence of their own choices rather than an arbitrary punishment.

translation: It will be said, "Enter the gates of Hell, abiding therein forever." So what an evil destination for the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe and eternal punishment awaiting those who exhibit arrogance and pride, particularly in their rejection of divine truth. The mention of 'gates of Hell' symbolizes the finality and inescapability of the punishment, while 'abiding therein forever' emphasizes its unending nature. The term 'arrogant' here refers not just to haughtiness in social conduct but, more importantly, to the spiritual arrogance of refusing to submit to God's guidance, which is the root of all disobedience and disbelief.

translation: And those who feared their Lord will be led to Paradise in groups until, when they reach it while its gates have been opened, its keepers will say to them, "Peace be upon you. You have done well, so enter [this Paradise], abiding eternally therein."
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine reward for the righteous, emphasizing that their entry into Paradise is not merely a reward but a culmination of their righteous deeds and God-consciousness, marked by a profound sense of peace and eternal bliss.

translation: And they will say, "Praise to Allah, who has fulfilled His promise to us and made us inherit the land [of Paradise], enjoying it wherever we will. And excellent is the reward of [righteous] workers."
interpretation: This verse reflects the ultimate fulfillment of divine promises and the reward of steadfast faith and righteous deeds, highlighting the justice and generosity of Allah in granting believers eternal bliss and sovereignty in Paradise as a recompense for their devotion and good actions.

translation: And you will see the angels surrounding the Throne, glorifying their Lord with praise. And it will be judged between them in truth, and it will be said, 'Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the absolute sovereignty and justice of Allah, where even the angels, who are in constant worship and obedience, acknowledge His supreme authority. The mention of judgment 'in truth' underscores the inevitability of divine justice, while the declaration of praise for Allah as 'Lord of the worlds' emphasizes His encompassing lordship over all creation, affirming that ultimate authority and praise belong solely to Him.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Ha, Meem.
interpretation: The opening of this surah with the invocation of Allah's names emphasizes seeking divine mercy and guidance before engaging with the revelation, while the disconnected letters (like Ha, Meem) are a linguistic feature in the Qur'an whose meaning is known only to Allah, often serving to draw attention to the miraculous nature of the Qur'anic discourse.

translation: This is the revelation of the Book [the Qur'an] from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Knowing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the Qur'an, attributing its revelation to Allah, who is characterized by absolute power (Al-'Aziz) and comprehensive knowledge (Al-'Alim). It serves as a foundational assertion of the Qur'an's authenticity and authority, emphasizing that its source is not human but God Himself, thereby affirming its infallibility and guidance for humanity.

translation: The Forgiver of sin, the Acceptor of repentance, the Severe in punishment, the Bestower of bounty. There is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him; to Him is the destination.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's dual nature of mercy and justice, emphasizing His absolute sovereignty and the ultimate return of all creation to Him, underscoring the balance between forgiveness for the repentant and accountability for the sinful.

translation: None argue concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve, so let not their movement throughout the land deceive you.
interpretation: This verse cautions against being misled by the apparent success or prosperity of those who reject faith, as their worldly achievements do not validate their disbelief or diminish the truth of Allah's signs.

translation: Before them, the people of Noah denied, and the factions after them [did likewise]. Every [disbelieving] nation plotted against their messenger to seize him, and they argued falsely to thereby disprove the truth. But I seized them, so how [terrible] was My punishment!
interpretation: This verse underscores the recurring pattern of human defiance against divine messengers and the ultimate consequences of rejecting truth, emphasizing that no nation is spared divine retribution when they persistently deny the truth and plot against the prophets.

translation: And thus the word of your Lord has been justified against those who disbelieved that they are the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice, emphasizing that the punishment of the disbelievers in the Hereafter is a predetermined and just outcome based on their conscious rejection of faith and divine guidance.

translation: Those who carry the Throne and those around it glorify the praises of their Lord, believe in Him, and seek forgiveness for the believers, saying: 'Our Lord, You encompass all things in mercy and knowledge. So forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of Hellfire.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound humility and intercessory role of the angels who bear the Throne of Allah. It underscores the boundless mercy and knowledge of Allah, which encompasses all things, and the importance of repentance and adherence to the divine path as means of seeking forgiveness and protection from punishment.

translation: Our Lord, and admit them into the Gardens of Eden which You have promised them, and those who were righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse reflects a supplication for the admission of believers into Paradise, emphasizing the inclusivity of divine mercy across generations, provided they remain righteous. It underscores the importance of familial righteousness and the continuity of faith within the family unit, while also highlighting Allah's attributes of might and wisdom in fulfilling His promises.

translation: And protect them from the evil deeds. And whoever is protected from the evil deeds on that Day will have been shown mercy. And that is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate success of those who are shielded from their own sins on the Day of Judgment, highlighting divine mercy as the pinnacle of achievement, where salvation is not earned through human effort alone but granted by Allah’s grace.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieve will be addressed by the greatest hatred from Allah—greater than the hatred they have for themselves—when they are invited to faith but refuse to believe.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity of rejecting faith, emphasizing that the disbelievers' own self-condemnation in the Hereafter will pale in comparison to the divine wrath they incur by turning away from truth, underscoring the gravity of their choice and the ultimate accountability before Allah.

translation: They said, 'Our Lord, You have caused us to die twice, and You have given us life twice. So we have confessed our sins. Is there then a way out [of the Fire]?'
interpretation: This verse reflects the despair of the disbelievers in the Hereafter, acknowledging their repeated cycles of life and death as divine signs, yet realizing too late that their sins have sealed their fate, leaving them with no hope of escape from punishment.

translation: That is because, when Allah alone is invoked, you disbelieve; but if partners are associated with Him, you believe. So the judgment is with Allah, the Most High, the Grand.
interpretation: This verse critiques the inconsistency in human nature, highlighting how people often reject the truth of monotheism when it is presented purely, but accept it when mixed with falsehood or when it aligns with their desires. It underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah, whose judgment prevails over all, and warns against the moral and spiritual confusion that arises from such hypocrisy.

translation: It is He who shows you His signs and sends down to you from the heaven provision. And none will remember except he who turns back [in repentance].
interpretation: This verse underscores the dual nature of divine signs—both as evidence of God’s existence and as means of sustenance—while emphasizing that true reflection and remembrance of these signs are reserved for those who turn to God in repentance and submission.

translation: So invoke Allah, being sincere to Him in religion, although the disbelievers dislike it.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sincere worship and devotion to Allah alone, regardless of the opposition or disapproval of those who reject faith. It underscores that true faith is not contingent upon the acceptance or approval of others, but rather on the purity of intention and sincerity in one's devotion to Allah.

translation: He is the Exalted in Degree, the Owner of the Throne. He sends the Spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants to warn [mankind] of the Day of Meeting.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's supreme authority and majesty, emphasizing His ability to convey revelation and guidance through divine means, such as the Spirit (Ruh), to chosen messengers. It underscores the purpose of divine communication: to warn humanity about the inevitability of the Day of Judgment (Yawm al-Talaq), where all will meet their Lord for reckoning.

translation: On that Day, all will be exposed; nothing about them is hidden from Allah. To whom belongs the dominion today? To Allah, the One, the Subduer.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and supreme authority of Allah on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that all creation is subject to His will and that no secret or hidden thing escapes His knowledge.

translation: This Day every soul shall be requited for what it earned; no injustice shall there be this Day: for Allah is Swift in reckoning.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of Allah on the Day of Judgment, where every individual will be held accountable for their deeds without any injustice or favoritism, reflecting the divine principle of fairness and the swiftness of Allah's reckoning.

translation: And warn them of the Day that is approaching, when hearts will be at the throats, choking [them]. The wrongdoers will have no close friend, nor any intercessor to be obeyed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the overwhelming terror and helplessness that will grip the wrongdoers when their hearts rise to their throats in sheer dread. It highlights the absence of any true ally or intercessor for the oppressors, as no one will be able to intervene on their behalf in a way that is pleasing to Allah, reinforcing the absolute justice and finality of divine judgment.

translation: He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the breasts conceal.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's omniscience, emphasizing that nothing escapes His knowledge—not even the subtle, hidden glances of the eyes or the deepest secrets concealed within the heart.

translation: And Allah judges with truth, while those they invoke besides Him do not judge with anything. Indeed, Allah is the Hearing, the Seeing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority of Allah in judgment and justice, contrasting His perfect knowledge and discernment with the impotence of false deities, which have no power to judge or intercede meaningfully. It emphasizes that true justice and hearing belong solely to Allah, who is fully aware of all things, including the hidden intentions and actions of humanity.

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in [the impact of their] traces upon the earth, but Allah seized them for their sins. And they had no protector from Allah.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly power and the inevitability of divine accountability, emphasizing that no matter how mighty or influential a civilization or individual may be, their ultimate fate is determined by their adherence to divine commandments and moral integrity.

translation: That is because their messengers used to come to them with clear proofs, but they disbelieved, so Allah seized them. Indeed, He is Powerful and severe in penalty.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine retribution for persistent rejection of truth and guidance, emphasizing that Allah's power and justice are absolute, leaving no room for impunity for those who obstinately deny the signs and messengers sent to them.

translation: And We certainly sent Moses with Our signs and a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine mission of Moses (peace be upon him) as a prophet, equipped with clear signs (miracles) and undeniable proof (authority) to guide his people and establish truth against the falsehood of Pharaoh.

translation: To Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun, they said, 'A magician and a liar!',
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and defiance of the leaders of Pharaoh's court in dismissing divine guidance, attributing the truth to mere trickery and deception, showcasing their refusal to acknowledge the signs of Allah's power and the message of truth brought by His messengers.

translation: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said, "Kill the sons of those who believe with him and spare their women." But the plot of the disbelievers is only in vain.
interpretation: This verse critiques the hypocritical and malicious intentions of those who reject divine truth despite its clear evidence, revealing their desire to eradicate faith by targeting the innocent (sons and women) while their schemes ultimately fail due to their misguided nature.

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'Let me kill Moses, and let him call upon his Lord. Indeed, I fear that he will change your religion or that he will cause corruption to appear in the land.'
interpretation: This verse reveals Pharaoh's arrogance and fear of losing control, as he attributes the potential downfall of his regime to Moses' call to monotheism, framing it as a threat to societal order rather than an invitation to truth.

translation: And Moses said, 'Indeed, I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord from every arrogant one who does not believe in the Day of Reckoning.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of seeking divine protection from those who reject the Day of Judgment and act arrogantly, emphasizing the need for humility and faith in divine justice.

translation: And a believing man from the family of Pharaoh who concealed his faith said, 'Would you kill a man because he says, My Lord is Allah, while he has come to you with clear signs from your Lord? And if he is a liar, his lie is upon him; but if he is truthful, some of what he promises you will strike you.' Indeed, Allah does not guide one who is a transgressor and a liar.
interpretation: This verse highlights the courage and moral integrity of a believer who, despite being part of Pharaoh's household, openly defends Prophet Moses (peace be upon him) and the truth of his message. It underscores the importance of standing for justice and truth, even when it comes at personal risk, and reminds us that divine guidance is reserved for those who are sincere and not prone to excess or deceit.

translation: O my people, sovereignty belongs to you today, dominant in the land. But who will help us from the punishment of Allah if it comes to us?
interpretation: This verse reflects Pharaoh's arrogance and delusion of power, where he boasts about his dominance and dismisses any warning of divine punishment, showing his refusal to acknowledge Allah's authority or the consequences of his oppression.

translation: And the one who believed said, "O my people, indeed I fear for you [a fate] like the day of the companies [of old],"
interpretation: This verse highlights the urgency of heeding divine warnings and the consequences of rejecting truth, as the believer invokes the historical precedent of the 'day of the companies'—a reference to the destruction of past nations who opposed their prophets—to emphasize the peril faced by those who persist in disbelief.

translation: Like the fate of the people of Noah, and 'Aad, and Thamud, and those after them. And Allah does not intend injustice for the servants.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute justice and warns that those who persist in disbelief and defiance, like the nations before them, will face a similar fate of destruction, not because Allah is unjust, but because their own actions have earned them that consequence.

translation: And O my people, indeed I fear for you the Day of the Call.
interpretation: This verse reflects a prophetic warning, emphasizing the urgency of heeding divine guidance before the Day of Judgment, when all will be summoned to account for their deeds, highlighting the consequences of disbelief and disobedience.

translation: On the Day when you will turn back, fleeing, having no protector from Allah. And whoever Allah sends astray, there is no guide for him.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power of Allah in guiding or misguiding individuals, emphasizing that no one can escape His decree or find protection outside of His will.

translation: And Joseph had already come to you before with clear proofs, but you remained in doubt about what he had brought to you, until when he perished, you said, 'Allah will never send a messenger after him.' Thus does Allah leave astray he who is a transgressor and a skeptic.
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent doubt and skepticism of people even when clear signs and proofs are presented to them, as seen in the case of Prophet Joseph (peace be upon him). It underscores the consequence of such doubt—being led astray by Allah—when it stems from arrogance (transgression) and uncertainty (skepticism), rather than sincere seeking of truth.

translation: Those who dispute the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them—great is the hatred for them in the sight of Allah and those who believe. Thus does Allah seal every arrogant, defiant heart.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and arrogance of those who reject divine signs without sound evidence, emphasizing that such behavior stems from a hardened, rebellious heart that Allah ultimately seals from guidance.

translation: And Pharaoh said, 'O Haman, construct for me a tower that I may reach the ways,'
interpretation: This verse reflects Pharaoh's arrogance and delusion in seeking to elevate himself beyond divine limits, demonstrating his refusal to acknowledge any power higher than his own.

translation: The originator of the heavens, so look to the God of Moses, while I surely think him to be a liar.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness of disbelief and the way misguidance can distort perception, as Pharaoh's advisors recognize the truth but are prevented from accepting it due to their attachment to power and arrogance.

translation: And the one who believed said, 'O my people, follow me; I will guide you to the way of right conduct.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral responsibility of those who have recognized the truth to guide others towards righteousness with wisdom and sincerity, emphasizing leadership through example and compassionate exhortation rather than coercion.

translation: O my people, this worldly life is only [temporary] enjoyment, and indeed, the Hereafter is the everlasting abode.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of worldly life compared to the eternal reality of the Hereafter, urging reflection on the fleeting nature of material pursuits and the ultimate importance of preparing for the life to come.

translation: Whoever does an evil deed will not be recompensed except by its like, but whoever does righteousness, whether male or female, while being a believer—those will enter Paradise, being provided for therein without account.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the principle of justice in divine recompense, where deeds are met with their equivalent measure, yet it also highlights the boundless mercy of Allah toward believers who perform righteous deeds, granting them Paradise without restriction or limitation, reflecting the overwhelming generosity of Allah's reward.

translation: And O my people, why should I call you to salvation while you call me to the Fire?
interpretation: This verse reflects the frustration and sorrow of a prophet (likely Prophet Shu'ayb, peace be upon him) when his people reject his guidance and persist in their disbelief, despite his sincere efforts to lead them to righteousness and warn them of the consequences of their actions.

translation: You invite me to disbelieve in Allah and associate with Him what I have no knowledge of, while I invite you to the Mighty, the Forgiver.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between truth and falsehood, emphasizing the futility of following baseless claims and the wisdom in adhering to divine guidance. It underscores the importance of knowledge and certainty in matters of faith, rejecting blind imitation or association of partners with Allah without evidence.

translation: Indeed, that which you invite me to has no [valid] call in this world or in the Hereafter, and indeed, our return is to Allah, and indeed, the transgressors will be the companions of the Fire.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of associating partners with Allah in worship or obedience, as such associations hold no true validity in this life or the next, and the ultimate return of all beings is to Allah, where justice will prevail, and those who transgress the bounds of monotheism will face severe consequences.

translation: But you will remember what I [now] say to you, and I entrust my affair to Allah. Indeed, Allah is Seeing of [His] servants.
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet's unwavering trust in Allah's wisdom and justice, even when facing rejection or opposition from others. It underscores the idea that ultimate success or realization of truth lies in Allah's hands, and that those who oppose divine guidance will eventually come to recognize its truth, though it may be too late for their benefit.

translation: Allah protected him from the evil consequences of their plot, and the people of Pharaoh were overwhelmed by the worst of punishments.
interpretation: This verse highlights divine justice and protection for the righteous, contrasting it with the severe punishment of those who persist in oppression and disbelief, demonstrating that no scheme against truth can ultimately succeed.

translation: They will be exposed to the Fire morning and evening, and on the Day the Hour [of Judgment] is established, [it will be said], "Make the people of Pharaoh enter the most severe punishment."
interpretation: This verse highlights the certainty of divine justice and the inevitability of punishment for those who persist in disbelief and oppression, as exemplified by the people of Pharaoh. The contrast between the temporary exposure to the Fire in this worldly realm and the permanent, intensified punishment in the Hereafter underscores the gravity of their crimes and the unrelenting nature of divine retribution.

translation: And [mention] when they will argue within the Fire, and the weak will say to those who had been arrogant, 'Indeed, we were [once] your followers, so will you avail us anything against the Fire?'
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate regret and helplessness of those who followed false leaders in this world, only to realize too late that their obedience to them in matters of disbelief or oppression brought them no benefit in the Hereafter. It underscores the severe accountability for misplaced allegiance and the futility of seeking intercession from those who themselves are doomed.

translation: Those who were arrogant said, 'Indeed, we are all in it (the Fire). Indeed, Allah has judged between (His) servants.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance of the disbelievers who, despite their defiance, ultimately acknowledge Allah's authority in judgment, revealing their helplessness in the face of divine justice.

translation: And those in the Fire will call to the keepers of Hell, 'Supplicate to your Lord to lighten for us [even] one day of the punishment.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the desperation and regret of the inhabitants of Hell as they plead for relief from their eternal torment, emphasizing the irreversible nature of divine justice and the finality of their punishment.

translation: They said, 'Did not your messengers come to you with clear proofs?' They said, 'Yes.' They said, 'Then call [upon your gods].' And the invocation of the disbelievers is only in [increasing] error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and defiance of the disbelievers despite the clear signs and guidance presented to them by the messengers. It underscores the futility of their reliance on false deities or misguided efforts when confronted with the truth, as their invocation leads only to further deviation and misguidance.

translation: Indeed, We support Our messengers and those who believe, in the life of this world and on the Day when the witnesses will stand forth.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine promise of victory and support for the messengers and believers, both in this world and in the Hereafter, affirming that ultimate triumph belongs to truth and righteousness, regardless of the transient struggles faced in the worldly life.

translation: The Day when the wrongdoers' excuses will not benefit them, and for them is the curse, and for them is the worst destination.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute finality of judgment on the Day of Resurrection, where no excuses or justifications from those who oppressed others or denied the truth will be accepted, regardless of their sincerity or desperation. It highlights the irrevocable consequences of injustice and disbelief, emphasizing that divine justice prevails without exception, and the ultimate abode for the wrongdoers is one of eternal damnation.

translation: And We gave Moses the guidance, and We bequeathed to the Children of Israel the Book.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine favor of guidance and scripture, emphasizing that God's guidance is a gift, and the responsibility to uphold and convey it is a legacy passed down through generations.

translation: A guidance and a reminder for those of understanding.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as both a source of divine guidance and a reminder for those who possess deep intellect and reflection, encouraging them to ponder its meanings and apply its lessons to their lives.

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad]. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. And ask forgiveness for your sin and exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord in the evening and the morning.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of steadfastness in faith and adherence to divine commandments, even in the face of adversity, as Allah's promises are always true. It also highlights the necessity of seeking forgiveness for one's shortcomings and maintaining constant remembrance and gratitude to Allah through regular acts of worship, such as prayer and dhikr (remembrance), both in the evening and morning.

translation: Indeed, those who dispute about the signs of Allah without any authority having come to them—there is nothing in their breasts except (the pursuit of) greatness, which they shall never attain. So seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, it is He who is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing.
interpretation: This verse addresses the arrogance and futility of those who reject divine truth without valid evidence, driven solely by their own inflated sense of superiority. Their inability to attain true greatness underscores the emptiness of their opposition to Allah’s signs, emphasizing the need for humility and reliance on Allah, the One who fully comprehends and observes all things.

translation: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know.
interpretation: This verse highlights the vast difference between the grandeur of Allah's creation of the universe and the relatively smaller scale of human creation, emphasizing the limited understanding of most people regarding Allah's power and wisdom.

translation: And not equal are the blind and the seeing, nor are those who believe and do righteous deeds [equal] to the evildoer. Little do you pay heed.
interpretation: This verse underscores the fundamental distinction in moral and spiritual consequences between those who embrace faith and righteousness and those who persist in disbelief and wrongdoing, emphasizing that divine justice is not blind to these differences.

translation: Indeed, the Hour is coming - no doubt about it - but most people do not believe.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of the Day of Judgment while highlighting humanity's general skepticism or neglect of this fundamental truth, despite its certainty.

translation: And your Lord said, 'Call upon Me; I will respond to you.' Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humiliated.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of humility and sincere devotion in one's relationship with Allah. It conveys that Allah invites all to seek Him through prayer and supplication, promising acceptance and response, while warning that arrogance and refusal to submit to His worship will lead to severe punishment and degradation in the Hereafter.

translation: It is Allah who made the night for you that you may rest in it and the day as a means of sight. Indeed, Allah is full of bounty to the people, but most of the people are not grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and wisdom in creating the natural cycles of night and day for human benefit. The night is a time for rest and rejuvenation, while the day provides light and visibility to carry out daily activities. Despite these clear signs of Allah's favor, the verse underscores the ingratitude of many people, who fail to recognize and acknowledge these blessings.

translation: That is Allah, your Lord, the Creator of all things; there is no deity [worthy of worship] except Him, so how are you deluded?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah as the sole Creator and Sustainer of all existence, rejecting any form of idolatry or misdirection in worship, and calls into question the human tendency to stray from this fundamental truth despite clear evidence.

translation: Thus are those deluded who used to deny the signs of Allah.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of persistently rejecting the truth and signs of Allah, leading to a state of delusion and misguidance.

translation: It is Allah who made for you the earth a place of settlement and the sky a canopy; and He formed you and perfected your forms and provided you with good things. That is Allah, your Lord; then blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute power and wisdom in creating the universe and everything within it for the benefit of humanity, emphasizing His role as the sustainer and provider, while also reminding humans of their purpose and the perfection of their creation as a sign of Allah's artistry and mercy.

translation: He is the Ever-Living; there is no god ˹worthy of worship˺ except Him. So call upon Him, being sincere in your devotion to Him. All praise is for Allah, Lord of all the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and uniqueness of Allah (Tawheed), affirming His eternal existence and the exclusivity of His right to worship. It commands believers to direct their supplications solely to Him, with pure and undivided devotion, while acknowledging that all praise and gratitude belong to Him as the sustainer of all creation.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], "Indeed, I have been forbidden to worship those you invoke besides Allah once clear proofs came to me from my Lord, and I was commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds."
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and the rejection of associating partners with Him. It highlights the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) unwavering commitment to monotheism, despite societal pressures, and his submission to Allah alone as the Lord of all creation.

translation: It is He who created you from dust; then from a sperm-drop; then from a clinging substance; then He brings you out as a child; then [He develops you] that you reach your [time of] maturity; then [further] that you become elders. And among you is he who is taken in [early] death; and [it is] so that you complete a specified term; and so that you may use reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stages of human creation and development, emphasizing Allah's power and wisdom in designing life with a purpose. It underscores the transient nature of human existence, from birth to old age, and the inevitability of death at a predetermined time, urging reflection on the transient nature of life and the importance of using reason to understand one's purpose and the signs of Allah.

translation: It is He who gives life and causes death. And when He decrees a matter, He only says to it, 'Be,' and it is.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah in creation, life, and death. It highlights that Allah's command is instantaneous and unchallenged, demonstrating His supremacy over all existence and the inevitability of His will.

translation: Have you not considered those who argue about the signs of Allah? How they are turned away [from the truth]?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and intellectual dishonesty of those who reject divine guidance despite clear evidence, as they deliberately divert attention from the truth to avoid confronting their own misguidance.

translation: Those who deny the Book and what We sent down with Our messengers—soon they will know.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject divine revelation and the messages brought by the prophets, indicating that their denial will be exposed in the Hereafter, where the truth will become undeniable to them.

translation: When the shackles are around their necks and they are dragged [by them],
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describes the severe consequences of disbelief and disobedience to divine commandments, portraying the burden of sin as an inescapable and humiliating physical restraint, emphasizing the inevitability of accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: Then in boiling water they will be scalded.
interpretation: This verse describes the severe and inescapable punishment of the disbelievers in the Hereafter, emphasizing the intensity and unbearable nature of their torment in Hellfire, where they will be immersed in boiling water as a manifestation of divine justice.

translation: Then it will be said to them, "Where are those [false deities] you used to associate [with Me]?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment of ultimate truth in the Hereafter, where the polytheists will be confronted with the reality of their false worship, realizing the futility of their associations with anything other than Allah, as their 'partners' will neither answer nor benefit them in any way.

translation: They said, "They have strayed from us rather, we were not calling upon anything before." Thus does Allah send astray the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and denial of the disbelievers, who refuse to acknowledge their past ignorance and false worship, attributing their straying solely to Allah's will as a consequence of their disbelief.

translation: That is because you used to take pleasure in the earth wrongfully and because you used to exult arrogantly.
interpretation: This verse critiques the indulgence in falsehood and arrogance in worldly matters, warning that such behavior leads to divine accountability and punishment.

translation: Enter the gates of Hell, to abide eternally therein. And how wretched is the residence of the arrogant.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe punishment awaiting those who exhibit arrogance and pride, particularly in their rejection of divine guidance. It serves as a stark warning against the destructive consequences of arrogance, emphasizing that such an attitude leads not only to moral and spiritual downfall in this life but also to eternal damnation in the Hereafter.

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad]. Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth. Whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you [in death], then to Us they will be returned.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty of divine justice and the ultimate accountability of all deeds, emphasizing that patience in the face of adversity is a virtue, and that the fulfillment of Allah's promises—whether in this life or the Hereafter—is inevitable.

translation: And We have already sent messengers before you. Among them are those We have mentioned to you, and among them are those We have not mentioned to you. And it was not for any messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah. But when the command of Allah comes, it will be decided in truth, and the wrongdoers will be lost there.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin and authority of prophethood, emphasizing that messengers are chosen and empowered by Allah alone, not by their own will or ability. It also highlights the inevitability of divine judgment, where truth prevails and falsehood is ultimately destroyed, reinforcing the concept of accountability in the Hereafter.

translation: It is Allah who made for you the grazing livestock, from which you eat and ride.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's role as the Provider of sustenance and means of livelihood, emphasizing the practical and spiritual significance of the blessings He has granted to humanity, such as livestock for food and transportation.

translation: And for you in them are benefits, and that you may seek from them what you need. And upon them and on the ships you are carried.
interpretation: This verse highlights the multifaceted blessings of Allah, where He points out that animals and ships serve not only practical purposes but also fulfill deeper needs of the heart and spirit, demonstrating the comprehensive mercy and wisdom in creation.

translation: And He shows you His signs; then which of the signs of Allah do you deny?
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of recognizing and affirming the signs of Allah in the universe and in one's life, urging reflection and gratitude rather than denial or ingratitude.

translation: Have they not traveled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them? They were greater than them in strength and in impact on the earth, but what they had earned did not avail them.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly power and the ultimate accountability of human actions, urging reflection on historical consequences to draw lessons for present conduct.

translation: But when their messengers came to them with clear proofs, they rejoiced in what they had of knowledge, but they were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of those who possess knowledge yet reject divine guidance, finding pride in their limited understanding while mocking the truth brought by the messengers. Their arrogance blinds them to the consequences of their disbelief, leading to their ultimate downfall.

translation: But when they saw Our punishment, they said, "We believe in Allah alone and reject what we used to associate with Him as partners."
interpretation: This verse highlights the insincerity of faith when it is driven by fear of punishment rather than genuine conviction, as the declaration of belief comes only at the moment of unavoidable consequence.

translation: But their faith could not avail them when they saw Our punishment. [It is] the established way of Allah which has passed on among His servants, and there the disbelievers were lost.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of faith that comes too late, after the signs of divine punishment have manifested. It serves as a warning that true faith must precede the arrival of decisive evidence, as mere acknowledgment after the fact does not alter one's fate. The 'established way of Allah' refers to the consistent pattern in human history where those who persist in disbelief meet their end, reinforcing the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Ha, Meem.
interpretation: The opening of this surah (chapter) begins with the basmala, affirming Allah's attributes of mercy and compassion, followed by the disconnected Arabic letters 'Ha, Meem,' which are among the 'mysteries of the Qur'an' (mutashabihat) whose precise meaning is known only to Allah, though some scholars suggest they may signify emphasis, divine secrets, or a challenge to the disbelievers to produce something similar.

translation: A revelation from the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
interpretation: This opening phrase establishes the divine origin of the Qur'an, emphasizing that its message is not human-made but a direct revelation from Allah, characterized by His boundless mercy and compassion.

translation: A Book whose verses are detailed, an Arabic Qur'an for people who know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the clarity and comprehensibility of the Qur'an's guidance, tailored specifically for those who possess true knowledge and understanding, implying that its message is accessible to those who seek wisdom with an open and discerning mind.

translation: As a bearer of good tidings and a warner; but most of them turn away, so they do not hear.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as both a bringer of glad tidings for the righteous and a warner against punishment for the disbelievers, yet the majority of people reject his message and refuse to listen, demonstrating their spiritual deafness and hardened hearts.

translation: And they say, 'Our hearts are wrapped in covers against what you invite us to, and in our ears is deafness, and between us and you is a barrier. So act, for indeed we are acting.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the hardened hearts and closed minds of those who reject the truth despite clear evidence, choosing willful ignorance and defiance over guidance.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'I am only a man like you, to whom it has been revealed that your god is but one God; so take a straight path to Him and seek His forgiveness.' And woe to those who associate others with Allah.
