interpretation: This verse highlights the dual foundation of true faith: unwavering belief in the divine signs (evidence of Allah's existence, power, and guidance) and complete submission to Allah's will, demonstrating that genuine faith is not merely intellectual assent but also a lived reality of obedience and surrender.

translation: Enter Paradise, you and your spouses, rejoicing.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for the righteous in the Hereafter, where they will be reunited with their righteous spouses in a state of eternal joy and bliss, emphasizing the beauty of companionship in Paradise.

translation: There will be circulated among them vessels of gold and cups, and therein is whatever souls desire and [what] delights the eyes. And you will abide therein eternally.
interpretation: This verse illustrates the luxurious and abundant provisions in Paradise, emphasizing that believers will experience ultimate satisfaction and joy, both in their desires and in what pleases their senses, without any limitation or end, reflecting the boundless generosity of Allah in the Hereafter.

translation: And this is the Paradise you have been made to inherit for what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that Paradise is not granted arbitrarily but is the just reward for one's righteous deeds and sincere devotion in this world.

translation: Therein (the Garden) is abundant fruit from which you will eat.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the generosity and abundance of Allah's provision in Paradise, highlighting that the blessings are not only plentiful but also accessible and meant for the enjoyment of the believers.

translation: Indeed, the criminals will be eternal in the punishment of Hell.
interpretation: This verse underscores the eternal and unchanging nature of divine justice, where those who persist in grave wrongdoing face an irreversible fate, highlighting the gravity of moral choices and the consequences of persistent injustice.

translation: They will not be relieved of it (the punishment), and they will be in despair within it.
interpretation: This verse underscores the unrelenting and inescapable nature of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief or wrongdoing, emphasizing the permanence of their despair and the absence of any respite or hope for relief.

translation: And We did not wrong them, but it was they who were the wrongdoers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the principle of divine justice, affirming that God does not oppress anyone, and any suffering or punishment faced by individuals or communities is a consequence of their own actions and choices, not divine injustice.

translation: And they will cry, 'O Mālik, let your Lord put an end to us!' He will say, 'Indeed, you will remain [in punishment].'
interpretation: This verse underscores the irreversible nature of divine justice and the finality of the Hereafter, where no plea or request for relief from punishment will alter the decree of Allah, emphasizing the absolute authority and unchanging nature of His judgment.

translation: We have brought you the truth, but most of you hate the truth.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to reject truth when it conflicts with personal desires or established norms, emphasizing the challenge faced by messengers in conveying divine guidance.

translation: Or do they intend a plan? But I (Allah) am planning (against their plans).
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over all affairs, assuring believers that no plot or scheme against them can succeed without His permission, as He is the ultimate planner and executor of all outcomes.

translation: Do they think that We do not hear their secrets and their private counsels? Yes [We do], and Our messengers are with them recording.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's omniscience and the inevitability of accountability for all actions, even those hidden in secrecy or whispered in private. The recording by angels signifies that nothing escapes divine knowledge, and all deeds—public or private—will be accounted for on the Day of Judgment.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'If the Most Merciful had a son, I would be the first of [His] worshippers.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness and transcendence of Allah, rejecting any notion of Him having offspring or partners, as such concepts are incompatible with His divine nature and sovereignty.

translation: Glory be to the Lord of the heavens and the earth, the Lord of the Throne, above what they describe.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transcendence and absolute perfection of Allah, declaring Him free from any imperfections or false descriptions attributed to Him by those who associate partners with Him or distort His nature.

translation: So leave them to indulge and play until they meet their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: This verse advises patience and restraint in the face of those who mock or reject the truth, as their denial will ultimately lead them to face the consequences of their actions on the Day of Judgment.

translation: And He is the God in the heaven, and the God in the earth; and He is the Wise, the Knower.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and unity of God, emphasizing that He is the sole deity in both the heavens and the earth, with perfect wisdom and knowledge over all creation.

translation: Blessed is He who has the dominion of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, and with Him is the knowledge of the Hour, and to Him you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty over all existence and His exclusive knowledge of the unseen, including the timing of the Day of Judgment, reminding humanity of their ultimate return to Him for judgment.

translation: And those whom they invoke besides Him have no power of intercession, except for whoever bears witness to the truth while they know [it].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true intercession (shafa'ah) is only granted by Allah's permission and is reserved for those who testify to the truth with full knowledge and conviction, highlighting the exclusivity of divine authority in matters of intercession and the importance of sincerity in faith.

translation: And if you ask them, 'Who created them?' they will surely say, 'Allah.' Then how are they deluded?
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent human recognition of Allah's existence as the Creator, yet it underscores the paradox of how people, despite acknowledging this truth, turn away from Him in disbelief or disobedience.

translation: And he said, 'My Lord, indeed these are a people who do not believe.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the despair and frustration of a prophet or believer when faced with the persistent rejection and disbelief of their people, highlighting the limits of human influence in guiding others and the need for divine intervention or patience in the face of adversity.

translation: So pardon them and say, 'Peace.' And they will come to know.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believer to respond to hostility with forbearance and a peaceful attitude, trusting that the consequences of such behavior will become clear to others over time, reinforcing the principle of patient perseverance in the face of adversity.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Ha, Meem.
interpretation: The opening of this surah (chapter) with the basmalah (the invocation of Allah’s names) establishes a tone of divine mercy and compassion, while the disconnected letters like 'Ha, Meem' are a stylistic feature in the Qur'an whose meaning is known only to Allah, often serving as a reminder of the Qur'an's miraculous and inimitable nature.

translation: By the clear Book (the Qur'an).
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the Qur'an's clarity and its role as a definitive source of guidance, distinguishing between truth and falsehood, and serving as a manifest proof of divine revelation.

translation: Indeed, We sent the Qur'an down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn [mankind].
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine origin and significance of the Qur'an, emphasizing its revelation during a night of immense spiritual value (often understood as Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Decree). The mention of warning signifies the Qur'an's role as a guidance and admonition for humanity, calling them to righteousness and warning them of the consequences of straying from God's path.

translation: In it [the Night of Decree] is decreed every matter of wisdom.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound significance of the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), during which Allah decrees all matters of wisdom and importance for the coming year, emphasizing divine wisdom, order, and the predetermined course of events.

translation: An order from Us; indeed, We were the senders [of the messenger].
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of the commandments conveyed through the prophets, emphasizing that they are not human inventions but revelations from Allah, sent down to guide humanity with truth and wisdom.

translation: A mercy from your Lord. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the guidance and blessings bestowed upon humanity are acts of divine mercy, underscoring Allah's attributes of being All-Hearing and All-Knowing, which highlight His awareness of all things and His responsiveness to the needs of His creation.

translation: Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, if you should be certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty and unity of Allah over all creation, including what lies beyond human perception ('whatever is between them'), while subtly reminding believers that true certainty in faith is the key to recognizing this truth.

translation: There is no god except Him. He gives life and causes death. (He is) your Lord and the Lord of your first forefathers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and sovereignty of Allah (SWT), affirming that He alone is the true God who sustains all existence, controls life and death, and is the Lord of all creation, including the ancestors of the believers. It serves as a reminder of Allah's ultimate authority and the necessity of worshipping Him alone without associating any partners with Him.

translation: Nay, but they are in doubt, playing.
interpretation: This verse underscores the frivolous and dismissive attitude of those who reject faith, treating matters of ultimate truth with levity rather than sincere contemplation or conviction.

translation: So watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke.
interpretation: This verse is a warning of a future Day of Judgment when a manifest smoke will envelop the sky, signaling the approach of the end times and the inevitability of divine reckoning.

translation: Covering the people will be this painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability and inescapability of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief or transgression, emphasizing that no one will be spared from its grasp.

translation: Our Lord, remove the punishment from us; indeed, we are believers.
interpretation: This verse reflects the plea of those who are suffering from divine punishment due to their past disbelief or sins, seeking repentance and mercy from Allah. It highlights the importance of faith and the possibility of divine forgiveness when one turns to Allah in sincere belief and remorse.

translation: How can they be reminded when a clear Messenger has already come to them?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and willful ignorance of those who reject the truth despite the arrival of a clear and unambiguous messenger (the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ) with divine guidance. It underscores the idea that some people are so entrenched in their disbelief or heedlessness that even the most evident signs and messengers fail to awaken them.

translation: Yet they turned away from him and said, 'A madman!'
interpretation: This verse highlights the rejection of truth by those who dismiss it out of arrogance or disbelief, attributing divine guidance to madness rather than acknowledging its divine origin.

translation: Indeed, We will remove the punishment for a little while, but you will surely return [to disbelief].
interpretation: This verse underscores the temporary nature of divine respite granted to people, even when they persist in disbelief or wrongdoing. It serves as a reminder that such relief is not a sign of approval but rather a test or an opportunity for reflection, with the expectation that they will eventually return to their prior state or face greater consequences.

translation: The Day We will strike with the greatest assault, indeed, We will take retribution.
interpretation: This verse refers to the Day of Judgment when Allah will decisively punish the oppressors and wrongdoers for their transgressions, demonstrating His justice and retribution against those who denied His signs and oppressed others.

translation: And We had already tested [the people of] nations before them, [such as] the people of Pharaoh. And there came to them a noble Messenger.
interpretation: This verse underscores the historical pattern of divine testing and the consistent response of rejecting messengers despite clear signs, warning of the consequences of arrogance and disbelief.

translation: That you deliver to the servants of Allah. Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger.
interpretation: This verse underscores the primary duty of conveying the message of Islam to all people, emphasizing the trustworthiness and honesty of the messenger in delivering divine guidance without alteration or distortion.

translation: And do not exalt yourselves against Allah. Indeed, I come to you with a clear authority.
interpretation: This verse warns against arrogance and defiance towards Allah's commands, emphasizing that true authority and proof come from Him alone, not from human pride or power.

translation: And indeed, I seek refuge in my Lord and your Lord lest you stone me.
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) reliance on Allah as his protector when facing threats from his people, highlighting the importance of seeking divine refuge in times of danger and opposition.

translation: But if you do not believe in me, then leave me alone.
interpretation: This verse reflects the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) call to the people of Mecca to accept Islam, emphasizing his patience and persistence despite their rejection, while also asserting his right to be free from their disbelief.

translation: So he called upon his Lord, 'Indeed, these are a criminal people.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the supplication of a prophet (likely Hud, peace be upon him) against his people who rejected his message and persisted in their disbelief and wrongdoing, invoking divine judgment upon them due to their extreme transgression and rejection of truth.

translation: So travel with My servants by night, for indeed you will be pursued.
interpretation: This verse underscores the urgency and divine protection granted to the believers during a critical journey, emphasizing that their escape at night is divinely ordained and that their pursuers will ultimately fail in their mission.

translation: And leave the sea as it is, still. Indeed, they are a drowned army.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine power to control natural elements (the sea) and the ultimate fate of those who oppose divine will, emphasizing that their destruction is inevitable and divinely ordained.

translation: How many gardens and springs have they left behind?
interpretation: This verse reflects on the consequences of human actions, particularly the destruction or abandonment of once-thriving civilizations and their natural resources due to arrogance, injustice, or heedlessness of divine guidance.

translation: And gardens and an honorable station.
interpretation: This verse highlights the rewards of the righteous in the Hereafter, emphasizing both material blessings (gardens) and spiritual honor (an honorable station), reflecting the comprehensive nature of divine recompense.

translation: And [they will be] in what they used to take delight.
interpretation: This verse highlights the eternal joy and contentment that the righteous will experience in Paradise, contrasting it with the fleeting pleasures of this world, emphasizing that true fulfillment lies in the everlasting bliss of the Hereafter.

translation: Thus [it was]. And We caused it to be inherited by other people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transient nature of worldly power and the inevitability of divine justice, where the consequences of actions—whether of a nation or an individual—ultimately lead to a transfer of authority to others, often those who were previously oppressed or marginalized, as a fulfillment of God's wisdom and justice.

translation: So the heavens and the earth did not weep for them, nor were they given respite.
interpretation: This verse underscores the finality of divine judgment, indicating that even the heavens and the earth—symbols of the vastness and order of creation—do not mourn for those who persist in denial or wrongdoing, nor are they granted any delay in their reckoning.

translation: And We certainly saved the Children of Israel from the humiliating torment.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and power in delivering a specific group, the Children of Israel, from severe punishment, underscoring divine justice and the consequences of oppression and disbelief.

translation: From Pharaoh. Indeed, he was arrogant and one of the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and excessive transgression against divine commandments, highlighting Pharaoh's defiance as a cautionary example for humanity to avoid similar traits of oppression and moral corruption.

translation: And We have chosen them (the Prophets) knowingly above the worlds (of their time).
interpretation: This verse signifies that Allah has selected certain individuals for prophethood and elevated them above others in their respective eras, not by mere chance, but with full knowledge and wisdom, highlighting the divine wisdom in choosing the best for this noble mission.

translation: And We gave them clear signs, which were a trial manifest.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of divine signs (ayat) as both guidance and a test for humanity—those who recognize them with faith are guided, while those who deny them despite their clarity face trial and misguidance.

translation: Indeed, these [people] say...
interpretation: This verse likely refers to the disbelievers or hypocrites who are making false claims or spreading doubts about the Qur'an or the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It suggests a tone of refutation, indicating that their words are baseless or contrary to truth.

translation: It is but our first death, and we have never been resurrected.
interpretation: This verse reflects the denial of some people towards the Day of Resurrection, suggesting that death is a final end with no possibility of being brought back to life.

translation: Then bring our forefathers if you should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers to perform an impossible act—resurrecting their forefathers—as a test of the truthfulness of their claims against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It underscores the futility of their demands and the certainty of divine truth.

translation: Is it better, or the people of Tubba' and those before them? We destroyed them, for indeed they were criminals.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of worldly power and the inevitability of divine justice, warning that no civilization or people, regardless of their past glory or strength, are immune to accountability if they persist in injustice and transgression.

translation: And We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them in play.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the purposeful and meaningful nature of creation, negating any notion of frivolity or purposelessness in the existence of the universe and all that it contains.

translation: We did not create them except in truth, but most of them do not know.
interpretation: This verse underscores the purposeful and truthful nature of creation, emphasizing that everything exists for a just and meaningful reason, even if human understanding is limited or unaware of that wisdom.

translation: Indeed, the Day of Judgment is their appointed time, all together.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the inevitability and collective nature of the Day of Judgment, where all beings will be gathered to face the final reckoning, highlighting the absolute certainty of divine justice and the accountability of every individual.

translation: The Day when no protector will avail a protector at all, nor will they be helped.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute helplessness of all beings on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that no intercession or support—whether from worldly relationships, power, or influence—will be effective without Allah's permission. It highlights the ultimate sovereignty of Allah and the futility of relying on anything other than Him for salvation.

translation: Except for those upon whom your Lord has mercy. Indeed, He is the Exalted in Might, the Merciful.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and mercy of Allah, emphasizing that salvation and guidance are solely in His hands, as He is the Most Powerful yet the Most Merciful, highlighting that no one can attain mercy except by His will.

translation: Indeed, the tree of Zaqqum
interpretation: This verse refers to the tree of Zaqqum, which is mentioned in the Qur'an as a symbol of punishment and torment in Hellfire, designed to be a source of extreme suffering for the disbelievers and wrongdoers.

translation: The food of the sinner.
interpretation: This phrase refers to the sustenance that will be given to those who persist in sin and disbelief, which is not a true nourishment but rather a punishment or deprivation in the Hereafter, devoid of any benefit or blessing.

translation: Like molten brass boiling in the bellies
interpretation: This verse vividly describes the severe and unbearable torment awaiting the disbelievers in Hell, where their insides will be filled with scalding, boiling liquid that burns and churns within them, symbolizing the intensity of divine punishment for their rejection of faith.

translation: As boiling water.
interpretation: This phrase metaphorically describes a state of extreme distress, agony, or punishment, likening it to the unbearable heat and pain of boiling water, emphasizing the severity of the suffering endured.

translation: Seize him and drag him into the midst of Hell.
interpretation: This verse conveys the inevitability of divine justice for those who persist in disbelief and defiance against Allah’s guidance, emphasizing that their punishment is certain and inescapable.

translation: Then pour upon his head the punishment of scalding water.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity and inescapability of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief and defiance against God's signs and guidance, emphasizing the torment's intensity as a reflection of their rejection of truth.

translation: Taste [the punishment], for it is you who is the Almighty, the Most Generous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the irony of a person who, despite claiming greatness and generosity, faces divine punishment, highlighting the contrast between human arrogance and God's ultimate justice and power.

translation: Indeed, this is what you used to deny.
interpretation: This verse is a direct address to those who previously rejected the truth, emphasizing the certainty of their denial coming to pass, thereby highlighting the consequences of their disbelief and the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward of the righteous—security and peace in the Hereafter, free from fear, anxiety, or harm, reflecting their steadfast faith and righteous deeds in this life.

translation: In gardens and springs.
interpretation: This verse signifies the ultimate reward of Paradise, where believers will dwell in eternal bliss, surrounded by lush gardens and flowing springs—a symbol of purity, sustenance, and everlasting joy.

translation: They will wear fine silk and rich brocade, facing each other.
interpretation: This verse describes the luxurious garments of the believers in Paradise, symbolizing the ultimate reward and honor bestowed upon them, emphasizing both material and spiritual perfection.

translation: Thus We paired them with companions of large, beautiful eyes.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine reward of Paradise, where believers are paired with spouses of extraordinary beauty and purity, symbolizing the ultimate fulfillment of their righteous desires in the hereafter.

translation: Therein they will call for every kind of fruit in peace and security.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate state of contentment and fulfillment in Paradise, where believers will have unrestricted access to all varieties of fruit, symbolizing the abundance and perfection of divine provision, and they will experience complete safety and tranquility, free from any fear or want.

translation: They will not taste death therein except the first death. And He will have protected them from the punishment of Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse highlights the eternal nature of the Hereafter, where believers will be granted a life free from death after their initial death in this world, emphasizing the ultimate triumph over mortality and the complete removal of suffering.

translation: As a favor from your Lord. That is the great attainment.
interpretation: This verse underscores that true success and ultimate victory come not from one's own efforts alone, but as a divine gift from Allah, highlighting the importance of gratitude and reliance on His mercy.

translation: Indeed, We have made it easy in your tongue, that they may be reminded.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the accessibility and clarity of the Qur'an's message, tailored to the linguistic and intellectual capacity of its audience, ensuring that its guidance is within their reach for reflection and remembrance.

translation: So wait, for indeed they are waiting.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly affairs and the certainty of divine justice, urging patience and steadfastness in the face of opposition or delay in the fulfillment of divine promises.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Ha, Meem.
interpretation: The opening of this surah (chapter) begins with the basmala, affirming Allah’s mercy as the foundation for revelation, followed by the disconnected Arabic letters (ḥāʾ, mīm), which are a common feature in several Meccan surahs and are interpreted by scholars as signs pointing to the miraculous nature of the Qur’an itself—its linguistic inimitability (i'jāz) and divine origin, inviting reflection on the profound truths that follow.

translation: This is the revelation of the Book [the Quran] from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Quran, attributing its revelation to Allah, who is characterized by absolute power and perfect wisdom, thereby affirming its truth and guidance as unquestionable.

translation: Indeed, in the heavens and the earth are signs for the believers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the natural world and the universe are filled with signs and evidence of Allah's existence, power, and wisdom, which are perceptible to those who have faith and reflect upon them with a believing heart.

translation: And in the creation of yourselves and what is dispersed of moving creatures are signs for a people who are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse highlights the intricate design and diversity in creation—both human and other living beings—as profound evidence of Allah’s existence and power, inviting those with unwavering faith to reflect deeply on these signs.

translation: And [in] the alternation of night and day and [in] what Allah sends down from the sky of provision and gives life thereby to the earth after its lifelessness and [in] the directing of the winds are signs for a people who reason.
interpretation: This verse highlights the signs of Allah's power and wisdom in the natural world, urging reflection on the deliberate design behind creation—such as the cycle of day and night, the provision of rain to revive the earth, and the winds—all of which serve as evidence of divine order and purpose for those who think deeply.

translation: These are the verses of Allah which We recite to you, [O Muhammad], in truth. So in what statement after Allah and His verses will they believe?
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority and truthfulness of the Qur'an as the word of Allah, implying that any belief or discourse that contradicts or deviates from it is inherently flawed and lacks true validation.

translation: Woe to every scorner and sinner.
interpretation: This verse warns against those who engage in slander, deceit, and persistent sin, emphasizing the severe consequences awaiting such individuals in the Hereafter.

translation: He hears the verses of Allah recited to him; then he turns away arrogantly as if he had not heard them. So give him tidings of a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences of rejecting divine guidance out of arrogance and pride, despite having the capacity to understand and reflect upon it.

translation: And when he knows anything of Our verses, he takes them in mockery. For such there will be a humiliating punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe consequences for those who ridicule or dismiss the divine signs and revelations of Allah, emphasizing that such behavior is not only disrespectful but also spiritually perilous, leading to a degrading punishment in the Hereafter.

translation: Behind them is Hell, and what they have earned will not avail them in the least, nor will those they took besides Allah as allies. For them is a great punishment.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute futility of relying on worldly achievements or false deities for salvation in the Hereafter, emphasizing that only true faith and righteous deeds, as ordained by Allah, can avert divine punishment.

translation: This is guidance. And those who disbelieve in the signs of their Lord will have a painful punishment of severe intensity.
interpretation: This verse underscores the dual response to divine guidance: acceptance leads to righteousness, while rejection invites severe retribution, emphasizing the gravity of disbelief in divine signs.

translation: It is Allah who subjected the sea for you so that ships may sail upon it by His command and that you may seek of His bounty; and perhaps you will be grateful.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's supreme power in subjecting natural elements like the sea for human benefit, emphasizing the importance of recognizing divine favor and expressing gratitude through ethical and responsible use of these blessings.

translation: And He has subjected to you whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, all from Himself. Indeed in that are signs for a people who give thought.
interpretation: This verse highlights the comprehensive nature of God's blessings and the signs of His omnipotence in the natural world, urging reflection on the purpose and gratitude for these provisions.

translation: Say to those who believe that they should forgive those who do not expect the days of Allah, so that Allah may reward a people for what they have earned.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to respond to the oppression or harm they receive from others with forgiveness and patience, trusting in Allah's justice and divine retribution. It implies that by showing mercy, they align themselves with Allah's attribute of justice, which will ultimately reward the righteous and hold the wrongdoers accountable for their actions.

translation: Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own soul; and whoever does evil, it is against the self. Then to your Lord you will be returned.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes personal responsibility and accountability in one's actions, highlighting that righteous deeds benefit the doer in the Hereafter, while evil deeds harm only the perpetrator, underscoring the ultimate return to Allah for judgment.

translation: And We did certainly give the Children of Israel the Scripture and judgment and prophethood, and We provided them with good things and preferred them over the worlds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the special favor and distinction Allah granted to the Children of Israel by bestowing upon them divine guidance (Scripture), wisdom (judgment), and prophethood, alongside material blessings and a position of honor over other nations. It underscores the concept of divine selection and the responsibility that comes with it, as well as the transient nature of worldly favor, which is subject to Allah's will and the actions of the people.

translation: And We gave them clear proofs of the matter [i.e., the truth]. And they did not differ except after knowledge had come to them, out of injustice among themselves. Indeed, your Lord will judge between them on the Day of Resurrection concerning that over which they used to differ.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to distort truth and create divisions despite clear evidence, driven by arrogance and selfish motives, while affirming divine justice as the ultimate arbiter of disputes.

translation: Then We put you, [O Muhammad], on an ordained way concerning the matter [of religion]; so follow it and do not follow the inclinations of those who do not know.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of adhering to the divine guidance and law (Sharia) established by Allah, rather than being swayed by the whims and ignorance of those who lack true knowledge. It underscores the necessity of steadfastness in faith and the rejection of misguided opinions or practices that contradict Allah's commandments.

translation: Indeed, they will not avail you against Allah at all. And indeed, the wrongdoers are allies of one another; but Allah is the ally of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of seeking protection or support from those who oppose Allah, as their power is ultimately meaningless against divine decree. It also highlights the natural alliance between wrongdoers, who unite in their rebellion against truth, while Allah stands as the sole protector and guardian of the righteous, ensuring their ultimate triumph over oppression.

translation: These are enlightenments for mankind and a guidance and a mercy for a people who are certain [in faith].
interpretation: This verse highlights the Qur'an's dual role as both a source of intellectual and spiritual enlightenment and a practical guide for those who possess unwavering faith, emphasizing that its guidance and mercy are accessible only to those who genuinely believe and trust in its divine origin.

translation: Do the ones who committed evil deeds think that We will make them like those who believed and did righteous deeds, equal in their life and death? How wretched is the judgment they make!
interpretation: This verse refutes the notion that people who commit evil deeds will be treated equally in the Hereafter as those who believe and do good deeds, highlighting the injustice of such a belief and emphasizing divine justice.

translation: And Allah created the heavens and the earth in truth so that every soul may be recompensed for what it has earned, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the justice of Allah in creation and the Hereafter, ensuring that every individual will be fairly rewarded or punished for their deeds without any injustice.

translation: Have you seen he who has taken as his god his [own] desire, and Allah has sent him astray due to knowledge and put a seal upon his hearing and his heart and put a covering over his vision? So who will guide him after Allah? Then will you not be reminded?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against the dangers of following one's own desires and ego without regard for divine guidance, illustrating how such behavior can lead to spiritual blindness and deafness, ultimately resulting in divine abandonment.

translation: And they say, "There is not but our worldly life; we die and live, and nothing destroys us except time." And they have of that no knowledge; they are only assuming.
interpretation: This verse critiques the materialistic worldview that reduces existence to mere physical life and death, attributing all change and destruction to the passage of time rather than divine will or purpose. It highlights the ignorance and baseless assumptions of those who deny the Hereafter, emphasizing that their belief is rooted in speculation rather than knowledge or revelation.

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, their only argument is that they say, "Bring back our forefathers, if you should be truthful."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth despite clear evidence, resorting to demands for supernatural proof or historical precedent rather than engaging with the message itself.

translation: Say, 'Allah gives you life, then causes you to die, then He will gather you for the Day of Resurrection about which there is no doubt. But most of the people do not know.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over life, death, and resurrection, emphasizing the certainty of the Hereafter while highlighting humanity's frequent neglect of this fundamental truth.

translation: To Allah belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And the Day the Hour appears - that Day the falsifiers will lose.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that ultimate authority and control belong solely to Him. On the Day of Judgment, those who engaged in falsehood, corruption, or injustice in this world will face loss and regret, as their deeds will be exposed and their claims of truth or righteousness will be rendered meaningless before divine justice.

translation: And you will see every community kneeling. Every community will be called to its record: 'Today you will be recompensed for what you used to do.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the accountability of every individual and community for their deeds, emphasizing that no one will escape the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.

translation: This is Our record, speaking about you in truth. Indeed, We were recording what you used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute accountability of every individual before Allah, emphasizing that all actions—whether good or evil—are meticulously recorded and will be presented as evidence on the Day of Judgment, ensuring divine justice and the inevitability of recompense.

translation: As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, their Lord will admit them into His mercy. That is the clear triumph.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for believers who not only have faith but also act upon it through righteous deeds—entering into Allah's mercy is the most evident and undeniable success, underscoring that true faith is validated by righteous action.

translation: But as for those who disbelieved, were My signs not recited to you? Then you turned away in arrogance, and you were a people of criminals.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of rejecting divine guidance despite its clear presentation, attributing the rejection to arrogance and persistent wrongdoing rather than a lack of evidence.

translation: And when it is said, 'Indeed, the promise of Allah is true and the Hour [of Judgment] is coming - no doubt about it,' you [i.e., the disbelievers] say, 'We do not know what the Hour is. We assume only assumption, and we are not certain.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and denial of the disbelievers who refuse to acknowledge the certainty of the Day of Judgment despite clear evidence and divine promises, reflecting their intellectual arrogance and refusal to submit to the truth.

translation: And their evil deeds will appear plain to them, and they will be overwhelmed by what they used to mock at.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning that the consequences of one's actions—both good and evil—will inevitably manifest in this life or the Hereafter, and those who ridicule faith or divine justice will face the reality of their misdeeds in a manner they never anticipated.

translation: And it will be said, "This Day We will forget you as you forgot the meeting of this Day of yours, and your refuge is the Fire, and for you there are no helpers."
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute justice of the Day of Judgment, where divine retribution is meted out with perfect precision—those who neglected their moral and spiritual duties in life will face eternal consequences, devoid of any intercession or escape, highlighting the irreversibility of their choices.

translation: That is because you took the signs of Allah in mockery and the worldly life deluded you. So today, they will not emerge from it, nor will they be reprieved.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severe consequences of mocking divine signs and being deceived by the allure of worldly life, highlighting the irreversible nature of judgment and the finality of one's fate in the Hereafter.

translation: So to Allah belongs all praise—Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth, Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and uniqueness of Allah as the sole deserving recipient of all praise, encompassing His dominion over all creation, from the heavens to the earth and beyond, affirming His unparalleled authority and the comprehensive nature of His Lordship.

translation: And to Him belongs the grandeur in the heavens and the earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and unmatched power over all creation, highlighting that His greatness is not confined to any particular realm but encompasses the heavens and the earth. The mention of His might and wisdom together underscores that His grandeur is not arbitrary but rooted in perfect justice and divine purpose.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Ha, Meem.
interpretation: The opening of this surah (chapter) begins with the invocation of Allah's mercy and compassion, emphasizing His dual attributes of being Rahman (the source of all mercy) and Rahim (the source of all compassion). The letters 'Ha, Meem' are among the 'Mysteries of the Qur'an' (Muqatta'at), whose meanings are known only to Allah, though some scholars suggest they may symbolize the divine secrets of creation or the unseen aspects of revelation.

translation: The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Exalted in Might, the Wise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and authority of the Qur'an, highlighting Allah's supreme power and perfect wisdom in its revelation, underscoring that it is not a human composition but a direct, transcendent communication from the Almighty.

translation: We did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except in truth and for a specified term. But those who disbelieve, from what they have been warned, are turning away.
interpretation: This verse underscores the purposeful and deliberate creation of the universe by Allah, emphasizing that everything exists for a meaningful and predetermined duration ('for a specified term'), not by chance or without reason. The mention of 'those who disbelieve' turning away from divine warnings highlights the consequences of rejecting truth, suggesting that their denial is not due to lack of evidence but rather a willful disregard for the signs and guidance provided by Allah.

translation: Say, 'Have you seen that which you invoke besides Allah? Show me what they have created from the earth, or did they have a share in [creation of] the heavens? Bring me a scripture [revealed] before this or a [remaining] trace of knowledge, if you should be truthful.'
interpretation: This verse challenges the polytheists to provide evidence for their claims of other deities besides Allah, emphasizing the absurdity of worshipping false gods who have no role in creation or sustaining the universe, and underscores the burden of proof on those who deviate from monotheism.

translation: And who is more astray than he who invokes besides Allah those who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they, of their invocation, are unaware?
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility and misguidance of worshipping or supplicating to anything or anyone other than Allah, as such entities cannot respond or aid the supplicant, being themselves unaware of their worship.

translation: And when the people are gathered [for Judgment], they will be enemies to them and [will be] deniers of their worship.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate futility of worship directed towards anything other than Allah. On the Day of Judgment, those who were worshipped or followed besides Allah will disown their followers and deny their devotion, revealing the falsehood of associating partners with Allah (shirk). It underscores the importance of sincere and exclusive worship of Allah alone, as any other form of worship will be exposed as invalid and rejected.

translation: And when Our clear verses are recited to them, the disbelievers say of the truth when it has come to them, 'This is obvious magic.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the persistent denial and deflection of truth by those who reject faith, attributing divine guidance to mere trickery or deception rather than acknowledging its divine origin.

translation: Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"? Say, "If I have fabricated it, then you have no power to help me against Allah. He knows best what you spread about it. Sufficient is He as a witness between me and you, and He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
interpretation: This verse addresses the accusations of fabrication leveled against the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) by the disbelievers. It asserts that the Prophet has no control over divine revelation and that Allah is fully aware of the falsehoods being spread. The verse underscores Allah's omniscience and His role as the ultimate judge between the Prophet and his detractors, while also highlighting His attributes of forgiveness and mercy.

translation: Say, [O Muhammad], 'I am not something original among the messengers, nor do I know what will be done with me or with you. I only follow what is revealed to me, and I am not but a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the humility and submission of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) to divine revelation, emphasizing that his role is not one of innovation but of conveying the message as instructed. It also highlights the uncertainty of outcomes for both the messenger and his people, reinforcing reliance on Allah’s will rather than personal agency.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if it is from Allah and you disbelieve in it, while a witness from the Children of Israel has testified to something similar and believed, while you acted arrogantly?' Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth despite clear evidence. It underscores that true guidance is not granted to those who persist in injustice and refuse to acknowledge the truth, even when it is supported by witnesses from among their own people.

translation: And those who disbelieved said to those who believed, "If it [the Qur'an] were good, they would not have preceded us to it." And since they are not guided by it, they will say, "This is an ancient lie."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and stubbornness of those who reject faith, attributing their disbelief to a false sense of superiority and dismissing divine guidance as mere fabrication, revealing their deep-seated aversion to truth and divine authority.

translation: And before it, the Book of Moses was a guide and a mercy. And this (Quran) is a Book confirming (previous scriptures) in the Arabic tongue, to warn those who do wrong and as good tidings to the doers of good.
interpretation: This verse highlights the continuity and confirmation of divine guidance across different scriptures, emphasizing the Quran's role as a universal message in the Arabic language, tailored to address the moral and spiritual needs of its audience—warning the unjust while offering hope to the righteous.

translation: Indeed, those who have said, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remained steadfast—there will be no fear upon them, nor will they grieve.
interpretation: This verse assures believers who affirm their faith in Allah and remain steadfast in their devotion that they will be free from anxiety and sorrow in the Hereafter, highlighting the reward of unwavering faith and righteous conduct.

translation: These are the companions of Paradise, abiding eternally therein—a reward for what they used to do.
interpretation: This verse underscores the eternal nature of Paradise as a just recompense for righteous deeds, emphasizing that the reward is not merely temporary but everlasting, reflecting the divine justice and mercy in fulfilling promises to the believers.

translation: And We have enjoined upon man, to his parents, good treatment. His mother carried him with hardship and gave birth to him with hardship, and his gestation and weaning [period] is thirty months. [He grows] until, when he reaches his prime and [also] reaches forty years of age, he says, "My Lord, enable me to be grateful for Your favor which You have bestowed upon me and upon my parents and to work righteousness of which You will approve and make righteous for me my offspring. Indeed, I have repented to You, and indeed, I am of the Muslims."
interpretation: This verse underscores the profound responsibility of treating parents with utmost kindness and gratitude, reflecting the Qur'an's emphasis on filial piety. The mention of the mother's hardship in pregnancy and childbirth serves as a poignant reminder of the immense sacrifices parents make, which obligates children to reciprocate with lifelong devotion and service. The supplication of the forty-year-old man highlights the human desire for righteousness and divine guidance, illustrating that spiritual maturity often comes with age and reflection. It also signifies the importance of seeking God's help in fulfilling one's duties toward parents and progeny, reinforcing the concept of tawheed (oneness of God) and submission to His will.

translation: It is these from whom We accept the best of what they have done and overlook their misdeeds, [they will be] among the companions of Paradise. [This is] the true promise which they had been promised.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's mercy and justice, emphasizing that He accepts the good deeds of His servants and overlooks their shortcomings, rewarding them with Paradise as a fulfillment of His true promise to them.

translation: And [there is] the one who says to his parents, "Uff to you! Do you promise me that I will be raised [from the dead] when generations before me have passed away?" While they call upon Allah, [saying], "Woe to you! Believe! Indeed, the promise of Allah is truth." He says, "This is not but legends of the former peoples."
interpretation: This verse highlights the arrogance and ingratitude of those who reject the truth despite clear signs and the pleas of their parents. It underscores the futility of human denial in the face of divine promises, as well as the stubbornness of those who dismiss divine revelation as mere myths, ignoring the lessons of history and the inevitability of resurrection.

translation: It is these upon whom the word has come due among nations before them from the jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who persist in disbelief and defiance of divine guidance, illustrating that their fate will mirror that of past nations who rejected truth and were consequently destroyed or left in ruin.

translation: And for all [people] are degrees [of reward] for what they have done, and [ Allah ] will fully compensate them for their deeds, and they will not be wronged.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes divine justice and the principle of proportional reward based on one's deeds, ensuring that no individual is deprived of their rightful due or subjected to any form of injustice in the reckoning of their actions.

translation: And [mention] the Day when those who disbelieved will be brought to the Fire [and will be told], "You exhausted your pleasures during your worldly life and enjoyed them, so this Day you will be awarded the punishment of [extreme] disgrace for what you were arrogant upon the earth without right and [for] what you were defiantly disobedient."
interpretation: This verse underscores the accountability of human beings for their actions in this world, particularly the misuse of blessings and the arrogance that stems from them. It serves as a reminder that the temporary enjoyments of this life are not the ultimate goal, and that true justice will be meted out in the Hereafter, where arrogance and defiance of divine commands will be met with severe punishment.

translation: And remember the brother of 'Aad, when he warned his people among the dunes [of the ancient cities of 'Aad], and indeed warners had already passed on before him and after him [saying], 'Worship none but Allah; indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a tremendous Day.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the consistency of divine guidance across generations, highlighting that the message of monotheism and the warning of divine punishment are recurring themes in prophetic missions. It also serves as a reminder of the consequences of rejecting truth and the importance of heeding warnings before it is too late.

translation: They said, 'Have you come to us to turn us away from our gods? Then bring us what you threaten us with, if you should be of the truthful.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject the truth despite clear signs. Their demand for punishment is not a genuine request for proof but a challenge rooted in disbelief and defiance, showing their unwillingness to accept guidance even when confronted with it.

translation: Indeed, the knowledge is only with Allah, and I convey to you what I have been sent with, but I see you are a people who are ignorant.
interpretation: This verse underscores the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) role as a messenger conveying divine revelation, while acknowledging that ultimate knowledge belongs to Allah alone. It also highlights the people's rejection or lack of understanding of the message, despite its clear transmission.

translation: Then when they saw it as a cloud approaching their valleys, they said, "This is a cloud bringing us rain." Rather, it is what you sought to hasten—a wind in which is painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of human perception and divine justice. The people, seeing an approaching cloud, mistakenly believed it to be a source of mercy (rain), only to realize it was the very punishment they had arrogantly demanded to hasten. It underscores how humans often misinterpret divine signs, confusing temporary comforts or trials for blessings or curses, while God’s wisdom and justice transcend human understanding.

translation: Their Lord destroyed them completely, so they became such that nothing was left except their dwellings. Thus do We recompense the criminal people.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power of Allah in executing His divine decree, demonstrating that even the most prosperous and mighty civilizations can be utterly obliterated when they persist in injustice and transgression, leaving behind only remnants of their existence as a lesson for others.

translation: And We had firmly established them in [the land] in which We have placed you, and We gave them hearing and vision and hearts [i.e., intellect]. But their hearing, vision, and hearts availed them not from anything [i.e., against Allah], since they used to reject the signs of Allah; and they were enveloped by what they used to ridicule.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of worldly power and privilege when devoid of faith and righteousness, highlighting that divine signs are the ultimate truth, and mocking them leads to inevitable punishment.

translation: And We have already destroyed what surrounds you of [those] cities, and We have diversified the signs [or verses] that perhaps they will return [from disbelief].
interpretation: This verse underscores the historical precedent of divine punishment for those who persist in disbelief despite clear signs and warnings, while also highlighting Allah's mercy in repeatedly presenting evidence and opportunities for reflection to guide humanity back to the truth.

translation: Then why did not the gods they invoked besides Allah help them? Rather, they vanished from them. That was their falsehood, and what they were inventing.
interpretation: This verse critiques the futility of associating partners with Allah and relying on false deities, emphasizing that such idols cannot provide aid or support, as they are mere illusions created by human fabrication and misguidance.

translation: And [mention] when We directed a group of jinn to you, [O Muhammad], listening to the Qur'an. And when they attended it, they said, 'Listen attentively.' And when it was concluded, they returned to their people as warners.
interpretation: This verse highlights the transformative power of the Qur'an, even among those who were initially skeptical or distant from its message, such as the jinn. It demonstrates that divine guidance can penetrate hearts and minds regardless of their origin, compelling even outsiders to recognize its truth and urgency, compelling them to convey its warning to others.

translation: They said, 'O our people, indeed we have heard [a revelation] which has been revealed after Moses, confirming what was before it, guiding to the truth and to a straight path.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the transformative impact of divine revelation on those who recognize its truth. It highlights the continuity of God's guidance through successive prophets, emphasizing that the new revelation (the Qur'an) not only affirms the previous scriptures but also provides clear direction toward truth and righteousness, steering people away from deviation and toward a straight and unerring path.

translation: O our people, respond to the caller of Allah and believe in him; Allah will forgive you your sins and protect you from a painful punishment.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the urgency of responding to the divine call to faith and righteousness, promising forgiveness and protection from severe punishment as a direct consequence of such belief and submission.

translation: And whoever does not respond to Allah's Caller will never be able to escape [from Allah] on earth, and there will be no protectors for him besides Him. Those are in manifest error.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute necessity of responding to Allah's guidance and the futility of resisting it, as no one can evade Allah's decree or find protection outside of Him, highlighting the severe consequences of rejecting divine truth.

translation: Have they not seen that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and did not tire by their creation, is [also] Able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed, He is over all things competent.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power of Allah by drawing a parallel between His ability to create the heavens and the earth without fatigue and His ability to resurrect the dead, emphasizing that the latter is no more difficult for Him than the former.

translation: And [mention] the Day when those who disbelieved will be brought to the Fire [and will be told], "Is this not the truth?" They will say, "Yes, by our Lord." He will say, "Then taste the punishment for what you used to disbelieve."
interpretation: This verse underscores the undeniable reality of the Hereafter and the certainty of divine justice. The disbelievers, despite their denial in the worldly life, will be forced to acknowledge the truth of their punishment in the Hereafter, but their acknowledgment will come too late to avert it. It highlights the justice of Allah in recompensing people according to their deeds, emphasizing that disbelief and rejection of truth are met with severe consequences.

translation: So be patient, [O Muhammad], as were the messengers of determination among the messengers. And do not seek to hasten for them. On the Day they see what they are promised, it will be as if they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of a day. [This is] notification. And will [any] be destroyed except the defiantly disobedient people?
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of patience in the face of adversity and rejection, as exemplified by the resolute prophets before the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It reassures the Prophet that divine justice will prevail, and the disbelievers' punishment—though delayed—is inevitable. The fleeting nature of worldly life compared to the Hereafter is highlighted, emphasizing that the arrogant and defiantly disobedient are the only ones who face destruction.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [people] from the way of Allah - He nullified their deeds.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of obstructing the path of truth and guidance, indicating that such actions lead to the invalidation of one's deeds, even if they were otherwise righteous, as the intention behind them is corrupted by disbelief and obstruction of faith.

translation: And those who believe and do righteous deeds and believe in what has been sent down to Muhammad - and it is the truth from their Lord - He will remove from them their misdeeds and amend their condition.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound mercy and justice of Allah, emphasizing that true faith combined with righteous actions leads to the forgiveness of sins and the improvement of one's state in this life and the Hereafter, underscoring the transformative power of divine guidance and the believer's sincere devotion.

translation: That is because those who disbelieved followed falsehood, while those who believed followed the truth from their Lord. Thus does Allah present examples for the people.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental distinction between faith and disbelief, emphasizing that true guidance comes solely from Allah, while misguidance stems from following falsehood. It underscores the accountability of individuals for their choices, as their paths are shaped by their adherence to either truth or falsehood.

translation: So when you meet those who disbelieve [in battle], strike [their] necks until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, then secure their bonds, and either [confer] favor afterwards or ransom [them] until the war lays down its burdens. That [is the command]. And if Allah willed, He could have taken vengeance upon them [Himself]; but [He ordered this] to test some of you by means of others. And those who are killed in the cause of Allah - never will He waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse outlines the conduct of warfare in Islam, emphasizing restraint and proportionality even in battle. It permits fighting against those who initiate hostilities but mandates humane treatment of captives, offering them either clemency or ransom to hasten the end of hostilities. The verse underscores that Allah’s power is absolute, yet He allows trials between people to test faith and resilience. The mention of those who die in His cause highlights the divine validation of their sacrifice, ensuring their deeds are not in vain, reinforcing the sanctity of struggle for justice and truth.

translation: He will guide them and rectify their condition.
interpretation: This verse signifies divine guidance and correction, implying that Allah will lead those who are sincere to the right path and improve their state of affairs, both spiritually and materially, as a result of their faith and righteous deeds.

translation: And He will admit them into Paradise, having made it known to them.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's ultimate mercy and generosity, where He not only grants the believers Paradise but also makes it familiar and welcoming to them, ensuring they feel at home in their eternal abode.

translation: O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and plant firmly your feet.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the reciprocal relationship between human effort and divine support, highlighting that steadfastness in faith and righteous action leads to divine assistance and stability in one's path.

translation: But as for those who disbelieved, may they be ruined, and He will make their deeds go astray.
interpretation: This verse expresses a strong condemnation of disbelief, invoking ruin upon the disbelievers and declaring that their actions will be rendered futile or misguided in the sight of Allah, emphasizing the ultimate consequence of rejecting faith.

translation: That is because they disliked what Allah revealed, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of rejecting divine revelation out of dislike or rejection, emphasizing that such an attitude nullifies all righteous deeds, as true acceptance of Allah's guidance is essential for deeds to be meaningful and rewarded.

translation: Have they not traveled through the land and observed how was the end of those before them? Allah destroyed [everything] over them, and for the disbelievers is something similar [in consequence].
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject faith or fail to reflect on historical lessons, emphasizing that the fate of past nations who denied the truth was destruction—a consequence that awaits those who persist in disbelief or heedlessness.

translation: That is because Allah is the Protector of those who have believed, while for the disbelievers there is no protector.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fundamental difference in the spiritual and existential support systems of believers versus disbelievers, emphasizing that true protection and guidance come solely from Allah for those who have faith in Him.

translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds to gardens beneath which rivers flow. But those who disbelieved enjoy [this world] and eat as the animals eat, and the Fire will be their accommodation.
interpretation: This verse contrasts the eternal reward of the believers with the fleeting enjoyment of the disbelievers in this world, emphasizing that true success lies in faith and righteous deeds, while unbelief leads to a humiliating and painful end.

translation: And how many a city that was stronger than your city which has driven you out - We destroyed them, so they had no helpers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the transient nature of worldly power and the inevitability of divine justice, reminding us that no matter how formidable or dominant a civilization may appear, it is ultimately subject to God's will and can be swiftly dismantled if it deviates from righteousness or oppresses others.

translation: So can someone who was given clear evidence from his Lord be like someone whose evil deeds have been made attractive to him and who follow their own desires?
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between those who are guided by divine truth and those who are deceived by their own inclinations and misguided desires, emphasizing the accountability of human choices.

translation: The example of Paradise which the righteous are promised is [that beneath it] rivers of unstaling water, and rivers of milk unchanging in flavor, and rivers of wine - a delight for the drinkers, and rivers of purified honey. And for them therein is every kind of fruit and forgiveness from their Lord, like [that of] one who abides eternally in the Fire and is made to drink scalding water which will sever his intestines?
interpretation: This verse contrasts the eternal bliss of Paradise with the eternal torment of Hell, emphasizing that the rewards of the righteous are incomparable to the punishments of the wicked, thereby underscoring the justice and mercy of Allah in His treatment of His servants.

translation: And among them are those who listen to you, until when they leave your presence, they say to those who have been given knowledge, "What did he just say?" Those are the ones upon whose hearts Allah has set a seal, and they have followed their [own] desires.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of certain individuals who feign interest in the message but only seek to distort or mock it once out of earshot, revealing their true rejection of divine guidance and their enslavement to personal whims rather than submission to Allah's will.

translation: And those who are rightly guided, He increases them in guidance, and He grants them their righteousness.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that true guidance from Allah is not static but grows stronger in those who sincerely seek it, and that righteousness (taqwa) is both a divine gift and a reward for those who strive to follow the path of guidance.

translation: Do they await except that the Hour comes upon them unexpectedly? But already have come [some of] its indications. Then what good to them, when it has come, will be their remembrance?
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of the Hour (Day of Judgment) and the futility of heedlessness despite clear signs of its approach. It serves as a warning that no amount of reflection or remembrance will benefit those who persist in denial when the event itself arrives, highlighting the importance of recognizing and acting upon the signs before it is too late.

translation: So know [O Muhammad] that there is no deity except Allah and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women. And Allah knows of your movement among those who are with Him and your place of dwelling.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) as the foundational truth, commanding the Prophet (peace be upon him) to affirm it and seek forgiveness for himself and the believers. It also highlights Allah's comprehensive knowledge of all human actions and states, both in this world and the Hereafter, emphasizing accountability and divine awareness.

translation: And those who believe say, "Why has a surah not been revealed?" But when a decisive surah is revealed and fighting is mentioned in it, you see those in whose hearts is hypocrisy looking at you with a look of someone overcome by death. So woe to them!
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who claim to believe but waver when faced with the practical demands of faith, particularly in times of trial or conflict. Their reluctance to act decisively reveals a lack of true conviction, as their faith is superficial and contingent on ease rather than conviction.

translation: Obedience and good speech [are better]. But when the matter is resolved, if they had been true to Allah, it would have been better for them.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and truthfulness in one's actions and words, especially in matters of faith and commitment to Allah. It suggests that mere outward obedience and speech are not sufficient; true faith requires internal conviction and honesty with Allah.

translation: Do you expect that if you turn away, you will cause corruption in the land and sever your ties of kinship?
interpretation: This verse warns against the moral and social consequences of turning away from faith and righteousness, which lead to societal decay and the breakdown of familial and communal bonds.

translation: It is these whom Allah has rejected, so He has made them deaf and blinded their eyes.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequence of divine rejection, where the individuals are deprived of spiritual guidance, resulting in their inability to perceive truth (blinded eyes) and respond to moral calls (deafness), symbolizing a complete loss of receptivity to divine guidance.

translation: Then do they not reflect upon the Qur'an, or are there locks upon [their] hearts?
interpretation: This verse questions the lack of deep contemplation of the Qur'an by some people, suggesting that their hearts may be hardened or closed off to its guidance, preventing them from understanding its true meanings and benefiting from its wisdom.

translation: Indeed, those who reverted back on their heels after guidance had become clear to them—it was Satan who enticed them and prolonged their delusion.
interpretation: This verse warns against the danger of apostasy after recognizing the truth, attributing such a fall to the whisperings of Satan and his false promises of prolonged deception, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness in faith once it is firmly established.

translation: That is because they said to those who disliked what Allah revealed, "We will obey you in some matters." And Allah knows their secrets.
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocrisy of those who outwardly claim faith but secretly align with the disbelievers to gain their approval, even in matters contrary to divine guidance. It underscores Allah's omniscience, as He is aware of their hidden intentions and deviations from true obedience.

translation: So how [will it be] when the angels take them in death, striking their faces and their backs?
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning about the severity of divine accountability, emphasizing that the angels' treatment of the deceased—striking their faces and backs—symbolizes the inescapable reality of divine justice and the consequences of one's deeds in the Hereafter.

translation: That is because they followed what angered Allah and disliked His pleasure, so He rendered their deeds worthless.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of prioritizing worldly desires or actions that displease Allah over seeking His pleasure, emphasizing that such choices nullify the value of one's deeds in the sight of Allah.

translation: Do the people who have disease in their hearts think that Allah will not expose their malice?
interpretation: This verse addresses the hypocrites who harbor hidden resentment and ill-will in their hearts, suggesting that they mistakenly believe their true intentions will remain concealed from Allah, who is fully aware of all hidden thoughts and motives.

translation: And if We willed, We could show them to you, and you would know them by their mark; but you will surely know them by the tone of [their] speech. And Allah knows your deeds.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute power and knowledge, emphasizing that He could easily expose the hypocrites if He willed, but He tests His servants by allowing them to remain hidden, thereby testing their faith and discernment. The mention of recognizing them by their speech suggests that their true nature will eventually be revealed through their words and actions, underscoring the importance of sincerity and the inevitability of divine justice.

translation: And We will surely test you until We make evident those who strive and the patient, and [until] We test your news.
interpretation: This verse highlights that trials and tribulations are a means by which Allah distinguishes between those who truly strive in His cause and those who merely claim to do so, as well as those who remain patient in adversity. It also implies that Allah tests not only faith but also the sincerity and steadfastness of believers, refining their resolve and exposing the truth of their commitment.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and averted [others] from the path of Allah and opposed the Messenger after guidance had become clear to them - they will not harm Allah at all. And He will waste their deeds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of opposing divine guidance and obstructing the path to truth, emphasizing that such actions do not harm Allah but instead nullify the efforts and deeds of those who persist in disbelief and defiance.

translation: O you who have believed, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and do not invalidate your deeds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of complete obedience to Allah and His Messenger, warning that any act of worship or righteous deed can be rendered null and void if it is not performed with sincerity and in accordance with divine guidance, highlighting the need for purity of intention and adherence to the Sunnah.

translation: Indeed, those who disbelieved and obstructed [others] from the path of Allah and then died while they were disbelievers—for them Allah will not forgive.
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of rejecting faith and actively hindering others from the truth, emphasizing that such a stance, if maintained until death, leads to an irreversible state of divine displeasure and unforgiveness.

translation: So do not weaken and call for peace while you are superior; and Allah is with you and will never deprive you of [the reward of] your deeds.
interpretation: This verse encourages steadfastness in faith and perseverance in the face of adversity, rather than seeking compromise or surrender when one is in a position of strength. It reassures believers that divine support is with them, and their efforts will not go unnoticed or unrewarded by Allah.
