interpretation: This verse highlights the intense regret and helplessness of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, as they face the consequences of their rejection of divine warnings. The 'rage' reflects the torment's unbearable severity, while the keepers' question underscores the justice of their punishment—no excuse remains for those who ignored clear guidance.

translation: They said, 'Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied [him] and said, "Allah has not sent down anything. You are not but in great error."'
interpretation: This verse highlights the stubbornness and arrogance of those who reject divine guidance despite clear signs, attributing the truth to falsehood and the messengers to delusion, reflecting a deep-seated resistance to truth and accountability.

translation: And they will say, 'If only we had listened or reasoned, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the regret of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, acknowledging that had they paid heed to the truth and used their intellect to discern it, they would not have faced the punishment of Hellfire.

translation: So acknowledge your sin, then woe to the companions of the Blaze.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice and the consequences of unrepentant sin, emphasizing that acknowledgment of wrongdoing without sincere remorse or change is insufficient for salvation.

translation: Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and a great reward.
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound reward for those who maintain taqwa (God-consciousness) even in private, without seeking recognition, demonstrating that true faith is rooted in sincerity and reverence for Allah, not outward displays.

translation: Whether you conceal your speech or declare it, indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute awareness of all thoughts, intentions, and secrets hidden within the human heart, regardless of whether they are expressed outwardly or kept concealed. It serves as a reminder of the omnipresence of divine knowledge and the accountability of every individual for their innermost feelings and motives.

translation: Does He not know who created? And He is the Subtle, the Acquainted.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's perfect and encompassing knowledge of all things, including the innermost details of His creation. The mention of 'the Subtle' (اللطيف) and 'the Acquainted' (الخبير) highlights His meticulous awareness and intimate understanding of every aspect of existence, even the most subtle and hidden matters, affirming that nothing escapes His knowledge.

translation: It is He who made the earth subservient to you, so walk among its slopes and eat of His provision, and to Him is the resurrection.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine design behind the earth's accessibility and resources, urging humanity to utilize the earth responsibly, sustainably, and gratefully, while recognizing that all provisions come from Allah and that ultimate return is to Him.

translation: Do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you up as it quakes?
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning against arrogance and complacency in one's perceived security, reminding humanity that divine power is absolute and that no earthly stability is guaranteed without divine will.

translation: Or do you feel secure that He who is in the heaven will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know how (severe) was My warning.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against arrogance and complacency in the face of divine power, reminding humanity that no matter how secure they may feel in their perceived invincibility, God's punishment can come suddenly and decisively, leaving no room for doubt about the truth of His warnings.

translation: And certainly did those before them deny, so how [terrible] was My reproach.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who reject the truth, reminding them of the fate of previous nations that denied their messengers, emphasizing that denial of divine guidance leads to severe consequences.

translation: Do they not see the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them? None holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed, He is, of all things, Seeing.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's absolute power and control over all creation, even the smallest and most seemingly insignificant creatures like birds. It serves as a reminder of His continuous oversight and sustenance of the universe, encouraging reflection on His signs to strengthen faith and trust in His divine plan.

translation: Is He [not best] who is a contingency for you to support you against the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are [only] in delusion.
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion that any power or support outside of Allah can truly aid or protect a person, emphasizing that reliance on anything other than Allah is a form of delusion and misplaced trust.

translation: Is it they who provide you with sustenance if He withholds His provision? Rather, they persist in arrogance and aversion.
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelief of those who attribute provision and sustenance to false deities or powers other than Allah, while ignoring the fact that true sustenance comes solely from Him. The persistence of the disbelievers in their arrogance and refusal to acknowledge Allah's sole authority over provision reflects their deep-seated aversion to the truth and their rejection of divine unity (tawhid).

translation: Then is he who walks fallen on his face better guided or he who walks upright on a straight path?
interpretation: This verse contrasts two paths of life: one of misguidance, represented by the person walking on their face, symbolizing confusion and moral deviation, and one of guidance, represented by the person walking upright on a straight path, symbolizing righteousness and clarity in faith and action.

translation: Say, 'It is He who has produced you and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine origin of human existence and the endowments of perception and intellect bestowed upon humanity, while lamenting the rarity of gratitude for these blessings, highlighting a fundamental aspect of human ingratitude despite the profound gifts received.

translation: Say, 'It is He who has dispersed you [mankind] throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over human life, from the initial creation and dispersion of humanity across the earth to the ultimate gathering on the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing accountability and divine justice.

translation: And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
interpretation: This verse reflects the skepticism and impatience of those who deny the truth, challenging the believers to hasten the fulfillment of divine promises or punishments as if they were in control of time and divine decree.

translation: Say, 'The knowledge is only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute sovereignty of Allah's knowledge and the limited role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a warner, underscoring that divine knowledge encompasses all things beyond human comprehension.

translation: But when they see it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieved will be distressed, and it will be said, "This is what you were calling for."
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the believers' hope and the disbelievers' despair on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the finality and inescapability of divine justice.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if Allah should destroy me and those with me or have mercy upon us, who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?''
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty of Allah over life, death, and mercy, and highlights the helplessness of disbelief in the face of divine justice, emphasizing that no one can avert Allah's punishment except through His mercy and faith.

translation: Say, 'He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him, and upon Him we rely. You will soon know who is in clear error.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of unwavering faith in Allah's mercy and complete reliance on Him, while also conveying a warning to those who oppose or doubt this truth, assuring that their error will become evident in due time.

translation: Say, 'Have you considered: if your water were to become sunken [into the earth], then who could bring you flowing water?'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute dependence of humanity on divine providence, highlighting that even the most essential and seemingly self-evident resources—like water—are entirely within God's control, and human ingenuity or effort alone cannot secure them without His will.

translation: Nun. By the pen and what they inscribe.
interpretation: This verse begins with a mysterious letter 'Nun,' whose meaning is known only to Allah, symbolizing the divine origin and wisdom of the Qur'an. The subsequent oath by the pen and what it writes signifies the importance of knowledge, writing, and the recording of deeds, highlighting the value of literacy, wisdom, and the preservation of truth in human affairs.

translation: By the grace of your Lord, you are not a madman.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) that his sanity and soundness of mind are evident to those around him, despite the accusations of madness leveled by some disbelievers. It underscores that his message and mission are divinely guided, not the product of insanity.

translation: And indeed, for you is a reward that will never be cut off.
interpretation: This verse reassures the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) of an eternal and uninterrupted reward from Allah, emphasizing the permanence and boundlessness of divine recompense for his efforts and sacrifices in conveying the message of Islam.

translation: And indeed, you are upon an exalted character.
interpretation: This verse underscores the moral and spiritual excellence of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), highlighting his exemplary conduct and noble character as a model for all humanity.

translation: You will see, and they will see.
interpretation: This verse is a declaration of divine justice and the certainty of accountability, indicating that the truth will ultimately become clear to all—both the oppressors and the oppressed—revealing the consequences of their actions in this life or the Hereafter.

translation: By which of your trials [are you distracted]?
interpretation: This verse is a rhetorical question from Allah, addressing the distractions and trials that divert people from their true purpose. It highlights the futility of being ensnared by worldly temptations or doubts, urging reflection on what truly matters in life.

translation: Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of whoever has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of the guided.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's perfect knowledge and justice, affirming that He is fully aware of those who deviate from the truth and those who remain steadfast on the right path, emphasizing that guidance and misguidance are ultimately determined by divine wisdom.

translation: So do not obey the deniers.
interpretation: This verse instructs believers to reject the influence and demands of those who reject the truth, emphasizing steadfastness in faith and adherence to divine guidance despite opposition.

translation: They wish that you would soften (in your opposition to them), so they would soften (towards you).
interpretation: This verse highlights the insincerity and manipulative nature of those who oppose the truth and its bearers, hoping that by compromising principles, the believers will be deceived into abandoning their stance, thereby making it easier for the opponents to prevail.

translation: And do not obey every worthless, disdainful swearer (of oaths).
interpretation: This verse warns against following those who are habitual liars, boastful, and devoid of integrity, as their influence can lead one astray from truth and righteousness.

translation: A slanderer, going about with malicious gossip.
interpretation: This verse condemns those who engage in backbiting and spread harmful rumors, highlighting the destructive nature of such behavior in society.

translation: One who prevents good, transgressing and sinful.
interpretation: This verse describes a person who not only abstains from doing good deeds themselves but also actively obstructs others from doing good, exhibiting arrogance and a persistent inclination toward wrongdoing and moral corruption.

translation: Then after that, a worthless slanderer.
interpretation: This verse is part of a condemnation of a person who is arrogant, oppressive, and spreads falsehood. The term 'عتل' (transliterated as 'atil') refers to someone who is harsh, aggressive, and unjust, while 'زنيم' (transliterated as 'zanīm') denotes a worthless or base person, often one who is a habitual liar or slanderer. The verse highlights the moral depravity of such an individual, emphasizing their negative traits and the harm they cause to society through their deceitful and oppressive behavior.

translation: If he has wealth and sons.
interpretation: This verse highlights the common human tendency to place undue confidence in material wealth and progeny as sources of security or status, subtly warning against such misplaced reliance and emphasizing the transient nature of worldly possessions.

translation: When Our verses are recited to him, he says, "Legends of the former peoples."
interpretation: This verse highlights the attitude of those who reject divine guidance out of arrogance or stubbornness, dismissing the Qur'an as mere tales from the past rather than acknowledging its truth and divine origin.

translation: We will brand him on the snout.
interpretation: This verse is part of a warning against those who deny the truth and persist in their arrogance, indicating that their punishment will be humiliating and inescapable, leaving a permanent mark of disgrace upon them.

translation: Indeed, We have tested them as We tested the companions of the garden when they swore to cut its harvest at dawn
interpretation: This verse highlights the concept of divine testing (fitnah) and the consequences of arrogance and breaking oaths. It serves as a reminder that human plans are subject to God's will, and that reliance on divine decree is essential rather than boasting about one's own power or resources.

translation: And they do not seek exemption.
interpretation: This verse implies a strong condemnation of hypocrisy and insincerity in faith, where individuals outwardly claim belief but inwardly withhold full commitment or obedience, refusing to submit wholeheartedly to divine commandments.

translation: Then a calamity from your Lord passed over it while they were asleep.
interpretation: This verse highlights the sudden and unexpected nature of divine trials or punishments, which can strike even when people are unaware or unprepared, emphasizing the importance of constant vigilance and righteousness in all states.

translation: So it became like the barren land devoid of vegetation.
interpretation: This verse signifies the sudden and complete transformation of a once-thriving state into one of desolation and ruin, often as a consequence of divine punishment or the natural consequences of human actions, reflecting the irreversible and stark nature of such a change.

translation: Then they called out while they were in the morning.
interpretation: This verse reflects the urgency and desperation of people who realize too late the consequences of their actions, calling out in the morning after having been negligent or heedless the night before, highlighting the regret and futility of their pleas when the time for repentance has passed.

translation: Go early to your crop if you are going to reap.
interpretation: This verse encourages proactive effort and diligence in one's responsibilities or work, emphasizing the importance of seizing the right time to act for optimal results.

translation: So they departed, conversing secretly among themselves.
interpretation: This verse reflects the hidden intentions and whispered plots of people who, despite outward appearances, harbor malicious thoughts and plans against the truth, often in hushed tones to avoid detection or confrontation.

translation: That no poor person should enter it among you today.
interpretation: This verse underscores the importance of prioritizing personal needs or immediate responsibilities over acts of charity in certain circumstances, highlighting the wisdom of deferring generosity when it could lead to greater hardship or neglect of essential duties.

translation: And they went forth in the morning determined with full power.
interpretation: This verse highlights the determination and resolve of a group of people who set out with unwavering commitment and strength, suggesting their actions were driven by a clear purpose or mission, possibly with negative or destructive intent.

translation: But when they saw it, they said, 'Indeed, we are lost!',
interpretation: This verse reflects the moment of realization and acknowledgment of error or deviation when confronted with the truth or divine guidance, often accompanied by a sense of bewilderment or regret for having strayed from the right path.

translation: Nay, but we are deprived.
interpretation: This verse reflects a state of despair and loss, where the speaker feels utterly cut off from divine favor or success, suggesting a deep sense of helplessness and abandonment.

translation: The middle one among them said, "Did I not say to you, 'Will you not glorify [Allah]?'"
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret of the righteous person who had advised their companions earlier to remember and glorify Allah, but they failed to heed the advice. The statement reflects a sense of 'I told you so' in a moment of realization, emphasizing the importance of constant remembrance of Allah and the consequences of neglecting it.

translation: They said, 'Glory be to our Lord! Indeed, we were wrongdoers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the humility and repentance of those who acknowledge their past transgressions and submit to the divine will, recognizing the error of their ways and the mercy of Allah.

translation: Then they turned to one another, blaming each other.
interpretation: This verse highlights the regret and mutual blame that will occur on the Day of Judgment among those who were partners in sin, as they realize the consequences of their actions and seek to shift responsibility, but their blame is futile in the face of divine justice.

translation: They will say, "O woe to us! Indeed, we were transgressors."
interpretation: This verse reflects the regret and despair of people in the Hereafter when they realize the gravity of their past wrongdoings and the consequences of their arrogance and defiance against divine guidance.

translation: It is hoped that our Lord will give us a better replacement in her place; indeed, we are turning to our Lord in hope.
interpretation: This verse reflects a believer's trust in Allah's wisdom and mercy, acknowledging that He may replace a loss or hardship with something better, and that true solace lies in seeking Allah's guidance and turning to Him in all circumstances.

translation: Such is the punishment [in this world]. And indeed, the punishment of the Hereafter is greater, if they only knew.
interpretation: This verse underscores the severity of the Hereafter's punishment compared to the trials in this life, emphasizing that the ultimate consequence for disbelief or wrongdoing is far more severe than any earthly retribution, urging reflection on the fleeting nature of worldly suffering versus the eternal nature of the Hereafter.

translation: Indeed, for the righteous, with their Lord are gardens of pleasure.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for those who embody piety and righteousness, emphasizing that their recompense is not merely material but a state of eternal bliss and closeness to Allah, reflecting the profound spiritual and emotional fulfillment that awaits the God-conscious.

translation: Then shall We treat the Muslims like the criminals?
interpretation: This verse questions the fairness of divine justice, implying that if God were to hold people accountable without distinction, the righteous would be treated no differently than the wicked, which would contradict His wisdom and mercy.

translation: What is the matter with you? How do you judge?
interpretation: This verse is a reproach to those who judge unjustly or hypocritically, questioning their moral integrity and the basis of their decisions, implying that their judgments are flawed or influenced by improper motives rather than justice and truth.

translation: Or do you have a scripture in which you study?
interpretation: This verse is part of a rhetorical question challenging the disbelievers who reject the Qur'an as divine revelation, implying that if they possess a scripture that confirms their claims, they should present it for examination.

translation: Indeed, in it (the camel) there is a lesson for you. Do you not see?
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and contemplation over blind imitation or superficial observation, urging believers to ponder the signs of Allah in creation to recognize His power and wisdom.

translation: Or do you have oaths binding upon Us, extending to the Day of Resurrection, that indeed you will have whatever you judge?
interpretation: This verse questions the false sense of security and arrogance of those who believe they have absolute authority or unchallengeable decrees from Allah, implying that their judgments are final and binding without accountability to divine justice.

translation: Ask them, 'Which of them will take responsibility for that? [i.e., the Quran's revelation]'
interpretation: This verse challenges the disbelievers to acknowledge the divine origin of the Quran by identifying who among them could possibly claim responsibility for its revelation, thereby exposing their inability to refute its miraculous nature.

translation: Or do they have partners [to Allah]? Then let them bring their partners if they should be truthful.
interpretation: This verse challenges those who associate partners with Allah (shirk) to prove their claims by demonstrating the power or authority of their alleged partners, implying that such partners are incapable of independent action and thus do not possess true divinity.

translation: The Day the shin will be uncovered [i.e., the matter will become severe] and they will be called to prostration but will not be able [to do so],
interpretation: This verse describes the overwhelming terror and helplessness of the Day of Judgment, where the severity of the situation will be laid bare, and people will be commanded to prostrate in submission to Allah, but their pride and disbelief will render them unable to comply, reflecting their ultimate inability to escape divine justice.

translation: Their eyes humbled, covered with humiliation—they were already destined to humiliation. And they had been invited to prostrate while they were whole.
interpretation: This verse describes the regret and humiliation of those who rejected the truth in their worldly life, despite having been invited to submit to Allah. The 'humility of their eyes' signifies the deep shame they will face in the Hereafter, contrasting with their arrogance in the past. The mention of 'being whole' emphasizes that they had every opportunity to believe but chose denial, leading to their eternal regret.

translation: So leave Me and those who deny this discourse (the Qur'an); We will progressively seize them from where they do not perceive.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine principle of gradual accountability, where Allah allows wrongdoers to persist in their disbelief temporarily, but their eventual reckoning is inevitable and will come from unexpected directions, highlighting both Allah's patience and the certainty of divine justice.

translation: And I will give them time. Indeed, My plan is firm.
interpretation: This verse reflects the divine principle of granting respite to those who oppose truth, allowing them to persist in their ways so that their eventual downfall is more decisive and serves as a clear lesson for others.

translation: Or do they ask you for a reward, so they are [heavily] burdened by debt?
interpretation: This verse highlights the ingratitude of those who reject the message of the Qur'an, suggesting that their demand for a worldly reward implies they are burdened by their own expectations or debts, rather than seeking the truth for its own sake.

translation: Or do they possess the knowledge of the unseen, so they write it down?
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion that anyone other than Allah has access to the unseen (ghayb), implying that human claims to such knowledge are baseless and arrogant, as only Allah possesses true foreknowledge and divine revelation.

translation: So wait patiently for the judgment of your Lord, and be not like the companion of the fish—when he called out while he was distressed.
interpretation: This verse cautions against impatience and despair in the face of divine trials, urging steadfastness in faith and reliance on Allah's wisdom, as exemplified by the Prophet Jonah (peace be upon him) who, despite his distress, turned to Allah in repentance and was ultimately forgiven.

translation: But for the grace of his Lord reaching him, he would certainly have been cast off on the naked shore, despised.
interpretation: This verse highlights the fragility of human resolve without divine intervention, emphasizing that even the most steadfast individuals are dependent on God's mercy to avoid ultimate ruin and disgrace.

translation: So his Lord chose him and made him of the righteous.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine selection and favor granted to a person, elevating them to a state of righteousness through their obedience and submission to God, emphasizing that true success lies in aligning one's will with the divine will.

translation: And indeed, those who disbelieve would almost make you slip with their glances when they hear the Reminder, and they say, 'Indeed, he is mad.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense hostility of the disbelievers toward the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Qur'an, manifesting in both their physical reactions (averting their gaze in aversion) and their verbal accusations (labeling him as mad to undermine his message). It underscores the psychological and spiritual challenge faced by the Prophet in conveying the truth, while also subtly affirming his steadfastness and divine protection despite such opposition.

translation: And it is not but a reminder for the worlds.
interpretation: This verse underscores the universal and timeless nature of the Qur'an's message, emphasizing that its guidance is intended for all of humanity, not just a specific group or time period.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. The Inevitable Reality.
interpretation: This verse introduces Surah Al-Haqqah, emphasizing the certainty and gravity of the Day of Judgment ('the Inevitable Reality'), which will inevitably come to pass, underscoring the importance of preparing for it through righteous deeds and unwavering faith.

translation: What is the inevitable reality?
interpretation: This verse introduces the concept of *Al-Haqqah* (The Inevitable Reality), which refers to the Day of Judgment—a reality that is certain to occur, beyond which there is no doubt or escape. It serves as a reminder of the absolute truth of divine justice and the accountability of human deeds, urging reflection on the transient nature of worldly life and the permanence of the Hereafter.

translation: And what can make you know what is the Inevitable Reality?
interpretation: This verse underscores the profound mystery and overwhelming certainty of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that its true nature is beyond human comprehension, yet its reality is absolute and unavoidable.

translation: The people of Thamud and ‘Aad denied the Stunning Calamity.
interpretation: This verse highlights the historical rejection of divine signs by two ancient nations, warning of the severe consequences that follow when communities persist in denial despite clear evidence of truth.

translation: As for Thamud, they were destroyed by the overpowering [torment].
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of defying divine commandments and the arrogance of rejecting truth, as exemplified by the people of Thamud who were destroyed by an overwhelming punishment due to their persistent disbelief and transgression.

translation: As for 'Aad, they were destroyed by a screaming, violent wind.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the consequences of arrogance and defiance against divine commandments, illustrating how natural forces can be employed as instruments of divine justice when a people persist in their transgressions.

translation: He made it (the punishment) rage against them for seven nights and eight days continuously, so that you would see the people in it (lying) fallen down as if they were hollow trunks of date-palms.
interpretation: This verse describes a severe and relentless punishment that befell a transgressing people, rendering them lifeless and utterly destroyed, emphasizing the absolute and irreversible nature of divine retribution against those who persist in defiance and oppression.

translation: So do you see for them any remnant?
interpretation: This verse questions the inevitability of consequences for actions, implying that no one can escape accountability for their deeds in the hereafter, as divine justice ensures no remnant of wrongdoing remains unaddressed.

translation: And Pharaoh came and those before him, and the overturned cities, with the same sin.
interpretation: This verse highlights the recurring pattern of arrogance and defiance against divine guidance, exemplified by Pharaoh and the nations before him, as well as the people of the overturned cities (e.g., Sodom and Gomorrah), all of whom were destroyed due to their persistent sin and rejection of truth.

translation: But they defied the command of their Lord’s Messenger, so He seized them with a severe grip.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of defying divine guidance and the authority of the Messenger, emphasizing that rejection of truth, despite clear signs, leads to severe punishment as a manifestation of divine justice.

translation: Indeed, when the water overflowed [its limits], We carried you in the ship [of Noah].
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine mercy and protection extended to humanity during times of overwhelming calamity, highlighting that salvation is a gift from Allah, not a result of human effort alone.

translation: So that We may make it for you a reminder and an admonition for those who listen attentively.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of reflection and attentive listening to the divine message, suggesting that true understanding comes from those who are spiritually attuned and receptive to guidance.

translation: Then when the Trumpet is blown with a single blast
interpretation: This verse signifies the inevitability and suddenness of the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that the resurrection will occur instantaneously with no prior warning, catching all of humanity unprepared.

translation: And the earth and the mountains were lifted up and crushed with a single crushing.
interpretation: This verse describes a moment of divine reckoning where the stability and permanence of the earth and mountains are utterly destroyed in an instant, symbolizing the absolute power of Allah to dismantle all that seems unshakable, emphasizing the inevitability and finality of the Day of Judgment.

translation: So that Day the inevitable event will occur.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and inevitability of the Day of Judgment ('the inevitable event'), highlighting that it is a predetermined reality that will come to pass without fail, underscoring the importance of preparing for it through righteous deeds and faith.

translation: And the sky is split asunder, so it becomes frail that Day.
interpretation: This verse describes a moment of cosmic upheaval on the Day of Judgment, where the heavens themselves are torn apart, symbolizing the complete dismantling of the existing order to make way for divine reckoning and the establishment of a new, eternal reality.

translation: And the angels will be on its edges, and eight will, that Day, carry the Throne of your Lord above them.
interpretation: This verse underscores the immense power and majesty of Allah, emphasizing that even the heavens and the earth are but a small part of His creation, and that the carrying of His Throne by eight angels on the Day of Judgment highlights the grandeur and weight of His sovereignty, which no created being can fully comprehend or challenge.

translation: On that Day you will be brought forth, and no secret of yours will be hidden.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute transparency of human deeds and intentions before Allah on the Day of Judgment, where nothing—no matter how concealed in this world—will remain hidden from divine knowledge.

translation: But as for he who is given his record in his right hand, he will say, "Here, read my record!"
interpretation: This verse highlights the stark contrast between the righteous and the wicked in the Hereafter, emphasizing the joy and confidence of the righteous who are granted their deeds in their right hand—a symbol of honor and salvation—with a sense of eagerness and pride in their righteous record.

translation: Indeed, I thought that I would encounter my account.
interpretation: This verse reflects the realization of an individual who, in the moment of reckoning, acknowledges that their deeds will be accounted for, highlighting the inevitability of divine justice and the consequences of one's actions in the Hereafter.

translation: So he will be in a life of pleasure.
interpretation: This verse refers to the ultimate reward of the righteous in the Hereafter, describing their state as one of complete satisfaction and contentment, free from any hardship or distress, reflecting the fulfillment of their deepest spiritual and worldly desires.

translation: In a lofty Paradise.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the elevated and supreme status of Paradise, highlighting its unparalleled honor and distinction as a reward for the righteous, far beyond mere physical elevation.

translation: Its fruits are within reach.
interpretation: This verse metaphorically describes the ease and accessibility of the rewards and blessings promised to the righteous in Paradise, emphasizing that they are not distant or unattainable but readily available to those who strive for them.

translation: Eat and drink pleasantly for what you sent ahead in the former days.
interpretation: This verse encourages believers to enjoy the permissible blessings of this world (food and drink) in moderation, while also reminding them to reflect on their past righteous deeds as a source of true contentment and reward in the Hereafter.

translation: But as for he who is given his record in his left hand, he will say, "Oh, I wish I had not been given my record!"
interpretation: This verse highlights the intense regret and despair of those who are given their book of deeds in their left hand, symbolizing their misdeeds and rejection of faith, as they realize the irreversible consequences of their actions in the Hereafter.

translation: And I do not know what my account will be.
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound sense of humility and uncertainty before divine judgment, highlighting the human inability to comprehend the full weight of one's deeds or the criteria of divine assessment.

translation: Oh, would that it were decisive!
interpretation: This exclamation reflects a deep longing for a final, definitive resolution—whether in judgment, justice, or the end of a trial—suggesting a plea for closure or an end to suffering and uncertainty.

translation: His wealth will not avail him [when the punishment comes].
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark reminder that material wealth, no matter how abundant, cannot shield a person from divine accountability or protect them from the consequences of their actions in the Hereafter. It underscores the transient nature of worldly possessions and the ultimate futility of relying on them for salvation.

translation: My authority has perished from me.
interpretation: This verse reflects the profound realization of the impermanence of worldly power and authority, emphasizing the transient nature of human control and the inevitability of its loss, which serves as a reminder of the greater, eternal sovereignty of Allah.

translation: Seize him and shackle him.
interpretation: This verse conveys a command of decisive action against a wrongdoer, emphasizing both restraint (shackling) and accountability in the face of transgression, reflecting the gravity of justice in Islamic teachings.

translation: Then let them enter Hellfire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning to those who persist in disbelief or defiance of divine commandments, emphasizing the inevitability of their punishment in the Hereafter as a consequence of their choices.

translation: Then its length is seventy cubits; so drive him into it.
interpretation: This verse describes a severe and inescapable punishment for those who reject faith and persist in their wrongdoing, emphasizing the inevitability and magnitude of divine justice.

translation: Indeed, he used to not believe in the Great Allah.
interpretation: This verse underscores the consequences of rejecting faith in Allah, highlighting the gravity of such disbelief and its implications for the individual's spiritual state and ultimate fate.

translation: And they do not urge the feeding of the poor.
interpretation: This verse criticizes those who fail to encourage or facilitate the act of feeding the needy, highlighting a lack of compassion and social responsibility.

translation: So this Day he has no devoted friend here.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute isolation of the disbeliever or wrongdoer on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing that no personal connections or worldly alliances—no matter how strong—can avail them in the face of divine justice.

translation: And [there is] no food except from the excrement of the inhabitants of Hell.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute deprivation and suffering of the inhabitants of Hell, where even their sustenance is repulsive and unworthy of consumption, symbolizing the ultimate consequence of their deeds in the Hereafter.

translation: It is eaten only by the sinners.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity of a certain action or consequence, suggesting that only those who persist in sinfulness will partake in or suffer from it, highlighting the divine justice that aligns outcomes with the nature of one's deeds.

translation: So I swear by what you see
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the certainty and truthfulness of the oath, invoking the visible signs in the universe as witnesses to the divine reality and the truth of the Qur'an's message.

translation: And what you do not see.
interpretation: This verse underscores the limitations of human perception and the vastness of the unseen world—whether in the spiritual realm, the future, or the intricacies of creation—reminding us of the need for humility and reliance on divine knowledge.

translation: Indeed, it is the word of a noble Messenger.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine origin and high status of the Qur'an, attributing its revelation to a noble and trustworthy messenger (the Angel Gabriel), thereby affirming its authenticity and importance as a message from Allah.

translation: And it is not the speech of a poet. Little do you believe.
interpretation: This verse challenges the notion that the Qur'an could be the work of a human poet, emphasizing its divine origin and the profound truth it conveys, which demands sincere faith rather than mere intellectual acknowledgment.

translation: Nor the word of a soothsayer. Little do you remember.
interpretation: This verse underscores the futility of seeking guidance from false sources like soothsayers or fortune-tellers, emphasizing that true remembrance and reflection on divine guidance are rare among people.

translation: A revelation from the Lord of the worlds.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an is a divine revelation, not a human creation, as it originates from Allah, the Lord and Sustainer of all creation, thereby establishing its divine authority and truth.

translation: And [even] if you [O Muhammad] should say (present) to us some sayings (or claims)
interpretation: This verse underscores the gravity of attributing false statements to Allah or His Messenger, warning against fabricating claims about divine matters without absolute certainty, as it constitutes a grave sin and a distortion of truth.

translation: Then We would have seized him by the right hand
interpretation: This implies a decisive and firm action taken by Allah against someone who persists in wrongdoing, demonstrating His absolute power and justice.

translation: Then We would surely cut the aorta.
interpretation: This verse underscores the certainty and inevitability of divine justice, implying that if Allah were to withhold His mercy or allow evil to go unchecked, the consequences would be so severe that it would be as if the very lifeline (the aorta) of existence were severed, leading to total annihilation or absolute chaos.

translation: But there is none of you that could prevent [Allah] from [seizing him by] a decisive grip.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah over all creation, emphasizing that no individual—no matter their status, wealth, or influence—can escape His decree or prevent His will from being fulfilled.

translation: And indeed, it is a reminder for the God-conscious.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes that the Qur'an serves as a profound reminder and guidance specifically for those who are mindful of their duties to Allah, embodying piety and righteousness.

translation: And indeed, We know that among you are those who deny [the truth].
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine knowledge of Allah, acknowledging that despite the guidance provided, some individuals will persist in rejecting the truth due to their free will and inherent disbelief.

translation: And indeed, it will be a source of regret for the disbelievers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the irreversible nature of regret that the disbelievers will experience on the Day of Judgment, highlighting the futility of their denial and the eternal consequences of their disbelief.

translation: And indeed, it is the truth of certainty.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute certainty and undeniable truth of the message being conveyed, leaving no room for doubt or ambiguity.

translation: So exalt the name of your Lord, the Most Great.
interpretation: This verse instructs the believer to glorify and praise Allah (SWT) by acknowledging His greatness and majesty, emphasizing the importance of recognizing Allah's supreme status in all aspects of life and worship.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The one who asks will be afflicted with a punishment that will inevitably occur.
interpretation: This verse serves as a warning to those who mock or doubt the divine message, indicating that their denial will not go unpunished and that the consequences of their actions are certain to befall them.

translation: For the disbelievers, there is no one to avert [the punishment].
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute and inescapable nature of divine justice for those who persistently reject faith, emphasizing that no power or intercession can prevent the consequences of their disbelief.

translation: From Allah, the Owner of the Ways of Ascent.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute sovereignty and control over all means of ascension—whether physical, spiritual, or metaphorical—highlighting His unmatched power and the inevitability of His decree.

translation: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day whose duration is fifty thousand years.
interpretation: This verse underscores the majesty and transcendence of Allah’s command, emphasizing that His temporal measures are beyond human comprehension, and the Day of Judgment’s duration—though seemingly long from a human perspective—is effortless for Allah, reflecting His absolute power and sovereignty over time and creation.

translation: So endure patiently, with beautiful patience.
interpretation: This verse encourages steadfastness and resilience in the face of hardship or adversity, emphasizing that patience should be maintained with grace, dignity, and without complaint, reflecting inner strength and trust in divine wisdom.

translation: Indeed, they see it (the Day of Judgment) as distant.
interpretation: This verse highlights the skepticism of those who deny the Hereafter, perceiving the Day of Judgment as something far off or unlikely to occur, despite its inevitability and proximity in divine reality.

translation: And We see it (the Hour) near.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the nearness of the Day of Judgment from Allah's perspective, reminding believers of the inevitability and urgency of the Hereafter, urging them to prepare for it through righteous deeds and constant remembrance of the transient nature of this world.

translation: The Day when the sky will be like murky oil.
interpretation: This verse describes the Day of Judgment, emphasizing the overwhelming and oppressive nature of the events that will unfold, where even the sky will appear dark, thick, and burdensome, reflecting the severity and dread of that Day.

translation: And the mountains will be like wool.
interpretation: This verse signifies the immense power and transformative nature of the Day of Judgment, where even the mighty mountains, typically symbols of strength and permanence, will be reduced to a state as soft and fleeting as wool, demonstrating the absolute sovereignty and control of Allah over all creation.

translation: And no friend will ask a friend.
interpretation: This verse underscores the overwhelming nature of the Day of Judgment, where even the closest relationships—such as those between intimate friends—will be rendered meaningless as each person becomes solely preoccupied with their own fate and accountability before Allah.

translation: They will see them. The criminal will wish on that Day that he could ransom himself from the punishment with his children.
interpretation: This verse highlights the depth of regret and despair that will overwhelm the wrongdoers on the Day of Judgment, where even the most precious worldly attachments—like one's own children—will be insufficient to avert divine punishment.

translation: And his companion and his brother.
interpretation: This phrase highlights the close relationship and shared responsibility between two individuals, suggesting a bond of partnership or kinship that implies mutual support and accountability in their actions or mission.

translation: And his clan that shelters him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of familial and communal support in the face of adversity, suggesting that even those who oppose the truth may find refuge in their social ties, but such shelter does not validate their actions or beliefs.

translation: And all those on earth entirely, then He will save him.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over all creation, highlighting that no matter how many or how few are on earth, Allah can single-handedly save or redeem an individual, regardless of their status or circumstances.

translation: No! Indeed, it is a blazing Fire.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stern warning against arrogance and disbelief, emphasizing that such behavior will lead to severe punishment in the Hereafter, specifically in the form of a scorching Fire.

translation: It will be a plucking out of the scalp.
interpretation: This verse refers to the severe and painful consequences of the Day of Judgment, where the skin and flesh will be torn away, emphasizing the intense suffering of the wrongdoers.

translation: It invites whoever turns away and withdraws.
interpretation: This verse highlights the Qur'an's call to all people, even those who may initially reject or turn away from its message, urging them to reflect and return to the path of guidance.

translation: And he gathered and hoarded.
interpretation: This verse is a critique of greed and miserliness, highlighting the moral failing of accumulating wealth without spending it in righteous causes or helping those in need.

translation: Indeed, mankind was created anxious:
interpretation: This verse highlights a fundamental aspect of human nature—its inherent tendency toward anxiety and impatience, suggesting that these traits are intrinsic to human creation, yet they are to be managed through faith and reliance on Allah.

translation: When evil touches him, he is despondent.
interpretation: This verse highlights the human tendency to despair and lose hope when faced with hardship or misfortune, contrasting it with the steadfastness and trust in Allah that believers are encouraged to maintain.

translation: And when good touches him, he becomes preventer (of charity).
interpretation: This verse highlights the hypocritical behavior of some individuals who, despite receiving blessings and goodness, become stingy and refuse to share their wealth or help others, showing ingratitude for God's favors.

translation: Except those who pray.
interpretation: This verse highlights the distinction between those who fulfill their religious obligations, particularly the prayer, and those who do not, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness in worship as a defining characteristic of the righteous.

translation: Those who are constant in their prayers.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of steadfastness and consistency in maintaining a strong connection with Allah through regular prayer, highlighting that true believers are distinguished by their unwavering commitment to their religious duties, even in the face of distractions or hardships.

translation: And [also] in their wealth and possessions is a known right (24:72)
interpretation: This verse highlights the inherent social responsibility within wealth, emphasizing that those who possess wealth must allocate a fixed portion for the needy and less fortunate, reflecting a system of economic justice and compassion mandated by divine guidance.

translation: For the one who asks and the deprived.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of addressing the needs of those who seek help and those who are in a state of deprivation, highlighting the moral and social responsibility of individuals and communities to provide assistance and support to the less fortunate.

translation: And those who believe in the Day of Judgment
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of faith in the Hereafter as a fundamental aspect of a believer's conviction, shaping their moral conduct and accountability in this life.

translation: And those who are fearful of the punishment of their Lord.
interpretation: This verse highlights the believers' consciousness and reverence for divine justice, indicating that their piety stems from a sincere awareness of accountability before Allah, which shapes their moral conduct and devotion.

translation: Indeed, the punishment of their Lord is not to be taken lightly.
interpretation: This verse serves as a stark warning to those who persist in disbelief or wrongdoing, emphasizing that divine retribution is inevitable and severe, and that no one should assume they are immune from it.

translation: And those who guard their private parts,
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of sexual modesty and self-restraint, urging believers to protect their chastity and avoid illicit sexual relations, reflecting a broader moral and spiritual discipline in Islam.

translation: Except from their wives or those their right hands possess, for indeed, they are not to be blamed.
interpretation: This verse clarifies that sexual relations are permissible only within the bounds of marriage or with one's lawful concubines (those owned through lawful means), and those who restrict themselves to these categories are not blameworthy.

translation: But whoever seeks beyond that [i.e., beyond marriage between spouses], then those are the transgressors.
interpretation: This verse establishes the lawful boundaries for sexual relations, which are confined to marriage between a man and a woman. Any pursuit of sexual gratification outside these divinely ordained limits—such as through fornication, adultery, homosexuality, or other prohibited acts—is deemed a transgression against Allah’s commandments, violating both moral and legal boundaries set for the preservation of societal and spiritual integrity.

translation: And those who are faithfully observant of their trusts and their covenants.
interpretation: This verse highlights the moral and ethical responsibility of believers to honor their commitments and fulfill their obligations with integrity, reflecting a deep sense of trustworthiness and reliability in both personal and communal dealings.

translation: And [they are] those who are upright in their testimonies.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of sincerity and integrity in bearing witness, emphasizing that true believers uphold their testimonies with steadfastness and truthfulness, not swayed by falsehood or personal gain.

translation: And those who are ever mindful of their prayers.
interpretation: This verse highlights the importance of consistency and attentiveness in performing the obligatory prayers, emphasizing that true believers maintain their prayers with regularity and devotion, not merely as a ritual but as a constant connection with Allah.

translation: It is they who will be in gardens, honored.
interpretation: This verse highlights the ultimate reward for the righteous in the Hereafter, emphasizing their high status and honor in Paradise, reflecting Allah's justice and generosity.

translation: So what is (the matter) with those who disbelieved before you, hastening (towards evil)?
interpretation: This verse critiques the hasty and reckless behavior of those who reject faith, implying that their rush towards disbelief is a sign of their lack of reflection and wisdom, contrasting it with the patient and thoughtful approach of believers.

translation: From the right and from the left, in separate groups.
interpretation: This verse highlights the division of people on the Day of Judgment, where individuals will be separated into distinct groups based on their deeds and allegiances, emphasizing accountability and the consequences of one's actions.

translation: Does every one of them hope to enter a Garden of Bliss?
interpretation: This verse questions the sincerity of those who claim to desire Paradise without fulfilling the necessary conditions of faith and righteous deeds, exposing their hypocrisy or false expectations.

translation: Nay, but We have created them from what they know not.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute power and sovereignty of Allah in creation, emphasizing that human beings are created from sources beyond their limited knowledge or comprehension, thereby affirming divine omnipotence and the mystery of existence.

translation: So I swear by the Lord of the rising and setting suns; surely We are able [to replace them with something better].
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's absolute power and control over all creation, including the celestial bodies, and reassures that He has the ability to bring about any change or transformation He wills, even if it seems impossible to human perception.

translation: Except that We will replace them with better [than they], and We are not to be outrun.
interpretation: This verse underscores Allah's absolute power and sovereignty over creation, affirming that He can replace any people or generation with others who are better in faith, righteousness, or deeds, and that no one can evade or challenge His decree.

translation: So leave them to indulge and play until they meet their Day which they are promised.
interpretation: This verse serves as a reminder of the transient nature of worldly pursuits and the inevitability of divine accountability, urging patience and detachment from those who mock or reject the truth.

translation: The Day they will come out of the graves quickly, as if they were, towards an erected idol, hastening.
interpretation: This verse vividly depicts the Day of Resurrection, emphasizing the swift and urgent movement of people emerging from their graves, as if driven by an irresistible force toward a false idol, symbolizing their ultimate accountability and the futility of their worldly attachments.

translation: Their eyes humbled, overwhelmed by humiliation. That is the Day they were promised.
interpretation: This verse describes the state of the disbelievers on the Day of Judgment, emphasizing their complete submission and degradation as they face the consequences of their actions, fulfilling the divine promise of punishment for their disbelief and arrogance.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Indeed, We sent Noah to his people, [saying], 'Warn your people before there comes to them a painful punishment.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine mission of Prophets as warners to their people, emphasizing the urgency of heeding divine guidance to avert impending punishment, reflecting Allah's mercy in providing clear warnings before accountability.

translation: He said, 'O my people, indeed I am to you a clear warner.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the role of prophets as bearers of divine warnings, emphasizing their duty to convey God's message clearly and unambiguously to their people, even if the message is met with rejection or hostility.

translation: Worship Allah, fear Him, and obey me.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the core principles of monotheism (Tawhid), God-consciousness (Taqwa), and submission to divine guidance through obedience to the Prophet (peace be upon him). It underscores that true worship is inseparable from righteous conduct and adherence to the teachings of Allah and His Messenger.

translation: He will forgive you your sins and delay you for a specified term. Indeed, the term of Allah, when it comes, is not delayed—if you only knew.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the divine mercy of Allah in granting respite to humanity, allowing time for repentance and reform before the inevitable Day of Judgment. It underscores the certainty of the appointed time, which cannot be postponed, urging reflection on the fleeting nature of life and the urgency of preparing for the Hereafter.

translation: He said, 'My Lord, indeed I invited my people night and day.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the relentless effort and perseverance of the prophets in conveying the message of Allah, emphasizing the importance of steadfastness and dedication in the face of rejection and opposition.

translation: So their invocation of Me has only increased them in flight.
interpretation: This verse highlights the irony of people turning away from Allah even when they invoke Him, as their supplication does not lead to reflection or repentance but rather to increased aversion and avoidance of the truth.

translation: And indeed, every time I called them that You may forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears, covered themselves with their garments, persisted, and were arrogant with extreme arrogance.
interpretation: This verse highlights the extreme resistance and defiance of those who reject guidance, even when faced with repeated calls to repentance and forgiveness. Their actions—blocking their ears, covering themselves, and persisting in arrogance—symbolize their deliberate rejection of truth, their refusal to listen, and their stubborn pride, which blinds them to divine mercy.

translation: Then indeed, I called them openly.
interpretation: This verse reflects the prophet's persistent and public efforts to convey the message of Islam to his people, despite their rejection, highlighting the duty of conveying divine guidance with clarity and without fear.

translation: Then indeed, I proclaimed to them openly and I whispered to them secretly.
interpretation: This verse highlights the dual nature of divine communication—both public and private—indicating that Allah conveys His message in ways that are accessible to all while also addressing the innermost thoughts and intentions of individuals, emphasizing accountability and the depth of divine knowledge.

translation: So I said, 'Seek forgiveness of your Lord. Indeed, He is ever a Perceiver of sin and oft-Forgiving.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the importance of seeking forgiveness from Allah, highlighting His attributes of being All-Forgiving and Acceptor of repentance, thereby encouraging believers to turn to Him in repentance and seek His mercy.

translation: And He will send down upon you rain in abundance.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and provision, indicating that He will shower blessings and sustenance upon the believers in times of need, reinforcing trust in divine favor and the certainty of His support.

translation: And He increases you in wealth and children, and He makes for you gardens and makes for you rivers.
interpretation: This verse highlights Allah's blessings in both worldly provisions and the Hereafter, emphasizing that material and familial prosperity are granted by Allah as signs of His favor, while also reminding believers that such blessings are tests of gratitude and responsibility.

translation: What is the matter with you that you do not have awe (taqwa) for Allah?
interpretation: This verse questions the lack of reverence and consciousness of Allah's majesty and power in the hearts of people, implying that true faith should naturally inspire awe and respect for the Almighty.

translation: And He has created you in stages.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the gradual and meticulous process of human creation, highlighting Allah's perfect design and the complexity of the stages from conception to birth, reflecting divine wisdom and power.

translation: Do you not see how Allah has created seven heavens in layers?
interpretation: This verse invites reflection on the intricate and layered structure of the universe, highlighting Allah's supreme power and wisdom in creation, and encouraging believers to ponder the signs of His existence and majesty.

translation: And He placed the moon among them as a light and made the sun a lamp.
interpretation: This verse highlights the divine wisdom in creating celestial bodies with distinct functions— the moon as a reflective source of light and the sun as a radiant, self-luminous entity— demonstrating Allah's perfect design in the universe.

translation: And Allah caused you to grow from the earth, a growing.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's power and role as the Creator, highlighting that human life originates from the earth, symbolizing both physical and spiritual growth under divine will.

translation: Then He will return you into it and bring you forth a (new) bringing forth.
interpretation: This verse underscores the power of Allah to resurrect humanity after death, emphasizing the certainty and completeness of this event, as if it were a second birth from the earth.

translation: And Allah has made the earth a spread for you.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's mercy and provision, highlighting that the earth is made subservient and accessible for human benefit, allowing them to inhabit, cultivate, and utilize it for their needs.

translation: So that you may follow from it (the heavens and the earth) pathways, wide and numerous.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the vastness and accessibility of the signs of Allah in the universe, encouraging humanity to explore and reflect upon them to find guidance and direction in their lives.

translation: Noah said, 'My Lord, indeed they have disobeyed me and followed those whose wealth and children only increase them in loss.'
interpretation: This verse highlights the frustration of Prophets when their people reject guidance despite their own prosperity, suggesting that material wealth and lineage do not guarantee righteousness or divine favor, and that disobedience to God's messengers leads to ultimate loss.

translation: And they plotted a mighty plot.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severity and cunning of those who conspire against truth and righteousness, often with malicious intent, but ultimately their plots are futile against the will of Allah, as divine justice prevails.

translation: And they said, 'Never leave your gods, nor leave Wadd, nor Suwa', nor Yaghuth, and Ya'uq, and Nasr.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the deep attachment of polytheistic Arabs to their idols, which they believed provided protection, sustenance, and intercession. The names mentioned—Wadd, Suwa', Yaghuth, Ya'uq, and Nasr—were deities they worshipped, and the command to abandon them signifies the rejection of false gods in favor of monotheism, emphasizing that only Allah is worthy of worship.

translation: And they have led many astray. And You will increase the wrongdoers only in error.
interpretation: This verse highlights the consequences of persistent wrongdoing and the deception of those who mislead others, emphasizing that Allah's response to the wrongdoers is not to affirm their misguidance but to allow their deviation to deepen as a natural consequence of their choices.

translation: Because of their sins they were drowned, then were made to enter the Fire. And they found not for themselves besides Allah any helpers.
interpretation: This verse underscores the inevitability of divine justice, where wrongdoing leads to severe consequences, and no external force—no matter how powerful—can intervene to save the wrongdoer from the consequences of their actions.

translation: And Noah said, 'My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any dweller from the disbelievers.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the intensity of Prophet Noah's (peace be upon him) supplication to Allah, seeking the eradication of disbelief from the earth. It underscores the severity of disbelief in the sight of Allah and the righteous, highlighting that true guidance and faith are matters of divine will and wisdom, not human force.

translation: Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except [a] wicked, disbeliever [offspring].
interpretation: This verse highlights the destructive influence of those who deviate from guidance, emphasizing that their presence can lead others astray, and their progeny will likely perpetuate their corrupt nature, underscoring the importance of divine protection against such influences.

translation: My Lord, forgive me and my parents and whoever enters my house as a believer, and the believing men and believing women. And do not increase the wrongdoers except in destruction.
interpretation: This supplication reflects the comprehensive mercy and compassion that Islam encourages, encompassing not only personal forgiveness but also extending to parents, the entire believing community, and even a plea for the ultimate downfall of the oppressors as a manifestation of divine justice, underscoring the balance between mercy and accountability in the divine scheme.

translation: In the name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful. Say, [O Muhammad], 'It has been revealed to me that a group of jinn listened and said, "Indeed, we have heard an amazing Qur'an."
interpretation: This verse highlights the profound impact of the Qur'an's divine message, even reaching beyond the human realm to the jinn, who acknowledge its uniqueness and power. It underscores the Qur'an's universal appeal and its ability to captivate listeners with its unparalleled eloquence and truth, transcending cultural and spiritual boundaries.

translation: It guides to the right path, so we believed in it. And we will never associate anyone with our Lord.
interpretation: This verse reflects the acceptance of divine guidance and the firm commitment to monotheism, rejecting any form of association or partnership with Allah, affirming absolute devotion and submission to Him alone.

translation: And [say] that Exalted is the grandeur of our Lord; He neither has a consort nor a child.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness and transcendence of Allah, negating any anthropomorphic or polytheistic notions of Him having partners, spouses, or offspring, thereby affirming His uniqueness and incomparability.

translation: And indeed, our foolish one used to say about Allah an excessive transgression.
interpretation: This verse refers to the baseless and exaggerated accusations made by ignorant people against Allah, attributing to Him falsehoods or unjust claims that exceed all bounds of reason and truth.

translation: And we had thought that mankind and the jinn would never speak against Allah a lie.
interpretation: This verse highlights the naivety of human and jinn assumptions about Allah's nature, emphasizing that only Allah possesses absolute truth and that any claim to the contrary is a falsehood, underscoring the importance of recognizing Allah's uniqueness and avoiding attributing falsehoods to Him.

translation: And that there were men from mankind who sought refuge in men from the jinn, so they increased them in burden.
interpretation: This verse highlights the futility and danger of seeking protection or help from sources other than Allah, as such actions can lead to increased hardship and misguidance rather than true security.

translation: And they thought, as you thought, that Allah would never raise anyone from the dead.
interpretation: This verse highlights the disbelief of those who, like the disbelievers of the past, deny the possibility of resurrection and the Hereafter, reflecting a shared skepticism rooted in arrogance and ignorance of Allah's power.

translation: And indeed, We have touched the heaven with Our punishment, and found it filled with strong guards and shooting stars.
interpretation: This verse signifies that divine punishment or trials are not arbitrary but are part of a structured and guarded system of justice, where no wrongdoing goes unnoticed or unchecked by Allah’s decree.

translation: And indeed, we used to sit near it (the heaven) to listen; but whoever listens now will find a burning flame lying in wait for him.
interpretation: This verse highlights the heightened vigilance of the heavens against any attempt to eavesdrop on divine decrees or unseen matters, emphasizing the futility and danger of seeking knowledge that is not meant for human access, as it is now guarded by a prepared flame to deter such intrusions.

translation: And we do not know whether harm is intended for those on earth or whether their Lord intends for them guidance.
interpretation: This verse reflects the human inability to fully comprehend the divine wisdom behind trials and tribulations, reminding us that apparent hardships may ultimately serve a greater purpose, such as guidance or purification.

translation: And among us are the righteous, and among us are [others] besides that; we were [once] distinct ways.
interpretation: This verse highlights the diversity within human societies, acknowledging that people follow different paths—some righteous and others not. It serves as a reminder of the natural variation in human beliefs and actions, urging reflection on one's own choices and the consequences of deviating from moral and righteous paths.

translation: And we certainly thought that we would never be able to escape Allah in the earth, nor would we escape Him by fleeing.
interpretation: This verse reflects a profound realization of human helplessness in the face of divine power and justice, acknowledging that no matter how one may try to evade accountability, it is ultimately unattainable before Allah.

translation: And when we heard the guidance, we believed in it. So whoever believes in his Lord will not fear deprivation or burden.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the transformative power of true guidance and the security it provides to the believer. It suggests that genuine faith in Allah eliminates fear of loss or undue hardship, as divine providence ensures justice and sustenance for those who trust in Him.

translation: And among us are the Muslims [in submission to Allah], and among us are the Qasitun [the unjust, the oppressors]. So whoever submits [to Allah], those have sought out the right path.
interpretation: This verse highlights the coexistence of righteous and deviant individuals within the same community, emphasizing the importance of personal choice in determining one's spiritual fate. It underscores that true guidance is found only through submission to Allah, distinguishing the righteous from the unjust.

translation: But as for the unjust, they will be fuel for Hell.
interpretation: This verse highlights the severe and irreversible consequence of injustice (qist), indicating that those who persistently oppress others or deviate from the path of truth and equity will ultimately face eternal punishment, serving as fuel for the fire of Hell.

translation: And [had they remained steadfast on the straight path], We would have certainly given them abundant rain in abundance.
interpretation: This verse underscores the conditional nature of divine blessings, suggesting that true and unwavering commitment to the path of righteousness and faith would have led to material and spiritual prosperity in this life, as a sign of God's favor and mercy.

translation: We will certainly test them through it (the worldly life). And whoever turns away from the remembrance of their Lord, He will place for them a punishment in an ascending way.
interpretation: This verse underscores the divine test inherent in worldly life, where trials and tribulations serve as a means to purify and elevate believers. Turning away from the remembrance of Allah—whether through heedlessness, rejection, or neglect of spiritual obligations—leads to a punishment that intensifies progressively, reflecting the consequences of severing one's connection with the divine source of guidance and mercy.

translation: And the mosques are for Allah, so do not invoke anyone besides Allah within them.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the exclusivity of Allah's right to worship and devotion, particularly in places of worship like mosques. It prohibits associating partners with Allah or directing any form of supplication or worship to other entities, reinforcing the core Islamic principle of Tawhid (monotheism).

translation: And indeed, when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him, they almost became about him a compacted mass.
interpretation: This verse highlights the intensity of the Prophet Muhammad's (peace be upon him) devotion and supplication to Allah, to the extent that his enemies were overwhelmed by his sincerity and commitment, nearly forming a dense crowd around him in their opposition or curiosity.

translation: Say, 'I only invoke my Lord and I do not associate anyone with Him.'
interpretation: This verse emphasizes the absolute oneness of Allah (Tawheed) and the rejection of any form of polytheism or association in worship, affirming that all acts of devotion and supplication should be directed solely to Allah without any partners or intermediaries.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, I possess no power to harm you or guide you to the right path.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the fundamental Islamic belief in the absolute sovereignty of Allah and the limited role of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a messenger. It emphasizes that the Prophet cannot compel guidance or impose harm upon anyone; his mission is solely to convey the divine message, while the ultimate acceptance or rejection lies with Allah and the free will of individuals.

translation: Say, 'Indeed, no one can protect me from Allah, nor will I find besides Him any refuge.'
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute sovereignty and uniqueness of Allah, emphasizing that no power or refuge exists outside of Him, and it serves as a reminder of complete reliance on Allah alone for protection and salvation.

translation: But [We sent them] only for a clear notification from Allah and His messages. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger will have the fire of Hell, wherein they will abide eternally.
interpretation: This verse underscores the absolute authority of Allah and His Messenger, emphasizing that obedience to divine commands is non-negotiable. It serves as a stern warning against defiance, highlighting the eternal consequences of such disobedience, thereby reinforcing the gravity of submission to Allah's will.

translation: Until when they see what they are promised, they will then know who is weaker in support and fewer in number.
interpretation: This verse underscores the ultimate realization of truth when the consequences of one's actions or beliefs become manifest, revealing the fragility of false alliances and the inadequacy of worldly power in the face of divine justice.

translation: Say, 'I do not know whether what you are promised is near or whether my Lord will extend it for a [long] period.'
interpretation: This verse reflects the humility of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) in acknowledging his limited knowledge of the unseen, particularly regarding the timing of divine decrees or the Hereafter, while affirming that ultimate authority rests with Allah, who alone determines the appointed time.

translation: Knower of the unseen, so He does not disclose His unseen to anyone.
interpretation: This verse emphasizes Allah's exclusive knowledge of the unseen (ghayb), highlighting that no one—not even the most righteous servants—has access to His divine knowledge unless He wills to reveal it.
